title: Caller-supplied natural die results and model-supplied campaignId in in-force tools: verify integrity boundary
description: Reported by the eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12 inventory pass (2026-10-09, main 6f57be85), not yet verified as defects. (1) record_death_save (toolRecordDeathSave.ts) and restore_usage (toolRestoreUsage.ts) accept a caller-supplied natural d20/recharge result and only range-check it; nothing binds it to a roll-tool result. ADR 0020 section 3 makes random-number generation a deterministic responsibility. Determine whether another layer (mechanics auditor, roll ledger/playerVisibleRollLedger, turn audit) already enforces that the natural came from a seeded roll this turn; if not, the defect class is 'declared die result accepted without seeded-roll evidence' - enumerate every tool taking a natural/roll input (sibling search) and bind them to roll evidence (compare validateDiceRollEvidence used by level-up HP rolls). (2) memory_drilldown (toolMemoryDrilldown.ts) passes the model-supplied campaignId to memoryDrilldown(ctx.db, selector) without comparing it to ctx.campaignId; determine whether ctx.db is campaign-scoped (then no requirement) or shared (then a cross-campaign read). (3) the roll tool description omits category hit_die although the schema enum accepts it (model-facing doc mismatch). Profile: semantic-system. The capability inventory already states each trust boundary truthfully, so this is not an inventory defect.
notes:
Additional suspects from the 19.5.12 attempt-2 re-derivation (2026-10-09), unverified: (4) accept_ambiguity_precedent description tells the model to supply all matching interpretation ids, but the schema/code accept exactly one (model-facing contract mismatch). (5) set_suffocation description says the drop to 0 HP happens at the start of the next turn, but the tool applies it when called (check against SRD Suffocating: 'At the start of its next turn, it drops to 0 hit points and is dying' - a description/behavior mismatch that can misplace the SRD timing). (6) expend_ammunition does not verify the item is ammunition. (7) reset_usage fails the whole call if any spent in-scope counter belongs to a pack-bound item. (8) resolve_concentration rolls the d20 before checking the owner is concentrating (no state persisted, RNG advances). (9) applyLevelUp relies on callers to gate eligibility. Triage each: operative invariant + authority, or 'no requirement'.
TRIAGE 2026-10-09 (Claude Captain, main 6413bcc7). (1) caller-supplied naturals in record_death_save / restore_usage: NOT a code defect against current authority - the design deliberately routes them through the mechanics auditor (turnAuditor.ts ~L158-167: 'Any dice roll ... requires roll'; 'Reject if a hand-written roll result contradicts tool output'), i.e. model-audited, not deterministically bound. Whether dice-consuming mutation tools must instead bind seeded roll evidence deterministically (as level-up HP rolls do via validateDiceRollEvidence) is an ARCHITECTURAL DECISION under ADR 0020 section 3 (RNG ownership) - surfaced to the user; no change without that decision. The capability inventory states the trust boundary truthfully. (2) memory_drilldown campaignId: no requirement - each campaign has its own SQLite file (CLI resolves target.entry.dbPath; ESHYRA_DB_PATH is an explicit single-campaign DB, ADR 0004), so a mismatched campaignId cannot read another campaign. (3) roll description omits hit_die: REAL model-facing contract mismatch (schema enum ROLL_CATEGORIES includes hit_die; description hand-lists the others). Fix: derive the description's category list from ROLL_CATEGORIES + a test that the description names every category. (4) accept_ambiguity_precedent: no requirement - matchingInterpretationIds is deliberately an array the model fills with ALL matches and the engine refuses unless exactly one matches (fail-closed ambiguity gate); description and code agree. (5) set_suffocation: no requirement - the description tells the DM to call event drop at the start of the creature's next turn after the survival interval; applying when called is that contract. (6) expend_ammunition not checking ammunition: no requirement - no authority requires the defensive check; the DM names the item. (7) reset_usage atomic refusal: no requirement - fail-closed all-or-nothing is correct. (8) resolve_concentration advancing RNG before the concentrating check: no requirement - replay re-executes the identical call sequence, so the seeded stream stays deterministic and nothing persists on refusal. (9) applyLevelUp eligibility gated by callers: no requirement - the inventory states it; callers (guidedLevelUpFlow, playProgression) gate.

Found by the 2026-10-09 engine/pack rebaseline (Claude Captain), verified against main a961fb0b.

DEFECT (state integrity of capabilities in force): resolve_check now derives skill/ability/save modifiers from the character sheet (eshyra-r8en, PR #637; toolResolveCheck.ts reads sheet.savingThrows[ability].proficient and the sheet's skill proficiency), and the engine refuses a caller-declared proficiency when skill/ability is given. But level-up never sets a proficiency that a FEATURE or a chosen OPTION grants:
- feature:rogue:slippery-mind (rogue 15): 'you gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws'. levelUpEngine.ts (~L1550) copies each sheet.savingThrows[ability].proficient unchanged, so a level-15 rogue's derived Wisdom save omits proficiency.
- feature:monk:diamond-soul (monk 14): 'proficiency in all saving throws'. Same path; never applied.
- eldritch-invocation:beguiling-influence (option of feature:warlock:eldritch-invocations): 'You gain proficiency in the Deception and Persuasion skills.' levelUpFeatureChoices.ts records the chosen option (eshyra-ug4i.3) but applies no grant; the option carries only source text.
Consequence: a deterministic check/save total that contradicts the SRD (hard blocker under the srd-fidelity rule). Pack side: the first two carry free-text effects {kind:'proficiency', grant:'Wisdom saving throws'} (the opus:F-13 'proficiency-grants' class owned by eshyra-o9bd.19.2.3); the invocation has no structured grant at all.

SCOPE: make creation and level-up apply source-backed proficiency grants from class features, subclass features, and chosen options to the sheet (saves, skills; record armor/weapon/tool grants where the sheet carries them), with the minimal source-faithful typed grant on the pack side under docs/importer-fix-protocol.md where the current free text cannot be consumed. Sibling check (enumerate by query over feature/feat descriptions and option text, do not stop at these): feature:life-domain:bonus-proficiency (heavy armor, creation-time L1 subclass); other invocation options with sheet-state grants (e.g. Devil's Sight sense) only if the sheet models that state. Already handled elsewhere, verify not regressed: feature:college-of-lore:bonus-proficiencies (eshyra-91o0).
EXCLUSIONS: no universal per-option mechanics projection; unconsumed option prose stays DM-adjudicated source material.
design:
DESIGN (Claude Captain, 2026-10-09, survey at main a961fb0b). Effective review profile: rules-clause-complete (pack typing) + semantic-system (durable sheet state).

SIBLING ENUMERATION (query: every feature/subclass/feat record description + every choices[].options[].text sentence containing 'proficien'; plus every mechanics.effects[kind=proficiency]):
 APPLY (sheet models the state):
  - feature:rogue:slippery-mind (L15) 'You gain proficiency in Wisdom saving throws.' -> savingThrows.wisdom.proficient
  - feature:monk:diamond-soul (L14) 'proficiency in all saving throws' -> all six saves
  - eldritch-invocation:beguiling-influence (option of feature:warlock:eldritch-invocations, choice id eldritch-invocations) -> skills Deception, Persuasion. REPLACEABLE (warlock may swap one invocation per level, levelUpFeatureChoices replacementDescriptor) so removal must be exact.
  - feature:life-domain:bonus-proficiency (subclass L1, chosen at CREATION) 'proficiency with heavy armor' -> armorProficiencies += 'heavy armor'
 ALREADY HANDLED, must not regress: feature:college-of-lore:bonus-proficiencies (skill choice, levelUpSkillChoices.ts, eshyra-91o0); Expertise (levelUpExpertise.ts); ancestry fixed skills (srdAncestrySkills.ts).
 RECORDED NOT-APPLIED (reason: no sheet state / not a standing grant): feature:warlock:pact-boon Pact of the Blade 'proficient with it while you wield it' (conditional on wielding the pact weapon; attack-time DM adjudication, sheet has no per-weapon conditional proficiency); feature:monk:deflect-missiles (one attack 'with proficiency'); feature:druid:wild-shape (retain/gain creature proficiencies while transformed; no sheet form state); eldritch-invocation:devils-sight etc. (senses not modeled on the sheet); magic-item proficiency effects (attunement-scoped, owned by the magic-item backlog, not the sheet). Bard/Rogue Expertise are not grants.

DECISIONS:
 D1 Pack: proficiency mechanics effects gain OPTIONAL typed fields alongside the verbatim free text (never replacing it): savingThrows: AbilityScoreName[] (lowercase), skills: string[] (canonical SRD skill names, Title Case as in the College of Lore from[] list), armor: string[] (subset of 'light armor'|'medium armor'|'heavy armor'|'shields'). Emitted ONLY when the whole grant phrase parses into that vocabulary; otherwise free text only (fail closed, no invention). Diamond Soul keeps scope:'all-saving-throws' and adds all six. Options: a FeatureChoiceOption may carry mechanics:{effects:[...]} containing ONLY typed proficiency effects derived from its own text (no other projectors run on option text, to avoid unrelated churn). Weapons/tools/languages stay untyped (no consumer).
 D2 Engine: resolver exposes typed grants per feature and per option. Grants apply at the acquisition boundary: creation finalize (all level-1 class + subclass features and level-1 chosen options) and level-up (newly gained features + newly chosen options). Level-up also RECONCILES legacy sheets: any held feature/option whose typed grant has no ledger entry is applied then (idempotent), so sheets created before the fix converge at their next level-up.
 D3 Durable provenance ledger: CharacterSheet.proficiencyGrants?: {sourceRef, savingThrows?, skills?, armor?}[] recording ONLY what each source newly ADDED (items already held from any source are not recorded and therefore never removed). Optional (legacy sheets omit it); validated with the other sheet validators. One entry per sourceRef; never duplicated.
 D4 Replacement: replacing an option removes exactly that option's recorded additions and drops its ledger entry; then the incoming option's grants apply. If a recorded skill to be removed is an expertise target on the sheet, the replacement is refused fail-closed with a clear message (SRD expertise presupposes the proficiency; the engine does not guess).
 D5 Saves recomputed in recomputeAfterChoices/changeSet so preview shows the delta and resolve_check (reads sheet.savingThrows[ability].proficient and sheet skill proficiency) needs no change.
EXCLUSIONS: no universal option-mechanics projection; unconsumed option prose stays DM-adjudicated. No freeze-manifest hash changes, no thaw notes (re-freeze is reserved).
DECOMPOSITION: child .1 pack typing (Haiku) -> child .2 engine consumption (Sonnet; durable state + replacement integrity), sequential on parent branch eshyra-olc5.7. One PR.
acceptance_criteria:
- A character who gains Slippery Mind, Diamond Soul, or Beguiling Influence (via level-up or creation) has the granted proficiency on the persisted sheet, and resolve_check's derived save/skill modifier includes it.
- Every sibling found by the enumeration is either applied the same way or recorded with an explicit reason the sheet does not model that state; none is silently skipped.
- Pack-side typing (if added) is source-faithful and regenerates byte-exactly; no proficiency is invented.
- Evidence distinguishes the defective state (proficiency missing after level-up) from the repaired one.
notes: PR #642 opened at head bb0d9eb2 (children .1, .2 integrated; captain fix bb0d9eb2 removal-before-addition). Sol review child eshyra-olc5.7.3.
close_reason: PR #642 merged after GPT-6.1-Sol APPROVED at exact head bb0d9eb2 (eshyra-olc5.7.3). Typed pack grants + engine ledger; Slippery Mind, Diamond Soul, Beguiling Influence (with exact replacement removal), Life Domain heavy armor applied at creation/level-up; legacy sheets reconcile at next level-up.

title: Rest resolves class data from bundled pack instead of campaign binding
description: Aggregate review of run #625-#638 (main a23bf6d5): completeShortRest/completeLongRest call restoreSpellSlots without a RulesPackCharacterResolver (falls back to bundled), and rest.ts resolvePool hard-codes getBundledDnd5eCharacterResolver for Hit Dice. An add-on Wizard-5 level-4 slot spent via spend_spell_slot is deleted by short-rest reconciliation and re-inserted full later (recharge); Hit Die overrides are ignored. title: Repair PR #600 review 5449078494: successor-id reservation and legacy revert-form cleanup guard (captain inline)
description:
Review 5449078494 on head 27d013e2 (CHANGES REQUESTED, two blockers).
B1 (7vh3): '<id>:uncontrolled' is caller-claimable in either order (active or ended squatter), so a concentration break throws in finalizeEnd and rolls back its cause (damage/death, replacement, combat closure). Fix: reserve the ':uncontrolled' effect-id suffix as engine-owned at createActiveEffect, and refuse creating a cast-anchored-removal spell effect whose derived successor id already exists (legacy squatters). Replace the 'refuses to invent another id' test with identity-admission evidence for both orderings plus a causal break (damage-save failure) proving the damage commits and the successor is created.
B2 (ysr3): migration 0040 leaves a v39 Giant Insect link with remove/remove and no natural form; end/break/remove_effect_target would make it absent. Fix: fail closed at the cleanup seam (cleanupOwnedState + removeEffectTarget) for an actor link whose holder's 0-HP rule is 'revert-form' but whose policy is not 'revert' (no snapshot); never translate legacy remove into absence. Evidence: migrated v39 Giant Insect refused on end, break and target removal with creature/effect unchanged; Animate Objects migration stays the negative sibling.
notes: Both blockers repaired in c3b9ffc0 (pushed). verify:worktree green: 326 files, 5915 tests. Negative proofs run for both guards. Inline replies posted; awaiting fresh full review as the reviewer required.

title: Dispatch: ysr3 Animate Objects / Giant Insect 0-HP reversion (Sonnet 5.5, attempt 1)
description:
Implement eshyra-ysr3 (read it: `bd show eshyra-ysr3`). Parent integration bead: eshyra-j3yp. All design decisions below are made; do not re-decide them. If something here contradicts the code or the SRD record text, stop and record the contradiction in your notes rather than improvising.

HARD RULE (bd memory srd-fidelity-hard-blocker): nothing may contradict the SRD. Source text is in packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json (records `spell:animate-objects`, `spell:giant-insect`; read `data.description` and `data.effects[0].profile/transitions`). Do NOT edit records.json or any importer file.

## Source facts
- Animate Objects (profile `animated-object`): "Each target animates and becomes a creature under your control until the spell ends or until reduced to 0 hit points." / "When the animated object drops to 0 hit points, it reverts to its original object form, and any remaining damage carries over to its original object form." Transitions: spell-end-reversion and zero-hp-reversion (effect->ended, form->original; the 0-HP one has operation carry-remaining-damage-to-original-form). The original form is an OBJECT, not a creature.
- Giant Insect (profile `target-transformation`, identity existing-targets, "targets transform in place"): "A creature remains in its giant size for the duration, until it drops to 0 hit points, or until you use an action to dismiss the effect on it." Transitions spell-end-reversion, zero-hp-reversion, action-dismissal-reversion (effect->ended, form->original, scope each-target). The original form is the same CREATURE at natural size. No damage carry-over is stated (contrast Animate Objects), so none is applied.

## Decisions (captain + user, 2026-10-04)
1. Split the durable 0-HP rule value 'revert' into two values:
   - `'revert-object'` (Animate Objects): at 0 HP the creature leaves play exactly like 'vanish' (status absent, never dead/dying/stable/unconscious), its actor link closes (status removed, reason zero-hit-points) and the effect ends (source-removed) when no owned creature remains (reuse closeActorLinkAtZeroHp 'close' mode). The result reports the reversion plus `carriedOverDamage` = damage beyond the hit points it had (`max(0, damage - hpBefore)`; 0 for suffocation drops and exhaustion clamping). The engine does not track object hit points: report the amount, do not invent object state.
   - `'revert-form'` (Giant Insect): at 0 HP by ANY route (damage, suffocation drop, exhaustion clamp to 0; exhaustion 6 is still death) the creature reverts to its recorded natural form and STAYS IN PLAY: status alive, hpCurrent/hpMax/rulesRef restored from the snapshot (decision 2), hpCurrent clamped to the effective max (exhaustion still applies), conditions kept (the same creature; effect-owned condition projections are cleaned by normal link cleanup), zero_hp_rule cleared to null, its actor link closes (status removed, reason zero-hit-points) and the effect ends (source-removed) when no owned creature remains. Never dead/dying/stable/unconscious/absent.
   `vanishesAtZeroHp` currently covers vanish|vanish-bonded; introduce a clearly named predicate for "leaves play at 0 HP" (vanish, vanish-bonded, revert-object) and use it wherever the guards mean "cannot be present at 0 HP / cannot be admitted at 0 HP / absent at 0 HP"; audit every `vanishesAtZeroHp` and `=== 'revert'` site in packages/core/src (combatantLifecycle.ts, encounterCombatants.ts, activeEffects.ts) and route each to the right predicate. The knockout / player-character-death-rules refusals keep applying to all four rule values.
2. Natural-form snapshot (user chose "snapshot at cast"): `start_effect` actors entries gain `naturalForm: { hpCurrent: int > 0, hpMax: int >= hpCurrent, rulesRef: non-empty string }`. REQUIRED when the derived rule is 'revert-form', REFUSED otherwise (including for ruling-sourced actors; `atZeroHitPoints` stays 'vanish' | 'vanish-bonded' only). rulesRef is required so the reverted row never keeps the giant stat-block ref; it need not resolve in the rules stack (lookupCreatureRecord already tolerates unresolved refs; e.g. 'creature:spider' resolves, a centipede has no SRD record). Store it durably on the actor link (new nullable column, decision 4). Reversion restores exactly these values: the hit points it had when transformed.
3. Cleanup policies: add `'revert'` to EffectCleanupPolicy. Derive from the record (extend deriveSummonCleanup / deriveZeroHpRule in packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts, near line 2600):
   - profile `animated-object`: spell-end-reversion -> cleanupOnEnd 'remove'; concentration spell -> cleanupOnBreak 'remove' (the object stops being a creature: it leaves play). A contradicting explicit value (e.g. 'release') is refused with the record's transition id in the message, like the existing derived-policy refusals.
   - profile `target-transformation`: cleanupOnEnd 'revert' and cleanupOnBreak 'revert'; contradictions refused.
   - A form->original zero-hit-points transition on any OTHER profile: throw (unknown reversion target) rather than guess.
   - 'revert' is only legal on an actor link carrying a natural form; refuse it anywhere else (condition/zone/form links, ruling sources, explicit declarations without a snapshot).
   Cleanup action for 'revert': restore the natural form through a new engine seam (mirror removeCombatantFromPlay / removeCampaignActorFromPlay in packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts ~2658-2760: combatant in an active instance, else the campaign actor, delegating to its active combatant projection), then close the link with status 'removed' and report action 'reverted' (add 'reverted' to EffectCleanupAction['action']; do not add a link status). Apply it in cleanupOwnedState (~2286) and removeEffectTarget (~4390, per-target action dismissal) — both currently treat everything that is not 'release' as remove. Unreachable holder -> 'missing' as for remove.
4. Migration `packages/core/data/migrations/0040_*.sql` (follow 0024 and 0039 for the table-rebuild pattern and PRAGMA handling; check how migrationRunner registers/validates migrations):
   - active_effect_link: cleanup_on_end / cleanup_on_break CHECKs add 'revert'; add `natural_form_json TEXT` (NULL unless link_kind = 'actor'; consider a CHECK that 'revert' policies imply link_kind 'actor' AND natural_form_json IS NOT NULL). Keep the zone/form remove-only CHECK.
   - encounter_combatant.zero_hp_rule CHECK becomes ('vanish','vanish-bonded','revert-object','revert-form'). Rewrite existing 'revert' rows: 'revert-object' when any actor link (any status) holding that combatant belongs to an effect whose source_ref = 'spell:animate-objects', otherwise 'revert-form'. Apply the same rewrite to the mirrored campaign-actor lifecycle JSON (`combatLifecycle.zeroHpRule`; find the column via encounterCombatants.ts ~1176-1250 readCombatLifecycle/upsertCampaignActor) and to readCombatLifecycle's accepted values. Nothing has been released since v0.2.0 (2026-06-28), so legacy 'revert-form' rows without a snapshot only exist in dev DBs: durable-state validation reports them, and a 0-HP reversion of such a creature refuses with a message naming the missing natural form (ending/removing its owning effect target still works under its stored legacy policy).
5. validateActiveEffectDurableState (activeEffects.ts ~1490): report a 'revert' policy link without a natural form, a natural form on a non-actor link, and an active 'revert-form' creature with no active snapshot-carrying link.
6. Results and model-facing text. Generalize the update_combatant outcome (encounterCombatants.ts `VanishedOutcome` ~496-510, toolUpdateCombatant.ts ~200-220, exhaustionMutation.ts ~91, the suffocation path ~3308 and toolSetSuffocation.ts text): 'revert-object' reports that the animated object reverted to an object and left play, with carriedOverDamage and the link/effect outcome; 'revert-form' reports a `reverted` outcome with the restored natural form (hpCurrent, hpMax, rulesRef) and the link/effect outcome. Never say "vanished" for a reversion. Update the descriptions in toolUpdateCombatant.ts, toolStartEffect.ts (naturalForm property + cleanup 'revert' + derived policies), toolSetSuffocation.ts, toolStartEncounter.ts if it mentions the rule, toolRemoveEffectTarget/toolEndEffect if they describe cleanup actions. Every model-facing sentence must be re-derived against the source text above and the actual tool contract.
7. docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md: replace the "`revert` ... only feeds the guards; its 0-HP behaviour is pending (eshyra-ysr3)" text in §9 and the §8 remove/absent notes with the executed contract for both values, the 'revert' cleanup policy, the snapshot, and the migration's legacy rule.

## Evidence (packages/core/test/zeroHpVanishAndRemovePolicy.test.ts is the home; add a sibling file only if it grows unwieldy)
Registry-level evidence per source sentence, asserting identities and exact values (no count-pinned assertions):
- Animate Objects: damage past 0 -> status absent (not dead), link removed reason zero-hit-points, carriedOverDamage exact (e.g. hp 7, hpDelta -10 -> 3); last object -> effect ended source-removed; with two objects the effect continues; spell end (end_effect expired/dismissed) and concentration break -> absent via derived 'remove'; explicit cleanupOnEnd 'release' refused; suffocation drop -> absent with carriedOverDamage 0.
- Giant Insect: damage to 0 -> alive with exactly the snapshot hp/hpMax/rulesRef, zeroHpRule null, link removed (zero-hit-points), never dead; exhaustion clamp to 0 and suffocation drop -> same reversion; spell end, concentration break, and remove_effect_target (per-target dismissal) -> reverted in play with action 'reverted'; missing naturalForm refused; naturalForm on a vanish spell or ruling source refused; explicit cleanup 'remove'/'release' refused; knockout and player-character death rules still refused.
- Migration: a DB at 0039 with a 'revert' Animate Objects row and a 'revert' Giant Insect row migrates to 'revert-object' / 'revert-form' (follow migrationRunner.test.ts / migrationLegacyAdoption.test.ts patterns); legacy revert-form without snapshot is reported by validation.
- Replace the existing test "a reverting creature gets the guards but no automatic 0-HP behaviour" (it encodes the pending state and passes release/release, which is now refused). Update persistence/migration tests that enumerate zero_hp_rule values.

## Procedure
Work only in this worktree. Run `npm ci` first if node_modules is missing. Run `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing (it rewrites files); it must be fully green (documented skips only). Commit on this branch with a message starting `eshyra-ysr3`, ending with the line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
notes:
COMPLETE, commit 5b642b45 on eshyra-j3yp.1 (not pushed). verify:worktree fully green (324 files passed, 2 skipped; 5881 tests passed, 3 skipped).
CHANGED: combatantLifecycle.ts (ZeroHpRule now vanish|vanish-bonded|revert-object|revert-form; leavesPlayAtZeroHp/revertsFormAtZeroHp/describeZeroHpRule replace vanishesAtZeroHp; revert-form is a transient alive-at-0 state restored by the adapter in the same txn); activeEffects.ts (revert policy, NaturalForm, naturalForm on actor input + natural_form_json link column, deriveZeroHpRule/deriveSummonCleanup per profile, refusals, applyLinkPolicy/revertProjection, findActiveNaturalForm, closeActorLinkAtZeroHp 'how' param, audit checks); encounterCombatants.ts (RevertedOutcome, revert seams, completeZeroHpObjectReversion/FormReversion, out-of-combat actor reversion, admission/knockout guards, suffocation path, syncCombatantActor now syncs rulesRef); exhaustionMutation.ts; internal.ts; tools: toolUpdateCombatant (revertedMessage), toolSetSuffocation, toolStartEffect (naturalForm, revert cleanup), toolEndEffect, toolRemoveEffectTarget, toolStartEncounter; migration 0040_zero_hp_revert_rules_natural_form.sql; data/schema.snapshot.sql regenerated; docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md.
TESTS: new packages/core/test/zeroHpRevertRules.test.ts (20 tests, sibling file since zeroHpVanishAndRemovePolicy.test.ts is already ~770 lines; covers every source sentence for Animate Objects and Giant Insect incl. out-of-combat, legacy audit, refusals); combatantLifecycle.test.ts 'zero-hit-point reversion rules...'; migrationRunner.test.ts 'migration 0040 splits the legacy revert rule...'. Replaced 'a reverting creature gets the guards but no automatic 0-HP behaviour' in zeroHpVanishAndRemovePolicy.test.ts (regex now /original object form/); updated persistence/migrationLegacyAdoption version lists.
DEVIATIONS/NOTES: (1) Restored combatant ac is taken from the natural rulesRef record when it resolves, else NULL (snapshot has no AC). (2) A dead or absent holder at reversion cleanup reports 'missing'. (3) Closing combat with a combatant concentration owner breaks concentration so Giant Insect creatures revert at combat close (correct per cleanupOnBreak revert); the out-of-combat reversion test therefore uses a character concentrator. (4) closeActorLinkAtZeroHp audit note text for non-reverting case changed from 'disappeared' to 'left play'. (5) A recast concentration replacement re-applies the zero_hp_rule after the replaced effect's cleanup clears it. (6) Pre-existing audit quirk observed: auditActiveEffectIntegrity reports 'persistent actor link still points at combatant' for any active durable-actor link on a combatant even mid-combat.
close_reason: Closed

title: Integrate the PR #599 follow-ups: summon reversion, uncontrolled 1-hour removal, bonded recast (single PR)
description:
Supervisor-owned integration bead. One branch and one PR carrying eshyra-ysr3 (Animate Objects / Giant Insect 0-HP reversion), eshyra-7vh3 (Conjure Elemental/Fey cast-anchored 1-hour removal after a concentration break) and eshyra-s02z (Find Familiar / Find Steed recast restores an absent bonded creature). Children are serialized (all three touch packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts, encounterCombatants.ts and docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md).

DECISIONS (captain, 2026-10-04):
- ysr3 Giant Insect: user chose 'snapshot at cast'. start_effect captures each target's natural form (hit points current/max, optional rulesRef) for a target-transformation spell; reversion (0 HP by any route, spell end, concentration break, per-target action dismissal) restores that form with the HP it had when transformed, no damage carry-over (the source states carry-over only for Animate Objects). The creature stays in play.
- ysr3 Animate Objects: the original form is an object, not a creature: the combatant leaves play (absent), its link closes, the effect ends when no animated object remains, and the result reports the damage beyond 0 carried over to the object (objects are not tracked).
- 7vh3: a concentration break of Conjure Elemental/Fey ends the controlled effect with release (unchanged) and in the same transaction starts a non-concentration, non-dismissible successor effect inheriting the original cast anchor with a 1-hour timer and remove cleanup, so the creature becomes absent at cast+1h.
- s02z: recast operation on the existing bonded effect (Find Steed: same actor, max HP; Find Familiar: restore presence + optional new form); refused after release.

title: Repair S50 from PR review 5404411821 (captain inline)
description: S50 (S1 invariant 8 + lifecycle matrix rows 138-139): (1) 'vanish-bonded' requires a durable campaign-actor identity (explicit campaignActorId or an existing campaign_actor projection); start_effect refuses it otherwise, because combat closure releases instance-only links. (2) start_encounter must not restore an absent actor still held by an active actor link: presence returns only through the source recast (Find Familiar cast / Find Steed recast to max HP), which is not executable yet, so refuse and disclose. description:
SRD contradiction (pre-existing on main; hard blocker class per bd memory srd-fidelity-hard-blocker): a creature animated by Animate Objects or enlarged by Giant Insect that drops to 0 HP is killed by the engine (monster death rules => status dead). The source says it reverts instead.

- spell:animate-objects: "Each target animates and becomes a creature under your control until the spell ends or until reduced to 0 hit points." / "When the animated object drops to 0 hit points, it reverts to its original object form, and any remaining damage carries over to its original object form." title: Dispatch: S44 repair - SRD 0-HP summon lifecycle and remove-policy integrity (Sonnet 5.5, attempt 1)
description:
Repair for PR #599 review finding S44 (review 5403780189 at head 7414d014; S43 withdrawn in 5403787349), widened by the user on 2026-10-03 to every SRD contradiction in the same defect class.

GOVERNING RULE (user, hard blocker; bd memory srd-fidelity-hard-blocker): no change may modify or contradict the SRD in letter or spirit. Before each behaviour decision, read the governing record text in packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json (data.description plus data.mechanics.effects[*].transitions).

SOURCE AUTHORITY
- Conjure Animals, Conjure Celestial, Conjure Elemental, Conjure Fey, Conjure Minor Elementals, Conjure Woodland Beings: "disappears when it drops to 0 hit points or when the spell ends". Records carry transition {trigger:'zero-hit-points', changes:[effect->ended, presence->absent]}.
- Find Familiar / Find Steed: "When the [familiar|steed] drops to 0 hit points, it disappears, leaving behind no physical form" (transition zero-hp-absence, presence->absent). Both spells are instantaneous, so start_effect refuses them as spell sources (activeEffects.ts ~2600); they can only be modelled as ruling-sourced summoning effects.
- Simulacrum: "lasts until it drops to 0 hit points, at which point it reverts to snow and melts instantly" (zero-hp-destruction, integrity->destroyed).
- Animate Objects / Giant Insect: 0 HP -> form->original (reversion; Animate Objects also carries remaining damage over to the object). This family is NOT a disappearance and is OUT OF SCOPE for 0-HP behaviour (follow-up bead). It is in scope for the guards in (C).
- rule:monsters-and-death: the GM may give mighty villains and special NPCs player-character death rules. A summon whose spell overrides 0 HP can never be dying, stable, knocked out, or a corpse.
- S1 design (docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/2026-07-06-o9bd-18-7-9-s1-summoning-contract-design.md lines 129-142) assigns 0-HP removal to F3 runtime as engine-pending. The engine has never executed it: summoningSchema.ts is consumed only by validation.

DEFECTS BEING REPAIRED
1. S44: activeEffects.ts removeProjection (~2401-2412, added in 7414d014 for S42) returns 'released' for a dead/dying/stable summon under a stored 'remove' policy. That silently turns F3 remove into release and erases the end-vs-break distinction.
2. Root SRD gap: an effect-owned summon at 0 HP becomes 'dead' (monster rules), 'dying'/'stable' (player-character rules), or 'unconscious' (knockout) and stays in play. The source says it disappears.
3. update_combatant deathRules:'player-character' (and the knockout statuses) can be applied to such a summon, contradicting its spell.
4. A dead summon cannot leave play when its spell ends, because I8 (dead is terminal) refuses 'inactive'. On main this worked; I8 is new in this PR.
5. Sibling: a campaign_actor-target actor link with remove calls updateCampaignActor(status:'inactive'). With no active projection, that overwrites a dying actor's status (life state lost); with an active projection it throws, which is reported as 'missing'.
6. Sibling: caller-declared cleanup policies can contradict the spell (e.g. Conjure Animals with cleanupOnEnd 'release' keeps the beasts after the spell ends).

DESIGN (supervisor decisions; do not re-decide; stop and report in bd notes if one is impossible)

A. New status 'absent' = out of play under a rule (vanished, melted, removed by its owning effect). Add it to CombatantStatus, ActorStatus, CombatantLifeStatus, and to the status CHECK of encounter_combatant and campaign_actor through migration 0039 (table rebuild, same pattern as 0033_combatant_death_rules.sql; keep every other column/constraint/index byte-identical). Update any migration list or schema registry and its tests.
   - Engine-owned: update_combatant / update_campaign_actor refuse an explicit 'absent' (as 'dying' is refused today).
   - A combatant that is absent is not a participant: no turn, no action economy, no death saves, no stabilize, no stable recovery, no suffocation, no healing or damage, no condition writes. Refuse those writes with a clear error, using the same mechanism that refuses writes to dead combatants.
   - Lifecycle invariants: absent requires stableRecovery null, recoveryBlock null, and death-save counters 0. I8 is amended so that dead may become absent and nothing else. Absent never returns to any other status on the same combatant row.
   - Projection to the campaign actor maps absent->absent. The S41 rule (monster 0 HP with no terminal cause projects as unconscious) must not turn absent into unconscious.
   - Admitting an absent campaign actor to an encounter is a new manifestation. title: Dispatch: lifecycle design consolidation, batch E (attempt 2)
description:
Repair batch E for the integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8, from the Sol fourth pass, bead eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.8 (run `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.8`; read S3, S4, S14, S19, S20, S22, S23, S24, S25, S26 in full; history in .8.1, .8.4, .8.6, .8.7). The combatant lifecycle class has survived several repair cycles because rules are spread across many writers and batch D's checker only REJECTS invalid results instead of PRODUCING valid ones (S3, S22: a required exhaustion-6 death is refused by the checker). Per the review policy, this batch is a design consolidation, not another per-path patch. Migration 0038 is authorized only if the ammunition ledger needs a durable identity column (S19).

DESIGN (decided by the supervisor; implement exactly):
D1. One pure transition function for combatants, e.g. `nextCombatantLifecycle(current, event, context)` in a new module state/combatantLifecycle.ts, returning the complete next lifecycle state (status, hp, counters, recovery block, schedule + settled, head facts) or a typed refusal. `current` includes death rules, exhaustion level, head count/mechanic, effective max. Events: damage {amount, critical, damageTypes}, heal {amount}, clampToEffectiveMax (non-damage), setStatus {status}, optIntoPlayerCharacterRules, deathSave {roll}, stabilize, knockout, suffocationDrop, suffocationBreathe, exhaustionChanged {newLevel}, headDied, headsRegrown {count, hpPerHead}, recoveryDue {roll-free; uses stored schedule}, admission {suppliedHp?, suppliedStatus?} (start_encounter / projection / promotion). Priority inside every transition: terminal causes first (exhaustion 6 → dead; zero heads → dead; already dead stays dead except the I8 monster-healing exception), then the event's own rules, then the I6 clamp (non-damage; a clamp never changes 'dead'). The function never produces a state that violates I1-I8; the existing assert stays as a backstop only. Every combatant writer (updateCombatant, death saves, stabilize, suffocation, clamp, adjust_exhaustion's combatant path, head settlement, begin_turn accumulator resets, start_encounter insert/admission, actor projection and promotion, recovery resolution, schedule transfer/invalidation) computes its result through this function and validates every row it writes (S26).
D2. Monster-rules ordinary death stays revivable by healing (pre-PR behaviour, the I8 exception): heal on a dead monster-rules combatant with no exhaustion-6/zero-head cause → alive with the healed HP (S23).
D3. Exhaustion: adjust_exhaustion computes the new level, then applies `exhaustionChanged` (character and combatant) as ONE transition: level 6 → dead (HP clamped to the new effective max without changing dead); level 4+ → non-damage clamp; then character death side effects (attunement end, concentration break 'dead') run once (S3, S22). Mirror the same ordering for characters in hpLifecycle (a combined character transition; never write the condition and validate before the death is applied).
D4. Stable recovery ownership (S4): there is exactly one owner of a pending schedule — the actor's current projection row (active projection, else last-inserted combat instance row, per the existing helper). Promotion into a durable actor COPIES lifecycle (incl. schedule) into combatLifecycle for continuity but does NOT clear or settle the source row's schedule while that row is still the current projection; only projecting the actor into a NEW encounter transfers the schedule to the new row and invalidates old rows. Repeated promotion never overwrites an owned schedule with an invalidated one. resolveCombatantRecoveries resolves the owner row and syncs the actor. 'settled' only ever means a resolved zero-regain recovery (D5).
D5. Settled stable state (S14): settled = 1 is valid only with status stable and an all-null schedule; any partial schedule (some fields null, some not) is invalid regardless of settled, in both the clock integrity check and the invariant. Unrelated writes to a settled creature preserve settled (temporary HP grants, zero-regain heals, exhaustion changes that keep the max at 0). A heal or exhaustion change that raises the effective max above 0 while settled re-arms a fresh 1d4-hour schedule and clears settled (this is the existing batch-D rearm, keep it) — for characters (hpLifecycle writeHpFields path) and combatants alike. temp HP at 0 HP does not wake or heal.
D6. Actor invariants regardless of combatLifecycle presence (S25): campaign_actor writes always enforce I1 (exhaustion 6 → dead) and I6 (HP <= effective max), whether or not the subtree exists. Exhaustion on a campaign actor through start_effect condition projections (activeEffects.ts) is refused with the same error that points to adjust_exhaustion (single owner), like add_condition / update_combatant addCondition.
D7. Resolver threading (S20): thread resolveRulesPack into combatantHeadCount, anyConditionImpliesIncapacitated/conditionImpliesIncapacitated and every profile/mechanic lookup reachable from set_surprised and adjust_exhaustion's combatant path. Regression with installLateAmbiguityAddon for an ordinary goblin COMBATANT observer, a hydra observer, and combatant exhaustion (both succeed with the resolver; genuine unavailability still fails with no writes).
D8. Ammunition identity (S19): the expenditure ledger stores the ammunition identity (name, pack_ref, variant_id, properties_json) at expenditure time (migration 0038 adding these columns to ammunition_expenditure, backfilled from the current expended row where present). Entitlement per identity = floor(sum of original quantities / 2); returned = min(entitlement, present pieces of that identity across ALL its expended rows); remaining present pieces destroyed; report entitlement/returned/destroyed/unavailable. Test first/last/all/partial destruction, odd/even, mixed identities.
D9. Proof (S24): replace the seeded random sequence with a STATE-AWARE scenario generator: from each current state it picks among the events valid-or-meaningfully-invalid for that state (so record_death_save runs on dying creatures, stabilize on dying, set_suffocation drop and breathe both occur, healing and damage both occur, exhaustion both up and down, close/reopen, promotion via a summoning effect with campaignActorId), asserts the tool's expected outcome (success vs refusal) for each call, keeps the previous state to check I8 transitions, checks complete I7 (no partial schedules), and checks actor/projection parity including schedule owner and pending head facts after every reopen and promotion. Assert minimum success counts per event class so a generator regression that stops reaching a class fails. Keep the step count modest (a few hundred).
Also: table-driven unit tests for nextCombatantLifecycle covering every event × {monster, PC} × {alive, dying, stable, dead} × terminal causes, asserting the full next state.

Map every finding (S3, S4, S14, S19, S20, S22, S23, S24, S25, S26) to its tests in your notes, and list every writer you routed through D1 with file:line.

description:
Repair batch D for the integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8, from the Sol fresh full review bead eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.6 (run `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.6`; read S3, S4, S12, S14, S19, S20, S21 in full — every failure family listed must be closed). This batch must close it STRUCTURALLY, not by another per-path guard. Migration 0037 is authorized for S14 only.

SUPERVISOR DECISIONS (implement exactly):
STRUCTURAL INVARIANT (closes S3's class): add one function in encounterCombatants.ts, e.g. assertCombatantLifecycle(row, record context), that is called on the FINAL state of every combatant write (updateCombatant, death saves, stabilization, suffocation, clamps, head settlement, start_encounter admission/projection, promotion, recovery resolution) and on every campaign-actor lifecycle write, before commit; a violation throws (the transaction rolls back) with a message naming the violated rule. Invariants:
  I1 exhaustion level 6 → status 'dead'.
  I2 a multi-head creature with head_count 0 → status 'dead'.
  I3 status 'dying' or 'stable' → death_rules 'player-character' and hp_current 0.
  I4 death_rules 'player-character' and hp_current 0 → status is 'dying', 'stable', or 'dead' (never alive/unconscious/escaped/inactive at 0 HP).
  I5 recovery_block set → status 'dying' (a dead/alive/stable creature carries no block).
  I6 hp_current <= effectiveHpMax(hp_max, conditions).
  I7 a stable-recovery schedule exists only on status 'stable' (see S14 for the settled form).
  I8 a dead combatant (or actor lifecycle) never leaves 'dead' through any write (no revival operation exists in this PR); monster-rules ordinary revival-by-healing is the ONE allowed exception, and only when neither I1 nor I2 applied (preserve today's monster behaviour).
  Then make every write path produce valid states:
S3 decisions: (1) explicit 'escaped'/'inactive'/'unconscious' statuses are accepted only for a combatant that is alive with hp above 0 under player-character rules (monster rules unchanged apart from I1/I2/I8); (2) opting into player-character rules is refused for a combatant at 0 HP whose status is not 'dead' (incompatible state); (3) non-damage clamps never override 'dead' (a dead creature's HP is clamped but its status stays dead); (4) start_encounter admission of an EXISTING campaign actor: supplied hpCurrent/status may not move the actor out of dead, dying, or stable, may not raise HP while a recovery block is set, and may not admit an I1/I2 creature as anything but dead — such inputs are refused with an error telling the DM to use the lifecycle tools; alive actors still accept supplied HP (clamped by I6).
S4: ensureCampaignActorFromCombatant (and every promotion of a module/anonymous combatant into a durable campaign actor — find all callers, e.g. activeEffects.ts effect creation and combat closure) writes the source combatant's complete combatLifecycle (death rules, counters, block, schedule, head count, pending own-turn facts) through the same reserved engine seam used by actor sync, in the enclosing transaction, transferring schedule ownership so exactly one projection owns it. Preserve unrelated actor state.
S12: rule:suffocating's known limit becomes a trap statement: applying the drop to 0 hit points as damage through adjust_hp or update_combatant does not block healing or stabilization (and for a character starts ordinary dying), so the suffocation drop and later breathing are recorded with set_suffocation. The timing (breath runs out → survival interval from calc suffocation_survival_rounds → drop at the start of the creature's next turn after that interval) and the target contract (characters; combatants under player-character rules are dying, under monster rules dead) move into set_suffocation's own description. Keep participants valid and the source-timing assertions (adapt them to the tool description).
S14: add migration 0037 with a stable_recovery_settled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK IN (0,1) column on character and on encounter_combatant (follow ADR 0015; regenerate the schema snapshot; update migration list expectations). A due recovery at zero effective maximum regains nothing, clears the schedule fields, sets stable_recovery_settled = 1, and the creature stays stable. The clock/recovery integrity check accepts stable + all-null schedule ONLY when settled = 1 and still rejects every partially null or unsettled-null schedule as incomplete. Any later write that leaves 'stable' clears settled. Include settled in the actor combatLifecycle snapshot. Test: settle at max 0, then multiple further advance_time calls succeed for characters and combatants; reducing exhaustion afterwards does not deadlock; a genuinely incomplete schedule is still rejected.
S19: recover_ammunition's entitlement per ammunition identity = floor(total ORIGINAL expended quantity / 2) from the expenditure rows; returned = min(entitlement, pieces still present); destroy the remaining present pieces; report entitlement, returned, destroyed, unavailable. Update the tool description and the rule:weapon-properties statement wording to match ("half the expended ammunition, rounded down, limited to what is still there").
S20: thread ctx.resolveRulesPack through set_surprised (setSurprisedInTransaction and every profile/head/legendary lookup it performs) and adjust_exhaustion's combatant path (and the new clamp), exactly as update_combatant does. Test with the installed add-on fixture (installLateAmbiguityAddon) for a surprised observer and combatant exhaustion; a genuinely unavailable pack still fails with no writes.
S21: in hpLifecycle.ts applyDamage, damage to a character ALREADY at 0 HP (dying or stable) compares the full damage amount (before temporary HP absorption) with effectiveHpMax for instant death, before failure accounting; temporary HP is still consumed. The initial drop from above 0 keeps the overflow rule (rule:instant-death). Matrix test: dying/stable × critical/non-critical × below/equal/above effective max × temp HP absent/partial/full.

TESTS: an invariant test that drives a generated sequence of tool calls (deterministic seed, at least a few hundred random steps over update_combatant / record_death_save / stabilize_character / set_suffocation / adjust_exhaustion / begin_turn / close + start_encounter for a PC-rules goblin, a monster goblin, and a hydra) and asserts I1-I8 after every step, plus actor/projection parity after every reopen — this is the permanent evidence for the class. Plus the specific failure families from the review for S3, S4, S12, S14, S19, S20, S21. Map each finding to its tests in your notes.
