description:
READ-ONLY REVIEW. Do not edit, create, or delete any file; do not commit; do not push. Your only writes are bd notes on this bead and closing it.

SCOPE: the full diff of branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 against origin/main (`git diff origin/main...HEAD`) — one PR carrying eight beads: eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.4 (character suffocation recovery gate, migration 0032, set_suffocation, calc breath formulas), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.5 (player-character death rules for encounter combatants, migration 0033), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.6 (adjust_hp knockOut), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.3 (adjust_exhaustion, derived level-4 HP maximum, level-6 death), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.11.4 (expend_ammunition / recover_ammunition, migration 0034), eshyra-o9bd.19.5.10.3 (roll_retained_check / resolve_retained_check / end_retained_check, set_surprised derived from comparisons, migration 0035), eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.6 (hydra Multiple Heads curated mechanic, tracked head count, derived reaction allowance, migration 0036), eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.5 (action:use-an-object ordinaryInteractionRuleRef -> rule:other-activity-on-your-turn, importer). Run `bd show` on each bead and on eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 for the specs and acceptance criteria.

AUTHORITY: AGENTS.md; docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md (profile rules-clause-complete); ADR 0020 §§2-3 (dice, arithmetic, atomic state mutation, resource accounting, state integrity are deterministic; adjudicated outcomes still pass through those boundaries); docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md amendments A3-A5 and invariants 12-13; ADR 0015 (migration-first schema); docs/importer-fix-protocol.md for the importer parts; the committed SRD source text for every rule (packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json, records use the `key` field).

METHOD (review the mechanism, not the narrative):
1. For each capability, print the governing SRD source text beside the implementation and check source fidelity of every engine rule (thresholds, tie semantics, rounding, ordering, what counts as damage/healing, lifecycle start/end).
2. Check every model-facing surface (tool descriptions, schemas, Hybrid Contract in protocol.ts, known-limit statements in ruleKnownLimits.ts, error/rejection messages) against the real code: truthful, no model-side arithmetic/comparison or model-held canonical state offered as a fallback, target domain correct (character vs combatant), no stale wording from the pre-capability disclosures.
3. State integrity: atomicity (single transaction), invariants across the full state space (alive/dying/stable/dead, monster vs player-character rules, recovery block, exhaustion levels, closed vs active combat instances, missing/malformed rows), concentration and attunement side effects, campaign-actor sync, provenance conventions, deterministic ids/replay, write paths that bypass established helpers (mutateState, claimItem, removeItem), migration correctness (constraints, indexes, data preservation, contiguity, schema snapshot).
4. Write paths that let a model persist an unsupported/derived value (the A5 forbidden-substitution class), and any place a refusal could be bypassed through another tool (e.g. add_condition, update_combatant status, rest, level-up).
5. Test evidence: does each acceptance criterion have a test that distinguishes the bad state from the good state? Name missing evidence only where a real requirement is unprotected.
6. Sibling search: for each defect, look for the same class elsewhere in the diff.

REPORT with `bd update <this bead> --append-notes`, then `bd close <this bead>`. One entry per finding: ID (S1, S2, ...), severity (blocker / should-fix / nit), file:line, the violated requirement and its authority, a concrete failure scenario (inputs -> wrong state), and the minimal fix. Then a short list of what you checked and found correct. Apply the review policy's "From observation to finding" test: an observation without an operative requirement is "no requirement" in one line, not a finding. Do not stop at the first defect; batch everything you can find.

THIRD PASS — FRESH FULL REVIEW. Prior Sol reviews: eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.1 (S1-S15) and eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.4 (confirmation; S3, S4, S5, S8, S11, S14 open, S16-S18 new). Repairs landed through .8.2, .8.3, .8.5 and supervisor commits. Under docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md, the combatant lifecycle classes have now been through two repair cycles, so this is a FRESH FULL REVIEW of the affected subsystem (encounter combatant lifecycle, campaign-actor lifecycle persistence/projection, HP lifecycle incl. exhaustion clamps, ammunition accounting) plus the whole PR — not a replay of earlier scenarios. First state CLOSED/OPEN for each of S1-S18 with fresh adversarial evidence; then report every new finding (IDs from S19). Apply "From observation to finding" strictly: speculative robustness is "no requirement". Close with an explicit overall disposition: APPROVE-READY (no blockers or should-fix findings) or CHANGES REQUESTED.
acceptance_criteria: S1-S18 closure plus any new findings recorded in bd notes with an overall disposition; no file changes; bead closed by the reviewer.
notes:
Fresh full rules-clause-complete review at HEAD e892bfc2ef921359d465e6250429b9fe3c34f2af, identical to integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8; origin/main 18c1b30575d082afcc6c2df76e981bcb7be7a9d1. Reviewed the full 77-file diff and the affected combatant, actor, HP and ammunition subsystems, rather than replaying only prior examples. Read all eight scope beads, the integration bead, prior review notes, batch-C decisions, AGENTS, review policy, ADRs 0015/0020, design A3-A5/invariants 12-13, and importer protocol. refs/beads/state is dated 2026-09-09 and lacks these rows; live bd records supplied current authority. Governing committed SRD texts were printed beside the implementations.

S1-S18 disposition FIRST (fresh adversarial probes plus permanent-evidence inspection):
S1 CLOSED: 48 fresh registry cases vary dying/stable, critical/noncritical, maxima 9/27, exhaustion 0/4, and damage below/equal/above effective maximum. Threshold outcomes and failures are correct for combatants with their proper life-state marker; participation bypass is S3.
S2 CLOSED: fresh dying entry at 1 success/2 failures, followed by drop/breathe/drop, preserves earned counters. Stable entry clears obsolete schedules; gated recovery and breathing tests pass.
S3 OPEN: participation-only writes still erase the lifecycle marker; zero-result clamps override terminal death; actor admission bypasses terminal/recovery rules. Detailed finding follows.
S4 OPEN: ordinary recurring-actor pending head facts and blocked regrowth now persist correctly, but the real module-combatant-to-durable-actor promotion producer loses lifecycle state. Detailed finding follows.
S5 CLOSED: a fresh stable actor transfers its deadline from z to a at identical timestamps, invalidates z's deadline, recovers through a, and synchronizes the actor. Inserted-row ordering, active-projection priority, custom-id tests and stale manual-write refusal hold.
S6 CLOSED: fresh N=1/5/8 reserved expenditures reject claim_item and give_item and disappear from nearby context; custody/reacquisition sibling guards and atomic settlement evidence inspected.
S7 CLOSED: 12 fresh long-rest cases (base maxima 17/30, exhaustion 3/4/5, food/drink true/false) restore HP to the resulting effective maximum, after the authorized exhaustion reduction.
S8 CLOSED for the HP-bound defect: nine fresh admission cases (maxima 1/7/28, exhaustion 3/4/5) keep actor/combatant HP equal and bounded; four fresh fighter progression cases (maxima 17/30, exhaustion 3/5) preserve sheet max and clamp live HP. Death precedence/admission is separately S3.
S9 CLOSED: fresh odd-max exhaustion-five roster/snapshot parity (14/14 from base 29) holds; permanent evidence covers a nonacting member.
S10 CLOSED under the accepted most-recent-20 contract: 23 fresh rolls produce a bounded fresh snapshot, resolve an exposed original identity without rerolling it, preserve passive tie behavior, and omit the ended check. Fresh opposing-search probe leaves the retained rolls/total unchanged.
S11 CLOSED: a NULL-head recurring hydra receives a harmless update, closes/reopens, and is truthfully refused at begin_turn with cannot-reconstruct wording; no restart promise remains. Damage/healing/extra-reaction and migration/admission guards inspected.
S12 OPEN in its remaining statement-boundary class: timing arithmetic is repaired, food/water/speed limits are retired, and hiding/surprise name actual wrong-tool traps. The suffocation row is still only a positive recipe/source-timing explanation without a named remaining Eshyra trap. Detailed finding follows.
S13 CLOSED: fresh PC-rules dying/suffocating hydra skipped-turn settlement commits six heads, zero regained HP, and successful turn completion; the actor and reopened projection retain that result. Fire/dead and ordinary healing coverage passes. Promotion continuity is S4.
S14 OPEN in the zero-maximum lifecycle class: natural-20/ordinary healing and first deadline processing no longer revive at zero maximum; the authorized cleared deadline makes a character fail its next clock advance as malformed. Detailed finding follows.
S15 CLOSED: fresh alternate injected gap passes through the real report producer with operation, owner and unresolved-work projection; permanent fixture regression distinguishes nonempty behavior from the real empty registry.
S16 CLOSED: fresh N=5/8 whole-row recovery, re-expenditure and second recovery succeed, retaining resolved first-battle history. Permanent whole/partial/single-piece cases inspected.
S17 CLOSED for reserved subtree injection/replacement: a fresh no-active-encounter model call injecting headCount 999 is refused specifically as engine-owned; unrelated state replacement on a suffocating, regrown actor preserves its head count, PC mode and block across reopening. Admission through other HP/status inputs is S3.
S18 CLOSED for the non-damage accounting defect: fresh temporary HP 0/2/50 remains unchanged while base-23 character HP clamps to 11; hydra exhaustion-five clamp retains five heads and zero damage/pending-loss counters. The terminal-state precedence defect is S3.

Overall disposition: CHANGES REQUESTED. Reopened findings S3/S4/S12/S14 and new findings S19-S21 follow; closure of this review bead means the review is complete, not approval of the implementation.
S3 | OPEN | blocker | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:2091, :2115, :1261, :1318
Requirement/authority: SRD rule:death-saving-throws, rule:healing, rule:suffocating, condition:exhaustion and creature:hydra; .19.5.7.5 PC parity, .19.5.7.4 recovery prohibition, .19.5.7.3 level-six death; ADR 0020 §§2-3. Batch-C .8.5 S3 expressly requires participation never to suppress lifecycle derivation and exhaustion-six terminality on every write.
Fresh registry failures:
(1) PC-rules 20/20 -> hpDelta:-20 -> status:inactive (or escaped) in its own permitted call -> hpDelta:-20. The final call succeeds at 0 HP/status:inactive or escaped with zero failures instead of instant death. The life marker was overwritten, so the damage-at-zero branch no longer runs. Stable->participation likewise loses its stable marker/schedule; opting a monster's unconscious-at-zero knockout into PC rules leaves an unreachable unconscious PC state that neither death-save nor stabilization tools accept.
(2) PC-rules 1/1 -> adjust_exhaustion(delta:6) returns died:true but persists status:dying/exhaustion:6. The zero-result clamp overwrites the previously derived death. Sibling: an explicitly dead 1/1 PC combatant -> exhaustion +4 -> exhaustion -4 -> hpDelta:+1 becomes alive/1. Ordinary terminal-heal/status guards at maxima 5/24 work; this bypass is through the new clamp.
(3) Kill a recurring PC-rules actor, close combat, then start_encounter actors:[{actorId:'A',hpCurrent:10,status:'alive'}]. The actor and projection become alive/10 without revival. The same admitted inputs give a suffocating actor 10 HP while preserving recoveryBlock:suffocating, admit exhaustion-six actors as alive, and admit a zero-headed hydra as alive. This is a real registered alternate write path, not raw database corruption. The zero-head terminal input was established by a head-loss transition.
Minimal fix: keep canonical life state independent of participation, or refuse transitions that discard it; process mandatory death/damage outcomes despite participation status. Terminal death must take precedence over non-damage clamps and other statuses. Actor admission must preserve/validate existing lifecycle, refuse healing through admission while dead/blocked, and enforce exhaustion/no-head death; do not accept free HP/status as a substitute for qualified lifecycle operations. Normalize or explicitly refuse incompatible zero-HP opt-in.
Permanent evidence: generalized transition/admission invariant across death mode, life/participation states, base/effective maxima 0/1/larger, exhaustion/head terminal causes, separate-call sequences, and close/reopen with supplied HP/status. Proportionate because these are canonical death/revival and recovery-gate violations. Owner: combatant/actor/HP integration; material repair; required next state is invariant-preserving transitions plus fresh subsystem review.
S4 | OPEN | blocker | packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:356; real callers packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts:2903, :4787
Requirement/authority: ADR 0020 durable state/identity integrity; the existing F3 actor-persistence producer; .19.5.7.5 one-way PC opt-in, .19.5.7.4 persisted recovery block, .19.3.4.6 tracked head lifecycle; .8.5 S4 requires lifecycle continuity for durable actors.
Fresh failure through a real producer: instantiate a module goblin, link it to an until-removed summoning effect with campaignActorId:'durable', opt it into PC rules, drop it to 0, record a natural-1 death save (two failures), then suffocate it. Close combat and start_encounter with actorId:'durable'. The new projection is dead under monster rules, counters 0, block null: promotion copied HP/status/conditions but no combatLifecycle. A stable variant loses its recovery deadline and is projected dead. A module hydra variant loses a head with 25 damage, is promoted at closure, and reappears with source five heads and no pending regrowth instead of four tracked heads and one pending loss. Both effect creation and closure use ensureCampaignActorFromCombatant, which passes only existing state to upsertCampaignActor. The ordinary already-campaign_actor path now correctly synchronizes blocked regrowth and transfers pending facts; it does not cover this producer.
Minimal fix: transfer the actual source combatant's complete canonical lifecycle into the durable actor through the reserved engine seam when establishing/refreshing that identity, in the enclosing effect/closure transaction. Preserve unrelated state and correctly transfer/invalidate schedule ownership so the promoted actor's subsequent projection or recovery has one authoritative owner.
Permanent evidence: generalized real-producer promotion/close/reopen invariant over module/anonymous combatants with PC dying counters, suffocation, stable deadlines, and hydra lost/pending/fire-suppressed heads. Assert actor state and projected state together, rather than only already-persistent actor fixtures. Proportionate to irreversible canonical state loss across identity promotion. Owner: actor lifecycle integration; material repair; required next state is complete producer coverage and fresh subsystem review.
S12 | OPEN | should-fix | packages/core/src/rules/ruleKnownLimits.ts:152-161; packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolSetSuffocation.ts:27
Requirement/authority: design rule-record-runtime-statements.md R0, amendments A3/A4 and invariant 12: each known limit must name a specific Eshyra trap; tool-contract knowledge belongs in the participating tool descriptions, and source/countdown explanation alone is not a known limit. A5's intended bounded-limit classification does not waive those criteria.
Fresh full-surface check: lookup_rules/discovery will label rule:suffocating partial and expose a statement that only explains the source survival interval and maps drop/breathe and deathRules to tools. It identifies no remaining behavior of a named tool/state that contradicts or silently omits the clause. The recovery/death-rule capability gaps formerly supplying that trap have landed; ordinary relevant calls conform. toolSetSuffocation's own description is just 'Record the suffocation drop or breathing event for a character or combatant', while the invocation/timing recipe lives in the per-rule annotation. Food/water/speed retirement, hiding/surprise wrong-tool traps and CON formulas at -4/-2/0/2/6/9 are correct; this is the remaining positive-mapping class from S12, not renewed timing arithmetic.
Minimal fix: re-derive this row under R0. Retire it if no actual trap survives, or explicitly identify the source-backed participating-tool trap if one does; move the useful bounded drop/breathe timing and target contract to the tool's own description. Preserve the corrected survival-interval timing.
Permanent evidence: preserve the existing source-timing and runtime-statement separation assertions, adapting membership only to the justified R0 disposition and asserting the retained tool contract if the recipe moves. No broad new audit is warranted for this localized prose boundary. Owner: A5/runtime-statement integration; non-material repair; required next state is a conforming bounded statement or justified retirement.
S14 | OPEN | blocker | packages/core/src/state/hpLifecycle.ts:838-847, :876-879; packages/core/test/exhaustion.test.ts:502
Requirement/authority: .8.5 S14 expressly authorizes a due stable recovery at zero maximum to regain nothing, clear the deadline and leave the creature stable; ADR 0020 state integrity requires that authorized state remain valid for the canonical advance_time operation. The existing incomplete-schedule rejection must distinguish corruption from this newly valid lifecycle state.
Fresh registered sequence: initialize a character at 1/1; adjust_exhaustion(delta:4) -> dying at effective max 0; stabilize_character -> stable with a deadline; advance_time(minutes:240) succeeds, restores zero HP and clears all schedule fields as directed. The next advance_time(minutes:1) fails 'stable recovery schedule is incomplete for character(s): pc-1' and rolls back the campaign clock. Removing one exhaustion level does not clear the deadlock. A combatant sibling processes the first deadline identically and allows subsequent clock advances, demonstrating the target-domain inconsistency. The new test stops after checking the cleared deadline and never runs the next clock operation.
Minimal fix: represent/recognize the deliberately settled zero-regain stable state separately from a malformed missing schedule, while preserving rejection of genuinely incomplete/corrupt schedules and the accepted no-revival/deadline-clear rule. Do not restore a minimum-one maximum or invent automatic retry as a requirement.
Permanent evidence: generalized lifecycle-sequence regression across character/combatant, effective max 0/1/larger, first and subsequent advances, and deliberately settled versus actually incomplete schedules. Assert clock progress and persisted HP/life state together. Proportionate because one valid character state blocks all campaign time/rest progress. Owner: shared HP/clock lifecycle integration; material repair; required next state is valid repeated clock consumption of the authorized settled state.
S19 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/ammunition.ts:237-255, :278; packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolRecoverAmmunition.ts:17; packages/core/src/rules/ruleKnownLimits.ts:250
Requirement/authority: SRD rule:weapon-properties says to recover half the expended ammunition; .19.5.11.4 selects floor(half) of the engine-recorded expenditure, with atomic custody/destruction; ADR 0020 resource accounting. Availability limits what can actually be returned, but does not change the number originally expended. The tool/known-limit wording is implementation prose, not authority to replace the denominator with surviving pieces.
Fresh reachable scenario: hold four identical arrows; expend_ammunition(quantity:2) twice in one battle. Destroy the first two-piece drop with remove_item(disposition:'destroyed'), an explicitly supported reserved-row operation advertised by claim_item's rejection. Close combat and recover at the same battlefield. The operation reports recovered:1/destroyed:1/movedAway:2, consuming one of the two surviving arrows; half of the four expended arrows is two, and two are still available. The algorithm first excludes the destroyed expenditure and sums present pieces, then halves that smaller quantity, discounting known unavailability a second time. Partial destruction of a drop is the same class. No permanent test exercises this supported composition.
Minimal fix: derive each selected ammunition identity's recovery entitlement from its immutable original expenditure quantities, then cap/apply that entitlement against actual available pieces without returning absent/destroyed pieces or double-counting rows. Retain enough expenditure identity to account for a row after deletion, and make the tool/known-limit descriptions match the source-grounded operation.
Permanent evidence: generalized accounting invariant varying original quantities, missing/partially destroyed physical pieces, and ammunition identities: returned count is bounded by both source entitlement and availability, while returned/destroyed/unavailable accounting balances. Proportionate to deterministic item-count loss on a permitted inventory operation. Owner: .19.5.11.4/integration; material resource-accounting repair; required next state is source-grounded expenditure accounting.
S20 | should-fix | packages/core/src/state/exhaustionMutation.ts:75-84; packages/core/src/state/actionEconomy.ts:1447-1458; packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolSetSurprised.ts:213
Requirement/authority: the existing exact campaign-rules binding/resolver contract (state/campaignRecordLookup.ts and ToolContext.resolveRulesPack), ADR 0020 positively selected provider-neutral operations, and .19.5.7.3/.19.5.10.3 capabilities. These model tools must operate on the same available bound stack as start_encounter/update_combatant; an installed add-on does not authorize silently dropping the resolver.
Fresh registry failures with the real installLateAmbiguityAddon fixture: the resolver is installed on ToolContext; roll_retained_check and a passive comparison against an ordinary goblin succeed. set_surprised with that comparison then fails tool_error saying the bound add-on is unavailable. It passes no resolveRulesPack into the state seam, and setSurprisedInTransaction explicitly uses undefined/default resolution for the head/reaction/legendary profile. Sibling: adjust_exhaustion(delta:1,combatantId) fails the same way because its updateCombatant call omits the resolver and updateCombatant now resolves creature mechanics unconditionally. An exact nonbundled base carrying otherwise unchanged SRD records reproduces both failures, while update_combatant with the same ToolContext succeeds. These are actual installed-stack consumer paths, not a proposed new mechanic.
Minimal fix: thread ctx.resolveRulesPack through both mutation inputs and every participating profile/head/mechanic lookup, using the already established campaign resolver boundary. Preserve exact-binding failures when a pack truly is unavailable and transactional rollback.
Permanent evidence: generalized tool-consumer parity regression using the existing installed add-on fixture, covering a surprised ordinary/hydra observer and combatant exhaustion with/without a resolver; assert correct mutation when the bound pack is available and no writes on genuine resolution failure. Proportionate to failure of the selected operations for otherwise supported bound campaigns. Owner: exhaustion/surprise integration; material consumer-wiring repair; required next state is consistent exact-stack resolution.
S21 | blocker | packages/core/src/state/hpLifecycle.ts:591-597
Requirement/authority: committed SRD rule:death-saving-throws, Damage at 0 Hit Points, makes DAMAGE equal to or greater than the HP maximum instant death; rule:temporary-hit-points distinguishes the damage event from buffered HP loss. ADR 0020 owns that threshold; .19.5.7.5 mirrors these rules, and this review expressly includes the full shared HP lifecycle subsystem. The initial-drop overflow rule remains a separate source clause (rule:instant-death).
Fresh registered source-boundary probe: character at 0 HP/max 20, dying (or stable), receives 10 temporary HP, then adjust_hp(amount:-20). It persists dying with one failure and instantDeath:false; critical:true gives two failures. It should die immediately because the damage at zero equals the maximum. Eight fresh cases (dying/stable x critical/noncritical x maxima 10/20) reproduce it. The branch compares overflow, after subtracting the temporary buffer, instead of the original damage. Its failure-count logic already correctly treats absorbed damage as a damage event; its instant-death logic does not. Combatants without a temporary buffer now correctly check full damage (S1), so shared-rule parity diverges. This is pre-existing in the character algorithm but lies within the expressly assigned fresh full subsystem review, and the PR changes the effective-maximum comparison here.
Minimal fix: at an already-zero-HP character's boundary compare actual applied damage with effectiveHpMax before failure accounting, while still consuming temporary HP correctly. Preserve remaining-damage/overflow semantics for the distinct initial drop from positive HP.
Permanent evidence: generalized source-backed threshold regression across dying/stable, critical/noncritical, below/equal/above effective maximum, and temporary buffers absent/partial/full. Assert instant death, buffer consumption and counter behavior; this preserves the exact source claim without multiplying near-identical reproducers. Proportionate to incorrect death outcomes. Owner: shared HP lifecycle integration; material repair; required next state is source-correct damage-event versus HP-loss accounting.
Checked and found correct, subject to S3/S4/S12/S14/S19-S21:
- Character suffocation preserves dying counters, blocks healing/stabilization/natural-20 HP regain and third-success stabilization, clears on breathing/death, and uses the normal concentration/attunement boundaries. Selected knockout consumes temporary HP, overrides lethal overflow, enters stable and arms recovery atomically.
- Ordinary exhaustion increments, reductions, caps, level-six death at nonzero effective maxima, long-rest final-maximum ordering, progression clamping and party/detail HP projections work. Non-damage clamps preserve temporary HP and hydra damage/head accounting; terminal precedence is S3.
- Current recurring-actor projection ownership follows active projection then combat-instance insertion order, not timestamps or ids. Old schedules transfer/invalidate correctly and archived manual mutations are refused. Reserved combatLifecycle state cannot be injected through start_encounter, and unrelated state edits preserve it.
- Ammunition reservations prevent ordinary claim/give bypasses and are excluded from nearby-item discovery. Even/odd and selected mixed-identity recovery, second-battle reuse, co-location/closed-battle checks, canonical custody/destruction and rollback evidence pass. S19 is the distinct original-expenditure versus remaining-availability boundary.
- Retained comparisons preserve the original check, strict observer-win ties, passive score adjustments, campaign/participant identity validation, ended-check refusal and fresh context visibility. Direct model surprise lists and supplied reaction totals are refused. The bounded resumption contract and real player-roll ledger, trace and audit-presentation consumers are wired.
- For the committed source hydra, the curated mechanic pins five heads, the 25-damage single-turn threshold, two regrown heads per lost head, fire suppression, ten HP per regrown head and zero-head death; reactions derive from tracked heads with opportunity-attack-only extra spends. Own-turn/skipped-turn settlement and blocked healing work on already-persistent projections.
- The use-an-object relationship resolves to rule:other-activity-on-your-turn, the actual combat free-interaction passage. Reviewed generated changes are limited to that pointer and source-pinned Multiple Heads curation. The exact-source importer guard, mechanics validator and evidence were inspected.
- Migrations 0032-0036 are contiguous. Constraints, indexes, row-preservation, adopted/migrated/fresh parity and generated snapshot tests pass. Unknown upgraded hydra head state is explicitly refused rather than reset or treated as one head.
- Retained gap-registry/audit infrastructure has its explicit retained disposition and a real nonempty injected report-projection regression.

Additional fresh S3 corroboration entirely through registered/source transitions: a 172-HP hydra takes five separate 25-fire-damage turns, reaches dead/47 HP/zero heads, then closes/reopens with actors:[{actorId:'A',hpCurrent:10,status:'alive'}] and becomes alive/10 HP/zero heads. No raw head edit is needed for that admission bypass.

No requirement: unlimited retained-check enumeration beyond the accepted most-recent-20 context bound.
No requirement: manual combatant lifecycle writes after encounter closure; the supervisor explicitly reserves that state to clock-driven recovery.
No requirement: automatically rearming the deliberately cleared zero-regain recovery deadline; .8.5 explicitly specifies clearing it. S14 concerns rejection of the authorized state by the next clock operation.
No requirement: generic configurable regrowth suppression outside the positively selected committed hydra mechanic.
No requirement: an additional permanent test merely because a throwaway review probe exists; published findings specify the operative invariant and proportionate replacement evidence.

npm run test PASSED: 5688 passed / 3 documented skips; 320 passed / 2 skipped files.

title: Dispatch: Sol confirmation repairs batch C (attempt 1)
description:
Repair batch C for the integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8: the Sol confirmation review (bead eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.4 — run `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.4` and read S3, S4, S5, S8, S11, S14, S16, S17, S18 in full; each has fresh reproduced failures) found these still open or new. Earlier repair context: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8.1`, `.8.2`, `.8.3`. This is the second repair cycle for S3/S4/S5: fix the CLASS, not the example — every failure family listed under each finding must be closed and tested. You own all files needed. No new migration unless strictly unavoidable (if unavoidable, 0037, and record why).

SUPERVISOR DECISIONS (implement exactly):
S3 (terminal death, both death-rule modes): (a) a combatant whose status is 'dead' stays dead: any explicit status other than 'dead' is refused, and any positive hpDelta is refused — in BOTH monster and player-character modes when the death came from exhaustion level 6 or zero heads; in player-character mode for any death; monster-mode ordinary revival-by-healing (pre-existing behaviour) stays only when neither exhaustion 6 nor zero heads applies. 'inactive' is no longer accepted for a dead combatant (a dead combatant needs no removal). (b) Under player-character rules, an explicit 'escaped' or 'inactive' status in the SAME call as an hpDelta is refused ("apply damage and participation status in separate calls"), so participation status never suppresses lifecycle derivation. (c) Exhaustion level 6 is terminal in both modes on every write.
S4 (actor lifecycle continuity): every write that changes head_count, heads_died_since_own_turn, fire_damage_since_own_turn, death_rules, counters, recovery block, or recovery schedule syncs the campaign actor's combatLifecycle in the same transaction — including head settlement with suppressed or zero healing (sync must not depend on a healing call). combatLifecycle also persists and transfers the pending own-turn facts (headsDiedSinceOwnTurn, fireDamageSinceOwnTurn) so a close/reopen before the creature's next own-turn end keeps the pending regrowth/suppression. Per-turn damage accumulation (damage_this_turn, damage_turn_key, head_died_this_turn) is turn-scoped and does not transfer.
S5 (projection ownership): the actor's current projection is: the row in the ACTIVE combat instance if one exists for that identity; otherwise the row whose combat_instance was inserted last (SQLite rowid of combat_instance — insertion order), never timestamps or lexical ids. One shared helper decides it, used by actor sync, recovery-schedule transfer, and resolveCombatantRecoveries. Test equal timestamps with ascending, descending, and custom ids.
S8 (HP admission): start_encounter / any projection of an actor or creature into a combatant row clamps hp_current to effectiveHpMax(hp_max, conditions) through the non-damage clamp of S18 (never damage), for supplied, defaulted, and inherited HP; the actor row is written consistently. S11 (unknown head state): keep the explicit refusal for a multi-head combatant with NULL head_count, but make the message truthful: the head count is unknown because this creature's state predates head tracking, Eshyra cannot reconstruct it, and head-dependent operations (damage, healing, turn settlement, extra reactions) are refused for it. Do not promise that restarting the encounter fixes it, and do not reset heads to the source value. Test the recurring-actor retry path asserts the truthful continued refusal.
S14 (zero effective maximum): regaining hit points is capped at the effective maximum for characters and combatants on every path (heal, natural-20 death save, clock stable recovery, regrowth healing). When the cap leaves 0 HP regained: a natural 20 counts as one death-save success (like the suffocation block) and never reports 'revived'; healing at a zero maximum changes nothing (no alive, no counter reset; report 0 regained); a due stable recovery at a zero maximum regains nothing and clears its deadline while the creature stays stable. Revival and counter resets happen only when HP actually rises above 0. Do not restore any minimum-one rule.
S16 (ammunition reuse): the guard in ammunition.ts refuses a new expenditure only when the physical row is referenced by an UNRESOLVED ('expended') expenditure; resolved history never blocks re-firing recovered ammunition. Keep the no-double-unresolved-accounting proof; add a two-battle recover-then-re-expend test over whole, partial, and single-piece rows.
S17 (reserved lifecycle state): the combatLifecycle key in campaign_actor.state_json is engine-owned. start_encounter actors[].state (and every other model-facing input that writes actor state) refuses a combatLifecycle key with a clear error, and updating an actor's other state preserves the existing combatLifecycle subtree untouched (merge, never replace). New lifecycle facts are initialized only from source/engine transitions.
S18 (non-damage clamp): add explicit non-damage clamp operations — characters in hpLifecycle.ts, combatants in encounterCombatants.ts — that lower hp_current to the effective maximum without touching temporary HP, damage-per-turn accounting, head loss, death-save failures, or concentration DCs; if the clamp brings HP from above 0 to 0, apply the 0-HP lifecycle (character → dying with concentration break as incapacitation; monster combatant → dead; player-character combatant → dying) atomically, with actor sync. adjust_exhaustion uses these instead of adjustHp/updateCombatant hpDelta, and returns the persisted HP.

title: Dispatch: retained check totals and deterministic surprise (attempt 1)
description:
Implements capability bead eshyra-o9bd.19.5.10.3 (read `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.5.10.3`, including its acceptance criteria — they include closing the set_surprised write path). Integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 (single PR); your branch already contains migrations through 0034 — the next contiguous number is 0035. Read AGENTS.md; docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md amendment A5; ADR 0020 §§2-3; orchestrator/resolution.ts (resolveD20, resolveContest), toolResolveCheck.ts, toolResolveContest.ts, toolResolutionShared.ts, calc.ts passive_score, toolSetSurprised.ts, state/actionEconomy.ts setSurprised, orchestrator/protocol.ts (Hybrid Contract surprise text), orchestrator/turnTraceProjection.ts (how resolve_check/resolve_contest results reach the turn trace / roll ledger — new rolling tools must be captured the same way), and the turn auditor's roll-visibility rules.

SOURCE. rule:hiding: "When you try to hide, make a Dexterity (Stealth) check. Until you are discovered or you stop hiding, that check's total is contested by the Wisdom (Perception) check of any creature that actively searches for signs of your presence." Contest rule: higher total wins; on a tie the situation stays as it was (the hider stays hidden). Passive: "the GM compares your Dexterity (Stealth) check with that creature's passive Wisdom (Perception) score". rule:surprise: "If neither side tries to be stealthy, they automatically notice each other. Otherwise, the GM compares the Dexterity (Stealth) checks of anyone hiding with the passive Wisdom (Perception) score of each creature on the opposing side. Any character or monster that doesn't notice a threat is surprised at the start of the encounter."

SUPERVISOR DECISIONS (implement exactly):
- Tie semantics for a passive comparison: the passive score is the observer's check total, so a tie keeps the situation as it was — the hider is NOT noticed. A creature notices only when its score (or rolled total) is strictly higher than the retained total. Cite this in a code comment.
- Migration packages/core/data/migrations/0035_retained_checks.sql: table retained_check (campaign_id, retained_check_id TEXT PK, label, participant_kind/participant_ref nullable (character|combatant), combat_instance_id nullable, dice, rolls_json, natural, modifier_total, total, visibility, status CHECK IN ('active','ended'), end_reason nullable, provenance, session_id, created_at, ended_at); table retained_check_comparison (campaign_id, comparison_id TEXT PK, retained_check_id FK, mode CHECK IN ('search','passive'), observer_label, observer_kind/ref nullable, observer_total, noticed INTEGER 0/1, resolution_json, provenance, session_id, created_at). ADR 0015 conventions; regenerate the schema snapshot; document in schema.ts.
- New tool `roll_retained_check` (mutates): rolls an ability check through resolveD20 (no vs) with the same declared-modifier/proficiency/advantage vocabulary as resolve_check (reuse toolResolutionShared parsing), persists it, returns retainedCheckId plus the full resolution. Optional participant ({character} or {combatantId}) identifies the roller. Description: use for a check whose total the rules keep for later comparisons (for example a Stealth check made to hide).
- New tool `resolve_retained_check` (mutates; writes comparison rows) with { retainedCheckId, reason, visibility?, search?: side (rolled now: label, participant?, modifiers, proficiency, advantage/disadvantage) , passive?: [{ label, participant?, modifier, advantage?, disadvantage? }] } — exactly one of search/passive. search: rolls the searcher's check now and compares (searcher notices iff its total > retained total). passive: computes each score through the calc passive_score formula (evaluateCalc, not reimplemented) and compares each. Refused when the retained check is 'ended'. Returns per-observer noticed flags and the comparison ids; rolled dice must surface in the turn trace / roll ledger exactly as resolve_contest's do (update turnTraceProjection and any tool-name lists that drive the roll ledger or auditor).
- New tool `end_retained_check` (mutates) { retainedCheckId, reason: 'discovered' | 'stopped' }: marks it ended. Whether the hider was discovered or stopped hiding is the DM's interpretation; the engine never auto-ends it.
- set_surprised is rebuilt on these comparisons and its free-list inputs are REMOVED (closing the write path: a model call can no longer persist a model-chosen surprise list). New args { comparisonIds: string[] } (all 'passive' comparisons, all from active retained checks, all observers identified as participants of the active combat instance). For each observer that appears in the given comparisons, it is surprised iff it noticed none of the hiders compared against it. Refuse when the hiders do not all cover the same observer set (every hider must be compared with every observer, per the source), when an observer has no participant identity, or when no comparison is given. If neither side tries to be stealthy there is no surprise and the DM simply does not call the tool (say so in the description). Keep setSurprised's existing state semantics (first turn, begin_turn clearing) by deriving the participant list and passing it to the existing state function inside the same transaction; the state function itself may stay as an internal seam but must not be reachable with a free list from any tool.
- resolve_contest description: keep "Both sides always roll ..." and add that a contest against a retained total goes through resolve_retained_check. resolve_check unchanged.
- Hybrid Contract (protocol.ts): replace the surprise sentence ("Surprise depends on comparing ... cannot currently be determined; never make that comparison yourself ...") with the deterministic path (roll_retained_check for each hider's Stealth, resolve_retained_check passive against the opposing side, then set_surprised with those comparison ids). Keep "never compare totals yourself".
- Known limits (ruleKnownLimits.ts), R0 re-derivation for rule:hiding and rule:surprise: rewrite each to the bounded statement naming the new tools (participants exactly the tools named; each appears in the statement), or retire if nothing misleading remains — supervisor preference: keep short bounded statements, because resolve_contest and resolve_check remain traps for a retained total. Remove 'retained-check-total-resolution' from ENGINE_CAPABILITY_GAPS and every capabilityGaps (delete empty fields). Update the identity-pinned gapsByKey map, the hiding assertions in packages/core/test/rules/ruleAwareness.test.ts, and the set_surprised / prompt assertions in tools.test.ts and protocol.test.ts (replace the "cannot currently be determined" assertions with assertions on the new contract; keep a regression that neither resolution tool's description offers a model-side comparison). Keep the 8-word source-restatement test green. description:

SOURCE (SRD rule:weapon-properties, Ammunition): "You can use a weapon that has the ammunition property to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from the weapon. Each time you attack with the weapon, you expend one piece of ammunition. Drawing the ammunition from a quiver, case, or other container is part of the attack ... At the end of the battle, you can recover half your expended ammunition by taking a minute to search the battlefield." SRD division rule: round down.

DESIGN (decided by the supervisor; implement exactly):
1. Migration packages/core/data/migrations/0034_ammunition_expenditure.sql: table ammunition_expenditure (campaign_id, expenditure_id TEXT PK, combat_instance_id TEXT NOT NULL, character_id TEXT NOT NULL, source_inventory_id TEXT NOT NULL (the held stack spent from), expended_inventory_id TEXT NOT NULL (the unheld dropped row holding the spent pieces), quantity INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK > 0, world_location_id TEXT NOT NULL, status TEXT NOT NULL CHECK IN ('expended','resolved'), provenance, session_id, created_at, resolved_at). Indexes for (campaign_id, combat_instance_id, character_id). Follow ADR 0015 conventions; regenerate the schema snapshot (`npm run -w @eshyra/core schema:snapshot`); document the table in schema.ts comments.
2. New tool `expend_ammunition` (mutates) { itemId, quantity? (default 1, integer >= 1), character? }: requires an ACTIVE combat instance (the battle); requires the item to be a held row of the character with quantity >= quantity. It moves `quantity` pieces out of custody exactly as remove_item with disposition 'dropped' does for a partial stack (reuse that code path, do not duplicate it), at the character's current world location, and records an expenditure row linked to the active instance, in one transaction. Whether the item is the right ammunition for the weapon stays DM interpretation; the tool does not resolve attacks.
3. New tool `recover_ammunition` (mutates) { combatInstanceId, character? }: allowed only when that combat instance is CLOSED (the end of the battle) and the campaign's current location equals the expenditures' world location; refused if the character has no 'expended' rows for that instance. For each ammunition identity (group by the identity the inventory code already uses to merge stacks), N = total expended pieces still present in their expended rows (pieces another tool already moved, e.g. via claim_item or destroy, are not counted — report them); recoverable = floor(N / 2). In one transaction: return `recoverable` pieces to the character's custody (merge into a matching held stack when the inventory code supports merging, else claim/split rows), destroy the remaining unrecovered pieces of those expended rows, and mark the expenditure rows 'resolved'. Second call for the same instance/character is refused. The tool does not advance the clock (the minute of searching is the DM's narrative time).
4. Descriptions: contracts only. expend_ammunition: call after each attack with an ammunition weapon (one piece per attack), only during combat. recover_ammunition: after the battle's combat instance is closed, recovers half (rounded down) of the pieces still lying where they were expended and destroys the rest. Known limit rule:weapon-properties (ruleKnownLimits.ts), R0 re-derivation: rewrite to the bounded statement (resolve_check does not spend ammunition; for a character, spend with expend_ammunition after each attack with an ammunition weapon and recover with recover_ammunition after the battle; loading restriction stays). SOURCE (SRD rule:knocking-a-creature-out): "Sometimes an attacker wants to incapacitate a foe, rather than deal a killing blow. When an attacker reduces a creature to 0 hit points with a melee attack, the attacker can knock the creature out. The attacker can make this choice the instant the damage is dealt. The creature falls unconscious and is stable."

SCOPE: CHARACTERS (adjust_hp / hpLifecycle.ts). Encounter combatants already take status 'unconscious' through update_combatant; do not touch encounterCombatants.ts (another child owns it concurrently).

DESIGN (decided by the supervisor; implement exactly):
1. adjustHp / applyDamage gain an optional `knockOut: true` on a damage application (negative amount). Semantics, in one transaction:
   - Temporary HP absorb damage first, exactly as today.
   - If the character was above 0 HP and the remaining damage reduces hp_current to 0 (including any overflow, however large), the result is hp_current 0, life_state 'stable', both death-save counters 0, and the stable-recovery deadline armed exactly as stabilizeCharacter arms it (seeded rng). No instant death, no 'dying' step. Leaving 'alive' breaks concentration through the existing writeHpFields hook (incapacitated, not dead). The result reports `knockedOut: true` and the overflow that was NOT applied as death.
   - If the damage does not reduce the character to 0, knockOut has no effect: normal damage, result `knockedOut: false`.
   - If the character is already at 0 HP (dying or stable) or dead, knockOut is refused with a MutateStateError ("a knockout applies only when the damage reduces the character to 0 hit points"), so damage-at-0 rules are never bypassed.
   - knockOut with a positive amount (healing) is refused.
   - While a suffocation recovery block is set (recovery_block, from eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.4), knockOut is refused: the character cannot be stabilized.
   Whether the attack was a melee attack and whether the attacker chose to knock out stay DM interpretation.

description:
Implements capability bead eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.5 (read `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.5`). Integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 (single PR for eight beads). Read AGENTS.md; docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md amendment A5; ADR 0020 §§2-3.

SOURCE: SRD rule:monsters-and-death: "Most GMs have a monster die the instant it drops to 0 hit points, rather than having it fall unconscious and make death saving throws. Mighty villains and special nonplayer characters are common exceptions; the GM might have them fall unconscious and follow the same rules as player characters." SRD rule:suffocating makes any creature "drop to 0 hit points and [be] dying, and it can't regain hit points or be stabilized until it can breathe again." The character death rules live in packages/core/src/state/hpLifecycle.ts (header comment lists them).

DESIGN (decided by the supervisor; implement exactly):
1. Migration packages/core/data/migrations/0033_combatant_death_rules.sql (next contiguous number). SQLite cannot alter a CHECK, so rebuild encounter_combatant per the ADR 0015 conventions already used in this repo (find a prior table-rebuild migration and copy its pattern, preserving every column, index, and trigger): status CHECK gains 'dying' and 'stable'; new columns death_rules TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'monster' CHECK IN ('monster','player-character'); death_save_successes / death_save_failures INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK BETWEEN 0 AND 3; recovery_block TEXT CHECK (NULL or 'suffocating'); stable recovery columns mirroring character 0020 (stable_recovery_roll 1..4, anchor/deadline elapsed minutes). If campaign_actor's status CHECK (0001) is synced from combatant status in updateCombatant, extend it the same way in this migration (dying/stable) or map them explicitly in the sync — choose extending the CHECK so actor state is not lossy. Regenerate the schema snapshot with `npm run -w @eshyra/core schema:snapshot`. Update schema.ts column-semantics comments.
2. Default behaviour is unchanged: a 'monster' combatant reaching 0 HP is dead unless another status is passed.
3. update_combatant gains `deathRules?: 'player-character'` (one-way opt-in per combatant; once set it persists for that combatant) and `critical?: boolean` (meaning as adjust_hp's: damage at 0 HP from a critical hit). For a 'player-character' combatant the engine applies the character death rules: hpDelta bringing it to 0 → 'dying' with counters reset, or 'dead' when the overflow beyond 0 (|hpDelta| - previous hp) is >= hpMax (instant death); damage while dying/stable at 0 → one death-save failure (two if critical), stable → dying, three failures → dead; healing from 0 → 'alive', counters reset (refused while recovery_block is set). Combatants have no temporary HP column today: do not invent one. Factor the shared transition logic out of hpLifecycle.ts into a pure function both paths call, rather than duplicating rules.
4. Death saves and stabilization for combatants: record_death_save and stabilize_character accept an optional `combatantId` (mutually exclusive with `character`; error if both). Same outcome rules as characters, including the suffocation block semantics from 0032 (nat 20 = one success no HP while blocked; third success does not stabilize while blocked). Only a 'player-character' combatant that is dying may make death saves / be stabilized. Stabilizing arms the 1d4-hour recovery deadline exactly as for characters (seeded rng), and the existing world-clock resolution path (resolveStableRecoveries, called from rest.ts and the clock advance path — find every caller) also resolves due combatant recoveries (regain 1 HP → alive). title: Dispatch: suffocation recovery gate for characters (attempt 1)
description:
Implements capability bead eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.4 (read it: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.4`). Integration branch eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.8 (single PR for eight beads). Read first: AGENTS.md; docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md amendment A5 and invariants 12-13; ADR 0020 §§2-3; packages/core/src/rules/ruleKnownLimits.ts (rule:suffocating entry and ENGINE_CAPABILITY_GAPS).

SOURCE (SRD rule:suffocating): "A creature can hold its breath for a number of minutes equal to 1 + its Constitution modifier (minimum of 30 seconds). When a creature runs out of breath or is choking, it can survive for a number of rounds equal to its Constitution modifier (minimum of 1 round). At the start of its next turn, it drops to 0 hit points and is dying, and it can't regain hit points or be stabilized until it can breathe again."

SCOPE: CHARACTERS ONLY. The encounter-combatant dying state is a separate bead (eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.5); do not touch encounterCombatants.ts / update_combatant.

DESIGN (decided by the supervisor; implement exactly):
1. Migration packages/core/data/migrations/0032_character_recovery_block.sql (the next contiguous number; follow ADR 0015 conventions used by 0020/0022, plain ALTER TABLE): add `character.recovery_block TEXT CHECK (recovery_block IS NULL OR recovery_block = 'suffocating')`. Update the schema.ts column-semantics comment.
2. state/hpLifecycle.ts gains two operations, each one transaction through the existing writeHpFields/mutateState path (so concentration breaks and provenance work as today):
   - `beginSuffocation(db, ctx)`: refuses a dead character; sets hp_current = 0, life_state = 'dying' (from alive, dying, or stable), resets both death-save counters when the character was not already dying, clears any stable-recovery deadline (writeHpFields already nulls it when not stable), and sets recovery_block = 'suffocating'. hp_temp is NOT changed: temporary hit points are not hit points (record this as a code comment citing the source wording). It is NOT damage: no overflow/instant death, no damage-at-0 failure, no concentration DC (leaving 'alive' breaks concentration as incapacitation via the existing hook). Calling it while already suffocating is an idempotent no-op that reports `alreadySuffocating: true`.
   - `endSuffocation(db, ctx, rng)`: refuses when no block is set; clears recovery_block. If the character is dying with death_save_successes = 3 (accrued while blocked, see 3), it becomes stable in the same transaction (counters reset, scheduleStableRecovery as stabilizeCharacter does).
3. While recovery_block is set:
   - applyHealing / any positive HP adjustment through adjustHp is refused with a MutateStateError naming the block ("cannot regain hit points while suffocating").
   - stabilizeCharacter is refused.
   - recordDeathSave: a natural 20 counts as one success (no HP regained); successes accumulate to at most 3 and a third success does NOT stabilize; failures and natural 1 behave as today (three failures kill). The result reports `recoveryBlocked: 'suffocating'`.
   - Every other path that raises hp_current or changes life_state toward alive/stable must respect the block: grep for hp_current writes (rest.ts short-rest hit-dice healing around the hit-dice spend, long-rest HP restoration, resolveStableRecoveries, grant paths). Refuse or skip with a clear error; never silently heal. Temporary HP grants are not hit points and stay allowed.
   - Death clears nothing special: a character that dies keeps no meaningful block; clear recovery_block when life_state becomes 'dead' (in writeHpFields or the transitions) so a dead row never carries it.
4. New tool `set_suffocation` (packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolSetSuffocation.ts, registered in tools.ts DEFAULT_TOOLS, mutates: true, follows toolStabilizeCharacter.ts patterns incl. CHARACTER_TARGET_SCHEMA): args { event: 'drop' | 'breathe', character? }. Description states only the contract: 'drop' applies the moment the rule drops the character to 0 hit points (dying, recovery blocked); 'breathe' records that it can breathe again; while blocked, healing and stabilize_character are refused and record_death_save does not stabilize or restore hit points; characters only. No arithmetic or timing recipe.
5. calc formulas in orchestrator/calc.ts (registry pattern of days_without_food_limit): `breath_hold_duration` → { minutes } = max(0.5, 1 + constitutionModifier) (0.5 = 30 seconds; return minutes as a number, plus `seconds`), and `suffocation_survival_rounds` → max(1, constitutionModifier). Each cites SRD rule:suffocating in its comment like the others. Add calc.test.ts cases incl. the source example (Con 14 → +2 → 3 minutes; 2 rounds) and minimums.
6. Update tool descriptions truthfully: record_death_save (blocked behaviour), stabilize_character (refused while suffocating), adjust_hp (healing refused while suffocating). Keep existing sentences otherwise; do not add per-rule prose.
7. Known limit (ruleKnownLimits.ts) rule:suffocating: re-derive under R0. The CHARACTER clause is now executable: rewrite that part to the bounded trap/path statement (e.g. a character whose breath runs out is dropped with set_suffocation event drop at the start of its turn, and event breathe when it can breathe again; durations come from calc breath_hold_duration and suffocation_survival_rounds). Remove 'suffocation-recovery-gate' from this limit's capabilityGaps and from ENGINE_CAPABILITY_GAPS. KEEP the encounter-combatant sentence and the 'combatant-dying-state' gap unchanged. participants must list every tool named and each must appear in the statement (validator). Update the identity-pinned gapsByKey map in packages/core/test/rules/ruleAwareness.test.ts and the suffocation statement tests there and in tools.test.ts (the old 'record_death_save is not gated' / 'do not call stabilize_character' wording assertions must be replaced by assertions on the new contract, not deleted without replacement). The 8-word source-restatement test in ruleDispositions.test.ts must stay green.
8. Design doc: in docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md A5 classification table, move the suffocation-recovery-gate cell to landed (one short note: "landed in eshyra-o9bd.19.5.7.4"). Do not rewrite other text.

TESTS (permanent evidence, generalized not per-wording): hpLifecycle.test.ts: beginSuffocation from alive/stable/dying; refused on dead; temp HP untouched; concentration broken from alive; healing refused while blocked; stabilize refused; nat 20 = one success no HP; third success does not stabilize; three failures kill and clear the block; endSuffocation with 3 successes stabilizes and arms recovery; endSuffocation with <3 leaves dying; every other HP-regain path you gated has a refusal test. A tool-registry test invoking set_suffocation end to end. Migration test pattern as used for 0020 if one exists.

title: Resolve a retained d20 check total against later checks and passive scores (rule:hiding, rule:surprise)
description:
Problem. SRD rule:hiding: the hider's Dexterity (Stealth) check total is retained ('that check's total is contested by the Wisdom (Perception) check of any creature that actively searches'), a contest tie leaves the situation as it was (the hider stays hidden), and the GM compares the same retained total with each creature's passive Wisdom (Perception) score. No registered tool resolves either comparison: resolve_contest always rolls both sides (it would reroll the hider); resolve_check resolves total >= vs with vs limited to 1..99 (wrong tie direction for a later searcher's roll against the hider's total); calc passive_score computes the score but compares nothing. Comparing totals is the d20 outcome itself, which the Hybrid Contract keeps engine-owned, so the DM may not compare them. Current disclosure: RULE_KNOWN_LIMITS['rule:hiding'] with capability gap 'retained-check-total-resolution' (packages/core/src/rules/ruleKnownLimits.ts).

Required capability (positive, bounded). Operation: resolve outcomes against a RETAINED check total: (a) a fresh opposing d20 check rolled now vs the retained total, with source contest semantics (higher wins; tie = situation unchanged); (b) one or more passive scores vs the retained total. Inputs: an engine-recorded prior check result (identity from the roll ledger / resolution result, never a model-typed number), the opposing side's declared modifiers/proficiency/advantage, or passive scores derived through calc passive_score inputs. Exclusions: whether a creature is actively searching, can see the hider clearly, whether the hider gave away its position, or whether circumstances permit hiding at all (DM interpretation). Residual DM interpretation: applicability and which observers are relevant.

Sibling consumer (do not change without a user decision): set_surprised's description has the DM 'adjudicate the Stealth-vs-passive-Perception determination' (accepted eshyra-2n1t.4 design; state/actionEconomy.ts header). A multi-observer surprise comparison is the same retained-total operation. Downgrading that contract was NOT done in #596 because it would regress surprise support; route it through this capability or an explicit authority decision.

Selection basis: the governing SRD clause requires an engine-owned step (ADR 0020 §3: arithmetic / resolution of a d20 outcome / atomic state mutation / resource accounting / lifecycle), and no registered tool performs it. Under F-09 design amendment A5 (docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md, PR #596) the rule's known limit only DISCLOSES this gap; it does not satisfy or retire the obligation. This bead blocks eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4 (owning rules work for opus:F-09 / sol:CAP-001) until the capability lands or accepted authority explicitly changes the requirement. Do not close it because PR #596 recorded the gap. Enters this engine family by explicit positive selection (the family's out-of-backlog entry clause).
acceptance_criteria:
- A deterministic operation resolves (a) a fresh opposing check against a retained total and (b) passive scores against a retained total, from an engine-recorded check result, exposed through a provider-neutral tool with tie semantics per source.
- Tests prove: retained total is never rerolled; tie keeps the hider hidden; passive comparison per observer (including several observers against one Stealth total, as surprise needs); rejects a model-typed total with no recorded identity.

Minimal fix: qualify resolve_damage with “when that attack actually calls for damage”; retain resolve_check for its attack roll.

F8 [omitted tool-backed step]: rule:combat-step-by-step. Source explicitly says “Roll initiative. Everyone involved in the combat encounter rolls initiative” between surprise/positions and turns. Context lists start_encounter, set_surprised, begin_turn, close_combat_instance, but omits resolve_check and moves straight from surprise to turns. Evidence: ruleAdjudicationContext.ts row; toolResolveCheck.ts:resolveCheckTool; toolBeginTurn.ts:beginTurnTool (caller supplies initiative order). Minimal fix: add resolve_check to tools/context for the initiative checks before begin_turn; leave any untracked positioning to source adjudication.

F9 [omitted tool-backed step]: rule:complex-traps. Source: “When a complex trap activates, it rolls initiative” and “On its turn, the trap activates again.” Context includes the trap with start_encounter and records combatant changes with update_combatant, but gives no initiative resolution or turn boundary; begin_turn is what maintains per-participant turns/timers. Evidence: ruleAdjudicationContext.ts row; toolStartEncounter.ts:startEncounterTool; toolResolveCheck.ts:resolveCheckTool; toolBeginTurn.ts:beginTurnTool; state/actionEconomy.ts:beginTurn. Minimal fix: add resolve_check and begin_turn for the trap’s initiative and recurring turns (and spend_turn_resource only if the trap actually spends an action budget), or narrow the current text to only the combatant registration/change subset so it does not read as the trap’s combat procedure.

F10 [omitted tool-backed state transition]: rule:grappling. Source: “A grappled creature can use its action to escape” via contested check, and on release the grappled condition ends. Context handles the initial contest/addCondition only; it names no spend_turn_resource for the grapple or escape action and no remove_condition/update_combatant removeCondition for a successful escape/release. A model following the entire row can leave the target grappled after escape. Evidence: ruleAdjudicationContext.ts row; toolSpendTurnResource.ts:spendTurnResourceTool; toolRemoveCondition.ts:removeConditionTool; toolUpdateCombatant.ts:updateCombatantTool; toolResolveContest.ts:resolveContestTool. Minimal fix: add action expenditure and the character/combatant condition-removal path to tools/context, or expressly scope this entry to initial grapple application and leave escape as no statement.

F11 [omitted tool-backed outcome]: rule:jumping. Source permits “DC 10 Strength (Athletics) check” for a low obstacle and requires “DC 10 Dexterity (Acrobatics) check” to land on feet in difficult terrain, else prone. Context maps only jump_distance calculation although resolve_check and character/combatant condition tools handle these later steps. Evidence: ruleAdjudicationContext.ts row; toolCalc.ts:calcTool; toolResolveCheck.ts:resolveCheckTool; toolAddCondition.ts:addConditionTool; toolUpdateCombatant.ts:updateCombatantTool. Minimal fix: add the optional/conditional checks and target-correct prone write to the tool list/text, or explicitly scope the positive mapping to distance calculation alone.

F12 [omitted damage rule]: rule:two-weapon-fighting. Source: “You don’t add your ability modifier to the damage of the bonus attack, unless that modifier is negative.” Context covers bonus-action spend and attack roll but does not map resolve_damage, whose damage packet modifiers are the existing tool path for this specific source clause. A generic damage path can add a positive ability modifier in violation of the rule. Evidence: ruleAdjudicationContext.ts row; toolResolveDamage.ts:resolveDamageTool inputSchema; state/resolution.ts:resolveDamage. Minimal fix: add resolve_damage and instruct omission of a positive ability modifier (retain a negative one) on the bonus-attack damage packet, subject to any source exception.

F13 [omitted post-save state]: rule:recuperating. Source: on a successful save, the character chooses either “End one effect ... that prevents you from regaining hit points” or “For the next 24 hours, gain advantage” on saves against a disease or poison. Context ends at advance_time and resolve_check, so it presents no state path for either successful outcome although end_effect can terminate a tracked effect and start_effect can own a timed effect. Evidence: ruleAdjudicationContext.ts row; toolRest.ts:advanceTimeTool; toolResolveCheck.ts:resolveCheckTool; toolEndEffect.ts:endEffectTool; toolStartEffect.ts:startEffectTool. Minimal fix: include the applicable effect tools and the chosen result’s duration/target scope, or state that this mapping covers only the time and saving-throw stages and do not imply the whole recuperation procedure is represented.

F14 [lossy ammunition disposition]: limit rule:weapon-properties. Source: “Each time you attack ... expend one piece of ammunition” and “At the end of the battle, you can recover half your expended ammunition.” Statement directs remove_item “after each such attack” but does not supply its required disposition; choosing destroyed deletes the item/row and prevents the source recovery, while choosing dropped creates recoverable physical state. Evidence: ruleKnownLimits.ts row; toolRemoveItem.ts:removeItemTool inputSchema/description; state/domainMutations.ts:removeItem; toolClaimItem.ts:claimItemTool. Minimal fix: specify a recoverable disposition and the half-recovery path where appropriate (or disclose that exact recovery is not representable if it cannot be done); do not leave a required argument whose destructive value silently discards source meaning.

F15 [incomplete graded limit]: limit rule:water. Source: “If the character already has one or more levels of exhaustion, the character takes two levels in either case.” Shared exhaustionLevelLimit says an existing condition cannot be incremented and “a further level from this rule” cannot persist, singular. It does not warn that the water procedure can demand TWO additional levels even when the half-ration save succeeds/fails as specified. Evidence: ruleKnownLimits.ts:exhaustionLevelLimit and RULE_KNOWN_LIMITS['rule:water']; toolAddCondition.ts:addConditionTool; state/domainMutations.ts:addCondition. Minimal fix: make water’s known-limit statement source-specific about the two-level case while keeping the existing findingId and no-DM-held-state boundary.

Audit/proof skim: ruleDispositions.ts:materializeEngineProcedureCoverage independently preserves implementation/context/limits by object identity; ruleDispositions.test.ts checks coexistence and plural limits, and ruleAwareness.test.ts covers prior hiding, target-domain, and exhaustion repairs. I found no new audit-projection blocker. Existing statement tests assert selected examples and tool-name registration; they do not catch the source-identity, conditional-result, or exact-tool-argument defects above. Supervisor review of 742651c5 found:

Restating rules text is NOT Eshyra context: the source record is already beside the envelope in lookup_rules, and design R6 / invariant 4 separate Eshyra-authored annotation from rules text.

## Content standard for each dmContext (what "Eshyra context" means)
A dmContext is Eshyra's statement to the DM about THIS rule at THIS table. Useful content is, in priority order:

## Per-row R0 procedure (every row, no mechanical copying)
1. Read the rule record's source text in packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json.

A sibling dispatch is concurrently implementing condition relationships. ## Completion report (bd update --append-notes)
R0 outcome tally by outcome and channel (computed, from a script); every RETIRED claim and every row that changed channel or status vs legacy, each with its evidence; rows that landed in both channels; externalClauses kept/retired; any row you stopped on. Follow-ups via bd create (parent eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4).

Update the module doc comment's "exactly one typed outcome" list to name all four. The resolver must never reach `declaration.relation as string` for a table-bearing declaration.
2. **C2** fixed-relation record-name (relationField omitted, `relation` used verbatim); `relationByFieldValue` without `relationField` rejected.
3. **C3 importer** (scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/conditionMechanics.ts, Grappled): add `triggerCondition: 'incapacitated'` ONLY to the `grappler-incapacitated` conditionEndsWhen effect; `trigger` unchanged; nothing on `removed-from-grappler-reach`. 5. **C5 loader** (src/rules/packLoader.ts `parseRecordRelationshipDeclaration`): accept exactly the declared field set incl. `relationByFieldValue` (parse + shape-check it), throw RulesPackError naming any unknown key and its path. Run it against the committed SRD manifest and every in-repo fixture manifest; if any committed/fixture manifest is rejected, that is a design failure case (§8) — STOP and record it on this bead rather than loosening the check.
6. **Consumers**: discovery/expansion.ts loss accounting becomes an exhaustive per-outcome switch (a `never` check so a fifth outcome fails typecheck): `excluded` is recorded in relationshipResolutions, creates no traversal, and records NO StageLoss. Traversal passes that select only `resolved` stay unchanged. ruleAwareness / lookup_rules: NO code change (contract amended already as A2 in docs/design/rule-record-runtime-statements.md).
7. **Invariant 2 gate** (packages/core/test/rules/recordRelationships.test.ts, "resolves every declared reference occurrence in the committed pack"): exhaustive switch — resolved accepted; unresolved-target and indeterminate fail; excluded accepted ONLY when its (declaration.kind, declaration.pointerPrefix, relationFieldValue) triple is in an explicit justified-exclusion list whose only entry today is (condition, /mechanics/effects/*/condition, conditionEndsWhen); anything else fails. Identities, not counts.
- Resolver unit tests with synthetic manifests: the four-distinct-outcomes test on one synthetic record (table string, table null incl. non-string leaf -> exactly one `excluded`, value absent from table -> indeterminate/relation-not-recognized, missing and non-string sibling -> indeterminate); fixed-relation record-name; every C1/C2 build rejection.

- Loader test: unknown declaration key rejected naming key and path.

- Importer test (conditionMechanics.test.ts): Grappled's triggerCondition present only on grappler-incapacitated; EXTEND any existing exact projection assertion, never weaken; cite the §2 source clause.

- Discovery probe and intervention suites (test/discovery/discoveryProbes.test.ts, packetIntervention.test.ts) must stay green WITHOUT retuning any budget. If a new candidate displaces must-consider material, STOP and record it on this bead (design §8 failure case).

A sibling dispatch is concurrently editing the rule-channel datasets. ## A1 — design amendment (supervisor decision, already made; you implement it)

The four R3 `duplicate-of` candidates FAILED source comparison as duplicates (supervisor compared against SRD_CC_v5.1.pdf via pdfjs):
- rule:armor-class (p.80) is the one-sentence "Armor Class" item under the Dexterity ability's uses ("Depending on the armor you wear, you might add some or all of your Dexterity modifier to your Armor Class."). rule:armor-guidance (pp.62-63) says armor determines BASE AC; the Dex rules are the Light/Medium Armor paragraphs. Not the same rule.
- rule:senses-darkvision (p.257, monster appendix) states "can see in dim light within the radius as if it were bright light"; rule:darkvision (p.86) does NOT contain that clause. Texts state different rules.
- rule:senses-truesight adds "within the same range" to the Ethereal Plane clause; rule:truesight does not.
- rule:senses-blindsight adds the naturally-blind parenthetical stat-block convention.
Pack text matches the PDF in all eight records (no extraction defect).
Therefore: NO `duplicateOf` field, NO importer change, NO pack regeneration, NO relationship-manifest change, NO field-provenance change, NO kindSchemas change in this slice. Emit nothing for these pairs.
Amend the design doc in this PR: add a short "Amendment A1 (vertical slice)" subsection at the end of §3 R3 recording the four comparisons above (the quoted differing clauses and page numbers), stating that no duplicate-of edge is emitted, and that whether a non-duplicate source relation (e.g. a parallel definition of the same sense in another chapter) is warranted is deferred to a follow-up bead (you create it: `bd create --type=task --priority=3 --title="Decide source relation for parallel sense definitions (rule:senses-* vs rule:*)"` with the evidence, parent eshyra-o9bd.19.3). Update §2's third example bullet, §4 invariant 8, §5 row 1 and §7/§8 wording accordingly. Change the doc Status line to "accepted (revision 4) + amendment A1 from the vertical slice". Keep edits minimal.
§5 row 1's permanent evidence ("bundled SRD record -> present, SRD semantics, resolved relationship through lookup_rules") is instead proven with `action:help`, whose `ruleRef` is already a declared, resolving `record-key` relationship (PR #582). Verify the exact pointer in records.json / record-relationships.json before writing the assertion.

## R0 outcomes for the slice rows (supervisor-derived; record each outcome + evidence in the PR description AND as a code comment beside the row's dataset entry)

1. rule:long-rest — legacy `unimplemented` is STALE -> RETIRED as a limit; REWRITTEN to implemented-not-positively-selected. Evidence: packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolRest.ts restTool(name,'long') + packages/core/src/state/rest.ts completeLongRest (qualification, 24 in-game hour gate "a participant already benefited from a long rest within 24 in-game hours", >=1 HP, HP/Hit Dice/resource resets); bead eshyra-2n1t.9 closed. Do NOT add a binding.

3. rule:suffocating — `partial` CONFIRMED (no breath-duration or suffocation-countdown state anywhere in src/; the 0-HP/dying transition is applied by adjust_hp through state/hpLifecycle.ts). -> ruleKnownLimits entry, limit 'partial', findingId 'readiness-integrity' (what materializeEngineProcedureCoverage already assigns). Model-facing statement, e.g.: "Eshyra does not track how long a creature has held its breath or the suffocation round countdown; the DM tracks both from this rule. When the creature drops to 0 hit points, apply it with adjust_hp, which runs the dying rules." (Tool names must be validated against DEFAULT_TOOLS.)
4. rule:charges — REWRITTEN. The external clause 'pack-side charge data' (eshyra-o9bd.18.7.7.1) is RETIRED: that bead is closed and the pack carries charge economies (e.g. magic-item:wand-of-magic-missiles data.mechanics.economies.charges {max:7, reset dawn 1d6+1, onDepleted}). What survives is disclosure adjudication: remaining charges are revealed by identify or attunement, and the attuned creature learns how many charges were regained. -> NO known limit; ruleAdjudicationContext entry with tools [lookup_rules, spend_usage, reset_usage(, restore_usage if it exists)] and dmContext about disclosure timing. The audit coverage row therefore becomes 'model-adjudicated-supported' sourced from the runtime dataset.
5. rule:cover — adjudication context CONFIRMED: tools [lookup_rules, resolve_check]; dmContext: the DM chooses the degree of cover; the +2 / +5 AC and Dexterity saving throw bonuses must be passed as declared modifiers to resolve_check; total cover means the target can't be targeted directly.

7. rule:channel-divinity — this record is the MULTICLASSING Channel Divinity rule (text: "If you already have the Channel Divinity feature and gain a level in a class that also grants the feature ..."). design-blocked -> ruleKnownLimits limit 'deferred', findingId 'engine-capability-ownership' (current materialized id), statement from ADR 0018 §1/§6: Eshyra supports single-class characters only (ADR 0018), so this multiclass interaction is deliberately unsupported; a character with more than one class is refused, not adjudicated.

## F1 fail-closed gate (sourceInventoryCoverage.ts assertSourceCoverage, or a sibling assert called beside it in index.ts)
With `requireComplete` (the real CLI import, `assertDeclarationsAreLive`) the import FAILS, listing every offender, when:
 (a) any entry's final resolution is `ambiguous-normalized-name`; and
