## F2 structural resolution (sourceInventoryCoverage.ts name auto-match, ~L440-470 where `ambiguous-normalized-name` is produced)
When the normalized name has >1 candidate, apply in order and stop at the first step that leaves exactly one candidate:
 1. structure filter: `table-caption` items keep only `table:*` candidates; `heading` items drop `table:*` candidates.
 2. class-chapter scope: item.section in CLASS_CHAPTER_SECTIONS -> keep candidates starting `feature:<section-lower>:`.
 3. page locality: keep candidates whose provenance.locator cites item.page.
A single survivor becomes status `record:<key>` with a NEW resolution kind `structural-normalized-name` { normalizedName, ownerKey, step: 'structure' | 'class-chapter' | 'page-locality', candidateKeys }. Otherwise it stays ambiguous (and F1 fails the real import). Apply the filters cumulatively (1 then 2 then 3 on the survivors) — deterministic and documented in a header comment. Add the new kind everywhere resolution kinds are switched over (assertSourceCoverage, diagnostics, formatters, the ledger) and to docs of CoverageResolution. Curated rules still outrank everything (eshyra-erf5.1 ordering unchanged).

Predicate on page + the preceding ability heading (derive from the inventory order; no bare line numbers unless nothing else distinguishes them — then document why).

The pack ALSO emits duplicate `rule:<slug>` records with the same text; do NOT delete them here — file a follow-up bead "Duplicate rule:* records for the ten combat actions" (P2, labels importer,srd,thaw) naming all ten keys and the evidence.

 Anything else still ambiguous or non-local after F2+F3 = stop and report the exact items; do not invent owners.

- Unit: F2 resolver steps (structure, class-chapter, page-locality, cumulative, no-survivor stays ambiguous); F1 gate throws listing every ambiguous and every non-local owner, passes when clean, inert when requireComplete is false.

Update the `contentMatch` doc comment (L121-130) to say continuation matches are excluded. Verified simulation over the committed ledger: this rule clears contentMatch on exactly the same-record chains (bard/cleric/druid/... spellcasting subsections, wild-shape, font-of-magic, dragon-ancestor, scrying, teleport, reincarnate, objects, candle-of-invocation, carpet-of-flying, cube-of-force, deck, feather-token, figurine, horn-of-valhalla, manual-of-golems, ring-of-shooting-stars, hit-points, half-dragon-template, ability-checks, speed, weapon-proficiency, improvised-weapons, acolyte, paladin sacred-oath) and leaves equipment segment matches, rule:coinage p62, rule:weapons p64, spell-scroll p242, pantheons p360, planes p363 as contentMatch. title: Dispatch: fail-closed record source-anchor gate so no compiler-authored record acquires SRD provenance by default (attempt 1)
description:
Implementation dispatch for parent eshyra-o9bd.19.1.3 (read `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.1.3`, esp. its NOTES and ACCEPTANCE). All design decisions below are made. If reality contradicts this spec, STOP, record findings with `bd update <this-id> --append-notes`, and close with a reason instead of improvising. Read docs/importer-fix-protocol.md first. Do NOT touch docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/freeze-manifest.json or add thaw notes.

GOAL: a compiler-authored record must not be able to acquire the SRD license/provenance block by default. Today every importer emitter in packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/emit.ts stamps `license: SRD_5_1_LICENSE` + `provenanceFor(page)` from nothing more than a page number, and no gate checks the record against the page it cites. That is exactly how table:starting-wealth-by-class (removed in PR #504) carried "SRD 5.1 p. 38" while no starting-wealth text exists in SRD 5.1.

DESIGN: a fail-closed, output->source RECORD ANCHOR GATE inside the importer pipeline.
Invariant: every emitted SRD record's anchor text occurs in the extracted text of at least one page its `provenance.locator` cites. The anchor is the record `name` by default; a record whose name is compiler-constructed must carry an explicit DECLARED anchor (printed text) with a reason, and that declared anchor is itself verified against the cited pages. There is no path by which a record passes without a verified printed anchor.

1. New module packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/recordSourceAnchors.ts:
   - `normalizeAnchorText(s)`: lower-case; map ’‘ to ', “” to "; map hyphen/dash variants to '-'; remove a hyphen followed by whitespace (line-break hyphenation); then drop every non [a-z0-9] char. (This is the normalization the supervisor's probe used; keep it unless it provably causes a false pass/fail, and say so in notes if you change it.)
   - `citedPages(locator)`: parse "p. N", "pp. N, M, ..." (list) and "pp. N-M" / "pp. N–M" (range, inclusive). Throw on an unparseable locator (fail closed).
   - `DECLARED_RECORD_SOURCE_ANCHORS: ReadonlyMap<recordKey, { anchor: string; reason: string }>`.
   - `assertRecordsAnchoredInSource(records, pages, { requireDeclarationsLive: boolean })`: throws one error listing EVERY failing record key (not just the first) when (a) a record without a declaration has a name not found on its cited pages, (b) a declared anchor is not found on the record's cited pages, (c) a declared anchor exists for a record whose name IS found (redundant declaration — remove it; the default must stay the rule), or (d) with requireDeclarationsLive, a declaration's key matches no emitted record (stale).
2. Call it in `runImporter` (index.ts, around line 2707+) on the FINAL record list that is written to records.json, with the extracted `pages`, and `requireDeclarationsLive: input.assertDeclarationsAreLive === true` (follow how that flag is used for relationship declarations). Synthetic-PDF importer tests run runImporter too; they must still pass. If a synthetic fixture legitimately fails the gate, report which and why in notes rather than weakening the gate.
3. Populate the declarations. The supervisor's probe (default rule only) found exactly 39 records failing on current main ddc231be: equipment:saddle-military/-pack/-riding (p.72); rule:armor-guidance (pp.62,63), rule:coinage (p.62), rule:oath-of-devotion-oath-spells (p.33), rule:the-fiend-expanded-spell-list (p.50), rule:weapons "Weapons Guidance" (p.64); tables: acolyte-bonds/-flaws/-ideals/-personality-traits (p.61), armor-of-resistance (p.209), circle-of-the-land-{arctic,coast,desert,forest,grassland,mountain,swamp} (p.22), confusion-behavior (p.127), creation-material-duration (p.132), cube-of-force-charges-lost (p.215), deck-of-many-things (p.217), draconic-bloodline-draconic-ancestry (p.44), half-dragon-breath-weapon (p.321), half-dragon-damage-resistance (p.320), reincarnate-race (p.174), scrying-connection/-knowledge (p.176), sentient-magic-item-{alignment,communication,senses} (p.251), sentient-magic-item-special-purpose (p.252), sphere-of-annihilation (p.243), staff-of-power (p.244), staff-of-the-magi (p.245), teleport-familiarity (p.186), wand-of-wonder (p.250). Reproduce this list with your gate before declaring anything and report any difference.
   For each, find the PRINTED text on a CITED page that the record is actually extracted from — e.g. the table's printed caption or header row ("d6 Bond"), the printed owner heading, the printed sub-row label ("Saddle" + "Military" style: pick a distinctive printed span such as the row text). Declare it with a reason naming what the text is (e.g. "caption-less table; printed header row", "compiler-named guidance section; printed section heading 'Armor'" etc.). The anchor must be specific to that record, not a generic word that appears everywhere on the page (no single common words like "Armor" alone if a longer printed phrase exists; prefer >= 2 words / distinctive row text).
   If a record's only printed anchor lies on a page its locator does NOT cite, do NOT extend the locator and do NOT declare an off-page anchor: that is a locator-completeness defect owned by eshyra-o9bd.19.2.2. Record each such case in your notes, add a note to eshyra-o9bd.19.2.2 with `bd update eshyra-o9bd.19.2.2 --append-notes`, and STOP (close your bead with a reason) so the supervisor can decide.
4. Tests (packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/recordSourceAnchors.test.ts), synthetic PageText only — no PDF extraction:
   - negative regression: a record named "Starting Wealth by Class" with locator "p. 38" over page text lacking it throws, naming table:starting-wealth-by-class;
   - a declared anchor absent from the cited page throws; a declared anchor present passes; a redundant declaration throws; a stale declaration throws only when requireDeclarationsLive;
   - locator parsing for p./pp. list/pp. range, and an unparseable locator throws;
   - every DECLARED_RECORD_SOURCE_ANCHORS entry has a non-empty reason and an anchor normalizing to >= 8 chars (guard against trivially-matching anchors).
   The real-PDF proof is the importer run itself (CI srd-importer-reproducibility runs verify:dnd5e-srd-pack whenever importer/pack files change); do not add a new whole-pack PDF extraction test.
5. Proof: temporarily re-add a fake record (e.g. push a table named "Starting Wealth by Class" citing p. 38 into the final record list in runImporter), run the importer, confirm the gate throws naming it, then remove it. Record this in notes.

REGENERATE + VERIFY: `npm run import:dnd5e-srd -- --pdf packages/core/sources/dnd5e-srd-5.1/SRD_CC_v5.1.pdf --out packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/` then `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack` must be exact. Expected pack diff: NONE (the gate adds no output). Any pack change must be explained in notes. Run `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing (it rewrites files); if CLI suites fail on import, run `npm run build` first (fresh worktree has no dist). Memory is tight: use VITEST_MAX_FORKS=4 if tests time out.
Commit message prefix `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.3 `, ending `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
Completion report via `bd update <this-id> --append-notes`: commit SHA, the reproduced failing list, the declaration table (key -> anchor -> reason), the fake-record proof, verify results.

title: Disposition reviewLifecyclePolicy.test.ts under the new permanent-evidence policy
description:
Applies AGENTS.md "Permanent Test Evidence" and docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md
"From observation to finding" (both landed in PR #553, merge commit 3f5693a0) to one
piece of existing proof machinery: packages/core/test/reviewLifecyclePolicy.test.ts.

CENTRAL QUESTION: which responsibilities in that file justify permanent executable
evidence, and which assertions merely turn editable policy prose into executable
snapshots of itself?

PROBLEM. The file is 318 lines, 17 tests, ~60 assertions. Most have the shape
  policy prose -> regex asserting the policy still contains equivalent prose
which is recursive proof machinery: an authorized bad policy edit simply updates
both the document and the regex, while a legitimate equivalent rewording breaks the
regex. That is a false-failure generator, not evidence.

ORIGINAL AUTHORITY, checked: eshyra-w65u acceptance criteria authorized "a lightweight
policy test pins the essential distinctions" around the abandoned eshyra-review-v2
machinery; eshyra-o9bd.19.1.18 authorized a "lightweight extension" when the canonical
policy document was introduced. Neither authorized executable semantic ownership of
the review policy, and neither makes every later assertion permanent.

SCOPE: this file only. beadLifecyclePolicy.test.ts has the same defect class and is
explicitly OUT of scope here; file it separately if the analysis holds.

EXCLUSIONS. No replacement policy schema, snapshot, policy hash, manifest, generated
baseline, approval marker, certification file, or new checker. Do not move the same
semantic mirrors into another test file. Do not create a registry of required policy
sentences. Do not replace ten regexes with one giant regex. No new proof machinery to
prove the old proof machinery was safely removed.

Effective review profile: semantic-system. This changes durable proof responsibilities
around repository review authority.

Also in scope: disposition the AGENTS.md sentence "Proof machinery ... is implementation
and needs its own tests, but it does not inherit the proof burden of the product."
Determine whether "needs its own tests" materially creates an unintended universal
test obligation that recurses one level outward. Narrow it only if it does.
notes:
DISPOSITION LEDGER (2026-09-22), format: existing evidence -> claimed invariant -> authority -> actual boundary -> disposition -> replacement.
Blanket replacement responsibility for every RETIRED prose assertion: semantic correctness of repository review policy is owned by the authority hierarchy (AGENTS.md + docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md), the owning Bead or accepted design, and semantic-system review of any change to that authority. A regex copy of editable authority cannot establish that a FUTURE version of that authority is valid: an authorized bad edit updates document and regex together, while a legitimate rewording breaks the regex. Demonstrated empirically - see ADVERSARIAL EVIDENCE below.

RETAINED / CONSOLIDATED (4 tests, 8 assertions):
1. 'points common authority at a review policy document that exists' <- old test 1. Invariant: AGENTS.md's pointer to the canonical policy resolves to a real file. Authority: AGENTS.md 'PR Review Authority and Lifecycle' makes the linked document mandatory; a dangling pointer makes the obligation unfollowable. Boundary: two independently editable artifacts plus the link between them. STRENGTHENED: the path is now parsed FROM the AGENTS.md link instead of hardcoded, so renaming the document with its pointer updated passes (the old file FAILED that good edit) and renaming it with the pointer left dangling fails (the old file could not detect it). The prose mirror of 'Anyone authorizing a design...' is retired.
2. 'keeps CLAUDE.md loading AGENTS.md instead of owning policy itself' <- old test 16. Invariant: CLAUDE.md still carries the @AGENTS.md import. Authority: CLAUDE.md is the Claude Code entry point and AGENTS.md is the single source. Boundary: an executable import mechanism, not prose. Consequence of loss: sessions stop loading repository authority entirely, whatever either document says.
3. 'does not revive the abandoned PR #481 review machinery' <- consolidates old tests 3, 6, 16-negatives and 17. Invariant: eshyra-review-v2 / REVIEW CONTRACT / contract hash absent from AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md; no review:* script in ANY workspace manifest; no docs/review/ protocol directory. Authority: eshyra-w65u acceptance criteria, which this file was created to serve; bd memory pr481-review-contract-framework-superseded. Boundary: executable command surface, repository tree shape, and common-authority text. STRENGTHENED two ways: script scan now covers packages/core and packages/cli manifests (the old test saw only root), and docs/review/ is now checked at all. Note the canonical policy document is deliberately NOT scanned - it legitimately names eshyra-review-v2 to record it as superseded. Concrete harm this prevents recurring: PR #504 was rejected solely for lacking these absent artifacts.
4. 'keeps the disposition gate ahead of findings discipline' <- old test 11 (ordering assertion only). Invariant: '## From observation to finding' precedes '## Findings discipline'. Authority: the policy section's own text states it runs before findings discipline and the gate only functions upstream of what it gates. Boundary: actual document topology, checked against the claim - not a copy of the claim. Retained because a gate placed after the stage it gates is not a gate, and no other mechanism encodes that relation structurally. Both headings are now existence-checked so a deleted section fails rather than silently passing on indexOf -1.

title: T6: Amend the review policy with an observation-to-disposition gate
description:
AUDIT REFERENCE: finding F6 and section 10.2.

PROBLEM
docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md is individually sound but composes into an
accretion loop, because THE DISPOSITION GATE IS ASYMMETRIC. "Findings
discipline" requires every valid finding be repaired in the current PR;
"Review the mechanism" requires each defect be generalized, sibling-searched,
varied across state dimensions, and given permanent regression evidence. The
only escape is permanent rejection, which uniquely requires "recorded
reasoning that explains why the governing invariant and authority require no
change."

Accepting a finding therefore costs nothing extra; rejecting one costs work.
When accepting is cheaper than rejecting, a sufficiently capable reviewer
accepts by default -- and each acceptance mandates generalized repair plus
permanent evidence plus a widened sibling search, enlarging the surface the
next review examines.

MEASURED SIGNATURE
1,103 beads; 100 named "Dispatch:"; a 15-round rev chain on eshyra-jhpt; and
an attempt distribution of 45 tasks at attempt 1 but 4 reaching attempt 6, 2
attempt 7, 2 attempt 8, 2 attempt 9. The policy already says a defect class
surviving two repair cycles warrants a fresh full review; attempt-9 tasks show
that escape hatch is not firing.

REQUIRED WORK
Add an explicit observation -> disposition -> finding pipeline AHEAD of
"Findings discipline", and make the two paths symmetrically cheap. Proposed
text is in audit section 10.2. Load-bearing clauses:

- A technically correct observation is not a finding. Before publishing one,
  record: the governing invariant; the authority for it; the ownership and
  consumer boundary; applicability or reachability where material; the actual
  consequence of violation; the proportionate closure condition; and the
  proportionate permanent evidence.
- An observation that cannot name an operative authority and a real producer
  or consumer is dispositioned as "no requirement", IN ONE LINE, and is not a
  finding. THIS MUST COST NO MORE THAN ACCEPTING IT. "We could make this more
  defensive" is not "the system requires this defense."
- A finding must state whether its permanent evidence is a generalized
  invariant or an exact reproducer, and why that choice is proportionate.
- Reachability is a first-class disposition axis. A defect on a path no
  producer or consumer reaches is dispositioned at its real severity.

Also make the two-cycle rule mechanical: a THIRD dispatch on the same defect
class REQUIRES a fresh full review of the subsystem.

MUST NOT CHANGE
Sibling search, state-dimension variation, proof-mechanism review, and the ban
on nonblocking/follow-up/deferred labels. Those produce genuine defect
discovery. The amendment targets ONLY the disposition gate. Do not weaken
"every valid finding blocks approval" -- the failure is upstream of it.

ACCEPTANCE
- The pipeline is stated before "Findings discipline" and the one-line
  rejection path is explicit and demonstrably no more costly than acceptance.
- The two-cycle escalation is mechanical.
- No review contract, hash, checkpoint, certification, or other artifact is
  introduced; the policy's existing prohibition on such ceremony holds.

EXCLUSIONS
Documentation only.

1. SCOPE. 'EXCLUSIONS: Documentation only.' superseded on the same grounds as eshyra-9l5s.3: docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md is already guarded by reviewLifecyclePolicy.test.ts, and this bead's change to the two-cycle clause breaks an existing assertion there. Disposition of the two added guards under eshyra-9l5s.3's standard:
- 'gates observations on disposition before they become findings' — pins the gate and its cost-symmetry clause, the mechanism that keeps acceptance from being the cheaper default.
- 'keeps the defect-finding search undiminished by the disposition gate' — the highest-value of the three. Without it, a later edit could quietly turn a convergence mechanism into a defect-hiding one. Sibling search, state-dimension variation, and proof-mechanism review must stay required.
Both are document-text assertions costing ~1 ms and gating repo-wide review behavior.

2. WORDING NARROWED. This bead previously mandated that an observation unable to name an operative authority AND A REAL PRODUCER OR CONSUMER be dispositioned 'no requirement'. That is overstrong and is withdrawn.

It made present reachability a prerequisite for a requirement EXISTING, which:

title: T5: Adopt the permanent-evidence policy in AGENTS.md
description:
AUDIT REFERENCE: section 10.1.

PROBLEM
Nothing in repository authority states when a test earns permanent status, so
every reproducer produced during review becomes permanent by default. The
audit measured the result: 151 bead-named describe blocks across 52 files,
8,747 LOC of proof machinery tested by 17,736 LOC, and a 7,642-line SRD test
file organized by originating bead rather than by invariant.

REQUIRED WORK
Add a permanent-evidence policy to AGENTS.md. Proposed text is in audit
section 10.1; refine it against repository evidence rather than pasting it.
Load-bearing clauses:

- A permanent regression test protects a durable invariant, contract,
  independently meaningful boundary, or justified known defect class that
  stronger evidence does not already protect.
- A reproducer created during development or review is NOT automatically
  permanent. After disposition and repair it normally becomes generalized
  regression evidence or is retired, unless the exact case has independent
  semantic significance. EXACT SOURCE-FIDELITY REGRESSIONS AGAINST A VENDORED
  SOURCE ARTIFACT ALWAYS HAVE THAT SIGNIFICANCE and are never retired under
  this rule (docs/importer-fix-protocol.md).
- Tests are evidence of requirements, never authority for requirements.
- Permanent proof burden is proportionate to the governing invariant, and A
  PROOF MECHANISM'S OWN COST IS PART OF THAT PROPORTIONALITY. An assertion
  costing seconds of wall clock or hundreds of megabytes must be justified
  against a correspondingly serious consequence of failure. (F1 exists because
  nobody costed an assertion.)
- Proof machinery needs tests but DOES NOT INHERIT THE PROOF BURDEN OF THE
  PRODUCT. Test it in proportion to the decisions it gates.
- Infrastructure authorized for a bounded experiment or transition MUST CARRY
  AN EXPLICIT DISPOSITION AT THAT BOUNDARY -- retained as product
  implementation carrying a responsibility shipped behavior exercises,
  demoted to development-only tooling, or retired naming the responsibility
  that replaces it. Absent a stated disposition, scaffolding acquires
  permanent-contract status by default. (F3 exists because the transition
  design dispositioned every pre-existing artifact and none of the new
  scaffolding.)
  Judge this by RETAINED RESPONSIBILITY AND REAL RUNTIME USE, never by whether
  a symbol is exported from a package's public surface: per AGENTS.md core
  symbols default to internal, so private implementation is the normal,
  correct state for most product code.

ACCEPTANCE
- AGENTS.md carries the policy, sited so it governs both test authoring and
  review.
- It does not contradict docs/importer-fix-protocol.md or the standing ban on
  weakening SRD regressions.
- It states no test-count target.
- It creates no new proof machinery, checker, or required artifact.

EXCLUSIONS
This bead changes documentation only. It retires no existing test.

SCOPE AMENDED 2026-09-15 (PR #553 review, head ade2cdc5).

It retires no existing test.' line was wrong as written and is superseded for this bead. docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md and AGENTS.md are ALREADY guarded by packages/core/test/reviewLifecyclePolicy.test.ts, so a documentation change to them is not test-neutral: editing the two-cycle clause broke that file's existing assertion, and no doc change of this kind can land without updating it. A documentation-only exclusion was therefore unsatisfiable.

- Adding guard assertions for the new AGENTS.md 'Permanent Test Evidence' section, in that same existing file.

Not authorized: any new test file, checker, script, or required artifact. That part of the original exclusion stands.

DISPOSITION under the standard this bead itself introduces:
- Governing invariant: AGENTS.md 'Permanent Test Evidence' exists and retains the absolute source-fidelity carve-out and the proof-cost clause.
- Authority: AGENTS.md is repository authority; docs/design-and-pr-review-policy.md binds every reviewer to it.
- Real consumer: every author and reviewer.
- Consequence of silent removal: the accretion loop the audit measured resumes, undetected.

- Cost: file read, ~1 ms. Proportionate to a repo-wide review contract.

That left authorized staged product implementation with NO valid disposition: 'retained' was forbidden for want of a current consumer, 'demoted' was false because it is not merely tooling, and 'retired' was false because the responsibility survives. T6 in the same PR explicitly says an accepted ADR/design/Bead may require an implementation before its consumer is integrated. title: T2: Cap Vitest workers and add process-tree memory measurement
description:
AUDIT REFERENCE: section 2 (OOM assessment), recommendations R1 and R7.

EXISTING
vitest.config.ts sets only `include`. Everything else is Vitest 5 defaults, so
maxWorkers = os.availableParallelism() = 20 on the primary agent host
(20 CPU, 7,790 MB RAM, 2,048 MB swap already 91% consumed at idle).

MEASURED
Process-tree peak RSS: 3,051 MB @ 1 worker, 4,116 MB @ 4, 4,897 MB @ 6.
Wall clock: 181 s @ 1, 55 s @ 4, 48 s @ 6.
Projected >= 13 GB at the default, against a ~9.8 GB RAM+swap envelope. The
default was deliberately never executed.
Parallelism past ~6 buys nothing: the run is latency-bound on
contextAssembler.test.ts. The default costs ~3x the memory for ~0 wall-clock
gain -- strictly worse on both axes, with no trade-off to weigh.

REQUIRED WORK

1. Cap workers in vitest.config.ts. Use an ABSOLUTE value, not a percentage,
   so a 20-CPU agent host and a 2-CPU CI runner both land in a measured
   envelope. Suggested: maxWorkers: process.env.CI ? 4 : 6. Re-measure and
   adjust from evidence rather than adopting the suggestion unmeasured.

2. Record wall clock and peak memory per verification run.

   CRITICAL -- do NOT use /usr/bin/time -v for memory. Its "Maximum resident
   set size" is getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN) ru_maxrss, the peak RSS of the
   LARGEST SINGLE CHILD, never the sum across concurrently live children.
   Verified on the agent host: three concurrent children at ~448 MB each
   (~1.34 GB aggregate) reported 458,656 KB.

   Applied to this suite it would report ~2.5 GB while the process tree is at
   4.9 GB, and would show NO difference between the 4- and 6-worker configs
   whose aggregate peaks differ by ~780 MB -- reassuring numbers in exactly
   the scenario that causes the OOM.

   Use instead:
   - sample the run's process group at ~1 Hz (ps -e -o pgid=,rss= with the run
     launched under setsid) and record the peak sum; or
   - read cgroup v2 memory.peak for the run's cgroup, which is exact and
     cannot miss a spike between samples. GitHub-hosted runners expose
     cgroup v2.

   /usr/bin/time -v remains fine for WALL CLOCK and for single-process steps
   (typecheck, format) where largest-child and tree totals coincide.

ACCEPTANCE
- maxWorkers is capped absolutely and the chosen value is justified by a
  recorded measurement on at least two worker counts.
- Memory instrumentation reports aggregate process-tree or cgroup peak, and
  its correctness is demonstrated (a run whose reported peak tracks the tree,
  not the largest child).
- Wall clock and peak memory are recorded per CI verification run and
  retained as an artifact.
- The authoritative gate still runs the full suite. No test is excluded.

EXCLUSIONS
No suite partitioning here (audit T4/R3, not materialized). No isolate:false
-- the audit measured only ~4.93 s available there and it trades away
per-file module-registry isolation several suites rely on.

FOLLOW-ON
Once this lands, re-examine eshyra-da8d and eshyra-5g3d. Both are
load-dependent timeouts whose cause this makes deterministic; eshyra-da8d was
previously treated by raising a timeout budget (commit 473424d), which is the
symptom layer.

F1: guard moved from contextAssembler.test.ts to packLoader.test.ts as a SHA-256 digest, per this bead's own siting requirement. F2: sampler rewritten from process-group to descendant-tree closure after demonstrating a detached 600 MB grandchild reported as 47 MB; detached:true removed and SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP forwarded. Corrected peak is HIGHER (2,923 MB vs 2,532 MB at the 6-worker cap) because the old figure under-reported.

Durability: membership now persists across samples with an etimes PID-reuse guard. Cancellation: wrapper signals the whole owned workload. Residual limit stated, not hidden: a descendant that both detaches AND is orphaned before first observation is unreachable by any /proc walk and needs kernel containment (cgroup subtree_control write denied unprivileged; Node exposes no prctl). Records now carry boundary/unmeasured fields. title: T1: Replace the 7.4 MB Buffer deep-equality pack-immutability assertion
description:
AUDIT REFERENCE: finding F1 / consolidation C1, section 5 and 7 of
docs/audits/test-suite-and-verification/2026-09-14-test-suite-and-verification-audit.md

EXISTING
packages/core/test/contextAssembler.test.ts reads
data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json (7.4 MB) at line 518 and
again at 778, then asserts expect(packBefore).toEqual(packAfter) at 779.

MEASURED COST
toEqual on two 7.4 MB Buffers: 14,354 ms and 2,414 MB peak RSS.
expect(a.equals(b)).toBe(true): 1 ms.
That single assertion is ~12% of the suite's summed file duration, the whole
critical path at any worker count >= 4, and the largest single allocation in
the verification run. It makes contextAssembler.test.ts (3,009 MB, 18 s) the
most expensive file in the repository.

CLAIMED INVARIANT
Assembling campaign-rules context does not mutate the bundled rules pack on
disk.

ACTUAL AUTHORITY
None located. ADR 0013 makes the generated pack the runtime pack; nothing
requires a runtime READ path to prove non-mutation of its source file. The
loader (rules/packLoader.ts via bundledSrdPack.ts) opens the pack read-only
and exposes no write path; assembleCampaignRulesContext never touches the
filesystem. The property is guaranteed by the module boundary.

REQUIRED WORK
Retire the assertion. If the team judges a non-mutation guard still worth
keeping as defence-in-depth against a future write path, do NOT keep the
current form: re-implement narrowly as Buffer.equals, a content hash, or an
mtime check, and site it once in a pack-loader test rather than inside the
heaviest context-assembly test.

ACCEPTANCE
- The 7.4 MB toEqual comparison is gone from contextAssembler.test.ts.
- Any retained guard is O(1)-ish and documents what it guards and why.
- Every other assertion in that test is preserved unchanged.
- Re-measure and record the file's new wall time and peak RSS.

EXCLUSIONS
Do not split the surrounding mega-test here; that is audit T3, not
materialized yet. Change only the pack-comparison assertion.

RISK
Low. If a future path can write the pack, a hash or mtime check preserves the
guard at ~0 cost and documents intent, which the current form does not.

2. Stop review/disposition failures from regenerating unnecessary

title: Audit test suite cost, execution topology, and evidence policy
description:
Audit-and-design pass over the verification system at post-PR-#546 main
(baseline a3a5219). Audit only: no tests deleted, no production code
refactored, no new proof machinery.

DELIVERABLE
docs/audits/test-suite-and-verification/2026-09-14-test-suite-and-verification-audit.md
PR: https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/551

KEY MEASURED FINDINGS

1. Raw test count is not the defect. The test:source LOC ratio has been flat
   at ~1.4 since June (1.67 -> 1.40), so suite growth tracks system growth.

2. The OOM is execution topology, not suite size. Vitest maxWorkers defaults
   to availableParallelism() = 20 on a 7.8 GB host whose swap is 91% consumed
   at idle. Measured process-tree peaks: 3,051 MB @ 1 worker, 4,116 MB @ 4,
   4,897 MB @ 6; projected >= 13 GB at the default, which was deliberately
   not executed. Wall clock 181s / 55s / 48s at 1/4/6 workers, so parallelism
   past ~6 buys nothing and costs ~3x the memory.

3. contextAssembler.test.ts:779 runs toEqual on two 7.4 MB Buffers:
   14,354 ms and 2,414 MB, versus 1 ms for Buffer.equals. ~30% of the suite's
   critical path and the largest allocation in the run, protecting a property
   the read-only pack loader boundary already guarantees.

4. The discovery subsystem (~20,700 LOC since July) has discoveryMode
   defaulting to 'off', no production caller, and no root export; for
   measurements.ts, blockerRepairs.ts, traceDerivation.ts and harness.ts the
   test suite is the entire consumer set. Authority is real and current (the
   accepted transition design, Phase 4 still open as eshyra-o9bd.19.15) but
   carries no sunset for experiment scaffolding. Disposition: legitimize with
   an explicit sunset, do NOT retire.

5. The review policy's disposition gate is asymmetric: accepting a finding
   costs nothing extra, rejecting one requires recorded reasoning. That
   asymmetry is the structural driver of contract accretion. Live signature:
   1,103 beads, 100 'Dispatch:' beads, a 15-round rev chain on eshyra-jhpt,
   and tasks reaching attempt 9.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-ON WORK
The audit proposes 13 beads (T1-T13) in section 11, plus amendments to
existing beads rather than duplicates. These are deliberately NOT filed yet:
the document is a proposal, not authority, and filing them before review
would pre-commit the repo to dispositions a reviewer may reject. File them
once the PR is reviewed.

EXISTING BEADS TO UPDATE (not duplicate)
- eshyra-da8d and eshyra-5g3d: this audit supplies the verified cause both
  lack. Note that commit 473424d treated eshyra-da8d by raising a timeout
  budget, which is the symptom layer. Both should be re-examined after a
  worker cap makes them deterministic.
- eshyra-o9bd.19.15: amend with Phase 4 exit dispositions for discovery
  scaffolding.
- eshyra-o9bd.19.1.8: already open and adjacent to the proposed T7;
  reconcile scope before either starts.
- eshyra-tba9: proposes new proof machinery; re-disposition against the
  proposed permanent-evidence policy before building it.

VERIFICATION
format, check, typecheck clean. Tests 5,608 passed / 3 skipped / 0 failed.
Test step run at --maxWorkers=6 rather than the unbounded default, because
the audit measures that default as a >= 13 GB projected peak against a
9.8 GB envelope. Worker count does not affect which tests run.
notes:
PR #551 review at head c046c47: CHANGES REQUESTED, three blockers, all in the audit artifact itself. All three verified against the tree and repaired at head 3fe86230.

F3 — claimed 'the test suite is the entire consumer set' for measurements.ts/blockerRepairs.ts/traceDerivation.ts/harness.ts and used root-export absence as evidence. Both wrong: shadow.ts calls observeBlockerRepairs + runDiscoveryStages and orchestrator.ts:883 calls captureDiscoveryShadow, so a real production chain exists, gated off by discoveryMode defaulting to 'off'. Root-export condition also contradicted AGENTS.md (core symbols default to internal). F3/T9 now classify by retained responsibility and real runtime use.

R7 — /usr/bin/time -v reports ru_maxrss = largest single child, not aggregate tree RSS. Verified: 3 children at ~448 MB each (~1.34 GB aggregate) reported 458,656 KB. Would report ~2.5 GB while the tree is at 4.9 GB and show no 4-vs-6-worker difference. R7/T2 now specify process-group sampler or cgroup v2 memory.peak.

F5 — overgeneralized. No authority requires global ADR number uniqueness and the repo already disambiguates by linking the file. Real defect is 3 bare citations (install.md:32, the-hollow-beneath-emberfall-outline.md:20,32). T11 narrowed to those; renumbering and the proposed uniqueness checker dropped. Recorded in-document as an instance of the F6 loop occurring inside the audit that describes it.

Headline measurements and the central test-policy conclusion were not challenged. Approval binds to an exact head SHA, so 3fe86230 needs re-review. Reviewer has not posted the review to GitHub.

ruleDispositions.ts:3042, where `validateRuleDeterministicCapabilityContracts`
has to exempt `derived-magic-item-clauses-v1` because it is not a registered
tool - the adapter is reporting a different CLASS of contract than it was
reviewed for.

the magic-item readiness contract as real; the defect is not its existence, it is
that this PR decided a capability REPORT's membership, which belongs to
eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12.

REPORT'S PRIOR REVIEWED MEMBERSHIP. The rule-disposition report emits the three
rule contracts it has always emitted. The magic-item readiness contract stays a
real member of the RUNTIME ledger (packet presentation and lookup are unchanged)
but is outside that report's reviewed scope. Because the report no longer carries
a non-tool contract, the `derived-magic-item-clauses-v1` exemption at :3042 goes
away with it - if you find yourself keeping that exemption, the split is wrong.
Do not instead delete the contract from the ledger, and do not ask the report to
grow a fourth member.

Shape it so the runtime ledger and the report share ONE definition of every row
they both use - re-introducing a second copy is the defect the previous round
fixed (see the bead's ROUND 1 review note, finding X1).

R7 MUST BE RE-GROUNDED. The current R7 test pins a newly authored four-row set, so
it cannot detect the very drift it is supposed to catch - a pin authored AFTER a
change ratifies it. Compare against the PRE-MOVE identities as they exist on
`origin/main` (read
`git show origin/main:packages/core/scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/ruleDispositions.ts`
and take the three contract revisions, eight bindings and thirty-one disposition
keys from there), and assert the post-move REPORT still emits exactly those. A
`toBe` identity check that each shared name resolves to the single runtime
definition is still wanted, but it is not the membership proof.

disposition keys differ from the pre-move set; and a test that the runtime ledger

`createDeterministicCapabilityLedger` rejects an unknown contract key and a key
that is both bound and dispositioned, and nothing else. It accepts:

presentation. Constructor tests for duplicate `(ruleKey, capability)`,

overlap cases passing.

title: Dispatch: PR #546 repair - relationship producer binding and evidence discipline (F1,F2,F3,F4,F6)
description:
PR #546 review repair, relationship half. Findings F1, F2, F3, F4, F6 of the
2026-09-13 review by jbongaarts on head e73b588. Read `bd show
eshyra-o9bd.19.1.4` and the note beginning "=== PR #546 REVIEW" IN FULL before
writing code: it carries the supervisor's verification of each finding and the
design decisions D1-D3 that are already made and are NOT yours to revisit.

Authority: ADR 0020 §§3, 4; docs/design/evidence-trust-model.md ("Required
failure behavior" and "Bounded positive absence"); docs/importer-fix-protocol.md.

DO NOT TOUCH the capability half: deterministicCapabilityLedger.ts,
deterministicCapabilityContract.ts, itemExecutionReadiness.ts,
create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/, packet.ts, packetMessage.ts,
test/deterministicCapabilityLedger.test.ts. A sibling child owns those.

=== F1 (MATERIAL) Pack-owned semantics are applied across producer boundaries ===
`harness.ts` lines 33 and 75 pass ONE `getBundledDnd5eSrdRecordRelationshipManifest()`
for the whole resolved stack and `expandTypedRelationships` applies it to every
`RulesStackRecordEntry`. Add-on, override, and foreign-pack records are therefore
interpreted with the SRD producer's declarations. `test/discovery/support/
lateAmbiguityAddon.ts` already creates an add-on `feature` carrying `data.source`
and no manifest of its own; today discovery traverses it under SRD semantics.
That contradicts this bead's own rationale - relationship meaning is PACK-specific,
which is the entire reason it is a pack artifact rather than a runtime module. The
harness comment copied from field provenance ("declared per RulesRecordKind, not
per pack identity") is TRUE for provenance and FALSE here; do not preserve it.

REQUIRED (design decision D1, already made): resolve declarations by PRODUCING
PACK. `RulesStackRecordSource` carries `pack`, so a resolved record's producer is
`entry.pack` - the WINNING entry for an override; `overrideChain` holds the losers
and must NOT be consulted for semantics. `expandTypedRelationships` takes a
producer-keyed manifest SOURCE (a lookup from pack identity to manifest-or-
explicit-absence), never a single manifest. Absence is per producer and explicit:
only the SRD pack ships a manifest today, so every add-on resolves to explicit
absence, and that is the honest state rather than a gap. Never fall back to
another pack's manifest, and never infer one from base/system compatibility.

Evidence: (a) a base SRD record resolves under the SRD manifest; (b) an add-on with
no manifest does NOT inherit it and its absence is recorded; (c) an add-on carrying
its OWN differing manifest resolves under its own semantics; (d) an overriding
record is interpreted under the winning producer's manifest. Use the existing
add-on fixtures where they fit.

=== F2 (MATERIAL) Malformed declared input disappears as an empty result ===
In `resolveRecordRelationships`, a declared reference whose value is not a string
returns nothing, and a `record-name` occurrence whose declared relation sibling is
missing, non-string, or not in CONDITION_RELATION_VALUES also returns nothing.
Separately, `buildRecordRelationshipManifest` validates `decl.kind` against
RULES_RECORD_KINDS but NEVER `targetKind`, which is later used via
`as RulesRecordKind` (recordRelationships.ts:266); and
`loadRecordRelationshipManifest` casts parsed JSON straight to the interface, so a
malformed on-disk manifest becomes `no-record-with-name` instead of failing closed.

REQUIRED: every DECLARED occurrence produces a typed outcome - positive, negative,
or indeterminate. Add an indeterminate variant to the resolution union carrying a
closed reason discriminant covering at least: value-not-a-string, relation-sibling-
missing, relation-sibling-not-a-string, relation-not-recognized. Validate the
manifest's closed vocabulary (schema tag, disposition, targetResolution, kind,
targetKind) at BOTH build and load, so an unknown `targetKind` fails closed at the
loader rather than degrading into a lookup miss.

DESIGN DECISION D3, ALREADY MADE: the existing test in
`test/rules/recordRelationships.test.ts` that asserts
`expect(resolveRecordRelationships(manifest, renamed, stack)).toEqual([])` for the
renamed-sibling case is the CODIFIED DEFECT and must be REPLACED, not preserved. Its
replacement asserts the typed indeterminate outcome. Do not keep any assertion whose
expected value is an empty array standing for "a declared occurrence was skipped".

=== F3 Bounded coverage gate is one-sided ===
Only `assertRecordRelationshipDeclarationsAreLive` exists (dead-declaration check).
The design called for BOTH directions. A future importer change can emit one of the
old relationship-bearing shapes for a new kind/field occurrence with no declaration;
every existing declaration stays live, the gate passes, and discovery silently
classifies that occurrence as nothing.

REQUIRED: enumerate the bounded population from the DELETED consumer allowlist as an
explicit, committed contract - the field shapes `data.source`, `data.parentClass`,
`data.progressionTableRef`, `data.tableRefs[]`, `data.spellTableRefs[]`,
`data.statBlockRefs[]`, `data.mechanics.conditions[].condition` - derived from that
contract and NOT from the manifest under test, and fail the PRODUCTION IMPORTER when
an emitted occurrence of one of those shapes has no declaration for its kind. Keep
the dead-declaration check. This stays BOUNDED: it is a claim about those seven
shapes only. Do NOT turn it into a corpus-wide `RulesRecord.data` coverage claim -
ADR 0020 rejects that global negative explicitly.

=== F4 (MATERIAL) Durable trace drops the manifest-absence fact ===
`ExpansionTrace.relationshipManifestAbsent` (types.ts:201) is not persisted by
`ProjectedExpansionStage` / `projectExpansion` in traceProjection.ts, and runtime
shadow evidence persists the projected trace - so the fact vanishes before durable
audit. Note one boolean cannot describe a mixed stack anyway once F1 lands.

REQUIRED: persist ONE canonical, producer-qualified relationship-artifact state
through the durable trace, replacing the boolean. Round-trip evidence for a
manifest-present producer, a manifest-absent producer, AND a mixed stack, proving
the distinction survives `projectDiscoveryTrace()` and JSON encode/read. Do not
redundantly persist anything already derivable from canonical traversals or losses.

=== F6 Resolution/loss evidence is double-recorded ===
`expandTypedRelationships` resolves every stack entry to build the reverse index and
records each unresolved result and loss, then calls `manifestLinks` AGAIN per
expandable candidate and records the same unresolved result and loss a second time.
`measureDiscovery` counts `stage.losses.length`, so this corrupts measured evidence,
not just an internal list. The existing unresolved test cannot expose it because it
mutates the candidate entry while leaving the stack's source entry valid.

REQUIRED: resolve each relationship occurrence ONCE per expansion pass and reuse
that result for both inbound and outbound processing. Evidence: a stack containing
one unresolved declared edge, expanded from that source, asserting exactly ONE
canonical unresolved resolution and ONE loss for that edge; and a case varying
first-pass vs second-pass expansion so genuinely repeated PASS events stay
distinguishable from duplicate work inside one pass.

=== VERIFICATION ===
`npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing (it rewrites files). Regenerate through
the importer and run `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack`; `records.json` must stay at 0
records added/removed/changed. Explain every generated diff in your report.

=== PROHIBITIONS ===
Assert identities, never counts. No corpus-wide coverage or completeness claim. No
alias/topic content (eshyra-o9bd.19.2.4 owns it). Do not weaken or delete an
existing assertion to make something pass, except the one D3 replacement named
above, which must get a STRONGER assertion in its place. If a fix needs a new parser
or extractor strategy, or creates generated churn beyond the direct consequences of
these five findings, STOP and report instead of broadening.

title: Dispatch: runtime-owned deterministic capability ledger (attempt 1)
description:
PARENT SPEC: eshyra-o9bd.19.1.4 (run `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.1.4` and read the
2026-09-12 DESIGN SESSION note in full before writing code). Authority: ADR 0020
(especially section 3 and its two load-bearing asymmetries),
docs/design/evidence-trust-model.md (the "Subject authority within adjudication
support" section is directly load-bearing here), the CLOSED W13 bead
eshyra-olc5.6 (which owns capability CONTRACT SHAPE - you do not redefine it),
and AGENTS.md. This child delivers DELIVERABLE 2 only. Deliverable 1 (the record-
relationship manifest) is a sibling child and is NOT yours - do not touch
discovery/expansion.ts, rules/fieldProvenance.ts, rules/packLoader.ts,
rules/bundledSrdPack.ts, or scripts/importers/.

WORKTREE: .worktrees/eshyra-xus8 on branch eshyra-xus8 (already created for you, cut from
branch eshyra-o9bd.19.1.4). Run `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` first and
work only from there. Run `npm ci` in the worktree before verifying.

=== THE DEFECT (verified; reproduce it before you fix it) ===
The only reviewed statement of Eshyra's positively selected deterministic
capabilities and their bindings to record identities lives inside an AUDIT-BUNDLE
SCRIPT that no runtime consumer may import:
  packages/core/scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/ruleDispositions.ts
    RuleDeterministicCapabilityContract   (type; DeterministicCapabilityContract
                                           plus inputSchemaOperation, runtimeOwner, evidence)
    RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_CONTRACTS    resolve-check-v1,
                                               resolve-concentration-v1,
                                               resolve-spell-upcast-v1
    RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_BINDINGS     8 rows, rule key -> capability, many-to-many
    RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_DISPOSITIONS 31 explicit not-positively-selected rows
    requireRuleDeterministicCapabilityContract / validateRuleDeterministicCapabilityContracts
Because runtime cannot reach it, packages/core/src/discovery/packet.ts's
capabilities() instead hardcodes `candidate.entry?.record.kind !== 'magic-item'`
plus a direct import of ONE contract constant
(MAGIC_ITEM_OPERATION_READINESS_CAPABILITY from state/itemExecutionReadiness.ts),
and every other declaration arrives from a TEST FIXTURE table
(packages/core/test/discovery/support/scenario.ts DECLARED_OFFLINE_CAPABILITIES,
reaching the run as DiscoveryScenario.declaredCapabilities).
Verified consequence: all eight W13-bound rule records exist in the shipped pack -
rule:ability-checks, rule:advantage-and-disadvantage, rule:attack-rolls,
rule:modifiers-to-the-roll, rule:proficiency-bonus, rule:saving-throws,
rule:concentration, rule:casting-a-spell-at-a-higher-level - and every one of them
reaches the DM context packet with ZERO capability entries, byte-identical to a
record for which nothing was positively selected. That directly violates the
parent bead's third acceptance criterion. packetMessage.ts already renders the
non-claim correctly ("no capability was positively selected. / This is not a claim
that the record has no mechanics, is irrelevant, or is safe to ignore.") - the
renderer is honest, the DATA is missing.

=== REQUIRED INVARIANT ===
A runtime consumer obtains positively selected capability bindings and their
declared limits from runtime-owned data reachable from @eshyra/core, without
reading an audit-only artifact; and every negative result is a distinguishable
typed disposition, never an empty value.

=== BUILD THIS ===
1. NEW packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityLedger.ts.
   MOVE - do not copy - the type, the three contracts, the eight bindings, the 31
   dispositions, and the two fail-closed helpers out of
   scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/ruleDispositions.ts into this module. The
   audit bundle then IMPORTS them from src, reversing the dependency and keeping
   its reporting byte-identical. Keep inputSchemaOperation, runtimeOwner and
   evidence: those are real capability-OWNER facts, not audit decoration. Do not
   change the contract shape defined by rules/deterministicCapabilityContract.ts -
   eshyra-olc5.6 owns it.
   Also register the existing MAGIC_ITEM_OPERATION_READINESS_CAPABILITY
   (state/itemExecutionReadiness.ts, revision derived-magic-item-clauses-v1) in
   the ledger's contract table so the ledger is the single runtime-owned index of
   selected capabilities. Watch the import direction: if state/ importing rules/
   (or the reverse) would create a cycle, keep the contract constant where it
   lives and have the ledger reference it - say which you did and why in your
   notes.
2. LOOKUP IS A DISCRIMINATED UNION, never a bare array:
     export type CapabilityLedgerLookup =
       | { outcome: 'bound'; recordKey; bindings: readonly CapabilityBinding[] }
       | { outcome: 'not-positively-selected'; recordKey; disposition }
       | { outcome: 'no-statement'; recordKey };
   'no-statement' means the ledger makes NO statement about this record. Document
   in the module doc comment, in ADR 0020 section 3's own terms, that it is a
   statement about Eshyra and never about the rules: it does not mean the record
   has no mechanics, is irrelevant, is safely unsupported, or that the pack is
   complete. A binding QUOTES its contract's identity, revision, required inputs,

allowlist of traversable fields and a per-field target-resolution mode:

The field NAME does not determine the meaning. Over the shipped pack
(packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json, 1812 records):
  feature   /source  n=184 resolved=184  value is a record key ("class:barbarian")
  ancestry  /source  n=13  resolved=0    value is the literal label "race" - a
                                         source SECTION name, not a record key
  subclass /parentClass 12/12 | class /progressionTableRef 12/12
  rule /tableRefs 38/38 | magic-item /tableRefs 32/32 | magic-item /statBlockRefs 2/2
  spell /tableRefs 9/9 | feature /tableRefs 4/4 | background /tableRefs 4/4

packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/fieldProvenanceDeclarations.ts:
  ancestry '/source' -> "a structural field describing where this ancestry sits in
                         the source (page/section), not narrative prose."
  feature  '/source' -> "the granting class/subclass record-key, not source text."
No consumer can act on prose, so expansion applies one meaning to both kinds and
silently drops all 13 ancestry values: directLinks' inner add() returns early when
the key does not resolve. "not a reference", "target absent" and "found nothing"
become indistinguishable - recurring fail-open idiom 1 of eshyra-o9bd.19.7 and the
behaviour ADR 0020 section 3 forbids.

A runtime consumer obtains a record's declared relationships from pack-owned data,
and every non-resolution is a distinguishable typed outcome, never a silent drop.

1. NEW packages/core/src/rules/recordRelationships.ts.
   Model it CLOSELY on packages/core/src/rules/fieldProvenance.ts - same module
   doc-comment style (state what the module replaces and WHY a default is
   forbidden), same (kind, pointerPrefix) declaration model with every array index
   collapsed to the literal segment '*', same longest-prefix-wins matching, same
   "an unmatched lookup returns undefined, never a default" rule.
     export type RelationshipDisposition = 'reference' | 'not-a-reference';
     export type RelationshipTargetResolution = 'record-key' | 'record-name';
     export interface RecordRelationshipDeclaration {
       kind: RulesRecordKind; pointerPrefix: string;
       disposition: RelationshipDisposition;
       relation?: string;                       // required iff disposition==='reference'
       targetResolution?: RelationshipTargetResolution;  // same
       targetKind?: RulesRecordKind;            // required iff targetResolution==='record-name'

     }

     export interface RecordRelationshipManifest { schema: ...; declarations: readonly ... }
     export function buildRecordRelationshipManifest(decls): RecordRelationshipManifest
   'not-a-reference' is the load-bearing half: ancestry '/source' is DECLARED not a
   reference, with its reason, so "declared not to be a link" is distinguishable
   from "nobody classified it". Reject a declaration whose optional fields
   contradict its disposition (a 'not-a-reference' carrying a relation, a
   'reference' missing targetResolution, a 'record-name' missing targetKind), a

   unresolved target is RETAINED in the output as 'unresolved-target'. A leaf
   matching a 'not-a-reference' declaration contributes nothing and is not an
   error. A leaf matching NO declaration contributes nothing and makes no claim -
   the manifest's claim is bounded to what it declares; do not invent a
   corpus-wide coverage gate over RulesRecord.data (ADR 0020 rejects that global
   negative explicitly).

description:

`eshyra-o9bd.19.1.3.1` (a child of `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.3`) OWNS the provenance
representation, the declarations, the fail-closed gate, and the emitted
`field-provenance.json`. It is already merged into your base branch. **You do
not modify any of it.** W10 is purely a CONSUMER here. If the fact is wrong or
insufficient, record it with `bd update` and file a follow-up against
`eshyra-o9bd.19.1.3.1` — do not fix it in discovery code.

## What exists on your base branch

- `packages/core/src/rules/fieldProvenance.ts` — `FieldProvenanceClass`
  (`source-prose` | `source-derived` | `compiler-projection`),
  `FieldProvenanceManifest`, `classifyFieldPointer(manifest, kind, pointer)`
  (returns `undefined` when nothing covers the pointer — deliberately),
  `walkFieldPointers`, `buildFieldProvenanceManifest`.
- `packages/core/src/rules/packLoader.ts` — `loadFieldProvenanceManifest`,
  `PACK_FIELD_PROVENANCE_FILE`; `loadRulesPackFromDirectory` exposes it.
- `packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/field-provenance.json`
  — 207 declarations covering all 68,231 emitted leaves, all 16 record kinds.
- All of the above are exported from `packages/core/src/internal.ts`.

Pointer convention, which you must match exactly: pointers are rooted at
`data` and every array index is collapsed to the literal segment `*`, so
`actions[5].mechanics.damage[0].dice` classifies as
`/actions/*/mechanics/damage/*/dice`.

## The defect being closed

`packet.ts` currently splits a record body with `PROJECTION_CONTAINER_KEYS`, a
consumer-side heuristic. It is the SECOND such heuristic and the re-review
rejected a third. It classifies `creature:adult-black-dragon`
`armorClass.value: 19` — a parser product — as `sourceMaterial`, which the
renderer then presents under "Source prose (verbatim; authoritative)".

## What to change

1. **Delete `PROJECTION_CONTAINER_KEYS` and the container walk** in
   `packages/core/src/discovery/packet.ts`. Classify each leaf by asking the
   pack's manifest. Nothing in discovery may keep a fallback name list.
2. **Three buckets on `PacketCandidate`, not two.** `sourceMaterial` /
   `projection` becomes a partition over the three real classes. Name them for
   what they are; `source-derived` is neither verbatim prose nor an
   interpretive projection, and collapsing it into either is the defect in a
   new form.
3. **The renderer states each honestly.** Only `source-prose` may appear under
   "Source prose (verbatim; authoritative)". `source-derived` gets its own
   heading saying plainly that these are deterministic parser products of the
   cited source and are NOT verbatim quotations. `compiler-projection` keeps
   the existing typed-projection heading and its "does not replace the source
   prose above" line. Projection-limit notes stay in band beside the
   projection they qualify.
4. **A pointer the manifest does not cover is a residue entry**, disclosed in
   band exactly as the existing `residue` list is — never silently assigned to
   a bucket. `classifyFieldPointer` returns `undefined` for a reason.
5. **The pack may ship no manifest at all** (`loadFieldProvenanceManifest` is
   optional, and an add-on pack in the test corpus may lack one). Decide that
   case deliberately and write the reasoning down: discovery must not claim
   "verbatim; authoritative" for material whose provenance nothing attests.
   Whatever you choose, a reader must be able to tell "attested prose" from
   "unattested content" in the delivered text.
6. Follow the shape change through `measurements.ts` (M9's `exactSubstring`
   and `typedPath` matching, M8's attribution check) and `shadow.ts`'s v2
   admission.

## Evidence required

Use REAL records through the offline harness. Do not hand-author a packet, and
do not derive expectations from the declaration table — derive them from the
record and assert the delivered text.

E1. `creature:adult-black-dragon`: `armorClass/sourceText` under source prose;
    `armorClass/value` and `armorClass/source` under source-derived, NOT under
    the verbatim heading; `actions/*/text` under source prose;
    `actions/*/mechanics` under projection.
E2. The sibling class the re-review named: hit points, speed, ability scores
    and structured statline metadata all render as source-derived, never as
    verbatim prose.
E3. `spell:fireball`: `description` and `higherLevels` verbatim under source
    prose; `mechanics.saves[0].ability` and `damageOnSuccess` under projection;
    "a 20-foot-radius sphere" still present verbatim.
E4. A generic sweep over every retained candidate of at least one probe: no
    pointer whose manifest class is `source-derived` or `compiler-projection`
    appears under the verbatim heading. This must be driven from the manifest
    at assertion time, so a future reclassification moves the test with it.
E5. The no-manifest case from item 5, asserting whatever you decided.
E6. M9 still reports zero missing facts for every probe that reported zero
    before, including P8's typed path `/data/mechanics/economies/use`.

## Non-negotiables

- `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing.
- Biome is canonical; CI fails on warnings.
- Do not weaken or skip an existing test. Tests encoding the container
  heuristic SHOULD change — name each and why.
- Do not edit `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, anything under `.claude/`, the design
  document, or anything owned by `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.3.1`.
- Known flake: `packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts > packs publishable tarballs`
  times out at 10s under full-suite load. Pre-existing, filed, unrelated.

title: Emit authoritative field-level provenance for every importer-emitted record value
description:
Narrowly scoped prerequisite child of `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.3` (field provenance),
under the SRD source-authority epic `eshyra-o9bd.19.2`. Created 2026-09-11 at
the user's direction after PR #543's re-review finding 1.

**This bead owns the provenance representation and the importer/schema change.**
`eshyra-o9bd.19.12` (W10) only CONSUMES the resulting fact. The two share PR
#543 for delivery; sharing a PR transfers no ownership. Enumerate this bead's
scope and evidence separately from W10's in any handoff.

## Why this exists

PR #543's re-review established that the context packet cannot tell literal
source prose from compiler/parser products, because **the pack does not carry
the fact**. `RulesRecord.data` is typed `unknown` and declares no per-field
provenance (`packages/core/src/rules/types.ts`). Two successive consumer-side
heuristics were tried in W10 and both failed:

1. split by primitive JS type — promoted `spell:fireball`
   `mechanics.saves[0].ability: "dexterity"` to "verbatim; authoritative";
2. split by declared projection container — promoted
   `creature:adult-black-dragon` `armorClass.value: 19` to the same heading.
   `parseArmorClassText` (`parseCreatures.ts:310`) parses the printed AC into
   `{value, source, sourceText}`: `sourceText` is literal, `value` is a parser
   product. The sibling class includes hit points, speed, ability scores,
   components, and structured statline metadata.

A third heuristic is explicitly out of bounds. The importer KNOWS which fields
it copied and which it parsed; the pack must say so.

`eshyra-o9bd.19.1.3`'s own acceptance already requires this: *"Derived and
compiler-authored values identify their derivation and are never presented as
verbatim source."* This child discharges exactly that clause for the emitted
record body, and nothing else in its parent's scope.

## Scope — in

The **field-provenance classification of every value the importer emits into
`RulesRecord.data`**, for every record kind, as a producer-declared fact.

## Scope — out (belongs to the parent or elsewhere)

Bidirectional source validation, span pinning, multi-page locator repair,
supplemental-content license identity, the clean-coverage gate, and the
`table:starting-wealth-by-class` disposition. Do not touch them.

## The representation (decided)

Three classes, declared per `(record kind, JSON pointer prefix)`, NOT per
record — a field's class is a property of the kind's schema, not of a
particular dragon. A declared prefix covers its whole subtree unless a deeper
prefix overrides it.

- `source-prose` — literal text reproduced from the source. The only class the
  consumer may present as verbatim source authority.
- `source-derived` — deterministically parsed or computed from pinned source
  text. Truthful, attributable, and NOT verbatim (`armorClass.value`,
  `hitPoints.formula`, `speed.walk`).
- `compiler-projection` — interpretive or curated typed material authored by
  the compiler's curation stage (`mechanics`, `upcast`, `executionReadiness`,
  `projection`, `useProfile`).

Emit it as a pack artifact the loader exposes, alongside `records.json`.
Do NOT inline a copy per record: `records.json` is already 7.1 MB and the
classification is identical across every record of a kind.

Survey result to size the work, verified 2026-09-11: **458 distinct
`(kind, pointer)` prefixes to depth 3** across 16 kinds (magic-item 103,
creature 61, spell 52, equipment 43, class 36, stat-block 35, …). Prefix
inheritance should cut the declaration count well below that; report what you
actually needed.

## The gate that closes the semantic class

**The importer must FAIL when it emits a value no declaration covers.** This is
the difference between closing the class and patching today's fields: a future
importer change that adds a field must declare its provenance or the build
stops. Implement it as a verification pass over the emitted records, not as a
lint over source code.

State the rule explicitly where it is implemented: an unclassified field is a
build failure, never a default class. Defaulting to `source-prose` would
recreate the exact defect; defaulting to `compiler-projection` would silently
demote real prose.

## Evidence required (permanent, pack-side)

E1. The fail-closed gate rejects an emitted field with no declaration — prove
    it by adding a field to a builder in a test fixture or by removing one
    declaration and asserting the importer fails, not by asserting the current
    pack happens to be covered.
E2. Over the REAL regenerated pack, every emitted field resolves to exactly one
    class, and the counts per class per kind are reported.
E3. `creature:adult-black-dragon`: `armorClass.sourceText` is `source-prose`,
    `armorClass.value` and `armorClass.source` are `source-derived`,
    `actions[5].text` is `source-prose`, `actions[5].mechanics` is
    `compiler-projection`. Assert against the real record.
E4. The sibling class the review named: hit points, speed, ability scores, and
    structured statline metadata are `source-derived`, not `source-prose`.
E5. `spell:fireball`: `description` and `higherLevels` are `source-prose`;
    everything under `mechanics` and `upcast` is `compiler-projection`.
E6. A record whose prose lives in a nested array — `magic-item:ioun-stone`
    `variants[i].text` is `source-prose` while `variants[i].mechanics` is
    `compiler-projection` — so the declaration model handles nesting.

## Protocol

`docs/importer-fix-protocol.md` governs. Specifically:

- Do not hand-edit generated records.
- Regenerate through the importer and commit the regenerated artifacts.
- The committed pack must match regenerated output exactly. VERIFIED 2026-09-11
  that it currently does, byte-for-byte, for all five pack files, so any diff
  you produce is attributable to your change.
- Review and explain the generated diff. Adding a new artifact is expected
  churn; a change to `records.json` content is NOT — investigate before
  broadening.
- The freeze gate (`npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-freeze`) may require a thaw note
  under `docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/thaw-notes/`. If it does, write one.
- Report the required PR summary fields the protocol lists.

Regeneration: `npm run import:dnd5e-srd -- --out packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1`
(the default `--out` is a scratch path; the PDF default already resolves).
A full run takes a few minutes.

## Completion proof

The importer fails closed on an undeclared field; the regenerated pack carries
the classification for every emitted field; E1–E6 pass over real records; and
`eshyra-o9bd.19.12` can replace its container heuristic with a read of this
fact. Record in the notes exactly which clause of `eshyra-o9bd.19.1.3` this
discharges and which remain open, so the parent's remaining scope stays visible.

title: Repair F1: preflight declared operations instead of a future model tool choice
description:
Repair dispatch for PR #543 review finding **F1** (`eshyra-o9bd.19.12`, ADR 0020
W10). Parent authority: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.12` — its notes carry the review
and the integrating agent's verification. This is a MATERIAL, architectural
change to the pre-model discovery/preflight boundary.

WORKTREE `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.12.9`, BRANCH `eshyra-o9bd.19.12.9`, cut
from `eshyra-o9bd.19.12` AFTER the F2 repair merged into it. Dependencies
installed. Touch nothing outside it.

Supersedes `eshyra-o9bd.19.12.6`, which recorded this as a deferred finding.
Close that bead as part of this work, pointing at your commit.

## The defect

W10's acceptance requires the DELIVERED text to carry a positive bounded
capability contract, and M10 to compare discovery's preflight against the real
runtime invocation. The live `intervene` path delivers the NEGATIVE form for
P8 and records the real `use_item(hit-target)` invocation in
`m10.runtimeInvocationsAbsentFromPacket`.

Verified root cause, `packages/core/src/discovery/signals.ts:230`:

```ts
if (leaf.path.endsWith('/operationId') && typeof leaf.value === 'string') {
```

The `capability-preflight` signal fires only when the pre-model state already
contains an `/operationId` leaf. Real campaign state deliberately does not
synthesize one, because **which operation gets invoked is a future model tool
choice**. So pre-model capability selection depends on a parameter that does
not exist until after the model has chosen — the generalized defect, not a P8
quirk.

**Do not fix this by putting an `operationId` into fixture or runtime state.**
The review explicitly forbids it, and it would encode a prediction of the
model's choice as though it were campaign state.

## The decided approach

Capability **availability** is a property of the record plus the item's own
state. It is not a prediction of which operation the model will pick. So
discovery stops waiting to be told an operation and instead enumerates the
operations the record itself declares, preflighting each.

Verified against the real pack:

| record | declared operations |
|---|---|
| `magic-item:ammunition-1-2-or-3` | `hit-target` (1) |
| `magic-item:cube-of-force` | `press-face-1`…`press-face-6`, `spell-contact-loss` (7) |
| `magic-item:ring-of-protection` | none |

That distribution is the point: P8 gets a real positive contract, the cube is a
genuine multi-operation case, and the ring keeps an honest "no capability
positively selected".

**`variantId` stays an input and is NOT enumerated.** It is a property of the
item instance in inventory, so it is genuinely available pre-model, and
`deriveItemOperationReadinessInput(record, variantId, operationId)` resolves
the operation set through `effectiveMagicItemMechanics(record, variantId)` —
the operation set is variant-dependent. Enumerate operations *for the
instance's actual variant*. Enumerating variants too would preflight item
states the campaign is not in.

**Enumerate the union** of `mechanics.operations[].id` and the non-null
`mechanics.stateMachine.transitions[].via` ids.
`deriveItemOperationReadinessInput` accepts `activate`/`deactivate` sourced
from a state-machine transition even when `operations` does not list them
(read that function before you write the enumeration), so an
`operations`-only walk would under-enumerate a record whose activation lives
only in its state machine. For the cube the two sets coincide; do not conclude
from that that one of them is redundant.

## What to change

1. **`signals.ts`** — the `capability-preflight` signal derives from the BOUND
   ITEM INSTANCE, not from an `/operationId` leaf: for each item instance the
   scenario binds (and each state-referenced item record), emit a preflight
   signal per declared operation, carrying `operationId` and the instance's
   `variantId` as evidence. An explicit `/operationId` in state, where one
   exists, must not produce a duplicate preflight for the same
   `(record, variant, operation)` triple.
2. **`packet.ts`** — `capability()` returns the preflight for ONE
   `(record, variant, operation)` triple today. A candidate can now carry
   several, so `PacketCandidate.capability?: CapabilityPreflight` becomes a
   list. Name it so the plural reads as the bounded set it is, and keep the
   existing `available` / `blocked` derivation per entry unchanged — this
   change is about WHICH triples get preflighted, not about how a preflight is
   judged.
3. **`packetMessage.ts`** — render every contract in the candidate's block.
   The negative form ("no capability was positively selected", with its full
   disclaimer) now applies when the bounded set is EMPTY. A record that
   declares operations but whose every preflight is `blocked` is not the
   negative case: it is a set of blocked contracts, and each still states that
   a blocked contract is not an executable capability.
4. **`measurements.ts` M10** — already pairs on the
   `(recordKey, operationId, variantId)` subject, so it should extend
   naturally to a set. Verify that `runtimeInvocationsAbsentFromPacket` empties
   for P8 and that a runtime invocation of an operation the packet did NOT
   preflight is still reported there.
5. **`shadow.ts`'s `assertV2`** — follow the packet shape change so the durable
   reader admits the bounded set and still fails closed on a malformed entry.

## Evidence required

The reviewer named this evidence specifically; it is the acceptance bar.

E1. A real P8 `intervene` turn where the ACTUAL DM input contains the positive
    bounded contract for `hit-target` — operation, capability id, revision,
    inputs, exclusions, residual interpretation — asserted against the model's
    captured `ModelCompleteInput`, not against the offline packet.
E2. The same turn's M10 contains a REAL discovery/runtime comparison that
    reports `agreed`, and `m10.runtimeInvocationsAbsentFromPacket` is empty.
E3. The adversarial non-fixture-specific case: a different operation and a
    different variant. Use `magic-item:cube-of-force`'s multi-operation set,
    and the variant-bearing item in
    `packages/core/test/discovery/support/variantReadinessAddon.ts`. Prove the
    packet preflights the operations the record declares for the instance's
    actual variant, that a runtime invocation of one of them pairs and agrees,
    and that an invocation of an operation the record does NOT declare is
    reported as absent from the packet rather than silently paired.
E4. `magic-item:ring-of-protection` (P11) declares no operations: the delivered
    text carries the negative form with its full disclaimer and no contract.
E5. The blocked case stays distinct from the negative case — a blocked contract
    is rendered as a contract, not as "no capability positively selected".
E6. The offline probe suites still report their pinned M1–M9, and the
    intervention suite's pinned per-probe report is updated deliberately:
    name every pinned number that moved and why in your notes. Numbers WILL
    move — P7 and P8 gain capability entries — and a pin that silently
    absorbed the change would defeat the pin.

## Non-negotiables

- `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing.
- Biome is canonical; CI fails on warnings. Do not suppress a finding.
- Do not weaken, skip, or reshape an existing test to make this pass. Tests
  that encode the old operationId-driven selection SHOULD change — name each
  and why.
- Do not edit `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, anything under `.claude/`, or the
  design document.
- House style: read the doc comments in `discovery/types.ts`, `packet.ts` and
  `shadow.ts` and match them. Every non-obvious shape says WHY it has that form
  and what wrong thing it makes unrepresentable.
- Known flake: `packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts > packs publishable tarballs`
  times out at 10s under full-suite load. Pre-existing, filed, unrelated.
  Confirm standalone, note it, do not fix it.
