title: Repair F2: provenance-preserving source/projection split in the packet
description:
Repair dispatch for PR #543 review finding **F2** (`eshyra-o9bd.19.12`, ADR 0020
W10). Parent authority: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.12` — its notes carry the review
and the integrating agent's verification. This is a MATERIAL change: it alters
the semantic shape of what the DM receives.

WORKTREE `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.12.8`, BRANCH `eshyra-o9bd.19.12.8`, cut
from `eshyra-o9bd.19.12`. Dependencies installed. Touch nothing outside it.

Sibling dispatches own F1 (`signals.ts` + the capability preflight) and F3/F4/F5
(`orchestrator.ts`, the v2 reader, `measurements.ts`). Stay out of those.

## The defect

`packet.ts:packetCandidate()` sets `sourceProse: { data: object(record.data) }`
— the ENTIRE record body. `packetMessage.ts` then sends every string-valued
leaf to `### Source prose (verbatim; authoritative)` and every non-string leaf
to `### Typed projection`. **A primitive-type split is not a provenance
boundary.**

Verified failure, real pack, `spell:fireball`:
`data.mechanics.saves[0]` is `{ability: 'dexterity', damageOnSuccess: 'half'}`.
Both are importer-derived typed projection values. Both are strings. Both are
therefore presented to the DM under "verbatim; authoritative". The same class
covers typed string arrays, enum-like fields, and dice/damage strings, while a
mixed-type projection object is split across BOTH headings.

ADR 0020 and design section 7.2 require source prose and typed projections to
stay distinct, and forbid a projection from carrying source authority.

## Constraints on the fix

- **No field-name allow/deny list.** A growing list of leaf names
  (`ability`, `dice`, `damageOnSuccess`, …) is not a provenance boundary either
  and is explicitly rejected by the review.
- **Verified constraint:** `RulesRecord.data` is typed `unknown` and the pack
  carries NO per-field provenance (`packages/core/src/rules/types.ts:127`). You
  cannot read an existing boundary. W10 must ESTABLISH one and state it.
- **The producer owns it, not the renderer.** `PacketCandidate` must carry the
  distinction so it is durable in the evidence and measurable, rather than
  re-guessed at render time. Changing the packet shape is in scope and expected.

## The decided approach

The rules-pack compiler emits its derived material into declared projection
CONTAINERS; everything else in a record body is source-extracted. Establish
that boundary once, explicitly, and apply it RECURSIVELY by path:

- Declare the projection containers in ONE named constant with a comment
  explaining that this is W10's stated boundary, that the pack declares no
  per-field provenance of its own, and that the constant is a container rule
  and not a leaf-name list. The containers present in the corpus are
  `mechanics`, `upcast` and `executionReadiness` — VERIFY that against the pack
  before you rely on it, and say in your notes what you actually found.
- The rule is positional, not top-level-only: at any depth, a key that names a
  projection container makes everything beneath it projection. This is what
  makes `creature:adult-black-dragon` `data.actions[5]` split correctly —
  `actions[5].text` is source prose, `actions[5].mechanics` is projection.
- Everything not under a projection container is source material.
- **Residue is disclosed, not guessed.** If the walk meets a shape the rule
  cannot classify, it is reported in band rather than silently assigned. Do not
  invent a third silent default.

`data.mechanics.scaling.sourceText` quotes source text from INSIDE a
projection. It stays under projection — its value is still rendered verbatim,
correctly labelled as the projection's record of what it derived from. Do not
special-case it out; special-casing it is the beginning of the leaf-name list

title: Repair F3/F4/F5: retry trace fidelity, v2 effect lifecycle admission, M12 deep equality
description:
Repair dispatch for PR #543 review findings **F3, F4 and F5** (`eshyra-o9bd.19.12`,
ADR 0020 W10). Parent authority: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.12` — its notes carry
the full review and the integrating agent's verification of each finding.

WORKTREE `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.12.7`, BRANCH `eshyra-o9bd.19.12.7`, cut
from `eshyra-o9bd.19.12`. Dependencies installed. Touch nothing outside it.

Sibling dispatches own F1 and F2. Do NOT touch
`packages/core/src/discovery/signals.ts`, `packet.ts`, or `packetMessage.ts`.

---

## F3 — `retrieved_context` is false on an auditor-retry turn

**The defect.** `orchestrator.ts` computes `baseUserMessage` once, then on an
audit retry calls `runModelLoop` with `baseUserMessage + '\n\n' + correctiveNote`.
After acceptance the trace persists `retrievedContext: [baseUserMessage]`. So
the accepted narration and tool calls can describe attempt 2 while the
persisted input describes the pre-correction context. This PR's own comment on
`TurnTraceRecord.discoveryShadow`/`retrievedContext` now claims the field is
the message the model actually received, which makes the comment a false
statement rather than merely an omission.

**The repair.** Record the input the ACCEPTED attempt actually received.

Read `orchestrator.ts` around the attempt loop and `runModelLoop`'s call sites
first. Capture the exact user message used for the attempt that is accepted —
at the same place the accepted candidate's `narration` and `toolCalls` are
taken — and persist that. Do not reconstruct it afterwards by re-concatenating
`baseUserMessage` with the last corrective note: a reconstruction is a second
account of the input that can disagree with the one actually sent, which is
the defect in a new form. Record what was passed.

Every accepted attempt following one or more rejections is affected. Do not
special-case a single corrective note.

Keep `baseUserMessage` as the exact prefix property intact: the assembled
context is still a prefix of whatever the accepted attempt received, and the
packet still sits where injection put it.

**Evidence (`shadowRuntime.test.ts`, beside the existing intervene cases):**
- An `intervene` turn with a first-attempt audit REJECTION and second-attempt
  acceptance: capture the provider-neutral `ModelCompleteInput` the accepted
  attempt actually received (the scripted model already records `seen`), reread
  the trace out of SQLite, and assert `retrieved_context[0]` equals that exact
  string — including the corrective note.
- Assert in the same test that `delivery.renderedSha256` still equals the
  SHA-256 of the packet portion of that recorded message, so the binding
  survives the repair.
- A two-rejection case if the auditor's retry budget allows it; if it does not,
  say so explicitly in your notes rather than silently testing only one.
- The existing no-retry intervene case must still hold.

---

## F4 — the v2 reader admits impossible accepted-state-effect lifecycles

**The defect.** `RuntimeStateEffect` is by contract an effect of the ACCEPTED
candidate: a rejected attempt's writes roll back and contribute no event. The
reader already derives the real candidate-attempt count and constrains
capability invocations to attempts `1..attemptCount` (see `checkAudit`'s return
value and its use). `runtime.stateEffects` is constrained only to a
non-negative integer `attempt`, so it admits `0`, out-of-range attempts, and
effects attributed to a rejected attempt. `measureAcceptedStateEffect` then
pairs effects without consulting attempt identity, so malformed rejected-attempt
evidence can satisfy an accepted-turn expectation.

(The weak rule came from the parent bead's own spec. It is wrong; fix it.)

**The repair, in `shadow.ts`'s `assertV2`.** Apply the SAME lifecycle
constraint the capability events get, plus the constraints that follow from
`stateEffects` being one accepted attempt's stream:

- `attempt` is an integer in `1..attemptCount`, where `attemptCount` is the
  value the audit lifecycle already yields — reuse it, do not recompute it.
- All recorded effects share ONE attempt. They come from a single accepted
  candidate; two different attempt numbers in one array is an impossible
  producer output.
- `ordinal` values are the canonical positions of that one stream: integers
  starting at 0, strictly increasing, with no duplicates and no gaps.

Fail closed with `DiscoveryShadowSchemaError` in the established style. Keep the
validator's declared-here-not-imported discipline.

**Evidence (`shadowEvidenceIntegrity.test.ts`, beside the existing
`accepted state effects` block):** reject each of — `attempt: 0`; an attempt
above the row's real candidate count; two effects with different attempts;
duplicate ordinals; a gap in ordinals; descending ordinals. Admit the
well-formed multi-effect stream. Each case must install an otherwise valid
effect stream first so no rejection passes vacuously.

---

## F5 — M12's argument comparison is not structural equality

**The defect.** `measureAcceptedStateEffect` compares declared argument values
with `JSON.stringify(a) === JSON.stringify(b)`. Two structurally equal nested
objects whose keys were inserted in different orders therefore disagree. The
contract says each declared expected argument field DEEP-EQUALS the executed
value. P8's current expectation is flat strings and never exercises this.

**The repair, in `measurements.ts`.** Replace the stringify comparison with a
real structural deep equality: key-order-independent for objects, order- AND
length-significant for arrays, exact for primitives (including the
`null`/`undefined` distinction and `NaN` if you handle numbers generically).
Keep it small and local; do not add a dependency.

**Evidence (`stateEffectMeasurement.test.ts`):** nested objects with reordered
keys agree; arrays in a different order DISAGREE; a nested field with a
different value disagrees and names the top-level declared field; a declared
nested field absent from the executed args disagrees; extra executed keys
inside a declared nested object — decide deliberately whether the subset rule
recurses, state your decision in the doc comment and the bead notes, and test
the behaviour you chose.

---

## Non-negotiables

- `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing.
- Biome is canonical; CI fails on warnings. Do not suppress a finding.
- Do not weaken, skip, or reshape any existing test to make these pass. If an
  existing test encodes the old wrong behaviour, changing it is correct — name
  every such change and why in your notes.
- Do not edit `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, anything under `.claude/`, or the design
  document.
- House style: read the doc comments in `discovery/types.ts` and `shadow.ts`
  and match them. Every non-obvious shape says WHY it has that form and what
  wrong thing the form makes unrepresentable. Never store a fact twice in two
  shapes that could disagree.
- Known flake: `packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts > packs publishable tarballs`
  intermittently times out at 10s under full-suite load. Pre-existing, filed,
  unrelated. Confirm with `npx vitest run packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts`, note
  it, do not fix it. Any other failure is yours.

description:

sections 12.3, 13.1, 13.3). Parent authority: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.12`, and

from `eshyra-o9bd.19.12` AFTER dispatches 1 and 2 merged into it. Dependencies
are installed. Touch nothing outside it.

depends on already exists on your base branch:

- `packages/core/src/discovery/packetMessage.ts` —
  `renderContextPacketMessage(trace): RenderedContextPacket` (dispatch 1). Read

STOP and report it in your notes rather than reimplementing it.

## Code survey (read before writing)

- `packages/core/src/orchestrator/orchestrator.ts:163-171` — the
  `recordDiscoveryShadow` dep and its doc comment; `:806-838` — the Phase 2 seam
  between `assembleContext` and `renderContextMessage`, where `baseUserMessage`

- `packages/core/src/orchestrator/contextAssembler.ts:982` —
  `renderContextMessage`: the sections and their joining (`\n\n`).
- `packages/core/src/model/client.ts:158-182` — `ModelCompleteInput`. This is
  the ADR 0010 provider-neutral seam: `messages` is what every adapter family
  receives identically.
- `docs/adr/0010-api-native-vs-agent-harness-model-adapter-seam.md` — read
  decisions 1 and 2. "Provider-neutral" in this bead means the packet reaches
  the model through the shared `ModelClient` surface, never through one
  provider's agent loop, system-prompt shaping, or MCP channel.

  `../discovery/shadow.js` and `../discovery/types.js`. Do not widen this list.
  Route the renderer through `shadow.js`.
- `packages/core/src/memory/turnTrace.ts:55-65` — the `discoveryShadow` column
  comment, which currently states that nothing in the column reached the DM.

## Deliverable 1 — the mode, as a union

Replace `RunTurnDeps.recordDiscoveryShadow?: boolean` with

```ts
discoveryMode?: 'off' | 'shadow' | 'intervene';   // default 'off'
```

and update every caller and test. Two booleans would make
`{shadow: false, intervene: true}` representable and meaningless; this codebase
consistently prefers a union that makes an impossible state unrepresentable, and
the three states really are exclusive. `'off'` runs no discovery at all.
`'shadow'` keeps W9's contract exactly: discovery observes, records, and
injects nothing, and the DM message stays byte-identical with `'off'`.
`'intervene'` observes, records, AND injects.

Write the doc comment to say that `'intervene'` is the first mode in which the
DM's input differs, that it is an experiment and not part of released play, and
that packet presence is never evidence the model used the material (§12.3).

## Deliverable 2 — the intervention entry point, inside `shadow.ts`

The orchestrator must not gain a new discovery import. Add to `shadow.ts`:

```ts
export interface DiscoveryInterventionCapture {
  readonly capture: DiscoveryShadowCapture;
  /** Absent when the capture failed, so nothing can be injected. */
  readonly rendered?: RenderedContextPacket;
}
export function captureDiscoveryIntervention(
  input: ShadowDiscoveryInput,
): DiscoveryInterventionCapture;
```

It runs the SAME capture path as `captureDiscoveryShadow` and then renders the
packet. It must be as total and failure-tolerant as the shadow capture is: a
render failure is recorded as a capture failure and injects nothing, and never
propagates into the turn. An observation point that can abort a player's turn is
worse than no observation point — that reasoning is already in `shadow.ts`'s
header and applies with more force once the packet is load-bearing.

To render, `captureDiscoveryIntervention` needs the LIVE `DiscoveryTrace`, not
the projection. Restructure the shared capture so both entry points build the
live trace once and project it once; do not run discovery twice, and do not
render from the projection.

## Deliverable 3 — injection, through the shared model seam

In `orchestrator.ts`, when the mode is `'intervene'` and a rendered packet
exists, the DM's user message becomes the base message plus the rendered packet
appended as a further section, joined exactly as `renderContextMessage` joins
its own sections (`\n\n`).

Three hard requirements:

1. **Additive, never rewriting.** The base message must survive as an exact
   prefix of the injected message. Discovery does not edit, reorder, or filter
   what the context assembler produced.
2. **One message, one seam.** Injection happens by composing the string handed
   to `ModelCompleteInput.messages`. Do NOT put it in `system`, do NOT change
   the tool definitions, do NOT touch `buildSystemPrompt`, and do NOT add a
   provider-conditional branch anywhere.
3. **The trace records what was actually sent.** `retrievedContext` at
   `:1145` currently re-calls `renderContextMessage(assembled)`, which would
   record the base message while the DM received the injected one. Record the
   message that was actually sent. This also means the injected text is durably
   recorded exactly once — do not store a second copy in the discovery
   evidence.

## Deliverable 4 — the delivery record, extending v2

Dispatch 2 introduced `discovery-shadow-v2`. Extend it; do NOT bump again.
Add a required field to `DiscoveryShadowEvidence`:

```ts
export type ShadowDelivery =
  | { readonly mode: 'observed'; readonly injected: false }
  | {
      readonly mode: 'intervened';
      readonly injected: true;
      readonly renderedBytes: number;
      /** SHA-256 of the rendered packet text, binding this evidence to the
       *  message recorded in `turn_trace.retrieved_context`. */
      readonly renderedSha256: string;
      readonly candidateCount: number;
      readonly mustConsiderOverflow: readonly RetentionOverflow[];
    }
  | { readonly mode: 'intervened'; readonly injected: false; readonly reason: string };

readonly delivery: ShadowDelivery;
```

The third arm is the honest one and is the reason this is a union rather than a
boolean plus optional fields: intervention was requested but the capture or the
render failed, so nothing was injected, and the reason is recorded. A reader
must never have to infer "did the DM actually get this?" from whether an
optional field happens to be present.

Extend the fail-closed reader to admit `delivery` and reject every malformed
arm, in the same declared-here-not-imported style the existing validator uses.

Update the `discoveryShadow` column comment in
`packages/core/src/memory/turnTrace.ts`: the claim that nothing in the column
reached the DM is no longer unconditionally true, and the comment must now point
at `delivery` as the field that says which it was.

## Deliverable 6 — keep W9's guarantees intact

`'shadow'` mode must remain byte-identical to `'off'`. The existing parity test
in `shadowRuntime.test.ts` proves that for the old boolean; port it to the mode
union and ADD the complementary assertion that `'intervene'` is NOT byte-
identical — a parity test that would pass in all three modes proves nothing
about the mode that matters.

## Non-negotiables

- `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing.
- Biome is canonical; CI fails on warnings. Do not suppress a finding.
- Do not weaken, skip, or reshape any existing test, and do not widen
  `SHADOW_SEAM_MODULES` in `discoveryBoundary.test.ts`.
- Do not edit `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, or anything under `.claude/`.
- No ADR and no new design-document section is authorized here. If you believe
  the design is wrong, record it with
  `bd update eshyra-o9bd.19.12.3 --append-notes` and file a follow-up with
  `bd create`.

## Scope boundary for this dispatch

You deliver the SEAM (deliverables 1-4 and 6). A sibling dispatch
(`eshyra-o9bd.19.12.4`) owns the intervention evidence suite
`packages/core/test/discovery/packetIntervention.test.ts` and runs after you.
Do not create that file.

You still owe evidence for the seam ITSELF, in the suites that already own
these surfaces:

S1. `shadowRuntime.test.ts` — the ported parity test: `'shadow'` mode leaves the
    whole model input byte-identical with `'off'`, AND `'intervene'` does NOT.
    A parity test that passed in all three modes would prove nothing about the
    mode that matters.
S2. `shadowRuntime.test.ts` — an intervention turn's model input contains the
    shadow turn's rendered context as an exact PREFIX, and the remainder is the
    rendered packet text. Injection is additive; it never rewrites what the
    context assembler produced.
S3. `shadowRuntime.test.ts` — `turn_trace.retrieved_context` for an
    intervention turn equals the message the model actually received, not the
    base message. Recording the base message while the DM got the injected one
    would make the trace lie about the turn.
S4. `shadowEvidenceIntegrity.test.ts` — the v2 reader admits each valid
    `delivery` arm and rejects every malformed one, including the shape that
    claims `mode: 'intervened'` with `injected: true` while omitting the
    rendered identity, and an `injected: false` intervened arm with no reason.
S5. `shadowRuntime.test.ts` — a capture FAILURE under `'intervene'` injects
    nothing, records the third `delivery` arm with its reason, and does not
    fail the turn. An observation point that can abort a player's turn is worse
    than no observation point.

title: Dispatch: M12 accepted deterministic state-effect evidence and measurement (attempt 1)
description:
Dispatch 2 of 3 for W10 (`eshyra-o9bd.19.12`, ADR 0020 transition design
section 13.1 M12, section 11 fixture contract). Parent authority:
`bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.12`, and
`docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md`.

WORKTREE `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.12.2`, BRANCH `eshyra-o9bd.19.12.2`, cut
from `eshyra-o9bd.19.12`. Dependencies are installed. Touch nothing outside it.

## What this dispatch delivers, and nothing more

M12 — accepted deterministic state-effect agreement — end to end: the canonical
runtime event, its durable admission, the measurement, and the machine-
comparable fixture expectation it is measured against. It does NOT inject a
packet, does NOT render a packet, and does NOT create the intervention seam.
Those are dispatches 1 and 3. Do not create
`packages/core/src/discovery/packetMessage.ts`; another agent owns that file on
a parallel branch.

## Why M12 does not exist yet

Design §13.1 defines **M12** as *accepted state-effect agreement* — "whether the
accepted deterministic state effect matches the fixture's expectation
(including the expectation that there is none)". §13.3 admits M1–M11 at Phase 2
and M1–M12 from Phase 3, and Erratum 1 (§9.6) confirms M12, not M11, is the
deterministic-agreement measurement B3 gates. W9 shipped M1–M11. M12 is
missing, and it is the measurement that separates Phase 3 from Phase 2.

Two things block it today:

1. **No canonical accepted-state-effect event.** `turn_trace.accepted_state_delta`
   (`packages/core/src/orchestrator/turnTraceProjection.ts:138-153`) records the
   mutating calls' ARGS but drops the tool name for every tool except
   `spend_spell_slot`, and carries no attempt number. An anonymous args blob
   cannot be compared with an expectation.
2. **The fixture expectation is prose.** `DeterministicStateEffect` in
   `packages/core/test/diagnostics/fixtureContract.ts` carries only `statement`
   and `evidence`. Prose is not comparable. Design amendment 11.1 already set
   the precedent for this exact defect class: field 9 held material M9 could
   not measure, and the fix was to narrow the CONTRACT, not to add
   classification logic inside the measurement.

## Code survey (verified at 71c322f, read these before writing)

- `packages/core/src/discovery/types.ts` — `RuntimeCapabilityInvocation` and
  `RuntimeAudit`. These are the two existing canonical runtime event shapes and
  their doc comments state the doctrine you must follow: an event is recorded
  at the boundary where it happens, is structurally complete or is rejected at
  the durable read boundary, and is never reconstructed later from state.
- `packages/core/src/discovery/measurements.ts:509-655` —
  `RuntimeDiscoveryObservations`, `RuntimeDiscoveryMeasurements`,
  `measureRuntimeDiscovery`, and the `IncomparableReason` doctrine (a refusal to
  compare is never reported as a disagreement).
- `packages/core/src/discovery/shadow.ts:266-315` —
  `ObservedCapabilityInvocation` and `runtimeCapabilityInvocation()`: the exact
  pattern for "the runtime hands an observation in structurally, discovery owns
  the durable projection, the orchestrator imports nothing from discovery except

```ts
export interface ExpectedStateEffectOperation {
  readonly tool: string;
  /** Argument fields that must match exactly on the paired accepted call.
   *  A subset: fields absent here are not compared. */
  readonly args?: Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>;

      readonly operations: readonly ExpectedStateEffectOperation[];

export interface StateEffectMeasurement {
  readonly expectation: 'none' | 'effect';
  readonly expectedOperations: readonly ExpectedStateEffectOperation[];
  readonly acceptedEffects: readonly RuntimeStateEffect[];
```

title: Dispatch: provider-neutral context-packet renderer (attempt 1)
description:
Dispatch 1 of 3 for W10 (`eshyra-o9bd.19.12`, ADR 0020 transition design section
7 and 12.3). Parent authority: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.12`, and
`docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md`
sections 7.1, 7.2, 7.3.

WORKTREE `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.12.1`, BRANCH `eshyra-o9bd.19.12.1`, cut
from `eshyra-o9bd.19.12`. Dependencies are installed. Touch nothing outside it.

## What this dispatch delivers, and nothing more

The provider-neutral RENDERER that turns a built context packet into the text a
DM would actually receive, plus its unit tests. It is a pure function over an
already-built packet. It does NOT inject anything, does NOT touch the
orchestrator, does NOT touch `shadow.ts`, `measurements.ts`, `packet.ts`,
`retention.ts`, or any test under `packages/core/test/discovery/` other than a
new file of your own. Injection is dispatch 3's job; M12 is dispatch 2's.

## Code survey (verified at 71c322f, read these before writing)

- `packages/core/src/discovery/types.ts` — `ContextPacket`, `PacketCandidate`,
  `ProjectionLimitNote`, `CapabilityPreflight`, `DiscoveryRoute`,
  `TypedTraversal`, `RetentionOverflow`, `DiscoveryTrace`.
- `packages/core/src/discovery/packet.ts:285-432` — how `packetCandidate()`
  fills each field. Note especially: for a rules record `sourceProse` is
  `{ data: <the whole record.data object> }`; for an adventure entity it is the
  entity object itself. `identity.kind` is the record kind or the literal
  `'adventure-entity'`.
- `packages/core/src/discovery/packet.ts:117-164` — the three
  `ProjectionLimitNote` kinds (`success-branch`, `area`,
  `execution-readiness`), each carrying `note`, `evidence` and
  `preservedProse`.
- `packages/core/src/campaign/campaignRules.ts:101-121` —
  `CampaignRuleProjection` / `CampaignRulingProjection` fields. These are
  `eshyra-jhpt`-owned. Read them; never redefine them, never declare a local
  rule or ruling shape (design section 8.4; the analyzer in
  `packages/core/test/discovery/support/discoveryOwnership.ts` enforces it and
  WILL fail you).
- `packages/core/src/rules/types.ts` — `RulesAmbiguity` (`id`, `question`,
  `interpretations[]`, `canonicalResolution`, always `null` in the pack).
- `packages/core/src/orchestrator/contextAssembler.ts:982` —
  `renderContextMessage`, for house style: `## Section` headings joined by
  blank lines, `- ` bullets, no JSON dumps of prose.
- `packages/core/src/discovery/traceDerivation.ts:260-405` — the derived trace
  shape carrying `retention.overflow` and `packet.byteOverflow`. Your input
  type must be satisfied by BOTH the live `DiscoveryTrace` and this derived
  trace.

## The deliverable

New file `packages/core/src/discovery/packetMessage.ts`, exporting:

```ts
export interface RenderablePacketTrace {
  readonly retention: { readonly overflow: readonly RetentionOverflow[] };
  readonly packet: {
    readonly packet: ContextPacket;
    readonly byteOverflow: readonly RetentionOverflow[];
    readonly dropped: readonly {
      readonly candidateKey: string;
      readonly band: CandidateBand;
      readonly routes: readonly DiscoveryRoute[];
      readonly reason: string;
    }[];
  };
}

export interface RenderedContextPacket {
  readonly text: string;
  readonly bytes: number;           // Buffer.byteLength(text, 'utf8')
  readonly candidateCount: number;
  /** Every must-consider candidate a budget could not hold, from BOTH budgets. */
  readonly mustConsiderOverflow: readonly RetentionOverflow[];
  /** Design section 12.3: presence is never evidence of use. Always null. */
  readonly modelUsageClaim: null;
}

export function renderContextPacketMessage(
  trace: RenderablePacketTrace,
): RenderedContextPacket;
```

Add both types and the function to `packages/core/src/internal.ts` beside the
existing `buildContextPacket` export. Do NOT add them to the root
`packages/core/src/index.ts` (AGENTS.md: new core symbols default to internal).

## What the rendered text must contain, and why

Design section 7.1 lists the required per-candidate content. Every one of these
must appear in the TEXT, not merely be reachable in the object — the text is
what a DM receives.

Per retained candidate, in packet order:

1. **Identity** — `key`, `kind`, `name`.
2. **Provenance** — `sourceRef`, `locator` when present, `source` label, and
   the licence identity. A rules-record candidate whose `provenance.sourceRef`
   is empty must be rendered with an explicit `unattributed` marker rather than
   an empty field; design section 7.3 forbids presenting a record as
   authoritative merely because it was retrieved, and M8's standing structural
   check is exactly "reached the packet carrying no source attribution".
3. **Source prose, VERBATIM.** Walk `sourceProse` and emit every string-valued
   leaf as RAW TEXT under its JSON pointer path. Do not `JSON.stringify` a
   string leaf: an escaped `\"` or `\n` is no longer the source text, and the
   fixture corpus's field-9 `exactSubstring` facts are matched against what the
   DM can read. Non-string leaves (the typed projections) are rendered
   separately under a heading that states plainly that they do not replace the
   prose above.
4. **Every retrieval route** — route class AND the trigger detail for each.
5. **Traversed relationships** — source record, link field, relation, target,
   one line each.
6. **Known source ambiguity** — `id`, `question`, every interpretation id, and
   the canonical resolution stated as absent when `canonicalResolution` is
   null. Never present an interpretation as the answer.
7. **Applicable campaign rules and rulings** — for each, the identity, kind,
   scope, provenance, effective position, and supersession status
   (`supersededBy` / `revokedPosition` rendered explicitly, including when they
   are null), plus the governing record keys and the prose when present, and
   for a ruling its ambiguity id and selected interpretation id. The governing
   source material stays present and attributed beside them — that is satisfied
   by rendering rules inside their candidate's block, never in a detached list.
8. **Deterministic capability.** When `capability` is present, render it as a
   POSITIVE BOUNDED CONTRACT: the operation, the capability id, the revision,
   the status, the required inputs, the explicit exclusions, and the residual
   DM interpretation. When `capability` is absent, render exactly the negative
   form the parent bead requires: no capability was positively selected, AND an
   explicit statement that this is not a claim that the record has no
   mechanics, that it is irrelevant, or that it is safe to ignore. Never infer
   a capability from the presence of typed fields.
9. **Projection limits, in band.** Each `ProjectionLimitNote` must be rendered
   INSIDE its own candidate's block, adjacent to the typed projection it
   qualifies — not collected into a trailing appendix. A partial projection
   whose limits are disclosed three hundred lines away is not disclosed in
   band, and design section 7.2's two worked cases
   (`creature:adult-black-dragon` `/data/actions/5` success branch and area;
   `spell:fireball` missing typed area) are the cases this must hold for.

Packet-level, once:

10. **Must-consider overflow.** Concatenate `retention.overflow` and
    `packet.byteOverflow`. If non-empty, the text must carry an explicit
    overflow section naming EVERY dropped must-consider candidate, each of its
    routes, and the reason recorded by the producer. A must-consider candidate
    never disappears silently.
11. **Other drops.** Every `packet.dropped` entry whose band is not
    `must-consider` is rendered with its candidate key and the producer's
    recorded reason. Reasons are the producer's strings; never author a
    replacement reason here.

Explicitly NOT in the text:

- No coverage figure, completeness figure, readiness score, or candidate
  percentage. No "N of M rules found". Design section 13.2.
- No statement that the material was, will be, or should be used, and no
  instruction that presence implies relevance. `modelUsageClaim` stays `null`
  on the value and no equivalent claim appears in the prose.
- No re-ordering, summarizing, truncating, or paraphrasing of source prose. If
  a record's prose is long, it is long.

## Structural rules for the implementation

- The renderer is TOTAL and pure: no I/O, no `Date`, no randomness, no reads of
  the db or the pack. Same input, byte-identical output.
- An empty packet (`candidates: []`) with no drops and no overflow renders a
  block that says the run retained nothing, not an empty string. Design section
  13.3 forbids a green-looking nothing; a caller must be able to tell "the
  renderer produced nothing" from "discovery retained nothing".
- `bytes` is the UTF-8 byte length of `text`. It is NOT `ContextPacket.bytes`
  (which counts the serialized JSON) and must not be copied from it.
- Derive `mustConsiderOverflow` from the two producer lists. Do not recompute a
  band, do not re-derive an exclusion from "absent from `candidates`". W9's
  canonical-events doctrine applies: a reason you did not receive is a reason
  you may not invent.

E2. **In-band limits.** For both worked cases, assert the projection-limit note

title: Dispatch: implement Captain seat routing, handoff tooling, and regression matrix (attempt 1)
description:
Implement the repo-local half of eshyra-kusc. The design is fixed; implement it
exactly. Do not redesign, do not widen scope, do not touch anything outside this
worktree.

Read eshyra-kusc for objective, category model, and acceptance criteria.

=== VOCABULARY ===

Two durable seats: "Claude Captain" (id claude-captain) and "Codex Captain"
(id codex-captain). A seat is a durable organizational role; "main session" is
only a harness/runtime classification and one eligibility condition. Never emit
the strings "Claude-main" or "Codex-main".

Three layers compose at startup: charter (durable, user-local, personal) +
live repository authority (unchanged, everyone gets it) + advisory predecessor
handoff. Only the middle layer is authority.

=== FILES TO CREATE ===

1. scripts/seats/seatContext.mjs   (shared library, ESM, no dependencies)
2. scripts/seats/claude-captain-context.mjs  (Claude Code SessionStart hook)
3. scripts/seats/codex-captain-context.mjs   (Codex CLI SessionStart hook)
4. scripts/seats/seat-handoff.mjs            (handoff CLI)
5. scripts/seats/install-captain-seats.mjs   (user-local installer/verifier)
6. packages/core/test/captainSeats.test.ts   (regression matrix)
7. docs/agent-captain-seats.md               (concise operator doc)

FILES TO EDIT

8. .claude/settings.json  - register hook 3 lines below
9. package.json (root)    - two npm scripts
10. AGENTS.md             - one short neutral subsection (exact text below)

=== 1. scripts/seats/seatContext.mjs ===

Named exports:

  CAPTAIN_MODEL_PATTERN = /fable|opus/i

  SEATS = { claudeCaptain: 'claude-captain', codexCaptain: 'codex-captain' }

  readHookInput(raw) -> object | null
    JSON.parse a string; return null on any parse failure or when the result is
    not a non-null, non-array object. Never throw.

  classifyClaudeSession(input) -> { eligible: boolean, reason: string }
    Fail closed. Ineligible, with these exact reason strings, checked in order:
      'malformed-input'      input is null (per readHookInput)
      'subagent'             input.agent_id is truthy
      'resume'               input.source === 'resume'
      'no-model-identity'    typeof input.model !== 'string' || model is empty
      'unauthorized-model'   !CAPTAIN_MODEL_PATTERN.test(input.model)
    Otherwise { eligible: true, reason: 'authorized-main-session' }.

  classifyCodexSession(input, env) -> { eligible, reason }
    Fail closed. Ineligible, exact reasons, in order:
      'malformed-input'      input is null
      'dispatched-worker'    env.ESHYRA_SEAT_ROLE is a non-empty string other
                             than 'captain', OR env.ESHYRA_DISPATCH_CHILD is a
                             non-empty string
      'subagent'             input.agent_type is a non-empty string
      'wrong-event'          input.hook_event_name is present and !== 'SessionStart'
      'resume'               input.source === 'resume'
    Otherwise { eligible: true, reason: 'captain-profile-session' }.
    NOTE: Codex Captain occupancy is gated primarily by WHICH CONFIG LAYER
    registers this hook (a profile overlay the dispatch path never loads), so
    this function is defence in depth, not the only boundary. Say so in a
    comment. Do not add model-name, cwd-basename, branch-name, bead-title, or
    permission-mode tests: they are explicitly rejected as identity signals.

  resolveSeatRoots(cwd, env) -> { charterDir, stateDir, mode } | null
    If env.ESHYRA_SEAT_TEST_ROOT is a non-empty string:
      charterDir = <root>/charters, stateDir = <root>/state, mode = 'test'.
    Otherwise:
      charterDir depends on the seat, so return charterDir = null here and let
      resolveCharterPath compute it; stateDir is
        <git common dir>/eshyra-seats
      resolved by running `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` with cwd, then
      making it absolute. Return null if cwd is missing, is not a directory, or
      git fails. mode = 'repo'. Use node:child_process execFileSync with
      stdio pipe and a short timeout; never throw out of this function.

  resolveCharterPath(seatId, env) -> string
    test mode:  <ESHYRA_SEAT_TEST_ROOT>/charters/<seatId>.md
    claude-captain: <homedir>/.claude/seats/claude-captain.md
    codex-captain:  <homedir>/.codex/seats/codex-captain.md

  readCharter(seatId, env) -> string | null   (null when absent/unreadable/blank)

  readHandoff(seatId, cwd, env) -> { text, path, ageHours } | null
    Reads <stateDir>/<seatId>/handoff.md. null when roots unresolvable, file
    absent, unreadable, or blank. ageHours = (now - mtimeMs)/3600000, rounded
    to one decimal.

  RECONCILIATION_BLOCK  (exported constant string, used verbatim by both hooks)
    Must start with the line '### Reconcile before acting' and must state, in
    prose: that everything in the handoff is a lead and not a fact; that the
    occupant must re-derive current work from live state before acting; and it
    must name each of these check targets explicitly by these words - 'beads',
    'branch', 'worktree', 'Git ancestry', 'commits', 'pull request', 'dispatch
    registry', 'recorded PGID', 'process identity'. It must state that a
    handoff is never permission to kill a process, reset a branch, force-push,
    merge, or discard a commit without live verification.

  renderSeatContext({ seatId, seatTitle, harness, charter, handoff, occupant })
    -> string
    Emits, in this order, and omitting nothing:
      '<!-- eshyra-seat: <seatId> -->'
      '# <seatTitle> - standing seat'      (use an em dash, not a hyphen)
      charter text
      '## Occupant (runtime metadata, not seat identity)' followed by a bullet
        list: seat, harness, model, session, started (ISO 8601 from Date.now).
        Missing values render as 'unknown'. Add one line stating that occupant
        metadata never confers seat identity and that capability is not
        inherited from a predecessor.
      '## Predecessor handoff (advisory - not authority)'  (em dash)
        Either the handoff text plus a line 'Recorded <ageHours>h ago at
        <path>.', or exactly 'No handoff recorded for this seat.'
      RECONCILIATION_BLOCK

=== 2. scripts/seats/claude-captain-context.mjs ===

Executable ESM script, shebang '#!/usr/bin/env node'.
Reads all of stdin (fd 0) as utf8; on any read error exit 0 silently.
Guard process.stdout against EPIPE exactly as .claude/hooks/supervisor-context.mjs does.
input = readHookInput(raw); c = classifyClaudeSession(input).
If !c.eligible -> exit 0 with NO output.
charter = readCharter('claude-captain', process.env); if null -> exit 0 with NO
output (absent seat state degrades to ordinary repository behaviour).
Else write renderSeatContext(...) with seatTitle 'Claude Captain', harness
'Claude Code', occupant model/session from input.model / input.session_id, and
handoff = readHandoff('claude-captain', input.cwd ?? process.cwd(), process.env).
Never let a handoff read failure prevent charter emission.

=== 3. scripts/seats/codex-captain-context.mjs ===

Same shape, using classifyCodexSession(input, process.env), seat
'codex-captain', seatTitle 'Codex Captain', harness 'Codex CLI'.
Additional guard, applied only when ESHYRA_SEAT_TEST_ROOT is NOT set: the
session cwd must resolve to a checkout that looks like Eshyra - the directory
containing the git common dir must contain BOTH 'AGENTS.md' and
'.beads/metadata.json'. If not, exit 0 with no output (reason 'not-eshyra-repo').

=== 4. scripts/seats/seat-handoff.mjs ===

CLI: node scripts/seats/seat-handoff.mjs <command> <seat>
  path <seat>          print the resolved handoff path
  show <seat>          print current handoff text plus its age, or a notice
  write <seat>         read markdown from stdin and write it (mkdir -p first),
                       prefixed with a single line
                       '<!-- recorded <ISO> -->'; refuse empty stdin (exit 2)
  clear <seat>         delete the handoff file if present
Unknown seat or command -> usage on stderr, exit 2.
Seat ids accepted: claude-captain, codex-captain. Nothing else.

=== 5. scripts/seats/install-captain-seats.mjs ===

Idempotent installer for the USER-LOCAL Codex pieces only. It must never write
inside the repository and never overwrite a file without first copying it to
'<path>.bak.<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS>'.
  --check   report status of every managed path and exit 1 if any is missing or
            differs from what would be installed; write nothing
  (default) install/refresh
Managed paths (compute the repo root from this script's own location):
  ~/.codex/seats/codex-captain-context.sh   POSIX sh shim, mode 0755, which
      reads the hook payload on stdin, extracts .cwd with node, resolves the
      git common dir from it, and execs
      'node <repo>/scripts/seats/codex-captain-context.mjs' with the payload
      piped back in; it must exit 0 silently on every failure path. Keep this
      shim byte-stable: Codex hashes the hook COMMAND STRING for hook trust, so
      the config must invoke this fixed path and the shim absorbs all change.
  ~/.codex/eshyra-captain.config.toml       profile overlay registering
      [[hooks.SessionStart]] with matcher "" and one command hook invoking the
      shim above, statusMessage 'Loading Codex Captain seat'.
  ~/.local/bin/codex-captain                mode 0755 wrapper: refuses with a
      clear message and exit 1 when ESHYRA_SEAT_ROLE is set to anything other
      than 'captain'; otherwise
      'exec env ESHYRA_SEAT_ROLE=captain codex -p eshyra-captain \"$@\"'.
It must NOT create or modify the charters (~/.claude/seats/claude-captain.md,
~/.codex/seats/codex-captain.md); it only reports whether they exist.
It must NOT modify ~/.codex/config.toml or ~/.claude/settings.json.
Print every path it touched and the backup it made.

=== 6. packages/core/test/captainSeats.test.ts ===

Vitest. Follow the style of packages/core/test/beadLifecyclePolicy.test.ts
(a leading comment naming the bead and why the evidence is permanent).
Run the REAL scripts as child processes:
  execFileSync(process.execPath, [scriptPath], { input: JSON.stringify(payload),
    env: { ...process.env, ESHYRA_SEAT_TEST_ROOT: tmp, ...overrides },
    encoding: 'utf8' })
Build a temp root per suite with mkdtempSync containing charters/ and state/
fixtures. Delete ESHYRA_SEAT_ROLE and ESHYRA_DISPATCH_CHILD from the base env
so an ambient value cannot mask a case. Cover exactly these, one test each:

CLAUDE
  1  model 'claude-opus-5', source startup  -> emits '<!-- eshyra-seat: claude-captain -->'
  2  model 'Fable 5.1'                      -> emits it
  3  Opus and Fable payloads also make .claude/hooks/supervisor-context.mjs
     emit its overlay (run that script too; assert its output contains
     'You are the supervising agent')
  4  model 'claude-sonnet-5'  -> claude-captain script emits NOTHING, and

  6  malformed stdin ('{'), empty stdin, absent model, and model 'gpt-5.6-sol'

CODEX
  7  SessionStart payload, no worker markers -> emits '<!-- eshyra-seat: codex-captain -->'
  8  same payload with env ESHYRA_SEAT_ROLE=dispatched-worker and
     ESHYRA_DISPATCH_CHILD=eshyra-kusc.1 -> emits NOTHING; assert each marker

  9  the same dispatched-worker invocation produces no Claude supervisor policy:
     assert the codex script output never contains 'You are the supervising
     agent' in ANY of the codex cases, and that supervisor-context.mjs emits

  10 payload carrying agent_type 'reviewer' -> emits NOTHING; also assert the
     installed profile template registers SessionStart ONLY (read the installer
     source and assert it contains no 'SubagentStart' registration)
  11 malformed stdin, empty stdin, and hook_event_name 'SubagentStart'

HANDOFF

     contains the claude handoff text and NOT the codex handoff text
  13 the codex script output contains the codex handoff text and NOT the claude

  14 with ESHYRA_SEAT_ROLE=dispatched-worker, neither handoff text appears in

WIRING

=== 7. docs/agent-captain-seats.md ===

Short and neutral. Cover: the two seats and that they are seats rather than
models; the three composed layers and which one is authority; exact storage
paths (charters user-local, handoffs at <git common dir>/eshyra-seats/<seat>/
handoff.md so every worktree of a clone resolves the same state, untracked and
never part of a clone or release); how to install, check, and roll back the
user-local Codex pieces; how to record a handoff; and an explicit statement

workflow, and do not describe dispatch mechanics beyond the bare fact that

=== 8. .claude/settings.json ===

title: Establish Claude Captain and Codex Captain persistent agent seats
description:
OBJECTIVE

Give the two long-lived Eshyra coding agents durable organizational identities -
Claude Captain and Codex Captain - occupied by disposable model sessions.
A Captain is a durable seat; "main session" is only a harness/runtime
classification and one eligibility condition for occupying a seat.

NOT the in-game Dungeon Master seat. eshyra-plwe owns persistent DM-seat
reconstruction inside the Eshyra product; this bead owns the development-agent
harness seats and must stay separate from it.

FOUR SEPARATE CATEGORIES (the design must not merge them)

1. Standing seat identity / charter - long-lived role and operating behavior
   that survives context resets, CLI restarts, and compatible model upgrades.
2. Repository/task authority - AGENTS.md, ADRs, owning beads, findings, exact
   implementation, Git/PR state. Authoritative; always reread and revalidated.
3. Advisory predecessor handoff - unfinished cognitive state, hypotheses,
   salient next investigation, references to active beads/branches/PRs/
   dispatches. NOT authority.
4. Transient runtime session - occupant harness, model, session id, time.
   Occupant metadata only; seat identity must not depend on it, and seat
   history must never be read as inherited capability.

Invariant: the seat remembers how to work; repository systems remember what is
true; the handoff remembers what was happening.

SCOPE

- A Claude Captain charter and a Codex Captain charter, each bounded, stored as
  personal user-local content, never as tracked repository authority.
- Per-seat advisory handoffs that do not share one mutable store, resolve
  identically from every worktree of the same clone, and are untracked.
- Technical routing that decides which prompt material reaches which context.
  Gating must be structural, never a prose request to ignore text.
- Permanent regression evidence for the routing and handoff boundaries.

VISIBILITY MATRIX TO PROVE

- General repository authority reaches every agent, unchanged.
- Claude Captain identity reaches only authorized Claude Captain occupants.
- The existing privileged Claude supervisor overlay keeps its current gate and
  reaches no other context - not Sonnet, not Claude subagents, not Codex
  Captain, not dispatched Codex workers.
- Codex Captain identity reaches a direct Codex Captain session only, and not a
  Claude-dispatched Codex worker or a Codex-native subagent.
- Each Captain sees only its own handoff; dispatched children see neither.

KNOWN CONSTRAINT (measured, not assumed)

codex exec fires SessionStart. A Codex SessionStart event is therefore NOT
proof of Codex Captain occupancy, because dispatch-codex.sh launches workers
through codex exec. The discriminator must be an explicit durable launch
identity, not model name, cwd, bead title, branch name, or permission mode.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

1. Owning bead exists and carries the design; no duplicate seat bead created.
2. Both charters exist, are bounded, and are stored outside tracked repository
   source.
3. Claude Captain injection is gated to an authorized main Claude session and
   fails closed on unknown/absent model identity, on subagents, and on
   malformed hook input.
4. The privileged supervisor overlay stays out of AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, bead
   descriptions, and bd memories, and its gate is unchanged.
5. Codex Captain injection is unreachable from the dispatch launch path by
   construction, with defense-in-depth checks on top.
6. dispatch-codex.sh marks its children explicitly as dispatched implementation
   workers, and every existing safety property and default of that launcher is
   preserved.
7. Handoffs are advisory: startup material requires reconciliation of any
   handoff claim against current beads, Git, PR, and dispatch/process state
   before acting, and correctness never depends on a graceful-shutdown hook.
8. Missing, stale, or corrupt seat state degrades to ordinary repository
   behavior rather than blocking work.
9. Repo-local regression tests execute the real routing scripts against
   representative hook payloads and prove the matrix above.
10. Hard-reset smoke evidence for both seats, plus proof that a dispatched
    worker receives neither Captain identity nor supervisor policy.
11. npm run verify:worktree passes; work lands by PR per AGENTS.md.

NON-GOALS

Not a multi-agent framework, agent ontology, reputation system, capability
ledger, or cross-agent shared memory. Not a reverse Codex-to-Claude dispatch
system. Not a replacement for AGENTS.md, ADRs, or beads as the inter-agent task
protocol. Not a reason to widen the audience of the privileged supervisor
policy.
notes:
PR #527 opened 2026-09-07 from branch eshyra-kusc (head f39d089): https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/527 . Per AGENTS.md this bead stays in_progress until that PR merges.

Architecture: three composed layers (personal charter + live repository authority + advisory handoff), only the middle one authoritative. Claude Captain gated by the existing fail-closed main-session gate (no agent_id, not a resume, supervisor-class model). Codex Captain gated by CONFIG LAYER: measured that codex exec fires SessionStart identically to an interactive session, so the seat hook is registered only in the eshyra-captain profile overlay that the dispatch path never loads; ESHYRA_SEAT_ROLE/ESHYRA_DISPATCH_CHILD are defence in depth, not the boundary. Privileged supervisor overlay untouched, same gate and audience.

Storage: charters user-local and untracked; handoffs at <git common dir>/eshyra-seats/<seat>/handoff.md so every worktree of a clone resolves the same file while git status stays clean.

Child eshyra-itnm closed. 22 regression tests; verify:worktree green (4943 passed, 20 documented skips). Live smoke evidence recorded on the PR for both seats and for a dispatched worker.

OPEN ITEM with a concrete owner (me, on this bead): Codex hook trust has not been granted interactively yet - smoke tests used --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust. First real codex-captain launch prompts once; until then Codex skips the hook silently. seat:install --check infers trust by finding the shim path in ~/.codex/config.toml because the trust hash scheme could not be derived; confirm that inference against a genuinely trusted hook.
REVIEW #5565764326 (head f39d089) REPAIRED at head 2951fb2. All three blocking findings fixed.

F1 (material trust-boundary): CONFIRMED and repaired. Codex runs command hooks OUTSIDE its sandbox (its own prompt says so: 'Hooks can run outside the sandbox after you trust them') and trust covers the declaration, not the transitive closure. The shim resolved the seat script from the active worktree, so any branch or any dispatched worker able to write repo files could gain unsandboxed user-level execution at the next Captain startup with no new prompt. Closure is now user-local: installer copies seat runtime + library into ~/.codex/seats/, trusted shim execs only that fixed path. Negative regression poisons BOTH the entrypoint and a transitive dependency in the repo and proves the installed hook output is unchanged, and that --check reports the drift. The prior test that pinned the unsafe property was removed.

F2 (trust reporting): CONFIRMED and repaired, with the open trust item now CLOSED by real evidence. Completed a genuine first-launch trust grant through the interactive prompt with NO --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust, then measured where Codex records it. Ground truth (Codex 0.153.4): trust is keyed by the DECLARING file plus event and group/handler indices - here /home/jhbongaarts/.codex/eshyra-captain.config.toml:session_start:0:0 - and is written back INTO THAT PROFILE FILE, not into ~/.codex/config.toml. The old heuristic therefore reported a genuinely trusted hook as untrusted. Fixed to the real key in the real file. This exposed a further defect the review did not name: the installer compared and rewrote the profile byte-for-byte, so every reinstall DESTROYED the trust record Codex writes there; it now owns the hook declaration only and leaves [hooks.state] intact. Verified: reinstall preserves trusted_hash and the hook still fires unbypassed. --check now reports trusted/untrusted/stale/unknown and exits non-zero when untrusted. The hash algorithm is not derivable, but it is not needed: trust was granted for the exact declaration text, so a byte-matching declaration is still the trusted one, and a hand-edited one reports 'differs' and is rewritten, which is exactly when Codex re-prompts.

F3 (producer evidence): repaired. scripts/seats/check-dispatch-markers.mjs verifies both markers are set AND that they reach the child process rather than staying in the parent, with fixture coverage (env-prefix form, export form, each marker missing, wrong role value, parent-only assignment, digest determinism). Real-artifact controls: PASS on the current launcher, FAIL on the pre-change backup dispatch-codex.sh.bak.20260907T000837 with both markers reported missing. Current launcher digest sha256:308a4280a12a71549d9d71836b7939d98e91c6b7c4d91d6f137c0962f6e1655e; --baseline pins it so unrelated edits are caught. The checker takes the launcher path as an argument and carries no dispatch policy, so it exposes no supervisor-only instructions.

Also fixed install-on-import: the installer's main block executed on import, so importing it from a test performed a real install against $HOME.

verify:worktree green at 2951fb2 (4946 passed, 20 documented skips). Live smoke re-run after the repair: hook fires with NO bypass flag and the seat answers 'Codex Captain; no, a predecessor handoff is advisory, not authority.'

KNOWN AND DELIBERATELY NOT CHANGED: the Claude-side hook runs repo code via .claude/settings.json. That is Claude Code's existing project-trust model, predates this PR, and is the same posture as the pre-existing supervisor hook; changing it would require fighting the harness and is not authorized by this bead. Flagged for the reviewer rather than silently ignored.
RE-REVIEW #5566119556 (head 2951fb2) REPAIRED at head c702e90. Prior F1 closed by the reviewer. Two remaining findings fixed; both had one root cause - inferring a runtime property from static text instead of observing it.

F2: Codex runs a hook only when enabled AND stored trusted_hash == its computed current_hash. The old checker read neither, and its test asserted a fabricated 'sha256:x' was trusted. Tried the reviewer's preferred route and both paths closed: (a) hooks/list is authoritative and exposes key/enabled/currentHash/trustStatus - confirmed working against trusted project hooks in another repo - but returns [] for a PROFILE-declared hook, and app-server rejects --profile ('--profile only applies to runtime commands and codex mcp'); declaring the hook anywhere hooks/list can reach would put it in a layer dispatched workers load, destroying the boundary. title: Dispatch: Resolve known rules-pack ambiguities as campaign rulings (attempt 1)
description:
Implements eshyra-jhpt.6 (read its spec + acceptance criteria). Base: eshyra-jhpt @ b79112c (main + .4 auditor parity + .5 'eshyra rules' CLI). Everything below is DECIDED; implement it, do not redesign. Amendment A2 (capability preflight) is OUT of scope here and tracked as a separate child under eshyra-jhpt.6.

WORKTREE / BRANCH: .worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.6.1 on branch eshyra-jhpt.6.1. npm ci already run.

CODE SURVEY (supervisor, exact pointers):
- Ambiguity metadata + active rulings: assembleCampaignRulesContext(db, campaignId, formattedPosition, resolveStrictCampaignRulesStack(db, resolveRulesPack?)) in packages/core/src/campaign/campaignContext.ts returns .ambiguities[{ambiguity: RulesAmbiguity {id, question, interpretations[{id, summary}], affects[], ...}, ruling?: CampaignRulingProjection, conflictingRulings[]}]. renderCampaignRulesSection(ctx) renders UNRESOLVED / Active ruling / CONFLICT lines and is shared by DM and auditor (.4).
- Bundled SRD ambiguity ids and interpretation ids (verified by running the built CLI): ambiguity:create-undead-ghast-wight-composition -> homogeneous-alternative | mixed-within-total; ambiguity:find-familiar-permanent-dismissal-after-zero-hp -> presence-required | active-link-sufficient; ambiguity:cube-of-force-same-face-duration-reset (leave to A2).
- Storage: createCampaignRule(db, rule, {currentPosition, validation:{ambiguity}}) in packages/core/src/campaign/campaignRuleStore.ts; ordinary rulings are prospective with effective ordinal > persisted current (getCurrentCampaignPosition(db, campaignId) in campaign/campaignPosition.ts; bootstrap current = {sessionId:'cli', turnId:'bootstrap', ordinal:0} when undefined — see packages/cli/src/rules.ts BOOTSTRAP constant and effectivePosition()). Ambiguity rulings for the same ambiguity may not overlap (store rejects). CampaignRule shape: see campaign/campaignRules.ts (provenance {kind:'ambiguity', ambiguityId, selectedInterpretationId}; origin 'player-approved'; temporalMode {mode:'prospective'}; supersededBy null; revokedPosition null).
- Tools: packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolRegistry.ts Tool {name, description, mutates, requiresExplicitAction?, inputSchema, run(args, ctx: ToolContext {db, campaignId, sessionId, turnId, at, resolveRulesPack?, ...})} with ok(data)/err(code,message,data?)/asRecord(args). Template: toolLookupRules.ts (mutates:false). Register in packages/core/src/orchestrator/tools.ts (import + add to the tool list near lookupRulesTool, line ~95). Executed calls reach the CLI as RunTurnResult.toolCalls: ExecutedToolCall[] {tool, args, result:{ok, data|code,message}} (orchestrator.ts RunTurnResult ~line 163).
- DM system prompt: buildSystemPrompt in packages/core/src/orchestrator/protocol.ts (tool guidance bullets around lines 240-330, e.g. the lookup_rules bullet at ~321). Auditor: packages/core/src/orchestrator/turnAuditor.ts buildAuditSystemPrompt (the .4 campaign-rules paragraph at ~line 300) and AUDIT_POLICY (~line 155).
- CLI play loop: packages/cli/src/playTurnLoop.ts turnLoop(): after deps.runTurn(...) resolves with result.ok it writes result.narration (line ~125). deps.io: CliIO {write(line), prompt(question) -> Promise<string|undefined>} (packages/cli/src/playTypes.ts). Tests fake deps.runTurn (PlayDeps.runTurn is injectable) — see packages/cli/test/play.test.ts for the harness.
- CLI rules command: packages/cli/src/rules.ts (parseArgs/flag/requiredFlag/withCampaign/validateAmbiguity/contextAmbiguity helpers; dispatcher runRulesCommand; USAGE string). Tests: packages/cli/test/rules.test.ts (invoke(dbPath, args) harness).
- Root export boundary: CLI imports only '@eshyra/core' (packages/cli/test/internalBoundary.test.ts). Promote the two new core functions below to packages/core/src/index.ts (next to the .5 block) and also export them from internal.ts.
- Scripted model doubles for orchestrator tests: packages/core/test/orchestrator.test.ts ScriptedModel (fenced tool protocol replies) and StructuredScriptedModel (native toolCalls) — copy an existing test that scripts a lookup_rules call to see the exact reply format.

DESIGN (decided):
1. Core service packages/core/src/campaign/ambiguityResolution.ts:
   - export function lookupCampaignAmbiguity(db, {campaignId, ambiguityId, position: CampaignPosition, resolveRulesPack?}): {ambiguity: RulesAmbiguity, status: 'unresolved'|'resolved'|'conflicting', ruling?: CampaignRulingProjection, conflictingRulings: CampaignRulingProjection[]}. Unknown id -> throw CampaignRuleError('unknown ambiguity <id>; known ambiguity ids: a, b, c') (sorted). Uses assembleCampaignRulesContext at formatCampaignPosition(position) — NO new store, no pack write.
   - export function recordAmbiguityRuling(db, {campaignId, ambiguityId, interpretationId, prose?, currentPosition, effectiveOrdinal?, sessionId?, resolveRulesPack?}): {created: boolean, rule: CampaignRule}. If an active ruling for that ambiguity exists at the position immediately after current -> return {created:false, rule: existing} WITHOUT writing (idempotent; 'existing active ruling prevents re-prompting'). Else validate interpretationId against ambiguity.interpretations (unknown -> CampaignRuleError listing the known interpretation ids), build the ruling: ruleIdentity 'ruling:<ambiguityId without the "ambiguity:" prefix>:<effective ordinal>', ruleKind 'ruling', origin 'player-approved', provenance {kind:'ambiguity', ambiguityId, selectedInterpretationId}, effectivePosition {...currentPosition, ordinal: effectiveOrdinal ?? currentPosition.ordinal + 1}, temporalMode prospective, scope 'rules-ambiguity', governingRecordKeys = ambiguity.affects (non-empty; if the pack's affects is empty use ['ambiguity:<id>']), prose = provided ?? `${ambiguity.question} Ruling: ${interpretation.summary}`; persist via createCampaignRule with validation {ambiguity}. Return what was persisted.
2. Tool packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolRequestAmbiguityRuling.ts: name 'request_ambiguity_ruling', mutates:false, args {ambiguityId: string}. run: lookupCampaignAmbiguity at the turn's current persisted position (getCurrentCampaignPosition(ctx.db, ctx.campaignId) — the turn's own row exists because runTurn resolves the position first). Returns ok({ambiguityId, question, interpretations:[{id, summary}], status, ruling: {ruleIdentity, selectedInterpretationId, prose} | null}); unknown id -> err('unknown_ambiguity', message, {knownAmbiguityIds}). Description tells the DM: call when an outcome depends on an ambiguity marked UNRESOLVED in Campaign Rules; then narrate the published uncertainty, present the interpretations neutrally, and tell the player they will be asked to choose; never choose yourself; if status is 'resolved', apply the ruling.
3. Prompts: add ONE bullet to buildSystemPrompt tool guidance (protocol.ts) stating the above. Add ONE line to the auditor's campaign-rules paragraph (turnAuditor.ts): a candidate that asserts a definite outcome for an ambiguity listed as UNRESOLVED without an active ruling must be rejected, reason citing the ambiguity id; a candidate that surfaces the uncertainty and defers to the player is acceptable.
4. CLI play loop: new file packages/cli/src/playRulings.ts exporting async function offerAmbiguityRulings(deps: PlayDeps, db: Db, campaignId: string, toolCalls: readonly ExecutedToolCall[]): Promise<void>. For each executed 'request_ambiguity_ruling' call with result.ok and data.status === 'unresolved' (dedupe by ambiguityId): io.write the question and numbered interpretations, io.prompt('Choose an interpretation number, or press Enter to leave it unresolved: '); Enter/undefined/invalid -> write 'Left unresolved.' and create nothing; a valid number -> recordAmbiguityRuling with currentPosition = getCurrentCampaignPosition(db, campaignId) and write 'Ruling <identity> recorded (<interpretationId>); takes effect from turn <ordinal>.' Errors -> write the message, create nothing. Call it from turnLoop right after deps.io.write(result.narration). (The ruling is prospective, so the NEXT turn's DM and auditor contexts carry it; that is the spec's 'prospectively active'.)
5. CLI rules command additions (packages/cli/src/rules.ts): 'rules ambiguities [campaign-id]' lists every ambiguity id with status (unresolved/resolved:<ruleIdentity>/conflicting) and its interpretation ids; 'rules resolve <ambiguity-id> --interpretation <id> [--prose <text>] [--effective <ordinal>] [campaign-id]' calls recordAmbiguityRuling and prints the same confirmation shape as 'add' (identity, effective ordinal, provenance, takes effect from turn N), or 'already resolved by <identity>' with exit 0 when created:false. Update USAGE.
6. Pack immutability: never write to the pack; tests assert the resolved stack's ambiguity record is unchanged (deep-equal before/after) and that no row other than campaign_rule changed.

EVIDENCE (each must FAIL against b79112c; report observed counts):
E1 packages/core/test/ambiguityResolution.test.ts: for create-undead, recording homogeneous-alternative in one db and mixed-within-total in another both persist one ruling with correct provenance/identity/effective position; find-familiar both interpretations; unknown ambiguity and unknown interpretation messages list the known ids; recording twice returns created:false and the same rule (one row); lookup status transitions unresolved -> resolved at the next position and stays unresolved at the current position; assembleCampaignRulesContext at the next position shows the ruling, and renderCampaignRulesSection output is byte-identical for the DM path (renderContextMessage section) and the auditor path (buildAuditUserMessage section) — reuse .4's parity helpers; pack record unchanged.
E2 packages/core/test/orchestrator.test.ts (or a new toolRequestAmbiguityRuling.test.ts): a ScriptedModel turn that calls request_ambiguity_ruling for create-undead gets status 'unresolved' with both interpretations; after recordAmbiguityRuling, the next turn's call returns 'resolved' with the ruling; unknown id -> err with knownAmbiguityIds; the tool is registered (registry.list() contains it) and mutates:false; the DM system prompt and auditor system prompt contain the new guidance.
E3 packages/cli/test/playRulings.test.ts: with a fake runTurn returning an ok result whose toolCalls include an unresolved request, choosing '2' records the ruling (assert via getCampaignRule) and prints the confirmation; pressing Enter creates nothing; an invalid number creates nothing; a 'resolved' status prompts nothing; two calls for the same ambiguity prompt once.
E4 packages/cli/test/rules.test.ts: 'rules ambiguities' lists the three bundled ids with statuses; 'rules resolve' creates the ruling and re-running reports already resolved with exit 0; unknown interpretation lists known ids.

title: Dispatch: Supervisor self-review round 5 findings on PR #524 head d3d8781
description:
Supervisor self-review round 5 of PR #524 head d3d8781. SIX findings (4 medium, 2 low). No highs; the sweep independently re-verified as clean the interval-overlap algebra, __future__ anchor ordering, revoked/superseded predicates in activeRows, savepoint placement (failed turns leave no ordinal hole), nested withTransaction, the seenRuleIdentities/includeAllActive interaction, and the sessionDebug section labels.

Findings 2, 3 and 4 are all consequences of round 4's __future__ canonicalization. Fix the CLASS: that canonicalization rewrites a value the caller supplied, and every path that reads, returns, or compares that value must agree about which form it is looking at.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.rev8 on branch eshyra-jhpt.rev8, cut from eshyra-jhpt at d3d8781. npm ci already run there.

=============================================================
FINDING 1 (medium) — the per-turn degrade path still does not catch the pack-defect class it exists for.
=============================================================
contextAssembler.ts catches CampaignRulesBindingResolutionError and CampaignRulesPackAuthoringError, but assembleCampaignRulesContext -> ambiguitiesFromStack also calls optRulesAmbiguities, which throws RulesPackError on any malformed mechanics.ambiguities block. resolveRulesStack performs only meta-level assertions, so a pack supplied through deps.resolveRulesPack is never record-validated. A record declaring ambiguity id 'ambiguity:Foo_Bar' (fails the kebab-case regex) makes every runTurn throw out of assembleContext and roll back, instead of degrading to ambiguitySourceUnavailable.
This is the THIRD instance of this class: each round a new error type reaches the per-turn path and the catch list does not include it.
FIX: stop enumerating error types. Decide the rule positively — any failure to interpret PACK CONTENT while assembling per-turn context degrades to ambiguitySourceUnavailable with the error recorded; failures that are not about pack content still propagate. Implement it so a future pack-content error class is covered by construction rather than by remembering to add it. State how you achieved that.

=============================================================
FINDING 2 (medium) — createCampaignRule returns a rule that does not match what it stored.
=============================================================
writeRule canonicalizes a future-dated prospective effectivePosition to the reserved __future__ anchor, but createCampaignRule returns the CALLER'S rule object, not what was persisted.
REPRODUCED at d3d8781 (supervisor), current ordinal 3, scheduling for ordinal 9:
    returned effectivePosition: {"sessionId":"s1","turnId":"t9","ordinal":9}
    stored   effectivePosition: {"sessionId":"__future__","turnId":"__future__","ordinal":9}
A caller that round-trips the returned value gets different ordering under compareCampaignPositions (future anchors sort before real anchors at equal ordinal) and a position assertPersistedPosition will reject. The existing test asserts canonicalization only via getCampaignRule, so the divergence is uncovered.
FIX: return what was persisted. Test that the returned value deep-equals getCampaignRule for both the future-dated and the ordinary case.

=============================================================
FINDING 3 (medium) — same divergence in supersedeCampaignRule.
=============================================================
It returns input.successor rather than what writeRule persisted, so a successor scheduled for a future ordinal is reported with anchors that were rewritten before insert. Same fix, same test shape.

=============================================================
FINDING 4 (medium) — a future-scheduled rule can NEVER be revoked before it takes effect.
=============================================================
Three guards compose into an unsatisfiable constraint: assertCurrentPosition forces currentPosition to equal the latest persisted turn; assertPersistedPosition forces revokedPosition to be a persisted turn; and revokedPosition >= currentPosition. Together those pin revokedPosition to the current ordinal — and the effective-position guard then rejects it for any rule effective later.
REPRODUCED at d3d8781 (supervisor): a rule scheduled at ordinal 9, player changes their mind at ordinal 2 ->
    campaign rule 'sched' cannot be revoked before its effective position
Every revoke attempt fails until ordinal 9 arrives, at which point revoking leaves the rule active for zero turns. There is no way to cancel a scheduled rule. supersedeCampaignRule has no equivalent block, so the two mutations disagree about the same lifecycle.
FIX: cancelling a not-yet-effective rule is a legitimate operation and must be possible. Decide the semantics deliberately — most likely revoking a rule that has not taken effect removes it from ever being active (revocation at its own effective position, or an explicit cancel), rather than requiring a revocation position that cannot exist. Make revoke and supersede consistent about not-yet-effective rules, and say in your notes what you chose. Test: schedule at ordinal 9, cancel at ordinal 2, prove the rule is never active at any position including 9 and later.

=============================================================
FINDING 5 (low) — duplicate governingRecordKeys duplicate the rule in the context packet.
=============================================================
The seam's governed loop pushes one entry per governingRecordKeys element with no dedup, and withRule appends to campaignRules/campaignRulings unconditionally (only routes is dedup-guarded by trigger). validateCampaignRule never rejects duplicate or empty governingRecordKeys, and keysColumn.decode returns the array verbatim. A rule persisted with ['spell:fireball','spell:fireball'] attaches twice, emits two identical placedRules trace entries, and duplicates the prose against the packet byte budget.
FIX: reject duplicate and empty governingRecordKeys in validateCampaignRule (write-side), and make the seam's placement idempotent per (ruleIdentity, governingRecordKey) so restored or legacy rows cannot duplicate either. Test both sides.

=============================================================
FINDING 6 (low) — a house-rule carrying ambiguity provenance is silently dropped from every context branch.
=============================================================
Such a rule is excluded from `rules` (provenance.kind !== 'ambiguity'), from unboundRulings (ruleKind === 'ruling'), and from `rulings` (isAmbiguityRuling requires ruleKind === 'ruling'). validateCampaignRule rejects the pairing on the write path, but migration 0025's CHECK constraints do not, and CheckpointStore restore inserts snapshot rows directly with no domain validation. Restoring such a checkpoint yields a rule active in listCampaignRules that never reaches the DM prompt, with no loss or diagnostic.
This is the silent-disappearance class again, and the same restore-bypass route as round 3 finding 7.
FIX: the context must not silently drop an active rule for any reason. Give the assembly a total accounting — every active rule lands in exactly one branch or is explicitly recorded as unrepresentable, with its identity visible. Consider also whether migration 0025 should carry the CHECK constraint that matches the domain invariant; if you think it should, file a bead rather than editing the merged migration.

GENERAL
  - NEGATIVE PROOF per finding against d3d8781; report observed counts and quote the asserted guard messages.
  - Every negative assertion must assert the distinctive guard message.
  - Do not weaken existing tests, do not touch merged migrations, the position encoding, eshyra-umyb, or eshyra-jhpt.2.5.
  - Keep every earlier fix intact, especially the deterministic future-anchor ordering from round 4.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing. Report pass/skip counts and confirm worktree-local resolution.
