title: Dispatch: implement the offline discovery stage harness (attempt 1)
description:
WORKTREE `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.10.1`, BRANCH `eshyra-o9bd.19.10.1`
(cut from parent branch `eshyra-o9bd.19.10`, which is `origin/main` @ fbd3efd).

Parent bead `eshyra-o9bd.19.10` (Transition W8) carries the authority, scope,
prohibitions, and acceptance criteria. Read it with `bd show` first. The
governing design is
`docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md`
sections 6, 7, 8.2, 11, 12.1, 13.1, 13.2, 13.3; ADR 0020 controls. Read
sections 6, 7, 8.2, 12.1, 13 yourself before writing code — this plan
summarises them but the document is the authority and wins on any conflict.

The supervisor has already surveyed the substrate. What follows is the
pre-planning, not a licence to skip verification: check every claim marked
[VERIFY] against the tree before you rely on it.

====================================================================
A. WHAT EXISTS ALREADY (verified by the supervisor at fbd3efd)
====================================================================

W7 landed the fixture corpus:
- `packages/core/test/diagnostics/fixtureContract.ts` — types + validator.
  Key exported types: `DiagnosticFixture`, `FixtureExecution`, `RouteClass`
  (the nine section-6.2 labels), `DiagnosticTarget` (`rules-record` |
  `adventure-entity` | `absent-rules-record`), `DiagnosticSelector`,
  `RetainedFact`, `TypedRelationshipExpectation`, `RouteExpectation`,
  `AmbiguityExpectation`, `CampaignRuleCase`, `CapabilityExpectation`,
  `OracleSignal`, `ExplicitNone`.
- `packages/core/test/diagnostics/probes/p01..p12*.ts` and
  `packages/core/test/diagnostics/index.ts` exporting `DIAGNOSTIC_FIXTURES`.
- `packages/core/test/diagnosticFixtureCorpus.test.ts` validates the fixtures
  against the real pack and module. Do not weaken it, and do not edit the
  fixtures to make the harness pass. If a fixture expectation is genuinely
  wrong, stop and file a bead against `eshyra-o9bd.19.9` instead.

Canonical target reference strings (match the private `targetReference()` in
`fixtureContract.ts`): rules-record and absent-rules-record use `recordKey`;
adventure-entity uses `${moduleId}#${entityKind}:${entityId}`. Reuse exactly
this convention for candidate keys so measurements line up.

Real substrate you MUST use (no fixture copies of packs):
- `packages/core/src/rules/stack.ts` — `resolveRulesStack`,
  `ResolvedRulesStack` (`recordsByKey`, `recordsByKind` with `byKey`/`byName`),
  `RulesStackRecordEntry` (`record`, `pack`, `license`, `overrideChain`),
  and `normalizeRulesRecordName`.
- `packages/core/src/state/campaignRecordLookup.ts` —
  `resolveStrictCampaignRulesStack(db, resolver)`, `CampaignRulesPackResolver`.
- `packages/core/src/rules/bundledSrdPack.ts` — `getBundledDnd5eSrdPack()`
  loads the generated pack (1812 records) from `packages/core/data`.
- `packages/core/src/rules/conditionRelations.ts` —
  `CONDITION_RELATION_VALUES` (the closed relation vocabulary).
- `packages/core/src/state/itemExecutionReadiness.ts` —
  `assertMagicItemOperationReady(record, variantId, input)`,
  `ItemOperationReadinessInput`, `ItemExecutionReadinessError`.
- `packages/core/test/support/db.ts` — `bareDb()`, `freshDbWithSession()`.
- `packages/core/test/support/cursedAttunementAddon.ts` —
  `installCursedAttunementAddon(db, at)` returns the resolver and writes the
  campaign binding; P11 needs it.
- `packages/core/src/adventure/` — module loading (`loadAdventureModuleFromDir`
  via `src/internal.ts`) and `adventure/references.ts`.

Verified pack facts you may rely on (re-check if surprised):
- `rule:cover`, `rule:opportunity-attacks`, `rule:concentration` carry only
  `data.text` — no typed mechanics, so they are reachable only by cue.
- `condition:incapacitated` has `data.effects` and `data.mechanics`.
- `mechanics.conditions` entries carry `{condition: "<name>", relation: "<rel>"}`
  where `condition` is the bare name (e.g. `"incapacitated"`), NOT the record
  key. 136 records carry `mechanics.conditions`; 21 name `incapacitated`.
- Typed link fields present in the pack: `data.source` (197),
  `data.mechanics.conditions` (136), `data.tableRefs` (73),
  `data.progressionTableRef` (12), `data.parentClass` (12),
  `data.spellTableRefs` (4), `data.statBlockRefs` (2).
- `feature:fighter:action-surge` has `data.source === 'class:fighter'`.
- `action:dodge` has `mechanics.conditions = [{condition:'incapacitated',
  relation:'exclusion'}]`.
- `magic-item:ammunition-1-2-or-3` readiness: C1 `economies/use` green, C2
  `effects` engine-pending (F8). Operation `hit-target`.
- `magic-item:cube-of-force` readiness: `operations/press-face-1` is
  engine-pending (F5), so preflight for `press-face-1` must be BLOCKED.
- Only 3 records carry `mechanics.ambiguities`.

====================================================================
B. WHERE THE CODE GOES
====================================================================

Production module tree, exported ONLY through `@eshyra/core/internal`
(`packages/core/src/internal.ts`), never through `src/index.ts`:

  packages/core/src/discovery/
    types.ts              stage/trace/packet/route types
    signals.ts            stage 1
    candidates.ts         stage 2
    expansion.ts          stage 3
    campaignRuleSeam.ts   stage 4 seam (interface + null implementation)
    dedup.ts              stage 5
    retention.ts          stage 6
    packet.ts             stage 7
    harness.ts            runDiscoveryStages(): orchestrates 1-7, returns trace
    measurements.ts       M1-M9

Rationale for `src/` rather than `test/`: AGENTS.md's convention is that new
core symbols default to the `/internal` subpath, which exists for
co-developed in-repo callers; W9 (`eshyra-o9bd.19.11`) has to wire this same
pipeline into the orchestrator seam, and a test-only home would force a move.
This stays experiment-only in the sense the bead requires: NOTHING in
`src/orchestrator`, `src/state`, `src/session`, or the CLI may import it. Add a
test that asserts that (grep-style guard, in the same spirit as
`packages/core/test/nodeRuntimePolicy.test.ts`).

Tests:
  packages/core/test/discovery/discoverySignals.test.ts
  packages/core/test/discovery/discoveryStages.test.ts
  packages/core/test/discovery/discoveryProbes.test.ts
  packages/core/test/discovery/support/scenario.ts        fixture -> harness input
  packages/core/test/discovery/support/oracleCampaignRules.ts  the jhpt stub

====================================================================
C. THE PIPELINE
====================================================================

Stages, in order (design section 12.1):
  signals -> candidates -> typed expansion -> campaign-rule/ruling join
  -> dedup -> priority/retention -> context packet

EVERY stage returns its own trace object, and `runDiscoveryStages` returns
`{ signals, candidates, expansion, ruleJoin, dedup, retention, packet }` plus a
flat `stageOrder` list. No stage may mutate a prior stage's trace. Nothing is
persisted anywhere: no DB writes, no files, no artifact emission. The harness
takes a `Db` ONLY to resolve the campaign rules binding through
`resolveStrictCampaignRulesStack`; it must never write to it.

Every stage trace records, at minimum: inputs consumed, outputs produced,
and losses (with a reason). A stage that produced nothing and recorded no
loss must be reported as `failed-to-run`, not as passing (design 13.3).

--- Stage 1: signals (`signals.ts`) ---

Input: `DiscoveryScenario`:
  {
    playerInput: string,
    actingCharacterId?: string,
    stateFields: Record<string, unknown>,   // the fixture's campaignState
    adventure?: { moduleId, locationId?, encounterId?, module: AdventureModule },
    itemInstances?: readonly { instanceId, recordKey, variantId? }[],
    oracleSignals?: readonly InjectedSignal[],   // for stage-independent tests
  }

Output signals, each `{ signalId, kind, evidence, proposes }` where `evidence`
names the exact input field or text span it came from.

Signal kinds and their extractors:
1. `state-ref`: walk `stateFields` (recursively, recording the JSON path of
   every value visited). Any string value matching `^<kind>:<slug>$` where
   `<kind>` is a member of `RULES_RECORD_KINDS` becomes a state-ref signal
   proposing that record key. Also resolve the declared `itemInstances`
   bindings (instanceId -> recordKey) when a state field's value equals a
   known instanceId. Record the binding in the trace as a scenario-state
   binding so it is never hidden.
   `conditions: ['condition:incapacitated']` and
   `activeEffects: [{kind:'concentration', source:'spell:hold-person'}]`
   are both covered by the generic walk.
2. `adventure-ref`: from `scenario.adventure`, propose the selected
   location and encounter entity targets, and every `rulesRef` carried by the
   selected encounter's creature entries and the selected location.
3. `name-mention`: normalize `playerInput` with `normalizeRulesRecordName`,
   tokenize, and look up token n-grams (up to the longest indexed record name,
   bounded) against each kind's `byName` index. A hit where the name maps to
   exactly ONE entry proposes that record key. A hit where the name maps to
   several entries is recorded as an `ambiguous-name` observation (not a
   candidate) with every colliding key listed — that mirrors the `lookup.ts`
   exact/ambiguous contract and must never be resolved by picking one.
4. `situation-cue`: a small, explicit, declared cue table (see D below).
5. `capability-preflight`: when the scenario names an `operationId` together
   with an item record (directly or through an `itemInstances` binding),
   propose that record with the operation id attached.
6. `auditor-missing-target`: define the signal kind for completeness, but no
   extractor is required — no fixture exercises it. Say so in the module doc.

MANDATORY: any `stateFields` leaf the signals stage did NOT consume must be
reported in the trace as `unconsumedStateFields` (path + value shape). Silently
ignoring scenario state is exactly the "recognising nothing looks green"
failure the design forbids.

`oracleSignals` are merged in, each flagged `oracleSupplied: true` with the
label the caller supplied, and the stage trace exposes
`oracleSuppliedSignalLabels` so downstream reporting can label the probe.

--- Stage 2: candidates (`candidates.ts`) ---

Resolve every signal's proposed target against the REAL resolved stack
(`ResolvedRulesStack.recordsByKey`) and, for adventure entities, against the
loaded module. Produce `DiscoveryCandidate`:
  { candidateKey, targetKind: 'rules-record'|'adventure-entity',
    entry?: RulesStackRecordEntry, adventureEntity?: {...},
    routes: DiscoveryRoute[] }
`DiscoveryRoute` = { routeClass: RouteClass, trigger: string,
  evidence: Record<string, unknown>, signalId: string }.

A proposed target that does not resolve is a recorded loss
(`unresolved-target`), never a silent drop.

--- Stage 3: typed expansion (`expansion.ts`) ---

ONE hop, only over links the pack already types. Two directions, because the
fixtures require both:
- forward: from a candidate record, follow `data.source`, `data.parentClass`,
  `data.tableRefs`, `data.progressionTableRef`, `data.spellTableRefs`,
  `data.statBlockRefs`, and `data.mechanics.conditions` (relation value from
  `CONDITION_RELATION_VALUES`; the `condition` field is a bare NAME and must be
  resolved to a `condition:*` record key through the stack's condition-kind
  `byName` index, not by string-concatenating a key).
- reverse: records whose typed link points AT a candidate. Build the reverse
  index once per stack resolution from the same closed field list.

Every traversal is emitted as
`{ sourceRecordKey, linkField, relation, targetRecordKey }` matching
`TypedRelationshipExpectation` exactly, so M4 can compare directly. `linkField`
strings must match the fixture's declared form (P5 declares
`'data.mechanics.conditions'`); for fields with no relation value use the field
name as the relation (state the convention in the module doc and keep it
consistent). BOTH endpoints of an emitted traversal gain a `typed-relationship`
route: this is what P6 (`feature:fighter:action-surge` gains the route from its
own outgoing `data.source` link) and P5 (`condition:incapacitated` gains it from
the inbound `action:dodge` exclusion link) require. The endpoint that was not
already a candidate becomes a NEW candidate. Cap the expansion at one hop; new
candidates from expansion are never themselves expanded.

--- Stage 4: campaign-rule/ruling join (`campaignRuleSeam.ts`) ---

Define the narrow READ interface required by design 8.2, and nothing more:

  export interface CampaignRuleReadSeam {
    activeRulesAtPosition(query: {
      campaignPosition?: string;
      candidateRecordKeys: readonly string[];
    }): readonly ActiveCampaignRuleProjection[];
    activeRulingsForAmbiguities(
      ambiguityIds: readonly string[],
    ): readonly ActiveCampaignRulingProjection[];
  }

`ActiveCampaignRuleProjection` carries: `ruleIdentity`, `ruleKind`
('house-rule'|'ruling'), `status`, `origin`, `provenance`, `effectivePosition`,
`supersededBy` (null when none), `scope`, and `governingRecordKeys` (design
8.3 A1) and/or `ambiguityId`. `ActiveCampaignRulingProjection` additionally
carries `ambiguityId` and `selectedInterpretationId`.

Ship a `NULL_CAMPAIGN_RULE_SEAM` in `src` that returns empty arrays for both
methods, and document that `eshyra-jhpt` owns the real implementation (W11
consumes it). NO rule/ruling schema, store, resolver, lifecycle, persistence,
or supersession logic may be implemented here — the seam only reads.

The join stage: request active rules for the current candidate key set and
active rulings for every ambiguity id discovered on candidate records
(`data.mechanics.ambiguities[].id`). For each returned projection, attach a
`campaign-rule` or `campaign-ruling` route to the candidate(s) it governs, and
record the pairing (`ruleIdentity` -> governing candidate key) for M5. A
projection that names no resolvable governing candidate is recorded as an
`unplaced-rule` loss — never dropped silently. A discovered ambiguity with no
active ruling stays `unresolved` in the trace (design 8.2 R7); discovery must
NEVER resolve an ambiguity itself.

The test-side stub lives in
`packages/core/test/discovery/support/oracleCampaignRules.ts`: an explicit,
clearly-labelled table keyed by `${probeId}/${executionId}`, with entries only
for the two executions whose fixtures declare active campaign-rule state and
oracle signals (P7 `with-active-ruling`, P10 `default`). Every projection it
returns is flagged oracle-supplied, and any probe consuming it is reported
with the join stage labelled `oracle-supplied`.

--- Stage 5: dedup (`dedup.ts`) ---

Merge by canonical candidate key. Preserve EVERY route and EVERY traversal
reason. The trace records `routeCountBeforeDedup`, `routeCountAfterDedup` per
candidate and in total; any decrease is a hard failure (throw), not a warning
(design 6.2, M3). Route identity for dedup purposes is
(routeClass, trigger, signalId) — two genuinely identical route records may
collapse, but the trace must show that the collapse was of identical records.

--- Stage 6: priority and retention (`retention.ts`) ---

Bands (design 6.3):
  must-consider: direct-state-ref, direct-adventure-ref,
                 explicit-name-or-alias, campaign-rule, campaign-ruling,
                 capability-preflight
  related:       typed-relationship
  exploratory:   situation-cue, auditor-missing-target
A candidate's band is the strongest band any of its routes earns.

IMPORTANT: `situation-cue` is exploratory by section 6.3, and P1, P2 and P5's
`rule:concentration` are must-include TARGETS reached ONLY by cue. Retention
must therefore be generous enough that exploratory candidates for those probes
survive; a must-include target that is dropped by the budget is an M1/M2
failure the probe reports, not something to paper over by reclassifying the
band. Do NOT move `situation-cue` into must-consider — the bands come from the
design.

Ranking within a band: route count descending, then canonical key ascending.
Deterministic and simple only — no ranker, no scoring model, no embeddings.

Budget: `{ maxCandidates, maxPacketBytes }` with documented defaults chosen so
that no probe drops a must-include target. Must-consider candidates are NEVER
dropped: if the must-consider set alone exceeds the budget, emit an
`overflow` record naming every dropped candidate with its full route list and
mark the run `overflowed: true` — the probe runner MUST fail such a probe.
Related and exploratory drops are permitted and each records its reason.

--- Stage 7: context packet (`packet.ts`) ---

For each retained candidate emit the design 7.1 fields:
  canonical identity (key, kind, name);
  provenance (`provenance.sourceRef`, `provenance.locator`, `source` label,
    license identity from the stack entry);
  source prose (`description`, `text`, the relevant `actions[i].text`,
    `higherLevels`, ... — carry the record's prose fields verbatim; do not
    truncate a required retained fact out of the packet);
  every route with its trigger detail;
  every traversal that produced the candidate;
  known source ambiguity (`id`, `question`, `interpretations[].id`,
    `canonicalResolution`) — always surfaced, resolved or not;
  applicable campaign rule/ruling with identity, scope, provenance,
    supersession status, placed beside the governing material;
  capability status (see E) with inputs, exclusions, revision, and residual
    interpretation;
  projection-limit notes (see F).

Packet prohibitions (design 7.3) — enforce each with a test:
- never present a route-free record as authoritative (a candidate with zero
  routes is a bug: throw);
- never present a typed projection as a capability;
- never turn "no capability bound" into "no mechanics";
- never drop a must-consider candidate silently;
- never launder known-false provenance (P12);
- never claim the model used anything.

====================================================================
D. THE SITUATION-CUE TABLE
====================================================================

Section 6.2 says this class has no substrate today and that a cue "matches a
fixture-declared cue". The fixtures do not carry a cue field, so the harness
owns a small, explicit, DECLARED cue table. Rules for it:
- each entry is `{ cueId, description, derivationInputs, proposes: recordKey[],
  match(scenario): CueMatch | undefined }`;
- matching keys off STRUCTURED scenario state (and, where unavoidable, a
  narrowly documented text predicate), NEVER off a probe id, fixture identity,
  or the expected outputs. A cue that reads the fixture's expectations is a
  defect, not a shortcut;
- every match records the cue id, the exact derivation input, and the proposed
  record — that is the section 6.2 "recorded evidence" column;
- the table's module doc states plainly that it is a pilot cue set, that it is
  not a model of how rules become relevant, and that a cue's absence is
  evidence about the pilot rather than about the rules (section 6.4).

Three cues are needed by the corpus. Derive their exact match conditions from
the fixtures' campaignState yourself; the shapes are:
- geometry/obstacle cue: combat state carrying an obstacle description ->
  `rule:cover` (P1: `combat: {attacker, target, geometry: 'low wall between
  them'}`, and the player text deliberately never says "cover");
- movement-out-of-reach cue: a movement intent leaving melee reach ->
  `rule:opportunity-attacks` (P2);
- concentration-under-condition cue: an active `concentration` effect present
  together with condition state -> `rule:concentration` (P5).

Keep the obstacle vocabulary tiny, explicit, and documented (a short declared
noun list is fine); do not build a general text classifier.

====================================================================
E. CAPABILITY PREFLIGHT — SCOPE LIMIT, STATED HONESTLY
====================================================================

Only the magic-item readiness path has a real preflight in the tree today
(design 6.2 cites `assertMagicItemOperationReady`). Do this:

1. Extract, from `packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts` (the block running
   roughly from `const mechanics = mechanicsFor(hit.record, variantId)` to the
   `assertMagicItemOperationReady(...)` call, near lines 1834-1908 [VERIFY the
   exact range]), a pure helper that derives `ItemOperationReadinessInput` from
   `(record, variantId, operationId)` — the operation lookup including the
   activate/deactivate state-machine fallback, `economyIds` from the
   operation's cost entries, `operationEffectIds`, `effectIds` (operation
   effects plus possible transition effects), `usesStateMachine`, and
   `usesSpellStore`. Call it from BOTH `itemState.ts` and the harness. This
   must be a pure, behaviour-preserving extraction: the existing item tests
   must pass unchanged, and you must not alter error types, messages, or
   ordering. If the extraction cannot be done cleanly, STOP and record why in
   the bead rather than forcing it.
2. The harness's preflight stage calls the extracted derivation plus the real
   `assertMagicItemOperationReady`, and reports
   `available` (no throw) or `blocked` (throws `ItemExecutionReadinessError`,
   carrying the message and the blocking clause ids as evidence), along with
   the contract revision (`derived-magic-item-clauses-v1`), the operation's
   declared inputs, and the clause-level exclusions.
   Expected: P8 `hit-target` -> available; P7 `press-face-1` -> blocked.
3. For every OTHER capability a fixture declares (`spell-upcast`,
   `concentration-lifecycle`), the packet records
   `not-evaluated-offline` naming the capability id and stating that
   contract-declared capability status is owned by W13
   (`eshyra-olc5.6`) and by M10, which is a Phase 2 measurement. Do NOT
   fabricate an `implemented` status, and do NOT build a capability-contract
   registry — that is W13's, not yours. The probe report shows the fixture's
   expectation beside the harness's `not-evaluated-offline` finding as an
   explicit, visible gap. M1-M9 are the Phase 1 gate; capability agreement
   is M10 and is out of Phase 1 scope.

====================================================================
F. PROJECTION-LIMIT NOTES
====================================================================

Design 7.2 requires the packet to disclose, in band, what a partial typed
projection omits. Implement a small, declared, deterministic set of detectors,
each carrying the evidence it fired on:
- a typed `saves[]` entry with no `damageOnSuccess`, while the record's prose
  contains a success-branch phrase -> note that the projection omits the
  success branch (P3 `creature:adult-black-dragon` action index 5);
- prose describing an area (a "<n>-foot radius/line/cone/cube/sphere" form)
  with no `mechanics.area` present -> note that no typed area exists
  (P3's 60-foot line, P4's 20-foot-radius sphere);
- a record carrying `executionReadiness` clauses that are not `green` -> note
  which clauses are engine-pending and which engines they name.
Keep the detector list short and documented; each must state what it does NOT
detect. A projection-limit note must never be emitted as a capability, and the
prose must be preserved verbatim beside it.

====================================================================
G. MEASUREMENTS M1-M9 (`measurements.ts`)
====================================================================

Computed per probe AND per stage from the returned trace, never persisted:
- M1 must-target retrieval: per must-include target, reached the packet or not.
- M2 loss stage: for each missed must-include target, the exact stage that lost
  it (signals | candidates | expansion | rule-join | dedup | retention |
  packet). Derive this by walking the stage traces, not by guessing.
- M3 preserved route count: routes per retained candidate after dedup vs the
  routes produced before dedup.
- M4 relationship expansion: for each `requiredRelationshipExpansion` entry,
  whether it fired, did not fire, or fired and was later dropped.
- M5 campaign-rule/ruling result: which rules/rulings were requested from the
  seam, which matched, which were placed beside their governing material.
- M6 mandatory-candidate retention: whether every must-consider candidate
  survived; an overflow record fails the probe.
- M7 packet size: bytes and candidate count, plus the recorded reason for each
  related/exploratory drop.
- M8 false authoritative inclusions: any `absent-rules-record`
  must-not-include target present in the packet, and any candidate whose
  provenance is known-false (P12's standing check).
- M9 missing source facts: for each `requiredRetainedFacts` entry with an
  `exactSubstring` or `typedPath`/`expectedValue`, whether it survived into the
  packet. Facts carrying only `statement` prose are NOT machine-checkable:
  report them explicitly as `prose-only-not-checkable`, and never count them as
  satisfied.

Independence rules (design 13.2) — enforce them structurally:
- these are separate fields on a per-probe result; there is no combined score,
  no percentage, no coverage/readiness/completeness figure anywhere in the
  code, the report, or the test names;
- the only permitted aggregate is a COUNT of probes passing;
- add a test asserting that the measurement result type has no aggregate score
  field and that the reporter emits none.

====================================================================
H. TESTS AND THE EVIDENCE THE BEAD REQUIRES
====================================================================

1. `discoverySignals.test.ts` — signal extraction ALONE, per fixture, with no
   downstream stage in the assertion path (design 12.1: a failure at one stage
   must never be hidden by success at another). Assert the expected signal
   kinds and their evidence for each probe, assert `unconsumedStateFields`
   reporting works, and assert the ambiguous-name observation path.
2. `discoveryStages.test.ts` — each stage boundary independently, driven by
   INJECTED inputs (oracle signals / synthetic candidates), covering:
   forward and reverse typed expansion including the exact P5 and P6
   traversals; dedup route preservation and the hard failure when a route
   would be lost; the retention bands and ranking order; a DELIBERATE
   must-consider overflow with a tiny budget, asserting the overflow record
   names every dropped candidate with its routes and that the run is marked
   failed; the packet's 7.3 prohibitions; projection-limit notes on
   `creature:adult-black-dragon` and `spell:fireball`; the preflight
   available/blocked results for `hit-target` and `press-face-1`; the seam
   returning nothing leaving a discovered ambiguity unresolved.
3. `discoveryProbes.test.ts` — every fixture, every execution, end to end
   through `runDiscoveryStages`, computing M1-M9 per probe per stage. Each
   probe asserts:
   - each stage ran (produced output or recorded a loss) — a stage with no
     candidates, no routes and no losses fails the probe as `failed-to-run`;
   - every expected route class from `expectedRouteClasses` is PRESENT on the
     named target (superset allowed; extras are reported in the trace, and a
     `campaign-rule`/`campaign-ruling` route appearing with no active rule
     state is a failure);
   - M1 reaches every must-include target; M6 has no overflow; M8 finds no
     false authoritative inclusion; M9 finds no missing machine-checkable fact;
     M4 fires every declared traversal;
   - the probe result carries `oracleSupplied` labels naming every stage that
     was handed its answer (the two jhpt executions, and any scenario-state
     binding used), so a probe that passed on an oracle is reported as such.
4. `discoveryBoundary.test.ts` (or fold into the stages test) — assert no
   module under `src/orchestrator`, `src/state`, `src/session`, `src/campaign`,
   `src/memory`, or `packages/cli` imports `src/discovery`, and that
   `src/index.ts` does not export it.

The probe test must PRINT nothing that looks like a coverage figure. Report
per-probe results as structured data in assertions.

====================================================================
I. PROHIBITIONS (from the parent bead and ADR 0020) — read them again
====================================================================
- No durable store of ANY kind: no proof store, readiness artifact, finding
  registry, campaign-rule store, second audit database, no file emission.
- No production ranker, embedding model, vector database, or graph database.
- No universal relationship vocabulary, clause ontology, or obligation identity.
- No claim of universal discovery completeness anywhere in code or comments.
- No campaign-rule/ruling schema, storage, resolver, or lifecycle: those are
  `eshyra-jhpt`'s. Discovery may not resolve an ambiguity.
- No runtime integration: the orchestrator seam is W9. Nothing in the existing
  runtime may import the discovery modules.
- Do not weaken the W7 fixtures, `diagnosticFixtureCorpus.test.ts`, or any
  existing audit expectation to make a probe pass.

====================================================================
J. WORKFLOW
====================================================================
Work only inside `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.10.1`, on branch
`eshyra-o9bd.19.10.1`. Follow AGENTS.md: run `npm run verify:worktree` from the
worktree root BEFORE committing (it rewrites files). Commit on the branch.
Record your completion report with `bd update eshyra-o9bd.19.10.1
--append-notes`, file any discovered follow-ups with `bd create`, then
`bd close eshyra-o9bd.19.10.1`.

Then STOP. Do not push, do not open or comment on a PR, do not merge, and do
not close or modify `eshyra-o9bd.19.10`. Integration belongs to the supervisor.

If something in this plan turns out to be wrong against the tree, the tree and
the design document win: record the correction in your bead notes and proceed
with the corrected approach rather than bending a fixture or a test to fit.

description:
Dispatch child of eshyra-o9bd.19.9 (Transition W7). Read `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.9`
for the parent spec and `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.9.3` for the previous round.
This bead repairs the ONE remaining BLOCKING review finding on PR #515, reviewed
at head `7edcf64e14740ddc03f8aa50b7cf0fc40e1bb781`, profile
`rules-clause-complete`. Read the finding first with
`gh pr view 515 --json comments` (the most recent CHANGES REQUIRED comment).

ACCEPTED AND CLOSED — do not redo, do not "improve": the selected-interpretation
chain, the currency gate, the executions split, and the campaign-rule route
mapping. CI is green at the reviewed head; do not chase CI.

The reviewer classifies this repair as NON-MATERIAL provided it stays confined to
correcting P7's no-ruling representation plus fail-closed validation and tests,
changing no scenario meaning. Staying inside that boundary is worth real care: it
is what lets the next review be bounded fix verification instead of a fresh full
review. Do not refactor anything else.

BRANCH / WORKTREE
Branch `eshyra-o9bd.19.9.4`, worktree `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.9.4`, cut from
the parent branch `eshyra-o9bd.19.9` at its current head `c2b66cc` (which already
merged origin/main for PR #516). Work only inside that worktree;
`cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` after entering it.

The supervisor independently confirmed every claim below against the code before
filing this bead. They are real; implement rather than re-arguing, but verify
each mechanism yourself as you fix it.

=== THE DEFECT ===

Field 4 (`campaignRuleState`, active rules/rulings or explicit none) and field 12
(`expectedCampaignRuleOrRulingState`, which rules/rulings must appear) can
contradict each other, and the validator does not stop it. W8 needs both as a
machine-readable oracle; a generic consumer must not need prose interpretation or
P7-specific logic to decide whether a ruling exists.

P7's `without-active-ruling` execution is the concrete instance and, verified by
sweeping all twelve fixtures, the ONLY one:

  campaignRuleState:                    none(...)          <- says no ruling
  expectedRouteClasses:                 no campaign-ruling  <- correct
  expectedCampaignRuleOrRulingState:    campaign-rule-cases containing a case
                                        with ruleKind: 'ruling' whose prose
                                        explains that no ruling was supplied

Field 12 structurally asserts a ruling case while field 4 says none. The
unresolved / owner-`campaign-ruling` expectation already belongs in
`expectedAmbiguityState` and in field 4's own none-statement, so field 12 has
nothing left to carry here and should structurally be explicit none.

Confirmed validator gaps, all fail-open:
  - inactive `campaignRuleState` only prohibits the two campaign routes; it does
    NOT require field 12 to be explicit none;
  - active `campaignRuleState` performs no state->expected-case check at all, so
    field 12 may be explicit none;
  - the resolved-ambiguity <-> ruling-selection agreement check only runs when
    field 12 is `campaign-rule-cases`, so replacing field 12 with explicit none
    skips it entirely;
  - `CampaignRuleCase.ruleKind` is optional, so a case can evade the
    `CAMPAIGN_RULE_ROUTE_BY_KIND` mapping altogether;
  - a `ruling` case is not required to carry its route-evidence identity.

Generalized consequences the reviewer named, both currently accepted by the
validator: P7 with active ruling state and a `campaign-ruling` route but field 12
replaced by explicit none; and P10 with active house-rule state and its
`campaign-rule` route but field 12 replaced by explicit none. P10 is correct
today, but nothing protects that correctness.

=== REQUIRED REPAIR ===

1. P7 `without-active-ruling`: `expectedCampaignRuleOrRulingState` becomes
   explicit `none(...)` with a statement saying no ruling is active and that the
   unresolved state and its `campaign-ruling` owner are carried by the ambiguity
   state. Do not lose the owner fact — confirm it remains visible in
   `expectedAmbiguityState` and/or field 4's none-statement, and strengthen the
   ambiguity statement if it does not already say it. Nothing else about this
   execution changes: still unresolved, still both published interpretations,
   still no `campaign-ruling` route, still no selected interpretation, still
   capability `blocked`.

2. Make the state/result invariants fail closed in `validateDiagnosticCorpus`,
   as generic rules (no probe-specific branches):
   - inactive `campaignRuleState` (kind none) REQUIRES field 12 to be explicit
     none, AND neither `campaign-rule` nor `campaign-ruling` may appear in the
     routes (keep the existing route prohibition);
   - active `campaignRuleState` REQUIRES field 12 to be `campaign-rule-cases`
     with at least one case — explicit none is rejected;
   - every case in an active field 12 MUST declare `ruleKind`, so no case can
     evade the route mapping;
   - a case with `ruleKind: 'ruling'` MUST carry the design's route-evidence
     identity: ruling identity, ambiguity id, and selected interpretation id;
   - PRESERVE the existing resolved-ambiguity <-> ruling-selection agreement
     check, and make sure it can no longer be skipped by swapping field 12 to
     explicit none (the new active-state rule should make that unreachable, but
     confirm it rather than assuming).

3. Keep the `DiagnosticFixture` type, `FIXTURE_KEYS`, `EXECUTION_KEYS`, and the
   validation in sync. If you make a `CampaignRuleCase` field required in a
   context, express that in validation — the optional-in-type / required-in-
   context split is fine, but the validator is the enforcement layer because
   `test/**` is outside `tsc --build`.

Adversarial tests required (add to the existing mutation test):
  - P7 no-ruling execution mutated to carry a `campaign-rule-cases` field 12
    (i.e. today's shape) -> rejected;
  - P7 active-ruling execution with field 12 replaced by explicit none ->
    rejected;
  - P10 active house-rule state with field 12 replaced by explicit none ->
    rejected;
  - a case with `ruleKind` removed -> rejected;
  - a `ruling` case missing its ruling identity / ambiguity id / selected
    interpretation id -> rejected.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
- Test-only. No production code, generated pack data, or schema changes.
- NON-MATERIAL boundary: correct P7's no-ruling representation and add
  fail-closed validation plus tests. Change no other fixture's meaning, and do
  not restructure the contract beyond what these invariants need.
- P7 and P10 remain consumers of the eshyra-jhpt oracle; no discovery-owned
  ruling store, schema, resolver, or lifecycle.
- No fixture asserts a count of records; no coverage/readiness/completeness
  figure over the corpus.
- Every fixture keeps its bounded-evidence statement and `verifiedAtCommit`.
- Do not weaken or edit any existing test or audit expectation.

=== NON-VACUITY IS PART OF THE JOB ===
A previous round shipped a mutation test that was vacuous: it had to satisfy an
upstream invariant to construct its input, so an earlier check rejected it and
the guard under test never ran — the test passed identically with that guard
disabled. For EACH new rule you add: disable that rule alone, confirm the
matching mutation test FAILS, restore, and report what you observed. If a
mutation cannot isolate its guard because validation rejects the input earlier,
say so and unit-test the guard directly instead of pretending the composed case
proves it.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root, BEFORE committing (it rewrites
files). Expected: all non-skipped tests pass; documented skips are the live-API
integration tests and the Dolt-gated checkpoint tests. The one acceptable Biome
finding is the pre-existing biome.json schema-version info.

Adversarial tests reject P7 no-state-with-ruling-case, P7 active-state-with-explicit-none, P10 active-state-with-explicit-none, a case missing ruleKind, and a ruling case missing route-evidence identity. Per-rule non-vacuity demonstrated and reported. No production code, generated pack data, or schema changes; no other fixture meaning changed. npm run verify:worktree passes.

title: Dispatch: encode the concrete selected interpretation and generalize the jhpt route invariant (attempt 1)
description:
Dispatch child of eshyra-o9bd.19.9 (Transition W7). Read `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.9`
for the parent spec, and `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.9.2` for the previous repair
round. This bead repairs the ONE remaining BLOCKING review finding on PR #515,
reviewed at head `c1ac5abe6e37012cdb26997d92b8d12a03e24a40`, profile
`rules-clause-complete`. Read the finding first with
`gh pr view 515 --json comments` (it is the most recent CHANGES REQUIRED
comment).

The previous currency-gate finding is CLOSED and the P7 execution split is
accepted as correctly generalized. Do not redo either. Exact-head CI run
33577075936 is fully green; do not chase CI.

Authority: ADR 0020, design sections 6.2, 8, 10.7, 10.10, and 11 of
docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md.

BRANCH / WORKTREE
Branch `eshyra-o9bd.19.9.3`, worktree `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.9.3`, cut from
the parent branch `eshyra-o9bd.19.9` at its current head. Work only inside that
worktree; `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` after entering it.

The supervisor independently confirmed both halves of this finding against the
code before filing this bead. They are real; implement the repair rather than
re-arguing it, but verify each mechanism yourself as you fix it.

=== HALF A — a resolved ruling must name its selected interpretation ===

Confirmed defect. P7's `with-active-ruling` execution marks the ambiguity
`resolved` and lists BOTH published interpretation ids in `interpretationIds`
(correct — both must stay visible), but neither `campaignRuleState` nor
`expectedCampaignRuleOrRulingState.cases[0]` says WHICH interpretation the
ruling selected. `campaignRuleState` carries only
`{source, ruling: 'active ruling supplied by eshyra-jhpt', scope}`, and the
ruling case carries identity, scope, and provenance but no selection. The oracle
signal claims it supplies the "resolution" while the resolution value is absent.

Consequence: `expectedResolution: 'resolved'` is non-falsifiable for W8. A packet
carrying any ruling — or merely evidence that some ruling exists — would satisfy
the fixture without proving which published interpretation governs the campaign.
The accepted design defines the `campaign-ruling` route evidence as ruling
identity, ambiguity id, AND selected interpretation id, and records that
`eshyra-jhpt.1` already requires a ruling to carry the ambiguity id and selected
interpretation id as provenance. This matters even though `use_item` stays
readiness-blocked: discovery must still place the concrete campaign ruling beside
the ambiguity before DM adjudication.

REQUIRED REPAIR

1. Add `selectedInterpretationId` to `AmbiguityExpectation`.
   - REQUIRED when `expectedResolution === 'resolved'`.
   - FORBIDDEN when `expectedResolution === 'unresolved'` — an unresolved
     ambiguity cannot name a selection, and making the field's meaning
     conditional-but-unambiguous is the point.
   - The validator must reject a `selectedInterpretationId` that is not a member
     of that same expectation's declared `interpretationIds`.

2. Complete the route-evidence triple on the ruling record itself, so a consumer
   can recover identity + ambiguity id + selected interpretation id from the
   ruling case without cross-referencing by convention. A `CampaignRuleCase`
   with `ruleKind: 'ruling'` that resolves an ambiguity must carry the ambiguity
   id and the selected interpretation id, and the validator must reject
   disagreement between the ruling case and the corresponding
   `AmbiguityExpectation`. Model the new ruling-case fields explicitly rather
   than overloading the free-text `scope` string.

3. The currency test must validate `selectedInterpretationId` against the PACK:
   it must resolve as an actual published interpretation id on the named
   ambiguity of the named record (reuse the existing interpretation lookup that
   already checks `interpretationIds`). An unknown or stale selection must fail.

4. P7's `with-active-ruling` execution selects ONE concrete interpretation.
   Recommended: `same-face-resets`, which matches the fixture's player input
   (pressing the already-active face) — but whichever you choose, it is an
   ORACLE-SUPPLIED value owned by eshyra-jhpt, NOT a fact derived from the pack.
   The pack's `canonicalResolution` is null and must stay that way. State that
   distinction in-band, and update the `jhpt-active-ruling` oracle signal's
   `supplies` text so it names the concrete selected interpretation rather than
   a generic "resolution".

5. `without-active-ruling` is unchanged: still `unresolved`, still no
   `campaign-ruling` route, still no selected interpretation, and both published
   interpretations still visible.

6. Capability status stays `blocked` in BOTH executions. The ruling resolves
   interpretation only; it does not make an engine-pending readiness clause
   green. Do not let this change weaken that.

Negative regression evidence required (add to the adversarial mutation test):
  - a resolved expectation with `selectedInterpretationId` removed → rejected;
  - a `selectedInterpretationId` that is not in the declared
    `interpretationIds` → rejected by the validator;
  - a `selectedInterpretationId` that is well-formed but does not exist as a
    published interpretation on the pack's ambiguity (stale/unknown) → rejected
    by the currency assertions;
  - a ruling case whose selected interpretation disagrees with the
    `AmbiguityExpectation` → rejected;
  - an `unresolved` expectation carrying a `selectedInterpretationId` →
    rejected.

=== HALF B — generalize the jhpt state<->route invariant to campaign-rule ===

Confirmed defect. `fixtureContract.ts` around the `noActiveRuling` block
implements only the RULING half: it forbids a `campaign-ruling` route when
`campaignRuleState.kind === 'none'`, and requires one when a case has
`ruleKind: 'ruling'`. There is no symmetric rule for `ruleKind: 'house-rule'`
and the `campaign-rule` route. So the validator would today accept either of:
  - P10 changed to `campaignRuleState: none(...)` while keeping its
    `campaign-rule` route;
  - P10's active house-rule expectation with the `campaign-rule` route removed.
P10 is presently correct, which is exactly why it needs the guard.

REQUIRED REPAIR

Generalize the rule rather than pasting a second hardcoded copy. Drive it from a
single mapping of rule kind to its route class —
`ruling` → `campaign-ruling`, `house-rule` → `campaign-rule` — and apply both
directions uniformly:

description:
Dispatch child of eshyra-o9bd.19.9 (Transition W7). Read `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.9`
for the parent spec, and `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.9.1` for the original

repairs two BLOCKING review findings on PR #515, reviewed at head
`27d5e1b564a888a2ecb326cf3d4151eb9990e4a2`, profile `rules-clause-complete`.
Read both comments on https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/515 with
`gh pr view 515 --json comments` before starting.

Authority: ADR 0020, and design sections 6.1, 6.2, 10.7, 10.11, and 11 of
docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md.

BRANCH / WORKTREE
Branch `eshyra-o9bd.19.9.2`, worktree `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.9.2`, cut from
the parent branch `eshyra-o9bd.19.9` at its current head. Work only inside that
worktree; `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` after entering it.

The supervisor independently confirmed every sub-finding below against the code
before filing this bead. They are real; do not re-litigate them. Verify the
mechanics yourself as you fix them.

=== FINDING 2 (material — contract semantics change). Fix this first. ===

P7 collapses two mutually exclusive executions into one fixture. Today:
`campaignRuleState.cases` is the bare array
`['without-active-ruling', 'with-active-ruling-supplied-by-eshyra-jhpt']`;
the single `expectedRouteClasses` entry unconditionally requires
`campaign-ruling`; `expectedAmbiguityState` declares a single `unresolved`
expectation; and `expectedCampaignRuleOrRulingState` carries two cases. Those
cannot all describe one execution: with no active ruling there is no
`campaign-ruling` route by definition and the ambiguity stays unresolved; with
an active ruling that route exists and carries the supplied identity and
provenance. W8 measures preserved retrieval routes and campaign-rule/ruling
matches, so a generic harness cannot evaluate P7 without inventing P7-specific
semantics for the `cases` array — which defeats W7's purpose as the durable
diagnostic oracle.

REQUIRED SHAPE — make executions first-class and GENERIC, not P7-special.

Split `DiagnosticFixture` into scenario-level fields and a non-empty
`executions` list. Scenario-level (shared by every execution of the scenario):
`playerInput`, `campaignState`, `adventureState`, `mustIncludeTargets`,
`mayIncludeTargets`, `mustNotIncludeTargets`, `requiredRetainedFacts`,
`requiredRelationshipExpansion`, plus the metadata (`probeId`, `title`,
`verifiedAtCommit`, `gatingBlocker`, `boundedEvidenceStatement`).

Each `FixtureExecution` carries its own exact:
`executionId` (stable, kebab-case, unique within the fixture);
`campaignRuleState` (section-11 field 4, `ExplicitNone | Record`);
`expectedRouteClasses` (field 8);
`expectedAmbiguityState` (field 11);
`expectedCampaignRuleOrRulingState` (field 12);
`expectedCapabilityStatus` (field 13);
`expectedDeterministicStateEffect`;
`oracleSignals` (an execution that consumes a supplied answer must label it
there, so the label travels with the execution that actually used it).

Every one of the thirteen section-11 fields must still be declared for every
execution — nested, not dropped. Eleven fixtures become a mechanical
single-execution wrap; only P7 gets two. Do NOT introduce a "primary execution
plus alternates" shape: uniformity is the point, because the reviewer's core
objection is that a generic downstream harness must be able to enumerate
executions without probe-specific knowledge.

P7's two executions, exactly:
  1. `without-active-ruling` — `campaignRuleState` explicitly none-active;
     routes for `magic-item:cube-of-force` are `direct-state-ref` and
     `capability-preflight` and MUST NOT include `campaign-ruling`; ambiguity
     `ambiguity:cube-of-force-same-face-duration-reset` expected `unresolved`
     with both interpretation ids; `expectedCampaignRuleOrRulingState` carries
     only the no-ruling case; `oracleSignals` is empty; capability status
     `blocked`.
  2. `with-active-ruling` — `campaignRuleState` carries the jhpt-supplied active
     ruling; routes include `campaign-ruling` alongside `direct-state-ref` and
     `capability-preflight`; ambiguity expected `resolved`; the ruling appears
     with identity, scope, and provenance, all owned by eshyra-jhpt and NOT
     invented here; `oracleSignals` carries the `jhpt-active-ruling` label;
     capability status is STILL `blocked`, because the readiness clauses are
     engine-pending independently of ruling resolution. That invariance is the
     whole point of the probe — state it explicitly in both executions.

This must remain a CONSUMER of the eshyra-jhpt oracle. Do not create a
discovery-owned ruling store, schema, resolver, or lifecycle (design §8.4).

Regression evidence required (new assertions in the currency test):
  - no-ruling execution → no `campaign-ruling` route anywhere in it, and the
    ambiguity is unresolved;
  - active-ruling execution → a `campaign-ruling` route is present, and the
    supplied ruling identity/provenance is present and labelled as an oracle
    signal;
  - capability readiness is `blocked` in BOTH executions.

=== FINDING 1 (enforcement hardening — must not change fixture meanings) ===

The currency gate is selectively fail-open. Five defects, all confirmed:

1. `stable-id.idKind` is not enforced semantically. `assertSelector`'s
   `operation` and `clause` branches are byte-identical and both call the
   recursive `findById`, which matches any `id`, `clauseId`, or `via`. An
   operation could vanish while the same string survived in another identifier
   role and the gate would stay green. Make each selector kind check the
   identifier role it actually names: an `operation` id must resolve as an
   operation id (including a state-machine `via` operation), a `clause` id must
   resolve as a clause id. Locate the real shapes in the pack
   (`data.mechanics.operations[].id`, `data.executionReadiness.clauses[].clauseId`,
   `data.mechanics.stateMachine.transitions[].via`) rather than pattern-matching
   any key named `id`.

2. P7's declared interpretation ids (`same-face-resets`,
   `different-face-only-resets`) are never verified against the pack. The
   currency test checks the ambiguity id only. Verify every declared
   `interpretationIds` entry resolves as an actual interpretation id on the
   named record's ambiguity, and verify the declared `expectedResolution` is
   consistent with the pack's `canonicalResolution` for the no-ruling execution
   (the pack has `canonicalResolution: null`).

3. `validateDiagnosticCorpus` requires each supplied route to point at a
   must-include target, but never requires that every unique must-include
   target HAS route coverage. A required candidate can silently lose field-8
   coverage. Require, per execution, that every unique must-include target
   reference appears in that execution's `expectedRouteClasses`.

4. P11 declares the synthetic add-on `rules:test-cursed-attunement-addon`
   version `1.0.0` overriding `magic-item:ring-of-protection`, but nothing binds
   that declaration to its real producer,
   `packages/core/test/support/cursedAttunementAddon.ts` (which defines
   `OVERRIDDEN_ITEM_REF = 'magic-item:ring-of-protection'` at :11, packId at :47,
   version at :51). The declaration is correct today but nothing keeps it
   current. The cited `campaignRulesStackParity.test.ts` proves the repaired
   resolver class with a DIFFERENT synthetic stack; it does not pin P11's
   identity. Bind P11's declared pack identity, version, and overridden record
   to the producer module — import from it and assert equality, or export the
   identities from the producer and have P11 consume them. Prefer consuming the
   producer's own exported constants so the two cannot drift.

5. There is no adversarial regression suite for the validator. The real corpus
   passing proves current examples, not that the gate rejects bad input. The
   `findingRegistry` pattern this work cites DOES include mutation-based
   rejection tests. Add adversarial mutation tests that deep-clone the real
   corpus, mutate one thing, and assert `validateDiagnosticCorpus` (or the
   currency assertions) reject it. Cover at minimum: wrong selector kind;
   a selector identity that no longer resolves; a must-include target with no
   route coverage; a missing probe; a duplicate probe id; a duplicate
   `executionId` within a fixture; an unanchored `exactSubstring` (the
   already-designed rejection); an unknown route class; an unlabelled oracle
   signal; and P7's no-ruling execution mutated to carry a `campaign-ruling`
   route.

HARD CONSTRAINTS
- Test-only. No production code, generated pack data, or schema changes.
- Finding 1 is enforcement hardening: it must NOT change any fixture's meaning.
  If hardening a check makes a real fixture fail, the fixture's claim was wrong
  — fix the claim and say so in-band; do not weaken the check.
- No discovery implementation, no stage harness, no runtime integration.
- No fixture asserts a count of records; no coverage, readiness, or
  completeness figure over the corpus. Asserting twelve probes exist and that a
  fixture has N executions is contract structure, not a corpus count, and is
  fine.
- Every fixture keeps its bounded-evidence statement and `verifiedAtCommit`.
- P7 and P10 stay consumers of eshyra-jhpt; no second ruling model.
- Do not weaken or edit any existing test or audit expectation.
- Keep `VERIFIED_AT_COMMIT` current: if you re-verify at a newer merge base,
  update it and say why in the comment above it.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root, BEFORE committing (it rewrites
files). Expected: all non-skipped tests pass; documented skips are the live-API
integration tests and the Dolt-gated checkpoint tests. The one acceptable Biome
finding is the pre-existing biome.json schema-version info (config 2.5.5,
installed 2.5.10).

P7 declares two executions (without-active-ruling, with-active-ruling) whose routes, ambiguity resolution, and ruling state differ correctly and whose capability status is blocked in both. Selector checking respects the selector discriminant semantically. P7 interpretation identities are verified against the pack. Every unique must-include target has route coverage per execution. P11's synthetic add-on identity is bound to cursedAttunementAddon.ts. Adversarial mutation tests reject wrong selector kind, unresolvable selector identity, missing route coverage, missing probe, duplicate probe id, duplicate executionId, unanchored exactSubstring, unknown route class, unlabelled oracle signal, and a campaign-ruling route in P7's no-ruling execution. No production code, generated pack data, or schema changes. npm run verify:worktree passes.

title: Dispatch: pin audit aliases to canonical findings (attempt 2)
description:
Dispatch for eshyra-o9bd.19.1.15 (Foundation 2). Attempt 2 — bounded fix for the
single blocking finding on PR #507 review at head eff62bb.

## The finding (accepted; the reviewer is right)

Stable audit alias identity is no longer pinned to its canonical finding.

The shipped validator has two INDEPENDENT flat rosters — `CANONICAL_FINDING_IDS`
(68) and `FINDING_ALIASES` (70) — and only checks set equality plus uniqueness.
Nothing pins WHICH aliases belong to WHICH canonical row. So two rows can trade
aliases and `validateFindingRegistry` still accepts the registry, as long as
`provenance.auditFinding` is swapped along with them (the provenance check only
asserts membership in the row's OWN alias list, so it moves with the swap).

Concrete case named by the reviewer: `indep:001` (`audit-readiness-gate`) and
`sol:CAP-001` (`rule-corpus-procedures`) can trade. Those two aliases were
deliberately SPLIT into separate rows by a reviewed #476 correction because they
name distinct defects with different owners and recurrence boundaries. The hole
generalizes to all 68 rows / 70 aliases.

This is a regression against #476, which is the authority here: at head 9133201
`packages/core/src/rules/findingRegistry.ts:273` defines

    const CANONICAL_ROW_ROSTER: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>

and `canonicalRosterBlockers` (line ~1190) compares each row's alias array to
the roster entry for its canonicalId, SORTED on both sides, plus
duplicate/unexpected/missing canonicalId detection. Read that function before
writing the replacement:

    git show 9133201:packages/core/src/rules/findingRegistry.ts | sed -n '273,300p;1190,1235p'

## Required change — `packages/core/src/rules/findingRegistry.ts`

1. Replace the two flat rosters with ONE exact roster:

       export const CANONICAL_ROW_ROSTER: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>

   68 entries, in the registry's row order, each mapping canonicalId -> its
   exact alias list. Build it from the committed
   `docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.json` so it cannot drift;
   do not retype it by hand. Two rows have two aliases each
   (`rock-gnome-boundary`: indep:010 + sol:CAP-012; `point-origin-areas`:
   opus:F-08 + fable:F2); every other row has one.

2. KEEP both existing exports, derived from the roster so they cannot disagree
   with it:
       CANONICAL_FINDING_IDS  = Object.keys(CANONICAL_ROW_ROSTER)
       FINDING_ALIASES        = every alias, sorted
   They are already exported from internal.ts and asserted in tests; keep the
   names and the 68/70 counts.

3. Validation, replacing the two `exactSet(...)` calls at the end of
   `validateFindingRegistry`:
   - each row's `canonicalId` must be a roster key; if not -> unexpected
   - each row's alias list must equal that key's roster entry EXACTLY, compared
     sorted on both sides (match #476: sorted, not order-sensitive)
   - every roster key must appear exactly once across the rows -> missing /
     duplicate
   Keep the existing duplicate-canonicalId and cross-row duplicate-alias checks
   as belt-and-braces; they fire earlier and with clearer messages.
   Error messages must name the offending canonicalId, and the missing/unexpected
   wording must stay greppable — the existing tests assert
   /canonicalId set mismatch.*missing/ and /canonicalId set mismatch.*unexpected/,
   so either keep phrasing that still matches or update those two assertions in
   the same commit. Do not leave a test asserting a message the code no longer
   emits.

4. Everything else in the module stays as-is. Do NOT reintroduce any Foundation
   3 / Foundation 4 field, do not touch the deny-list, do not add a pack or
   subprocess read. The registry JSON itself does not change.

## Required regression test — `packages/core/test/findingRegistry.test.ts`

Add a test that swaps aliases between two canonical rows AND swaps their
`provenance.auditFinding` with them, then asserts validation rejects it. Use the
reviewer's pair: `audit-readiness-gate` (indep:001) and `rule-corpus-procedures`
(sol:CAP-001). The provenance swap is the point — without it the existing
provenance check would catch the mutation and the test would pass for the wrong
reason. Assert the thrown message names one of the two canonicalIds.

Also add: `CANONICAL_ROW_ROSTER` has 68 keys and 70 aliases total, and every
row's aliases equal its roster entry (a positive pin over the real registry, not
just the negative case).

Keep every existing test passing. Do not weaken an existing assertion to fit the
new code; if an existing message assertion must change, change it deliberately
and say so in your completion notes.

## Constraints

- Do NOT regenerate any rules pack; `packages/core/data/` is untouched.
- Do NOT modify `docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.json` or
  `finding-registry.md` unless the doc's validator paragraph becomes inaccurate
  — if it does, update that paragraph only.
- `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing (it rewrites files).
notes: COMPLETION REPORT 2026-08-30: Implemented the bounded PR #507 fix in commit e8b9b34. Replaced the independent canonical/alias flat rosters with CANONICAL_ROW_ROSTER generated from docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.json; derived CANONICAL_FINDING_IDS and FINDING_ALIASES; exported the roster through @eshyra/core/internal; added per-canonical sorted alias validation while retaining duplicate and set checks; added positive 68-key/70-alias pin coverage and the audit-readiness-gate/rule-corpus-procedures alias+provenance swap regression. npm run verify:worktree passed: 264 test files passed, 4 skipped; 4743 tests passed, 19 skipped. Pre-existing Biome schema info (2.5.5 vs installed 2.5.10) remains tracked by existing follow-up eshyra-wyga. No rules-pack or registry JSON changes.

title: Fix stale Codex dispatch recipe and make the beads protocol mandatory in supervisor context
description:
Two defects in the Codex-subagent supervisor workflow injected by
`.claude/hooks/supervisor-context.mjs`, both surfaced by a user correction on
2026-08-29 after they caused a bad dispatch on eshyra-o9bd.19.1.15.1.

1. STALE LAUNCH RECIPE. A previous session created
   `/home/jhbongaarts/.claude/dispatch-codex.sh` and allowlisted exactly that
   path in auto mode (`Bash(/home/jhbongaarts/.claude/dispatch-codex.sh:*)` in
   `~/.claude/settings.json`), but never updated
   `.claude/hooks/codex-subagent-workflow.md`. The doc still taught a hand-rolled
   `setsid … codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox …` command
   line, which is NOT allowlisted, so the auto-mode classifier refuses it. A
   supervisor following the injected doc literally cannot dispatch.

2. NO STATED RULE THAT THE BEADS PROTOCOL IS MANDATORY. The doc showed a launch
   prompt using `bd show` / `bd update --append-notes` / `bd create` / `bd close`
   but never said the channel is non-negotiable. When the launch above was
   refused, the supervisor downgraded to `--sandbox workspace-write` and rewrote
   the prompt to say "Do NOT run `bd`", passing the spec as a `.dispatch-plan.md`
   file and taking the report back as `.dispatch-report.md`. Because bd and git
   metadata both live in the PARENT checkout, that sandbox also blocked the
   child's commit, so the supervisor committed and closed the bead on its behalf.
   The task record was stranded outside Dolt, never reached `bd dolt push`, and
   was invisible to any other machine, Codex session, or future supervisor.

FIX (this bead): rewrite the Dispatch defaults section around
`dispatch-codex.sh`, replace the raw `setsid` block with a description of what
the script already guarantees (leader records its own `$$`, exec preserves the
PGID, runs in the child worktree, registry beside the worktrees, prior log kept
as .bak), add "if a dispatch launch is refused, STOP AND ASK", and add a new
subsection making the beads protocol non-negotiable with the 2026-08-29
violation recorded.

NOT DONE HERE, deliberately: the supervisor policy stays out of AGENTS.md,
CLAUDE.md, bd memories and bead descriptions, per the doc's own header — those
are all readable by Codex and Claude subagents, which must not receive
supervisor instructions. This bead description is the exception only insofar as
it states the defect, not the policy.
notes:
PR #509 open: https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/509 (branch eshyra-wmph, head 4eac24f). Docs-only. verify:worktree green (263 files/4732 tests, 0 failures). Leave in_progress until merged. Deliberately NOT recorded as a bd memory: bd memories reach Codex subagents via bd prime, and supervisor policy must not.
=== MERGED 2026-08-30 ===
PR #509 merged as bfa84da. Branch deleted local and remote; worktree removed. The injected
supervisor context now leads with /home/jhbongaarts/.claude/dispatch-codex.sh and makes the
beads protocol non-negotiable. Both fixes were exercised in the same session: the attempt-2
dispatch (eshyra-o9bd.19.1.15.2) launched through the approved script under YOLO and the
child read its spec, filed its report and closed its own bead entirely through bd.

## Why `title` becomes `invariant`

#476's typed `invariant` object was
`{kind:"source-semantic-preservation", dimensions:[branches,alternatives,timing,
lifecycle,termination], evidence:{kind:"audit-finding", locator:…}}` — and it was

content. The actual per-row generalized invariant prose is the `title` string,
which is already phrased as a durable "what must remain true" statement
("Ki abilities and save DC are structured", "Madness durations are retained").

So F2 carries the prose forward under its honest name and drops the uniform
typed object. Do NOT invent new per-row prose — that would be source invention.

(eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7 / .19.1.8). Do NOT ship them as reserved-but-empty

AC2 reads: "Audit fact, provenance, alias/status, owner, baseline membership,
current violation membership and closure evidence are separable fields."

title: Transition W13: normalize the ADR 0020 bounded capability contract
description:
Workstream W13 of the integrated ADR 0020 transition design (sections 5.4, 5.5,
7.2, and the ADR 0020 section 3 capability contract):
docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md.
That design is the accepted deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8 (PR #485, reviewed
head afd113c7090378c3a9f4122f246a6c32602a5164, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282). ADR 0020 controls. This bead is the
eshyra-olc5 owner of capability-contract shape.

OWNER
This bead owns the normalized shape of a deterministic capability contract under
ADR 0020. No other bead owns it.

SCOPE
Define and apply the positive capability contract. Every capability in force
declares, in band:

1. the operation it performs;
2. its required inputs;
3. its exclusions - what it explicitly does not do;
4. its revision or identity;
5. what interpretation remains with the DM;

and fails closed on unrecognized input.

The first real contract is assertMagicItemOperationReady
(packages/core/src/state/itemExecutionReadiness.ts, revision
derived-magic-item-clauses-v1), which is also the only capability in the
repository carrying an explicit revision identity today. Its unrecognized-scope
fail-open is repaired by eshyra-uiax (B5); this bead normalizes the contract
shape, it does not re-own that repair. The implemented rows of
ENGINE_PROCEDURE_COVERAGE - restated as positive deterministic-capability
bindings by the W14 split - are the input set for the rest.

BOUNDED MEANING OF engine:F1-engine:F10 (design section 5.5)
engine:F1-F10 is the GENERATED MAGIC-ITEM CAPABILITY BACKLOG: 240 magic-item
records carrying executionReadiness, 1,016 clauses, 795 clauses declaring engine
hooks. No other record kind carries executionReadiness. It is not a corpus-wide
engine inventory, and this bead does not make it one. A green clause may still
declare an engine hook (magic-item:candle-of-invocation/c1-burn-time), so "green"
is not interchangeable with "hook-free", and neither the 794 engine-pending count
nor the 795 hook-carrying count may be reported as a capability inventory.

NON-GOALS AND PROHIBITIONS
- No corpus-wide capability inventory, and no claim of corpus-wide capability
  completeness.
- No widening of engine:F1-F10 beyond the generated magic-item backlog.
- No global deterministic-closure claim, and no revival of the withdrawn
  zero-engine-pending bar.
- Absence of a capability binding is a statement about Eshyra, not about the
  rules: it means only that no deterministic capability was positively selected.
  It never means the record has no mechanics, the rule is irrelevant, or the pack
  is complete. "Unbound", "unclassified", and "not recognized" are not safety
  properties.
- A deterministic operation does not imply a complete record: one clause of a
  record may be a positively executable capability while another has no engine
  owner (magic-item:ammunition-1-2-or-3 exhibits exactly that).
- No capability may be inferred from the presence of typed fields.
- Taxonomy hazard preserved: engine:F1-F10, the CLOSED epic eshyra-2n1t's
  different F1-F10, and the fable:F1-F8 findings are unrelated namespaces.

DEPENDENCIES
eshyra-uiax (B5, fail-closed repair on the pilot contract) and the approved
ENGINE_PROCEDURE_COVERAGE split owned by W14 (design section 5.4 part 2, the
positive deterministic-capability bindings). Contract-shape design is
parallel-safe; applying it to the split rows is not.

PERMANENT EVIDENCE
For each capability in force, an in-band declaration of the five fields and a
test that feeds unrecognized input and asserts the failure; an assertion that no
capability is derived from typed-field presence; an in-band statement of the
bounded meaning of engine:F1-F10 wherever the families are reported.

REQUIRED NEXT STATE
Every positively selected capability declares operation, inputs, exclusions,
revision/identity, and residual interpretation, and fails closed on unrecognized
input. The eshyra-olc5 capability families are reassessed against the bounded
magic-item scope rather than deleted: the underlying magic-item obligations
remain real.

MATERIAL CHANGE: yes. It defines the capability-contract shape that ADR 0020
section 3 requires.
acceptance_criteria:
Every deterministic capability in force declares, in band, its operation, its
required inputs, its exclusions, its revision or identity, and the interpretation
that remains with the DM; each has a test that feeds an unrecognized or
malformed input and asserts fail-closed behavior rather than a skip or a pass.
assertMagicItemOperationReady (derived-magic-item-clauses-v1) is restated in that
shape once eshyra-uiax has repaired its unrecognized-scope fail-open, and the
implemented rows produced by the W14 ENGINE_PROCEDURE_COVERAGE split are restated
in the same shape. No capability is inferred from the presence of typed pack
fields. Every report of engine:F1-engine:F10 states in band that the families are
the generated magic-item capability backlog (240 magic-item records with
executionReadiness, 1,016 clauses, 795 declaring engine hooks) and not a
corpus-wide engine inventory; no readiness or engine-hook count is presented as a
capability inventory, and a green clause carrying an engine hook is handled
correctly. Nothing in this work claims corpus-wide capability completeness,
global deterministic closure, or that an absent capability binding says anything
about the rules; absence is reported only as "no deterministic capability
positively selected". The engine:F* / eshyra-2n1t F* / fable:F* namespace
distinction is preserved wherever the families are named.

title: Transition W10: context-packet intervention through the provider-neutral adapter seam (Phase 3)
description:
Workstream W10 of the integrated ADR 0020 transition design, Phase 3 (section
12.3), with the packet contract in section 7:
docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md.
That design is the accepted deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8 (PR #485, reviewed
head afd113c7090378c3a9f4122f246a6c32602a5164, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282). ADR 0020 controls.

OWNER
This bead is the single owner of context-packet intervention: the first change to
what the DM actually receives. No other bead owns it.

SCOPE
Inject the discovery context packet in scripted, provider-neutral tests and
compare against the recorded shadow baseline. Provider-neutral means through the
existing adapter seam (ADR 0010), not through one provider's agent loop.

The packet carries, per retained candidate (design section 7.1): canonical record
identity; source provenance and licence identity; the exact source prose the
fixture requires; every retrieval reason; traversed relationships; known source
ambiguity with its interpretations; the applicable campaign rule or ruling from
eshyra-jhpt with identity, scope, provenance, and supersession status;
deterministic capability availability with inputs, exclusions, revision, and
residual DM interpretation; and explicit projection-limit notes.

Observe: whether must-include material reaches the DM; whether routes survive
dedup; whether mandatory candidates survive budgets; whether source prose stays
intact; whether partial-projection limits are explicit; whether campaign rules
and rulings carry correct scope and provenance; whether capability limits are
shown correctly; auditor retries; explicit citations or tool calls; accepted
deterministic state effects. Report M1-M12 against the recorded baseline.

PROHIBITIONS (design sections 7.2, 7.3, 13.2)
- A typed projection is never presented as complete merely because it exists,
  and never converts into deterministic readiness. Source prose stays verbatim
  and authoritative; the projection's omissions are disclosed in band beside it
  (the verified worked cases are creature:adult-black-dragon /data/actions/5 and
  spell:fireball's missing typed area).
- A must-consider candidate never disappears silently. Overflow is explicit,
  names every dropped candidate and its routes, and fails the probe.
- A record whose provenance is known false is never laundered into the packet as
  authority (probe P12).
- "No capability bound" is never presented as "no mechanics", "irrelevant", or
  "safe to ignore"; capability availability is a positive bounded contract with

SCOPE
Run discovery in shadow mode on real turns, after assembleContext and before
renderContextMessage (the seam verified at orchestrator.ts:561 and :576), and
record, without altering DM input:

- explicit and derived signals;
- candidates and every retrieval route;
- relationship traversals;
- campaign-rule and ruling matches obtained through the eshyra-jhpt read seam;
- dedup decisions;
- priority band and retained candidates;
- rejected candidates, each with its reason;
- the proposed context packet;
- capability preflight results.

Shadow evidence attaches to the existing accepted-turn trace authority
(memory/turnTrace.ts TurnTraceRecord, written at orchestrator.ts:817) or returns
through that existing trace seam.

NON-GOALS AND PROHIBITIONS
- The DM sees exactly what it sees today. No packet is injected; changing DM
  input is W10.
- No competing readiness database, second campaign-rule store, or second finding
  registry (ADR 0017 section 8; ADR 0020 audit-architecture restraint).
- No discovery-owned campaign-rule persistence, ruling schema, or lifecycle;
  those stay with eshyra-jhpt.
- No claim of universal discovery completeness and no aggregate coverage figure.
  Measurements stay independent per probe and per stage.
- Presence of material in a shadow packet is never reported as evidence that the
  model used it.

BASELINE VALIDITY (design section 9.6)
Shadow evidence gathered before the applicable baseline repairs is diagnostic
only and may not be called a baseline. Specifically: no stat-block probe
evidence before B1 (eshyra-l3e5); no adventure-context evidence (P9) before B2
(eshyra-seoh); no deterministic-agreement measurement (M11) before B3
(eshyra-6vpw); no capability-agreement evidence (P8) before B5 (eshyra-uiax);
and table:starting-wealth-by-class is never treated as SRD authority at any time
(B4, eshyra-o9bd.19.2.1).

DEPENDENCIES
W8 accepted (Phase 1 exit criteria met), plus the baseline repairs applicable to
the probes being shadowed: eshyra-l3e5 (W1), eshyra-seoh (W2), eshyra-6vpw (W3),
eshyra-uiax (W5). Not parallel-safe with its own prerequisites.

PERMANENT EVIDENCE
Shadow traces for the probe corpus over real turns, attached to the existing
TurnTraceRecord seam; a test proving DM input is byte-identical with and without
shadow discovery enabled; M1-M11 derivable from the recorded trace without
re-running discovery.

REQUIRED NEXT STATE
Shadow traces exist for the probe corpus over real turns; every section-13
measurement through M11 is derivable from the trace; no new durable store was
introduced; each trace records which blockers were repaired at capture time so a
pre-repair capture can never be mistaken for a baseline.

MATERIAL CHANGE: yes. It adds a runtime observation point in the turn pipeline,
without changing what the DM receives.
acceptance_criteria:
Discovery runs after assembleContext and before renderContextMessage on real

TurnTraceRecord) or returns through that existing trace seam; no competing
readiness store, campaign-rule store, or finding registry is created. Both
retained and rejected candidates are recorded with every retrieval route and
every rejection reason, and dedup preserves all routes. Campaign rules and
rulings come only from the eshyra-jhpt read seam. Each capture records which

Its violated invariant was not an authorized W9 invariant: the finding rested on the assumption that a durable trace must detect semantically coordinated post-persistence mutation and must recursively re-derive producer observations from lower-level stored facts.
