=========================================================================
PHASE-2 EVIDENCE TRUST MODEL (owner-authorized clarification, 2026-09-10)
=========================================================================
This clarification is design authority for W9 and for any successor reading design section 12.2's exit criteria. It resolves the review churn caused by reading "M1-M11 derivable from the trace without re-running discovery" as if it required the durable trace to be a self-authenticating semantic proof object. That reading was TOO STRONG. The accepted Phase-2 requirement is a DATA-SUFFICIENCY requirement over internally produced observational traces, not an arbitrary-tamper-detection requirement.

TRUST MODEL. discovery-shadow-v1 is an INTERNAL EXPERIMENTAL OBSERVATION FORMAT produced by Eshyra's W9 runtime instrumentation and persisted through the existing accepted-turn trace authority. A valid Phase-2 trace is assumed to originate from that producer and to have survived the ordinary persistence/JSON round trip.
The durable reader is responsible for FAIL-CLOSED ADMISSION of the stored format wherever malformed data could make measurement undefined or silently weaken meaning. It must reject, where applicable:
- an unknown schema version;
- missing or malformed required identity;
- unknown values in closed semantic discriminants where treating "unknown" as some weaker known case could false-green a measurement;
- structurally incomplete discriminated unions;
- impossible lifecycle shapes;
- missing required decision/event membership that would cause evidence to disappear silently;
- malformed values that measurement code would otherwise reinterpret as absence.
The reader is NOT responsible for detecting arbitrary post-persistence semantic tampering, nor for proving that every otherwise well-formed producer-owned observation really occurred. In particular it need not detect an attacker or hypothetical mutation that consistently rewrites several semantically related, otherwise valid fields. SQLite/turn-trace storage is NOT a hostile trust boundary in W9.
If future requirements need tamper evidence, cross-version forensic replay, cryptographic authenticity, or hostile-store validation, that is a SEPARATE design requirement and must be explicitly authorized, never inferred from Phase 2.

MEANING OF "DERIVABLE". For W9, M1-M11 are "derivable from the recorded trace without re-running discovery" when, after the trace has been persisted through the existing turn-trace seam and read back, the measurement functions can compute M1-M11 without rerunning discovery, resolving the live rules stack again, repeating jhpt rule/ruling queries, reinvoking deterministic capability preflight, or rerunning the turn auditor.
Producer-owned observations, events and decisions are LEGITIMATE PRIMITIVE INPUTS to those measurements. They do not need to be re-derived from some lower-level stored representation merely because another representation could imply them. Legitimate producer-owned primitive evidence includes: stage execution outcome; a relationship traversal that actually fired; a retention decision and its reason; a packet inclusion/exclusion decision and its reason; a jhpt seam query/result; a real capability-preflight invocation; an auditor retry/lifecycle event. The design does not recursively require every such observation to be proven from another durable fact.

REDUNDANCY RULE (replaces the over-strong working rule). The working rule "every semantically irreducible fact must appear exactly once, and every implication must be derived" is REPLACED by the narrower operational rule:
  Each M1-M11 measurement has a designated authoritative evidence source. Convenience or diagnostic fields may coexist when useful, provided measurement does not combine contradictory copies in a way that can false-green normal internally produced evidence.
Do not reopen the current implementation merely because two stored observations have semantic implications for one another. A redundancy becomes a W9 defect ONLY when, under the supported producer/persistence/reader path, it can cause the measurement implementation to report a materially different result from the evidence source designated for that measurement. Arbitrary coordinated editing of persisted JSON is OUTSIDE this Phase-2 threat model.

STAGE OUTCOMES. ran / skipped / failed-to-run are PRODUCER-OWNED STAGE OBSERVATIONS under the Phase-1/Phase-2 experiment contract. They do not have to be inferred by the durable reader solely from output membership. Their meanings remain those of the accepted design:
- ran: the stage performed its defined work, INCLUDING a seam query that executed and returned no results;
- skipped: one of the specifically conditional stages had nothing applicable to do;
- failed-to-run: a non-conditional stage produced no usable stage evidence under the experiment's diagnostic accounting.
skipped remains DISTINCT FROM SUCCESS. failed-to-run remains NON-GREEN (design section 13.3; ADR 0020 section 3). The reader should validate closed lifecycle vocabulary and structurally impossible combinations where useful, but it is NOT required to rediscover the stage's execution history independently.

BASELINE QUALIFICATION. Authoritative Phase-2 baseline eligibility comes from the accepted transition plan (section 9.6 entry criteria) PLUS the actual resolved dependency/blocker state for the experiment. A trace does NOT have to independently prove that repository history contains every prerequisite repair.
Capture-local B1-B5 observations remain useful DIAGNOSTIC evidence about what the trace could discriminate at runtime. A 'not-discriminable' observation -- especially B2, whose repair is a CLI handoff outside core's observation boundary -- does NOT mean the prerequisite is unrepaired and does NOT invalidate an otherwise eligible Phase-2 trace. Pre-repair evidence remains diagnostic-only exactly as the integrated design requires (section 9.6; section 12.2 entry criteria).
Do not infer baseline eligibility from a vacuous or incomplete blocker list; equally, do not require the runtime trace to self-certify repository/process history.
B3/M11 ERRATUM RETAINED (see DESCRIPTION ERRATUM below): B3 gates the Phase-3 deterministic state-effect agreement measurement M12, NOT the Phase-2 M11 auditor retry count.

FORMAT LIFETIME. discovery-shadow-v1 is a PHASE-2 EXPERIMENTAL EVIDENCE FORMAT, not a public protocol and not a permanent canonical replay schema. W9 requires: current-format production; persistence through the existing turn-trace seam; successful current-format reread; and M1-M11 data sufficiency. It does NOT establish a promise of indefinite backward-compatible migration for every historical shadow schema. Unknown/unsupported schema versions must FAIL EXPLICITLY rather than become "no evidence". A future workstream may define migration/forensic compatibility if it becomes necessary.

=========================================================================
ACCEPTED AT THE APPROVED HEAD (8b67c33, review #5163108225)
=========================================================================
- M10 remains producer-observed at the real capability-preflight boundary, with exact capability and subject identity, audit-rejected-attempt preservation, and NO change to the public use_item result contract.
- Retention and packet dispositions are producer-owned decisions carrying explicit reasons.
- Expansion traversal events are stage-local producer events, so the same traversal may fire in BOTH bounded passes even when cumulative candidate state does not change.
- Closed discovery discriminants fail closed where an unknown value could soften measurement meaning; campaign-rule kind is validated from the jhpt/campaign owner rather than redefined by discovery.
- M11 derives from the recorded audit lifecycle.
- All authored W7 execution cases, including BOTH P7 executions, are exercised over real turns.
- The trace attaches to the existing TurnTraceRecord authority; no competing store.
- Shadow mode does not alter DM/model input.
- Packet intervention remains W10 (eshyra-o9bd.19.12).

=========================================================================
IMPLEMENTATION AS MERGED
=========================================================================
EVENT VS STATE (review 7 repair). A canonical fact is of exactly one of two kinds and neither is reconstructed from the other:
- STATE = what exists after a stage (candidate streams, packet content, a candidate's cumulative .traversals);
- EVENT/DECISION = what happened while it ran (a relationship the pass traversed, a candidate it excluded and why).
Producer-owned DECISIONS: retention dispositions (recorded at the ranking/budget comparison) and packet inclusion decisions (recorded at the byte comparison), both as the discriminated CandidateDisposition, so an exclusion cannot exist without its reason and a retained decision cannot carry one. The live RetentionTrace/PacketTrace convenience views (outputs, dropped, overflow, overflowed, losses, byte drops, byte overflow) are DERIVED from those lists, which also collapsed the two competing strings for one count-budget rejection into a single causal reason.
Producer-owned EVENTS: ProjectedExpansionStage.traversalEvents, copied from ExpansionTrace.traversals. Defining a stage's traversals as "newly appearing on the candidate stream" was false under the bounded two-pass architecture -- a relationship promoted into campaign-rule expansion fires again while cumulative state does not move -- so traversalsOf() is deleted. Not deduplicated across stages.
projectDiscoveryTrace() only COPIES. The packet-decision reconstruction and its invented fallback reason 'excluded from the packet' are gone; the derivation throws on an unexpected decision instead of skipping it.
The reader enforces the narrow event/state integrity relation (endpoints emitted, endpoints carry it afterwards, no repeat within one pass, gained state explained by an event, skipped traverses nothing) WITHOUT a global set difference: a repeat is legal and an applicable stage that found no links is legal.
CLOSED DISCRIMINANTS FAIL CLOSED. routeClass was an arbitrary string while candidateBand() sent every unrecognized value to exploratory, so a corrupted direct-state-ref could soften a mandatory drop and turn M6 green. The reader pins the v1 route vocabulary independently of the producer; candidateBand() is an exhaustive Record<RouteClass, CandidateBand> that fails to compile until a new route is classified and throws on an impossible one. Signal kind, candidate targetKind, pack role (base/addon by position) and projection-limit kind are validated the same way. ruleKind goes through the OWNER's isCampaignRuleKind()/CAMPAIGN_RULE_KINDS, exported from campaign/campaignRules.ts -- discovery does not define that domain, the deliberate contrast with the discovery-owned route list. Lifecycle siblings rejected: skipped with traversal events or a seam query, failed-to-run beside decisions, empty exclusion reason; pass-through on a skipped stage stays legal.
PERMANENT EVIDENCE: a repeated-traversal regression built from the real producers (condition:incapacitated must-consider -> expansion 1 traverses the action:dodge exclusion edge -> a jhpt house rule governing Dodge promotes it -> pass 2 traverses the same edge), verified to FAIL against the deleted traversalsOf(); real count-budget and byte-budget exclusion cases; reason removed/emptied, decision removed, event-without-carrier, state-without-event, carried-not-fired, fired-again; and mutations for every closed discriminant. traceDerivation.test.ts compares projected dispositions, packet decisions and both stages' traversal events against the LIVE producer trace across all 13 corpus executions.
Verification at 8b67c33: focused discovery suite 220 passed; npm run verify:worktree exit 0, 5251 passed / 20 skipped.

DURABLE RECORD SHAPE. The v1 record stores canonical facts and derives every M1-M11 summary at measurement time in discovery/traceDerivation.ts. Read this section under the REDUNDANCY RULE above -- it describes what the implementation does, and is NOT a standing requirement that every implication be eliminated:
- one candidate stream per stage; produced/modified/carried-forward derived, with a candidate's rule evidence taken from the join PLACEMENTS, not a copy on the candidate;
- expansion stages store their traversal EVENTS; a candidate's .traversals remains cumulative state;
- rule joins store seamQueries, the jhpt projections returned (unchanged, jhpt-owned type -- discovery declares no rule schema), placements and consideredAmbiguityIds; every M5 summary including returned/matched/unplaced/resolved is derived;
- retention stores one producer-authored disposition per candidate it decided over; retained/dropped/overflow/overflowed/losses derived;
- the packet stores one producer-authored inclusion decision per retained candidate plus the included content (two different facts); bytes, byte overflow, drop list and losses derived;
- audit is a discriminated lifecycle (absent | present with retries + accepted/repaired outcome), so an accepted verdict with a retry cause, an intermediate acceptance, a failing terminal state and a non-sequential attempt are UNREPRESENTABLE; M11 auditor presence and causes derive from it;
- stage outcome is a PRODUCER-OWNED OBSERVATION (see STAGE OUTCOMES above), validated for closed vocabulary and impossible combinations rather than re-derived;
- band, stageOrder, failedToRun, oracleSuppliedSignalLabels and unexpandedPromotions are derived, not stored.
readDiscoveryShadowEvidence is admissibility: schema, identity, closed discriminants, decision COVERAGE and lifecycle. Its stage table, route vocabulary and blocker set are declared in the validator independently of the producer; control-verified by renaming a producer stage and by dropping B5.

M10 DESIGN (accepted at review 4 and unchanged since). The runtime event is the instant preflightCampaignItemOperation returns, observed over a PRIVATE seam (UseItemInput.onCapabilityInvocation -> ToolContext.observeCapabilityInvocation -> a turn-owned buffer outside the candidate savepoint). Public tool results stay at their pre-W9 shape; events include audit-rejected attempts; M10 never reconstructs from a terminal tool result or a pre-model snapshot.

DESCRIPTION ERRATUM. This bead's BASELINE VALIDITY section says 'no deterministic-agreement measurement (M11) before B3', repeating design section 9.6. Corrected by design section 9.6 Erratum 1 (recorded in a20b1f6): section 13.1 defines M11 as auditor retry count and M12 as accepted state-effect agreement, so the measurement B3 gates is M12 -- a Phase 3 measurement. B3 therefore gates NO Phase 2 measurement, though it remains a prerequisite for a probe resolving an add-on stack (P11).

OTHER DELIVERED PIECES: capture-time B1-B5 observation (a probe must be unable to report 'repaired' for a defect it still contains; B2 is permanently not-discriminable from core -- see BASELINE QUALIFICATION above); total capture (trace XOR failure); one pinned pack resolution per capture; turn_trace.discovery_shadow (migration 0031) with no new store.

RUNTIME FINDINGS (recorded, not tolerated; successor questions for W10 eshyra-o9bd.19.12): P1/P2 lose their targets at 'signals' because their cues read fixture state fields with no live StateSnapshot equivalent; P5 misses rule:concentration; a real turn's shadow packet preflights nothing, so a real use_item event is reported as absent from the packet.

EXCLUSIONS: no CLI flag; no packet injection (W10).

title: Transition W8: build the offline discovery stage harness (Phase 1)
description:
Workstream W8 of the integrated ADR 0020 transition design, Phase 1 (section
12.1), with the stage model from sections 6-7:
docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md.
That design is the accepted deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8 (PR #485, reviewed
head afd113c7090378c3a9f4122f246a6c32602a5164, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282). ADR 0020 controls.

OWNER
This bead is the single owner of the experiment-only offline discovery stage
harness. No other bead owns it.

SCOPE
Build an experiment-only harness that executes and inspects the stage pipeline:

  signals -> candidates -> typed expansion -> campaign-rule/ruling join
          -> campaign-rule expansion -> late ruling join
          -> dedup with preserved reasons -> priority and retention
          -> context packet

  The nine-stage pipeline is the normative Phase-1 contract, consolidated into
  design section 12.1 on 2026-09-02. The original seven-stage list is
  superseded: it was coherent only while campaign-rule was an annotation
  rather than a route that proposes candidates. Expansion repeats once after
  the join, seeded only by candidates the join promoted; a late ruling join
  then queries rulings for ambiguity ids that second pass discovered. Active
  campaign rules are retrieved EXACTLY ONCE, from the complete
  active-at-position query, because eshyra-jhpt.3 owns that semantics and W11
  consumes it rather than redefining it. The late stage may not introduce
  candidates, which is what closes the pipeline: every ambiguity in the
  finished packet was offered to the seam.

- Route classes are the nine diagnostic labels of design section 6.2. They are
  provisional labels for why a candidate was proposed and may be split, added
  to, or retired by probe evidence.
- Deduplication is by canonical record key and preserves every route and every
  traversal reason; a lost route is a measured failure (M3), not an
  implementation detail.
- Retention uses the three experimental bands of section 6.3. A must-consider
  candidate may never be silently dropped: overflow is recorded explicitly,
  naming every dropped candidate and its routes, and the probe fails.
- The campaign-rule/ruling join goes through the narrow eshyra-jhpt read
  interface seam of section 8.2, which a stub satisfies until jhpt lands. W11
  owns the real integration.
- Measurements M1-M9 (section 13.1) are computable per probe and per stage.

NON-GOALS AND PROHIBITIONS
- No durable store of any kind: no proof store, no readiness artifact, no
  finding registry, no campaign-rule store, no second audit database. Traces are
  returned to tests. (ADR 0017 section 8; ADR 0020 audit-architecture
  restraint; design D12.)
- No production ranker, embedding model, vector database, or graph database.
  Ranking inside a band is deterministic and simple (route count, then canonical
  key order) so a ranking failure stays legible.
- No universal relationship vocabulary, clause ontology, or obligation identity.
- No claim of universal discovery completeness. A probe result is bounded
  evidence for its scenario; a route's absence is evidence about the pilot, not
  about the rules.
- No campaign-rule or ruling schema, storage, resolver, or lifecycle: those stay
  with eshyra-jhpt (design section 8.4). Discovery may not resolve an ambiguity.
- No runtime integration: the orchestrator seam is W9.

DEPENDENCIES
W7 (the fixture corpus) is required. B3 (eshyra-6vpw) bounds the P11 add-on
probe only; B1, B2, and B5 do not gate offline stages. Harness design may
proceed in parallel with the Phase 0 repairs (design sections 9.6 and 14.1).

PERMANENT EVIDENCE
Per-stage traces returned directly to tests; separate signal-extraction tests;
probe runs over the W7 corpus with M1-M9 computed per probe per stage; an
explicit label on any probe that passed only because the fixture supplied the
signal.

REQUIRED NEXT STATE
Every probe that does not require runtime state runs end to end through the
harness; every stage boundary emits its own evidence; no durable store was
introduced. 
  Stage accounting (design section 12.1): each stage states, by candidate key
  rather than by count, which candidates it PRODUCED, which existing
  candidates it MODIFIED, and which it CARRIED FORWARD untouched, and reports
  exactly one outcome:

    ran            - it performed its work, INCLUDING a seam query that
                     executed and returned nothing (absence is evidence under
                     section 8.2 R7)
    skipped        - a CONDITIONAL stage had nothing applicable to do: no
                     seeds to expand, or no newly discovered ambiguity id
    failed-to-run  - it recorded nothing and is not a conditional skip

  Only campaign-rule expansion and late ruling join are conditional and may
  report skipped. skipped is a truthful third state, NOT a pass, and may never
  be manufactured by forwarding upstream output as though this stage produced
  it. A stage that recorded no candidates, no routes and no losses, and is not
  a conditional skip, has not passed - it has failed to run.

  A record the late ruling join promotes does not receive a further expansion
  pass. That bound is deliberate and named rather than hidden: every such
  record is recorded in the trace, measured, and reported per probe as bounded
  evidence about the pilot.

MATERIAL CHANGE: yes. This introduces the discovery stage pipeline as a design
surface. It is experiment-only and does not alter runtime behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
The harness returns a per-stage trace directly to tests for every stage of
the nine-stage pipeline of design section 12.1 (signals -> candidates -> typed
expansion -> campaign-rule/ruling join -> campaign-rule expansion -> late
ruling join -> dedup -> priority/retention -> context packet), and no durable store, database,
readiness artifact, campaign-rule store, or finding registry is created by this
work. Signal extraction is tested separately from downstream stages, so a
failure at one stage is never hidden by success at another, and any probe that
passes only on a fixture-supplied oracle signal is reported as such. The harness
resolves records through the real active rules-stack resolution
(resolveRulesStack / resolveStrictCampaignRulesStack), not a fixture copy of a
pack, so override chains and stack semantics are the real ones. The
campaign-rule/ruling join goes through a narrow eshyra-jhpt read seam that a
stub satisfies until jhpt lands; no discovery-local rule or ruling store exists.
Dedup is by canonical record key and every route and traversal reason survives
the merge. A must-consider candidate is never silently dropped: overflow emits
an explicit record naming each dropped candidate and its routes, and fails the
probe. No production ranker, graph database, vector database, embedding model,
or universal relationship vocabulary is introduced. M1-M9 are computable per
probe per stage, reported independently, and never collapsed into a coverage,
readiness, or completeness score. Every runtime-independent probe in the W7
corpus executes end to end; a stage that records no candidates, routes, or
losses is reported as failed-to-run, not as passing.

Stage accounting: each stage reports produced/modified/carried-forward
membership by candidate key and exactly one outcome of ran/skipped/
failed-to-run. Only campaign-rule expansion and late ruling join are
conditional and may report skipped; a seam query that executed and returned
nothing reports ran, never skipped. Active campaign rules are retrieved exactly
once from the complete active-at-position query; the late stage queries rulings
only and introduces no candidates, so every ambiguity in the finished packet
was offered to the seam, which is asserted per probe. A record promoted by the
late ruling join receives no further expansion, and that residual is recorded
and reported per probe rather than hidden.

TRACEABILITY: every bead in the W7-W15 set was created 2026-07-31 to execute the
design accepted as the deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8 (PR #485, reviewed head
afd113c7090378c3a9f4122f246a6c32602a5164, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282). They are parented to the ACTIVE

title: Transition W7: author the twelve bounded diagnostic fixtures and the fixture contract
description:
Workstream W7 of the integrated ADR 0020 transition design, section 10 (the
twelve probes) and section 11 (the fixture contract):
docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md.
That design is the accepted deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8 (PR #485, reviewed
head afd113c7090378c3a9f4122f246a6c32602a5164, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282). ADR 0020 controls.

OWNER
This bead is the single owner of diagnostic fixture authoring and of the fixture
contract. No other bead owns it.

SCOPE
Author the twelve bounded diagnostic fixtures of section 10 and implement the
thirteen-field fixture contract of section 11:

  P1  rule:cover (implicit cover, player text never says "cover")
  P2  rule:opportunity-attacks (trigger plus all three exceptions)
  P3  creature:adult-black-dragon selector /data/actions/5 (Acid Breath)
  P4  spell:fireball
  P5  condition:incapacitated + rule:concentration
  P6  feature:fighter:action-surge
  P7  magic-item:cube-of-force with
      ambiguity:cube-of-force-same-face-duration-reset
  P8  magic-item:ammunition-1-2-or-3 operation hit-target
  P9  module eshyra:hollow-beneath-emberfall, encounter enc-mouth-ambush,
      creature:goblin
  P10 the jhpt-defined material-components house rule (no source ambiguity)
  P11 synthetic base + add-on override stack
  P12 table:starting-wealth-by-class as false SRD authority

Each fixture declares fields 1-13 of section 11 plus the expected deterministic
state effect, or the explicit expectation that there is none.

REQUIRED STATEMENTS (design sections 3.2, 6.1, 10, 11; ADR 0020 sections 3-4)
- Each scenario is bounded evidence for the situation it names. A scenario is
  never a completeness unit, never a partition of the corpus, and no report
  built from these fixtures may aggregate them into a coverage or completeness
  figure.
- Every identity in fields 5-13 must be verified against the current generated
  pack or adventure module at authoring time, and each fixture records the
  commit it was verified at. Where a framing and the pack disagree, the pack
  wins (feature:fighter:action-surge, not feature:action-surge; the Hollow
  Beneath Emberfall module contains no stat-block reference).
- Oracle-supplied signals must be labelled as such in the fixture, so a
  downstream stage passing on a supplied answer can never be reported as
  end-to-end success.
- Fixtures use diagnostic-fixture identity only: canonical RulesRecord.key,
  provenance.sourceRef, provenance.locator, narrowed where needed by a
  test-local selector limited to a JSON pointer, an existing ambiguity ID, an
  existing operation or compiler-emitted clause ID, or a narrowly described
  source-text predicate. These fixtures must not create a universal clause
  ontology, a universal obligation identity, or a closed relationship
  vocabulary. Source-obligation identity remains eshyra-o9bd.19.1.14's question.
- The campaign-rule fixtures (P7, P10) consume eshyra-jhpt outputs. They must
  not invent a second ruling model, schema, store, resolver, or lifecycle, and
  P10's acceptance shape is filled in by jhpt, not invented here.
- No fixture asserts a count of records ("all N creatures ..."). Assert
  identities; count-pinning is recurring failure idiom 3 of eshyra-o9bd.19.7.

NON-GOALS
- No discovery implementation, no stage harness (that is W8), no runtime
  integration, no generated-pack change, no schema change.
- No ranker, embedding model, vector database, or graph database.
- No finding is closed, retired, narrowed, or reclassified here.
- P8's target may not be re-pointed by hand: it was selected by executing
  assertMagicItemOperationReady over every magic-item operation, and any change
  requires re-running that query and restating the evidence.

DEPENDENCIES
None blocking; parallel-safe with W1-W6 (design section 14.1). Per-probe
blockers bound when a probe's evidence becomes valid, not when its fixture may
be authored: B1 eshyra-l3e5 (stat-block), B2 eshyra-seoh (P9), B3 eshyra-6vpw
(P11 "after" half), B4 eshyra-o9bd.19.2.1 (P12), B5 eshyra-uiax (P8). Each
fixture records which blocker gates its evidence.

PERMANENT EVIDENCE
Twelve committed fixtures, each recording its verification commit and gating
blocker, plus a check that every declared identity still resolves in the current
pack and module.

REQUIRED NEXT STATE
The twelve fixtures exist, are individually runnable, and are consumable by W8
without a change of shape.

MATERIAL CHANGE: no. This adds test data and a fixture contract; it introduces
no runtime surface and changes no architecture boundary.
acceptance_criteria:
Twelve fixtures exist, one per probe P1-P12, each declaring all thirteen
section-11 fields plus the expected deterministic state effect or the explicit
expectation that there is none. Every record key, selector, ambiguity ID,
operation ID, clause ID, module ID, and prose substring resolves against the
generated pack or the adventure module, and each fixture records the commit it
was verified at. Every oracle-supplied signal is explicitly labelled. Each
fixture states, in band, that it is bounded evidence for its named scenario and
not a completeness unit; no fixture or report derived from the corpus aggregates
probes into a coverage, readiness, or completeness figure. No fixture asserts a
record count. The campaign-rule fixtures reference eshyra-jhpt identities and
define no ruling schema, store, resolver, or lifecycle. P12 asserts the
false-authority evidence (source "SRD 5.1 p. 38", locator "p. 38", CC-BY block)
and never treats the record as SRD authority. Each fixture names the blocker,
if any, that gates the validity of its evidence. No production code, generated
pack data, or schema changes in this work.

these items. W11 consumes; it does not own. If the jhpt interface proves
insufficient, the correct response is an amendment or a child under eshyra-jhpt,
never a discovery-local store.

title: Magic-item readiness silently skips a clause with an unrecognized scope kind
description:
Verified at main f4b3461. packages/core/src/state/itemExecutionReadiness.ts:19-31 inSelectedScope returns false for any clause scope whose kind is neither 'parent' nor a matching 'variant', and :76-77 then skips that clause entirely, so a clause with a malformed or unrecognized scope CANNOT block the operation. assertMagicItemOperationReady is the only live runtime capability gate (called from state/itemState.ts:1888) and is otherwise correctly fail-closed.

No such clause exists in the committed pack, so this is latent. ADR 0020 section 3 makes it a defect regardless: 'any gate, report, or predicate that reads an unbound or unrecognized item as satisfied is a defect, not a green.' Recorded as ar72 D-9b in docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-29-current-state-claim-and-defect-map.md.

Blocker B5 of 2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md: the contract cannot serve as pilot capability evidence (probe P8, magic-item:ammunition-1-2-or-3 / hit-target) until an unrecognized scope fails closed.
acceptance_criteria: An unrecognized clause scope kind fails closed rather than being skipped; a test feeds a malformed scope and asserts ItemExecutionReadinessError; existing parent/variant scope behavior is unchanged and its tests still pass.
close_reason: Closed

title: Deterministic pack consumers use a base-only campaign lookup with a silent bundled-D&D fallback
description:
Verified at main f4b3461. packages/core/src/state/campaignRecordLookup.ts:85-98 lookupCampaignRecord selects a bundled base by packId ALONE, ignores systemId/version and every campaign add-on, and falls back to getBundledDnd5eSrdPack() when no base matches. packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts:527-533 campaignBasePack repeats the same pattern for creature AC/HP. Strict model-facing lookup uses resolveStrictCampaignRulesStack (campaignRecordLookup.ts:67-76), which resolves exact system/pack/version plus ordered add-ons.

Live legacy callers: state/actionEconomy.ts:297,374,445; state/activeEffects.ts:1824,2560,2583,4031; state/attunement.ts:538; state/usageCounters.ts:785.

Consequence: with a custom or add-on-bearing campaign stack, the DM can obtain the strict active-stack record through lookup_rules while the deterministic consumer that acts on it sees different base data, or silently falls back to bundled D&D. One coherent active-stack evidence path is violated.

Discovered by eshyra-jued (2026-07-29-existing-discovery-substrate-map.md defect 3). Blocker B3 of 2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md: deterministic-agreement measurement and probe P11 (add-on override) are invalid until this is repaired.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic pack consumers resolve through the same exact campaign stack as strict model-facing lookup (system, pack, version, ordered add-ons); no silent bundled-D&D fallback remains on any of the named call sites; a synthetic base+add-on stack test proves strict lookup and the deterministic consumer resolve the same active record, system, version, and override chain.
close_reason: Closed

title: Normal CLI play never passes the adventure-module resolver to runTurn
description:

Consequently contextAssembler.assembleAdventureContext returns [] (an active adventure run contributes no context to the DM turn) and encounterCombatants.ts:638-642 throws 'start_encounter requires an active adventure module resolver' for an authored encounterId. packages/cli/src/adventures.ts:101 makeModuleResolver exists but its real consumer is the read-only 'adventures show' path.

title: lookup_rules rejects the addressable stat-block kind
description:
Verified at main f4b3461. packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolLookupRules.ts inputSchema.properties.kind.enum lists sixteen kinds and omits 'stat-block', so ToolRegistry.invoke rejects the call with invalid_args before the tool body runs. title: Persist profile-based contract authorization and PR review state
description:
Durable, repo-wide contract-authorization and PR-review system, created because
PRs #475/#476/#477 reached DESIGN_INVALIDATED with no mechanism able to state,
authorize, or invalidate a change-specific review contract. Foundation 1
(eshyra-o9bd.19.1.14) R3 records the blocking consequence: F1 must CONSUME an
external eshyra-review-checkpoint binding
{reviewedHeadSha, contractHash, procedureIds[], reviewerRole, result,
implementationPermission} and is forbidden from building it. This bead builds
it, once, for the whole repository.

ONE lifecycle repo-wide; evidence requirements selected by REVIEW PROFILE.
Ordinary Eshyra work is NOT rules-pack work: standard < semantic-system <
rules-clause-complete. Foundation 1 is rules-clause-complete. This bead is
semantic-system.

Beads are the authoritative location for change-specific review contracts. PR
bodies and templates are explanatory only. No per-bead committed contract file.

## REVIEW CONTRACT

Protocol: eshyra-review-v2

### Review classification
- Declared profile: semantic-system
- Authorization required before implementation: yes
- Classification reason: This change creates the repository's evidence and
  review-governance system: persisted PR review state, authority boundaries,
  deterministic identity and hashing, and fail-closed CI gating. It is durable
  trust-boundary infrastructure, not rules-source work. It touches no rules
  source, no importer, and no generated pack record, so rules-clause-complete
  does not apply. Revision 2 additionally revises the minimum-profile policy to
  cover executable agent-authority surfaces, and revises the contract-hash
  function; both are material and both are declared below.
- Change characteristics: authorization-or-evidence-boundary-change;
  public-schema-or-protocol-change
- Escalation conditions: Escalate to rules-clause-complete if any change under
  packages/core/scripts/importers, packages/core/src/rules, or
  packages/core/data/rules-packs enters scope, or if the work begins asserting
  source-obligation, pack-membership, or engine-capability semantics rather
  than transporting reviewer-published evidence about them.
- Owning Bead: eshyra-o9bd.19.1.17
- Contract revision: 2. Supersedes revision 1
  (ff5e2eb3bd75448b6faa0cc77443709c539f537869e4264b9ec556125c0f8309), which was
  reviewed at head 1579b9835347422ef23d6045027143728ec44ea3 with result
  changes-requested and materialContractChange true. Revision 2 incorporates ten
  established defect classes D1-D10 and is a MATERIAL change: it moves the
  contract hash, mandates a policy change that moves the policy hash, and
  changes the contract-hash function itself. All prior authorization state is
  void. Fresh full contract authorization is required before implementation
  resumes.
- Bootstrap transition: This remains the one-time process bootstrap PR. The
  bootstrap exception is bounded, waives ONLY the otherwise-impossible
  pre-existing authorization checkpoint, authorizes nothing, and approves
  nothing. Revision 2 narrows it further under D4 and D5: it must fail closed on
  any unresolved predicate, and it may never produce a lifecycle state, output
  string, or CI conclusion containing "authorized".

### Objective and scope
- Intended outcome: One durable, versioned, machine-enforced review lifecycle
  that (a) selects a review profile from changed paths plus declared change
  characteristics, (b) validates exactly one normative bead REVIEW CONTRACT,
  (c) publishes contract handoffs and reviewer checkpoints as PR comments,
  (d) distinguishes contract authorization from implementation review, (e)
  detects staleness by hash and head SHA, (f) makes DESIGN_INVALIDATED a
  terminal state, and (g) states truthfully, at every surface, exactly which of
  its claims are machine-enforced and which rest on manual owner attestation.
- In scope: docs/review protocol and three profile documents; the
  machine-readable minimum-profile policy; reusable TypeScript modules under
  packages/core/scripts/review; npm scripts review:classify, review:preflight,
  review:handoff, review:checkpoint, review:invalidate, review:ci; PR CI
  enforcing the lifecycle; a trusted-context refresh path for comment changes;
  concise pointers in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md; unit tests behind injectable
  GitHub and Beads boundaries; test-fixture isolation; and the ten defect-class
  remediations D1-D10 below.
- Out of scope: Foundation 1 implementation of any kind; any change to
  generated SRD pack output; reopening, modifying, or republishing state for
  PRs #475, #476, or #477; a general workflow engine; branch-protection
  automation; hosted review tooling; migration of historical PRs; and any
  cryptographic, signed, or GitHub-App-backed reviewer-identity mechanism,
  which is future protocol work under a later protocol version.
- Exact affected surfaces: docs/review/**; packages/core/scripts/review/**;
  packages/core/test/review/**; packages/core/test/fixtures/review/**;
  package.json scripts; .github/workflows/review-governance.yml; AGENTS.md;
  CLAUDE.md.

### Authority and inputs
- Authoritative inputs: The owning bead's single normative "## REVIEW CONTRACT"
  block, retrieved from the Beads database, is the authority for
  change-specific requirements. docs/review/minimum-profile-policy.json is the
  authority for the minimum profile. The protocol and profile documents under
  docs/review are the authority for the lifecycle and the evidence bar. The
  independent reviewer's verdict, transported as a checkpoint comment and
  attested by the repository owner, is the authority for authorization and
  approval. The PR head SHA and changed-path set reported by GitHub are the
  authority for what is being reviewed.
- Derived inputs: protocol hash, selected-profile hash, policy hash, normalized
  contract hash, review-artifact digest, path-derived minimum profile,
  characteristic-derived minimum profile, effective profile, and every
  lifecycle state label. All are computed, never stored in the contract, and
  never author-asserted.
- Untrusted inputs: PR title, PR body, PR template checkboxes, branch names,
  commit messages, comment prose outside the canonical marker envelope, bead
  notes not named by the contract, bead TITLE, escalation reason text, any
  display string interpolated into a published comment, environment variables,
  and CI job success. None may grant authorization, satisfy an evidence
  requirement, or influence machine payload parsing.
- Ownership: This bead owns the protocol, the profile documents, the policy, the
  parser and normalizer, the checkpoint schemas, the comment markers and the
  machine envelope, the commands, the CI gate, and the trusted refresh path. It
  does not own any profile's domain evidence standards beyond stating them;
  rules-source semantics remain owned by eshyra-o9bd.19.1.14 and its successors.

### Behavior and representation
- Required behavior: Parse exactly one normative contract per bead. Normalize it
  deterministically into a canonical structure and hash it with SHA-256 over an
  RFC 8785 JCS serialization of NFC-normalized text. Reject duplicate semantic
  keys rather than committing to them. Compute the effective profile as the
  stricter of the declared profile and the minimum profile derived from paths
  and declared characteristics. Publish exactly one active
  eshyra-review-contract:v2 comment per PR, idempotently upserted, carrying its
  machine payload in an unambiguous marker-bound envelope. Parse checkpoint
  comments into typed contract-authorization or implementation-review
  checkpoints under an explicit authority mode. Treat any design-invalidation
  marker as terminal at every command and every output mode. Re-evaluate
  governance whenever authoritative comment state changes.
- Required distinctions: contract authorization versus implementation review;
  declared versus minimum versus effective profile; publication head versus
  reviewed head; material contract change versus ordinary implementation churn;
  path-derived versus characteristic-derived escalation; production versus
  fixture-only checkpoints; a hash constant matching versus a review having
  occurred; MACHINE-ENFORCED structural validity versus MANUALLY ATTESTED
  reviewer authority; what local preflight proves versus what CI proves versus
  what only the independent reviewer can establish; a resolved empty result
  versus an unresolved lookup; and a bootstrap waiver versus an authorization.
- Compatibility requirements: The protocol identifier eshyra-review-v2 and the
  profile identifiers standard-v1, semantic-system-v1, and
  rules-clause-complete-v1 remain stable across this revision. The normalization
  change in D8 and the policy change in D9 deliberately move published hashes
  and therefore void outstanding authorizations; that is the intended
  behavior, not a regression. Any future change to normalization rules,
  required-field sets, checkpoint schemas, the machine envelope, or the policy
  likewise voids outstanding authorizations and requires a versioned changelog
  entry in the protocol document.
- Negative behavior: Under-classification is rejected. A missing, duplicated,
  placeholder-only, or profile-inconsistent contract is rejected. A contract
  containing duplicate semantic keys is rejected rather than hashed. A
  checkpoint whose hashes or effective profile disagree with current state is
  stale and rejected. A partial-scope authorization grants nothing. A
  self-contradictory checkpoint is rejected. An unresolved lookup is an error,
  never an empty set and never a default classification. A comment carrying more
  than one candidate machine payload, or a malformed envelope, is rejected. No
  environment variable, flag, or path enables fixture acceptance in production.
  No output at any surface claims that reviewer identity or independence was
  machine-verified.

### Consumers and blast radius
- Direct consumers: every future PR in this repository; the review-governance CI
  workflow and its trusted refresh path; agents following AGENTS.md and
  CLAUDE.md; Foundation 1 (eshyra-o9bd.19.1.14), which consumes
  contract-authorization checkpoints and fails closed without one.
- Indirect consumers: all beads blocked on Foundation 1; the F1-A/F1-B
  decomposition to be created after this PR merges; every later foundation that
  needs an independent approval record rather than a self-asserted one; and any
  future signed or GitHub-App-backed authority mode, which must be able to
  replace manual-owner-attestation without redefining the lifecycle.
- Cross-surface checks: npm scripts resolve; the CI workflow calls only the
  published commands; the protocol and profile documents are the exact files
  hashed by the code; the policy file parses under the schema the tests assert;
  root instruction files stay within the size ceiling; and every lifecycle
  predicate renders identically across the lifecycle enum, human output, JSON
  output, CI conclusion, handoff display, checkpoint display, and next-action
  text.
- Migration implications: There is no prior review state to migrate, and none is
  preserved: revision 2 voids every hash published under revision 1. The
  handoff published at head 1579b98 becomes stale by construction and must be
  republished after re-authorization. PRs #475/#476/#477 remain terminal and are
  used only as regression fixtures. The gate applies to PRs opened or updated
  after merge.

### Failure, recovery, and residuals
- Fail-closed requirements: Every command exits nonzero on a malformed, stale,
  duplicated, under-classified, or contradictory contract or checkpoint, and on
  a design-invalidated PR. Every evaluation path that cannot resolve its
  authoritative input returns a typed unresolved error and never an
  empty-but-successful result; this covers changed-path discovery, base-ref and
  protocol-path lookup, bead retrieval, GitHub retrieval, and comment
  enumeration. A bootstrap predicate that cannot be resolved defeats the waiver.
  Production checkpoint loading rejects fixture-marked content unconditionally.
  Ambiguous machine-payload framing is rejected rather than resolved by
  position.
- Recovery or rollback: Recovery from a rejected state is republication, never
  suppression: correct the bead contract, re-run review:classify and
  review:preflight, republish the handoff, and obtain a fresh checkpoint. A
  material contract change requires re-authorization before substantive
  implementation resumes. There is no recovery from DESIGN_INVALIDATED for that
  PR; recovery is a successor bead and a new PR.
- Approved residuals: Reviewer identity and independence are NOT machine-
  verified under authority mode manual-owner-attestation; this is an accepted,
  explicitly disclosed limitation, not a defect, and the tooling must say so
  rather than imply otherwise. CI cannot prove that a published handoff was
  derived from the live bead; it validates a self-published copy and must say
  exactly that. Branch-protection rules cannot be configured from this
  repository and remain a manual owner step; the gate is advisory until a
  repository administrator makes the check required. Historical PRs are not
  retrofitted.
- Explicitly unsupported material: multi-repository review state; cryptographic
  signing of checkpoints; an authenticated reviewer principal distinct from the
  repository owner; automatic closing or mutation of PRs and beads; fork-PR
  privileged execution; and approval of a PR by any automated actor. Reviewer
  identity verification is no longer listed as merely unsupported: it is
  replaced by an explicit, declared manual trust model whose limits every
  surface must state.

### Verification and closure
- Required tests: every test required by revision 1 (contract extraction,
  per-profile required sections, missing and duplicate contracts,
  placeholder-only fields, deterministic normalization and hashing, profile
  ordering, path-derived and characteristic-derived escalation, voluntary
  over-classification, under-classification rejection, changed-profile and
  changed-policy invalidation, handoff formatting and idempotent upsert,
  authorization freshness, optional standard authorization, mandatory
  semantic-system and rules-clause authorization, implementation head freshness,
  incomplete-scope rejection, checkpoint-kind separation, new-defect-class
  transition, terminal design-invalidation, attempted approval after
  invalidation, fixture isolation, bootstrap-exception isolation, stale
  protocol/profile/policy detection, unrelated-path standard classification,
  malformed-comment parsing, duplicate and superseded comment handling, compact
  default output, verbose and JSON output, effective-profile-only reading
  guidance, and root instruction size ceilings), PLUS the permanent regression
  obligations R1-R10 stated under each defect class below.
- Permanent regression evidence: all of the above live under
  packages/core/test/review and run in the default vitest suite. They are
  permanent, not one-off. PRs #475/#476/#477 supply the design-invalidated
  regression fixture. Each defect class D1-D10 must fail its regression test
  when its fix is reverted.
- Generated or exact membership: not applicable - this change asserts no
  source-obligation, pack-record, or engine-capability membership. It transports
  and validates reviewer-published evidence about such claims.
- Closure evidence: npm run verify:worktree green from the owning worktree;
  bd dep cycles clean; an open, unmerged PR carrying a fresh full
  semantic-system implementation review at the then-current head under contract
  revision 2 or later; and the final report items enumerated in the protocol
  document.

### Semantic-system contract
- Trust boundaries: AUTHORITY MODE IS manual-owner-attestation. (1) CI
  machine-enforces exactly: contract and checkpoint schema validity;
  deterministic hashes; profile calculation; head and contract freshness; legal
  lifecycle transitions; fixture rejection; terminal invalidation; and
  internally consistent handoff and checkpoint state. (2) Local review:preflight
  additionally compares the LIVE bead contract against the published handoff,
  and only where Beads access exists. (3) CI CANNOT independently prove that a
  handoff was derived from the live bead, and no component may state or imply
  that it did. (4) The independent reviewer MUST read the authoritative bead
  contract and bind its contract hash and reviewed scope in the verdict. (5) The
  repository owner is the manual trust root, publishing or causing publication
  of an exact reviewer-produced checkpoint. (6) The tooling must NEVER claim
  reviewer identity or independence was machine-verified. (7) reviewerRole, the
  GitHub comment author, and publisherLogin are DESCRIPTIVE EVIDENCE ONLY. (8) A
  structurally valid checkpoint under this mode means "review record accepted
  under manual owner attestation", never "independent reviewer identity
  verified". The producer of an artifact still may not define the standard its
  own output is judged by; under this mode that separation is upheld by the
  owner's attestation and the reviewer's reading of the bead, not by machine
  identity checks - and that is exactly what must be disclosed.
- Stable identities and revisions: protocol identifier eshyra-review-v2; profile
  identifiers standard-v1, semantic-system-v1, rules-clause-complete-v1; the
  three canonical comment markers. Four SHA-256 digests carry semantic revision:
  protocol, selected profile, policy, normalized contract - all over NFC-
  normalized input per D8. A fifth digest, reviewArtifactDigest, binds the exact
  transported review result; it proves transport integrity ONLY and does NOT
  prove authorship, which must be stated wherever it is surfaced. Full 64-hex
  digests are authoritative; truncation is display-only. Checkpoints additionally
  carry authorityMode, identityAssurance, and publisherLogin per D3.
- State transitions and lifecycle: design-invalidated (terminal, absorbing, and
  enforced by EVERY command in EVERY output mode); authorization-pending;
  authorized-and-in-progress; ready-for-implementation-review;
  changes-requested; implementation-approved. Bootstrap adds a disjoint family
  that must never contain the substring "authorized" in any surfaced form:
  bootstrap-authorization-waived; ready-for-bootstrap-implementation-review;
  implementation-approved-under-bootstrap-review. Legal transitions are
  enumerated in code, not prose. Any new commit invalidates implementation
  approval; later implementation commits do NOT invalidate contract
  authorization while contract, profile, and policy hashes are unchanged. Every
  authoritative comment change forces re-evaluation per D1. Handoff replacement
  is an in-place upsert of exactly one active comment; superseded or malformed
  handoff comments are reported as defects, never silently ignored, and
  publication must not overwrite a malformed comment that may be evidence.
- Stale-state detection: a checkpoint is stale when any published hash, or the
  effective profile, disagrees with current computed state; an implementation
  checkpoint is additionally stale when its reviewed head is not the current
  head; a handoff is stale when its published hashes or, for implementation
  handoffs, its head no longer match. A previously computed CI conclusion is
  itself stale state: it must be recomputed on authoritative comment change, and
  a stale-green or stale-red check is a defect (D1).
- Migration and backward compatibility: revision 2 voids all revision-1 hashes
  by design. A future protocol revision must bump the protocol identifier and
  marker version and add a changelog entry; silent migration of contracts or
  checkpoints is prohibited. Reading a marker or envelope version this
  implementation does not understand is an error, never a skip. A future
  authority mode stronger than manual-owner-attestation must be additive: it
  changes authorityMode and identityAssurance without redefining the lifecycle.
- Adversarial scenarios: a PR author publishing their own approval checkpoint; a
  hostile bead title, escalation reason, or display string containing Markdown
  fences or JSON attempting to shadow a machine payload (D10); an author editing
  the contract after authorization; an author lowering the declared profile; an
  author editing or deleting a checkpoint comment after a green check (D1); a
  fixture checkpoint copied into a real PR; an environment variable used to relax
  the gate; the bootstrap exception invoked for a second bead, a second PR,
  another repository, or a fork head (D5); an unfetched or ambiguous base ref
  activating the bootstrap waiver (D5); a git failure silently producing an empty
  changed-path set and a standard classification (D6); a duplicate semantic key
  making one value drive classification while another is displayed as
  authoritative (D7); NFC/NFD-equivalent text moving a contract hash (D8); an
  agent-authority change under .claude/** classified as standard (D9); a second
  active handoff shadowing the first; a superseded checkpoint read as current; a
  malformed comment silently treated as absent; and a fork PR attempting
  privileged execution.

### Established defect classes
- D1 authoritative-comment refresh: INVARIANT - every change to authoritative
  handoff, checkpoint, or invalidation state must refresh the derived governance
  result; a prior conclusion must never survive a later terminal or
  approval-state change. SURFACES - the CI workflow, review:ci, and every
  handoff, checkpoint, and invalidation publication or editing path. BEHAVIOR -
  governance must re-evaluate on comment created, edited, and deleted, covering
  at least red-then-approved, green-then-DESIGN_INVALIDATED, a corrected handoff
  with no code commit, an edited or superseded checkpoint, and both stale-green
  and stale-red checks. The refresh must run in a TRUSTED EXECUTION PATH that
  never runs untrusted PR code with privileged credentials: the comment-driven
  job must execute only base-branch-trusted code, must not check out or execute
  PR head content, and must publish its result as a status against the head SHA;
  pull_request_target with a PR-head checkout is prohibited. Refresh failure
  must surface as failure, with defined retry semantics, never as a passing or
  absent check. R1 - an event matrix proving create, edit, and delete of each
  authoritative comment kind recomputes state, including stale-green and
  stale-red cases, and proving the refresh path executes no PR-head code.
- D2 bead-to-handoff authority boundary: INVARIANT - no component may claim CI
  verified the handoff against the live bead. SURFACES - review:preflight,
  review:handoff, review:ci, ciGate, workflow status text, merge-readiness
  interpretation, all JSON output. BEHAVIOR - each surface must state exactly
  what it proves: preflight proves handoff-equals-bead where Beads access
  exists; CI proves published state is structurally consistent, current, and
  sufficient for the stage; the reviewer must read the bead and bind its
  contract hash and reviewed scope. Unresolved bead or GitHub state fails closed
  and never becomes empty membership or a valid default. A bead contract edited
  without republishing the handoff must be detectable by preflight and must not
  read as current. R2 - tests asserting the exact claim strings at every surface,
  that no surface asserts live-bead verification, and that unresolved bead or
  GitHub access produces a typed failure.
- D3 reviewer and publisher authority: INVARIANT - a structurally valid
  checkpoint means "review record accepted under manual owner attestation", never
  "independent reviewer identity verified". SURFACES - review:checkpoint, the
  checkpoint parser, publication, discovery, computePrReviewState,
  mergeReadiness, CI output, JSON output. BEHAVIOR - checkpoints carry
  authorityMode (manual-owner-attestation), identityAssurance
  (not-machine-verified), reviewArtifactDigest, and publisherLogin.
  reviewArtifactDigest binds the exact transported review result and does not
  prove its authorship; that limitation is surfaced wherever the digest is.
  reviewerRole, comment author, and publisherLogin are descriptive evidence only
  and are recorded, surfaced, and never used as a gate. Approval under this mode
  means: the owner attests that the bound review artifact is the independent
  reviewer's verdict over the bound contract hash and scope. R3 - tests proving a
  role/author mismatch cannot become machine-verified approval, that every
  approval surface is labelled with its authority mode and identity assurance,
  and that no output asserts verified independence.
- D4 bootstrap state consistency: INVARIANT - authorizationSatisfied === false
  implies no surfaced state may contain "authorized". SURFACES - state, report,
  preflight JSON, CI JSON and conclusion, handoff display, checkpoint display,
  next-action text. BEHAVIOR - the bootstrap family
  (bootstrap-authorization-waived, ready-for-bootstrap-implementation-review,
  implementation-approved-under-bootstrap-review) is disjoint from the
  authorized family; the checkpoint formatter names an implementation verdict
  "verdict", never unconditionally "approval"; and handoff-published
  declaredProfile, minimumProfile, profileId, effectiveProfile, and
  authorizationRequired are cross-checked against the embedded contract and the
  computed classification rather than accepted as assertions. R4 - a cross-
  surface truth table asserting identical predicates across every surface, and
  asserting the invariant above.
- D5 bootstrap containment and base-state failures: INVARIANT - the exception
  requires all intended predicates simultaneously and fails closed when any is
  unresolved. SURFACES - bootstrap, the base-path lookup, local preflight, the CI
  gate, fork-PR behavior. BEHAVIOR - predicates extend to repository identity,
  PR identity or an immutable bootstrap identity, same-repository head, expected
  base branch, non-fork head, and the exact bead and branch. A protocol-path
  lookup error, a missing or unfetched base ref, unavailable PR metadata, or any
  unresolved predicate defeats the waiver; a lookup error must never read as
  "protocol absent". R5 - an eligibility matrix over repository, PR, same-repo
  head, expected base, exact bead, exact branch, protocol-presence resolution,
  malformed state, fork state, second-PR attempts, and lookup errors.
- D6 fail-closed changed-path calculation: INVARIANT - an evaluation path that
  cannot resolve its authoritative input must fail, not return an empty
  successful result. SURFACES - review:classify and review:preflight without
  --pr, pre-implementation authorization decisions, the agent entry workflow, and
  every other unresolved lookup returning a valid-looking empty value. BEHAVIOR -
  changed-path discovery returns a typed resolved(paths) or unresolved(error);
  merge-base, diff, and status failures are errors with nonzero exit; no
  unresolved state may produce a standard classification. The GitHub changed-file
  boundary must state and test its pagination guarantee for large PRs. R6 - tests
  proving each git failure mode exits nonzero and that no unresolved state
  yields standard, plus a large-PR pagination test.
- D7 duplicate semantic fields: INVARIANT - a normalized contract has exactly one
  unambiguous value per normative key. SURFACES - normalizeContractBlock,
  validateContractStructure, contract hashing, handoff publication, CI contract
  reconstruction, authorization freshness. BEHAVIOR - duplicate preamble keys,
  duplicate section titles, and duplicate field keys are REJECTED, not preserved;
  no value may be selected by field order; and no contract containing duplicates
  may be hashed or rendered into an authoritative handoff. Coverage includes
  duplicate declared profile, authorization requirement, owning bead, protocol,
  change characteristics, and every profile-specific required field. R7 - exact
  rejection tests for each duplicate identity kind and for a duplicate whose
  first and later values disagree.
- D8 Unicode normalization: INVARIANT - canonically equivalent text has one
  identity. SURFACES - contract normalization and hashing, document hashing, the
  protocol document, and the tests. BEHAVIOR - NFC is applied to contract text
  before canonicalization and hashing, matching document hashing; the protocol
  document states which strings are normalized; identifier-valued fields
  (protocol, declared profile, owning bead, change characteristics) additionally
  validate against a restricted character set rather than relying on
  normalization alone. Protocol, implementation, and tests must agree. This moves
  existing hashes and is explicitly material. R8 - NFC/NFD equivalence tests for
  contract hashing alongside the existing wrapping, whitespace, list-marker, and
  delimiter-bearing-value stability tests.
- D9 minimum-profile policy coverage: INVARIANT - the repository-calculated
  minimum independently catches representative semantic and trust-boundary
  changes without relying on a voluntary characteristic declaration. SURFACES -
  minimum-profile-policy.json, the policy tests, and the live agent-authority
  paths. BEHAVIOR - add a semantic-system rule covering executable agent
  authority and policy injection, justified per path rather than blanket-
  escalated: .claude/settings.json and .claude/hooks/** (hook registration and
  the fail-closed supervisor gate that grants dispatch, branch, and push
  authority); AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (the repository's normative agent
  instructions, including the standing push and PR authority); and
  .github/workflows/** (CI execution and token permissions). None of these is
  rules-clause-complete, because none asserts source, pack, or engine semantics.
  .github/pull_request_template.md and .github/dependabot.yml remain standard,
  the template because the protocol makes it explanatory only. Changing the
  policy moves the policy hash and invalidates prior authorization. R9 -
  historical-fixture tests binding changed-path memberships to expected profiles
  for representative merged PRs, including PR #468 as semantic-system, ordinary
  documentation as standard, provider-neutral orchestrator work as
  semantic-system, and pack-driven runtime work as rules-clause-complete.
- D10 unambiguous machine-payload framing: INVARIANT - a comment has exactly one
  machine payload, located by an unforgeable marker-bound envelope and never by
  the position of a generic Markdown fence. SURFACES - the marker module,
  handoff and checkpoint and invalidation formatters and parsers, and every
  interpolated display string. BEHAVIOR - the payload is delimited by an
  envelope bound to the canonical marker, of the form
  "<!-- eshyra-review-payload:v1:begin -->" then a fenced json block then
  "<!-- eshyra-review-payload:v1:end -->", parsed by locating the envelope
  delimiters and never by scanning for the first fence. Exactly one envelope may
  appear per comment; zero, two or more, unterminated, nested, or malformed
  envelopes fail closed. Every interpolated display string - bead title,
  escalation reason, bead id, reviewer role, scope notes, invalidation reason -
  is neutralized before rendering such that it cannot introduce an envelope
  delimiter, and the formatter and parser round-trip arbitrary hostile display
  text. An attacker-controlled title containing Markdown fences or JSON must not
  change the parsed handoff kind, head, hashes, contract, or profile. R10 -
  round-trip tests over hostile display strings including fenced JSON and forged
  envelope delimiters; multiple-candidate-payload and malformed-envelope
  fail-closed tests; and a regression reproducing the observed shadowing, in
  which a bead title carrying a fenced payload flipped a published
  contract-authorization handoff at one head into an implementation-review
  handoff at another while still validating.
acceptance_criteria: One repo-wide review lifecycle with evidence requirements selected by profile (standard < semantic-system < rules-clause-complete); Beads authoritative for change-specific review contracts and PR bodies explanatory only; deterministic contract normalization and SHA-256 hashing of protocol, selected profile, minimum-profile policy, and normalized contract; centralized and tested minimum-profile policy with path-derived and characteristic-derived escalation, under-classification rejected and over-classification permitted; review:classify, review:preflight, review:handoff, review:checkpoint, and review:invalidate implemented behind injectable GitHub and Beads boundaries with no live calls in unit tests; contract authorization and implementation review kept separate, with head-freshness and hash-freshness rules; DESIGN_INVALIDATED terminal for a PR; a narrowly bounded one-time bootstrap exception that cannot apply to another bead or after the protocol exists on the base branch; fixture checkpoints unable to authorize any real PR, bead, or contract; PR CI enforcing the lifecycle with a safe permission model; concise pointers only in AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md within the agreed size ceiling; default review:preflight output under 40 lines with --verbose and --json for detail.

title: Foundation 4: define evidence categories, trust models, and exact claims
description:
Define evidence categories across source fidelity, discovery, adjudication support,
deterministic capability, and state integrity, and state exactly what each proves and
does not prove. Different responsibilities may legitimately use different trust models.
Internal discovery telemetry may use producer-owned observations as primitives under
an explicit internal trust model; source-fidelity and capability/state claims may
require stronger independent evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every evidence category names its claim, trust boundary, owner, and explicit non-claims.
- Presence, ownership, candidacy, schema validity, or code-symbol existence cannot substitute for semantic implementation or runtime execution.
- Diagnostic telemetry, source proof, capability execution evidence, finding evidence, and state evidence are not forced into one proof standard.
- Positive absence is permitted only for an explicitly bounded property/population whose denominator makes absence provable.
- Unresolvable/unrecognized input cannot become satisfied through an empty result.

description:
Successor to the stable half of eshyra-o9bd.19.1.6 (PR #476, DESIGN_INVALIDATED).

PREMISE CHANGE (why this exists): PRs #475/#476/#477 reached DESIGN_INVALIDATED
after repeatedly producing NEW defect classes following material contract changes
and fresh full reviews. The shared root cause was not implementation quality: in
all three, unsettled concepts were GENERALIZED ACROSS THE CORPUS before their
trust boundaries had been proven by a small number of concrete
source-to-execution examples. Successor work inverts that order.

GOAL: preserve the audit metadata that survived review, as a registry of AUDIT
FACTS that explicitly does NOT yet claim executable exact membership or
zero-repeat certification. Making those claims before Foundation 1 settled is
what invalidated #476.

SALVAGE AS-IS / AFTER EXTRACTION from #476: canonical finding identities; alias
accounting (70 aliases across opus:F-*, sol:CAP-*, fable:F*, indep:*, each
resolving to exactly one row); accepted / narrowed / ambiguous /
disclosed-dependency statuses with their reasoning; generalized invariant
descriptions; source review references; owning beads; duplicate canonical-ID
validation; and the historical classification reasoning.

MUST SEPARATE, and keep separable:
  * the stable audit fact and its generalized invariant;
  * source or review provenance;
  * aliases and status;
  * owner;
  * baseline affected membership;
  * current violation membership;
  * permanent closure evidence.

EXPLICIT NON-GOALS: no executable exact membership, no zero-repeat certification,
no closure-readiness predicate. Those are Foundation 3 and are blocked on
Foundation 1. This artifact must be honest that it does not yet ground them.

DO NOT PRESUME SURVIVES: the current membership queries, the source identities,
or any zero-recurrence claim.
acceptance_criteria:
• Canonical finding identities, all 70 aliases, statuses with reasoning, invariants, provenance and owners are preserved and reviewable.
• Audit fact, provenance, alias/status, owner, baseline membership, current violation membership and closure evidence are separable fields.
• The artifact makes no executable-exact-membership or zero-repeat claim, and says so explicitly.
• Duplicate canonical IDs are rejected.

row derived, and the all-derived test explicitly expects pack-generated rows to

FIX: the validator must REJECT pack self-derivation. A registered pack generator
may supply CURRENT membership for comparison against an independent authority;
it may never be the authority that makes a row derived. The test that expects
pack-generated rows to stop blocking encodes the defect — change it deliberately

sentences. Consecutive checked-in rows still share identical sentence structures
with substituted values.

round-robin audit aliases, then title-substituted reasons, now a normalizer with
holes plus a sentence blacklist. Every previous fix hardened the detector and
every one was evaded within a round.

*** SUPERVISOR DECISION — STOP HARDENING THE DETECTOR. ***
A prose field derived from a row's own metadata carries no independent
information, so it will always be templatable. Replace it:

  underivedReason becomes STRUCTURED —

                rows; do not invent an 'other' escape hatch.

A structured value either resolves or does not; it cannot be paraphrased into

=== P1-A: projectionNodes EMITS ONLY OBJECTS ===
Supervisor-confirmed at bootstrapCapabilityLedger.ts:1539-1555:
  * arrays recurse per item, but a primitive item hits objectRecord() -> null ->
    return, so primitive array elements produce NO node;
  * scalars produce no node for the same reason;
  * the root 'data' object is deliberately skipped by
    "if (currentPath !== 'data')".
So paths the predicates explicitly list are invisible:
    data.halfDamage   = true                        -> no node
    data.saveAbilities = ['strength','dexterity']    -> no node
FIX: emit a node for every path — scalars, primitive array elements, and the
root data object included — carrying the path and its value so predicates can
see both.

=== P1-B: THE 'CLOSED ALLOWED SCHEMA' CLAIM IS UNSUPPORTED — THE DEEPER HALF ===
RulesRecord.data is typed 'unknown', and the baseline kind validator requires
only an object with an optional description. It does NOT reject unregistered
fields. There is therefore NO closed representation schema to enumerate against.

Consequence: a schema-valid field such as alternateSaveAbilities,
higherSlotScaling or trainingLedger can carry the missing semantic projection
while matching no hand-written applicability key, and the resolver returns
SATISFIED — concluding absence from its own failure to recognise the material.

DO NOT FIX THIS BY ADDING MORE KEYS. That is the same defect one iteration later,
and this program has already spent rounds on alias lists that were always one
unregistered field short.

REQUIRED — CLASSIFICATION-COMPLETE ABSENCE. For each record examined, every
structured path must land in exactly one of:
  (a) MATCHES the projection shape        -> the obligation is NOT absent;
  (b) REGISTERED IRRELEVANT to this shape -> ignore, by explicit registration;
  (c) UNCLASSIFIED                        -> the row resolves evidence-underived.
Absence may be concluded ONLY when zero unclassified structured material remains.
Recognising nothing is not evidence of absence — that equivalence is the defect.

=== GENERATED REGRESSION MATRIX ===
Produce permanent evidence for EVERY ProjectionShape crossed with:
  scalar field | primitive array | split sibling | cross-record structure |
  schema-valid unregistered key
Generate it from the shape list rather than hand-writing cases, so a newly added
shape cannot ship without coverage. The unregistered-key case must assert
evidence-underived, NOT satisfied.

=== EXPECT THE BLOCKER SET TO GROW, POSSIBLY TO ALL 12 AND BEYOND ===
Once unclassified material forces evidence-underived, many rows that currently
resolve will stop resolving. That is the correct and honest outcome; the
fail-closed closure gate already handles it and the PR body already states that
the gate reports not-ready. Do NOT register keys wholesale as irrelevant, widen
predicates, or otherwise tune the result to keep a smaller blocker count.
Registering a field as irrelevant is a claim that it CANNOT carry the shape —
make it only where that is true.
