title: Dispatch: canonical closure roster, pack-independent authority, closed hook relation (attempt 8)
description:
Fresh full review of PR #476 at 6a1b275: four P1, one P2. All remain inside
previously identified invariant classes, so NO rescope is required and a
FIX-VERIFICATION review is permitted next PROVIDED THE CONTRACT DOES NOT CHANGE.
Implement the existing invariants correctly; add no new invariant classes. If you
think the contract must change, report it rather than changing it.

TWO OF THESE PASSED SUPERVISOR REVIEW AND SHOULD NOT HAVE. Read F1 and F4 with
that in mind — the bar is higher than 'a test exists'.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.md
  packages/core/src/rules/findingRegistry.ts
  packages/core/test/findingRegistry.test.ts

=== F1 (P1): CLOSURE ACCEPTS AN OBLIGATION SUBSET ===
The committed test builds validFixture = registry.rows.filter(derived) — a
4-row subset — and asserts closure READY. The closure API validates only rows
that are PRESENT, so DELETING the 64 unresolved obligations produces green
closure. That is the cheapest possible way to fake closure and the gate permits
it. (The supervisor reviewed this exact fixture and called it valid. It is not.)

FIX: closure must validate against the CANONICAL obligation set, not against
whatever rows happen to be present. Commit a canonical row roster — the same
device that fixed the equivalent hole in the capability ledger — and make a
registry missing any canonical row report those rows as BLOCKERS. Test that
deleting rows increases blockers rather than clearing them.

=== F2 (P1): THE FOUR 'DERIVED' ROWS ARE DEFINED BY THE PACK UNDER REPAIR ===
Rule, spell, half-damage and engine-capability membership is generated from
current records, text, readiness states and hooks. An obligation already OMITTED
from the pack is absent from both the generated set and the stored snapshot, so
it is invisible in exactly the case the registry exists to catch. This
contradicts the contract's own rule that a row's authority may not be the pack
under repair.

FIX: a row may be 'derived' only when its authority is established INDEPENDENTLY
of the pack — from source or from an audit finding's own recorded scope — with
the pack query supplying CURRENT membership to be compared against that
authority. Where independent authority cannot be established, the row is
'underived'.
EXPECT THE DERIVED COUNT TO FALL, possibly to zero. If all 68 rows end
underived, that is an ACCEPTABLE AND HONEST outcome: this PR's value is the
model, the gate and a truthful status, not a derived count. Do NOT retain a row
as derived merely because a pack query returns something.

=== F3 (P1): CAPABILITY ASSIGNMENT IS HEURISTIC ===
primitiveForHook() lowercases the hook and keyword-matches with broad defaults,
so unknown or unrelated hook names receive valid primitives. The engine:F2
legendary-action primitive is not reachable through ANY branch.
FIX: replace it with a CLOSED hook-to-primitive relation. An unknown hook must
fail or resolve to an explicit unmapped state — never a guessed primitive. Make
the F2 legendary-action primitive reachable and test it. Add negative tests for
unknown and unrelated hook names.

=== F4 (P1): THE ANTI-TEMPLATE GUARD STILL ACCEPTS THE CHECKED-IN TEMPLATE ===
The normalizer removes literal titles and identifiers only. The checked-in
reasons and invariants share sentence SKELETONS with PARAPHRASED subjects, which
survive normalization and read as unique.

THE SUPERVISOR'S OWN REGRESSION TEST IS PART OF THE PROBLEM: it constructs two
rows whose reason text is byte-identical apart from an interpolated title. The
guard already caught that case. The test therefore proved nothing about the
pattern actually present in the data, and passing it created false confidence.

FIX:
 * Strengthen normalization to collapse paraphrased subject noun phrases, not
   just literal titles and IDs — compare structural skeletons after removing
   content words, or require measurable divergence (n-gram or edit-distance)
   between rows' residuals.
 * The new negative test must use THE ACTUAL CHECKED-IN PATTERN — same skeleton,
   paraphrased subject — as its failing case. A test that only catches
   byte-identical text is not sufficient.
 * Then REWRITE THE DATA the strengthened guard catches. Expect many rows to
   need genuinely distinct text. Do not relax the guard to fit the data; that is
   the failure this has now repeated four times in this program.

=== F5 (P2): FORBIDDEN TOTALS BYPASS VALIDATION INSIDE ARRAYS ===
hasForbiddenTotal() begins 'if (!isObject(value)) return;', so an array returns
immediately and nested count/total fields inside members or capability catalogs
are never inspected. FIX: recurse into arrays; add a test with a forbidden total
nested inside an array member.

=== PRESERVE ===
The durable obligation/target/invariant vs violation split; 68 rows and 70
aliases each resolving once; qualified engine capability targets from
eshyra-o9bd.19.1.9; exact structured identities; the fail-closed blocker-identity
assertions.

=== ENVIRONMENT / CONSTRAINTS ===
npm ci first; npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing. Edit only the four files
above. A sibling dispatch runs in parallel on PR #477. Do not touch package.json,
internal.ts, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .github/, or any script/CI file. Do not
regenerate the pack or run the importer. Do not modify any bead but your own; no
bd dolt push; no push, PR comment, or merge. The PR body is the supervisor's to
fix, after the push.
acceptance_criteria:
• Closure validates against a canonical row roster; deleting rows increases blockers rather than clearing them, with a test.
• A row is derived only with authority independent of the pack under repair; the derived count is allowed to fall to zero.
• primitiveForHook is a closed relation; unknown hooks fail or resolve unmapped; the engine:F2 legendary-action primitive is reachable and tested.
• The anti-template guard catches same-skeleton paraphrased-subject text, proven by a test using the actual checked-in pattern; caught data is rewritten rather than the guard relaxed.
• hasForbiddenTotal recurses into arrays, with a test for a total nested in an array member.
• Contract unchanged so fix-verification review remains permissible.
• npm run verify:worktree passes.
notes: Completion report (2026-07-27): Reworked the four owned files. Added an explicit 68-row/70-alias canonical roster and fail-closed closure blockers for missing, unexpected, duplicate, or misassigned identities; closure now validates the roster before readiness. Marked all 68 rows underived because current-pack generators cannot establish independent authority, and rewrote every underived reason and invariant with distinct evidence-specific text. Replaced heuristic capability primitive inference with a closed exact hook-to-primitive relation, including a reachable engine:F2 legendary-action primitive and negative unknown/unrelated-hook tests. Recursive forbidden-total validation now traverses arrays with nested-array mutation coverage. Updated the registry contract document and tests. No binding architecture decision is disputed. The obligation not satisfied in this bead is independent source/audit membership derivation for the 68 rows; it remains explicitly closure-blocking and owned by eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7. Filed integration follow-up eshyra-s6vo for replacing/diffing the local capability relation against the bootstrap ledger. npm run verify:worktree passed (4728 passed, 19 skipped).

title: Dispatch: pack-wide projection matching and fail-closed shape recognition (attempt 8)
description:
Fresh full review of PR #477 at 3236982: two P1. NO new defect class — both sit
inside the existing source-negative semantic-proof invariant — so a
FIX-VERIFICATION review is permitted next PROVIDED the contract and the
representation boundary remain unchanged. Therefore: implement the existing
invariant correctly and change NEITHER. If you believe the contract must change,
report it instead of changing it.

ACCEPTED AS FIXED — do not touch: exact four-segment ev::: validation; the
improved source-procedure anchors; the exported fail-closed closure assessment;
exact blocker identity assertions.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.md
  packages/core/src/rules/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.ts
  packages/core/test/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.test.ts

=== P1-A: THE RESOLVER SCANS ONE RECORD WHILE REPORTING IT SCANNED THE PACK ===
Supervisor-confirmed in the code. The loop ending near line 1500 iterates all
records but only accumulates scannedClauses. Projection MATCHING happens solely
at 'for (const node of projectionNodes(sourceData, 'data'))' — sourceData is the
SINGLE source-anchor record. Line 1524 then reports
'scannedRecords: records.length'.

That metric is worse than the bug: it states the whole pack was examined when
one record was, so the defect is concealed from anyone reading the evidence.

A projection living on a sibling, child, or separately owned record is therefore
invisible, producing false 'absent' conclusions. Confirmed false-satisfied:
  * spell-slot / upcast   — nonempty readiness projection AND a source-negative
                            obligation in the same row;
  * spellbook copying     — nonempty readiness projection on one record, source
                            anchor on rule:wizard-your-spellbook;
  * downtime              — nonempty readiness projection AND a source-negative
                            obligation.
None appears in the pinned blocker list because the resolver never looks at the
records holding those projections.
AFFECTED MEMBERSHIP: all 12 known-missing-source-clause rows, not the three.

FIX: match projections across the ENTIRE record set, not the anchor alone.
Report a metric that describes what was actually examined — if you report
scannedRecords, it must equal the records genuinely searched for projections.
Re-derive the blocker set afterwards and let it GROW; do not tune anchors to
keep the pinned seven.

=== P1-B: SHAPE RECOGNITION IS HEURISTIC AND FAIL-OPEN ===
structuredProjectionTokens tokenizes arbitrary keys and values;
projectionShapeSignals then substring-matches hand-written alias lists. Top-level
objects are evaluated separately and the object's own PATH KEY is not in its
token set. So a representation split across siblings:
    data.legendaryBudget  = { points: 3 }
    data.legendaryOptions = [{ points: 2 }]
carries the required allowance and option-cost semantics, yet neither evaluated
node contains a 'legendary-action' or 'round-budget' token — and the resolver
certifies the obligation ABSENT.

FIX — this is the important one, and it is a fail-closed problem, not a
better-aliases problem:
 * Replace alias substring matching with CLOSED PREDICATES over every ALLOWED
   SCHEMA AND PATH for each projection shape, including cross-record and
   split-sibling representations. Include the node's own path key in what the
   predicate can see.
 * ANY applicable structure the predicates do not recognise must resolve
   evidence-underived, NEVER 'absent'. Inability to recognise a shape is not
   evidence of its absence — that equivalence is the entire defect.
 * Add tests for the split-sibling case above, for a cross-record projection,
   and for an unrecognised-but-applicable structure that must come back
   underived rather than passing.

EXPECT THE BLOCKER SET TO GROW under both fixes. That is the correct outcome and
the closure gate already handles it: a larger honest blocker list is the
artifact working. Do not adjust anchors, aliases, or the pinned set to restore a
smaller number.

=== ENVIRONMENT / CONSTRAINTS ===
npm ci first; npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing. Edit only the four
files above. Do not touch package.json, internal.ts, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md,
.github/, or any script/CI file. Do not regenerate the pack or run the importer.
Do not modify any bead but your own; no bd dolt push; no push, PR comment, or
merge. The PR body is the supervisor's to fix, after the push.
acceptance_criteria:
• Projection matching covers the entire record set; any reported scan metric equals what was actually searched.
• The three confirmed false-satisfied rows resolve correctly, and all 12 known-missing rows are re-derived.
• Shape recognition uses closed predicates over allowed schemas and paths, including cross-record and split-sibling representations, with the node path key visible to the predicate.
• An applicable structure the predicates do not recognise resolves evidence-underived, never absent, with a test.
• Tests cover the split-sibling legendary case and a cross-record projection.
• The blocker set is allowed to grow; nothing is tuned to preserve the pinned seven.
• Contract and representation boundary unchanged, so fix-verification review remains permissible.
• npm run verify:worktree passes.
notes: Completion report: Replaced heuristic substring/token projection matching with closed per-shape predicates over exact schema/path keys, including node path keys, split-sibling structures, and cross-record projections. The source-negative resolver now evaluates every structured data surface in every pack record and reports the records/clauses actually scanned. Recognized, partial, and applicable-but-unrecognized structures remain evidence-underived; the permanent tests now cover the 12-row blocker set, cross-record/split-sibling matching, and fail-closed unknown shapes. Updated the audit documentation to describe the invariant. No decision disagreement: I preserved the supervisor's binding contract and representation boundary. Obligations intentionally not satisfied: closure remains blocked by the honest twelve evidence-underived source-negative rows until clause-complete projection evidence exists; this is the required fail-closed outcome, not a weakened test. The generated ledger JSON/schema did not require content changes. No PR comment, push, or Dolt push was performed.

title: Dispatch: fail-closed registry gate and effective anti-template guard (attempt 7)
description:

  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.md
  packages/core/src/rules/findingRegistry.ts
  packages/core/test/findingRegistry.test.ts

=== D1: findingRegistryClosureReady() IS FAIL-OPEN ===
It checks only whether rows SAY membershipStatus='derived'. It never applies the
executable-generator and snapshot validations that sit directly below it in the
same module. Worse, the suite explicitly constructs an invalid all-derived
registry and asserts the gate returns true — the test encodes the defect.

CROSS-ARTIFACT PATTERN, recorded on the parent bead: PR #477's ledger closure
predicate shipped the SAME fail-open shape, built independently in a different
round. Assume fail-open is the DEFAULT failure mode of any ready/complete helper
in this program, and write this one to prove the negative.

FIX:
 * The predicate must apply the full validation chain, not read a status field.
   A row claiming 'derived' whose query re-run does not reproduce its stored
   snapshot must BLOCK closure, not pass.
 * Return the EXACT blocker set, not a boolean alone.
 * The regression must assert blocker IDENTITIES, never a count. A count-pinned
   test passes identically for a different set of the same size, which is how
   both fail-open predicates in this program survived review.
 * Test both directions: not-ready on the real registry naming its real
   blockers, ready only on a fixture where every row genuinely validates.
 * The committed test asserting true for an invalid all-derived registry must be
   changed deliberately; record why in your notes.

=== D2: THE ANTI-TEMPLATE GUARD IS INEFFECTIVE ===
The validator rejects only a reason that DUPLICATES another or that CONTAINS the
canonicalId. The checked-in reasons evade both by using a title-substitution
template — same sentence skeleton, row title interpolated — and most invariants
use the same pattern.

THIS IS THE THIRD OCCURRENCE OF ONE FAILURE MODE in this program: a required
field filled mechanically to satisfy a validator. First exemplarJustification —
one identical sentence across 61 rows. Then PR #477's audit aliases — indep:001
to 012 cycled round-robin. Now title-substituted reasons and invariants. A guard
that a constant or a template can satisfy is not a guard.

FIX:
 * Detect TEMPLATE STRUCTURE, not just equality: normalise each reason and
   invariant by removing row-specific tokens (title, canonicalId, aliases,
   target selector text) and reject when the residual skeletons collide across
   rows above a small threshold.
 * Apply it to BOTH underivedReason and invariant.
 * Add a test that constructs two rows differing only by interpolated title and
   asserts rejection.
 * Then FIX THE DATA the new guard catches. Expect a substantial number of rows
   to need genuinely distinct text. Do not weaken the guard to fit the existing
   data — that is the failure mode this bead exists to end.

=== DO NOT TOUCH ===
 * capability targets and their qualified engine identities — eshyra-o9bd.19.1.9,
   just landed in c73f6bc;
 * membership derivation for the 64 prose-scoped rows — eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7;
 * violation predicate executability — eshyra-o9bd.19.1.8.
If a fix here appears to need any of those, report it rather than widening
scope. Scope creep is what triggered the stop rule on this PR.

=== ENVIRONMENT / CONSTRAINTS ===
npm ci first; npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing. A sibling dispatch runs
in parallel on PR #477's files. Do not touch package.json, internal.ts,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .github/, or any script/CI file. Do not regenerate the pack
or run the importer. Do not modify any bead but your own; no bd dolt push; no
push, PR comment, or merge. The PR body is the supervisor's to fix.
acceptance_criteria:
• findingRegistryClosureReady applies the full validation chain; a row claiming derived whose query does not reproduce its snapshot blocks closure.
• The predicate returns the exact blocker set and the regression asserts blocker identities, never a count.
• Both directions tested; the committed test asserting true for an invalid all-derived registry is deliberately changed.
• The anti-template guard detects template structure after normalising row-specific tokens, applied to both underivedReason and invariant.
• A test constructs two rows differing only by interpolated title and asserts rejection.
• Data caught by the new guard is rewritten with genuinely distinct text; the guard is not weakened to fit existing data.
• No capability-target, membership-derivation or violation-predicate work is absorbed.

title: Dispatch: fail-closed ledger closure and true semantic absence (attempt 7)
description:
Fresh full review of PR #477 at 292b716: two P1, one P2, one P3. NO new defect
class, so a FIX-VERIFICATION review is permitted next — but only if the review
contract is UNCHANGED. Therefore this round implements existing contract
invariants correctly and adds NO new invariant classes. Do not propose contract
changes; if you believe one is needed, report it instead of making it.

ACCEPTED AS FIXED — do not touch: ev::: vs obl::: namespace separation; canonical
semantic facet validation and source/locator binding; registry-wide identity
uniqueness; removal of the five unsupported audit citations; the reviewed
relation table binding audit findings; duplicate projection query rejection
within and across rows.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.md
  packages/core/src/rules/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.ts
  packages/core/test/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.test.ts

=== P1-A: CLOSURE IS FAIL-OPEN FOR UNDERIVED EVIDENCE ===
The documentation says evidence-underived blocks closure. Nothing enforces it:
the full-ledger test ACCEPTS that status and explicitly expects five underived
results, and no fail-closed closure predicate exists in this PR at all. As
written, a DIFFERENT set of five unresolved rows would pass identically — the
test pins a count, not an identity.

NOTE A PATTERN: the sibling finding registry (PR #476) shipped the same defect —
a closure predicate that reports readiness without applying the validations
beneath it. Assume fail-open is the default failure mode of any 'ready' helper
and write this one to prove the negative.

FIX:
 * Export a fail-closed closure predicate that returns NOT-READY whenever any
   row carries evidence-underived, and NAMES the exact blocker set.
 * The regression must assert the EXACT blocker identities, not a count. A
   different set of five must FAIL.
 * Test both directions: not-ready on the current ledger with its real blocker
   set, and ready on a fixture where every row is resolved.
 * The committed test that expects five underived results encodes the defect —
   change it deliberately and record why in your notes.

=== P1-B: SOURCE-NEGATIVE EVIDENCE PROVES PHRASE ABSENCE, NOT SEMANTIC ABSENCE ===
The resolver checks selected terms at ONE generated-record path, then searches
only data.executionReadiness.clauses for selected substrings. It never inspects
other structured projection surfaces and cannot recognise an equivalent
representation expressed in different vocabulary. Substring absence is not
semantic absence.

Four anchors also identify the WRONG SOURCE UNIT:
  spell-slot / upcast   -> points at Wizard progression and the terms
                           'spellcastingProgression' and 'slots', not an upcast
                           procedure
  spellbook copying     -> points at the level-gain choice prompt, not the
                           copying time-and-cost clause
  multi-save            -> points at the generic Saving Throws rule, not the
                           audited entries whose later saves were dropped
  half-damage           -> points at the general resistance rule, not the
                           affected creature and hazard success branches
This affects ALL TWELVE source-negative primitives, not only the five currently
reported as underived. Re-audit every one.

FIX, per primitive:
 (a) anchor to the SPECIFIC source unit whose projection is missing;
 (b) search ALL structured projection surfaces, not data.executionReadiness
     alone;
 (c) detect semantically EQUIVALENT representations that use different

title: Dispatch: contract-review corrections - one obligation per clause, base requirements, evidence binding (attempt 4)
description:
Contract-grounded fresh full review of PR #475 at 1b33b18 returned nine P1 and one
P2. Supervisor spot-confirmed the most structural ones. Pre-contract findings
are superseded — do NOT re-litigate real pack-driven execution, SRD enumeration,
importer migration, or engine certification; the contract defers all of those.

  packages/core/test/clauseIrObligations.test.ts

=== SUPERVISOR ARCHITECTURE DECISION — READ BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE ===
Finding 4 offers two routes. TAKE THE SECOND: enforce ONE OBLIGATION PER CLAUSE
as an invariant.

Rationale: the clause IS the unit of one source obligation. A single obligation
may carry MANY FACETS (save + duration + repeat-check + termination from one
source sentence). Where a source sentence carries genuinely separable mechanics,
it decomposes into multiple CLAUSES, each with its own obligation and its own
projection. This dissolves the whole class of defects in findings 4 and 7:
  * two duration obligations can no longer share one duration atom;
  * negative facets become coherent — 'save-without-damage' meaning 'this
    clause's damage is empty' is exactly right when the clause is that single
    obligation;
  * option-local mechanics cannot be hoisted, because hoisting would put two
    obligations on one clause, which now fails validation.
Enforce it in the evaluator and registry, document it in ADR 0020 as the
load-bearing invariant, and add tests that a clause claiming two obligations
fails closed. Retain field-count multiplicity WITHIN a facet (two saves in one
clause).

=== F1 (P1) CANONICAL BASE REQUIREMENTS ARE GONE — contracts.ts:111 ===
The published contract makes identity, sourceSpans, provenance, semanticOwner
and recordOwner UNREMOVABLE canonical requirements. The facet re-architecture
deleted BASE_REQUIREMENTS entirely; FACET_REQUIREMENTS holds only facet rules
and the evaluator never validates identity/provenance/ownership. A generated
clause with empty identity or owner evaluates semantically complete. Affects
every facet and all 15 families.
FIX: reinstate executable canonical base requirements that apply to EVERY
obligation and cannot be removed or overridden, plus an adversarial matrix that
removes or corrupts each base field in turn.

=== F2 (P1) SPECIALIZED FACETS ARE NOT CLOSED UNDER THEIR BASE — contracts.ts:115 ===
'save-with-damage' requires only a damage atom, not a save, so saves:[] plus one
damage certifies. Same for save-without-damage, save-with-alternate-outcomes,
attack-with-one-damage-mode, attack-with-conditional-alternatives,
resource-with-reset, and effect-without-lifecycle.
FIX: define ENFORCED facet implications (specialized implies its base mechanic)
or make each specialized facet self-contained. Add GENERATED removal tests for
every specialized facet — remove the base atom, assert incomplete.

=== F3 (P1) FACET VOCABULARY CANNOT EXPRESS THE CONTRACT'S TIMING — types.ts:80 ===
The contract assigns duration, recurrence, repeatChecks, immunityWindows and
termination to this PR, required exactly when an obligation declares them. There
is no generic recurrence facet and no immunity-window facet, so an authoritative
obligation cannot state them without a caller-side extension. Cross-kind gap for
spells, creature entries, hazards, features, magic items.
FIX: add canonical facets and predicates for recurrence and immunity windows,
with permanent sibling coverage.

=== F5 (P1) ALTERNATIVES PROVE NOTHING — contracts.ts:427 ===
The check only requires each alternative to name SOME existing alternative, so
A<->B plus C->A passes though B and C may overlap, and the committed test
permits every clauseIds list to be empty. Branch predicates count shells without
proving a source-backed outcome or condition.
FIX: validate the exclusion GRAPH (symmetry and partition), bind branches and
alternatives to projected atom identities, and add asymmetric, partially
connected, empty-binding and cross-kind regression cases.

=== F6 (P1) OBLIGATION IDENTITY IS NOT TIED TO ITS EVIDENCE — obligations.ts:104 ===
Validation checks only the obl: shape and that the terminal facet appears in
requiredFacets. It never verifies the ID's sourceRef/locator against the
obligation's source-span or authoritative-input evidence. Tests append synthetic
::index suffixes to the ID locator while keeping a DIFFERENT evidence locator,
and two same-facet obligations at one locator collide.
FIX: define a stable source-derived occurrence/clause locator so repeated
clauses at one anchor are distinguishable, and validate EVERY identity component
against origin-appropriate evidence. Reject synthetic locator divergence.

=== F7 (P1) CLOSURE BYPASSES ITS SCOPE AND CROSSES RECORDS — obligations.ts:263 ===
evaluateObligationClosure accepts any structurally shaped ObligationScope and
never requires createObligationScope, so a selectively omitted membership
returns a false-green empty closure. It also never checks
clause.recordOwner.family/key against the scope, so another record's clause can
satisfy this scope. T1/T7 only cover the constructor path.
FIX: consume an OPAQUE validated scope (brand it so a raw object literal cannot
be passed), validate applicability evidence, enforce exact family+record owner
matching, report unexpected claims, and add bypass / wrong-family / wrong-record
tests.

=== F8 (P1) AUDIT-ONLY EVIDENCE SATISFIES CAPTURED — contracts.ts:516 ===
The ADR says CAPTURED requires source-span or authoritative-input evidence, but
the loop accepts ANY registry evidence kind when the injected resolver returns
resolved. Since audit-finding origin is valid with only audit-finding evidence,
a KNOWN MISSING source clause can become captured and therefore semantically
complete.
FIX: restrict CAPTURED satisfaction to source-span or authoritative-input
evidence tied to that obligation. audit-finding and known-missing-source-clause
evidence IDENTIFY a gap; they must never close one. Add audit-only and
known-missing fail-closed tests.

=== F9 (P1) THE ENGINE-CAPABILITY CONTRACT IS NOT ENCODED — types.ts:375 ===
'export type EngineCapability = string' — any string. The contract requires
qualified engine:F1..engine:F10 owned through the eshyra-olc5 family epics, yet
committed tests use engine:save / eshyra-cap-save and an injected resolver
certifies them. Separately, ClauseReadinessEvidence.supported is never consumed,
so stored evidence can drift from requiredEngineCapabilities.
FIX: encode the closed identity shape and validate it; reconcile the two
capability-evidence surfaces so they cannot diverge; test unqualified,
wrong-owner, stale and mismatched references. This does NOT require real
execution — the contract defers that.

=== F10 (P2) THE VALIDATED REGISTRY IS MUTABLE — obligations.ts:176 ===
Records are shallow-frozen; evidence arrays, requiredFacets and nested evidence
objects are not, and scope applicability/evidence are retained by reference.
FIX: deep-copy and deep-freeze validated artifacts, or encapsulate them behind
immutable accessors. Add mutation-attempt regression tests.

=== ADR 0020 ===
Update it for the one-obligation-per-clause invariant, the base requirements,
facet implications, the recurrence/immunity facets, the identity-to-evidence
binding, opaque scopes, the CAPTURED restriction, and the capability identity.

CROSS-PR HONESTY: the ADR currently claims a shared identity with #476/#477 that
does not mechanically exist — #476 uses MembershipIdentity{recordKey, clauseId?,
path?, sourceSpan?} with no obligationId, and #477 accepts a broad obl:::
string. Do NOT overclaim. State precisely what is shared today, what is not, and
that validated adapters or parity tests are required before this is treated as
an integration boundary. A supervisor correction to #477's identity validation
is already in flight.

scope only — no importer, projector, pack regeneration, or engine registry
implementation. Edit only the files above; do not touch package.json,
internal.ts, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .github/, or any script/CI file. Do not

Never delete a test to make a finding disappear.

ROOT REASON FOR THE SPLIT: the finding registry contains two different kinds of row and only one of them belongs to registry construction.
  * QUERY-SCOPED rows: membership is derivable by executing a predicate against the committed pack. These were derived correctly in eshyra-o9bd.19.1.6 — rule corpus 335, spells 319, engine-pending clauses 794, half-damage 93.
  * PROSE-SCOPED rows: membership must be reconciled against the prose of the four 2026-07-24 audit reviews before any predicate can be written. Two attempts filled these with a single exemplar plus a boilerplate justification sentence, which is a schema-conformant facade and cannot prove non-recurrence.

This bead owns the second kind. It is corpus analysis, not registry construction.

SCOPE: for every row that eshyra-o9bd.19.1.6 marks membershipStatus='underived', reconcile the finding's true population against /mnt/d/eshyra-2026-07-24-audit-repair-bead-plan.md and the committed pack, then replace the placeholder with an executable query plus a reproducible baseline snapshot of identities, and flip the row to membershipStatus='derived'.

KNOWN EXAMPLES (not the full set — the full set is whatever the registry marks underived):
  indep:008  '23 incomplete locators'                    currently n=1
  sol:CAP-003 spell mechanics shallower than source      currently n=1
  indep:006  creature trigger/branch/timing/lifecycle    currently n=1
  sol:CAP-004 creature/stat-block mechanics incomplete   currently n=1
  fable:F3   creature rider/ongoing damage untyped       currently n=1
  opus:F-15  spellcasting granularity                    currently n=1
  fable:F8   rule keying/duplication hygiene             currently n=1

LIKELY BLOCKED ON: eshyra-o9bd.19.1.1 (clause IR) for any row whose target is clause-level rather than record-level, because the pack cannot express clause identity until that lands.

GATE: while any row remains underived, the finding registry's closure predicate returns false and eshyra-o9bd.19.6.4 cannot certify zero-repeat closure. That is deliberate — an underived row must block closure rather than pass as an exemplar.

COUNT HYGIENE: a generated, regenerable snapshot of member identities is required and is NOT a hand-copied count. Transcribing a total (23, 79, 391) into an assertion remains forbidden.

title: Dispatch: derive real audited membership and specific invariants (attempt 5)
description:
Supervisor fresh full review of f0e367c found a NEW DEFECT CLASS: the durable
model is structurally correct but its CONTENT is synthesized. Per the churn stop
rule this is the ONE permitted contract update and correction round. If the next
fresh full review finds another new defect class, PR #476 gets decomposed rather
than patched again.

=== KEEP — do not rebuild ===
The row model is right and reviewed: obligation + target + invariant (durable)
separated from violation (transient), baselineMembership distinct from generated
current membership, 68 rows, 70 aliases resolving, indep:011 accepted, the
indep:001 / sol:CAP-001 split, duplicate-canonicalId rejection. Keep all of it
and its tests. This round replaces synthesized CONTENT, not structure.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.md
  packages/core/src/rules/findingRegistry.ts
  packages/core/test/findingRegistry.test.ts

=== DEFECT 1: baselineMembership IS EXEMPLAR DATA, NOT AUDITED MEMBERSHIP ===
59 of 68 rows carry exactly ONE member; 7 carry two; 2 carry three.
  * half-damage-branches IS opus:F-25, whose own title reads '79 creature + 8
    hazard half-damage branches omitted'. Its baseline has 2 members.
  * rule-corpus-procedures IS sol:CAP-001, the 335-record rule corpus. 1 member.
  * spell-completeness spans 319 spells. 1 member.
A single exemplar cannot detect a defect that recurs anywhere else in the
population, which is the registry's entire purpose at eshyra-o9bd.19.6.4.

REQUIRED: derive baselineMembership by GENERATING it against the committed pack
at packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json, reconciled
with the finding's own stated scope in
/mnt/d/eshyra-2026-07-24-audit-repair-bead-plan.md. Records use the `key`
field, not `id`; executionReadiness is at record.data.executionReadiness and
exists on MAGIC-ITEM RECORDS ONLY.

Where a finding's true population is large, enumerate it fully — a generated
snapshot of identities is not a hand-copied count and does not violate count
hygiene. Where the population genuinely cannot be derived yet (for example it
needs the clause IR from PR #475), the row must say so EXPLICITLY with a defined
follow-up and a status the validator recognises — it must NOT carry an exemplar
that reads as exact.

Add a validator rule and test: a row whose finding scope indicates a population
may not carry a baseline of one or two members without an explicit, reviewed
`exemplarJustification` naming why the population is genuinely that small.

=== DEFECT 2: INVARIANTS ARE TEMPLATED BOILERPLATE ===
All 68 read as 'The source-backed obligation for <canonicalId> remains
represented at the exact audited target and satisfies its authoritative source'
— the ID interpolated into one sentence. An invariant that is the same sentence
for every row states nothing and cannot be checked.

REQUIRED: each invariant states, in terms specific to THAT defect, what must
hold after repair — the positive semantic property. Add a test rejecting rows
whose invariant is derivable from the canonicalId by template substitution.

=== DEFECT 3: CASE 7 IS MIS-TYPED ===
No row uses target.kind='capability'. engine-capability-ownership is typed
'record' selecting the single record magic-item:bag-of-beans, though the finding
covers the engine-pending clause population. The test named 'represents nested,
artifact, narrowed, capability, and cross-kind cases' therefore asserts coverage
the data does not have — fix the data, and make the test verify the target kinds
it names rather than merely running.

Re-audit ALL TEN required cases the same way: confirm each is represented by a
row whose target KIND and selector actually match the case, not by a row that
merely exists.

=== ENVIRONMENT / CONSTRAINTS ===
Run `npm ci` first; `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing. Edit only
the files above; do not touch package.json, internal.ts, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md,
.github/, or any script/CI file. Do not regenerate the pack or run the importer.
Do not modify any bead but your own, do not bd dolt push, do not push or
comment on a PR, do not merge. Never delete a test to make a finding disappear.

title: Dispatch: per-source executable evidence model for all 31 rows (attempt 4)
description:
Human review of PR #477 at f2e7891 accepted the previous corrections but found six
further defects. The supervisor independently confirmed the two most serious in
the code. This is an evidence-model re-architecture, not six patches.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.md
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/2n1t-engine-closure-reconciliation.md
  packages/core/src/rules/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.ts
  packages/core/test/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.test.ts

=== SUPERVISOR-CONFIRMED DEFECT 1: THE EVALUATOR ONLY SEES MAGIC ITEMS ===
bootstrapCapabilityLedger.ts reads `record.data.executionReadiness` as its sole
executable evidence. In the committed pack `executionReadiness` exists on
MAGIC-ITEM RECORDS ONLY — verified against
packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json. So every row
across engine:F1..F10, including rest/time, downtime/currency, hit-point
lifecycle and geometry primitives, is "proved" by a magic-item-only evaluator.
The ledger claims five sources and proves one, narrowly.

=== SUPERVISOR-CONFIRMED DEFECT 2: UNCONSTRAINED SUBSTRING MATCHING ===
Hook matching is `text.includes(term.toLowerCase())` over free text. That will
assign hooks to the wrong primitive on near-matches, prefixes, suffixes, and
unrelated strings containing the token. "table" matches "comfortable";
"pool" matches "whirlpool"; "reset" matches "preset".

=== SUPERVISOR EVIDENCE MODEL — replace packEvidence entirely ===
A row carries an ARRAY of evidence items, each a discriminated union member with
its OWN executable resolver and its OWN expected-result semantics:

  { kind:'readiness-artifact', queryId, engine, hookSelector, expected }
      hookSelector uses EXACT structured hook identity — match
      engineHooks[].engine exactly and the hook's structured id/name exactly.
      No substring matching over free text. Ever.
  { kind:'code', queryId, module, symbol, expected }
      resolver proves the named symbol/site actually exists in @eshyra/core.
  { kind:'bead', beadId, expected }
      resolver checks via bd, SKIPPING GRACEFULLY when the binary is absent —
      keep the existing skip discipline, do not make the suite need bd.
  { kind:'audit-finding', findingAlias, expected }
      findingAlias must be fully qualified (engine:/fable:/opus:/sol:/indep:)
      and must resolve to a known finding.
  { kind:'known-missing-source-clause', sourceRef, locator, expected:'absent-from-pack' }
      must POSITIVELY PROVE absence from the pack, not merely return nothing.

Rules:
* Every row names at least one executable evidence item, or an explicit,
  reviewed non-query evidence method with a stated reason.
* A row's evidence must come from the source APPROPRIATE TO THAT ROW. A
  magic-item readiness query is not evidence for a rest/time primitive.
* EXPECTED-RESULT SEMANTICS ARE PER EVIDENCE KIND. Fail when a required baseline
  membership is unexpectedly empty; when a query is malformed or points at the
  wrong source; when a primitive has no independently grounded evidence; or when
  the evaluator never exercised the row. An empty result must never silently
  pass. Approved source-missing primitives may legitimately have no pack hook —
  but they must carry non-pack evidence AND prove the absence is expected.

=== QUERY IDENTITY BINDING ===
Validation must reject: unknown query IDs; duplicate or ambiguous query
ownership; a query used for a different primitive without explicit reviewed
multi-ownership; rows with neither an executable query nor a reviewed non-query
method; and evaluator results that cannot be traced back to their row.
Positional, implicit, or family-level association is inadequate.

=== PRIMITIVE-LEVEL SPECIFICITY ===
Three rows presented as primitive-level currently query or return whole engine
families. Family membership may GROUP, but never substitutes for primitive
identity or exact affected membership. Review ALL 31 ROWS for this failure mode,
not only the three observed.

=== SHARED SOURCE-OBLIGATION IDENTITY (binding across #475, #476, #477) ===
  obligationId := "obl:<sourceRef>:<locator>:<facet>"
EVIDENCE KIND closed union, shared conceptually:
  'source-span' | 'authoritative-input' | 'audit-finding' | 'code' | 'bead'
  | 'known-missing-source-clause'
Do NOT overload one `sourceSpan` field to represent incompatible evidence
types — that is exactly the current defect. Distinguish exact source span,
authoritative non-PDF input, audit-finding identity, code evidence, bead
evidence, and known-missing source clause.
Do NOT import code from the #475 or #476 branches; align concepts, duplicate the
small types locally, and record the temporary duplication and integration
boundary in bootstrap-capability-ledger.md.

=== PRESERVE — reverify, do not regress ===
The PREMATURE / OVERSTATED UMBRELLA CLOSURE classification of eshyra-2n1t and
its supporting argument; corrective routing of .6/.7/.9/.12 to the four child
beads; proposed-row ownership representability with its positive test; the
pinned seven non-pack primitives; recursive stored-total rejection. Keep their
tests. The legendary-action-budget row must remain demonstrable evidence that
the bootstrap method escapes pack-derived blind spots.

=== ENVIRONMENT AND VERIFICATION ===
Run `npm ci` FIRST. Run `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing — it
rewrites files. If rulesPackAuditCli or dolt-gated suites time out under load,
rerun that file in isolation before concluding a regression.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
* Edit ONLY the files above. Do not touch package.json,
  packages/core/package.json, packages/core/src/internal.ts, AGENTS.md,
  CLAUDE.md, .github/, or any script/protocol/CI file. Review infrastructure is
  OUT OF SCOPE this session.
* Do NOT regenerate the rules pack, run the importer, or edit packages/core/data.
* Do NOT create, reopen, or close any bead except your own. Do NOT run
  `bd dolt push`. Do NOT push, comment on a PR, or merge.
* Where a committed test encodes defective behavior, change it deliberately and
  record why. Never delete a test to make a finding disappear.
acceptance_criteria:
• Evidence is a per-source discriminated union with its own resolver and expected-result semantics; no magic-item readiness query is used as evidence for a non-magic-item primitive.
• Hook matching uses exact structured identity; negative tests cover near-matches, prefixes, suffixes, and unrelated strings containing the token.
• Every row binds to a named query identity; unknown, duplicate, ambiguous, untraceable, or missing query bindings are rejected.
• Empty results never silently pass; each evidence kind defines when empty is valid, and source-missing primitives positively prove expected absence.
• All 31 rows reviewed for family-substitution; every primitive row has primitive-specific evidence.
• Evidence kinds are distinct; sourceSpan is no longer overloaded; the shared cross-PR identity is used and the deferred integration boundary is documented.
• Umbrella-closure classification, .6/.7/.9/.12 routing, proposed-row representability, the seven non-pack primitives, and recursive count rejection are preserved with tests.
• npm run verify:worktree passes.

title: Dispatch: durable exact-membership model for all 68 rows (attempt 4)
description:
Human review of PR #476 at cd2d6ae accepted the previous corrections but found
one remaining P1: the membership model is not exact or durable enough to govern
repair and prove zero recurrence. This is a CONTRACT-LEVEL change affecting all
68 rows. The supervisor has fixed the model below; implement it and migrate
every row.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/finding-registry.md
  packages/core/src/rules/findingRegistry.ts
  packages/core/test/findingRegistry.test.ts

=== THE ROOT DEFECT ===
Today a row carries `membershipQuery` and nothing else that survives repair.
That single field conflates two different things: WHAT MUST HOLD (durable) and
WHAT IS CURRENTLY WRONG (transient). When the defect is repaired the query
returns zero rows and the obligation evaporates — so the registry cannot prove
non-recurrence, which is its entire purpose at eshyra-o9bd.19.6.4.

=== SUPERVISOR ROW MODEL — apply uniformly to all 68 rows ===
One coherent model. Do NOT create weak per-family conventions.

  canonicalId, aliases[], title, status, statusReasoning
  obligation {
    obligationId      shared format above where source-backed
    evidenceKind      the closed union above
    authority         what establishes this obligation INDEPENDENTLY of the
                      current pack — a source locator, an authoritative input,
                      or an audit-finding identity. The pack under repair may
                      never be the sole authority for its own obligations.
  }
  target {            what the obligation is ABOUT; survives repair
    kind              'record'|'clause'|'field'|'path'|'relationship'|'capability'
    selector          STRUCTURED and exact — not a text search
  }
  invariant           stated POSITIVELY, as what must hold. Durable.
  violation {         the CURRENT defect predicate. May legitimately go empty.
    queryId
    expectedAfterRepair  'empty' | 'stable'
  }
  baselineMembership { the audited baseline, reproducible
    capturedAtCommit
    members[]         exact member identities
  }
  currentMembership   GENERATED at evaluation time; never stored as authority
  owningBead
  regression { evidenceKind, locator }

The durable identity is obligation + target + invariant. The violation query is
separate and MAY become empty after repair WITHOUT the row losing meaning. That
separation is the whole fix — do not collapse them back.

=== THE MODEL MUST SUPPORT ALL TEN CASES ===
Each needs at least one real row and a test:
 1 clause missing entirely from the current pack
 2 clause present on the wrong owner
 3 field present with the wrong value
 4 missing branch or alternative
 5 unsupported output with no authoritative source
 6 provenance or locator defect
 7 engine capability gap
 8 finding whose violating membership becomes EMPTY after repair
 9 ambiguous/narrowed finding whose preserved boundary must not regress
10 cross-kind defect whose membership spans multiple record families

Case 1 and case 5 are why `authority` may not come from the pack: a clause
MISSING from the pack cannot be found by querying the pack.

=== EXACTNESS REQUIREMENTS ===
* Reject generic/substring searches that can silently overmatch or undermatch.
  Selectors must be structured identities.
* Reject empty CURRENT membership when the row claims a live baseline defect,
  unless an explicit reviewed status makes emptiness valid — and then the row
  must say so and why.
* Preserve baseline membership separately from current generated membership.
  Baseline is a reproducible snapshot of IDENTITIES, which is not a hand-copied
  count and does not violate count hygiene. A transcribed total (391, 399, 77,
  79, 794) remains forbidden.
* No hard-coded total may be authority anywhere.

=== ROW-BY-ROW MIGRATION IS REQUIRED ===
Migrate and review ALL 68 rows. Do not migrate representative rows and
extrapolate. For each row decide its target kind, its authority, its invariant,
and whether its violation is expected to go empty after repair. If a row's exact
membership cannot yet be expressed — for example because the clause IR from
PR #475 has not landed — say so EXPLICITLY on the row with a defined follow-up,
rather than substituting a thematic query that reads as exact.

=== SHARED SOURCE-OBLIGATION IDENTITY (supervisor decision, binding across
PRs #475, #476, #477) ===
Fixed by the supervisor so the branches cannot invent competing definitions.
PR #475 is implementing the same identity in the clause IR.

  obligationId := "obl:<sourceRef>:<locator>:<facet>"
     sourceRef  stable source document identity, e.g. "srd-5.1"
     locator    source anchor, e.g. "p.104#fireball"
     facet      semantic facet name

EVIDENCE KIND is a closed union. Never overload one "sourceSpan" field to carry
incompatible evidence types:
  'source-span' | 'authoritative-input' | 'audit-finding' | 'code' | 'bead'
  | 'known-missing-source-clause'

DO NOT import code from the #475 branch — it is unfinished and on another
branch. Duplicate the small identity/evidence types locally, and record the
intentional temporary duplication plus the follow-up integration boundary in
finding-registry.md.

=== finding-registry.md ===
Document the model, the ten cases, the durable-vs-transient separation, the
authority rule, and the cross-PR identity with its deferred integration
boundary. The JSON stays the single source of truth; the .md must not restate
row data that could drift.

=== ENVIRONMENT AND VERIFICATION ===
Run `npm ci` FIRST. Run `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing — it
rewrites files. If rulesPackAuditCli or dolt-gated suites time out under load,
rerun that file in isolation before concluding a regression.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
* Edit ONLY the files under FILES YOU OWN. Do not touch package.json,
  packages/core/package.json, packages/core/src/internal.ts, AGENTS.md,
  CLAUDE.md, .github/, or any script/protocol/CI file. Review infrastructure is
  explicitly OUT OF SCOPE this session.
* Do NOT regenerate the rules pack, run the importer, or edit packages/core/data.
* Do NOT modify any bead except your own. Do NOT run `bd dolt push`.
* Do NOT push, open/comment on a PR, or merge.
* PRESERVE and do not regress the three previously accepted corrections:
  indep:011 reclassified with its extension boundary; indep:001 and sol:CAP-001
  separated; duplicate canonicalId rejected via a real Set with mutation
  coverage. Keep their tests.
* Where a committed test encodes defective behavior, change it deliberately and
  record why. Never delete a test to make a finding disappear.

title: Dispatch: clause obligation-boundary architecture (attempt 3)
description:
Human review of PR #475 at b0395e4 found FIVE P1 ARCHITECTURAL defects. Per the
churn stop rule this is a NEW DEFECT CLASS, so this is a re-architecture of the
obligation boundary, NOT five isolated patches. The supervisor has done the
threat model and fixed the architecture below; implement it.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/adr/0020-source-clause-semantic-ir-and-completeness-contracts.md
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/types.ts
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/contracts.ts
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/obligations.ts        (new)
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/index.ts
  packages/core/test/clauseIrContracts.test.ts
  packages/core/test/clauseIrObligations.test.ts          (new)

=== SUPERVISOR THREAT MODEL — the evaluator must defeat all eight ===
T1 projector never declares an obligation the source contains -> nothing fails.
T2 projector misclassifies the clause to a narrower/laxer kind.
T3 projector declares the obligation but weakens its requirement list.
T4 caller passes a permissive or empty contract to the evaluator.
T5 caller asserts readiness dimensions true with no evidence.
T6 a kind contract demands semantically invalid things, pressuring projectors
   toward T2 to escape it.
T7 a family is reported covered although its obligations were never enumerated.
T8 unknown or contradictory contract selection silently defaults to something.

Every one of these needs an adversarial test named for the threat it defeats.

=== D1: OBLIGATIONS HAVE AN AUTHORITY INDEPENDENT OF THE PROJECTOR (T1,T2,T3) ===
Today `SourceObligation.requirements` is inline on the Clause, so the producer
of the output also defines the standard its output is judged by. That is the
root defect; the other four are consequences.

Introduce an OBLIGATION REGISTRY, separate from any clause:
  * a `SourceObligationRecord` carries obligationId (shared format above),
    `origin`, evidence, and `requiredFacets`.
  * `origin` is a closed union that CANNOT be 'projector':
    'source-extraction' | 'curated-specification' | 'audit-finding'.
  * a Clause REFERENCES obligations by id only. It must not be able to state
    their requirements.
  * the evaluator resolves each obligation FROM THE REGISTRY. A clause citing an
    obligationId absent from the registry FAILS CLOSED (defeats T2/T3).
  * registry construction validates that each record carries resolvable evidence
    of its declared origin.

=== D2: OMISSION MUST BE VISIBLE — CLOSURE OVER A SCOPE (T1, T7) ===
Add `evaluateObligationClosure(registry, clauses, scope)` returning, per
obligation: satisfied | claimed-incomplete | UNCLAIMED. An obligation in the
registry that no clause claims is the ONLY way T1 becomes visible, and it is the
real answer to finding 5: a record-family array establishes APPLICABILITY, never
closure. Keep these four concepts explicitly distinct in types and in the ADR:
family applicability; source-derived obligation membership; per-obligation
completeness; aggregate family closure.

=== D3: CANONICAL REQUIREMENTS ARE NOT BYPASSABLE (T4, T8) ===
`evaluateClauseCompleteness(clause, contract)` currently accepts ANY contract,
so an empty one certifies anything. Change the signature so the evaluator
derives the canonical contract internally from the resolved obligation's facets.
Extensions may only be ADDITIVE (`additionalRequirements`); there must be no
code path by which an ordinary caller removes a canonical requirement. Unknown
facet, unknown contract id, or contradictory selection FAILS CLOSED — never
defaults to a laxer contract.

=== D4: FACETS REPLACE UNIVERSAL KIND CONTRACTS (T6) ===
The `save` contract currently requires `nonEmpty('damage')`, so a save that
deals no damage — a save against being frightened — cannot be represented as
complete. That is an invalid universal assumption and it actively pressures
projectors toward T2.

Replace kind-level universals with COMPOSABLE SEMANTIC FACETS. Each facet owns
its own requirements; the OBLIGATION names which facets the source demands. The
model must express at least, and each needs a test:
  save with damage                     | save without damage
  save with alternate outcomes         | attack with one damage mode
  attack with conditional or mutually exclusive alternatives
  resource use with reset              | resource use without reset
  duration with concentration          | duration without concentration
  effect with lifecycle state          | effect without lifecycle state

DO NOT solve this by making requirements optional. The obligation must still
state EXACTLY which facets are required for that source clause; what changes is
that the requirement set comes from the source-declared facets rather than from
a blanket kind assumption.

=== D5: READINESS NEEDS EVIDENCE, NOT BOOLEANS (T5) ===
`ClauseReadiness.dimensions` is four caller-set booleans. Self-attestation is
not proof. Replace with per-dimension EVIDENCE:
  captured      resolvable source-span/authoritative-input evidence
  projected     DERIVED from the semantic evaluation — not settable by a caller
  supported     a capability reference naming an engine capability identity AND
                its owning bead; unresolved, unowned or unimplemented => failed
  discoverable  a resolver/index/path reference; unresolved => failed
Evidence must be inspectable and must reject stale or nonexistent references.
A clause must NOT be green when the representation exists but its required
engine capability is unowned.

This PR stays design/type-contract scope: do NOT build the engine capability
registry. Inject resolver interfaces (e.g. a CapabilityResolver and a
DiscoveryResolver) so the evaluator consumes evidence it cannot forge, and
provide test doubles. The requirement is that the TYPES AND EVALUATOR CANNOT
ENCODE SELF-ATTESTATION AS PROOF.

=== SHARED SOURCE-OBLIGATION IDENTITY (supervisor decision, binding across
PRs #475, #476, #477) ===
This identity is fixed by the supervisor so the three branches cannot invent
competing definitions. Implement it here; #476 and #477 will align to it.

  obligationId := "obl:<sourceRef>:<locator>:<facet>"
     sourceRef  stable source document identity, e.g. "srd-5.1"
     locator    source anchor, e.g. "p.104#fireball"
     facet      semantic facet name (see the facet model below)

EVIDENCE KIND is a closed union, shared conceptually across all three PRs. Never
overload one "sourceSpan" field to carry incompatible evidence types:

  'source-span'                 exact span in the licensed source document
  'authoritative-input'         non-PDF authoritative input (curated spec, table)
  'audit-finding'               a 2026-07-24 finding identity
  'code'                        an implementation site in @eshyra/core
  'bead'                        a bead identity
  'known-missing-source-clause' source clause known absent from projection

#475 owns 'source-span' and 'authoritative-input' in depth; the other members
must exist in the type so #476/#477 can align without redefining the union.

DO NOT import code across branches. Align the CONCEPTS; duplicate the small
identity/evidence types locally and note the integration boundary in the ADR.

=== ADR 0020 ===
Rewrite to describe this architecture: the obligation authority boundary, the
facet model, non-bypassable canonical requirements, evidence-backed readiness,
and the applicability/membership/completeness/closure distinction. State the
cross-PR identity and the deferred integration boundary. The ADR is what the
rest of the program cites — it must not describe the superseded design.

=== ENVIRONMENT AND VERIFICATION ===
Run `npm ci` FIRST. Run `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing — it
rewrites files. Machine load matters: if rulesPackAuditCli or dolt-gated suites
time out, rerun that file in isolation before concluding a regression.

title: Dispatch: bootstrap ledger review corrections from PR #477 (attempt 3)
description:
HUMAN REVIEW OF PR #477 at head 8fd61cf returned "request changes": three P1,
four P2 and one remaining P3. All are accepted. Read the review on
https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/477 for the reviewer's exact wording.
Both CI workflows pass — these are contract defects CI cannot catch.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.md
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/2n1t-engine-closure-reconciliation.md
  packages/core/src/rules/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.ts
  packages/core/test/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.test.ts

=== P1-A: THE VALIDATOR CAN NO LONGER REPRESENT proposed-new-bead ===
*** THIS IS THE SUPERVISOR'S REGRESSION, INTRODUCED IN COMMIT 8fd61cf. ***
The schema requires every row to have an owningBead. The new invariant then
UNCONDITIONALLY rejects 'eshyra-olc5' as owningBead — including when
ownershipStatus is 'proposed-new-bead'. The failure message advises using
ownershipStatus=proposed-new-bead, which does not bypass the rejection. There is
now no honest value for owningBead when no bead and no exact family owner
exists: a caller must invent a nonexistent bead ID or falsely assign a family
epic. That contradicts the documented workflow, which says future unowned
primitives are recorded as proposed in the same manner.

Fix: make owningBead optional/null for proposed rows, OR permit the engine epic
root ONLY when ownershipStatus === 'proposed-new-bead'. Then add a POSITIVE test
that constructs a proposed row and validates it successfully — the existing
proposed-row loop is vacuous because the checked-in ledger now contains none.
Keep the real invariant intact: an 'owned' row may never name the engine epic
root.

=== P1-B: THE RECONCILIATION STILL REACHES THE WRONG CONCLUSION ===
See the CORRECTION note on the parent bead eshyra-o9bd.19.5.1 — read it first;
it is authoritative over the parent description's four-category list.

The document concludes zero premature closures and classifies eshyra-2n1t itself
as only a taxonomy mismatch. But the PR that closed it was titled "Complete SRD
audit and engine gaps", claimed source-grounded executable mechanics for ALL 240
magic items, reported zero deep-audit findings, and named eshyra-2n1t and
eshyra-o9bd.18 as its beads.

Narrow child beads may still be correctly closed — their primitives landed. The
umbrella completeness claim is a different object. Distinguish explicitly:
  * narrow child acceptance genuinely completed;
  * broader integration not completed;
  * umbrella epic closed on a global claim later proven false.
Classify eshyra-2n1t as premature / overstated umbrella closure, or add an
equivalent explicit category and define it. Rewrite the "Why no category is
PREMATURE CLOSURE" section accordingly — do not leave a heading that contradicts
the table.

Also reconsider eshyra-o9bd.18.7: source clauses omitted or silently partially
projected are IMPORTER/COMPILER completeness defects, not merely downstream
engine work. Its current DIFFERENT SCOPE OR TAXONOMY classification rests on
that mischaracterization.

Still do not reopen, close, or modify any bead. Record recommendations as data.

=== P1-C: packEvidence IS PROSE, NOT AN EXECUTABLE QUERY ===
This is the deepest finding. The docs say membership is represented by generated
queries and tell consumers to execute them. In reality packEvidence is a
free-form string; validation only checks non-emptiness and the test only greps
for the substrings 'record.key' and 'data.executionReadiness'. There is no query
identifier, evaluator, predicate, generated record-key membership, or
source-comparison function.

Consequences: membership cannot be regenerated; two ledger versions cannot be
mechanically diffed; invalid or copy-pasted query prose stays green; and
eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12 cannot reliably reconcile the authoritative ledger against
this bootstrap one — which is that bead's entire purpose.

Fix: give rows STABLE QUERY IDS backed by executable functions, or a structured
query representation with a tested evaluator. Execute against the committed pack
at packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json. Rows whose
evidence is a negative or source-comparison claim need a REPRODUCIBLE SECOND
INPUT, not prose saying to compare against "the audit" — if the second input
cannot yet be expressed, say so explicitly on the row with a defined follow-up
rather than leaving prose that reads as executable.

Note the sibling work: eshyra-o9bd.19.1.6 (PR #476) is concurrently adding
stable membership identities {recordKey, clauseId/path, sourceSpan} to the
finding registry. Use a compatible identity shape so 19.5.12 can join them
later. Do not edit that file — it is on another branch.

=== P2-D: THE engine:F1 ROW QUERIES engine:F2 ===
Row capabilityId engine:F1, primitive 'seeded-selection-and-roll-replacement',
but its packEvidence selects hooks qualified as engine:F2 with activation /
action-economy semantics. That is unrelated evidence copied from the F2 family.
It should query F1 selection, table/pool/percentage, or roll-replacement hooks.
The executable query contract from P1-C must also ENFORCE that a row cannot
silently target another family.

=== P2-E: THE SEVEN-ROW NON-PACK PROOF IS NOT ASSERTED ===
The PR body claimed 7 of 31 rows are non-pack discoveries with a test asserting
it. The test only requires more than two rows plus the presence of the legendary
and point-origin primitives; the validator requires only three. The docs also
list retained-asset creation as a non-pack discovery, but that row includes
'readiness-artifacts' in discoveredBy, so by the ledger's own definition it is
not in the non-pack set.

Fix: pin the exact non-pack primitive IDs explicitly and assert that set. This
set is the evidence that the five-source method escaped the pack's blind spots,
so it must be exact and the prose must match the data.

=== P2-F: CORRECTIVE OWNERSHIP OMITS TWO OF FOUR OVERLAPS ===
The corrective section routes only eshyra-2n1t.7 and .12 to the new beads, but
the table itself establishes two more:
  * .6 includes spell copying among its missing engine:F4 procedures ->
    eshyra-o9bd.19.5.5.3
  * .9 includes planar-return clocks among its missing engine:F7 procedures ->
    eshyra-o9bd.19.5.8.3
Route .6, .7, .9 and .12.

=== P2-G: STORED-COUNT REJECTION IS NOT MEANINGFULLY TESTED ===
The validator rejects only four exact top-level keys: count, counts,
recordCount, clauseCount. Nested counts and names like total, storedCount or
hookTotal pass. Worse, the test mutates capabilityId AND count together, and
capability validation runs first — so the test can pass without ever exercising
count rejection.

Fix: split into separate tests, and either use a strict schema or recursively
reject count/total-shaped fields at any depth.

=== P3-H: THE VALIDATOR DOES NOT ENFORCE THE ADVERTISED SHAPE ===
The PR claims 31 rows and 2-4 per family; the validator enforces only >=2 per
family. It does not enforce a total, an upper bound per family, unique
primitives, or unique family/primitive pairs. Primitive uniqueness is checked
only against the current static file, not by the exported validator.
Enforce uniqueness of primitives and of family/primitive pairs in the validator.
Use judgement on hard totals — a fixed row count is itself a hand-copied number
and should NOT be asserted; an upper bound per family is also arbitrary. Prefer
enforcing the structural invariants and correcting the prose instead.

=== COUNT HYGIENE, CLARIFIED ===
A GENERATED, regenerable snapshot of member identities is NOT a hand-copied
count and is exactly the right instrument here. What is forbidden is a human
transcribing a total (391, 399, 77, 79, 794) into an assertion. Do not let the
count-hygiene rule block P1-C or P2-E.

=== ENVIRONMENT AND VERIFICATION ===
Run `npm ci` FIRST. Run `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing — it
rewrites files.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
* Edit ONLY the files listed above. Do not touch package.json,
  packages/core/package.json, or packages/core/src/internal.ts.
* Do NOT modify any bead except your own. Do NOT run `bd dolt push`.
* Do NOT push, do NOT open or comment on a PR, do NOT merge.
* Where a committed test encodes defective behavior, change it deliberately and
  record why. Do not delete a test to make a finding disappear.
* Do NOT regenerate the rules pack and do NOT run the SRD importer.

description:

  docs/adr/0020-source-clause-semantic-ir-and-completeness-contracts.md

  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/contracts.ts

  packages/core/test/clauseIrContracts.test.ts

=== P1-A: COMPLETENESS IS NOT SOURCE-SPECIFIC (contracts.ts:48) ===
Today the only authority is the projector-selected ClauseKind plus a generic
field list. Nothing binds an exact source clause to the semantic obligations
actually present in its source text.

The reviewer's worked example, which your tests must cover: a source clause
containing a save, a duration, a repeated save, and a termination condition can
be emitted as `kind: 'save'`. The save contract never requires duration,
repeatChecks or termination — so the evaluator CERTIFIES the partial projection.
That is the audit's root failure reproduced inside the very mechanism built to
prevent it.

Fix: completeness must be driven by SOURCE-BACKED PER-CLAUSE OBLIGATIONS, not by
the selected kind. Concretely, the clause must declare the obligations detected
in its source span, and the evaluator must require each declared obligation to
be discharged by a satisfied contract. Support composed contracts and/or child
clauses so one source clause can carry several obligations. A projector that
selects a narrower kind than its source text supports must fail closed rather
than silently narrowing.

You choose the exact representation, but the invariant is: the SOURCE decides
what must be present; the kind only decides HOW it is shaped.

=== P1-B: REQUIRED COLLECTIONS PASS WHEN EMPTY (contracts.ts:298) ===
Only `sourceSpans` has a cardinality check. Every other required array —
`saves`, `attacks`, `damage`, `alternatives`, `ledgerChanges`,
`stateTransitions`, `regressionEvidence` — passes when `[]`. A save clause
with `saves: []` and `damage: []`, populated branches and all dimensions true
returns `complete`. That directly violates the fail-closed invariant.

Fix: the contract vocabulary needs requirement PREDICATES with cardinality, not
boolean field presence. Include cross-field alternatives where the source
genuinely allows them (an attack roll XOR a saving throw, for example) so the
fix does not force absurd requirements. Add a test for the exact empty-array
case above.

=== P1-C: THE EVALUATOR COLLAPSES THE FOUR DIMENSIONS (contracts.ts:91) ===
ADR 0020 says CAPTURED, PROJECTED, SUPPORTED and DISCOVERABLE must fail
INDEPENDENTLY and no gate may collapse them. Requiring all four in every
ClauseCompletenessContract means a fully captured and projected clause that is
merely awaiting an engine or lookup path is labelled generically "incomplete".

*** THIS ONE IS MY FAULT, NOT YOURS. *** The attempt-1 dispatch spec explicitly
instructed that a CAPTURED+PROJECTED-but-not-SUPPORTED clause must not evaluate
complete, and the test at clauseIrContracts.test.ts:180-213 faithfully locks that
in. That instruction was wrong. You are expected to CHANGE that test.

The distinction to encode:
  * SEMANTIC COMPLETENESS — is the projection of this source clause complete?
    Determined by CAPTURED and PROJECTED and the source obligations from P1-A.
  * READINESS — can it execute end to end? SUPPORTED and DISCOVERABLE, reported
    per dimension.
A clause can be semantically complete and unsupported; that is the exact
distinction the audit needed and the pack lacked. Return independently gated
per-dimension results, or separate the two evaluations. Do not emit a single
all-or-nothing status that hides which dimension failed.

The nine-point green definition on eshyra-o9bd.19 still governs the FREEZE gate
and still requires an engine implementation — but that is a freeze gate, not a
clause-completeness verdict, and must not be smuggled into this evaluator.

=== P2-D: DISPOSITION CAN CONTRADICT THE CLAUSE (types.ts:277) ===
`disposition`, the dimension booleans and the free-text `note` can contradict
one another, and `evaluateClauseCompleteness` ignores `disposition` entirely.
So `disposition: 'complete'` with `projected: false` is legal, and
`disposition: 'incomplete'` with everything satisfied evaluates complete. The
clause also carries no structured failed-contract reasons, although the ADR
requires an emitted INCOMPLETE clause to NAME each failed requirement.

Fix: make the status derived/canonical, or validate consistency and fail closed
on contradiction; and carry structured contract failures on the emitted clause —
or make the evaluation result the sole authoritative readiness artifact and stop
storing a disposition that can drift.

=== ADR 0020 ===
Update it to match. It is the document the rest of the program will cite, so the
source-obligation rule, the cardinality rule, and the independence of the four
dimensions must be stated there, not only in code.

=== UNCHANGED ===
Design and type contracts only — no importer changes, no projector changes, no
pack regeneration. Small hand-built fixtures; do not load the 7.4 MB pack. No
hand-copied counts. Qualified engine:F* / fable:F* / opus:F-* / sol:CAP-* /
indep:* prefixes only, never a bare "F5".

=== DEFECT 1: THE RECONCILIATION OMITS NINE OF TWELVE CHILDREN ===
This is the important one. The document reconciles only eshyra-2n1t,
eshyra-2n1t.1 and eshyra-2n1t.2 — and .1/.2 are the two PRODUCT-DECISION
children (multiclass scope, creation-variant policy). The children that actually
claimed engine capability completeness were skipped entirely:

  eshyra-2n1t.3   F1: Dice-grammar extension (advantage/disadvantage, keep/drop)
  eshyra-2n1t.4   F2: Action-economy turn budget
  eshyra-2n1t.5   F3: Concentration & active-effect lifecycle
  eshyra-2n1t.7   F5: Usage/recharge, resource & attunement state
  eshyra-2n1t.8   F6: Death, dying & HP-buffer state
  eshyra-2n1t.9   F7: Rest engine (short/long rest)
  eshyra-2n1t.11  F9: Deterministic resolution & derived-math primitives
  eshyra-2n1t.12  F10: Canonical currency & trade gameplay surface
  eshyra-2n1t.13  Enforce fail-closed single-class character boundary

do not trust the list above to be exhaustive; there may be a .6 and a .10.

eshyra-o9bd.18.7.8 (attempt 1 already covered those last three; keep them).

These nine are the entire reason the deliverable exists: the audit found 794
engine-pending magic-item clauses three days after they closed claiming engine
capability work was done. Classifying only the two design-decision children
leaves that contradiction unexamined.

For each child: read its description, acceptance criteria and close reason, then
argue the classification PER BEAD — DIFFERENT SCOPE OR TAXONOMY | STALE READINESS
MAPPING | INCOMPLETE INTEGRATION | PREMATURE CLOSURE. Do not classify by number
similarity: eshyra-2n1t's F1-F10 is a DIFFERENT taxonomy from the pack's
engine:F1-F10 (that epic's F1 was dice grammar, F4 spell-slot economy, F8
character-build gaps, F9 derived math, F10 currency). Only F2/F3/F5/F7 roughly
correspond, and even those must be checked rather than assumed.

reached without examining these nine, so re-derive it rather than restating it.

the ledger to be the instrument that lets every missing hook find an owner. One
row per family cannot do that: engine:F5 alone carries 399 hook references
spanning charges, recharge scheduling, attunement, curse persistence and
per-instance state, which are distinct primitives with distinct implementations.

It also makes two acceptance criteria vacuous: "every engine:F1..F10 appears at
least once" is trivially true, and "every row maps to an existing bead" is
trivially true because the ten family epics exist.

    what they actually require, not by family label;
  * the 2026-07-06 inventories already in docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/
    (engine-coverage-inventory, execution-boundary-classification,
    rule-classification, magic-item-mechanics-inventory and siblings);
  * @eshyra/core as it exists today, for codeEvidence;
  * the audit findings in /mnt/d/eshyra-2026-07-24-audit-repair-bead-plan.md;
  * source clauses known to be missing from projection.

Consequences to handle:
  * `ownershipStatus` must now genuinely vary. Attempt 1 has all ten rows

    `proposed-new-bead` with a proposed title and parent, as DATA. Do not

description:
