parent spec first: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.1.1`, including its DESIGN section —
the scope guard there is binding.

=== SCOPE: DESIGN + TYPE CONTRACTS ONLY ===
The parent carries a TYPE GUARD: it may remain a task only while it is strictly
an ADR / schema-contract deliverable. This dispatch therefore delivers the
contract and its types and NOTHING ELSE. Do not touch the importer, do not
modify any existing projector, do not migrate any record, do not regenerate the
pack. Those belong to eshyra-o9bd.19.1.2, .19.3.*, .19.4.* and .19.6.1.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/adr/0020-source-clause-semantic-ir-and-completeness-contracts.md
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/types.ts
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/contracts.ts
  packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/index.ts
  packages/core/test/clauseIrContracts.test.ts
Do NOT edit packages/core/src/internal.ts — a sibling dispatch conventionally
owns it and export promotion is deferred to eshyra-o9bd.19.1.5. Your test
imports the new modules by relative path ('../src/rules/clauseIr/index.js'),
which is the established convention in packages/core/test.

=== WHAT TO BUILD ===

1. ADR 0020. It REFINES ADR 0017 — read docs/adr/0017-*.md and
   docs/rules-pack-compiler.md first and reference them explicitly. State:

   * The semantic unit is a source-backed CLAUSE, not a record. Records become
     materialized views that group clauses, with no loss of the current
     consumer surface.
   * The FOUR INDEPENDENT DIMENSIONS that replace the single overloaded word
     "modeled": CAPTURED (source text present), PROJECTED (structured fields
     exist), SUPPORTED (an engine capability can execute it), DISCOVERABLE
     (runtime lookup can find the canonical clause). They are orthogonal. A
     clause can be captured and projected yet unsupported and undiscoverable.
     No gate may collapse them into one verdict.
   * The scope guard, faithfully: the universal layer is ONLY clause identity,
     semantic ownership, completeness requirements, alternatives and branching,
     provenance, capability requirements, and readiness state. It explicitly
     PERMITS shared normalized primitives, kind-specific composition on top of
     them, curated source-backed specifications, and explicit
     unsupported/adjudicated clauses. It is NOT a universal rules DSL and does
     not require every D&D mechanic to compile into one generic runtime
     language.
   * THE DECISIVE RULE: when a projector recognizes that a deterministic clause
     exists but cannot completely represent it, it MUST emit an explicit
     INCOMPLETE clause and fail the appropriate gate. It must never produce a
     superficially valid partial record. Silent partial projection is the one
     forbidden behavior.
   * Why completeness cannot be judged from atom presence — it is evaluated
     against the clause KIND's contract. Ground this in the 2026-07-24 audit
     evidence: alternative damage modes stored as parallel damage, recharge
     triggers read as reset periods, partial saves treated as complete,
     legendary actions with no budget or cost, option mechanics hoisted onto
     parent features, typed records missing branching/timing/termination.

2. packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/types.ts — the IR expressed as TypeScript
   types. Every clause carries: stable clause identity; exact source span or
   spans; semantic owner and record owner; clause kind; trigger and eligibility
   predicates; activation / action-economy cost; targets and geometry; checks,
   attacks, saves, and MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE ALTERNATIVES; success, failure and
   partial-success branches; damage, healing, grants, ledger changes and state
   transitions; duration, recurrence, repeat checks, immunity windows and
   termination; execution owner and required engine capabilities; readiness
   disposition; regression evidence.
   Model INCOMPLETENESS as a first-class state, never as an absence: an
   incomplete clause names which contract requirement it fails and why.
   Required-capability values use the qualified engine:F1..engine:F10 form.

3. packages/core/src/rules/clauseIr/contracts.ts — the completeness contracts as
   DATA, not prose, with a pure evaluator.
   Contracts required for at least: attacks, saves, checks, branches, action
   economy, resources, durations, state transitions, geometry, choices,
   variants, entity lifecycles, ledgers, and model adjudication.
   A documented clause-completeness schema is required for every one of the
   fifteen mechanics-bearing record families: rule, feature, spell, creature,
   hazard, equipment, magic-item, ancestry, background, condition, action, feat,
   class, subclass, table.
   The evaluator takes a clause plus its contract and returns complete, or
   incomplete with named reasons. It must be structurally impossible to reach
   "complete" from atom presence alone.

4. packages/core/test/clauseIrContracts.test.ts. Assert at minimum:
   * every one of the fifteen record families has a registered contract;
   * every contract names its required clause kinds;
   * the four dimensions are independently representable, and a clause that is
     CAPTURED + PROJECTED but not SUPPORTED does not evaluate complete;
   * a clause with every atom present but a missing required branch evaluates
     INCOMPLETE with a named reason — this is the anti-silent-partial-projection
     regression and is the most important test in the file;
   * a projector that cannot fully represent a deterministic clause can express
     that ONLY as an explicit incomplete clause.

   is a contract, not a migration.

## REVIEW CONTRACT

Protocol: eshyra-clause-review-v1

Revised 2026-07-26 after DECOMPOSITION, approved by the user. Supersedes the
previous contract on this bead, which recorded an open failure. Derived from
commit f75acb2.

### Source obligation
- Source membership: 68 canonical rows covering all 70 review aliases from
  indep:*, opus:F-*, sol:CAP-* and fable:F*.
- Membership derivation: SPLIT. A row is membershipStatus='derived' only when its
  baseline snapshot is reproducible by re-running its named query and matching
  the stored identities. Every other row is 'underived' and carries a per-row
  underivedReason plus owningDerivationBead=eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7.
  CURRENT STATE: 0 derived, 68 underived. No row currently establishes
  authority independently of the pack under repair, so none qualifies. That is
  the honest measure of what this artifact grounds.
- Source spans or authoritative inputs: obligation.authority must be independent
  of the pack under repair.
- Complete obligations covered: the MODEL and the gating are complete here.
  Deriving membership for prose-scoped rows is eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7 and is
  explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for this PR.

### Pack or artifact representation
- Required semantic distinctions: target.kind in record|clause|field|path|
  relationship|capability with a structured selector, never a text search.
- Branches and alternatives: the ten required finding cases, verified by target
  kind and selector rather than by mere row existence.
- Timing, lifecycle, and termination: carried per finding.
- Provenance and ownership requirements: statusReasoning where status is not
  accepted; an owning repair bead; a regression form.

### Cross-kind and cross-surface checks
- Related kinds or subsystems: cross-kind findings use multi-family membership;
  target.kind=capability links engine findings to engine:F* families.
- Corpus-wide predicates or reconciliation: baselineMembership is a reproducible
  identity snapshot, distinct from generated current membership. The four
   half-damage 93.

### Engine capability
- Required capabilities: engine findings carry engineBoundary and
  target.kind=capability.
- Existing owner beads: eshyra-olc5 family epics.
- Known missing capability handling: routed through the owning repair bead.

### Reference execution or executable proof
- Real artifact or pack-driven scenarios: derived rows re-execute their query
  against the committed pack and must match the snapshot.
- Negative and fail-closed scenarios: findingRegistryClosureReady() returns
  false while any row is underived, naming them, tested in both directions;
  underivedReason may not be constant or template-derived; duplicate
  canonicalId rejected via a real Set; declared baseline member disappearance
  fails.
- Replay, rollback, or determinism requirements: bd owner checks skip gracefully
  when the binary is absent.

### Approved residuals
- Source ambiguities: none owned here.
- Deliberately model-adjudicated boundaries: indep:011 is an adjudication /
  policy extension point, status accepted with an escape-hatch regression.
- Explicitly unsupported scope: membership derivation for the 64 prose-scoped
  rows. This is DECLARED, machine-checkable, and blocks closure — it is not a
  silent gap. eshyra-o9bd.19.1.7 owns it and gates eshyra-o9bd.19.6.2 and
  eshyra-o9bd.19.6.4.

### Closure evidence
- Generated membership query: per-row violation queries plus the baseline
  snapshot for derived rows; findingRegistryClosureReady() is the gate.
- Permanent regression evidence: packages/core/test/findingRegistry.test.ts.
- Finding-registry aliases: this artifact IS the alias registry; all 70 aliases

description:
Own provider-neutral deterministic capabilities under ADR 0020. The legacy engine:F1-F10
inventory is a bounded backlog derived from magic-item executionReadiness, not a census of
all SRD mechanics. A capability is a positive commitment with operation, inputs, exclusions,
identity/revision, residual DM interpretation, real binding, provider-neutral execution,
and state effects.
acceptance_criteria:
- Selected capabilities have stable positive contracts, real bindings, provider-neutral execution, and correct deterministic state/resource effects.
- Legacy engine:F1-F10 membership is explicitly bounded and cannot be generalized to the rules corpus.
- Capability conformance proves only named operations/facets and declared exclusions.
- Unselected backlog entries may remain without being interpreted as source absence or a re-freeze failure.
- This epic cannot certify global deterministic completeness.
notes:
Supersedes the scope ambition of the CLOSED epic eshyra-2n1t, which used a DIFFERENT F1-F10 taxonomy. Do not treat eshyra-2n1t's closure as evidence of engine completeness; eshyra-o9bd.19.5.1 owns the four-way reconciliation of that contradiction.
*** GREEN DEFINITION REVISED (2026-07-25) — SUPERSEDES the 8-point version ***
DECISION: where structured pack data is a DIRECT INPUT to deterministic
execution, the pack contract and the reference engine are ONE co-designed
system. The pack defines what the engine must execute; the reference engine
proves the representation is sufficient and unambiguous. Freezing the pack
first would preserve a separation that does not exist in practice.

A deterministic clause that feeds engine execution is GREEN only when all nine
hold:
  1. Complete source-clause identification.
  2. Clause-complete structured representation.
  3. Complete field provenance.
  4. Explicit capability requirements.
  5. A provider-neutral engine implementation exists.
  6. Reference-engine conformance tests exercise the PACK representation.
  7. Correct tool exposure and state mutation.
  8. Fail-closed behavior for unsupported input.
  9. Successful replay / deterministic equivalence where applicable.

A clause is NOT green merely because the pack appears to contain enough data;
the reference implementation must demonstrate that it actually does. A
representation reference that merely RESOLVES to an existing object is not
green — the Opus amended magic-item pass proved reference integrity but
explicitly did NOT prove semantic appropriateness of free-form effects.

AT RE-FREEZE THERE MUST BE ZERO ENGINE-PENDING DETERMINISTIC CLAUSES. The only
permissible non-green clauses are four approved categories:
  * genuine source ambiguity routed to campaign rulings;
  * intentionally model-adjudicated material;
  * external content unavailable in the SRD;
  * explicitly deferred non-deterministic house-rule behavior.

Authority: ADR 0020, and the integrated transition design

sections 5.4, 5.5, 5.9 — the accepted deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8

   clause, and those obligations remain real.

   LONGER THE RE-FREEZE BAR. It requires a global negative the corpus cannot
   support: RulesRecord.data is typed unknown (rules/types.ts:135), kind
   validators accept unregistered data fields, and key closure over mechanics
   exists for magic-item only. The replacement is the nine-condition truthfulness
   bar in section 5.9 of the transition design, recorded on eshyra-o9bd.14 and

   3). A capability declares what operation it performs, its required inputs, its

MAGIC_ITEM_OPERATION_READINESS_CAPABILITY lives in deterministicCapabilityContract.ts. createDefaultToolRegistry (packages/core/src/orchestrator/tools.ts ~L178) registers DEFAULT_TOOLS (~70 tool modules under packages/core/src/orchestrator/tool*.ts). Non-tool deterministic engine paths exist too (character creation finalize/enforcement, level-up engine and its choice application, class resources, campaign binding resolution for rests/level-up, checkpoint/replay).
KNOWN TRUTHFULNESS DEFECT: resolve-check-v1 says 'Does not decide which modifiers apply' and residual 'The DM selects applicable modifiers', but since PR #637 (eshyra-r8en) resolve_check DERIVES the ability modifier and proficiency/expertise/half-proficiency/save-proficiency term from the actor's character sheet when skill/ability is given, and refuses caller-declared duplicates. The contract must be restated from the real tool contract, with a new revision ('resolve-check-v2'); every binding and reference to v1 moves to v2.
DECISIONS:
 D1 New internal module packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts exporting DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_INVENTORY: readonly entries, each EXACTLY ONCE: { revision, operationId, surface: {kind:'tool', name} | {kind:'engine', module, entryPoint}, category: 'state-integrity' (dice/RNG, arithmetic, atomic canonical mutation, resource accounting, identity/ownership, persistence/replay/rollback, visibility/authorization) | 'bounded-procedure' (a positively selected rules procedure), operation, requiredInputs, exclusions, residualDmInterpretation, runtimeOwner[], evidence[], ledgerContract?: revision }. For the three rule-bound contracts and the magic-item preflight the entry QUOTES the existing contract (spread/reference the object; never restate the same facts in different words). Read-only/query tools (lookup_rules, world_query, list_nearby_items, memory drilldown, ...) are included with category 'state-integrity' only if they enforce visibility/authorization; otherwise list them under a separate exported NON_CAPABILITY_TOOLS with a one-line reason each (e.g. 'read-only retrieval; makes no deterministic rules commitment'), so the closure test can account for every registered tool.
 D2 Every statement is derived from the tool's real input schema, description, and implementation (state functions it calls, refusals, what it does NOT decide). Exclusions and residual interpretation must name what the DM still decides. No statement may claim rules completeness. Prefer short, exact statements.
 D3 Closure evidence (the only closure claim, over Eshyra's own bounded registry): a test that every tool name in createDefaultToolRegistry() appears exactly once across inventory tool surfaces + NON_CAPABILITY_TOOLS, every inventory tool surface is registered, every RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_CONTRACTS revision is referenced exactly once by an inventory entry, MAGIC_ITEM_OPERATION_READINESS_CAPABILITY is referenced once, revisions are unique, and every runtimeOwner/evidence path exists on disk. Engine (non-tool) entries are curated with evidence pointers; no closure claim over engine code.
 D4 Backlog separation: export a function (e.g. summarizeMagicItemCapabilityBacklog(records)) that computes, from the pack by query, the legacy magic-item executionReadiness/engine:F backlog (records, clauses, engine-pending, hook-carrying) as a separate report object whose doc and fields state it is an UNSELECTED candidate backlog: never counted as implemented and never as absent. Test it against the real pack by structural assertions (non-negative, internally consistent), not hand-copied counts.
 D5 Presentation boundary: do NOT add new RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_BINDINGS or change RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_DISPOSITIONS (that would change what the DM model is told and needs its own presentation decision). Only the resolve-check v1->v2 truthfulness correction changes model-facing text. In the report, list each disposition row (e.g. rule:long-rest, rule:death-saving-throws) whose operation now has an inventory entry, as input to a later presentation decision.
 D6 Registry: finding row engine-capability-ownership (sol:CAP-007, owner eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12, disclosed-dependency) -> 'accepted' with statusReasoning naming this inventory, its closure test, and the separate backlog report.
EXCLUSIONS: no new capabilities, no behavior change to any tool, no corpus-wide completeness claim, no per-tool behavioral tests beyond existing evidence pointers.

- Completion proves the in-force capability set is truthfully stated; it does not prove deterministic completeness of the SRD.

title: Build the bootstrap capability ledger and reconcile prior engine beads
description:
Produce the FIRST capability inventory and the prior-bead reconciliation. This is
explicitly a BOOTSTRAP ledger, not the authoritative one (that is 19.5.12).

*** WHY THIS CANNOT BE DERIVED FROM THE PACK ***
The current pack OMITS whole clauses. A ledger generated only from its projected
mechanics inherits exactly the blind spots this audit exposed. Concretely: if
legendary-action budgets are absent from the pack, deriving requirements from the
pack cannot discover that a legendary-budget capability is needed. So the
bootstrap ledger must be assembled from FIVE sources, not one:
  1. current readiness artifacts (data.executionReadiness; the 2026-07-06
     execution-boundary and engine-coverage inventories);
  2. current code (what @eshyra/core actually implements today);
  3. current open AND closed beads;
  4. every accepted audit finding from the 2026-07-24 reviews;
  5. source clauses KNOWN to be missing from current projection (from the audit
     findings themselves — legendary budgets, point-origin geometry, multi-save
     entries, rider damage, half-damage branches, pit variants, etc.).
This bead can start immediately, before any A-epic work lands.

*** REQUIRED DELIVERABLE — the eshyra-2n1t contradiction ***
eshyra-2n1t (the "engine F1-F10" epic) was CLOSED 2026-07-21 claiming full
worktree/test/importer-reproducibility/freeze verification. Three days later the
audit finds 794 engine-pending magic-item clauses in the committed pack. Produce
a durable artifact classifying EACH old "engine complete" bead into exactly one:
  * DIFFERENT SCOPE OR TAXONOMY — correctly closed; never claimed the newly
    identified capability. (Most likely for engine:F1/F4/F8/F9/F10 given the
    taxonomy divergence.)
  * STALE READINESS MAPPING — the code exists, but readiness artifacts failed to
    recognize it.
  * INCOMPLETE INTEGRATION — a primitive exists but is not wired into the
    required execution path.
  * PREMATURE CLOSURE — the stated acceptance was objectively not satisfied.

Handling rules — PRESERVE HISTORICAL TRUTH, do not auto-reopen eshyra-2n1t:
  * Leave it closed where the scope was genuinely different.
  * Reopen the relevant old CHILD only where its stated acceptance was
    objectively unmet.
  * Otherwise create a new exact corrective child under eshyra-olc5 and link the old
    bead as historical context.
  * Add a note to the old epic linking the reconciliation result, so future
    reviewers cannot cite its closed status as proof of engine completeness.

Beads to reconcile (all currently CLOSED): eshyra-2n1t and its children,
eshyra-2n1t.1 (D1 multiclass scope -> ADR 0018), eshyra-2n1t.2 (D2
creation-variant policy), eshyra-b69j.13 (PR #311), eshyra-o9bd.18.7 and
eshyra-o9bd.18.7.8.

Baseline snapshot at 4384f25: 1,016 magic-item readiness clauses = 794
engine-pending + 218 green + 3 adjudicated-by-design + 1 design-blocked. Hook
references: engine:F1 83, F2 226, F3 31, F4 169, F5 399, F6 46, F7 15, F8 310,
F9 236, F10 9. Counts overlap because one clause may require several
capabilities.

COUNT HYGIENE: every number in this bead is a SNAPSHOT at commit 4384f25. The
generated ledger/predicate is authoritative. No acceptance test may require a
hand-copied number (e.g. 391, 399, 77, 79).

CANONICAL ALIAS PREFIXES — use these everywhere; never a bare "F1" or "CAP-001":
  engine:F1 .. engine:F10     pack executionReadiness engineHooks[].engine families
  fable:F1 .. fable:F8        Fable 5 audit findings
  opus:F-01 .. opus:F-35      Opus 5 original + amended audit findings
  sol:CAP-001 .. sol:CAP-014  GPT-5.6-Sol agent audit findings
  indep:001 .. indep:012      independent review (formerly "SOL-001..012"; renamed
                              so it stops colliding with the sol: model-name prefix)

## REVIEW CONTRACT

Protocol: eshyra-clause-review-v1

Migration baseline recorded 2026-07-26 during the final pre-protocol review
cycle. Derived from the corrected design at commit dee8d0a.

### Source obligation
- Source membership: 31 primitive rows spanning engine:F1..F10, each naming one
  implementation primitive rather than a family label.
- Membership derivation: the five bootstrap sources, each with its OWN
  executable resolver — readiness artifacts, @eshyra/core code, open and closed
  beads, accepted 2026-07-24 findings, and source clauses known missing from
  projection. A ledger derived from the pack alone inherits the pack's blind
  spots.
- Source spans or authoritative inputs: evidence is a discriminated union keyed
  by kind — 'readiness-artifact', 'code', 'bead', 'audit-finding',
  'known-missing-source-clause'. sourceSpan is NOT overloaded to carry
  incompatible evidence types.
- Complete obligations covered: bootstrap scope only. This ledger is explicitly
  NON-AUTHORITATIVE; eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12 regenerates the authoritative ledger
  from the clause-complete corpus and diffs against this one.

### Pack or artifact representation
- Required semantic distinctions: primitive identity, never family membership.
  Family grouping may organise rows but can never substitute for primitive
  identity or exact affected membership.
- Branches and alternatives: hook selection uses exact structured hook identity.
  Unconstrained substring matching is rejected, with negative tests for
  near-matches, prefixes, suffixes and unrelated strings sharing a token.
- Timing, lifecycle, and termination: carried by the individual primitives —
  planar-return and declared-window clocks, item-instance persistence,
  hit-point and death lifecycle.
- Provenance and ownership requirements: every row names an owning bead. An
  'owned' row may never name the engine epic root eshyra-olc5; a
  'proposed-new-bead' row may, and carries a proposed title and parent.

### Cross-kind and cross-surface checks
- Related kinds or subsystems: engine:F1..F10 plus the four cross-family
  primitive beads eshyra-o9bd.19.5.5.3, .19.5.6.3, .19.5.8.3 and .19.5.11.3.
- Corpus-wide predicates or reconciliation: 2n1t-engine-closure-reconciliation.md
  classifies eshyra-2n1t and all thirteen children plus eshyra-b69j.13,
  eshyra-o9bd.18.7 and .18.7.8. The epic itself is PREMATURE / OVERSTATED
  UMBRELLA CLOSURE; eight children are INCOMPLETE INTEGRATION. Corrective
  ownership routes .6, .7, .9 and .12 to the four new beads.

### Engine capability
- Required capabilities: all ten engine:F* families, at primitive granularity,
  several rows per family.
- Existing owner beads: the ten family epics under eshyra-olc5 own rows that fit
  a family; the four cross-family beads own the rest.
- Known missing capability handling: 'known-missing-source-clause' evidence must
  POSITIVELY PROVE absence from the pack. An empty query result is never
  accepted as proof.

### Reference execution or executable proof
- Real artifact or pack-driven scenarios: readiness-artifact evidence executes
  against the committed pack; code evidence proves the named symbol exists in
  @eshyra/core; bead evidence resolves through bd.
- Negative and fail-closed scenarios: unknown, duplicate, ambiguous, untraceable
  or missing query bindings are rejected; near-match hook identities are
  rejected; recursive stored-count/total fields are rejected at any depth;
  unexpectedly empty results fail per evidence kind.
- Replay, rollback, or determinism requirements: bd resolution SKIPS GRACEFULLY
  when the binary is absent, so the suite never depends on bd being installed.

### Approved residuals
- Source ambiguities: none owned here.
- Deliberately model-adjudicated boundaries: none owned here.
- Explicitly unsupported scope: implementing any engine capability. This bead
  inventories and reconciles; implementation belongs to the decomposition and
  certification tasks under eshyra-olc5.

### Closure evidence
- Generated membership query: per-row query identities resolved through the
  per-source evidence resolvers.
- Permanent regression evidence:
  packages/core/test/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.test.ts — exact structured hook
  identity, proof-of-absence, query-binding rejection, the pinned seven non-pack
  primitives, proposed-row representability, and rejection of the old overloaded
  pack evidence.
- Finding-registry aliases: sol:CAP-007, sol:CAP-014.

### Material contract changes in this cycle
1. Evidence became a per-source discriminated union with per-kind resolvers and
   per-kind expected-result semantics. Reason: the sole evaluator read
   data.executionReadiness, which exists on MAGIC-ITEM RECORDS ONLY, so every
   row across all ten families was proved by an evaluator that could not see its
   subject matter.
2. Exact structured hook identity replaced substring matching. Reason:
   text.includes() assigns hooks to the wrong primitive on near-matches.
3. Empty results must be positively justified per evidence kind. Reason: absence
   of evidence was passing as evidence of absence.
4. Rows bind to named query identities; positional or family association is
   rejected. Reason: results could not be traced back to their row.
5. eshyra-2n1t reclassified as premature/overstated umbrella closure. Reason:
   the closing PR claimed executable mechanics for all 240 magic items and zero
   deep-audit findings; narrow child acceptance does not validate a global
   claim later proven false.

Prior review approval does NOT survive these changes. A fresh full review is
required.

### Invariant classes added 2026-07-26 (contract-grounded review at dee8d0a)

- **CANONICAL PRIMITIVE ROSTER.** A committed, versioned roster of
  (capabilityId, primitive); the validator asserts exact set equality. Missing
  and unexpected rows both fail, tested both directions. Adding a primitive now
  requires deliberately editing the roster.
- **AUDIT-FINDING EVIDENCE MUST BE RELEVANT, NOT MERELY RESOLVABLE.** A committed
  alias-to-subject table grounds each citation, and every audit-finding evidence
  item carries a per-row relevance statement that may not be constant or
  derivable from the primitive name. The prior head cited indep:001..012
  round-robin (histogram 3,3,3,3,3,3,3,2,2,2,2,2); citations that no finding
  supports are now dropped rather than invented.
- **KNOWN-MISSING CLAUSES PROVE REAL ABSENCE.** A known-missing row names a REAL
  source anchor and proves both that the source material exists there and that
  no pack record or clause projects it. Synthetic `SRD5.1:<primitive>` markers
  are gone. Rows without a real anchor carry evidence-underived status that
  fails the closure predicate.
- **OWNERSHIP IS EVIDENCE-BACKED.** Every owned row's owningBead must appear as a

## REVIEW CONTRACT

Protocol: eshyra-clause-review-v1

Migration baseline recorded 2026-07-26 during the final pre-protocol review
cycle. Derived from the corrected design at commit dee8d0a.

### Source obligation
- Source membership: 31 primitive rows spanning engine:F1..F10, each naming one
  implementation primitive rather than a family label.
- Membership derivation: the five bootstrap sources, each with its OWN
  executable resolver — readiness artifacts, @eshyra/core code, open and closed
  beads, accepted 2026-07-24 findings, and source clauses known missing from
  projection. A ledger derived from the pack alone inherits the pack's blind
  spots.
- Source spans or authoritative inputs: evidence is a discriminated union keyed
  by kind — 'readiness-artifact', 'code', 'bead', 'audit-finding',
  'known-missing-source-clause'. sourceSpan is NOT overloaded to carry
  incompatible evidence types.
- Complete obligations covered: bootstrap scope only. This ledger is explicitly
  NON-AUTHORITATIVE; eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12 regenerates the authoritative ledger
  from the clause-complete corpus and diffs against this one.

### Pack or artifact representation
- Required semantic distinctions: primitive identity, never family membership.
  Family grouping may organise rows but can never substitute for primitive
  identity or exact affected membership.
- Branches and alternatives: hook selection uses exact structured hook identity.
  Unconstrained substring matching is rejected, with negative tests for
  near-matches, prefixes, suffixes and unrelated strings sharing a token.
- Timing, lifecycle, and termination: carried by the individual primitives —
  planar-return and declared-window clocks, item-instance persistence,
  hit-point and death lifecycle.
- Provenance and ownership requirements: every row names an owning bead. An
  'owned' row may never name the engine epic root eshyra-olc5; a
  'proposed-new-bead' row may, and carries a proposed title and parent.

### Cross-kind and cross-surface checks
- Related kinds or subsystems: engine:F1..F10 plus the four cross-family
  primitive beads eshyra-o9bd.19.5.5.3, .19.5.6.3, .19.5.8.3 and .19.5.11.3.
- Corpus-wide predicates or reconciliation: 2n1t-engine-closure-reconciliation.md
  classifies eshyra-2n1t and all thirteen children plus eshyra-b69j.13,
  eshyra-o9bd.18.7 and .18.7.8. The epic itself is PREMATURE / OVERSTATED
  UMBRELLA CLOSURE; eight children are INCOMPLETE INTEGRATION. Corrective
  ownership routes .6, .7, .9 and .12 to the four new beads.

### Engine capability
- Required capabilities: all ten engine:F* families, at primitive granularity,
  several rows per family.
- Existing owner beads: the ten family epics under eshyra-olc5 own rows that fit
  a family; the four cross-family beads own the rest.
- Known missing capability handling: 'known-missing-source-clause' evidence must
  POSITIVELY PROVE absence from the pack. An empty query result is never
  accepted as proof.

### Reference execution or executable proof
- Real artifact or pack-driven scenarios: readiness-artifact evidence executes
  against the committed pack; code evidence proves the named symbol exists in
  @eshyra/core; bead evidence resolves through bd.
- Negative and fail-closed scenarios: unknown, duplicate, ambiguous, untraceable
  or missing query bindings are rejected; near-match hook identities are
  rejected; recursive stored-count/total fields are rejected at any depth;
  unexpectedly empty results fail per evidence kind.
- Replay, rollback, or determinism requirements: bd resolution SKIPS GRACEFULLY
  when the binary is absent, so the suite never depends on bd being installed.

### Approved residuals
- Source ambiguities: none owned here.
- Deliberately model-adjudicated boundaries: none owned here.
- Explicitly unsupported scope: implementing any engine capability. This bead
  inventories and reconciles; implementation belongs to the decomposition and
  certification tasks under eshyra-olc5.

### Closure evidence
- Generated membership query: per-row query identities resolved through the
  per-source evidence resolvers.
- Permanent regression evidence:
  packages/core/test/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.test.ts — exact structured hook
  identity, proof-of-absence, query-binding rejection, the pinned seven non-pack
  primitives, proposed-row representability, and rejection of the old overloaded
  pack evidence.
- Finding-registry aliases: sol:CAP-007, sol:CAP-014.

### Material contract changes in this cycle
1. Evidence became a per-source discriminated union with per-kind resolvers and
   per-kind expected-result semantics. Reason: the sole evaluator read
   data.executionReadiness, which exists on MAGIC-ITEM RECORDS ONLY, so every

2. Exact structured hook identity replaced substring matching. Reason:

3. Empty results must be positively justified per evidence kind. Reason: absence

4. Rows bind to named query identities; positional or family association is

5. eshyra-2n1t reclassified as premature/overstated umbrella closure. Reason:

*** GREEN DEFINITION REVISED (2026-07-25) — SUPERSEDES the 8-point version ***
DECISION: where structured pack data is a DIRECT INPUT to deterministic
execution, the pack contract and the reference engine are ONE co-designed
system. The pack defines what the engine must execute; the reference engine
proves the representation is sufficient and unambiguous. Freezing the pack
first would preserve a separation that does not exist in practice.

A deterministic clause that feeds engine execution is GREEN only when all nine
hold:
  1. Complete source-clause identification.
  2. Clause-complete structured representation.
  3. Complete field provenance.
  4. Explicit capability requirements.
  5. A provider-neutral engine implementation exists.
  6. Reference-engine conformance tests exercise the PACK representation.
  7. Correct tool exposure and state mutation.
  8. Fail-closed behavior for unsupported input.
  9. Successful replay / deterministic equivalence where applicable.

A clause is NOT green merely because the pack appears to contain enough data;
the reference implementation must demonstrate that it actually does. A
representation reference that merely RESOLVES to an existing object is not
green — the Opus amended magic-item pass proved reference integrity but
explicitly did NOT prove semantic appropriateness of free-form effects.

AT RE-FREEZE THERE MUST BE ZERO ENGINE-PENDING DETERMINISTIC CLAUSES. The only
permissible non-green clauses are four approved categories:
  * genuine source ambiguity routed to campaign rulings;
  * intentionally model-adjudicated material;
  * external content unavailable in the SRD;
  * explicitly deferred non-deterministic house-rule behavior.
Each must be explicitly represented in-band, carry its alternatives and
campaign-ruling requirement, and fail CLOSED.

WHY (audit evidence): the 2026-07-24 findings were structures that looked
plausible in isolation but failed as executable inputs — alternative damage
modes stored as parallel damage, recharge triggers read as reset periods,
partial saves treated as complete, legendary actions with no budget or cost,
option mechanics hoisted onto parent features, typed records missing
branching/timing/termination. A completed reference implementation forces these
to surface: a dragon-breath scenario cannot pass without half-damage handling;
a legendary-creature scenario cannot pass without a budget; a versatile attack
cannot execute without a discriminated alternative.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING: eshyra-olc5 is no longer a downstream project that
may stay open after eshyra-o9bd closes. Its reference-implementation
certification gates eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1 and therefore the formal re-freeze in
eshyra-o9bd.14.

title: Harden creature attack/action source parsing and alternate-mode representation
description:
Repair demonstrated creature attack/action parser failures: alternate/swarm modes,
parenthetical bonuses, Unicode minus, swallowed action boundaries, nonstandard ranges,
inconsistent damage shapes, and truncated target qualifiers. An exhaustive attack/action
inventory is a source-fidelity claim only when source stat-block structure independently
establishes the denominator.
design:
2026-10-09 DESIGN (Claude Captain, main 6f57be85). Lane A, profile rules-clause-complete. Creature attack mechanics (mechanics.attacks[].hitDamage, mechanics.damage) are source projections for discovery/adjudication; no deterministic capability consumes creature hitDamage today (verify with grep before relying on it), so this is source fidelity.
DEFECT CLASSES (all in parseAttack / parseDamage, packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/mechanicsProjections.ts ~L84-100, ~L372-406):
 C1 Unicode minus (opus:F-29): parseDamage's dice grammar accepts only ASCII [+-]; 'Hit: 1 (1d4 − 1) piercing damage' (U+2212) yields no damage at all, and the flat-damage fallback also fails, so hitDamage is EMPTY. Population by query: every record whose text contains /\d+d\d+\s*−\s*\d+/ (snapshot: 18 creatures incl. awakened-shrub, baboon, bat, frog, giant-fire-beetle, hawk, kobold, owl, quipper, rat, raven, scorpion, sea-horse, spider, swarm-of-quippers/rats/ravens, weasel; magic-items deck-of-illusions, ioun-stone, ring-of-spell-storing - check those items' own projections render the printed value, repair only if a value is lost or altered). Normalize U+2212 to '-' in the dice expression consistently (the printed dice string in `dice` should use ASCII ' - ' like ' + '), and also accept U+2212 in attack bonuses ('[+−-]\d+ to hit') and every other shared numeric grammar in this file that reads signed modifiers (search the file for '[+-]' character classes and fix siblings; list them).
 C2 Parenthetical alternate attack bonus (opus:F-28): 'Melee Weapon Attack: +2 to hit (+4 to hit with shillelagh), reach 5 ft.' breaks the attack lead-in regex, so creature:druid Quarterstaff and creature:dryad Club have NO attacks[] and only a flattened damage list. Accept an optional '(<+N> to hit <condition>)' after the bonus and carry it on the matching alternative (C3).
 C3 Mutually exclusive damage alternatives flattened into cumulative arrays: in the 'Hit:' clause, ', or N (XdY + Z) <type> damage <condition>' is an ALTERNATIVE to the preceding damage, but hitDamage (and top-level mechanics.damage) list both as if cumulative (e.g. creature:drider Longsword hitDamage [1d8+3, 1d10+3] slashing). Population by query (snapshot 27 clauses): 'if used with two hands to make a melee attack' 9, 'if used with two hands' 6, 'if the swarm has half of its hit points or fewer' 6, 'with shillelagh' 2, 'while enlarged' 2, 'at range' 1, 'in Small or Medium form' 1.
REPRESENTATION DECISION: attacks[i].hitDamage = the DEFAULT mode only (the first damage plus any trailing 'plus N (XdY) <type> damage' riders that apply to every mode, e.g. Azer's fire). attacks[i].alternatives = [{ condition: '<verbatim condition text>', hitDamage: [complete damage list for that mode, including shared riders], attackBonus?: N (only when the source prints a mode-specific bonus, e.g. shillelagh +4) }]. Top-level mechanics.damage on such an entry equals the default mode (so nothing reads cumulative). Condition text stays verbatim; no condition is interpreted. Entries without an alternative are byte-identical.
F-31 (ranged-notation): currently no ranged weapon/spell attack lacks rangeFeet; verify the alternate notations present in the corpus ('range 30/120 ft.', 'reach 5 ft. or range 20/60 ft.', 'range 120 ft.' single value for spell attacks) all project; repair only if any is lost, and record the result.
CAP-004 (creature-statblock-mechanics, 'Creature stat-block mechanics are complete'): narrowed under ADR 0020 (no completeness claim); surviving obligation = emitted creature attack/damage projections agree with the printed stat block (this repair + existing statline fidelity gate).
CROSS-KIND (absorbed from retired 19.1.2): the same printed grammar must not project differently by kind; search spell, magic-item, equipment, hazard text for U+2212 dice and '(<+N> to hit ...)' and ', or N (XdY) ... damage <condition>' forms; repair or disposition each sibling with a source-backed reason in the report.
REGISTRY: druid-dryad-attacks (F-28), unicode-minus-damage (F-29), ranged-notation (F-31) stay accepted with reasoning naming this repair (F-31: verified, no loss); creature-statblock-mechanics (CAP-004) -> narrowed. damage-alternatives (F-27) is owned by eshyra-o9bd.19.3.1; add a sentence to the 19.3.1 bead notes (not the registry) that creature attack alternatives were repaired here, so 19.3.1 handles only its remaining option-local scope.
EVIDENCE: one new test file: (a) generalized invariant over the real pack: for every creature entry with an 'X Weapon/Spell Attack: ... Hit:' lead-in, attacks[] exists, attackBonus equals the printed bonus, and every printed damage expression in the Hit clause appears exactly once across hitDamage + alternatives (independent predicate in the test); (b) no projected dice string contains U+2212 and no record with a printed U+2212 dice expression has empty hitDamage; (c) exact source-fidelity regressions: druid Quarterstaff (default 1d6, alternatives two-hands 1d8 and shillelagh +4 1d8+2), drider Longsword, azer Warhammer (fire rider in both modes), a swarm half-HP case, baboon Bite 1d4 - 1. Update existing expectations only where this design proves them wrong; state preserves/strengthens/replaces.
acceptance_criteria:
- Every attack/action in the independently enumerated source structural population is represented with correct boundary and source values.
- Unicode minus, alternate range notation, and parenthetical alternate bonuses cannot silently erase printed values.
- Mutually exclusive modes remain alternatives, not cumulative arrays.
- Target qualifiers and source relationships survive projection.
- Passing this parser census does not prove complete creature mechanics or universal deterministic support.
notes:
Bead-writing contract (plan §VI) — this bead must state: exact scope membership
(explicit records/clauses or a deterministic query that enumerates them), root
cause, required invariant, source evidence, pack evidence, engine boundary,
regression predicate + committed assertions, generated outputs, no-repeat alias

title: Repair known spell projection losses and selected spell capability inputs
description:
Repair demonstrated spell projection defects such as area/origin geometry,
projectile/count/target relationships, ordered pools/allocation, multi-stage/repeat
effects, termination, upcast bases, successful-save branches, and known source
anomalies. Do not compile every spell into a deterministic clause-complete procedure.
design:
2026-10-10 DESIGN (Claude Captain, main f3ca1b6e). Lane A, profile rules-clause-complete. Consumers: discovery/packet.ts projectionLimits emits 'The source describes an area, but no typed mechanics.area projection exists.' when area prose has no typed area (read-only consumer; notes disappear as areas are typed). The in-force spell upcast capability (spellUpcastContract.ts; upcast.ts count-per-slot) encodes only the per-slot INCREMENT for projectile counts, so the base count is a source projection, not a capability input.
A1 POINT-ORIGIN AND OTHER AREAS (opus:F-08 / fable:F2): only 16 spells type mechanics.area, all origin 'self'. Snapshot: 46 spells describe an area of effect in prose only (e.g. fireball '20-foot-radius sphere centered on a point you choose within range', cloudkill, circle-of-death, darkness, daylight, delayed-blast-fireball, earthquake ...). Population by query over spell descriptions: N-foot-radius sphere/cylinder (with height), N-foot cube, N-foot cone, line N feet long and N feet wide, N-foot radius / emanation. Extend the existing area shape: {shape: sphere|cylinder|cube|cone|line|radius|hemisphere, size (radius or edge or length), height? (cylinder), width? (line), unit:'foot', origin: 'self' | 'point-within-range' | 'creature' | 'object' (from the printed anchor: 'centered on a point you choose within range', 'centered on you', 'centered on a creature/object'), }. Project ONLY when the sentence defines the spell's area of effect; a dimension describing something else (an object's size, a warded area that is not an effect area?) is reported, not projected. Every projected value must occur in the sentence. Report the full population with projected/not-projected and reason; validate shapes/origins in kindSchemas (fail closed). Check every consumer of mechanics.area (grep) before changing.
A2 BASE PROJECTILE COUNT (opus:F-11): spell:magic-missile projects per-dart damage and the upcast increment but not 'You create three glowing darts of magical force'. Add mechanics.projectiles {count: N, noun: '<printed noun>'} (e.g. {count:3, noun:'dart'}) from the printed creation sentence. Sibling population by query: 'create(s) N <noun>' / 'hurl N <noun>' / 'N rays/beams' (scorching ray three rays; eldritch blast scales by character level - its count comes from the cantrip-scaling sentence; project only the printed base 'a beam' -> count 1 only if the existing scaling projection represents the level steps, otherwise leave and report). Report each.
REGISTRY: point-origin-areas (F-08/fable:F2) and magic-missile-projectiles (F-11) stay accepted with repair reasoning; spell-completeness (indep:005) and spell-mechanics-depth (sol:CAP-003) -> narrowed under ADR 0020 (surviving obligation: emitted spell projections agree with source; unprojected semantics stay verbatim and model-adjudicated, never implied complete).
EVIDENCE: one new test file: generalized invariant that every spell whose description prints an area-defining phrase (independent regex in the test, same population) has a typed area whose shape/size/origin match the phrase, OR is in an explicit reviewed not-an-effect-area list with a reason; exact fireball, cloudkill, magic-missile cases; projectile siblings exact.

title: Repair ancestry, background, equipment-grant, and proficiency projections
description:
Repair known source-fidelity defects in ancestry traits, background/equipment grants,
language/proficiency grants, material constraints, and represented variants. Use typed
data where source structure is stable or a real discovery/state/capability consumer needs
it; do not require every ancestry mechanic to become a deterministic procedure.
design:
2026-10-10 DESIGN (Claude Captain, main 4d344bd1). Lane A + a bounded creation consumer change. Profile: rules-clause-complete (pack) + semantic-system (creation validation, durable sheet languages).
L1 LANGUAGE EXTENSION POINT (indep:011, LIVE): ancestry/background language choices emit choose/from with from = the 8 Standard Languages (e.g. background:acolyte 'Two of your choice'), but rule:languages says: 'Choose your languages from the Standard Languages table, or choose one that is common in your campaign. With your GM's permission, you can instead choose a language from the Exotic Languages table or a secret language, such as thieves' cant or the tongue of druids.' Pack: every language choice whose source text is an open 'of your choice' grant gains extension: {ruleRef: 'rule:languages', exoticTableRef: <the Exotic Languages table record key, if one exists; else omit>, requiresGmApproval: true} beside the unchanged default from list (the default domain stays the Standard table; nothing is silently widened). Validate in kindSchemas. Creation (characterDraft language choice validation + finalize): a selected language outside `from` is accepted ONLY when the selection carries an explicit GM-approval marker for that language (design a minimal typed input, e.g. the choice selection value { language, gmApproved: true } or a parallel approvedLanguages list on the draft selections - pick the smallest change consistent with existing selection shapes and document it); without the marker it is refused exactly as today. Never infer approval. CLI: in the interactive language choice, offer the default options plus an explicit 'other language with GM approval' entry that asks for the language name and records the approval marker. Persisted sheet languages unchanged in shape. Tests: refused without approval; accepted with approval (exotic and campaign-common examples); default domain unchanged; pack invariant that every open 'of your choice' language grant carries the extension marker.
F-18 (background-equipment, 'Background equipment is structured'): verify against the committed pack and creation consumer (backgrounds carry structured equipment grants; walletForDraft credits background gp). If fully satisfied, record accepted reasoning with evidence (test names); if a gap exists, repair it here.
indep:004 (ancestry-omissions, 'Ancestry deterministic semantics are complete'): narrowed under ADR 0020 (surviving obligation: ancestry projections consumed by creation are source-faithful - fixed skills, languages, ASI, traits; prose stays verbatim).
indep:012 (equipment-report): read its row and any source of its meaning; disposition with evidence or report that it cannot be evaluated.
EXCLUSIONS: no new languages invented; no change to the Standard default domain; no thaw/freeze changes.

title: Repair feature resources, resets, scaling, and selected feature capabilities
description:
Repair known feature/feat defects: source-governed resets, phantom resources, missing
use/scaling progression, option-local behavior, and specific source mechanics surfaced
by audits. Structured data must be source-faithful wherever emitted; deterministic
execution is required only for positive selected operations and state-integrity primitives.
design:
2026-10-09 DESIGN (Claude Captain, survey at main a961fb0b). Lane A, profile rules-clause-complete. mechanics.resources on features/traits is NOT consumed by any engine capability (class pools come from class-table columns via packages/core/src/state/classResources.ts), so this is source-fidelity projection only; no engine change.
ROOT CAUSE (one defect class): deriveFeatureMechanics (packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/mechanicsProjections.ts ~L5235-5285) emits resources:[{reset}] whenever the text merely CONTAINS 'short rest'/'long rest' (reset chosen by substring), and reads 'use this feature once|twice|three times' anywhere (so Indomitable's scaling sentence 'twice between long rests starting at 13th level' becomes uses:2). Shared by class/subclass features (emit.ts ~L910), feats (~L1016), ancestry traits (~L1539), background features (~L1599).
DECISION: emit a resource ONLY from a governing source relation that limits or restores uses: (a) 'you must finish a <R> before you can <use it|rage|do so> again' / 'you can't use <it|this feature> again until you <finish|complete> a <R>' / 'You must then finish a <R> to use your Channel Divinity again' / 'you can use it again after you finish a <R>'; (b) 'you regain <any|all> <of your>? expended uses <...> when you finish a <R>' / 'When you finish a <R>, you regain <all>? <your>? expended uses' / 'regain the ability to do so when you finish a <R>'; (c) pools: 'replenishes when you take a <R>', ki 'unavailable until you finish a <R>, at the end of which you draw all of your expended ki back'; (d) slots: 'You regain all expended spell slots when you finish a <R>' -> add resource:'spell-slots'. R in {short rest, long rest, short or long rest}; reset from the matched R, never from substring presence elsewhere. A rest mentioned only as a trigger/occasion (during a short rest, at the end of a long rest, can be done during a short rest, when you finish a short rest choose X, a DC/penalty counter that resets) yields NO resource.
USES: 'Once you use this feature'/(a)-forms with no count -> uses:1; 'You can use this feature twice' -> 2; 'a number of times equal to your <Ability> modifier (a minimum of once)' -> uses:'<ability>-modifier', usesMinimum:1; 'equal to 1 + your <Ability> modifier' -> uses:'1-plus-<ability>-modifier'; scaling sentences 'twice between rests starting at Nth level, three times ... Mth' / 'Starting at 17th level, you can use it twice before a rest' / 'Beginning at 6th level ... twice between rests, and beginning at 18th level ... three times' -> usesByLevel:[{level,uses}] starting at the feature's own level with its base count. A table-column pool (rage, ki, sorcery points) carries no uses.

 keep/adjust: barbarian:rage {reset:long-rest}; bard:bardic-inspiration {uses:'charisma-modifier',usesMinimum:1,reset:long-rest}; bard:font-of-inspiration {reset:short-or-long-rest, appliesTo:'feature:bard:bardic-inspiration'}; bard|cleric|druid|paladin|ranger|sorcerer|wizard:spellcasting {resource:'spell-slots',reset:long-rest} UNIFORMLY (remove RESOURCE_PROJECTION_WITHHELD_PENDING_F05 + withheldResources in emit.ts ~L884-898); warlock:pact-magic {resource:'spell-slots',reset:short-or-long-rest}; circle-of-the-land:natural-recovery {uses:1,reset:long-rest} (F-05); cleric:channel-divinity {usesByLevel:[{2,1},{6,2},{18,3}],reset:short-or-long-rest}; paladin:sacred-oath {uses:1,reset:short-or-long-rest}; druid:wild-shape {uses:2,reset:short-or-long-rest}; fighter:action-surge {usesByLevel:[{2,1},{17,2}],reset:short-or-long-rest}; fighter:indomitable {usesByLevel:[{9,1},{13,2},{17,3}],reset:long-rest} (F-03); fighter:second-wind, rogue:stroke-of-luck, the-fiend:dark-ones-own-luck {uses:1,reset:short-or-long-rest}; oath-of-devotion:holy-nimbus, the-fiend:hurl-through-hell, warlock:eldritch-master, way-of-the-open-hand:wholeness-of-body {uses:1,reset:long-rest}; monk:ki {reset:short-or-long-rest}; paladin:cleansing-touch {uses:'charisma-modifier',usesMinimum:1,reset:long-rest}; paladin:divine-sense {uses:'1-plus-charisma-modifier',reset:long-rest} (F-24); paladin:lay-on-hands {reset:long-rest}; warlock:mystic-arcanum {uses:1,reset:long-rest} (per arcanum spell, prose keeps that); wizard:signature-spells {uses:1,reset:short-or-long-rest}; wizard:arcane-recovery {uses:1,reset:'day'} (F-04: 'Once per day when you finish a short rest' - the use window is per day; add 'day' to the validated reset vocabulary with a doc comment; the short-rest occasion stays prose); ancestry traits dragonborn Breath Weapon, half-orc Relentless Endurance {uses:1,reset as now}; tiefling Infernal Legacy {reset:long-rest} unchanged.
 REMOVE (phantom, F-06): barbarian:relentless-rage (DC counter), bard:song-of-rest (occasion), school-of-evocation:overchannel (escalating-damage counter, uses unlimited), sorcerer:sorcerous-restoration (partial regain of 4 points; a full-reset entry would be false; font-of-magic's procedure pool already carries long-rest reset), the-fiend:fiendish-resilience (occasion), warlock:pact-boon (ritual occasion), way-of-the-open-hand:tranquility (occasion), cleric:divine-intervention (reset is conditional: 7 days if the deity intervened, else long rest; a flat long-rest entry is false; leave to prose).

Ki feature costs (Flurry/Patient Defense/Step of the Wind) stay verbatim prose: no capability consumes them; ki pool accounting is classResources' table pool with DM-declared spend. Registry: ki-abilities -> 'narrowed' with that reasoning.
indep:003 (class-feature-completeness, 'Class features and feats retain complete procedures'): -> 'narrowed': ADR 0020 withdraws completeness; surviving obligation = emitted structured feature data is source-faithful (this repair) and feature prose remains verbatim discoverable.

Do not add one test per feature beyond that table.

title: Preserve option-local choices, alternatives, variants, and prerequisites
description:
Repair known cases where source-defined choices/variants are absent, hoisted to a parent,
or flattened into cumulative behavior. Stable option identity/prerequisites are required
where runtime consumers reference them. A structural option family may be exhaustively
checked only when membership is independently source-enumerated.
design:
2026-10-10 DESIGN (Claude Captain, main 16eea662). Lane A, profile rules-clause-complete. Split: implementation child = O1-O4 (parser repairs + cross-kind siblings); Captain = registry dispositions O5-O8 in the same PR.
O1 ALTERNATIVE-ABILITY SAVE (opus:F-33 bulette-alternative): creature:bulette Deadly Leap prints 'must succeed on a DC 16 Strength or Dexterity saving throw (target's choice)' but projects saves [{ability:'dexterity', damageOnSuccess:'half'}] - the Strength alternative and the DC are lost. Representation: a save may carry abilityOptions: ['strength','dexterity'] (exactly the printed abilities, in printed order) plus chosenBy: 'target' (from '(target's choice)'; omit chosenBy if not printed) INSTEAD of ability, with its dc and success branch. Validate in kindSchemas: exactly one of ability | abilityOptions (>=2 distinct abilities). BEFORE emitting, grep packages/core/src for every consumer of mechanics saves[].ability; if any consumer requires ability, stop and report. Population by query across ALL kinds: '<Ability> or <Ability> saving throw' (with or without a DC); repair every sibling or disposition it with a source reason.
O2 PIT VARIANTS (opus:F-02): hazard:pits flattens four printed traps (Simple Pit, Hidden Pit, Locked Pit, Spiked Pit) into one record whose mechanics carry only the Spiked Pit poison variant's save (DC 13 Con half, 4d10 poison) plus the spikes' 2d10 piercing - read as if every pit poisoned. Representation: data.variants = [{name, text (verbatim span of that trap's paragraph), mechanics?}] one per printed trap, each with only its own projections (detection/investigation DCs as the existing check grammar yields them, Locked Pit's Strength check DC, Spiked Pit's 2d10 piercing and its poison clause DC 13 Constitution half 4d10 poison); top-level mechanics keep only what applies to every pit (falling damage by depth is prose: leave it unprojected unless the existing grammar already projects it) - in practice top-level mechanics should become absent or contain nothing variant-specific. The record's description stays verbatim. Validate variants in the hazard kind schema (reuse the creature variant shape {name, text, mechanics?}). Check consumers of hazard mechanics (grep) first; stop and report if a deterministic consumer exists. Sibling search: other hazard/trap records that print several named sub-traps in one record; repair or disposition.
O3 CROSS-KIND DAMAGE ALTERNATIVES (opus:F-27): creature attack alternatives are repaired in PR #646 (attacks[].alternatives). Search spell, magic-item, equipment, hazard, feature text for the same printed grammar (', or N (XdY) <type> damage <condition>' or 'deals XdY ... or XdY ... if/when ...' alternatives) whose projection lists both as cumulative damage; repair with the same alternative representation where a damage list exists, or disposition each with a source reason. Equipment 'versatile (1d10)' is already typed as a property - verify, do not re-model.
O4 CROSS-KIND TARGETING QUALIFIERS (opus:F-35): creature attack targets are repaired in PR #646. Search other kinds' projected target fields (spells' target text if projected, magic-item effect targets) for truncation of a printed qualifier; repair or disposition.
EVIDENCE: one new test file: exact bulette save; a generalized invariant over all records that every '<A> or <B> saving throw' clause projects abilityOptions [A,B] (independent regex); exact pits variants (four names, Spiked Pit alone carries the poison save); cross-kind dispositions listed in bead notes (not tests) unless a repair was made.
Registry (implementation child): bulette-alternative (F-33) and pit-variants (F-02) stay accepted with repair reasoning; damage-alternatives (F-27) and targeting-qualifiers (F-35) get reasoning citing PR #646 for creatures plus this PR's cross-kind result. Captain handles invocation-effects (F-07), choice-behavior (indep:002), language-universe-policy (indep:011), option-losses (CAP-005).
acceptance_criteria:
- A selected represented option grants only its own source-backed behavior; sibling alternatives are not cumulative.
- Stable identity/prerequisites exist for represented options consumed by discovery, state, or capabilities.
- Open-ended source choices remain open rather than falsely closed.
- Exhaustive predicates name an independently source-derived option family.
- Capability execution, tool exposure, and state effects are out of scope here; they belong to the capability lane (eshyra-o9bd.19.5 family epics, eshyra-olc5.1/.2).

title: Replace audit gates with clause-level completeness and a permanent finding registry
description:
Rebuild the source-coverage, playability, choice, creature, spell, and readiness
audits on the A1 clause IR, and make audit findings durable project data.

Root cause: audits sample record families and count mechanics-atom presence, so
they report clean while whole procedures remain prose. Findings also live only in
review transcripts, so a fix is silently lost when importers regenerate or
schemas change.

The checked-in finding registry must record, per finding: canonical finding ID;
all source-review aliases (e.g. Opus F-25, Sol CAP-004, Fable F3); affected
records or an exact membership query; violated invariant; owning bead;
regression test or generated predicate; closure evidence.

Closes findings: SOL-001, SOL-009, SOL-012, F-21, CAP-014, and the registry
obligation behind every other finding.
design:
The registry is the anti-regression mechanism for the whole program: the next
audit bundle ships it and proves every finding closed. V2 populates it; A5 builds
it and wires the CI enforcement.
acceptance_criteria:
- Metadata cannot report zero playability findings while pending or partial clauses remain.
- Coverage reports separate classified, resolved, ambiguous, unresolved, and excluded — ambiguous/unresolved never counts as covered.
- Every historical finding from the 2026-07-24 reviews has a checked-in invariant and an owning bead in the registry.
- The bundle emits a coverage-depth matrix proving semantic — not sampled — review for every mechanics-bearing family.
- CI fails on any unmapped finding, any pending capability without a real bead, and any registry row whose bead reference does not resolve.
notes:
Bead-writing contract (plan §VI) — this bead must state: exact scope membership
(explicit records/clauses or a deterministic query that enumerates them), root
cause, required invariant, source evidence, pack evidence, engine boundary,
regression predicate + committed assertions, generated outputs, no-repeat alias
list, and completion proof. "Fix the examples above" is not acceptable scope;
close the whole semantic class and reconcile exact membership.
SCOPE CHANGE: this bead no longer CREATES the finding registry — eshyra-o9bd.19.1.6 creates
registry v1 early, before C/D implementation. 19.1.5 rebuilds the audit gates on
the clause IR and wires CI enforcement over that registry; 19.6.2 adds closure
evidence.

DECOMPOSITION WATCH: spans multiple audit systems plus registry enforcement.
Convert to an epic with per-audit-system children if scoping confirms that
breadth.

GREEN DEFINITION — shared verbatim by 19.1.4, 19.1.5, 19.4.5 and 19.5.12. A
clause is green ONLY when all eight hold:
  1. The complete source clause has been identified.
  2. Every deterministic branch is projected.
  3. All source and derived fields are provenanced.
  4. Every required capability is identified.
  5. The engine implementation exists.
  6. An executable conformance scenario proves the intended outcome.
  7. Runtime lookup can find the canonical clause.
  8. Unsupported portions fail closed.
A representation reference that merely RESOLVES to an existing object is not
green. The Opus amended magic-item pass proved reference integrity but explicitly
did NOT prove the semantic appropriateness of every free-form effect.
*** GREEN DEFINITION REVISED (2026-07-25) — SUPERSEDES the 8-point version ***
DECISION: where structured pack data is a DIRECT INPUT to deterministic
execution, the pack contract and the reference engine are ONE co-designed
system. The pack defines what the engine must execute; the reference engine
proves the representation is sufficient and unambiguous. Freezing the pack
first would preserve a separation that does not exist in practice.

A deterministic clause that feeds engine execution is GREEN only when all nine
hold:
  1. Complete source-clause identification.
  2. Clause-complete structured representation.
  3. Complete field provenance.
  4. Explicit capability requirements.
  5. A provider-neutral engine implementation exists.
  6. Reference-engine conformance tests exercise the PACK representation.
  7. Correct tool exposure and state mutation.
  8. Fail-closed behavior for unsupported input.
  9. Successful replay / deterministic equivalence where applicable.

A clause is NOT green merely because the pack appears to contain enough data;
the reference implementation must demonstrate that it actually does. A
representation reference that merely RESOLVES to an existing object is not
green — the Opus amended magic-item pass proved reference integrity but
explicitly did NOT prove semantic appropriateness of free-form effects.

AT RE-FREEZE THERE MUST BE ZERO ENGINE-PENDING DETERMINISTIC CLAUSES. The only
permissible non-green clauses are four approved categories:
  * genuine source ambiguity routed to campaign rulings;
  * intentionally model-adjudicated material;
  * external content unavailable in the SRD;
  * explicitly deferred non-deterministic house-rule behavior.
Each must be explicitly represented in-band, carry its alternatives and
campaign-ruling requirement, and fail CLOSED.

WHY (audit evidence): the 2026-07-24 findings were structures that looked
plausible in isolation but failed as executable inputs — alternative damage
modes stored as parallel damage, recharge triggers read as reset periods,
partial saves treated as complete, legendary actions with no budget or cost,
option mechanics hoisted onto parent features, typed records missing
branching/timing/termination. A completed reference implementation forces these
to surface: a dragon-breath scenario cannot pass without half-damage handling;
a legendary-creature scenario cannot pass without a budget; a versatile attack
cannot execute without a discriminated alternative.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING: eshyra-olc5 is no longer a downstream project that
may stay open after eshyra-o9bd closes. Its reference-implementation
certification gates eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1 and therefore the formal re-freeze in
eshyra-o9bd.14.
