title: Dispatch: item economy reset/timer executor (attempt 1)
description:
Implement the deterministic item economy reset/timer executor specified by parent bead eshyra-c7sx (read `bd show eshyra-c7sx` first for scope, rationale, and acceptance criteria). This plan pins the design decisions; follow it unless the code contradicts it, in which case record the contradiction in your completion notes.

## Code survey (verified 2026-07-20, commit 958d6d0)

- `packages/core/src/state/rest.ts:159` `advanceWorldTime` is the ONLY clock-advance path; it already runs `expireElapsedWorldEffects` and `resolveStableRecoveries` inside its transaction and returns their evidence on `WorldClock`. Rest completion (`complete()`, rest.ts:485) calls it inside the same txn, then applies per-event restores (`restoreSpellSlots`, `resetUsage` with event `short_rest`/`long_rest`) per participant.
- `AdvanceWorldTimeInput` (rest.ts:32) has NO rng today. Tools have `ctx.rng` (see `spendRestHitDieTool`).
- `packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts`: `ItemEconomyState` = `{remaining, availableAt?, lastReset?}` (strings for the latter two; validated at itemState.ts:220-246 but NEVER written anywhere today). `useItem` (itemState.ts:1463) spends economies, resolves depletion (`resolveItemDepletion`), schedules `pendingTimers` via `resolveItemStateTimers`, and writes state through `validateItemStateForRecord` + `writeItemState`. `readItemState`/`writeItemState` are the authoritative row access.
- `packages/core/src/state/itemTimers.ts`: `resolveItemStateTimers` anchors at the CURRENT clock; timer deadlines are absolute `deadlineElapsedMinutes`. Round-unit timers are rejected (encounter-round scheduler is out of scope here too).
- `packages/core/src/state/itemDepletion.ts`: depletion rolls (destroyedOn/regainOn/loseProperty/becomes) happen at spend time. `lifecycle.pendingTerminal === 'destroyed'` is written by useItem (deferred destruction while a machine lifecycle is still active, e.g. bead-of-force sphere) and today NOTHING ever completes it.
- Committed pack (rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1): 240 magic items, 81 with economy resets, exactly 11 distinct reset shapes (enumerate them yourself from records.json to build the test matrix; the list below is verified):
  1. charges/dawn/dice-expr (39; e.g. cube-of-force, gem-of-seeing)
  2. charges/dawn/all (eyes-of-charming)
  3. charges/dusk/dice-expr (robe-of-stars)
  4. charges/days:7/all (figurine-of-wondrous-power; onDepleted becomes inert)
  5. per-day/dawn/all (31)
  6. per-day/long-rest/all (ring-of-x-ray-vision)
  7. cooldown/hour/all (frost-brand etc.; cooldown.duration 1 hour)
  8. cooldown/days:7/all (horn-of-valhalla, rod-of-security; cooldown.duration 7 day)
  9. budget/days/all (manuals/tomes, days:36500 = SRD century; onDepleted loseProperty+inert)
  10. budget/long-rest/all (boots-of-speed)
  11. budget/per-period/DurationSpec amount, period 12h, onlyIfUnused (winged-boots)
- Timer transitions (12, all via-less, minute/hour units, two dice-amount: potion-of-diminution/growth 1d4 hour). One pack defect: cube-of-force declares `stateMachine.duration` {1,minute} with NO timer transition and prose-only termination — its expiry is unexecutable as declared. Do NOT work around it; fail closed (schedule/execute nothing for duration-without-timer-transition) and file an importer finding with `bd create` (label: importer) describing it.

## Design decisions (binding)

1. **Module**: new `packages/core/src/state/itemResetExecutor.ts` exporting (internal surface only — export via `internal.ts`, NOT the root index):
   - `resolveDueItemClockEvents(txn, {campaignId, previousElapsedMinutes, elapsedMinutes, rng?, provenance, sessionId, at})` — clock-derived resets + pendingTimers, called from `advanceWorldTime` after `resolveStableRecoveries`, campaign-wide (all item_state rows, including items not currently held by a character).
   - `resolveRestEventItemResets(txn, {campaignId, event: 'short-rest'|'long-rest', participants, rng?, ...ctx})` — called from `complete()` in the per-participant phase, scoped to inventory held by rest participants.
   Both return evidence arrays; surface them on `WorldClock` (new field `itemResets`, `itemTimerResolutions`) and in rest `benefits` (persisted in benefits_json).
2. **Dawn/dusk are clock-derived, not a DM tool call.** Convention (document it): `elapsed_minutes ≡ 0` is midnight; minute-of-day = `elapsed_minutes mod 1440`; dawn = minute 360 (06:00), dusk = minute 1080 (18:00). A boundary fires for each crossing in the half-open interval `(previousElapsedMinutes, elapsedMinutes]`; advancing 3 days fires 3 dawns (dice regains roll per crossing, clamped at max — 'all' resets are naturally idempotent). Rationale to record in the doc: deterministic and testable, no new tool surface, the DM already owns elapsed minutes via advance_time, and free-text narration labels are already tracked via narrativeLabelStale. Write the semantics doc at `docs/item-reset-executor.md` (anchoring, per-period anchor, onlyIfUnused definition, fail-closed rules, idempotence keys) and link it from the restore_usage tool description's "semantic reset owner" phrase if a short pointer fits.
3. **RNG threading**: add optional `rng?: Rng` to `AdvanceWorldTimeInput` and `CompleteRestInput`; pass `ctx.rng` from `advanceTimeTool` and the rest tools. Fail closed: if a due reset/timer needs dice and rng is undefined, throw (aborting the txn) with a message naming the pack ref and shape.
4. **Idempotence**: per-economy `lastReset` = decimal string of the elapsed minute of the last applied boundary. A boundary applies iff `boundary > Number(lastReset ?? -1)` AND `boundary` lies in `(prev, next]`. The half-open interval already prevents re-firing across calls; lastReset is the recorded evidence + guard for any secondary path.
5. **hour/days anchors** (`availableAt`): these resets are anchored at a use event, not the calendar. Extend `useItem` cost application: when a spend brings an economy's `remaining` to 0 and the economy declares an `hour`/`days` reset (equivalently kind cooldown with cooldown.duration — verify the declared reset entry and cooldown.duration agree; mismatch = importer finding), set `availableAt` = String(spendElapsed + durationMinutes) where duration = cooldown.duration if present else days*1440 / 60 for hour. Executor: when `elapsedMinutes >= Number(availableAt)`, restore per the reset amount ('all' → max), clear `availableAt`, set `lastReset`. Pre-existing state rows without `availableAt` simply never come due — document this as the migration posture (no DB migration needed; state lives in item_state JSON).
6. **per-period + onlyIfUnused** (winged-boots): ANY spend of the economy overwrites `availableAt` = String(spendElapsed + periodMinutes) (this IS the onlyIfUnused definition: the period restarts on use — document it). Executor: while `Number(availableAt) <= elapsedMinutes` and `remaining < max`: `remaining = min(max, remaining + amountInBudgetUnits)`, `availableAt += periodMinutes`, set lastReset. Convert the DurationSpec amount into the SAME units `remaining` uses for budget economies — read `initialRemaining`/`durationRoundTicks` (itemState.ts:646-778) and reuse/extract that conversion; do not invent a second one.
7. **Regain clamp / 'all' target**: max must come from the same source `createInitialItemState` used — declared numeric max, or the seeded `randomInitialization` result for dice-derived maxima. Extract or reuse a `resolveEconomyMax(state, economy)` helper from the existing init logic. If the max is unrecoverable, fail closed (throw naming the instance + economy).
8. **Lifecycle gating**: `nonmagical` and `consumed` (and pendingTerminal) items never regain. `inert` regains ONLY when the resetting economy has a recorded depletion whose `becomes === 'inert'` (see `state.depletions`); applying that reset restores the economy AND removes the inert lifecycle (figurine after 7 days, manuals after a century). All state writes go through `validateItemStateForRecord` + `writeItemState`.
9. **pendingTimers execution**: resolve timers with `deadlineElapsedMinutes <= elapsedMinutes`, oldest first, per item: set `machineState = to`, drop the fired timer, then schedule the entered state's own timer transitions ANCHORED AT THE FIRED DEADLINE (not at `now`) so chains (eversmoking-bottle cloud-60 → cloud-growing → …) stay accurate across a large advance; cascade until no timer is due. `resolveItemStateTimers` anchors at the current clock — add an explicit anchor parameter rather than duplicating it. Surface fired transitions' `effects` in the evidence. If a fired transition lands on `destroyed` (bead-of-force sphere→destroyed) or the machine resolves while `lifecycle.pendingTerminal === 'destroyed'`, complete destruction via the same path useItem uses (`destroyInventoryItem`), surfacing attunementsEnded.
10. **Fail closed on unknown shapes**: any reset entry not matching the 11 shapes above (or a schema-legal combination this executor does not implement, e.g. numeric amount with at:'dawn') throws with pack ref + JSON of the entry. Never skip silently, never approximate.
11. **No new tables/migrations**: all state stays in item_state JSON; evidence rides tool results and rest benefits_json.

## Acceptance criteria (from the parent bead; all must have tests)

Every one of the 11 pack reset shapes exercised end-to-end (dawn dice regain with clamp; dawn all; dusk; per-day all at dawn; per-day long-rest; budget long-rest; budget per-period with onlyIfUnused including "use resets the period"; days cooldown incl. figurine inert-clear and manual century; hour cooldown); timers fire deterministically on advance_time AND on rest completion with recorded evidence (including a cascade case and a destruction case with attunement evidence); double-application impossible (advance twice / advance-then-rest across the same boundary; crossing 3 dawns rolls 3 times); fail closed on missing rng and on unknown shapes; inert/nonmagical/consumed non-regain cases; cube-of-force duration finding filed as a bead, not executed. Follow existing test conventions (see packages/core/test/itemState.test.ts, rest.test.ts / restRecovery tests) in a new `packages/core/test/itemResetExecutor.test.ts` plus targeted additions where wiring lives.

## Environment / workflow caveats

- Work ONLY in this worktree; run `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` first; `npm ci` before building.
- `npm run verify:worktree` must be fully green before commit (Biome warnings fail CI).
- This touches magic-item mechanics consumers but NOT the importer/pack data: do not edit anything under packages/core/data/rules-packs or packages/core/scripts/importers. Pack defects are beads, not edits.
- New exports go through `packages/core/src/internal.ts` only.
- Commit on this branch; do not push; do not open a PR (integration is handled after review).

title: Dispatch: PR #458 review fixes — zero-quantity resolution, scoped accepts, stale exceptions, repurchase regression (attempt 1)
description:
Fixes for the four PR #458 review findings (review ID 4731750399, branch eshyra-f0nz). Parent spec: eshyra-f0nz. Defect context beads: eshyra-eks3 (items 1), eshyra-2n3n (items 2-3), eshyra-4ygd (item 4).

Branch/worktree: this bead's id, cut from eshyra-f0nz.

## Item 1 (P1) — zero-quantity reviews are still permanently quarantined

`giveItem` permits quantity 0 (domainMutations.ts ~233: non-negative integer), and migration 0022 reclassifies oversized-stack reviews with quantity <= 100 INCLUDING 0 to malformed-evidence — but `adoptMagicItem` (itemAdoption.ts ~281) rejects `quantity < 1` BEFORE reading the review, so a zero-quantity quarantined row can never be resolved.

Supervisor decision — implement exactly this:
- In `adoptMagicItem`, permit quantity 0 ONLY when BOTH an existing review row AND an input.resolution are present (i.e. a GM is resolving a quarantine); all other calls keep the current positive-integer rejection.
- When such a resolution succeeds on a quantity-0 row: record the resolution (existing recordItemAdoptionResolution path), clear the review, then DELETE the empty inventory row instead of binding it (nothing physical remains; resolution evidence intentionally survives row deletion per the 0018 table comments). Return the existing result shape with `adopted: true`, `instanceIds: []`, and the original id as `originalInstanceId`.
- Tests (packages/core/test/itemAdoption.test.ts): a reclassified malformed-evidence review on a quantity-0 row resolves via discard-evidence; afterwards the inventory row is gone, the review is gone, and the inventory_adoption_resolution row records the action. Also assert a quantity-0 adoption WITHOUT a review/resolution still rejects.

## Item 2 (P2) — record-wide accepts suppress a whole direction

In packages/core/test/srdGeneratedPack.test.ts, FORWARD/REVERSE_NUMERIC_CONSERVATION_ACCEPTS suppress EVERY dice and DC finding for the listed record in that direction (e.g. apparatus-of-the-crab's DC 20 accept would also hide loss of its typed 2d6). Convert both record-wide accept maps into value-scoped exceptions:
- Extend the existing token-scoped mechanism to DCs (e.g. keys like `<record-key>|forward|dc:20` alongside dice `<record-key>|forward|4d4`), reusing each record's existing rationale on each scoped entry.
- To enumerate exactly which values each record currently needs suppressed, temporarily empty the accept maps and read the gate's findings; convert precisely those findings to scoped exceptions. Remove the record-wide maps entirely (including their bottom-of-test key assertions) in favor of the scoped exhaustive assertion.

## Item 3 (P2) — stale exceptions must fail

`usedExceptions.add(exceptionKey)` currently fires whenever the token exists at all, even when the exact match also exists and the exception suppresses nothing. Mark an exception "used" ONLY when it actually suppressed a would-be finding (the token/DC was missing from the other side). Add a targeted unit: a synthetic record whose prose token IS exactly present in mechanics plus a pointless exception for it → the exhaustive used-exceptions assertion fails (assert via the helper's returned usedExceptions rather than a failing test, e.g. expect the helper NOT to mark it used).

## Item 4 (P2) — restore the stateful repurchase success regression

packages/core/test/domainMutations.test.ts "reacquires the exact sold row without resetting state or attunement" (~line 1173) now only asserts the sold+returned rejection; the successful PAID repurchase of that stateful row is never exercised. Extend the same test (or add a sibling) so that after the rejection it performs `reacquireItem` with basis 'repurchased' and an exact payment (seed the wallet first; see currencyTools.test.ts for the payment shape), then asserts: custody restored on the ORIGINAL row id, item_state json unchanged, attunement row still present, wallet debited, and the custody event records the payment_event_id.

## Verification

`npm ci` first, then `npm run verify:worktree`. Item 2/3 touch an SRD gate test: follow docs/importer-fix-protocol.md — no expectation weakening; every scoped exception keeps a source-backed rationale. Commit on this branch only.

title: Dispatch: PR #459 review fixes — migration guard + canonical conditions validation (attempt 1)
description:
Fixes for the two PR #459 review findings (review of branch eshyra-geny). Parent spec: eshyra-geny. Defect context beads: eshyra-q93i (migration), eshyra-gacz (doff gate).

Branch/worktree: this bead's id, cut from eshyra-geny.

## Finding 1 (High) — migration 0022 must not rewrite partial schedules

`packages/core/data/migrations/0022_stable_recovery_adoption.sql` currently matches stable-at-zero rows where ANY of the three schedule fields is NULL and overwrites all three. The only legitimate legacy state is ALL THREE NULL (canonical stabilization writes all three atomically); a mixed row is corruption whose surviving evidence must not be destroyed — the runtime resolver (hpLifecycle.ts resolveStableRecoveries) now deliberately throws on partial schedules, and the migration currently "repairs" them before that check can ever see them.

Required changes (edit 0022 in place — it is new on this unmerged branch, not an applied/immutable migration; CI/main have never seen it):
1. Adopt (roll=4/anchor/deadline write) ONLY rows where all three fields are NULL.
2. Abort the whole migration when any stable-at-zero row has a MIXED NULL/non-NULL schedule. Use the same guard style as the existing clock guard in that file: e.g. create a temp guard table with a CHECK (violation_count = 0) and INSERT the count of mixed rows, so a violation makes the migration script fail and the runner rolls back.
3. Migration test (packages/core/test/migrationLegacyAdoption.test.ts pattern): seed a stable-at-zero row with roll=1, anchor=500, deadline=NULL → running migrations THROWS, the schema_migrations ledger does NOT contain version 22, and the row's surviving fields are unchanged (rollback proof). ## Finding 2 (Medium) — doff gate must use the canonical conditions validator

`packages/core/src/state/attunement.ts` (inside assertInventoryCurseCustodyReady) hand-rolls a weaker conditions_json shape check: it accepts entries whose id is any string (including empty) and ignores extension values. `[{"id":""}]` is malformed per the canonical schema but passes, and with no matching curse id the worn cursed item is released — contradicting the fail-closed contract.

## Verification

title: Integrate PR #455 review follow-ups (custody economics, adoption-review repair, dice gate)
description:
Integration parent for the three PR #455 post-merge review follow-ups:

- eshyra-4ygd (P1): sold-item 'returned' basis bypasses sale-proceeds reversal (economic dupe loop)

1. reacquire_item rejects sold+returned; lost+returned and sold+repurchased(+payment) still work; tests updated without weakening economic guarantees; tool schema/description and list_recoverable_items basis filtering consistent.
2. New migration reclassifies impossible oversized-stack reviews; genuine oversized rows (>100) unaffected; regression test proves the previously-permanent quarantine becomes resolvable.
3. Conservation gate requires exact dice tokens; scoped exceptions carry rationale; no weakened expectations; gate still fails on a synthetic dropped/invented modifier.

title: Dispatch: legacy stable-recovery adoption migration (attempt 1)
description:
Works defect bead eshyra-q93i (read it first: full analysis with file/line refs). Parent spec: eshyra-geny (acceptance criterion 2). NOTE: branched after the eshyra-r2ps/cc3c dispatch merged — `advanceWorldTime` now resolves recoveries inside its clock transaction; keep that invariant.

Branch/worktree: this bead's id, cut from eshyra-geny.

## Code survey (verified 2026-07-19)

- `packages/core/data/migrations/0020_stable_recovery_deadline.sql`: adds the three nullable schedule columns, no backfill. Migrations are checksummed/immutable — never edit an existing migration; add a new one (next free number after the current highest; 0021 was the highest on main when this was written — re-check in your worktree).
- `packages/core/src/state/hpLifecycle.ts:597-626` `resolveStableRecoveries`: WHERE clause silently skips stable-at-zero rows with any NULL schedule field.
- `packages/core/src/state/hpLifecycle.ts:138` `scheduleStableRecovery`: roll = 1d4, anchor = clock.elapsed_minutes, deadline = anchor + roll*60. Column CHECKs: roll BETWEEN 1 AND 4, anchor/deadline >= 0.
- `stabilizeCharacter` (line 555) rejects non-dying characters, so legacy rows have no repair path today.
- Migration runner: `packages/core/src/persistence/migrationRunner.ts`; existing migration tests give the pattern for testing a new migration against a pre-seeded legacy DB.

## Supervisor decision (implement this option)

Deterministic SQL backfill in a NEW migration, plus fail-closed resolver:

1. New migration `00NN_stable_recovery_adoption.sql` (next free number): for every character row with `life_state='stable' AND hp_current=0` and any of the three schedule columns NULL, set ALL THREE: `stable_recovery_roll = 4`, `stable_recovery_anchor_elapsed_minutes = (SELECT elapsed_minutes FROM clock WHERE id=1)`, `stable_recovery_deadline_elapsed_minutes = anchor + 240`. Rationale (document in the migration header comment): the original 1d4 roll is unrecoverable; 4 hours is the SRD maximum, deterministically chosen so migrated characters are never woken EARLIER than any outcome the real roll could have produced; anchor is adoption time because the original stabilization time was never persisted. Guard the clock subquery: if the clock row is missing/NULL, the migration must fail loudly rather than write NULL/garbage (COALESCE-to-0 silently is NOT acceptable; prefer a technique that makes the UPDATE violate a CHECK or an explicit failing statement).

title: advanceWorldTime clock commit and stable-recovery resolution are not atomic
description:
Post-merge review of PR #457 (verified against current main, 2026-07-19).

## Defect

Direct clock advancement and stable recovery are not atomic. `advanceWorldTime` (`packages/core/src/state/rest.ts:159-219`) commits the clock update, effect expiry, and short-rest-window closure inside one `withTransaction`, then calls `resolveStableRecoveries` only *after* that transaction has returned (line 217). Each recovery then runs through its own `adjustHp` transaction (`hpLifecycle.ts:624` maps over due rows calling `adjustHp(db, 1, ...)` per character).

Verified failure modes:

- An exception in `resolveStableRecoveries` (or in one `adjustHp`) leaves elapsed time advanced while recovery is unapplied, or several due characters only partially recovered (the `.map` applies recoveries one transaction at a time).
- In the orchestrator, tool errors are returned to the model without rolling back the attempt savepoint (`orchestrator.ts` per-turn/per-attempt SAVEPOINT design; a caught `MutateStateError` becomes an err tool result). So a failed `advance_time` tool call retains its already-committed clock mutation inside the surrounding turn savepoint — if the attempt is later accepted, the clock advance lands without its recoveries.
- Outside the orchestrator (tests, direct core consumers), the inner transaction has already really committed, so the inconsistency is durable.

Note: the rest `complete()` path (`rest.ts:588`) happens to be safe-ish because it passes its own `txn` in, so the post-transaction recovery calls still nest inside the outer rest transaction — the non-atomicity bites the direct `advanceWorldTime` path.

## Required fix (per review)

Resolve all due stable recoveries inside the same `withTransaction` callback as the clock transition and return them as part of that atomic result. (better-sqlite3 nests transactions as savepoints, so the inner `adjustHp` calls compose correctly once they run against the transaction connection.) Add a test that an injected failure during recovery rolls back the clock advance.

Related (same PR #457 review): Demon Armor permanent doff block, migration-0020 stranded stable characters, rest benefits evidence gap (fixing this one changes the shape `complete()` consumes, so coordinate with that bead).

Sibling beads from PR #457 post-merge review: eshyra-gacz (Demon Armor doff), eshyra-q93i (migration-0020 stranding), eshyra-cc3c (rest evidence gap — fix together with this one, shared advanceWorldTime result shape).
Fix merged to branch eshyra-geny; PR #459 open (https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/459). Close after PR merge.

title: Migration 0020 strands pre-existing stable-at-zero characters: recovery silently never fires
description:
Post-merge review of PR #457 (verified against current main, 2026-07-19).

## Defect

Characters already `stable` at 0 HP when migration 0020 runs are silently excluded from automatic stable recovery forever, violating the durable-deadline contract (eshyra-2n1t.8.1) for migrated campaigns.

Code facts (all verified):

- `packages/core/data/migrations/0020_stable_recovery_deadline.sql` only adds three nullable columns (`stable_recovery_roll`, `stable_recovery_anchor_elapsed_minutes`, `stable_recovery_deadline_elapsed_minutes`); no backfill for existing stable-at-zero rows.
- `resolveStableRecoveries` (`packages/core/src/state/hpLifecycle.ts:604-613`) requires all three fields `IS NOT NULL` in its WHERE clause, so legacy rows are silently skipped — no error, no evidence.
- There is no repair path: `stabilizeCharacter` (`hpLifecycle.ts:564-568`) throws unless `life_state === 'dying'`, so an already-stable character cannot be re-scheduled.

The only workaround is out-of-band (GM heals the character), which defeats the automatic-recovery feature the migration claims to complete.

## Required fix (per review)

Provide an explicit migration/adoption policy for legacy stable-at-zero rows. Options:

1. Quarantine legacy stable-at-zero rows with repair evidence and fail closed; or
2. Schedule them deterministically in a migration-aware domain step with recorded provenance (note: scheduling needs an RNG roll — if done in a SQL migration it must be deterministic and recorded; a code-level adoption step with provenance is likely cleaner than pure SQL).

Regardless of the option chosen, `resolveStableRecoveries` should throw (fail closed, consistent with the codebase's philosophy) on a stable-at-zero character with missing or *partially* populated schedule fields rather than silently ignoring it. Add tests for: legacy NULL-field stable row surfaced/adopted rather than skipped, and partial-field corruption raising an error.

Migration checksums are immutable — do not edit 0020; use a new migration.

Related (same PR #457 review): Demon Armor permanent doff block, advanceWorldTime recovery atomicity, rest benefits evidence gap.

Sibling beads from PR #457 post-merge review: eshyra-gacz (Demon Armor doff), eshyra-r2ps (clock/recovery atomicity), eshyra-cc3c (rest evidence gap). Reviewer recommends one follow-up PR; the first three are re-freeze blockers.

title: Demon Armor stays permanently undoffable after its curse ends (blocksDoff ignores live curse state)
description:
Post-merge review of PR #457 (verified against current main, 2026-07-19).

## Defect

Demon Armor (and any future `blocksDoff` cursed item) remains permanently impossible to doff after its curse is removed, contradicting the SRD ("you can't doff it unless you are targeted by the remove curse spell or similar magic").

Code facts (all verified):

- `donItem` (`packages/core/src/state/inventoryWear.ts:104-125`) attaches the source-defined curse condition on don (`m7-demon-armor-curse` via `findDonCurseState` + `addCondition`).
- The committed pack record `magic-item:demon-armor` encodes the release path: `curse.endedBy: ["spell:remove-curse", "similar magic"]` and the state definition carries `endsOn: [{trigger: "targeted-by-spell:remove-curse-or-similar-magic"}]`.
- `removeCondition` (`domainMutations.ts:154`) can remove the live condition freely.
- But `assertInventoryCurseCustodyReady` (`packages/core/src/state/attunement.ts:205-214`) treats `curse.blocksDoff === true` as permanently active whenever the item is worn (or wear state ambiguous). It never reads the wearer's `conditions_json` / live curse state.

So after Remove Curse: condition gone, `doff_item` still fails forever. Worse, the same gate throws for every custody mutation while worn (`doff`, `dropped`, `sold`, `transfer` — `lost`/`transfer` return only *after* the blocksDoff check), so the item is wholly stuck on the character.

## Required fix (per review)

Make the doff restriction depend on the applicable live curse state (e.g. the wearer still has the don-onset curse condition id), or persist an explicit active/resolved curse-instance state. Add a test covering: don Demon Armor → doff fails → remove/resolve the curse condition → doff succeeds → item remains held, `not_worn`.

Design note: keying off `conditions_json` means a plain `remove_condition` tool call (a DM adjudication) lifts the block — that is the existing condition-authority boundary and matches the pack's `endsOn` trigger being adjudication-mediated anyway. If a stricter evidence trail is wanted, persist a curse-instance row instead; either way the current permanent block is wrong.

Related (same PR #457 review): migration-0020 stranded stable characters, advanceWorldTime recovery atomicity, rest benefits evidence gap.

title: Sold-item 'returned' basis bypasses sale-proceeds reversal (economic dupe loop)
description:
Post-merge review of PR #455 (verified against current main, 2026-07-19).

## Defect

A sold inventory row can be restored payment-free via `basis: 'returned'`, leaving the character with both the item and the sale proceeds — the exact economic dupe loop the repurchase-payment work was built to close.

Code facts (all verified):

- `packages/core/src/state/domainMutations.ts` `reacquireItem`: the disposition/basis compatibility gate (~line 667) rejects only `sold+found` and `lost+repurchased`; `sold+returned` passes.
- Payment is *required* for `repurchased` and *forbidden* for `found`/`returned` (~lines 628-635), so the `returned` path performs no wallet mutation by construction.
- Schema agrees: `inventory_custody_event` CHECK `(basis='repurchased') = (payment_event_id IS NOT NULL)` (migration 0018).
- Existing tests pin the payment-free sold-item return ("The merchant rescinded the sale and handed it back") as passing behavior.

Loop: sell item → keep proceeds → narrate a return → `reacquire_item { basis: 'returned' }` → item + proceeds retained. In gameplay the DM model adjudicates the evidence string, so a player steering the narration is enough; there is no deterministic economic backstop on this path, unlike every other transition in this family.

## Fix direction (per review recommendation)

- Make `returned` valid only for `lost` rows (extend the compatibility gate).
- For sold rows, require either `repurchased` (existing atomic payment) or a new `sale-reversed` basis that atomically reverses the original sale proceeds (credit debit mirroring the sale wallet event).
- A genuinely gratuitous merchant gift-back, if it must be supported, should be its own explicit basis with a deliberate decision — not the default free path.

Note: adding a payment-carrying basis (`sale-reversed`) conflicts with the immutable migration-0018 CHECK `(basis='repurchased') = (payment_event_id IS NOT NULL)` on `inventory_custody_event`, so a new migration is required to widen that constraint (and the basis enum CHECK). Update `toolReacquireItem.ts` schema/description, `listRecoverableItems` basis filtering (`domainMutations.ts` ~line 440-463), and the tests that currently pin the payment-free sold-return.

Related: eshyra follow-ups from the same review — migration-0018 oversized-stack unresolvable edge, and the numeric-conservation dice-modifier gate.
notes:
Related beads from same PR #455 post-merge review: eshyra-eks3 (migration-0018 oversized-stack), eshyra-2n3n (dice-token gate).
Fix merged to branch eshyra-f0nz; PR #458 open (https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/458). Close after PR merge.

title: Implement item economy reset/timer executor (F5/F7 item semantic reset owner)
description:
Close the missing F5/F7 item boundary identified in the 2026-07-19 pre-re-freeze gap review: canonical pack-bound magic items have NO engine executor for their declared reset specs or state-machine timers. restore_usage's description already points at 'their semantic reset owner', but no such owner exists — itemState.ts exports no reset/regain function, no tool applies mechanics.economies[*].reset, and item pendingTimers are scheduled inside useItem with a comment deferring execution to 'the future F5/F7 scheduler/reset boundary' that was never built.

Symptoms today:
- reset: [{at:'dawn', amount:'1d6+4'}] is never applied by the engine; staff/wand charges only ever decrease deterministically, dawn regains are model-narrated.
- Item stateMachine timer transitions and machine duration never fire from the clock (e.g. cube-of-force barrier 1-minute expiry is listed in pendingTimers at use time and nothing ever resolves it).
- Budget economies (winged-boots flight, boots-of-speed) never regain via their per-period/long-rest reset declarations; cooldown availableAt is never set or honored by a scheduler; per-day 'all' resets at dawn never happen.

Scope: a deterministic executor that walks item_state rows and applies, against the campaign clock (clock.elapsed_minutes) and the F7 rest events:
- economy resets for every declared shape: {at: dawn|dusk|short-rest|long-rest|hour|days|per-period, amount: DiceExpr|'all'|DurationSpec, days?, period?, onlyIfUnused?} — seeded dice through the campaign RNG with recorded evidence, clamped to max; define and document anchoring semantics (what elapsed-minute anchor 'dawn'/'dusk' resolve to; per-period anchor point; onlyIfUnused definition) — if any pack reset shape proves ambiguous or insufficient, that is a pack schema finding to surface, not to work around;
- pendingTimers resolution when the clock passes deadlineElapsedMinutes (reuse the itemTimers anchor/deadline validation and the 2n1t.8.1 stable-recovery resolve pattern: resolution hooked into advance_time/rest completion, applied through the authoritative item-state write path with validateItemStateForRecord);
- onDepleted interplay on regain (regainOn results) and lifecycle statuses respected (inert/nonmagical items do not regain);
- wiring: advance_time (update_clock), complete_short_rest / complete_long_rest (F7), and an explicit dawn/dusk boundary derived from the clock — decide and document whether dawn is a clock-derived event or a semantic DM tool call, mirroring how rest events are DM-narrated today.

Rationale for priority (pre-re-freeze recommendation from the 2026-07-19 gap review): this is the single largest untested consumer of pack mechanics data — all 240 items' reset/timer/duration shapes — and therefore the most likely near-term engine work to surface a pack data-model defect that would force a post-freeze thaw. Recommended to land (with the PR #455-style adversarial review bar) BEFORE eshyra-o9bd.14 re-freezes the pack; if that ordering is confirmed, wire it with: bd dep add eshyra-o9bd.14 <this-bead>.

Acceptance criteria: every declared reset shape in the committed pack is exercised by tests (dawn dice regain, per-day all, budget per-period with onlyIfUnused, long-rest gate, days cooldown, hour); timers fire deterministically on clock advance with recorded evidence; double-application is impossible (idempotent per boundary crossing); no model-invented amounts (fail closed on unknown shapes); full verify:worktree green; any pack shape ambiguity discovered is filed as an importer finding rather than silently reinterpreted.

description: Extend the roll tool with declared modifier lists, vsDc/opposed resolution, post-roll transforms (half/double/min-0), plus a small deterministic calc primitive for non-roll formulas. notes:
Landed in PR #430 (branch eshyra-2n1t-f1-f9) on the F1 representation (no reparsing). resolve_check (declared modifiers w/ label+source, proficiency {bonus,multiplier} apply-once w/ floor-half + none-doubled=0, adv/dis cancellation, vs DC/AC incl. nat-1/20 attack-only overrides per the rolling-1-or-20 spec note), resolve_contest (fixed roll order, tie=status quo), resolve_damage (typed packets, engine crit dice-doubling, per-packet min-0, roll-once multi-target, immunity->resistance(floor)->vulnerability after modifiers, duplicate declarations rejected), calc (9 SRD-verified formulas: passive_score, carry_capacity+vehicle pull, encumbrance_thresholds, jump_distance, fall_damage_dice, grapple_escape_dc, days_without_food_limit, forced_march_dc, group_check_outcome). All read-only; ledger renders all entries; turn trace rulesResolution carries checks/contests/damage/calcs for deterministic replay. Coverage: 21 partial rows + adv-dis -> implemented; cover/hiding/two-weapon-fighting -> model-adjudicated-supported; census 36/100/24/5/10. description:

title: Model creature form-specific speeds, AC, and hover semantics
description:

close_reason: Implemented in PR #394: speed map now carries only unconditional modes; hover emitted as literal-true field (7 creatures); lycanthrope form parentheticals emitted as speedVariants [{condition, speed}]; Werebear no longer exposes unconditional climb 30 (now {walk:30} + variant {walk:40, climb:30} in bear or hybrid form); verbatim speedSourceText kept; tests for Werebear, Werewolf, Mage, Ankheg, Ghost (hover).

title: Preserve complete SRD creature statline semantics
description:
Finding source:
- Fable P1/P2 systemic modeling loss.
- All 317 creatures store armorClass and hitPoints as bare ints.
- Quantified losses:
  - 206 AC parentheticals dropped, such as "natural armor" or "leather armor, shield".
  - 316 HP dice formulas dropped, such as "19d12 + 133".
  - 7 hover speed annotations dropped, e.g. "fly 40 ft. (hover)".
  - 4 form-conditional speed lines dropped (Werewolf/Wereboar/Weretiger/Werebear), e.g. "30 ft. (40 ft., climb 30 ft. in bear or hybrid form)".
  - 6 conditional/alternate AC lines flattened: 3 lycanthrope dual-form ACs, Mage "(15 with mage armor)", Druid "(16 with barkskin)", Ankheg "14 (natural armor), 11 while prone".
- Examples:
  - Werewolf/Wereboar/Werebear lose beast-form AC; four lycanthropes lose form speeds.
  - Werebear currently has climb: 30 as a base speed, but source grants climb 30 only in bear/hybrid form, where walk is also 40 rather than 30. This is actively wrong data, not just loss.
  - Mage loses "(15 with mage armor)".
  - Druid loses "(16 with barkskin)".
  - Ankheg loses "11 while prone".
  - Hover/fly conditional data is invisible to deterministic behavior.
- Fable notes stat-block records already model hitPoints as { value, formula } (see stat-block:giant-fly), so there is a precedent; creature parser discards what another parser keeps.

Gameplay impact:
- No HP rolling/max-HP variants.
- Wrong AC for transformed/form-variant creatures.
- AC explanations lose armor/natural armor/spell context.
- Hover/prone/falling semantics unavailable to combat tools.

Acceptance criteria:
- Creature statline data preserves the full printed semantics rather than flattening to ints.
- Compatibility for existing consumers is maintained or migrated deliberately.
- Gates fail when printed AC parentheticals, HP formulas, XP, conditional AC/speeds, or hover semantics are dropped.
close_reason: Epic complete in PR #394: full printed creature statline semantics preserved (structured AC/HP/speed + hover + form variants + verbatim source texts), compatibility migrated deliberately (encounterCombatants accepts both shapes; schema/tests updated), gates fail on any dropped statline semantics. 317 creature records regenerated; verify:dnd5e-srd-pack exit 0; full suite green.

title: Correct unsafe mechanics.conditions relation semantics in spells and effects
description:
Finding source:
- Codex High finding: mechanics.conditions is not safe as deterministic effect semantics.
- Codex found 12 likely wrong relation: "applies" projections where source text is prevention, removal, immunity/protection, or gating instead.
- Concrete examples: branding-smite, calm-emotions, lesser-restoration, and protection-from-evil-and-good.
- ChatGPT confirmed branding-smite was already present before the latest erf5 changes: source says the target becomes visible if invisible and cannot become invisible, but mechanics records condition=invisible relation=applies.
- Fable independently confirmed in the committed pack: branding-smite marks invisible as applies (source: target cannot become invisible), calm-emotions marks charmed as applies (source: suppresses), lesser-restoration marks blinded as applies (source: ends a condition), protection-from-evil-and-good marks charmed as applies (source: protects against).

Why it matters:
- Deterministic tools may apply the opposite of the SRD effect.
- "Applies condition" must not be used for prevents/removes/protects-from/grants-advantage-against/gates-on/mentions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Audit every mechanics.conditions entry in spells and any shared effect parser output against source text.
- Replace unsafe relation values with a closed vocabulary that can express at least: inflicts, prevents, removes, suppresses, protectsFrom/immunizesAgainst, grantsAdvantageAgainst, excludes, gatesOn, mentions.
- Fix all 12 Codex-identified likely wrong cases plus any additional cases found.
- Add tests for branding-smite, calm-emotions, lesser-restoration, protection-from-evil-and-good, and at least one true condition-inflicting spell/effect to prevent overcorrection.
- Add a guard so prevention/removal/immunity phrases cannot be emitted as relation=applies.
- Document relation semantics for deterministic consumers.
notes: Implemented in PR #385 (branch eshyra-o9bd.18.3, awaiting review/merge). Shared classifier src/rules/conditionRelations.ts; vocabulary now applies/removes/prevents/suppresses/immune/advantage/disadvantage/exclusion/gates/mention; condition-relation-safety audit gate re-derives all 512 entries; 30 relation values fixed across 21 records (20 wrong applies incl. all Codex cases + 8 more, 10 mention upgrades); thaw note docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/thaw-notes/2026-07-02-o9bd-18-3-condition-relation-safety.md. Close on merge.
close_reason: Merged to main in PR #385 (merge commit 55f5f98). Reviewer non-blocking note recorded: the condition-relation-safety audit gate shares the classifier with the importer, so it is a drift/hand-edit guard, NOT an independent semantic oracle — semantic safety rests on the regression tests and the thaw note's full 512-entry manual audit. If future relation bugs surface, fix them with classifier regression tests (mechanicsProjections.test.ts / conditionRelations), not by relying on the gate.

title: Fix SRD concentration derivation for no-comma concentration durations
description:
Finding sources:
- ChatGPT, Codex, and Fable all found spell:protection-from-evil-and-good has data.duration "Concentration up to 10 minutes" but mechanics.concentration false.
- Fable notes the SRD PDF itself prints "Duration: Concentration up to 10 minutes" with no comma on p. 173; this is a known source typo compared to the usual "Concentration, up to ..." form.
- The text was copied faithfully, but the comma-dependent detector mis-derived the concentration flag.
- Git history comparison showed this was already present before the latest erf5 fixes, so it is not a new erf5 regression.

Why it matters:
- A concentration tracker could allow Protection from Evil and Good to stack with another concentration spell.
- This is a direct source-vs-derived-mechanics accuracy bug.
- Fable says this is the only spell in the pack with the non-standard concentration duration string.

Acceptance criteria:
- spell:protection-from-evil-and-good emits mechanics.concentration true.
- The detector accepts both "Concentration, up to ..." and "Concentration up to ...".
- Add a regression test for the exact no-comma SRD duration form.
- Add a pack-wide gate that compares mechanics.concentration against duration semantics for all 319 spells.
- Confirm no spell with a non-concentration duration starts emitting concentration true.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #383: detector accepts comma and no-comma concentration forms; protection-from-evil-and-good emits concentration true; pack-wide spell-concentration-flag gate added; source typo documented in known-source-typos.md.

title: Restore dropped SRD Skills proficiency prose after embedded skill list
description:
Finding source:
- Fable P1.
- rule:skills silently drops operative prose after the embedded skill-to-ability list.
- Existing rule:skills text ends at approximately: "...examples of how to use a skill associated with an ability" on p. 77 and carries structured skillsByAbility.
- Missing p. 78 prose resumes after the list and explains what skill proficiency means: an individual can add proficiency bonus to ability checks involving that skill; without proficiency the individual makes a normal ability check; it also includes the climbing-a-cliff example.

Root cause hypothesis from Fable:
- Parser does not resume prose capture after an embedded bullet/list region.
- The unaccounted=0 source-region ledger gate misses the loss because the region is owned by rule:skills, even though the post-list prose is not actually emitted.

Why it matters:
- This is a core D&D rule for what skill proficiency does.
- Primary DM lookup loses the canonical rule explanation.
- Deterministic ability-check and character proficiency tooling cannot cite/ground the rule from the pack.

Acceptance criteria:
- rule:skills includes the post-list p. 78 prose after the skillsByAbility embedded list.
- The structured skillsByAbility mapping remains intact.
- Add regression coverage for prose resuming after embedded lists/tables inside a rule region.
- Add or extend a source-coverage/source-region gate so owned regions only count as represented when their prose is emitted or deliberately transformed into a structured equivalent.
- Regenerate committed SRD artifacts and update freeze metadata/thaw note as required.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #383: parseRules re-flows post-bullet prose from excluded bullet captions into the enclosing rule; rule:skills carries the p78 proficiency prose; region ledger reclassifies to record:rule:skills with containment guard. General owned-region gate remains 18.9.2.

title: Close 2026-07-01 D&D SRD audit findings
description:
Parent epic for every finding from the 2026-07-01 D&D SRD audit synthesis. Do not treat closed older beads as satisfying these findings; the latest audit still found them or found residual issues after those beads closed.

Inputs synthesized:
- ChatGPT manual review of the audit bundle.

- Claude Fable-5 max-effort independent full-coverage audit.

- SRD source pages reviewed: 403.
- All bundle commands and existing gates were green, but the audits still found defects and gate blind spots.

Fable verification method worth preserving in downstream beads:
- Did not reuse repo audit code.
- Rebuilt column-aware source reading order from items.json coordinates because .txt interleaves columns.
- Normalized PDF hyphen/ligature/one-half/minus artifacts.
- Required every 6-token shingle on every source page to be reproducible from pack prose or reconstructed renderings of structured fields.
- Reconstructed spell headers, full creature statlines including derived ability modifiers and CR-to-XP, equipment/armor/weapon table rows, class hit-point/proficiency boilerplate from hitDie, and class spell lists from spell.classes[].
- Verified every prose string and every structured field of all 1,812 records against cited source windows.
- Ran a digit-bearing token pass for DCs, dice, ranges, durations, averages, attack bonuses, CR/XP, equipment values, armorClass structures, and concentration/ritual flags.
- Reported zero numeric corruptions, exact class spell-list parity, and strong source fidelity overall.
- Durable copy of the harness and its reports: ~/src/dnd5e-srd-audit-harness-070126/

Policy for this epic:
- Every finding below must be closed by code/data fix, durable gate, or explicit documented non-issue decision.
- Broad findings must be split into children rather than silently deferred.
- Ambiguous findings require research/verification beads.
- A subsequent audit should not find any noted issue still present unless an accepted non-issue is recorded.
- This epic blocks eshyra-o9bd.14 (regenerate + re-freeze): the pack must not be re-frozen while findings here are open or undecided.

title: Tag SRD focus symbol instrument and tool equipment groups
description:
Child of the equipment grouping audit epic.

The SRD equipment section groups several leaf items into gameplay-relevant item groups such as arcane focus, druidic focus, holy symbol, musical instrument, artisan tools, gaming sets, and similar tool/equipment categories. The generated records preserve the leaf items but do not carry enough structured group/subtype metadata for deterministic starting-equipment filters.

Examples:
- Arcane focus candidates: Crystal, Orb, Rod, Staff, Wand.
- Holy symbol candidates: Amulet, Emblem, Reliquary.
- Druidic focus candidates: Sprig of mistletoe, Totem, Wooden staff, Yew wand.
- Musical instrument candidates: Bagpipes, Drum, Dulcimer, Flute, Lute, Lyre, Horn, Pan flute, Shawm, Viol.

Acceptance criteria:

title: Tag SRD weapons with simple/martial and melee/ranged groups
description:

- Simple Melee Weapons
- Simple Ranged Weapons
- Martial Melee Weapons
- Martial Ranged Weapons

Acceptance criteria:
- Each generated weapon record has structured grouping metadata equivalent to:
  - weaponCategory: simple | martial
  - weaponRange: melee | ranged
- The metadata is derived deterministically from the SRD table grouping, not manually patched in the generated pack.
- Starting-equipment filters for martial melee weapons and similar weapon choices can enumerate concrete candidates.
- Class proficiencies for Simple weapons and martial weapons can resolve to concrete weapon records.
- Add regression tests for representative simple melee, simple ranged, martial melee, and martial ranged weapons.

title: Preserve SRD equipment grouping semantics for deterministic filters
description:
Combined audit finding from Claude Opus 4.8 and ChatGPT review.

The importer captures leaf equipment records but loses important SRD grouping semantics from equipment tables/lists. This makes several already-emitted deterministic filters and proficiencies unsatisfiable without prose/name heuristics.

Known problems:
- Weapon records lack simple/martial and melee/ranged classification, even though starting-equipment filters request martial melee weapons and class proficiencies refer to Simple weapons and martial weapons.
- Arcane focus, druidic focus, holy symbol, musical instrument, and similar item groups are represented as generic gear/tool records without machine-readable group/subtype tags.
- Starting-equipment filters such as select: "arcane-focus", "druidic-focus", "holy-symbol", and "musical-instrument" cannot enumerate candidates deterministically from the catalog.
- The pack handles armor grouping better than weapons, so weapons/foci/instruments should be brought to that level of resolvability.

Acceptance criteria:
- Preserve SRD equipment grouping headers as generated structured metadata.
- Every generated starting-equipment filter resolves to at least one candidate record unless intentionally documented as deferred.
- Class equipment proficiencies such as Simple weapons and martial weapons can resolve to concrete catalog entries.
- Add importer/audit regression coverage.
- Fixes belong in importer/modeling/resolver/audit code, not hand-edits to generated pack JSON.

title: Fix dropped SRD skill-to-ability mapping and coverage heading collision
description:
Combined audit finding from Claude Opus 4.8 and ChatGPT review.

The SRD p.78 skill-to-ability mapping is dropped from the generated records. rule:skills says the skills related to each ability score are shown in the following list, but the actual list is absent from the record body and appears in no structured record.

Missing mapping:
- Strength: Athletics
- Dexterity: Acrobatics, Sleight of Hand, Stealth
- Intelligence: Arcana, History, Investigation, Nature, Religion
- Wisdom: Animal Handling, Insight, Medicine, Perception, Survival
- Charisma: Deception, Intimidation, Performance, Persuasion
- Constitution: no skills

Impact:
- Deterministic character-sheet tools cannot reliably compute skill modifiers.
- Class/background skillChoices are structured, but there is no canonical generated-pack mapping from chosen skill to governing ability.
- The primary DM model sees rule:skills promise a list that is not present.
- The source-coverage guard falsely reports completeness because duplicate heading names such as Skills > Strength collide with later ability-section headings such as Strength.

Acceptance criteria:
- Represent the full p.78 skill-to-ability mapping in generated output, preferably as structured data rather than prose-only text.
- rule:skills no longer ends by referring to a missing list.
- Deterministic tools can resolve every canonical SRD skill to its governing ability.
- Add regression coverage for duplicate heading ownership collisions, especially Skills > Strength versus the later Strength ability description.
- Harden source-region coverage so a region cannot be counted as represented merely because a same-named heading maps to some record; the owning record must either contain the source text or structurally encode the region.
- Fix the importer/tests, not the committed generated pack by hand.
close_reason: Fixed p78 skill-to-ability mapping loss and the heading-collision auto-match bug

title: Fix SRD audit coverage holes for sidebars and continuation-only pages
description:
The 2026-06-30 audit bundle `/home/jhbongaarts/src/dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle-0630-1.zip` does not prove full SRD source coverage even though `reports/source-coverage.json` and `reports/source-region-ledger.json` both report zero unaccounted/unrepresented regions.

Confirmed gaps from exhaustive page/record review after extracting to `/tmp/eshyra-audit-bundle-0630-1`:

- All 17 source-coverage sidebar records have no `source-region-ledger` entry keyed to the emitted record: `rule:druid-sacred-plants-and-wood`, `rule:druid-druids-and-the-gods`, `rule:paladin-breaking-your-oath`, `rule:warlock-your-pact-boon`, `rule:wizard-your-spellbook`, `rule:equipment-packs`, `rule:self-sufficiency`, `rule:hiding`, `rule:combat-step-by-step`, `rule:interacting-with-objects-around-you`, `rule:contests-in-combat`, `rule:casting-in-armor`, `rule:the-schools-of-magic`, `rule:modifying-creatures`, `rule:armor-weapon-and-tool-proficiencies`, `rule:grapple-rules-for-monsters`, and `condition:exhaustion`.
- Three non-empty extracted source pages have no source-inventory, source-coverage, or source-region-ledger entries at all: p34 (continuation of `rule:paladin-breaking-your-oath`), p55 (continuation of `rule:wizard-your-spellbook`), and p362 (continuation rows for `table:norse-deities`).
- Additional pages with text but no ledger entries include p23, p69, and p361; p23 is the sidebar case and p69/p361 are table-heavy pages that need explicit coverage evidence or an intentional table-row representation proof.

The pack records do contain the sampled text, so this is primarily an audit-evidence/completeness failure rather than demonstrated pack content loss. The failure mode is that page/region accounting can silently omit source prose/table continuations while still claiming `unrepresented: 0`.

Likely code to inspect: `packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/sourceRegionLedger.ts`, `packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/sourceInventoryCoverage.ts`, and the audit bundle page-completeness checks.

Acceptance criteria:
- Every non-empty extracted SRD page has explicit inventory/coverage/ledger accounting or a narrow documented ignore that is valid for that page's content.
- Sidebar prose that emits a record is represented in `source-region-ledger.json` with the correct `targetKey`.
- Continuation-only prose/table pages such as p34, p55, and p362 are included in source evidence and cannot disappear behind a zero-unrepresented summary.
- Add regression coverage for the examples above.
notes:
Partial fix landed on branch eshyra-erf5-srd-audit-round: 17 sidebar records (+2 incidental creature-variant sidebars) that had a correct source-coverage status but zero source-region-ledger entries now have entries, via a fix to sourceRegionLedger.ts (sidebar body prose renders in the table-cell font band, so it was being silently skipped as table-row noise). This also fixes p23/p34/p55 continuation pages as a side effect.

Remaining gap (p69 Adventuring Gear sub-captions, p361 deity table captions, p362 Norse Deities continuation) is a DIFFERENT root cause (table-row/embedded-caption accounting, not sidebar misclassification) and requires either a new extractor strategy or a deliberate documented decision about what "coverage" means for table-only pages/continuations. Filed as follow-up eshyra-erf5.5 rather than broadening this fix per the importer-fix-protocol hard-stop guidance. Leaving eshyra-5c7f open pending that follow-up; not closing since not all acceptance criteria are met yet.

title: Add relation-aware SRD condition mechanics semantics
description:
Combined vk23 audit follow-up.

The current mechanics condition projection appears to collect condition mentions without distinguishing what the source text says about the condition. This is useful as a search hint, but unsafe as deterministic game-state logic.

Examples from the vk23 audit review:
- spell:shield can surface invisible because the prose says "An invisible barrier..." but the spell does not apply the Invisible condition.
- spell:sleep can surface charmed and unconscious, but charmed appears in an immunity clause while unconscious is the effect.
- spell:color-spray can surface blinded and unconscious, but unconscious appears in an exclusion/targeting clause.
- creature:death-dog has condition names in a trait that grants advantage against conditions, not conditions it applies.
- action:dodge mentions incapacitated because the benefit is lost if incapacitated; Dodge does not apply that condition.

This makes mechanics.conditions too ambiguous for deterministic tools. Runtime code must not treat raw condition mentions as "apply these conditions."

Acceptance criteria:
- Replace or augment raw condition mention projection with relation-aware semantics.
- Represent at least these relation classes, either as explicit fields or tagged entries:
  - applies / imposes condition
  - removes / ends condition
  - immunity or unaffected-by condition
  - advantage or disadvantage involving saves/checks against a condition
  - targeting exclusion or prerequisite involving a condition
  - descriptive mention only
- Add regression tests for Shield, Sleep, Color Spray, Death Dog Two-Headed, and Dodge.
- Update generated pack output and audit expectations so deterministic tools can identify condition application effects without false positives.
- Document the intended consumer contract: condition mentions are not authoritative state mutations unless relation says they are.
close_reason: parseConditions now classifies relation (applies/removes/immune/advantage/disadvantage/exclusion/mention) per sentence; regenerated pack; regression tests for all 5 named examples

title: Fix Warlock invocation prerequisite parsing
description:
Fix Warlock Eldritch Invocation prerequisite parsing from the ngcj SRD audit.

Problem:
Several invocation option prerequisites are clipped when the source wraps "Pact of the X feature" across lines/pages. The imported option data has prerequisite: "Pact of" and leaks the rest into the body text, e.g. "the Tome feature You can now inscribe...".

Affected examples:
- Book of Ancient Secrets
- Chains of Carceri
- Lifedrinker
- Thirsting Blade
- Voice of the Chain Master

Why this matters:
Deterministic tools cannot safely gate invocations if prerequisites are incomplete. A resolver needs to know whether an invocation requires Pact of the Tome, Pact of the Blade, Pact of the Chain, a minimum Warlock level, or both.

Scope:
- Fix extraction/parsing of wrapped invocation prerequisites.
- Add structured prerequisite fields for invocation options where possible.
- Preserve original prerequisite prose for DM context.
- Correct source attribution for invocation options spanning SRD pages 48-50, instead of collapsing them all to page 47.
- Add regression tests for wrapped prerequisite lines.

Acceptance criteria:
- No invocation option has prerequisite exactly "Pact of" or similarly dangling prerequisite fragments.
- Book of Ancient Secrets requires Pact of the Tome.
- Lifedrinker and Thirsting Blade require Pact of the Blade and the correct minimum Warlock level where present in the SRD.
- Chains of Carceri and Voice of the Chain Master expose their correct prerequisites.
- Option body text no longer begins with leaked prerequisite continuations such as "the Tome feature".
- Source pages/citations are accurate for invocation options spanning pages 48-50.

- npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack passes and regenerated pack output is intentional.

title: Quarantine invalid SRD mechanics projections
description:
Fix unsafe machine-readable mechanics projections discovered in the ngcj SRD audit.

Problem:
Some records expose fields that appear deterministic, such as spellGrants/resources/effects, but the values are clipped prose or regex residue rather than validated refs or typed objects. Deterministic tools should not have to guess whether a mechanics-looking field is trustworthy.

Examples from the audit:
- Bard Spellcasting includes spellGrants like "two cantrips of your choice from the bard".
- Ranger includes "and replace it with another".
- Warlock Eldritch Invocations includes "compulsion once using a warlock".
- Wizard Spellbook includes "a wizard" and questionable long-rest/proficiency mechanics.

Why this matters:
Missing structure is acceptable as an explicit gap. Bad structure is worse because deterministic tools may consume it as authoritative gameplay data.

Scope:
- Audit feature records and any importer projections that populate machine-readable mechanics-ish fields from regex/prose.
- Make projections fail closed unless they produce validated refs or typed objects.
- Quarantine unresolved extracted prose under an explicitly non-authoritative/evidence/unresolved field, or omit it.
- Add regression tests/gates for clipped prose fragments in mechanics fields.
- Ensure fields such as spellGrants do not contain plain natural-language fragments unless the schema explicitly says they are unresolved prose.

Acceptance criteria:
- No spellGrants/resources/effects/mechanics fields contain clipped natural-language fragments like "and replace it with another" or "two cantrips of your choice from the bard".
- Valid spell grants are stable spell refs or typed grant/choice objects.
- Unresolved prose remains available for DM-model context only in clearly named prose/evidence fields.
- The audit bundle or a dedicated report exposes any remaining unresolved mechanics projections as warnings, not as trusted data.
- npm run typecheck passes.
- npm test passes.
- npm run check passes.
- npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack passes and regenerated pack output is intentional.

title: Resolve class starting equipment into deterministic item grants

title: Model class and subclass feature option catalogs

title: Add choice-bearing prose coverage gate for SRD records
description:
Problem:
The current choice-coverage audit reports 60 structured choices and 0 findings, but it mostly validates choices that already exist. It does not reliably detect SRD records that contain build-choice prose without structured choices or option catalogs.

Examples from the 2026-06-29 audit:
- feature:warlock:pact-boon has Pact of the Chain / Blade / Tome only in prose.
- feature:warlock:eldritch-invocations embeds 32 invocations in prose behind one generic choice.
- feature:hunter:hunters-prey, defensive-tactics, multiattack, and superior-hunters-defense have option lists in prose.
- feature:sorcerer:metamagic has one generic choice while the eight options are prose only.
- Fighting Style features expose generic choice text but not structured option refs/effects.
- Bard Magical Secrets and Wizard Spell Mastery / Signature Spells are not structured spell choices.

Implement:
- Add a source/record audit that scans feature, class, subclass, ancestry, background, and similar records for choice-bearing language.
- Detect phrases such as:
  - choose one of the following
  - choose two
  - gain one of the following
  - select one
  - options
  - you learn additional spells of your choice
  - prerequisite
- Report records where choice-like prose exists but no structured choices, choice options, option catalog, spell-choice filter, or explicit allowlist explains the gap.
- Make the report actionable: record id, source location, matched phrase, surrounding snippet, and expected modeling area.
- Start as a report-only or warning gate if needed, but acceptance should include known 2026-06-29 misses being detected.

Acceptance criteria:
- The audit detects the known unstructured option cases listed above.
- False positives can be documented with a narrow allowlist and reason.
- The report is emitted into the audit bundle.
- Existing tests pass.
- The audit does not rely on LLM interpretation.

title: FINAL: independent ADR-0020 re-audit of the candidate SRD pack
description:
Perform the independent max-effort audit of the candidate after bounded automated gates
pass and before formal re-freeze. Adversarially inspect source fidelity/provenance,
discovery-supporting relationships, adjudication boundaries, selected capability correctness,
and state-integrity/runtime ownership as separate concerns. Automated green is entry evidence,
not universal completeness proof.
acceptance_criteria:
- Independent audit is performed against the exact candidate and current authority.
- Source fidelity, discovery, adjudication support, deterministic capability, and state integrity are reported separately.
- Known defect classes are attacked beyond original examples; any recurrence/new substantive defect blocks re-freeze and receives ownership.
- Unknown/unrecognized/unenumerable scope is reported as a limit, not a green result.
- A clean result means no blocker was found against the ADR-0020 truthfulness bar, not universal completeness.
notes:
2026-07-08 ADR 0017 adjustment: The final max-effort audit should use the compiler guide's dimensions explicitly: reproducibility, source completeness, structural fidelity, semantic modeling, runtime ownership/support, and end-to-end playable validation. Report them separately instead of collapsing them into a single 'represented somewhere' result.
*** ORDER INVERTED (2026-07-25) ***
This bead previously depended on eshyra-o9bd.14, i.e. the final re-audit ran
AFTER regeneration and re-freeze. That edge is removed. The corrected closure
chain audits the CANDIDATE bundle BEFORE the formal re-freeze:

  19.6.1 corpus migration -> 19.6.2 regression/finding closure
  -> 19.6.3 candidate bundle + automated no-repeat gates
  -> eshyra-o9bd.16 (THIS BEAD) independent max-effort re-audit
  -> 19.6.4 accept results and certify zero-repeat closure
  -> eshyra-o9bd.14 formal regeneration and re-freeze
  -> eshyra-2zyy re-enable post-freeze thaw-note gating

SCOPE CHANGE: this bead now audits a candidate, pre-freeze artifact rather than a
frozen one. Its original description ("After ... the pack is regenerated/re-
frozen, perform a MAX-EFFORT re-audit") reflects the old order — read the
dependency graph, not that sentence, for sequencing. Everything else about the
max-effort standard stands.

This bead is deliberately NOT superseded by the new program: eshyra-o9bd.19.6.3
generates the candidate and passes automated gates, but independent review
belongs here.
ADR-0020 authority reconciliation applied 2026-09-10 by eshyra-o9bd.19.6.5.
The operative title/description/acceptance criteria supersede contradictory
pre-ADR global-closure language in older notes. Historical notes remain evidence,
not current authority.

title: Regenerate and re-freeze the accepted ADR-0020 SRD candidate
description:
Formalize the exact candidate authorized by eshyra-o9bd.19.6.4. Re-freeze asserts the
ADR-0020 truthfulness bar: source fidelity/provenance/reproducibility; truthful audit
scope; durable known-finding dispositions; correctness of capabilities actually in force;
no known source invention or unowned live safety/state contract; and explicit unresolved
discovery/adjudication limits. It does not assert universal deterministic or discovery completeness.
acceptance_criteria:
- Formal regeneration matches the accepted candidate and is deterministic.
- Source/license/provenance and freeze-manifest checks pass.
- eshyra-o9bd.19.6.4 has authorized this exact candidate under ADR 0020.
- Capabilities actually in force are correctly bound/executed/state-safe; unselected backlog is not a freeze failure by itself.
- Freeze/readiness artifacts state bounded scope and non-claims.
- No re-freeze statement asserts universal deterministic or discovery completeness.
notes:
Gated on the 2026-07-01 audit epic eshyra-o9bd.18: hard dependencies wired to its concrete pack-changing defect beads (18.1-18.5, 18.6.1-18.6.3, 18.8.1, 18.8.2). bd forbids epic->task blocking, so the epic itself could not be wired; per the epic policy, remaining o9bd.18 children (gameplay modeling epics, gates, cleanup) must each be closed or carry an explicit documented non-issue/defer decision before re-freeze.
2026-07-08 ADR 0017 adjustment: The re-freeze evidence must distinguish the compiler-owned pack closure from external engine readiness. Green compiler closure requires deterministic regeneration, source/reference completeness, semantic projections or source-grounded curated specs where needed, and explicit hook/disposition bindings for runtime ownership. Do not count an unlanded engine dependency as green merely because the pack names it; it must stay represented as engine-pending or be backed by engine-side evidence under the appropriate owner.
*** SEQUENCING CORRECTED (2026-07-25) ***
Re-freeze now happens LAST. This bead depends on eshyra-o9bd.19.6.4
(certification of zero-repeat closure), which depends on eshyra-o9bd.16
(independent max-effort re-audit of the candidate bundle). The historic
eshyra-o9bd.16 -> eshyra-o9bd.14 edge was removed and reversed.

Do not regenerate or re-freeze until certification exists. eshyra-2zyy (restore
SRD thaw-note CI gating) now depends on this bead.
*** GREEN DEFINITION REVISED (2026-07-25) — SUPERSEDES the 8-point version ***
DECISION: where structured pack data is a DIRECT INPUT to deterministic
execution, the pack contract and the reference engine are ONE co-designed
system. The pack defines what the engine must execute; the reference engine
proves the representation is sufficient and unambiguous. Freezing the pack
first would preserve a separation that does not exist in practice.

A deterministic clause that feeds engine execution is GREEN only when all nine
hold:
  1. Complete source-clause identification.
  2. Clause-complete structured representation.
  3. Complete field provenance.
  4. Explicit capability requirements.
  5. A provider-neutral engine implementation exists.
  6. Reference-engine conformance tests exercise the PACK representation.
  7. Correct tool exposure and state mutation.
  8. Fail-closed behavior for unsupported input.
  9. Successful replay / deterministic equivalence where applicable.

A clause is NOT green merely because the pack appears to contain enough data;
the reference implementation must demonstrate that it actually does. A
representation reference that merely RESOLVES to an existing object is not
green — the Opus amended magic-item pass proved reference integrity but
explicitly did NOT prove semantic appropriateness of free-form effects.

AT RE-FREEZE THERE MUST BE ZERO ENGINE-PENDING DETERMINISTIC CLAUSES. The only
permissible non-green clauses are four approved categories:
  * genuine source ambiguity routed to campaign rulings;
  * intentionally model-adjudicated material;
  * external content unavailable in the SRD;
  * explicitly deferred non-deterministic house-rule behavior.
Each must be explicitly represented in-band, carry its alternatives and
campaign-ruling requirement, and fail CLOSED.

WHY (audit evidence): the 2026-07-24 findings were structures that looked
plausible in isolation but failed as executable inputs — alternative damage
modes stored as parallel damage, recharge triggers read as reset periods,
partial saves treated as complete, legendary actions with no budget or cost,
option mechanics hoisted onto parent features, typed records missing
branching/timing/termination. A completed reference implementation forces these
to surface: a dragon-breath scenario cannot pass without half-damage handling;
a legendary-creature scenario cannot pass without a budget; a versatile attack
cannot execute without a discriminated alternative.

CONSEQUENCE FOR SEQUENCING: eshyra-olc5 is no longer a downstream project that
may stay open after eshyra-o9bd closes. Its reference-implementation
certification gates eshyra-o9bd.19.6.1 and therefore the formal re-freeze in
eshyra-o9bd.14.
*** RE-FREEZE BAR REPLACED (2026-07-31) — ADR 0020 NINE-CONDITION MODEL ***
Authority: ADR 0020 ("Prior assumptions" item 4) and section 5.9 of the
integrated transition design
docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md
— the accepted deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8 (PR #485, reviewed head
afd113c7090378c3a9f4122f246a6c32602a5164, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282). Recorded here as accepted authority
and required next state; NOT implemented in code by this bead update.

The recorded bar in the description above — "ZERO engine-pending deterministic
clauses" — is WITHDRAWN. It requires a global negative the corpus cannot support
(RulesRecord.data is typed unknown; kind validators accept unregistered data
fields; key closure over mechanics exists for magic-item only). Re-freeze now
requires all NINE of the following, none of which is a global closure claim:

1. Source fidelity — every retained record's content is traceable to the licensed
   source, with the known source-authority defects repaired or explicitly
   re-sourced.
2. Truthful provenance — provenance.sourceRef and locator correspond to real
   source material; a record whose locator cannot be substantiated is not frozen
   as authoritative.
3. Deterministic reproducibility — npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack exits 0 against
   the pinned source.
4. Truthful scope for every audit and readiness artifact — every artifact in
   sections 5.1-5.6 states its scope in band and claims nothing outside it.
5. Durable disposition of known findings — every finding in the registry carries
   an explicit disposition under ADR 0020 section 7, including retirements that
   name their replacing responsibility.
6. Correctness of positively selected capabilities — each capability in force
   declares operation, inputs, exclusions, revision/identity, and residual
   interpretation, and each fails closed on unrecognized input.
7. No known source invention — no compiler-authored content carries source
   provenance or the source licence block.
8. No unowned live runtime safety contract — every runtime gate that can block a
   mutation has a live owner and a regression test.
9. Explicit unresolved discovery and adjudication limits — the re-freeze evidence
   states what discovery and adjudication do NOT guarantee.

EXPLICITLY NOT REQUIRED: global deterministic closure; universal discovery
completeness; zero engine-pending clauses; a corpus-wide negative claim of any
kind.

EVIDENCE PROVIDERS for the new conditions (dependencies wired on this bead):
• condition 1 and 7 — eshyra-o9bd.19.2.1 (source-authority repair, incl. the
  decided removal of table:starting-wealth-by-class from the SRD pack).
• condition 4 — eshyra-o9bd.19.14 (transition W14, artifact dispositions for
  sections 5.1-5.6).
• condition 5 — eshyra-o9bd.19.1.15 (durable finding registry); bulk finding
  disposition is sequenced after it exists and is not performed by this bead.
• condition 6 — eshyra-olc5.6 (transition W13, capability-contract
  normalization), which itself depends on eshyra-uiax.
• conditions 3 and 8 remain with the existing verifier and runtime-gate owners.

The freeze manifest and thaw-note POLICY are retained unchanged (transition
design section 5.8): a change to audited pack bytes stays a reviewed event. What
changed is the bar this bead waits on, not the mechanism. eshyra-2zyy still
depends on this bead.
ADR-0020 authority reconciliation applied 2026-09-10 by eshyra-o9bd.19.6.5.
The operative title/description/acceptance criteria supersede contradictory
pre-ADR global-closure language in older notes. Historical notes remain evidence,
not current authority.
