Loads via loadAdventureModuleFromDir; refs resolve against constructed stack. eh54.7.3 must reconcile rulesRef resolution against the shipped SRD pack (kind-prefixed keys). Unblocks eshyra-eh54.7.3.
close_reason: Merged via PR #269. Starter module fixture at packages/core/data/adventure-modules/eshyra_hollow-beneath-emberfall/; shared adventureModuleDirName helper added. Unblocks eshyra-eh54.7.3.

title: Outline The Hollow Beneath Emberfall starter module
description:
Design the small first-party starter module - The Hollow Beneath Emberfall - at outline level before authoring the full fixture.

The outline should identify the adventure premise, starting hook, key locations, NPC roles, likely scenes, objectives, secrets, encounter concepts, reward, and possible endings.
design:
Keep this intentionally small. Avoid turning the starter module into a campaign arc.

Naming (ADR 0012): the setting is Emberfall (campaign template); the module is The Hollow Beneath Emberfall (scenario). "Ember Hollow" is informal shorthand only, not a separate place. EMBERFALL_HOLLOW is the legacy conflated sample.

Possible placeholder concept:
A local disturbance near Emberfall reveals an old sealed place below a mundane landmark. The module should demonstrate how authored secrets, keyed locations, NPC motives, and player divergence are handled by the engine.
acceptance_criteria:
- The module has a title (The Hollow Beneath Emberfall), premise, intended level range, intended party assumptions, and short summary.
- The outline identifies 3 to 5 keyed locations.
- The outline identifies at least one social encounter, one exploration obstacle, and one combat-capable encounter.
- The outline identifies secrets/clues and which scenes or locations can reveal them.
- The outline identifies objectives and ending states.
- The outline explicitly ties the module to the Emberfall setting without expanding Emberfall into a full adventure script.
notes: Outline doc at docs/the-hollow-beneath-emberfall-outline.md; PR #268 open (https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/268). Awaiting review/merge. Mapped to AdventureModule schema for eshyra-eh54.7.2 to author the fixture; blocks eshyra-eh54.7.2.
close_reason: Merged via PR #268. Outline at docs/the-hollow-beneath-emberfall-outline.md, mapped to AdventureModule schema. Unblocks eshyra-eh54.7.2.

title: Build The Hollow Beneath Emberfall hello-world adventure module
description:
Create a small first-party starter adventure module - The Hollow Beneath Emberfall - that serves as Eshyra's gameplay hello-world module.

The Emberfall setting itself should remain setting-scale campaign template content. This work adds a separate scenario-scale module located within or near Emberfall. The module should be intentionally small and useful for testing real play: opening hook, locations, scenes, at least one social beat, exploration, encounter resolution, reward, ending states, persistence, and resume.

Naming glossary (ADR 0012):
- Emberfall - the setting-scale village/region; campaign template. Preserve as setting content.
- The Hollow Beneath Emberfall - this starter adventure module (scenario-scale).
- Ember Hollow - informal shorthand only; not a separate canonical entity. (The ember-hollow label is a project tag, not a third concept.)
- EMBERFALL_HOLLOW - the existing legacy sample that conflates setting and scenario, to be split by this work.
design:
Target size:
- 3 to 5 keyed locations
- 1 to 2 combat-capable encounters
- 1 social encounter
- 1 exploration obstacle
- 3 to 6 secrets or clues
- 1 meaningful choice
- 1 reward
- 2 to 3 possible ending states

The purpose is engine coverage and product shape, not a large polished adventure. The module is immutable authored scenario source; play progress is recorded in the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding (eshyra-eh54.4), not in the module.
acceptance_criteria:
- A small first-party starter adventure module (The Hollow Beneath Emberfall) exists.
- The module is scenario-scale, not a replacement for the Emberfall campaign template/setting.
- The module exercises the adventure module schema, loader, campaign-owned adventure run / module binding and progress, runtime context, and progress persistence.
- The module supports a short playable path suitable for smoke testing.
- The module has enough structure to test hidden secrets, objectives, encounters, rewards, and alternate outcomes.
close_reason: All children complete (.1 outline #268, .2 fixture #269, .3 smoke #270). The Hollow Beneath Emberfall starter module exists as immutable source, loads via the loader, binds to a campaign, feeds the DM runtime context, and round-trips through persistence.

title: Feed adventure module context into DM runtime
description:
Feed bounded adventure module context into the DM runtime.

The DM runtime should receive the relevant module slice for the current situation, not the entire module. The context is derived from BOTH the immutable adventure module source AND the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding (eshyra-eh54.4). The context should help the model run the authored scenario while respecting campaign instance state, hidden-information boundaries, and player-driven divergence. When campaign truth conflicts with module source assumptions, campaign truth wins.
design:
The bounded context is composed from the immutable module source plus the campaign-owned progress object. Suggested bounded context fields:

- current module id/title
- current scene/location candidate
- nearby locations and exits
- relevant NPCs
- active objectives (authored definition + campaign progress)
- encounter/threat options (with campaign outcomes applied)
- unrevealed secrets that may become relevant (filtered by campaign reveal state)
- completed/bypassed module elements (from campaign progress)
- module deviations (from campaign state)

The module should guide the DM, not railroad play. The runtime must prefer campaign truth over source-module assumptions when they conflict.
acceptance_criteria:
- The runtime context builder can include adventure module context when a campaign has an active adventure run / module binding.
- The context slice is composed from both immutable module source and campaign-owned progress, and is bounded and situation-relevant.
- The context includes current or likely scene/location, nearby exits or transitions, relevant NPCs, active objectives, pending encounters/threats, and relevant unrevealed secrets when appropriate for DM-only context.
- The context reflects campaign progress and known deviations, and campaign truth overrides conflicting module assumptions.
- The full module is not dumped into every turn by default.
- Tests or golden fixtures verify the context slice for at least one active-module campaign state.
- Existing campaigns without active modules continue to work.
close_reason: Implemented bounded adventure module context slice (buildAdventureContextSlice + renderAdventureContextSlice), wired into context assembler via optional resolver and threaded through RunTurnDeps. Composes immutable module source + campaign run progress; campaign truth overrides module assumptions. Tests added. PR #265.

title: Add campaign binding and module progress state
description:
Add the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding and mutable module progress to campaign instance state.

A campaign should be able to say which module or modules are active without copying or mutating the authored module source. This is done with a campaign-owned structured object - acceptable names include AdventureRun, CampaignModuleBinding, ActiveAdventureModule, or ModuleProgressState - that references the immutable module by id and records module-specific progress. This object is part of campaign instance state (the fourth layer in ADR 0012); it is NOT a fifth content/state layer and must not be modeled as a separate top-level "adventure instance" peer.

The campaign should persist progress such as visited locations, completed or bypassed scenes, revealed secrets, completed/failed objectives, encounter outcomes, claimed treasure, active clocks/threats, started/completed session ids, status, and explicit deviations from authored assumptions.
design:
The implementation may introduce a structured campaign-owned object (AdventureRun / CampaignModuleBinding / ActiveAdventureModule / ModuleProgressState). It must live inside campaign instance state and reference the immutable module; it must never be written back to the adventure module source pack. It is part of the existing campaign-instance layer, not a new fifth layer.

Suggested shape (campaign-owned, one per active module):
- activeModuleId (reference to the immutable module)
- status
- startedAtSessionId
- completedAtSessionId
- visitedLocations
- completedOrBypassedScenes
- revealedSecrets
- completedOrFailedObjectives
- encounterOutcomes
- claimedTreasure
- activeClocksOrThreats
- moduleDeviations
- notes

A campaign may hold more than one such adventure run / module binding.

Do not require a strictly linear module state machine. A module should support nonlinear exploration, skipped scenes, alternate routes, and emergent deviations. Progress is the only mutable side; the referenced module source remains immutable and re-forkable.
acceptance_criteria:
- Campaign instance state can record one or more campaign-owned adventure runs / module bindings.
- The campaign-owned object references the immutable module id and holds the mutable progress for that campaign; the module source is never mutated.
- The object is explicitly part of campaign instance state, not a separate top-level content/state layer (no "adventure instance" peer layer).
- Module progress can represent active module id, status, started/completed session ids, visited locations, completed or bypassed scenes, revealed secrets, completed/failed objectives, defeated/bypassed encounter outcomes, claimed treasure, active clocks/threats, and module-specific notes.
- Module deviations can be recorded explicitly when play invalidates or alters authored assumptions, as campaign facts rather than edits to the module source.
- Campaign save/resume preserves active adventure runs / module bindings and their progress.
- Tests cover starting a module, updating progress, saving, loading, and verifying the source module remains unchanged.
notes:
Campaign-owned adventure run / module binding + progress implemented: campaign/adventureRun.ts (start/get/list/recordProgress), new adventure_run table (SCHEMA_VERSION 12 + v11_to_v12 migration), exported via internal.ts; 11 tests in test/adventureRun.test.ts + v11->v12 migration test. Save/resume verified via file reopen; module-source-unchanged guard included. PR #264 open: https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/264 . Branch feat/eh54.4-adventure-run-state, worktree .worktrees/eh54.4. Left in_progress so dependents eshyra-eh54.5 and eshyra-eh54.6 stay blocked until merge. Close on merge.
Review fix (commit 56be370): added nested progress-delta validation at the write boundary (empty ids, encounter outcome enum + non-empty encounterId, non-negative integer clock fills, non-empty deviation id/description, non-empty optional session ids). Validation runs before the transaction so rejected deltas write nothing. +3 tests (now 16). Full suite 2239 pass / 0 fail.
close_reason: Campaign-owned adventure run / module binding + progress merged to main via PR #264 (squash, incl. nested progress-delta write-boundary validation review fix). Unblocks eshyra-eh54.5 and eshyra-eh54.6.

title: Add adventure module pack loading and validation
description:
Add loading and validation support for immutable adventure module source packs.

Adventure modules should be loadable as authored content alongside rules packs and campaign templates, but they should not be merged into the SRD rules pack or treated as mutable campaign instance state. This bead validates authored module source structure and references only; it does not load, validate, or model campaign progress (that is campaign instance state - eshyra-eh54.4).
design:
Keep the four layers logically separate (ADR 0012):

- rules pack: mechanical reference material (immutable)
- campaign template pack: setting/world reference material (immutable)
- adventure module pack: authored scenario source material (immutable)
- campaign instance: mutable actual-play state, including the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding that records progress (eshyra-eh54.4)

Loading and validation here applies only to the immutable module source pack. If the existing loader architecture already has a generic content-pack path, extend it in the smallest clean way. If it is rules-pack-specific, avoid forcing module content through SRD importer concepts.
acceptance_criteria:
- The content loading path can load an adventure module source pack or fixture.
- Module-pack validation fails closed on broken references.
- Validation catches at least: missing scene/location ids, missing scene exits, missing referenced NPCs, missing referenced objectives, missing encounter creature refs, missing treasure item refs, and incompatible or unknown setting/template refs where applicable.
- Module records can resolve references to existing rules-pack records without duplicating those records.
- Validation covers authored module structure and references only; it does not validate or require campaign progress state.
- Module loading is covered by focused tests and at least one small fixture.
- Existing rules-pack importer behavior remains unchanged.
notes:
Loader + cross-pack reference validation implemented: adventure/loadModule.ts, adventure/references.ts, exported via internal.ts; 15 tests in test/adventureModuleLoad.test.ts. Establishes the rulesRef '<kind>:<key>' resolution convention. PR #263 open: https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/263 . Branch feat/eh54.3-adventure-module-loader, worktree .worktrees/eh54.3. Left in_progress so dependents eshyra-eh54.4 and eshyra-eh54.7.2 stay blocked until merge. Close on merge.
Review fix (commit 1d03cfa): enforce rulesRequirements.baseVersions against base meta.version; check requiredAddonPackIds against rules.addons only (base pack id no longer satisfies an add-on requirement). +4 tests (now 19), both bug tests verified to fail pre-fix. Full suite 2225 pass / 0 fail.
close_reason: Loader + cross-pack reference validation merged to main via PR #263 (squash, incl. baseVersions + add-on-only requiredAddonPackIds review fixes). Unblocks eshyra-eh54.4 and eshyra-eh54.7.2.

title: Add adventure module schema and typed records
description:
Add an initial adventure module schema and typed record model for immutable authored scenario content.

The schema represents adventure module source only - the authored scenario as written. It must not contain campaign-specific progress fields. Authored elements such as objectives, secrets, scenes, and clocks/threats are modeled as definitions of what is possible in the scenario; whether any of them has been completed, revealed, or advanced is campaign instance state recorded by the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding (eshyra-eh54.4), not by the module record.

The schema should support a small dungeon/adventure module without assuming every module is a linear script. It should support keyed locations, scenes, hooks, NPC roles, encounters, secrets, objectives, treasure, clocks or threats, exits/transitions, and endings.

The first version should be intentionally conservative. The goal is to create a stable destination for starter module content and runtime integration, not to model every possible published adventure format.
design:
Suggested initial concepts (authored source only):

AdventureModule
- id
- title
- summary
- intendedLevels
- intendedPartySize
- rulesetRefs
- settingCompatibility
- startingSituation
- hooks
- locations
- scenes
- npcs
- encounters
- treasure
- secrets
- objectives
- clocksOrThreats
- randomTables
- milestones
- endingStates
- provenance
- license

Important modeling constraint (ADR 0012):

Authored module truth and runtime campaign truth must remain separate. The module record is immutable authored scenario source. For example, the module may define that a sealed shrine lies under the old mill. Whether the players found it, destroyed the mill, bypassed the shrine, or changed the situation is recorded in campaign instance state (the campaign-owned adventure run / module binding), never on the module record. Objectives/secrets/clocks here are definitions of possibilities, not progress flags.
acceptance_criteria:
- A typed adventure module root record exists, representing immutable authored scenario source.
- Module records include stable ids, title/name fields, summary/description fields, tags or categorization where useful, and provenance/license metadata.
- Initial child concepts are represented for hooks, locations, scenes, NPCs, encounters, secrets, objectives, treasure/rewards, clocks/threats, random tables if already supported by existing table concepts, and ending states - all as authored definitions, not progress.
- The schema contains no campaign-specific progress/status fields (no "visited", "revealed", or "completed" flags); progress lives in campaign instance state (eshyra-eh54.4).
- Module records can reference rules-pack content such as creatures, equipment, magic items, rules, actions, and tables without copying mechanical truth into the module.
- Module records can reference compatible campaign-template/setting ids or locations when applicable.
- Validation tests cover at least one small valid module fixture and several broken-reference failures.
- The schema does not mutate or extend SRD rules-pack records to store adventure-specific content.
notes:
Schema + validator implemented: packages/core/src/adventure/{types,validate}.ts, exported via internal.ts, 18 tests in test/adventureModule.test.ts. PR #262 open for review: https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/262 . Branch feat/eh54.2-adventure-module-schema, worktree .worktrees/eh54.2. Left in_progress (not closed) so dependent eshyra-eh54.3 stays blocked until merge. Close on merge.
Review fix (commit 989fb8c): removed root-id colon ban so namespaced module ids (eshyra:hollow-beneath-emberfall) validate; child ids stay colon-free. +1 test (now 19). Full suite 2206 pass / 0 fail.
close_reason: Adventure module schema + validator merged to main via PR #262 (squash, incl. namespaced-root-id review fix). Unblocks eshyra-eh54.3.

title: Define adventure module domain boundaries
description:
Define and record the domain distinction between campaign templates/settings, adventure modules, rules packs, and mutable campaign state.

This should prevent Ember Hollow and other future setting templates from becoming overloaded with adventure-module responsibilities. It should also document how authored module content differs from player-discovered campaign truth and player-created deviations.
design:
Likely file location: docs/adr or the nearest existing architecture-decision location.

Capture examples:

- Rules pack: D&D SRD 5.1.
- Campaign template: Ember Hollow, Karameikos-like regional setting, Forgotten Realms-like broad setting.
- Adventure module: a haunted mine under Ember Hollow, Castle Amber-like keyed scenario, Lost Mine-like starter adventure.
- Campaign instance: the user's actual campaign with its chosen rules, setting, active modules, runtime state, and history.

This is primarily design/documentation, but it should be precise enough to guide schema and runtime work.
acceptance_criteria:
- An ADR or equivalent design note exists describing the four-way distinction: rules pack, campaign template, adventure module, campaign instance.
- The note explicitly states that campaign templates are setting-scale and adventure modules are scenario-scale.
- The note uses Ember Hollow as the example campaign template and a separate Ember Hollow starter adventure as the example module.
- The note states that module source content is immutable and module progress belongs in campaign state.
- The note states that player-driven divergence from the module should be recorded as campaign facts or module deviations, not applied as edits to the source module.
- The note gives examples of setting-scale content and module-scale content.
notes: ADR 0012 written (docs/adr/0012-rules-pack-campaign-template-adventure-module-campaign-instance.md). PR #261 open for review: https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/261 . Branch feat/eh54.1-adventure-module-adr. Left in_progress (not closed) so dependent eshyra-eh54.2 stays blocked until merge. Close on merge.
close_reason: ADR 0012 merged to main via PR #261 (squash). Defines the four-way distinction; unblocks eshyra-eh54.2.

title: Add first-class adventure module support
description:
Problem

Eshyra currently has campaign state persistence and static rules-pack content, but it does not have a first-class representation for pre-written adventure or dungeon module content. That leaves no clear place for starter adventure content to go and forces setting-scale material such as the Emberfall setting to carry responsibilities that belong to a scenario-scale module.

A campaign template should represent a broad reusable world or setting, in the same general scope category as The Grand Duchy of Karameikos, Dragonlance, or Forgotten Realms. A dungeon or adventure module should represent an authored playable scenario, in the same general scope category as Castle Amber or The Lost Mine of Phandelver.

Goal

Introduce adventure modules as first-class immutable authored content, distinct from rules packs, campaign templates, and mutable campaign instance state. A campaign instance should be able to bind to one or more active modules via a campaign-owned adventure run / module binding, expose bounded module context to the DM runtime, persist module progress, and record player-driven deviations without mutating the source module.
design:
Architectural rule - four layers, defined in ADR 0012 (eshyra-eh54.1):

1. Rules packs define mechanical truth (immutable authored/imported source).
2. Campaign templates define reusable worlds/settings (immutable setting-scale source).
3. Adventure modules define authored playable scenarios (immutable scenario-scale source).
4. Campaign instances define actual play history and mutable state.

Adventure modules are immutable authored scenario content. A campaign may contain one or more campaign-owned adventure runs or module bindings that reference modules and record module-specific progress. These adventure runs are part of campaign instance state, not a fifth content/state layer. Do not introduce an "adventure instance" as a peer top-level layer.

Runtime adaptation belongs in campaign instance state as discovered facts, altered facts, completed objectives, revealed secrets, encounter outcomes, and explicit deviations from module assumptions - never written back to the module source.

This epic should avoid third-party adventure conversion until the module schema and runtime destination exist. The frozen starter-content bead can remain blocked until this epic creates somewhere for that content to go.

Naming glossary (see ADR 0012 and eshyra-eh54.7):
- Emberfall - the setting-scale village/region; campaign-template concept.
- The Hollow Beneath Emberfall - the first-party starter adventure module title (scenario-scale).
- Ember Hollow - informal project shorthand only; not a separate canonical entity.
- EMBERFALL_HOLLOW - the existing legacy sample that conflates setting and scenario, to be split by later eh54 work.
acceptance_criteria:
- Eshyra has a documented architecture distinction between the four layers: rules packs, campaign templates/settings, adventure modules, and campaign instances (ADR 0012).
- Adventure module content is represented as immutable authored source material.
- Module progress is represented as mutable campaign instance state via a campaign-owned adventure run / module binding, not as a fifth peer layer.
- A campaign instance can bind to one or more active adventure modules without mutating module source.
- The DM runtime has a path to receive bounded module context without dumping an entire module each turn.
- The Emberfall setting is preserved as setting-scale campaign template content, not forced to become the starter module itself.
- Follow-up work exists for a small first-party starter module (The Hollow Beneath Emberfall) that serves as the gameplay hello-world scenario.

title: Add opt-in session debug logging for prompt and turn diagnostics
description: Add an opt-in session debug logging mode to make live gameplay failures diagnosable without exposing secrets by default. The v0.1.1 native Windows smoke proved the packaged CLI can call the model, but the first turn produced a meta response claiming DM tools such as roll/world_query/mark_scene were unavailable. Debug logging should capture enough sanitized information to diagnose prompt/tool-protocol mismatches, context growth, character-creation state, and session recap behavior. Include per-session debug artifacts under the data root when enabled by an explicit flag/env var, such as ESHYRA_DEBUG_SESSION=1 or a CLI option. Log model call purpose, selected model/profile, prompt section names and approximate sizes, transcript/message counts, tool-protocol mode, available tool names or fenced-tool instructions, campaign/session ids, turn ids, checkpoint ids, and sanitized error/diagnostic events. Prefer redacted/structural logs by default; full prompt capture must be separately gated and clearly marked as sensitive if implemented. Add commands or documentation for locating and packaging debug logs for a bug report. Acceptance: a developer can reproduce a live turn issue and inspect what prompt/tool context was supplied, how large the session context was, and which model calls happened, without leaking API keys or OAuth tokens. Add tests for debug logging enabled/disabled, redaction, and log creation on both successful and failed turns.
close_reason: Implemented opt-in session debug logging (ESHYRA_DEBUG_SESSION). Adapter emits structural per-model-call records (ids, model/profile/auth label, tool protocol, provided-vs-forwarded tools, prompt section sizes, message structure, outcome) on success+failure; full mode adds sanitized content. File sink under <data-root>/debug. Docs + tests added. PR #240.

title: Add model usage tracking for gameplay and maintenance calls
description: Add structured model usage tracking so Eshyra can measure the real cost and context footprint of gameplay. The v0.1.1 native Windows smoke used about 3% of a Claude session for a short deferred-character run with one visible model turn and session close/recap, but it is unclear how much came from turn generation, session recap, prompt/context size, cache misses, or other maintenance calls. Track each model call with purpose, model/profile, provider/auth mode label, input token count, output token count, cache read/write token counts if exposed by the SDK/provider, elapsed time, success/failure, and a safe request/correlation id. Purposes should distinguish at least gameplay turn, session recap, campaign bible extraction, arc rollup, live test, and other maintenance calls. Persist usage in a local diagnostics/telemetry store under the data root and expose a CLI command to summarize usage by campaign/session/model/purpose. Do not log prompts, secrets, raw credentials, or player-private text by default. Acceptance: after a play session, the user can see how many model calls occurred, which purposes consumed tokens, and whether cache usage was observed. Add tests with fake model usage metadata and ensure failures are recorded without leaking secrets.
close_reason: Model usage tracking with best-effort sink complete. PR #243 open for review.

title: Replace brittle character creation prompts with guided session-zero flow
description: Native Windows v0.1.1 smoke showed character creation is too brittle for real use. The revision loop loses prior answers, validation cascades into nonsensical messages such as 'level-1 hit point maximum must be -4', point-buy errors are reported only after the whole draft is entered, and users must manually derive level-1 HP. Rework character creation into a guided session-zero flow that preserves draft state between revisions, validates fields incrementally, computes derived values such as HP from class hit die + Constitution modifier, accepts common SRD display names where records exist, and produces actionable validation messages. Do not block /defer. title: Repair SRD magic-item boundaries and embedded content
description:
Problem

Magic-item coverage improved substantially, but the latest audit found boundary and embedded-content failures.

Known high-confidence failures

- Figurine of Wondrous Power is present in the SRD but missing as magic-item:figurine-of-wondrous-power.
- magic-item:feather-token swallows the Figurine of Wondrous Power heading, rarity line, figurine variants, and Giant Fly stat block.
- Several magic-item tables are likely flattened into descriptions rather than emitted or structured.
- Magic items may contain embedded stat blocks, option tables, dice-result tables, command words, variants, and child entities that need explicit accounting.

Task

Repair magic-item boundary parsing and structured child content.

Implementation guidance

- Build on the bounded source span bead.
- Build on the document-wide table and stat-block inventory beads where available.
- Every magic item heading in the source should map to exactly one magic-item record unless intentionally ignored with reason.
- Magic-item descriptions should not swallow following magic-item headings.
- Embedded tables should be emitted as table records or structured child data.
- Embedded stat blocks should be linked to the stat-block representation chosen by the stat-block bead.
- Preserve source text and provenance for variants and subentries.

Regression cases

Add tests for:

- magic-item:feather-token does not include Figurine of Wondrous Power.
- magic-item:figurine-of-wondrous-power exists and has correct source span.
- Giant Fly is accounted for structurally.
- At least one magic-item option table is accounted for.
- At least one magic-item dice-result table is accounted for.
- Deck of Many Things accounts for Avatar of Death according to the stat-block modeling decision.

Acceptance criteria

- All source magic item headings are accounted for.
- Known boundary bleed is fixed.
- Magic-item tables and embedded stat blocks are not silently flattened without coverage mappings.
- Existing valid magic-item ids remain stable where possible.
notes: Implemented in worktree branch agent/eshyra-4a7.8-magic-item-boundaries. Added Figurine of Wondrous Power with 9 structured variants and Giant Fly link; bounded Feather Token; captured Avatar of Death traits/actions; emitted all 27 remaining Magic Items table structures with reviewed deterministic reconstruction. Source coverage known-gap eshyra-4a7.8: 27 -> 0. Generated semantic diff: 28 records added, 0 removed, only existing record changed is stat-block:avatar-of-death. Verification: npm run format/check/typecheck/test (1587 passed, 19 documented skips) and npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack pass.
close_reason: Magic-item boundaries, embedded stat blocks, variants, and all source table structures are now deterministically emitted and verified.

title: Complete SRD creature and NPC stat-block records
description:
Problem

Creature records are currently too skeletal for actual SRD-backed play. The audit found that creature records generally capture basic header stats but omit major stat-block content.

Example

creature:aboleth captures AC, HP, speed, ability scores, and CR, but the SRD stat block also contains saving throws, skills, senses, languages, Amphibious, Mucous Cloud, Probing Telepathy, Multiattack, Tentacle, Tail, Enslave, and Legendary Actions.

Task

Complete creature and NPC stat-block parsing so creature-like records preserve all structured source sections needed for play.

Expected fields or equivalent schema

- armor class,
- hit points,
- speed,
- ability scores,
- saving throws,
- skills,
- damage vulnerabilities,
- damage resistances,
- damage immunities,
- condition immunities,
- senses,
- languages,
- challenge rating,
- traits,
- actions,
- reactions,
- legendary actions,
- lair actions where present,
- regional effects where present,
- spellcasting blocks where present,
- variant notes where present.

Implementation guidance

- Use source-backed tests before changing parser logic.
- Preserve text where full semantic decomposition is not yet practical, but place it in the correct structured section.
- Do not discard action names, recharge text, attack bonuses, damage expressions, save DCs, or usage limitations.
- NPCs should follow the same stat-block completeness rules unless there is a documented reason for a separate schema.

Regression cases

Include tests for varied stat blocks:

- Aboleth: traits, actions, legendary actions.
- Dragon or similar complex creature: legendary/lair/regional content if present in SRD.
- Spellcasting creature/NPC.
- Creature with immunities/resistances.
- Embedded stat block from the document-wide stat-block bead.

Acceptance criteria

- Creature-like records contain all stat-block sections present in source.
- No major stat-block section remains only in flattened prose.
- Pack verification and importer tests cover representative complex stat blocks.

title: Extract and account for SRD stat blocks document-wide
description:

- Detect stat-block-shaped content across the full SRD, not only the monster/NPC appendix.
- Decide and document whether embedded stat blocks are emitted as normal creature records, emitted as a distinct embedded-stat-block kind, or stored as structured child data on the containing record.
- Whatever model is chosen, the coverage gate must account for the source stat block.
- Preserve source provenance linking embedded stat blocks to both their own source span and containing source item when applicable.
- Do not duplicate content in uncontrolled prose and structured records without clear ownership.

Regression cases

- Avatar of Death,

title: Extract and account for every SRD table document-wide
description:
Problem

The latest audit found that table coverage is still incomplete. The pack has more table records than before, but many SRD tables are still missing or flattened into prose.

High-confidence missing or insufficiently represented examples

- Dragonborn Draconic Ancestry table, p. 5.
- The 12 class progression tables.
- Druid Circle Spells tables.
- Oath of Devotion Spells table.
- Sorcerer Creating Spell Slots table.
- Draconic Bloodline Draconic Ancestry table.
- Apparatus of the Crab Levers table.
- Bag of Beans tables.
- Bag of Tricks table.
- Carpet of Flying table.
- Feather Token table.
- Horn of Valhalla table.
- Iron Flask table.
- Robe of Useful Items table.
- Wand of Wonder table.
- Sentient magic item property tables.
- Other magic-item option tables with dice rows or named choices.

Task

Make table extraction document-wide and require every source table to be accounted for.

Implementation guidance

- Use PDF text and coordinate artifacts where needed.
- Detect table captions, heading-adjacent tables, repeated column-header patterns, and dice-result tables.
- Do not limit table extraction to one chapter or to previously known tables.
- Preserve source row order, typography, and page provenance.
- For nested/grouped tables, use the representation already chosen for the importer, or document and test the chosen representation if not yet formalized.
- Some tables may ultimately become structured child data rather than top-level table records. That is acceptable if the coverage gate records the mapping.

Tests

Add regression tests for at least:

- Dragonborn Draconic Ancestry.
- One class progression table.
- One subclass spell table.
- Sorcerer Creating Spell Slots.
- One magic-item dice-result table.
- One magic-item option/property table.

Acceptance criteria

- Document-wide source table inventory exists.
- Every detected table is emitted, mapped to structured child data, or explicitly ignored.

- Table parsing fails closed when expected row counts or headers change.

Close this bead when the PR merges.

title: Refactor SRD parsers to consume bounded source spans
description:
Problem

Multiple audit findings point to parser boundary failures:

- Every subclass record description appears to swallow its subclass feature headings and feature bodies.
- magic-item:feather-token swallows the following Figurine of Wondrous Power entry.
- Flattened descriptions are masking places where structured records or child objects should exist.

These are not isolated content mistakes; they indicate that parsers are consuming source spans with brittle stop conditions.

Depends on

This should build on the source inventory/coverage gate bead if possible. The coverage gate should expose the incorrect spans and provide regression cases.

Task

Refactor SRD importer parsing so major record parsers consume explicitly bounded source spans derived from the source structure inventory or equivalent deterministic heading map.

Parser spans should be explicit for at least:

- classes,
- subclasses,
- class features,
- subclass features,
- magic items,
- rules sections,
- tables,
- stat blocks.

Implementation guidance

- Avoid parser logic that reads until a loose text pattern happens to match.
- Prefer start/end offsets, page ranges, or source item boundaries that are deterministic.
- A subclass record description should contain only the subclass overview text, not the subclass feature records.
- A magic-item record should stop before the next magic-item heading.
- Feature records should own feature text once, not duplicate it through parent descriptions.
- Preserve existing record ids unless a source item was genuinely missing.

Regression cases

Add tests for:

- subclass:champion does not include Improved Critical or later Champion feature bodies in its subclass description.
- subclass:circle-of-the-land does not include Natural Recovery or later Circle of the Land feature bodies in its subclass description.
- magic-item:feather-token does not include the Figurine of Wondrous Power heading or figurine variants.
- Figurine of Wondrous Power has its own bounded source span, even if actual record emission is completed in the magic-item bead.

Acceptance criteria

- Major record parsers operate on explicit source spans.
- Known subclass and magic-item boundary bleed cases are fixed or fail visibly in tests.
- No existing valid records lose source-backed content.
- Pack generation remains deterministic.
notes: Fixed via PR #194 (branch work/eshyra-4a7.2). parseSubclasses + parseMagicItems now bound bodies at deterministic font-tier heading boundaries (gated on multi-tier slice). Eliminated all 12 swallowed-feature-heading audit findings; Feather Token no longer swallows Figurine of Wondrous Power / Giant Fly. 13 generated records changed (12 subclass descriptions + feather-token), 0 added/removed. verify:dnd5e-srd-pack matches; source-coverage artifacts unchanged (Figurine stays known-gap for 4a7.8). Awaiting review.

title: Add SRD source inventory and coverage gate
description:
Problem

The importer can currently pass tests while the source PDF still contains untracked structured content. The latest audit found missing or flattened source structures even though there are no open importer issues.

Examples from the latest audit

- Figurine of Wondrous Power appears in the SRD but is not emitted as magic-item:figurine-of-wondrous-power.
- Avatar of Death and Giant Fly stat blocks appear outside the monster appendix but are not emitted as creature-like records.
- Many named tables are missing as table records or structured child data.
- Class progression tables are not represented.
- Dragonborn Draconic Ancestry table is not represented.
- Subclass descriptions swallow subclass feature text while separate feature records also exist.

Task

Create a deterministic SRD source inventory and coverage gate.

The inventory should scan the vendored SRD PDF text/coordinate artifacts and identify source structures that require accounting:

- major section headings,
- ancestry headings,
- class headings,
- subclass headings,
- feature headings,
- spell headings,
- magic item headings,
- creature/NPC/stat-block headings,
- table captions or table-shaped structures,
- condition headings,
- action headings,
- feat headings,
- trap, disease, poison, and hazard headings,
- embedded stat blocks outside the monster appendix.

For every inventoried source item, the coverage gate should require exactly one of:

1. emitted as a top-level record,
2. emitted as structured child data on a top-level record,
3. intentionally ignored with a stable reason.

Implementation guidance

- Prefer a machine-readable inventory artifact, for example JSON, committed only if it is deterministic and useful for review.
- Include source page, source heading text, inferred kind, and matching record id or ignore reason.
- The coverage check should fail closed when a new source item appears without a mapping.
- Do not rely on fuzzy prose containment as sufficient coverage for structured tables/stat blocks/options.
- It is acceptable to start with conservative heuristics and an explicit allowlist, as long as unaccounted source items fail the check.
- The output should be reviewer-friendly enough to explain why a source item was or was not expected to become a record.

Tests

Add focused tests proving that the inventory detects at least:

- Figurine of Wondrous Power,
- Avatar of Death,
- Giant Fly,
- Dragonborn Draconic Ancestry table,
- at least one class progression table,
- at least one subclass feature heading,
- at least one magic-item option table.

Acceptance criteria

- A new check exists that compares source inventory to generated records.
- The check fails for unaccounted source structures.
- Existing pack verification still passes.
- The current known gaps are visible in the new inventory/coverage output rather than hidden in passing tests.
- No manual content is inserted into records to satisfy the check.
design:
ARCHITECTURE (from 2026-06-11 empirical font-height probe of SRD_CC_v5.1.pdf via extractPdfText):

Font-height tier map (PageText.lineHeights, already exposed by extract.ts):
- h=25.9 chapter titles (25 lines)
- h=18.0 section titles (105)
- h=13.9 subsection headings incl. subclass names (307)
- h=12.0 RECORD-LEAF headings (1398): spell names (e.g. Acid Arrow p114), magic items (Feather Token p221, Figurine of Wondrous Power p221, Bag of Beans p209, Wand of Wonder p249), creatures (Aboleth p261), EMBEDDED STAT BLOCKS (Avatar of Death p218, Giant Fly p222), TABLE CAPTIONS (Draconic Ancestry p5+p44, The Barbarian p8), subclass features (Improved Critical p25)
- h=10.8 sidebar/callout headings (376; e.g. Sacred Plants and Wood p22, Equipment Packs p70) — parseClassCallouts territory
- h=10.0 page-1/2 legal front matter only (11)
- h=9.8 body prose
- h=8.9 TABLE CELLS/HEADERS (2489; e.g. 'd10 Damage Type Gem' rows in Ring of Resistance p237, progression rows p8)

Detectors:
1. Inventory item = line with h>=10.5 (~2211 items). Tier from height. Merge adjacent same-tier wrapped heading lines (extractor only merges h>=14).
2. Caption-less embedded table = maximal run of h~8.9 lines; attach to nearest preceding leaf heading.
3. Structural classification: heading followed by /^(Tiny|Small|Medium|Large|Huge|Gargantuan) .+,/ body line => stat-block; heading followed by 8.9-run => table-caption; else plain heading.
4. inferredKind from containing chapter via existing sections.ts anchors.

Coverage statuses per item: record:<key> | child-of:<key> | ignored:<reasonCode> | known-gap:<beadId>. Anything unmatched => UNACCOUNTED => gate throws (fail closed). Matching: (a) normalized-name auto-match against emitted records, (b) rule-based ignore predicates with stable reason codes (NOT giant per-item lists; e.g. spell-list headers, legal headings, TOC), (c) known-gap rules referencing epic children (4a7.3 tables, 4a7.4 stat blocks, 4a7.6 progression, 4a7.7 ancestry, 4a7.8 figurine).

FILE MAP:
- Create packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/sourceInventory.ts — pure PageText[] -> SourceInventoryItem[]
- Create packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/sourceInventoryCoverage.ts — (inventory, records) -> coverage report + SourceInventoryCoverageError
- Modify index.ts runImporter — build inventory + coverage post-parse, throw on UNACCOUNTED, write source-inventory.json + source-coverage.json artifacts
- Modify verify-dnd5e-srd-pack/cli.ts — regenerate-and-diff the new artifacts
- Modify create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/cli.ts — include artifacts in bundle reports
- Artifact location: pack dir alongside manifest.json IF pack loader tolerates extra files, else packages/core/data/srd-source-inventory/ (decide at impl; check loadRulesPack strictness)
- Tests: packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/sourceInventory.test.ts + sourceInventoryCoverage.test.ts (fixture PageText), packages/core/test/srdSourceInventoryArtifact.test.ts (committed-artifact sentinels)

Sentinel assertions (committed artifact): Figurine of Wondrous Power => known-gap:eshyra-4a7.8; Avatar of Death + Giant Fly => known-gap:eshyra-4a7.4 (stat-block classified); Draconic Ancestry p5 => table-caption, known-gap:eshyra-4a7.7; The Barbarian p8 => table-caption, known-gap:eshyra-4a7.6; Improved Critical => record:feature:improved-critical; Ring of Resistance embedded d10 table => known-gap:eshyra-4a7.3.

INTEGRATION: reports may flow through srdAudit finding category (new 'unaccounted-source-structure') for bundle visibility, but the HARD gate lives in runImporter. sourceCoverage.ts name-list layer stays (regression net) — this is the structural superset.
notes: IMPORTANT integration constraint (added by Claude review 2026-06-11): this is NOT greenfield. The repo already has a two-layer audit mechanism: packages/core/src/rules/srdAudit.ts implements the audit finding categories (swallowed-feature-heading, class-proficiency-bleed, missing-coverage) and packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/sourceCoverage.ts is the curated SOURCE-truth layer (name lists independent of what the importer emits; see its header comment for the lifecycle/design rationale). The new PDF-derived structural inventory must EXTEND or REPLACE this machinery deliberately — do not build a parallel third coverage system. Natural shape: the inventory becomes a generated source-truth artifact that supersedes/feeds the hand-curated gap lists in sourceCoverage.ts, and the coverage gate reports through the existing srdAudit finding pipeline (new finding category is fine). The current 13 structure-audit findings (12 subclass swallowed-feature + 1 druid proficiency-bleed) are existing srdAudit output, not new discoveries — keep them reproducible. Follow docs/importer-fix-protocol.md including its hard-stop wording.

title: Make SRD importer self-auditing against source PDF
description:
Problem

The SRD importer has no open tracked issues, but the latest manual audit shows the pack is not yet complete or accurately bounded against the source PDF. The importer has made real progress, but remaining failures are now systemic rather than isolated row omissions.

Observed audit facts

- The current generated pack has about 1,650 records.
- verify:dnd5e-srd-pack, check, typecheck, and tests pass.
- The audit bundle metadata still reported srdStructureAudit.hasFindings: true.
- The pack captures broad SRD content, but much of it is flattened into descriptions rather than represented as usable structured records.
- Some source boundaries are still wrong: subclass records swallow feature text, and Feather Token swallows Figurine of Wondrous Power.
- Some document-scoped structures are missed: embedded stat blocks such as Avatar of Death and Giant Fly are not emitted as creature-like records.
- Creature records are skeletal compared with SRD stat blocks.
- Class records omit class skill choices, tool proficiencies, starting equipment options, spellcasting progression, and class progression tables.
- Many source tables are missing as table records or structured child data.

Goal

Make the SRD importer self-auditing against the source PDF so future audits do not rely on manual archaeology. Every source heading, table, stat block, and structured rules object in the SRD should be accounted for as one of:

1. an emitted top-level record,
2. structured child data on an emitted record,
3. an intentionally ignored source item with an explicit reason.

Non-goals

- Do not hand-author canonical SRD pack content.
- Do not weaken current pack verification or regression tests.
- Do not claim source coverage based only on flattened prose when the source content is structured and needed for play.
- Do not opportunistically rewrite unrelated importer code without failing tests or audit findings motivating the change.

Agent instructions

Work in red/green slices. For every parser or schema fix, add or update source-backed tests first. Prefer deterministic extraction from the vendored PDF text/coordinate artifacts. Preserve source provenance and fail closed when expected source structures disappear or parse ambiguously.

Relevant areas to inspect

- packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1
- generated SRD pack records.json
- vendored SRD PDF and extracted pdf-text/page artifacts
- current SRD structure audit reports
- pack verification tests and importer pipeline tests

Completion criteria

- The child beads under this epic are complete.
- The importer has a deterministic source-structure coverage gate.
- Known audit findings are either fixed or represented as explicit expected gaps with rationale.
- A fresh audit bundle no longer reports untracked source content that should have records.
notes: Claude independent review 2026-06-11: epic verified against the generated pack and audit bundle; all headline claims confirmed (feather-token swallows Figurine of Wondrous Power + Giant Fly stat block; no figurine/avatar-of-death/giant-fly records; creature:aboleth has only header stats — no saves/skills/senses/traits/actions/legendary actions; class:barbarian lacks skills/tools/equipment/progression; 29 table records exist but no class progression or draconic-ancestry tables; all 12 subclasses swallow feature bodies per srd-structure-audit). Dependency edges added 2026-06-11 to encode execution order: 4a7.1 gates 2/3/4; 4a7.5 needs 4; 4a7.6 needs 2+3; 4a7.7 needs 3; 4a7.8 needs 2+3+4; 4a7.9 needs all. Recommended execution order: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 (or 8 before 5-7 — any topological order works). NOTE: 4a7.3 (document-wide tables) and 4a7.5 (full stat blocks for 317 creatures) are large; expect them to be split into sub-slices (.3a/.3b style or child beads) during execution rather than landing as single PRs. All children must follow docs/importer-fix-protocol.md.

title: Strengthen SRD audit command to catch boundary and coverage failures
description:

title: Fix SRD class and subclass feature boundary parsing
description:
Problem
The SRD importer still merges adjacent class and subclass features or allows class setup/proficiency prose to bleed into feature records.

Evidence from the 2026-06-07 audit
Affected examples include:
- feature:bard:spellcasting
- feature:cleric:spellcasting
- feature:druid:druidic
- feature:monk:martial-arts
- feature:paladin:divine-sense
- feature:ranger:favored-enemy
- feature:warlock:otherworldly-patron
- feature:wizard:cantrips
- feature:life-domain:bonus-proficiency
- feature:hunter:multiattack
- feature:circle-of-the-land:natural-recovery

Specific failures
- Several feature records include class proficiency blocks such as Weapons, Tools, Saving Throws, and Skills.
- Life Domain Bonus Proficiency swallowed Disciple of Life and Channel Divinity: Preserve Life.
- Hunter Multiattack swallowed Superior Hunter's Defense.
- Circle of the Land Natural Recovery swallowed Circle Spells and table content.
- Circle of the Land appears to be missing later features such as Land's Stride, Nature's Ward, and Nature's Sanctuary.

Required behavior
- Each class/subclass feature record should correspond to one source feature heading or intentionally modeled repeated feature.
- Adjacent feature headings must terminate the previous feature body.
- Class setup/proficiency blocks must not be emitted as feature body content.
- Subclass feature extraction must not silently skip later subclass features.

IMPORTER SAFETY
Importer safety: follow docs/importer-fix-protocol.md. Do not weaken regression tests or audit expectations to match current generated output; fix parser/extractor behavior or document source-backed evidence that the expectation was wrong.

title: Nesting-aware parseRules rewrite for SRD core-rules rule coverage

Land behind fixtures + a reviewed coverage baseline like the creature/magic-item name sets. See docs/audits/srd-5.1-rules-section-coverage.md (loreweaver-ars), root causes 1 and 4.

title: Reconcile SRD table parser scope with canonical output
description:
﻿Reconcile D&D SRD 5.1 table parser documentation, tests, and canonical generated output.

Problem:
The importer README documents table coverage beyond Difficulty Classes, including XP Thresholds by Character Level and treasure tables, but the committed canonical pack contains only one table record: table:difficulty-classes. This is either an importer coverage bug or stale documentation/scope.

Scope:
- Review the vendored SRD 5.1 PDF table content against the documented table parser scope.
- Decide based on existing ADR/importer intent whether XP thresholds and treasure tables should be imported as table records.
- If they are in scope, fix the table parser and regenerate the canonical pack.
- If they are out of scope, update README/tests/baselines to stop claiming they are covered.
- Prefer importing documented in-scope tables rather than silently narrowing scope.

Acceptance criteria:
- README table coverage accurately matches the committed canonical pack.
- table parser tests cover every table family claimed as supported.
- Canonical records include all table records claimed by the README.
- Add reviewed table count/key baselines so table coverage cannot silently collapse.
- npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack exits 0.
- npm run audit:rules-pack -- packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1 reports no new suspicious findings.
- npm run check, npm run typecheck, and npm test pass.
- Do not change source vendoring policy.
- Do not add unrelated parser fixes.
close_reason: Resolved as stale documentation: SRD 5.1 PDF contains only the Difficulty Classes reference table (p77); XP-threshold and treasure tables are non-SRD content absent from the source. README/test-header docs corrected, table key/name regression baseline added. verify:dnd5e-srd-pack=0, audit suspicious=0, check/typecheck/test pass.

Scope:

- Include armor, shields, weapons, and adventuring/equipment table rows that the current parser is intended to cover.
- Correct Padded armor fields, including stealth disadvantage and weight.
- Preserve deterministic keys and source provenance.
- Regenerate the canonical D&D SRD 5.1 pack after parser fixes.

Acceptance criteria:
- equipment:padded matches the SRD armor table, including stealth disadvantage and weight.
- Armor table rows are imported or explicitly documented as intentionally out of scope.
- Weapons table rows are imported or explicitly documented as intentionally out of scope.
- Adventuring gear/tool/equipment rows are imported or explicitly documented as intentionally out of scope.
- Add exact or reviewed equipment baseline tests that fail if major equipment categories collapse back to a single record.

title: Fix final SRD spell-section boundary contamination
description:
﻿Fix D&D SRD 5.1 spell parser boundary contamination found during the final pack accuracy audit.

Problem:
The committed canonical pack contains spell records whose descriptions include text from adjacent or non-spell sections:
- spell:word-of-recall has stray text contamination around the ending, including text associated with Wish / neighboring spell content.
- spell:zone-of-truth absorbs the following Traps section after the spell should end.

This means the spell parser can have correct spell counts while still corrupting the final spell bodies.

Scope:
- Fix spell-section slicing / spell body termination for the end of the Spell Descriptions section.
- Ensure the final spell, Zone of Truth, ends at the true spell text boundary and does not include Traps content.
- Ensure Word of Recall body text matches the vendored SRD 5.1 PDF and is not contaminated by neighboring spell content.
- Regenerate the canonical D&D SRD 5.1 pack after parser fixes.
- Keep verify:dnd5e-srd-pack strict and green.

Acceptance criteria:
- spell:word-of-recall description is supported by the vendored SRD 5.1 PDF and contains no neighboring-spell contamination.
- spell:zone-of-truth description ends at the spell text and does not contain Traps section content.
- Add targeted regression tests for both Word of Recall and Zone of Truth.
- npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack exits 0.
- npm run audit:rules-pack -- packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1 reports no new suspicious findings.
- npm run check, npm run typecheck, and npm test pass.
- Do not change source vendoring policy.
- Do not add exact creature name work; that is already covered by the reviewed creature baseline.
close_reason: Fixed in PR #143: added Traps to spellDescriptions end anchor (Zone of Truth boundary) and added gutter-straggler reassignment in extract.ts (Word of Recall 'wish' contamination). Pack regenerated; verify/audit/check/typecheck/test all green; regression tests added.

title: Fail closed when SRD ancestry extraction under-extracts races
description:
## Problem

The D&D SRD 5.1 importer slices the Races section and then calls parseAncestries. The section anchor failure path is fail-closed, but parseAncestries itself can still return an empty or partial result if the expected race/subrace boundaries are not found inside an otherwise valid slice.

This undermines the deterministic importer goal: a PDF extraction/layout drift could produce a valid-looking rules pack with missing ancestry records.

## Relevant files

- packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/index.ts
- packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseAncestries.ts
- packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseAncestries.test.ts or equivalent importer tests

## Requirements

- Add explicit ancestry coverage validation for the SRD 5.1 corpus.
- Fail closed when the parsed ancestry set is empty or missing expected parent/subrace records.
- Include useful diagnostics listing missing expected names.
- Keep section-anchor failures distinct from parser-coverage failures.
- Ensure the failure happens before writing manifest.json / records.json.

## Expected SRD 5.1 coverage

Parent races:
- Dragonborn
- Dwarf
- Elf
- Gnome
- Half-Elf
- Half-Orc
- Halfling
- Human
- Tiefling

Subraces:
- Hill Dwarf
- Mountain Dwarf
- High Elf
- Wood Elf
- Dark Elf (Drow)
- Lightfoot
- Stout
- Forest Gnome
- Rock Gnome

## Acceptance criteria

- A test fixture with a valid races slice but no recognized race headings causes runImporter or the ancestry parsing path to throw.
- A fixture missing one expected ancestry name throws and names the missing record.
- The happy-path SRD import still emits the expected ancestry count.
- Error messages are deterministic and suitable for CI logs.
close_reason: Implemented exact SRD 5.1 ancestry coverage validation before pack writes, with deterministic missing-name diagnostics and no/partial Races fixture coverage; verification passed: npm run typecheck, touched-file Biome CI, npm run test.

comments.text: Worktree baseline: npm install -> succeeded; npm run typecheck -> passed; npx vitest run packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseAncestries.test.ts packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/pipeline.test.ts -> passed (47 tests).

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts
comments.text: Debugging evidence: parseAncestries returns [] when no known race/subrace headings are found, and runImporter currently passes the resulting ancestries directly to buildPack without a validateAncestryCoverage guard. Working references are validateCreatureCoverage/validateClassCoverage/validateSubclassCoverage/validateFeatureCoverage in index.ts, which run after parsing and before writePackToDirectory. Root cause hypothesis: a valid Races slice can under-extract because ancestry coverage is not validated by expected name set before emit.

title: Fix demo rerun session id collision after PR rebase
description: During rebase of PR 25 onto origin/main, npm run test failed in packages/cli/test/play.test.ts: runDemo > reuses an existing demo campaign on a later run. Symptom: SessionError session 'session-2' already exists in campaign 'campaign-1'. Investigate whether the rebase integration introduced or exposed a demo rerun id-generation bug, then fix with verification. Parent context: loreweaver-d4r.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause is recorded; an automated test covers demo rerun without duplicate session ids; npm run typecheck and npm run test pass after the fix.
notes:
Evidence: after rebasing PR 25 onto origin/main, npm run test fails reproducibly in packages/cli/test/play.test.ts runDemo > reuses an existing demo campaign on a later run. Stack points to packages/cli/src/play.ts:149 createDemoCampaign, then core startSession rejects duplicate session 'session-2' in campaign 'campaign-1'. Recent change on main added runDemo and a test using baseDeps() twice; baseDeps resets deterministic IDs for each call, so a second demo run can generate IDs already used by the first run.
Pattern analysis: runPlay/runDemo expect PlayDeps.nextId to produce unique ids within the target DB. Production buildPlayDeps uses timestamp plus randomness, but packages/cli/test/play.test.ts baseDeps starts ids at 0 for each call. The failing demo rerun test uses a new baseDeps against the same in-memory DB, so the second run can reuse closed-session ids from the first run. Working pattern is to keep one ID source for multiple invocations against the same DB, or otherwise seed a unique offset.
Hypothesis: the implementation path is valid; the failing test fixture violates the nextId uniqueness contract by resetting the deterministic ID generator between demo runs against the same DB. Minimal test: reuse the same PlayDeps/id source for both runDemo calls while swapping the IO object for the second run. Expected result: second run takes the existing-campaign branch and starts a unique later session.
Result: changed packages/cli/test/play.test.ts demo rerun test to reuse the same PlayDeps/id source while swapping only IO for the second run. Targeted verification npm run test -- packages/cli/test/play.test.ts passed with 12 tests. Full verification npm run typecheck passed; npm run test passed with 35 files passed / 1 skipped and 223 tests passed / 1 skipped.
close_reason: Root cause was a test fixture resetting deterministic IDs across two demo runs against one DB; fixed the fixture to reuse the same ID source. Verification: npm run typecheck and npm run test passed.

title: E8 Dolt checkpoint/history/branching subsystem
description:
Goal: the Dolt-backed checkpoint / history / branching subsystem. SQLite stays the
authoritative live operational store; this subsystem makes Dolt the authoritative
checkpoint/history/branching store, OFF the per-turn hot path.

MVP must include (all in scope, none deferred):
- Deterministic SQLite -> Dolt checkpoint export (same SQLite state => identical bytes).
- A Dolt commit per meaningful checkpoint (session close; arc roll-up).
- List checkpoints.
- Restore a checkpoint into a NEW SQLite working copy.
- Fork a campaign from a checkpoint into a NEW Dolt branch (+ materialized SQLite copy).
- Explicit, verified separation from the beads Dolt storage / remotes / ref-namespace.

Hard constraints: Dolt is NEVER invoked in the per-turn write path; SQLite is the
single live truth (Dolt trails to last checkpoint, like a git working tree vs last
commit); there are NOT two independent live truths.

User-visible outcome: a player can checkpoint a campaign, list past checkpoints,
restore an old checkpoint into a fresh working copy, and fork a campaign timeline.
design:
## Architecture

Dolt is invoked via the `dolt` CLI ONLY at checkpoint time (no long-running
`dolt sql-server`, no per-turn calls) — this is what keeps it off the hot path and
avoids server-lifecycle complexity. Each campaign has its own Dolt repo directory,
created/located independently of the beads Dolt repo.

A `CheckpointStore` in core composes three lower units:
1. `serialize` — pure SQLite -> canonical snapshot (deterministic, no Dolt, offline-testable).
2. `doltRepo` — thin wrapper over the `dolt` CLI for one repo dir (the ONLY file that shells to `dolt`).
3. `separation` — guard proving the Loreweaver Dolt location/remote/ref-namespace is disjoint from beads.

## Determinism contract

`serialize(db)` reads every user table (excludes sqlite internal + any
`sqlite_%`), and emits a single canonical `snapshot.sql` string:
- tables ordered by name (ASCII);
- columns in `PRAGMA table_info` ordinal order;
- rows ordered by full-row tuple (stable total order);
- fixed value formatting (NULL as `NULL`, integers bare, text single-quoted with
  `''` escaping, blobs as `X'..'`).
Same SQLite content => byte-identical string (acceptance #8). This artifact is what
gets loaded into Dolt and committed, so `dolt_diff`/`AS OF` are meaningful.

## File map

- `packages/core/src/persistence/checkpoint/separation.ts` — `assertSeparateFromBeads(doltDir, beadsDir)`.
- `packages/core/src/persistence/checkpoint/serialize.ts` — `serializeCampaign(db): string`.
- `packages/core/src/persistence/checkpoint/doltRepo.ts` — `DoltRepo` (init, applySnapshot, commit, log, branch, checkoutInto).
- `packages/core/src/persistence/checkpoint/store.ts` — `CheckpointStore` (checkpoint, list, restoreToNewWorkingCopy, forkFromCheckpoint).
- `packages/core/src/index.ts` — barrel exports.
- `packages/core/test/checkpoint.*.test.ts` — one suite per unit.

## Hot-path / separation constraints

- `CheckpointStore` is invoked only by E6 session-close and E4 arc roll-up — never
  from `mutate_state` / the turn loop. This is a design rule enforced by where the
  call sites are (not by code in this epic).
- SQLite remains single live truth; restore/fork always materialize a NEW `.db`
  working copy and never mutate the live campaign DB in place.
- `separation` rejects any Dolt dir that is inside, equal to, or shares a remote
  URL / `refs/dolt/*` namespace with the beads Dolt repo.

## Test gating

`serialize` and `separation` are pure and run offline (no Dolt). `doltRepo` and
`CheckpointStore` suites use `describe.skipIf(!doltAvailable)` (probe `dolt version`)
so CI without the `dolt` binary stays green while the capability is proven where
`dolt` exists.

## Tradeoffs

The serializer is the deterministic export-mapping component Dolt-only would avoid;
accepted because it keeps the per-turn path embedded/zero-ops and yields a
diffable, byte-stable history at session granularity (the campaign's natural
versioning unit).
acceptance_criteria: 1. serializeCampaign is deterministic (same SQLite => byte-identical snapshot), proven offline. 2. A checkpoint creates a dolt commit; list returns it. 3. Restore materializes a NEW SQLite working copy round-trip-identical to the source. 4. Fork creates a NEW dolt branch + isolated SQLite copy; changes in fork do not affect origin. 5. Separation guard rejects any Dolt dir nested in/equal to/sharing remote or refs with the beads Dolt repo. 6. No checkpoint code path is reachable from the per-turn loop. All E8 child tasks closed.
notes: SYNTHESIS UPDATE 2026-05-17: Checkpoint/restore/fork remains a core text-first product differentiator and future demo surface. Keep Dolt checkpointing separate from both the per-turn path and beads storage; this supports restore/fork/history without early VTT/native-mobile scope.

title: E3 Game-state subsystem + mutate_state tool
description: Canonical, exact, provenance-annotated game state - the trust anchor for the whole system. Owns the single canonical character schema (also the convergence target for future character import). mutate_state is the SOLE writer of canon and overlay facts.
design: Tables: character (single-row sheet), inventory (item rows), plot_flags, clock (in-game time + current location_id); every mutable row carries provenance + session_id + ts. mutate_state(target, field, op, value, provenance) validates, applies transactionally (turn atomic), records provenance; also the writer for overlay_facts (used by E2). No free model text ever writes canon. Crash-safety from per-turn transaction commit.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Canonical character/inventory/plot_flags/clock schema defined and documented as the single source. 2. mutate_state applies a change transactionally with provenance and rejects invalid ops. 3. Simulated crash mid-turn leaves last committed state intact and in-flight turn rolled back. 4. Provenance is queryable for narrative callbacks.
notes: SYNTHESIS UPDATE 2026-05-17: Canon-changing state mutations remain deterministic, transactional, provenance-backed, and tool-mediated. Cheaper/helper models may propose state deltas, but accepted canon changes require premium-model or deterministic validation before commit.

title: E0 Foundation: TS scaffold, core/CLI boundary, SQLite, Agent SDK
description: Foundational scaffold every other sub-epic builds on. TypeScript project, UI-agnostic core library vs thin CLI boundary, SQLite persistence layer (one DB file per campaign), Claude Agent SDK wiring, configuration.
design:
## Architecture

npm-workspaces monorepo. `@loreweaver/core` is the UI-agnostic library; `@loreweaver/cli`
is a thin consumer that depends on core (never the reverse). The workspace package
boundary is the enforced core/CLI seam (acceptance #1). TypeScript strict, ESM
(`"type": "module"`, `NodeNext`). Tests: vitest. SQLite: `better-sqlite3` (synchronous,
real transactions with automatic rollback on throw). Model access is isolated behind a
local `ModelClient` interface; an `AgentSdkModelClient` adapts the Claude Agent SDK so
the rest of the codebase never imports the SDK directly.

## Tech stack

- Node 24, TypeScript ^5.6, ESM/NodeNext, `tsc --build` project references.
- vitest ^2 for tests (`vitest run`).
- better-sqlite3 ^11 (+ @types/better-sqlite3).
- @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk (Claude Agent SDK, TypeScript) — installed via npm,
  wrapped behind `ModelClient`; exact SDK surface confined to one adapter file.

## File map

- `package.json` — root: workspaces, scripts (build/test/typecheck), shared devDeps.
- `tsconfig.base.json` — shared strict compiler options.
- `tsconfig.json` — root solution file (project references to both packages).
- `vitest.config.ts` — test discovery (`packages/**/test/**/*.test.ts`).
- `.env.example` — documents LOREWEAVER_DB_PATH, LOREWEAVER_MODEL, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.
- `packages/core/package.json` — core package + deps.
- `packages/core/tsconfig.json` — composite build config.
- `packages/core/src/index.ts` — public barrel: re-exports config, persistence, model, seams, `CORE_VERSION`.
- `packages/core/src/config.ts` — `LoreweaverConfig`, `ConfigError`, `loadConfig(env)`.
- `packages/core/src/persistence/db.ts` — `openDatabase(path)`, `withTransaction(db, fn)`.
- `packages/core/src/persistence/schema.ts` — `SCHEMA_VERSION`, `initSchema(db)` (meta table).
- `packages/core/src/model/client.ts` — `ModelClient`, `ModelMessage` interfaces.
- `packages/core/src/model/agentSdkClient.ts` — `AgentSdkModelClient` adapter (only file importing the SDK).
- `packages/core/src/seams.ts` — empty interface stubs: Orchestrator, ContextAssembler, ToolLayer, MemorySubsystem, WorldSubsystem, Persistence (filled by E1–E7).
- `packages/core/test/*.test.ts` — unit tests per module.
- `packages/cli/package.json` — cli package, depends on `@loreweaver/core`.
- `packages/cli/tsconfig.json` — composite, references core.
- `packages/cli/src/index.ts` — thin entry: `buildBanner`, `main` (prints version + resolved config).
- `packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts` — tests pure `buildBanner`.

## Boundaries / tradeoffs

- Core has zero dependency on cli (asserted by core building standalone).
- SDK API surface is uncertain at plan time; confined to `agentSdkClient.ts` and verified
  against installed types during T5. Unit tests use a fake `ModelClient`; the real
  round-trip is a single integration test gated on `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
- Seam interfaces are intentionally empty now; "typecheck" == `tsc --build` succeeds.
acceptance_criteria: 1. Core package builds with zero UI deps; CLI consumes core. 2. SQLite layer creates a campaign DB and passes a transactional write/rollback test. 3. Agent SDK wrapper makes a successful round-trip model call behind the interface. 4. Component interface stubs exist and typecheck.
notes: SYNTHESIS UPDATE 2026-05-17: E0 must keep Claude Agent SDK as an adapter only. The core model seam should grow toward provider adapters and model profiles (premium_dm, state_extractor, summarizer, rules_adjudicator, memory_reconciler, embedding_provider, economy_or_experimental). Initial config may still expose Anthropic/Claude settings, but naming and interfaces should avoid implying Claude is the only provider.

title: Loreweaver: Agentic DM (solo persistent campaign MVP)
description:
Goal: a text-based agentic Dungeon Master that runs a single-player, persistent D&D campaign across many sessions, where the world changes over time and continuity is preserved within a bounded model-context budget.

User-visible outcome: from a local CLI, the player creates a character, starts/resumes/auto-closes play sessions, and converses with a DM agent that narrates, voices NPCs, adjudicates rulings, and advances an authored adventure while remembering the campaign across sessions.

Scope: MVP = solo persistent campaign on D&D 5e SRD content via the Claude Agent SDK (Pro plan), TypeScript. Non-goals (deferred): prose-rules RAG, semantic/RAG memory retrieval, general module importer, model-generated modules, web/multiplayer/long-running service, party/turn-taking, external character import.

This is an overarching epic decomposed into sub-epics E0-E7 (see Design).
design:
LOCKED DECISIONS:
- Rules: refined Hybrid. Model-trusted for narrative rulings; ALL math/dice/state via deterministic tools; structured SRD stat-block lookup (not fuzzy RAG); prose-rules RAG deferred.
- Memory: hierarchical pyramid (scene->session->arc->campaign_bible) as CORE; bounded always-on context independent of campaign length; anchored by exact provenance-annotated structured state re-asserted every turn; raw scene_log persisted from day one; semantic RAG deferred as future drill-down accelerator; never RAG-only.
- World: immutable authored module template (schema files) + per-campaign overlay-fact diff (latest-wins, git-like, provenance built in); module schema is the real deliverable; MVP seeds via ONE-TIME model-assisted conversion of ONE openly-licensed adventure; general importer deferred.
- Architecture: UI-agnostic TypeScript CORE library (Orchestrator, Context Assembler, Tool layer, Memory subsystem, World subsystem, Persistence) + THIN CLI front-end. Future web/multiplayer = new front-end on same core, deferred.
- Lifecycle: Campaign (long-lived) > Session (explicit start; AUTO-CLOSE on graceful exit runs recap + scene->session roll-up + state reconciliation + arc roll-up if milestone) > Scene (roll-up granularity, summaries written incrementally). Crash/hard-kill leaves session open; relaunch offers Resume vs Close&recap; canon crash-safe via transactional mutate_state + incremental scene summaries; close pipeline idempotent.
- Storage: HYBRID persistence (DECIDED, NOT deferred). SQLite is the AUTHORITATIVE LIVE operational store for active gameplay (embedded, per-turn ACID writes, one .db working copy per active campaign). Dolt is the AUTHORITATIVE checkpoint/history/branching store. At meaningful checkpoints (session close; arc roll-up) a DETERMINISTIC SQLite->Dolt export serializes all campaign tables and dolt-commits. Capabilities required in MVP: list checkpoints; restore a checkpoint into a NEW SQLite working copy; fork a campaign from a checkpoint into a NEW Dolt branch (+ materialized SQLite working copy). HARD CONSTRAINTS: Dolt is NEVER in the per-turn hot path; there are NOT two independent live truths (SQLite is the single live truth, Dolt trails to last checkpoint like a git working-tree vs last commit); Loreweaver Dolt storage/remotes/ref-namespace are EXPLICITLY separated from the beads Dolt repo (own dir, no piggybacking on refs/dolt/data). Authored module content remains version-controlled schema files imported at campaign creation.
- Language: TypeScript + official Claude Agent SDK (SDK is Python/TS only; TS chosen for schema typing, review legibility vs C#/Kotlin, shared types with future web front-end).

DECOMPOSITION (sub-epics, build order E0 -> E8 ; E1 || E3 ; -> E7 -> E4 -> E2 -> E5 -> E6):
- E0 Foundation: TS scaffold, core/CLI boundary, SQLite LIVE persistence, Agent SDK wiring, config. (Unchanged by Hybrid: SQLite remains the live store; persistence seam swappable.)
- E8 Dolt checkpoint/history/branching subsystem: deterministic SQLite->Dolt export, checkpoint commit, list checkpoints, restore-into-new-SQLite-working-copy, fork-from-checkpoint-into-new-branch, explicit beads-Dolt separation guard. NOT in per-turn path. (NEW, MVP, depends on E0.)
- E1 SRD reference store: structured monsters + spells + character-build options (races/classes/subclasses/backgrounds/feats/equipment/spell lists per SRD) + lookup_srd tool.
- E2 World subsystem: module schema, one-time model-assisted conversion of one open-licensed adventure, template + overlay-fact resolution, world_query tool. Conversion step gated on the legal-source blocker task; schema work not gated.
- E3 Game-state subsystem: canonical structured state tables (character/inventory/plot_flags/clock) with provenance, mutate_state tool as SOLE canon+overlay writer, transactional crash-safe writes.
- E4 Memory pyramid: scene_log (append-only), incremental scene_summary, session_recap + arc_summary roll-up steps, campaign_bible reconciliation, structural memory_drilldown tool.
- E5 Orchestrator + tools: turn loop, Context Assembler (bounded prompt = bible + arc + last recap + state snapshot + live scene transcript), roll, mark_scene, DM system prompt encoding the Hybrid rules contract.
- E6 Session lifecycle + CLI: campaign create/fork, start/resume/auto-close, idempotent close pipeline, thin CLI front-end. Session-close and arc roll-up INVOKE the E8 checkpoint export.
