acceptance_criteria:
MVP is complete when, from the local CLI on D&D 5e SRD/open-licensed content:
1. Player can create an SRD-legal character via guided flow; sheet persists as canonical state.
2. Player can start a campaign forked from an authored module template; the converted open-licensed adventure loads.
3. Player can play multiple sessions; DM narrates, voices NPCs, adjudicates, runs creatures using looked-up stat blocks; all dice/math/state changes go through tools.
4. World changes (killed NPC, flipped plot flag, spent gold) persist as overlay/state and are reflected on later turns and sessions.
5. Graceful exit auto-closes the session (recap + roll-up); crash leaves session resumable with zero canon loss.
6. After many sessions, the DM demonstrates campaign continuity while assembled prompt size stays bounded and roughly constant with campaign length.
7. memory_drilldown retrieves a specific older session/scene on demand without it being permanently in context.
8. Session close and arc roll-up produce deterministic Dolt checkpoint commits; Dolt is never written in a per-turn path.
9. Player can list checkpoints, restore a checkpoint into a new SQLite working copy, and fork a campaign from a checkpoint into a new Dolt branch with an isolated working copy.
10. Loreweaver Dolt storage/remote/ref-namespace is verifiably disjoint from the beads Dolt repo.
11. Core model integration exposes provider-neutral adapters and model profiles; Claude/Anthropic remains an initial adapter, not a core assumption.
12. The primary DM path is configured for a premium_dm quality floor; economy models are not the default public demo or canonical DM unless explicitly marked experimental/validated.
13. Rules/mechanics, campaign content, live state, user-private packs, and generated memory remain separated with provenance.
14. Pack metadata can enforce license, attribution, hosted-use, sharing, redistribution, and monetization policy.
15. The demo path is premium-model, bounded-turn, and preloaded rather than economy-model-first.
16. Remaining deferred items are recorded explicitly: native VTT, native mobile, hosted billing/credits, general importers, and custom/local primary DM replacement.
All sub-epics E0-E8 closed; deferred items explicitly recorded, not silently dropped.
notes:
DB ARCHITECTURE DECIDED (user + second-model concurrence): HYBRID, not deferred. SQLite = authoritative live operational store (per-turn ACID, never replaced). Dolt = authoritative checkpoint/history/branching store. MVP must include: deterministic SQLite->Dolt checkpoint export; dolt commit per checkpoint; list checkpoints; restore checkpoint into NEW SQLite working copy; fork campaign from checkpoint into NEW Dolt branch; explicit separation from beads Dolt storage/remotes. Prohibitions: Dolt NOT in per-turn hot path; Dolt NOT deferred; NOT two independent live truths. New sub-epic E8 created for the Dolt checkpoint subsystem. E0 SQLite tasks UNCHANGED (SQLite stays the live store).
STRATEGY SYNTHESIS 2026-05-17: Product direction is text-first long-campaign AI DM for tabletop-seeking solo players and living text-world nostalgists. MVP/medium-term remains text-first; native VTT and native mobile are non-goals. CLI/local remains the near-term development and power-user surface; hosted mobile-friendly web/PWA is the likely medium-term public surface. Model strategy is provider adapters + model profiles, not Claude-only. premium_dm targets Opus 4.6+ / GPT-5.5-class or future equivalent; economy models are auxiliary/experimental unless validated. Billing starts BYOK-first; hosted credits are future optional. Public demo should be premium-model, short, bounded, and preloaded rather than economy-model-first. Content strategy separates rules, campaign content, live state, user-private content, and generated memory; public/bundled packs must be open, public-domain, original, or licensed; no fair-use-dependent public pack strategy or ownership-gated closed-IP derived packs. See docs/architecture-report.md and ADR 0001.

The combatant branch (~line 790) is the precedent for "economies derive from the record; declared economies fail closed". Table entity_usage_counter: uses_max >= 1, CHECK uses_used <= uses_max, source IN ('record','declared'), reset_kind IN ('recharge_roll','short_rest','short_or_long_rest','long_rest','dawn').
- packages/core/src/character/levelUpEngine.ts: applyLevelUp (~line 437) runs in one transaction: store.save, projectToLiveCharacter, syncSpellSlots, recordProgressionEvent(appliedChanges: changeSet). computeLevelUpChangeSet (~line 603) builds the pure change set.

DECISIONS
1. Classification (record it in docs/design/character-progression.md, new short section): selected expendable capacities = barbarian rages (Rage), monk kiPoints (Ki), sorcerer sorceryPoints (Sorcery Points); gameplay consumer = spend_usage/restore_usage/reset_usage on a character ability. rageDamage = derived damage bonus, martialArts / sneakAttack = dice scaling, unarmoredMovement = speed bonus: all descriptive here (DM-adjudicated via lookup_rules), no deterministic handling. Prose-only capacities (Channel Divinity, Action Surge, Lay on Hands, Wild Shape...) not selected.
2. Resolver retains resources: ResolvedClassLevel gains `resources` (record keyed by the pack resource name) holding the raw value parsed as: number -> {kind:'count', value}; 'Unlimited' -> {kind:'unlimited'}; '—' -> {kind:'none'}; any other string kept as {kind:'text', value} (the descriptive columns). A non-string/non-number value stays malformed.
3. One binding table (usageCounters.ts or a small new module next to it): {classKey, resource, counterKey, displayName, aliases (normalized ability names), reset} for: barbarian rages -> 'ability:rage', 'Rage', aliases ['rage','rages'], long_rest; monk kiPoints -> 'ability:ki', 'Ki', aliases ['ki','ki-points'], short_or_long_rest; sorcerer sorceryPoints -> 'ability:sorcery-points', 'Sorcery Points', aliases ['sorcery-points','font-of-magic'], long_rest. Verify each reset against the feature text and cite it in a comment.
4. spend_usage on a character ability whose stored canonical sheet (createSqliteCharacterSheetStore) has the binding's class and whose normalized ability name is an alias: pack-bound. Any declared {maxUses, reset} is refused (fail closed, message says the capacity derives from the class table). First spend creates the counter from the pack value at the sheet's level, source 'record', canonical counterKey. Value 'none' (monk 1, sorcerer 1 with no entry) -> refuse with a reason (no such resource at this level). Value 'unlimited' (barbarian 20) -> the spend succeeds without consuming or creating a counter; result marks it unlimited. Characters without a stored sheet or of another class keep today's declared behaviour unchanged.
5. Legacy counters: a pre-existing counter under any alias key (e.g. a declared 'ability:ki-points') is adopted on the next pack-bound spend or level-up reconciliation: rekeyed to the canonical key, source 'record', uses_max set to the pack value, uses_used preserved (clamped to the new max). No counter -> nothing (first spend derives it). Ledger gets it through appliedChanges.
7. restore_usage / reset_usage keep their behaviour, operating on the reconciled max. Creature and item counters unchanged.
8. Update protocol.ts's spend_usage guidance in one sentence: class resources (Rage, Ki, Sorcery Points) derive from the class table; never pass maxUses/reset for them. Keep the protocol.test 'no SRD string' rule in mind.

title: Dispatch: 91o0 PR #613 review fixes - per-instance coverage + same-level Lore expertise (Sonnet 5.5, attempt 1)
description:
Fix dispatch for PR #613 review (GitHub review 5464545677, head 4ba97273), eshyra-91o0. Model: Sonnet 5.5 (Claude Agent). Worktree .worktrees/eshyra-91o0.2 on branch eshyra-91o0.2, cut from eshyra-91o0 @ 4ba97273 (already contains merged PR #612 expertise). Run `npm ci` first. Read the review: `gh api repos/jbongaarts/eshyra/pulls/613/reviews --jq '.[].body'`. Two blocking findings. Fix both in this one round, along with their siblings.

FINDING 1 — coverage invariant is per-feature, must be per-choice-instance.
packages/core/src/character/levelUpChoiceCoverage.ts builds `covered` from descriptor featureRefs and skips a whole feature once any descriptor names it. So a feature with one handled choice and one unhandled choice lets the unhandled one through. The base Spellcasting/Pact Magic exemption ("some level.N.spells.* descriptor exists") is the same mistake.

DESIGN (supervisor decision):
- Introduce an explicit HANDLED-INSTANCE contract. Every detector reports the choice instances it took responsibility for at this level as keys `${featureRef}\0${choiceId}`, INCLUDING instances it evaluated and decided need no descriptor. Examples: a replacement with nothing held; a conditional spell choice whose trigger was not picked; a non-due spell choice on a held feature. Put a small shared type/helper (e.g. `choiceInstanceKey(featureRef, choiceId)`) in levelUpChoiceCoverage.ts.
- Who handles what:
  * levelUpFeatureChoices.detectFeatureChoiceDescriptors: every list choice it processed (new, grown, repeated, replacement). Do NOT mark the CONDITIONAL_CHOICES ids handled here; the spell module owns them. Keep coveredFeatureRefs only for dropping the legacy fallback.
  * levelUpSpells.detectSpellDescriptors: (a) on non-base features, every spell/cantrip choice it evaluated in dueFeatureSpellChoices's scan (due or not, including conditional ones); (b) on the base Spellcasting/Pact Magic feature, when it is a target ref, map the bucket logic to the base choice ids it actually evaluates: cantrips->'cantrips', known->'spells', replacement->'spell-replacement', spellbook growth->'spellbook-growth', prepare->'prepared-spells'. Mark one handled only when the corresponding branch ran, i.e. `casts && toSpellcasting !== undefined` and the class preparation kind selects that branch. 'spellbook-initial' is creation-only. Do not mark it; if it is ever a level-up target instance, the invariant must block. When the legacy-classification failure returns early, its unsupported descriptor already blocks (see the next rule). Return handled instances alongside the descriptors (change the return shape, or add a sibling function; your choice, but keep one source of truth).
  * levelUpExpertise / levelUpSkillChoices: the choices they process. A repeated Lore grant is NOT handled by the skill module, so the invariant blocks it.
  * Legacy featureRequiredChoice in levelUpEngine.ts: a SUPPORTED 'subclass' descriptor handles the feature's 'subclass'-category choices. A SUPPORTED 'ability-score-improvement' descriptor handles the feature's 'asiOrFeat'-category choices (both 'ability-score-improvement' and the 'feat' marker: that descriptor's `from` already offers feats and resolution applies featRef; verify this before relying on it).
  * Blocking rule: an UNSUPPORTED descriptor carrying featureRef X blocks the level-up, so every instance on X counts as covered. Only that rule may cover by featureRef.
- The invariant then emits an unsupported descriptor for each instance at toLevel (keep choiceInstancesAtLevel semantics) that is neither handled nor covered by an unsupported descriptor on its feature, minus isUseTimeChoice. DELETE isBaseSpellcastingRef and the spellModuleEmitted shortcut.
- Re-run the class x subclass x level 1->20 enumeration (the existing test at levelUpSubclassChoices.test.ts ~434). Every transition must still report no uncovered instance. If one now appears, it is a real gap: fix the owning detector's handled set honestly, or report it. Never re-add a blanket exemption. Ranger/paladin 1->2 are the known sensitive cases (spell-replacement with nothing held -> the replacement branch evaluated it -> handled).

FINDING 2 — at bard 2->3, College of Lore's new skills must be eligible for Expertise in the same level-up.
detectExpertiseDescriptors reads only sheet.skillProficiencies (level 2), so a skill picked for Lore in this step is excluded and refused.
DESIGN: in detectLevelUpRequiredChoices, run detectSkillChoiceDescriptors BEFORE detectExpertiseDescriptors. For each supported skill descriptor that has a selection in `selections`, validate it with resolveSkillChoiceSelection (the same validation apply uses). Only on ok, collect its skillProficiencies as pending. Pass the pending skills to detectExpertiseDescriptors, e.g. as `pendingSkillProficiencies`, so eligibleOptions treats them as held. Invalid Lore picks contribute nothing, and the Lore descriptor still blocks on its own. applyLevelUp/preview already pass input.choices to detection, so resolution validates expertise against the expanded `from`. Persistence stays atomic: nothing is written while any blocker remains. The descriptor order (expertise before featureChoices) may change; that's fine. Check whether any other same-level interaction feeds expertise or skill eligibility (e.g. a background/feat grant at level-up). Report it if found; don't build speculative plumbing.

EVIDENCE (proportionate, generalized; extend levelUpSubclassChoices.test.ts):
- F1: one generalized test on a feature carrying BOTH a handled list choice and an unhandled choice (synthetic resolver/pack overlay, as the existing synthetic test does). The unhandled one must yield an unsupported descriptor and apply must refuse. Also cover a conditional sibling (e.g. a Pact-of-the-Tome-style requiresFeatureOption choice not triggered) to show it is not wrongly required, and a repeated grant.
- F2: a real bard 2->3 College of Lore regression using the REAL pack row (do not strip expertise; remove the existing test's expertise-stripping workaround, since expertise is now supported). Pick 3 Lore skills, including one not previously held, then Expertise on that new skill plus another: apply succeeds, and the sheet gets the skills and both featureChoices entries. Also: Expertise on a skill only in an INVALID Lore selection (held/duplicate) blocks; a duplicate Expertise pick blocks.
- `npm run verify:worktree` before committing.
notes:
Dispatched 2026-10-09 to Sonnet 5.5 Claude Agent (background), worktree .worktrees/eshyra-91o0.2 @4ba97273.
Completed @ffc2d6db (verify:worktree 6080 pass / 3 skip). F1: levelUpChoiceCoverage.ts now compares per instance via choiceInstanceKey(featureRef, choiceId) and a handled-instance set; isBaseSpellcastingRef and the spellModuleEmitted shortcut deleted. Only an UNSUPPORTED descriptor with featureRef covers by ref. descriptorId/featureSlug moved to coverage module (re-exported from levelUpFeatureChoices) to avoid an import cycle. Handled ownership: featureChoices = every list choice processed (new/grown/repeated/replacement, incl. held invocation choices); conditional ids NOT marked (spell module owns). Spells = non-base spell/cantrip choices evaluated in dueFeatureSpellChoices (due, untriggered conditional, or non-due on held/repeated feature) + base Spellcasting/Pact Magic: cantrips (casts&&toSpellcasting), spells+spell-replacement (kind known), spellbook-growth (spellbookStartingSpells), prepared-spells (kind prepared); spellbook-initial never marked; legacy-classification early return marks nothing. Expertise = expertise-category choices on target refs. Skills = skill list choices on first-grant refs (repeated Lore grant unhandled -> invariant blocks). Engine legacy: supported subclass descriptor handles 'subclass' category; supported ASI descriptor handles 'asiOrFeat' (both ability-score-improvement and feat; verified from offers feats and resolution sets featRef). detectSpellDescriptors/Skill/Expertise/FeatureChoices now return handledInstances. Enumeration: existing class x subclass x 1->20 test passes with no uncovered instance, so no real gaps surfaced (ranger/paladin 1->2 fine). Deviation: in the spell scan a FIRST grant of a non-conditional, non-due spell choice is deliberately left unhandled so the invariant blocks it (not a principled skip). F2: engine runs detectSkillChoiceDescriptors first, validates each selected skill descriptor with resolveSkillChoiceSelection, passes valid skills as pendingSkillProficiencies to detectExpertiseDescriptors (eligibleOptions treats them as held, case-insensitive dedupe); invalid Lore picks add nothing. Descriptor order is now expertise, featureChoices, skills. Other same-level interactions: none found (level-up feats grant no skills). Tests (levelUpSubclassChoices.test.ts): Lore tests now use the real bard row (expertise-stripping removed); real bard 2->3 apply with Expertise on new Lore skill + held skill; invalid/duplicate Lore selection and duplicate Expertise block; F1 synthetic tests: handled+unhandled on one feature (unsupported + preview refuses), untriggered conditional spell sibling not required, repeated Lore grant blocked.

- packages/core/src/character/levelUpEngine.ts: featureChoiceKind() maps suffix 'expertise' -> kind 'expertise'; featureRequiredChoice() emits it as status 'unsupported' (legacy fallback, id `level.N.expertise`, carries featureRef). detectLevelUpRequiredChoices() drops a fallback when its featureRef is in detectFeatureChoiceDescriptors().coveredFeatureRefs. resolveLevelUpChoices() routes supported choices by choice.featureChoice / choice.spellChoice.   feature:rogue:expertise choices[0] = {id:'expertise', category:'expertise', level:1, choose:2, from:{kind:'characterStateFilter', proficiencyTypes:['skill'], tools:['thieves-tools']}}; granted by class:rogue progression levels 1 and 6.

  The pack repeats only the feature ref at 6/10. Per SRD prose each repeated grant adds two more picks ("At 6th level, you can choose two more of your proficiencies (in skills or with thieves' tools)"; bard "At 10th level, you can choose another two skill proficiencies"). Re-derive both against the full feature description text in the pack before encoding them.
- packages/core/src/rules/repeatedFeatureChoices.ts documents the source-level vs grant-level contract for repeated choices.
- packages/core/src/character/guidedLevelUpFlow.ts presents descriptors to the player.

DESIGN DECISIONS (supervisor; do not re-decide):
1. New module packages/core/src/character/levelUpExpertise.ts holds the detection, validation and applied-choice logic. Keep levelUpEngine.ts edits to minimal wiring: kind unions, calling the detector, marking the feature covered so the legacy fallback drops, and routing the resolution. Do NOT add 'expertise' to LIST_CHOICE_CATEGORIES. A parallel dispatch (eshyra-91o0.1) is editing levelUpEngine.ts, levelUpFeatureChoices.ts and levelUpSpells.ts, so keep your diff in those files small and localized to ease the merge.
2. Descriptor: kind 'expertise', status 'supported', id descriptorId(toLevel, featureRef, 'expertise'), choose = record choose on first grant, or 2 on a repeated grant. Put the repeated count in a source-cited constant in the new module, not in REPEATED_GRANT_PICKS. featureRef set, and featureChoice {featureRef, choiceId:'expertise'}, so persistence reuses featureChoices. options/from = the eligible set.
3. Option ids: `skill:<exact string from sheet.skillProficiencies>`, and `tool:thieves-tools` when the filter's tools include thieves-tools AND sheet.toolProficiencies holds thieves' tools. Match the tool by normalized name: case-insensitive, straight/curly apostrophe agnostic. Option name = the display string.
4. Eligible = held proficiencies of the filter's types MINUS ones already holding expertise. Already-held expertise = union of optionIds across every sheet.featureChoices entry whose choiceId is 'expertise' and whose featureRef is any expertise feature (a rogue/bard multiclass cannot happen today, but don't key exclusion on one featureRef). Export a helper characterExpertise(sheet): ReadonlySet<string> of those option ids, from internal.ts only (not the root export).

Report what you found in your completion notes and file a follow-up bead if a real consumer gap exists.

title: Level-up: disposition every typed featureImprovement row (Cleric 20, Druid 4/8, Monk 9, Paladin 18, Ranger 6/10/14) instead of blocking advancement
description:

Leads to verify, not decisions: no engine consumer exists today for Wild Shape limits, Paladin auras, Divine Intervention or Monk movement; Monk 9's improvement is distinct from the unarmoredMovement resourceProgression speed column (eshyra-2llo).
Implement the minimum positively justified behavior. A genuinely unsupported requirement stays an explicit fail-closed blocker with a reason, never a silent skip.

title: Dispatch: ug4i.2 level-up spell selection (Sonnet 5.5, attempt 1)
description:
Implement eshyra-ug4i.2 (level-up spell selection). Read `bd show eshyra-ug4i.2` (its DESIGN field: settled; this description REFINES it and wins where they differ) and `bd show eshyra-ug4i` (decomposition). Worktree .worktrees/eshyra-ug4i.2.1, branch eshyra-ug4i.2.1 cut from eshyra-ug4i.2 (main @ 03a7c4d9, which includes eshyra-ug4i.3 / PR #609). Sonnet 5.5, attempt 1.

HARD RULE (srd-fidelity-hard-blocker): never contradict the SRD. Read each class's spellcasting feature prose and progression in packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json before coding. Do not edit records.json, importer scripts, or anything under packages/core/data/rules-packs.

CODE SURVEY:
- packages/core/src/character/levelUpEngine.ts: spellSelectionChoices (the single unsupported blocker to replace), gainsNewSpellLevel, detectLevelUpRequiredChoices, resolveLevelUpChoices (featureChoice branch from #609 is the model), applyChangeSetToSheet / projectToLiveCharacter / syncSpellSlots (unchanged).
- packages/core/src/character/levelUpFeatureChoices.ts (#609): CONDITIONAL_CHOICES (Tome cantrips, Book of Ancient Secrets rituals) currently emit UNSUPPORTED descriptors; make them supported spell descriptors here. Follow its descriptor-id, options, optional, featureChoice and sibling-distinctness patterns (and its newPicks rule: a replacement's first entry is given up, never a pick).
- packages/core/src/character/rulesPackResolver.ts: ResolvedLevelSpellcasting (cantripsKnown, spellsKnown, slots, pactSlots), ResolvedSpellPreparation (kind known|prepared, spellbookStartingSpells, preparationFormula {ability, classLevelDivisor, minimum}), resolveSpell, ResolvedFeatureData.choices.
- packages/core/src/character/finalizeCharacter.ts: CharacterSheet (spells: flat list of names/refs, cantrips mixed in), featureChoices + its validator (model for validating the new field), validateCharacterSheetRollEvidence (where #609 hooked validation).
- packages/core/src/character/requiredChoices.ts + characterDraft.ts: how creation fills sheet.spells (wizard: cantrips + 6 spellbook spells; prepared casters: their prepared list; known casters: known list). Do not change creation in this bead (eshyra-nnj6 owns it; add a note there that creation should write the structured field).
- packages/cli/src/playProgression.ts: the round-based choice collection from #609; spell descriptors must be presentable (option = spell ref + name + level) and must not dump the whole spell list unfiltered: offer the filtered legal list.
- packages/core/src/rules/featureChoices.ts: the `from` object of spell/cantrip choices is a `spellFilter`: classLists (class refs, or "any"), spellLevels, minSpellLevel, maxSpellLevel {classRef, atLevel}, castableLevelsOnly, includeCantrips, ritualOnly, mustBeInSpellbook, mustBePreparedToCast, alwaysPrepared, countsAsClassSpell, countsAgainstKnown, requiresFeatureOption. Spell records carry data.level, data.classes (class NAMES, e.g. "Wizard"; map class ref -> class record name), data.ritual.

DESIGN:
1. SHEET: optional `spellcasting?: { cantrips: string[]; known?: string[]; spellbook?: string[]; prepared?: string[]; mysticArcanum?: { level: number; spellRef: string }[]; designations?: { kind: 'spell-mastery' | 'signature-spell'; level: number; spellRef: string }[] }`, all canonical `spell:<slug>` refs. `sheet.spells` stays the derived union of all buckets, in canonical refs once `spellcasting` exists. Validate the field like featureChoices (shape, refs resolve where a resolver is available, no ref in two of cantrips/known/spellbook), old sheets still load.
2. LEGACY CLASSIFICATION on a sheet without `spellcasting`, at its first level-up: every sheet.spells entry must resolve (refuse the level-up naming the entry otherwise, never guess); level 0 -> cantrips; leveled -> known (spellPreparation.kind known), spellbook (spellbookStartingSpells defined: wizard), prepared (other prepared casters). A non-caster with no spells gets no field.
3. ONE shared spellFilter evaluator: (filter, sheet, class, targetLevel) -> legal spell refs. "Castable" = spell level 1..highest slot level at the TARGET level (warlock: pactSlots.level). maxSpellLevel {classRef, atLevel}: highest castable for that class at atLevel, EXCEPT a repeated grant (Magical Secrets at 14/18) uses the target level (SRD: "A spell you choose must be of a level you can cast"; the pack's atLevel describes the first grant). Unknown filter keys -> the descriptor is emitted UNSUPPORTED naming the key (fail closed, never ignore a constraint).
4. DESCRIPTORS (status supported unless stated; stable ids `level.<n>.spells.<bucket>` or the #609 feature id for feature choices):
   a. cantrips: cantripsKnown delta; the class's own cantrip filter (feature:<class>:spellcasting|pact-magic choice 'cantrips' filter), excluding held.
   b. known casters: ordinary picks = spellsKnown delta MINUS the picks of feature choices granted at this level with countsAgainstKnown true (bard Magical Secrets at 10/14/18: the bard's known growth at those levels IS the secrets). Filter: the class 'spells' filter with castable levels at the target level. Plus OPTIONAL replacement [oldRef, newRef] every level of the class (filter: the class 'spell-replacement' filter; old must be in known and not a Magical Secrets/arcanum pick... SRD: "you can choose one of the bard spells you know and replace it with another spell from the bard spell list" — old must be a known spell of the class list; new from the class list at a castable level).
   c. wizard: spellbook-growth 2 per wizard level (filter on feature:wizard:spellcasting 'spellbook-growth'), into spellbook.
   d. feature spell choices due at this level: any spell/cantrip choice on a feature granted at the target level (class row or subclass) or held whose choice.level === target level (Mystic Arcanum arcanum-6..9 at 11/13/15/17; Spell Mastery at 18; Signature Spells at 20; Magical Secrets 10 and its repeats at 14/18 via the repeated feature ref; College of Lore Additional Magical Secrets at 6; Tome cantrips and Book of Ancient Secrets rituals when the trigger option is picked this level-up or, for a held trigger, never re-asked). Exclude the base spellcasting feature's creation-time choices (cantrips, spells, spellbook-initial) — those are handled by (a)-(c). Persist: magical secrets / tome / book picks into known (countsAgainstKnown false ones still go into known; the field only affects counting); arcanum -> mysticArcanum; spell mastery / signature -> designations (mustBeInSpellbook: from the spellbook).
   e. prepared casters (spellPreparation.kind prepared, incl. wizard): NO blocker. One OPTIONAL descriptor 'prepare' that replaces `prepared` with up to max(minimum, abilityMod + floor(classLevel / classLevelDivisor)) refs (ability modifier from the sheet's final scores at the target level, after any ASI this level-up), filter = the class 'prepared-spells' filter (wizard: mustBeInSpellbook). Preparation is normally a long-rest action; record a follow-up bead for a long-rest prepare tool.

Do not edit records.json, importer scripts, or anything under packages/core/data/rules-packs.

SCOPE: structured choices whose `from` is a LIST (option ids/labels), with or without inline options[] — categories fightingStyle (fighter 1 via later levels' additional style: champion 10; paladin 2; ranger 2), metamagic (sorcerer 3 and later growth), invocation (warlock 2 and growth with progression invocationsKnown), 'other' (warlock pact-boon 3; hunter options at 3/7/11/15), favoredEnemy / naturalExplorer (ranger growth levels, if the pack carries them at those levels). 1. Sheet: CharacterSheet (packages/core/src/character/finalizeCharacter.ts) gains optional `featureChoices?: readonly { featureRef: string; choiceId: string; optionIds: readonly string[]; level: number }[]` in acquisition order. Optional, so existing sheets stay valid; check every sheet validator/serializer/schema test (grep CharacterSheet, characterSheetStore, validateCharacterSheet*) and extend validation of the new field (shape, known featureRef format) without rejecting old sheets.

Detection (levelUpEngine.ts detectLevelUpRequiredChoices / featureChoiceKind ~L280-310, ~L565+, ~L690-730): for each feature ref gained at the target level AND for count growth of an already-held feature, emit one descriptor per structured list choice. Count: the choice's `choose` when the feature is newly gained; for growth, the delta of the progression column the pack provides (warlock invocationsKnown; verify how sorcerer metamagic growth at 10/17 and ranger favored enemy/natural explorer growth appear in the pack — feature ref repeated on the row, a column, or prose only. If growth exists only as prose, emit an 'unsupported' descriptor naming it rather than skipping it: a silent skip is the failure mode). Descriptor id stays stable (e.g. `level.<n>.feature.<featureSlug>.<choiceId>`), status 'supported', choose = count, from = legal option ids, plus a new optional `options?: { id, name, prerequisite? }[]` for display. Conditional choices: a choice that only applies because of another option (pact-of-the-tome-cantrips when Tome is picked; Book of Ancient Secrets rituals) must be emitted (as unsupported, owned by eshyra-ug4i.2) only when that option is selected in this level-up or already held — never block Chain/Blade warlocks on Tome's cantrips. Remove 'pact-boon', 'eldritch-invocations', 'metamagic' from the blunt suffix denylist only where the structured path covers them; 'fighting-style' kind likewise. title: Level-up: spell selection (design first)
description: Slice 3 of eshyra-ug4i. Design before dispatch: what spell choices a level-up really carries per caster type (known casters: new spells from the class list up to the castable level plus one optional replacement; cantrips; wizard +2 spellbook spells; warlock mystic arcanum; bard magical secrets; pact-of-the-tome cantrips and Book of Ancient Secrets rituals when those options are held), how sheet.spells distinguishes known/spellbook/prepared, and whether prepared casters (cleric/druid/paladin) should be blocked at all at level-up (preparation is a long-rest action, not a level-up choice). Re-derive spellSelectionChoices in levelUpEngine.ts against that.
design:
DESIGN (Claude Captain, 2026-10-08). Dispatch after eshyra-ug4i.3 merges into eshyra-ug4i (same files; reuse its featureChoices/validation patterns).

FACTS (main @ 41c395d4): CharacterSheet.spells is one flat list of names/refs mixing cantrips and leveled spells, with no known/spellbook/prepared distinction. Creation validates only that each spell resolves and is on the class list. No runtime tool reads sheet.spells to gate casting; it feeds DM context. spellSelectionChoices (levelUpEngine.ts) emits ONE unsupported blocker when cantripsKnown or spellsKnown grows, a new slot level appears, or the class keeps a spellbook. Prepared casters are therefore blocked at every new spell level, though SRD preparation happens after a long rest ("You can change your list of prepared spells when you finish a long rest"), not at level-up.

1. SHEET. Add optional `spellcasting?: { cantrips: string[]; known?: string[]; spellbook?: string[]; prepared?: string[]; mysticArcanum?: { level: number; spellRef: string }[] }`, all canonical `spell:<slug>` refs. `sheet.spells` stays as the derived union, so existing consumers are unchanged. Legacy sheets (no `spellcasting`) are classified deterministically on their first level-up: every entry must resolve; level 0 goes to cantrips; leveled spells go to known (bard/sorcerer/ranger/warlock), spellbook (wizard) or prepared (cleric/druid/paladin). Refuse the level-up, naming the entry, if any entry fails to resolve. Never guess.
2. LEVEL-UP DESCRIPTORS (supported, one per need, ids stable):
   - cantrips: cantripsKnown delta; class list, level 0, not held.
   - known casters: spellsKnown delta; class list, levels 1..highest castable at the new level (warlock: pact slot level), not held. Optional non-blocking replacement [oldRef, newRef] (SRD: when you gain a level, replace one known spell with another of a level you can cast).
   - bard Magical Secrets (10/14/18; College of Lore Additional Magical Secrets at 6): choose per the feature's spellFilter (any class list, incl. cantrips, up to castable level). These count as known spells.
   - warlock Mystic Arcanum (11/13/15/17): 1 warlock spell of exactly that level, into mysticArcanum.
   - wizard: +2 wizard spells of a castable level into the spellbook every level.
   - Pact of the Tome cantrips (3, any class list) when Tome is held or picked; Book of Ancient Secrets (2 first-level rituals, any class) when that invocation is held or picked. These replace ug4i.3's unsupported conditional descriptors.
   - prepared casters (cleric, druid, paladin; wizard's preparation): NO blocker. Offer one OPTIONAL non-blocking 'prepare' descriptor that sets `prepared` up to the class limit (paladin: half level, rounded down + CHA mod, min 1; cleric/druid: level + WIS mod, min 1; wizard: level + INT mod, from its spellbook). Use the pack's structured prepared-count data (eshyra-b69j.12.2) rather than hard-coding.
3. VALIDATION: resolves, on the allowed list(s), level bound, not already held (any bucket), exact counts, a replacement's old ref held. Fail closed on anything unresolved.
4. APPLY: update `spellcasting` and the `spells` union; ledger change set lists added/replaced refs per bucket; syncSpellSlots is unchanged.
5. FOLLOW-UP (file at dispatch): long-rest spell preparation as a model tool/lifecycle (prepare after a long rest), which owns `prepared` outside level-up.
Evidence: bard 2 (+1 known; replacement), sorcerer 4 (+1 cantrip, +1 known), warlock 3 Tome (3 any-list cantrips), warlock 11 arcanum, wizard 2 (+2 spellbook, castable level only), cleric 3 (new spell level: no blocker; optional prepare within the limit), paladin 2 (optional prepare), ranger 2 (2 known), a legacy flat-list sheet classified and leveled, and an unresolved legacy entry refused.

title: Bonded-summon presence transition leaves a participant-turn clock anchored to the departed combatant (begin_turn/close_combat_instance then refuse)
description:
DEFECT CLASS (state integrity, reachable): a participant-turn clock whose participant leaves play or changes identity during a bonded-summon presence transition. transition_bonded_summon rebinds the leaving combatant's target/link/source-actor references to its campaign_actor, but the clock's anchor_participant_kind/ref still name the combatant. The committed row then violates the participant-timer invariant, and every later validation of that combat's timers refuses.

## Steps to Reproduce
Static trace (confirmed by Claude Captain against main f7d70b64, packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts):
1. start_effect accepts a timed round duration anchored 'target-turn-start' to a single combatant target (toolEffectShared.ts anchor enum).
2. A bonded familiar/steed combatant can be that sole target.
3. transitionBondedSummon (~l.5703) for every non-recall trigger (action-temporary-dismissal -> pocketed; action-permanent-dismissal, action-dismissal, action-release -> absent) calls rebindCombatantReferencesToActor (~l.6564), which rewrites active_effect_target combatant->campaign_actor (and links, and source_actor) but never touches anchor_participant_*.
4. requireParticipantTimerDeadline (~l.1129) requires a target-turn-start anchor to equal the effect's sole target -> now mismatched.
5. settleEffectsAtTurnBoundary (~l.6408) validates EVERY participant timer anchored to the combat instance before any settlement, so the next begin_turn throws and rolls back: the combat cannot advance.
6. Sibling consequence: combat closure (~l.6725) runs the same pre-validation, so close_combat_instance also refuses.
Sibling to check (include only if reachable by a legitimate tool sequence): a 'source-turn-start' clock whose source actor is the departing combatant — the source_actor rebind produces the same anchor/source mismatch.

DESIGN REQUIREMENT: choose a bounded, source-justified disposition for a participant-turn clock whose participant leaves play (settle/expire at the transition, or another SRD-justified behavior) and apply it inside the transition transaction with ledger evidence. Mechanically rebinding the anchor to campaign_actor is NOT acceptable: a campaign actor is not a turn participant and the clock could never advance. Decide explicitly what temporary dismissal (pocket) followed by action-recall means for the clock (recall enters as a NEW combatant identity).
History: eshyra-82uk.1 deliberately left participant-turn clocks and concentration out of the rebind, deferring this decision here.
design: 2026-10-08 Claude Captain (supersedes the earlier design text). DISPOSITION: expire. Inside transitionBondedSummon, for the departing kinds (pocket, dismiss, release) and BEFORE rebindCombatantReferencesToActor, every live (active/suppressed) participant-turn timer (target-turn-start OR source-turn-start) anchored in this instance to the departing combatant ends with reason 'expired' via finalizeEnd; reported as result.timersExpired and in the presence-transition event. RATIONALE: participant clocks are combatant-only by contract (closure rebind comment); the transition rebinds the effect's target/source to campaign_actor, which is not a turn participant, and a recall enters as a NEW combatant identity, so the clock can no longer describe the creature in play. Mechanically rebinding the anchor is invalid; keeping target+anchor on the absent row (as the 0-HP vanish path does, which never rebinds) would split the effect's references and leave it on a stale row after recall. Closure precedent: round-scale timers whose clock leaves expire. NOTE: begin_turn does still establish boundaries for absent participants, so the justification is identity, not 'the clock can never tick'. If the bond effect itself carries such a clock, the transition refuses (fail closed). Source-turn-start sibling is reachable (start_effect accepts a combatant source actor) and is included.
acceptance_criteria:
- Permanent regression via a legitimate model-tool sequence: start_effect with a target-turn-start clock on a bonded familiar/steed combatant -> transition_bonded_summon dismissal -> begin_turn advances (and close_combat_instance closes) without refusal.
- The test distinguishes the invalid retained clock (must not survive) from a valid surviving or settled effect (asserts the chosen disposition and its ledger evidence).
- Sibling triggers (pocket/temporary dismissal, permanent dismissal, dismissal, release) covered where the same invariant applies; source-turn-start sibling covered only if reachable.
- No mechanical rebinding of a participant-turn anchor to campaign_actor.
notes:
2026-10-08 (Claude Captain): raised P4->P2 and retyped bug after confirming audit result C against main f7d70b64 — the sequence is reachable through ordinary model tools and blocks turn advancement and combat closure. Previous description (dismissal 'would keep referencing the now-absent row; decide whether dismissal should settle') superseded by the full defect class above.

Implemented inline by Claude Captain: expireDepartingParticipantTimers in transitionBondedSummon; timersExpired in result/event/tool description; 5 regression tests in bondedSummonTransitions.test.ts with negative proof (pre-fix begin_turn refuses with the anchor/target mismatch). Bond self-clock branch dropped: unreachable (start_effect forces bonded-summon effects to until-removed). verify:worktree green (6044 passed / 3 skipped). Stays in_progress until merge.

title: Admit creatures into an active combat instance (mid-combat summons and arrivals)
description: Discovered while designing eshyra-82uk (2026-10-08). start_encounter only opens a NEW combat instance, and only one instance may be active per campaign (turnAuditor). Nothing adds a combatant to the running instance, so a summon cast mid-combat (Conjure Animals in round 3, Animate Dead, Find Familiar recall from its pocket) or a reinforcement cannot become a combatant, and start_effect's actors entries need an existing combatantId. eshyra-82uk factors an internal seam that projects a campaign actor into the active instance (used by the pocket recall). This bead owns the model-facing capability: a tool (e.g. join_combat { actors: [...] , encounter creatures? }) with the same admission rules as start_encounter (absent/bonded/pocketed refusals, 0-HP rules, lifecycle carry-over), instance-only creatures as well as campaign actors, and the turn/round consequences (initiative is model-narrated; begin_turn boundaries). Design the instance-only case: combatant ids, side, and start_effect linking afterwards.
design:
DESIGN (Claude Captain, 2026-10-08)

Tool join_combat { creatures?: [...], actors?: [...] } admits creatures into the campaign's ACTIVE combat instance. At least one entry is required. It is refused when no instance is active ("start_encounter opens one"). One transaction: every entry is validated before any row is written, and a refusal leaves state unchanged.

- creatures[] (instance-only, identity encounter_instance): { rulesRef (required, must resolve as a creature record), count? (int >= 1, default 1), side (REQUIRED), faction?, displayLabel?, placement? }. HP/AC/heads come from the creature record exactly as start_encounter's template creatures do (readCreatureHp, readCreatureAc, initialHeadCount; admitCombatantLifecycle). Row id: `${instance}-${slug(rulesRef)}-${n}` with n the next free ordinal for that prefix (existence check loop, as the recall's suffix loop). Label: displayLabel ?? record name, numbered " 1".." n" when count > 1.
- actors[] (persistent campaign actors): same schema and admission rules as start_encounter actors (reuse admitCampaignActorToInstance; refuse state.combatLifecycle as start_encounter does) with `side` REQUIRED. Extra rules: refuse an actor that already has a non-absent row in this instance (it is already in this combat, alive, dead or otherwise); an actor whose only rows here are absent is admitted under the existing absent rules (new manifestation with hpCurrent > 0; bonded absent refused; pocketed refused -> recall). Row id via ONE shared helper used by both join_combat and recallPocketedCampaignActor: `${instance}-${slug(actorId)}`, else -2, -3...
- Initiative and turn order stay model-narrated (actionEconomy.ts); a joiner's turn budget row is created by its first begin_turn. The tool description says so, and says a summon's effect is recorded afterwards with start_effect using the returned combatant ids (actors[].combatantId; campaignActorId for durable summons).
- Result: { combatInstance, joined: [combatant views of the new rows] }.
- protocol.ts (system prompt) mentions start_encounter for starting combat; add one line that creatures arriving mid-combat (summons, reinforcements, a recalled familiar is automatic) join with join_combat.
Not in scope: authored encounter template reinforcement waves (encounterId), placement/geometry.

title: Dispatch: qxnc spell-sourced bonded summons with one bond per caster per spell (Sonnet 5.5, attempt 1)
description:
Implement eshyra-qxnc (read it: bd show eshyra-qxnc). Parent integration bead: eshyra-qxnc. The captain has made every design decision below. Do not re-decide them. If the code or the SRD record contradicts any of them, stop and record the contradiction in your notes rather than improvising.

HARD RULE (bd memory srd-fidelity-hard-blocker): nothing may contradict the SRD. Source: packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json, records spell:find-familiar and spell:find-steed (data.duration "Instantaneous", data.description, data.mechanics.effects[0].identity {kind: persistent-linked, maximumLinked: 1}, initialState {presence: present, link: active}, transitions). Do NOT edit records.json or any importer file. This branch is stacked on eshyra-71u1 (PR #605): recastBondedSummon already selects transitions by presence.

## Source facts
- Find Familiar: "You can't have more than one familiar at a time. If you cast this spell while you already have a familiar, you instead cause it to adopt a new form."
- Find Steed: "You can't have more than one steed bonded by this spell at a time. As an action, you can release the steed from its bond at any time, causing it to disappear."
- Both are Duration Instantaneous. The bond persists through the record's persistent-linked identity, not through a duration.

## Today (survey)
- packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts createActiveEffect, spell-source block (~3425-3460): it throws "'<name>' is instantaneous per its record; instantaneous spells leave no active effect" for any instantaneous record. Record duration/concentration binding follows (recordDuration). Check every later use of recordDuration so an instantaneous record does not then refuse an until-removed duration.
- deriveZeroHpRule (~3119) already yields 'vanish-bonded' for the zero-hp-absence transition. deriveSummonCleanup (~3154) finds no spell-ended transition for these records, so policies default to remove/remove. That is correct: release and permanent dismissal make the creature disappear. vanish-bonded already requires campaignActorId (~3859).
- recastBondedSummon (~5270): checks row.source_kind === 'spell' && row.source_ref !== input.spellRef, so ruling bonds accept any spellRef. That is the defect.
- Today the tests create bonds as ruling-sourced: packages/core/test/bondedSummonRecast.test.ts setup().bond uses source {kind: 'ruling'} and atZeroHitPoints 'vanish-bonded'.
- Tool texts: packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolStartEffect.ts (the "Do NOT use this for instantaneous spells" sentence; the actors description "A ruling-sourced creature declares its rule with atZeroHitPoints: vanish-bonded for a familiar or steed"; the atZeroHitPoints property description) and toolRecastBondedSummon.ts. Run rg -n -i "ruling-sourced|vanish-bonded|familiar|steed" packages/core/src packages/cli/src docs and update every stale sentence (DM prompt text included, if any).

## Decision (captain, 2026-10-07)
1. Persistent-linked exception, decided by the record. In the spell-source block, an instantaneous record is allowed ONLY when input.kind is 'summoning' AND some entry of record.data.mechanics.effects has kind 'summoning', identity.kind 'persistent-linked' and initialState.link 'active'. Call that the bonded-summon effect. Otherwise keep today's refusal and message, unchanged. For an allowed record:
   a. The duration must be {kind: 'until-removed'}. Refuse anything else, saying the record bonds the creature until it is released or dismissed, so the effect lasts until removed.
   b. source.actor is required (the caster the creature is bonded to). Refuse its absence.
   c. The number of actors entries must be at least 1 and at most identity.maximumLinked (when it is a positive integer). Refuse otherwise.
   d. One bond per caster per spell. Refuse when another effect, not ended (active or suppressed), has source_kind 'spell', the same source_ref, and the same stored source actor (compare the engine's stored source_actor_kind/source_actor_ref after the same normalization this create applies; check how source.actor is normalized and resolve this input the same way before comparing), and holds an active actor link. The refusal names the existing effect and says casting the spell again while the bond lasts is recast_bonded_summon (Find Familiar reforms, Find Steed restores an absent steed), and that ending that effect releases the bond. An ended effect, or one whose links are all closed, does not block.
   e. Concentration is forbidden by the record (not concentration) and the 0-HP rule is derived ('vanish-bonded'), both through the existing path. A declared atZeroHitPoints that contradicts it is refused by the existing check.
2. Recast identity. In recastBondedSummon, right after the summoning-kind check, refuse an effect whose source_kind is not 'spell'. Say the bond was not recorded from its spell, so the engine cannot tell which spell created it, and a recast applies only to a bond created with start_effect source {kind: 'spell', ref}. The existing source_ref check then binds spellRef. Keep it, and keep its message.
3. Ruling-sourced 'vanish-bonded' stays legal at creation (homebrew bonded creatures). It just cannot be recast.
4. No migration, no new event kind, no root-export change.

## Texts and docs
- toolStartEffect.ts: say instantaneous spells leave no active effect EXCEPT a bonded summon whose record keeps a persistent link (Find Familiar, Find Steed). Those are spell-sourced with duration until-removed and source.actor = the caster, one bond per caster per spell. atZeroHitPoints is derived for them, and the ruling form is for homebrew bonded creatures.
- toolRecastBondedSummon.ts: the bond must have been created from its spell, and spellRef must be that spell.
- docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md: the recastBondedSummon paragraph, plus the creation/source-validation and vanish-bonded paragraphs (rg for "ruling" and "vanish-bonded"). Re-derive every sentence against the source text and the real tool contract.

## Evidence (packages/core/test/bondedSummonRecast.test.ts; adapt setup so bonds are spell-sourced with a caster source.actor; use whatever caster participant the harness can create, a character or a combatant)
Convert the existing tests to spell-sourced bonds (steed: spell:find-steed; familiar: spell:find-familiar), with no declared atZeroHitPoints, so the derived rule is exercised. The assertions themselves stay as they are. Add these cases, asserting identities and exact values and pinning no counts:
- A steed bond (spell:find-steed), recast with spellRef spell:find-familiar and form creature:owl, is refused (/was cast from/), and the actor is unchanged, both present and absent.
- A ruling-sourced vanish-bonded bond: creation succeeds, and a recast is refused with the new message.
- A second spell:find-familiar bond for the same caster is refused while the first is active, while its familiar is absent at 0 HP, and while the effect is suppressed. After end_effect on the first, a new bond succeeds. A different caster may hold its own bond at the same time.
- A spell:find-steed bond and a spell:find-familiar bond for the same caster coexist (different spells).
- Two actors entries on one Find Familiar bond are refused (maximumLinked 1).
- A missing source.actor is refused. A non-until-removed duration is refused.
- An instantaneous record without a persistent-linked summoning effect (e.g. spell:magic-missile with kind 'summoning') is still refused with the original instantaneous message.
- atZeroHitPoints 'vanish' declared on a Find Familiar spell bond is refused (contradicts the record).
- Run the whole suite. Other tests that create ruling vanish-bonded effects must stay green unchanged.

## Procedure
Work only in this worktree (/home/jhbongaarts/src/eshyra/.worktrees/eshyra-qxnc.1, branch eshyra-qxnc.1); use worktree paths only, never the parent checkout. Run npm run verify:worktree from the worktree root BEFORE committing (it rewrites files). It must be fully green, documented skips only. Commit on this branch with a message starting "eshyra-qxnc.1 " and ending with the line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
notes:
Dispatched 2026-10-07 as a Claude Sonnet 5.5 Agent subagent, worktree .worktrees/eshyra-qxnc.1 on branch eshyra-qxnc.1 cut from eshyra-qxnc at b0e71eba (stacked on eshyra-71u1 / PR #605).
Complete, commit 0fb3f93e. activeEffects.ts: findPersistentBondEffect + createActiveEffect instantaneous exception (until-removed, source.actor, 1..maximumLinked actors, one bond per caster/spell via stored source_actor kind/ref, no normalization exists); recastBondedSummon refuses non-spell source. Texts: toolStartEffect.ts, toolRecastBondedSummon.ts, docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md. Tests: bondedSummonRecast.test.ts converted to spell-sourced bonds (derived vanish-bonded) + 11 new cases. DEVIATION: two existing tests could not keep assertions because a spell bond now reaches the spellRef check first: 'no restoring cast-again transition' (conjure-animals) and 'unknown spell' now assert /was cast from/ (renamed). Those later branches are unreachable via spell bonds. verify:worktree green: 326 files passed, 2 skipped; 5932 tests passed, 3 skipped.

title: Pact of the Chain: accept the imp/pseudodragon/quasit/sprite familiar forms (needs pact-boon persistence + curated form grant)

BLOCKED ON TWO MISSING PIECES:

title: Bonded summons: record the spell that created the bond, and enforce one bond per caster per spell
description:
Found while integrating eshyra-71u1 (2026-10-07). SCOPE NARROWED the same day (captain): this bead now owns BOND IDENTITY only. The Pact of the Chain special forms moved to their own bead (discovered-from this one), which is blocked on pact-boon persistence and a curated form grant.

DEFECT. Find Familiar and Find Steed have Duration "Instantaneous". createActiveEffect refuses an instantaneous spell as an effect source, so every bond is recorded as source kind 'ruling' (atZeroHitPoints 'vanish-bonded'). recastBondedSummon checks spellRef against the effect only when source_kind is 'spell'. So recast_bonded_summon { effectId: <steed effect>, spellRef: 'spell:find-familiar', form: 'creature:owl' } turns a bonded warhorse into an owl, from absent (s02z) and, since 71u1, from present. Sibling defect of the same class: nothing stops a second bond for the same caster and spell. The SRD says "You can't have more than one familiar at a time. If you cast this spell while you already have a familiar, you instead cause it to adopt a new form", and "You can't have more than one steed bonded by this spell at a time". Both records carry identity { kind: 'persistent-linked', maximumLinked: 1 }.

DESIGN (captain): make these bonds spell-sourced, decided by the record, never by spell name.
1. An instantaneous spell record may source a 'summoning' effect only when one of its summoning effects declares identity.kind 'persistent-linked' with initialState.link 'active'. The SRD record keeps that bond after the instant of casting. Such an effect must use duration until-removed and must have a source.actor (the caster the creature is bonded to). Every other instantaneous spell is still refused with today's message.
2. At creation, the effect may link at most identity.maximumLinked actors. The same caster may not already hold an active effect from the same spell with an active actor link; the refusal points at recast_bonded_summon.
3. recastBondedSummon refuses a bond that is not spell-sourced. The engine cannot tell which spell a ruling bond came from, and a homebrew bond has no SRD recast. The existing spell-source check then binds spellRef to the spell that created the bond.
4. The derived 0-HP rule ('vanish-bonded' from zero-hp-absence) and the default cleanup (remove/remove: release and permanent dismissal make the creature disappear) come from the record path that already exists. Ruling-sourced 'vanish-bonded' stays legal for homebrew.
Dispatch spec: the child bead.

title: Dispatch: s02z recast_bonded_summon restores an absent familiar/steed (Sonnet 5.5, attempt 1)

- Find Familiar: "When the familiar drops to 0 hit points, it disappears, leaving behind no physical form. It reappears after you cast this spell again". "If you cast this spell while you already have a familiar, you instead cause it to adopt a new form. Choose one of the forms from the above list." Transition `restore-and-reform-absent-familiar` (trigger cast-again, when presence absent + link active: presence->present, operation select-new-form, reappearancePlacement creation-placement). Casting time 1 hour (ritual).
- Find Steed: "When the steed drops to 0 hit points, it disappears ... You can also dismiss your steed at any time as an action, causing it to disappear. In either case, casting this spell again summons the same steed, restored to its hit point maximum." Transition `restore-same-steed` (cast-again, absent + link active: presence->present, operation restore-same-actor, hitPoints maximum). Casting time 10 minutes. `release-bond` sets link none: no restoration after release.
- `ambiguity:find-familiar-permanent-dismissal-after-zero-hp` stays engine-pending: do not implement permanent dismissal from 0-HP absence.

## Today
Both spells are instantaneous, so they are modelled as RULING-sourced summoning effects whose actor declares `atZeroHitPoints: 'vanish-bonded'` with a durable `campaignActorId` (packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts ~3200-3250; toolStartEffect.ts). At 0 HP the creature becomes absent while its link and effect stay active (S50). `start_encounter` refuses to admit such an absent bonded actor (packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts ~1910-1935) because the recast was not executable.

## Decision (captain, 2026-10-04): a `recast_bonded_summon` tool
Add a model-facing tool `recast_bonded_summon` (new packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolRecastBondedSummon.ts, registered like toolRefreshEffect/toolRemoveEffectTarget in toolRegistry.ts/tools.ts; check how other tools are registered and listed in any tool-inventory tests) backed by a core operation in activeEffects.ts (export through `@eshyra/core/internal` only; root export unchanged). Args: `{ effectId, spellRef, form?: string }`.
- `spellRef` must resolve in the campaign rules stack to a spell record that has a `cast-again` transition whose `when` is `presence: absent, link: active` and changes presence->present. Derive behaviour from that transition's operation, never from the spell name:
  - `restore-same-actor` with `hitPoints: 'maximum'` (Find Steed): `form` is refused. The same campaign actor returns: status alive, hpCurrent = its effective hit point maximum (the stored hpMax adjusted by exhaustion, as everywhere else). Nothing else about the actor changes (the source names only presence and hit points; conditions, exhaustion and the 0-HP rule are left as stored).
  - `select-new-form` (Find Familiar): `form` is REQUIRED and must be a `creatureRef` listed in the record's `creation.forms` (the same form as before is allowed). The same campaign actor returns with rulesRef = that creature ref, hpMax = that creature record's hit points (use the existing readCreatureHp / lookupCreatureRecord helpers in encounterCombatants.ts), hpCurrent = hpMax, status alive. Other stored state unchanged, as above.
  - Any other operation: refuse (not executable).
- Preconditions (each a clear refusal, validated before any mutation): the effect exists, is active (not ended, not suppressed: a suppressed effect -> refuse), kind 'summoning'; it holds exactly one active actor link whose campaign actor has zero-HP rule 'vanish-bonded' and status 'absent'. Refuse when the actor is present (reform of a present or pocketed familiar is NOT in scope: say so in the refusal and file a follow-up bead), when the link was released / the effect ended (S1: with no link a cast creates a new familiar or steed: use start_effect + start_encounter), and when the actor has a combatant projection in an ACTIVE combat instance (both spells take 10 minutes or longer to cast, so the recast cannot happen mid-combat; the absent combatant row is terminal and combat closure would otherwise sync 'absent' back over the restored actor — check syncCombatantActor / closeCombatInstance and prove with a test that a restore after closure survives).
- Durable writes through an engine seam in encounterCombatants.ts (e.g. `restoreBondedCampaignActor`, mirroring removeCampaignActorFromPlay ~2720) — the only path allowed to move a campaign actor from absent back to alive, and only with the active bonded link present. Keep the mirrored `combatLifecycle` JSON consistent (status, hp, zeroHpRule stays 'vanish-bonded' so it can vanish again next time).
- Audit: append a typed effect event (new kind, e.g. 'recast', with detail { spellRef, transitionId, actor, hpCurrent, hpMax, form? }) — extend the event-kind union and detail validators and any SQL CHECK on event kinds (if the event kind column has a CHECK, that needs a migration with the next free number under packages/core/data/migrations/).
- No spell-slot spending (the model uses spend_spell_slot / ritual casting separately; say so in the tool description).
- After restoration `start_encounter` admits the actor normally (it is no longer absent). Update the start_encounter refusal text (toolStartEncounter.ts description and encounterCombatants.ts message) to point at `recast_bonded_summon` instead of "which the engine cannot yet execute", and the toolStartEffect.ts / toolUpdateCombatant.ts texts that say the return is "not yet executable".

## Docs
docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md §6 (operations list) and §8/§9 (vanish-bonded paragraphs, which currently say "not yet executable (eshyra-s02z)"): describe the executed recast, its preconditions, and what it leaves unchanged. Re-derive every sentence against the source text and the real tool contract.

## Evidence
Tests (new `packages/core/test/bondedSummonRecast.test.ts`; reuse setup helpers from zeroHpVanishAndRemovePolicy.test.ts where practical) asserting identities and exact values: steed at 0 HP -> absent -> combat closed -> recast restores the same actor id to hpMax with status alive and the link still active, then start_encounter admits it; steed under exhaustion level 4 restores to the halved effective max; familiar recast with a new form (e.g. creature:bat -> creature:owl) sets that rulesRef and that record's HP; form outside the list refused; form passed for the steed refused; recast with an active combat projection refused; recast of a present familiar refused; recast after the effect ended / link released refused; non-cast-again spell refused; restored creature can vanish again at 0 HP; the event ledger has the recast event. No count-pinned assertions.

## Procedure
Work only in this worktree. Run `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing (it rewrites files); it must be fully green (documented skips only). Commit on this branch with a message starting `eshyra-s02z`, ending with the line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.

Added recast_bonded_summon tool (toolRecastBondedSummon.ts), recastBondedSummon in activeEffects.ts, restoreBondedCampaignActor seam in encounterCombatants.ts (exported via internal.ts only), migration 0041_active_effect_recast_event.sql (rebuilds active_effect_event CHECK to add 'recast'; schema.snapshot.sql regenerated), updated start_encounter/start_effect/update_combatant texts and docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md (§6 operation entry, §8, §9). Updated migration-count expectations in persistence.test.ts, migrationLegacyAdoption.test.ts, tool inventory lists in tools.test.ts. verify:worktree fully green (326 files passed, 2 skipped; 5912 tests passed, 3 skipped). title: Dispatch: 7vh3 Conjure Elemental/Fey uncontrolled successor with cast-anchored 1-hour removal (Sonnet 5.5, attempt 1)
description:
Implement eshyra-7vh3 (read it: `bd show eshyra-7vh3`). Parent integration bead: eshyra-j3yp. All design decisions below are made; do not re-decide them. If something here contradicts the code or the SRD record text, stop and record the contradiction in your notes rather than improvising.

HARD RULE (bd memory srd-fidelity-hard-blocker): nothing may contradict the SRD. Source: packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json, records `spell:conjure-elemental` and `spell:conjure-fey` (`data.description`, `data.effects[0].transitions`). Do NOT edit records.json or any importer file.

## Source facts
"If your concentration is broken, the elemental doesn't disappear. Instead, you lose control of the elemental, it becomes hostile toward you and your companions, and it might attack. An uncontrolled elemental can't be dismissed by you, and it disappears 1 hour after you summoned it." (Conjure Fey identical for the fey creature.) Record transitions: `concentration-break-loss-of-control` (trigger concentration-broken: control->uncontrolled, attitude->hostile, restriction caster-cannot-dismiss, NO effect->ended), `cast-anchored-removal` (trigger absolute-time-reached, when control uncontrolled: effect->ended, presence->absent, timer {amount 1, unit hour, anchor spell-cast}), `zero-hp-removal` (applies controlled or uncontrolled). Duration "Concentration, up to 1 hour".

## Today
A concentration break ends the effect (`finalizeEnd`, packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts ~2480, mode 'break') and the record-derived cleanupOnBreak 'release' (deriveSummonCleanup ~2625) releases the actor link: the creature stays present but nothing ever removes it at cast+1h.

## Decision (captain, 2026-10-04): successor effect
Keep F3's terminal end semantics. When finalizeEnd ends a spell-sourced effect with reason 'concentration-broken' and the spell record (derive from transitions, NOT from spell names) has an `absolute-time-reached` transition that removes presence (presence->absent) with `when.control` 'uncontrolled', then in the SAME transaction, for the actor links that this break released, create one successor effect:
- effect_id `<original>:uncontrolled` (refuse/throw on collision rather than inventing another id), kind 'summoning', display_name `<original display_name> (uncontrolled)`, source kind 'spell' with the same source_ref and source actor, NO concentration (requires_concentration 0, no owner), NOT dismissible (source: "can't be dismissed by you"), status active.
- duration timed, amount 1, unit 'hour', and the ORIGINAL effect's anchor evidence copied verbatim (anchor kind, anchor_at, anchor_game_time, anchor_elapsed_minutes, and the deadline_elapsed_minutes = original anchor + 60). The record says cast-anchored: the deadline is 1 hour after the summoning, never 1 hour after the break. The original's declared duration already had to match "1 hour", so its world-time deadline equals the cast-anchored removal time; assert that (amount 1, unit hour) and fail closed otherwise. Round-unit or missing elapsed evidence -> fail closed with a clear error (do not guess).
- an active actor link for each released creature (same target_kind/target_ref/projection_ref/campaign_actor_id as the released link) with cleanup_on_end 'remove' and cleanup_on_break 'remove'; the creature also becomes a target if it was a target of the original.
- audit: the original's 'ended' event records the successor id; the successor's 'created' event records the predecessor id and the record transition id ('cast-anchored-removal'). Extend the typed event-detail validators rather than bypassing them.
The successor must not be created through the public createActiveEffect validation path that requires concentration for a "Concentration, up to" spell; write it through an internal path that still validates everything else. If validateActiveEffectDurableState or a strict read re-derives concentration from the spell record and would flag the successor, add an explicit durable marker (new migration `packages/core/data/migrations/00NN_*.sql` with the next free number, e.g. a nullable `predecessor_effect_id` column with a CHECK) and teach validation to accept exactly that case — never weaken the check for other effects.

Consequences that must then hold with no further special-casing (verify each in tests):
- advancing world time to the deadline (`advanceWorldTime` / `expireElapsedWorldEffects`) ends the successor 'expired' and its 'remove' cleanup makes the creature absent; one minute earlier it is still present; explicit `expired` before the deadline is refused.
- the creature dropping to 0 HP while uncontrolled still vanishes (closeActorLinkAtZeroHp finds the successor link) and the successor ends 'source-removed'.
- `end_effect` with 'dismissed' on the successor is refused (not dismissible); 'dispelled' / 'ruled' still work.
- the caster can start a new concentration effect (the successor holds no concentration).
- every concentration-break route produces the successor: failed damage save (resolveConcentrationCheck), incapacitation/death life-state hook, new-concentration replacement, voluntary break, and owner removal at combat closure if that route uses reason concentration-broken (check ~5199-5220 and closeCombatInstance; if combat closure releases the instance-only creature anyway, document what happens and test it).
- an ordinary end (expired at the 1-hour deadline while still controlled, dismissed) still removes the creature (existing derived cleanupOnEnd 'remove'); no successor.
- Spells whose break transition removes presence (e.g. Conjure Animals) are untouched: no successor.

## Model-facing text and docs
Update descriptions that state break/release behaviour (toolResolveConcentration.ts, toolEndEffect.ts, toolStartEffect.ts and any result text that reports cleanup actions) so the model learns that a broken concentration on Conjure Elemental/Fey leaves the creature present, uncontrolled and hostile under successor effect `<id>:uncontrolled`, which removes it 1 hour after it was summoned and which the caster cannot dismiss. Results that report the break should name the successor id. docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md: update §2 (the "Conjure Elemental distinction"), §4/§9 (S1 summons: the cast-anchored removal is executed) and remove the "not yet" wording. Re-derive every sentence against the source text and the real tool contract.

## Evidence
Add tests (packages/core/test/zeroHpVanishAndRemovePolicy.test.ts or a sibling `conjureUncontrolledRemoval.test.ts`; look at activeEffects.test.ts helpers for world-clock setup) asserting identities and exact values: successor id, kind, no concentration, dismissible false, deadline_elapsed_minutes = original anchor + 60 (create the effect, advance 20 minutes, break concentration, check the deadline is still anchor+60, not break+60), expiry at exactly the deadline makes the creature absent, 59 minutes after the summoning it is still present, 0-HP vanish ends the successor, dismissal refused, Conjure Fey parity, Conjure Animals unchanged, each break route above. No count-pinned assertions.

## Procedure
Work only in this worktree. Run `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing (it rewrites files); it must be fully green (documented skips only). Commit on this branch with a message starting `eshyra-7vh3`, ending with the line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
notes:
Completed on branch eshyra-j3yp.2. activeEffects.ts: finalizeEnd (break mode) calls new createUncontrolledSuccessor after cleanupOwnedState; derives the transition from the record (absolute-time-reached, presence->absent, when.control only 'uncontrolled', timer) via extended recordTransitions (whenControl, timer); fails closed if original duration/anchor/elapsed evidence != record timer; throws on id collision; writes through internal SQL (not createActiveEffect); EffectCleanupSummary.successorEffectId; ended event gets successorEffectId, successor created event gets predecessorEffectId + recordTransitionId. No migration needed (durable validation never re-derives concentration from the record). Tool descriptions (end_effect, start_effect, resolve_concentration) and docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md (§2, §9) updated. New test file packages/core/test/conjureUncontrolledRemoval.test.ts (14 tests: Elemental/Fey parity, exact deadline anchor+60 after break at +20, 59min alive/60 absent, early expired refused, 0HP vanish, dismissal refused/dispelled/ruled ok, new concentration allowed, ordinary end no successor, Conjure Animals none, id collision, routes: failed save, caster death, replacement, combat closure). Two existing tests updated (activeEffects.test.ts release-on-break: released creature can no longer be re-owned by a new effect, it is owned by the successor; zeroHpVanishAndRemovePolicy: vanished.effectId is now fx:uncontrolled). Combat closure note: a creature with a durable campaign-actor identity has the successor link rebound to the campaign actor and is still removed at cast+1h (tested); an instance-only creature link is released at closure per existing behaviour (successor then has no live link). Verification: npm run verify:worktree fully green (325 files passed, 2 skipped; 5895 tests passed, 3 skipped). Deviations: none.
Captain review fix (2026-10-04): the successor creation threw inside the concentration break when the original anchor was not exactly 'spell-cast' (start_effect also admits 'effect-created' and 'trigger-occurred' for hour timers), which would roll back the write that broke concentration (e.g. the caster's damage). Fixed: createActiveEffect now gates such spells to a 1-hour timer anchored to 'spell-cast' or 'effect-created' (SUMMONING_MOMENT_ANCHORS), and the break-time check accepts both. Tests added in conjureUncontrolledRemoval.test.ts; docs and start_effect text updated.

title: Declare or disposition undeclared condition-name reference leaves outside condition records
description: Found while designing condition->condition relationships (docs/design/condition-condition-relationships.md C6, eshyra-o9bd.19.3.4.2). Condition-name leaves with the same fail-open shape (no relationship declaration, so discovery never follows them) exist outside condition records. Snapshot at de7df402 (membership must come from a generated query, not these counts): creature /actions|legendaryActions|reactions|traits/*/mechanics/conditions/*/condition (~359 leaves) -> owner eshyra-o9bd.19.4.2/.3; ancestry /traits/*/mechanics/conditions/*/condition (5) -> eshyra-o9bd.19.3.1; magic-item /mechanics/effects/*/conditions/* (18, includes non-condition values suffocating/any-disease) and /mechanics/effects/*/failedSaveCondition (9, includes 'one exhaustion level') -> eshyra-o9bd.19.4.5. Also: (a) whether /mechanics/effects/*/condition belongs in LEGACY_RELATIONSHIP_BEARING_POINTER_SHAPES (it is overloaded: prose preconditions in magic-item/creature/feature/action/spell, condition names in condition records) with explicit not-a-reference declarations per kind; (b) the five existing mechanics.conditions record-name declarations carry a placeholder relation 'condition' always overridden by the sibling (required-field-filled-mechanically idiom) - migrate them to relationByFieldValue or a declared vocabulary once C1 lands. Uses the C1/C2 resolver generalization from the condition design.
notes: 2026-10-09 bounded review (Claude Captain, main a961fb0b; requested by the resume campaign). QUESTION: do the undeclared condition-name leaves violate an operative live-discovery invariant, or are they a bounded limitation ADR 0020 permits to remain disclosed? FINDINGS: (1) Producer/gate: the only coverage gate over relationship-bearing leaves, assertRecordRelationshipDeclarationsCoverBoundedShapes (packages/core/src/rules/recordRelationships.ts ~L574-623), covers exactly seven top-level pointer shapes incl. '/mechanics/conditions/*/condition'; the nested creature '/actions|legendaryActions|reactions|traits/*/mechanics/conditions/*/condition', ancestry '/traits/*/...', and magic-item '/mechanics/effects/*/conditions/*' and failedSaveCondition leaves are outside it, and its own doc forbids widening it into a coverage claim over RulesRecord.data (ADR 0020 section 6). The manifest rule 'every declared reference yields exactly one typed outcome' binds declared references only. No violation of either. (2) Accepted authority: docs/design/condition-condition-relationships.md C6 and section 7 explicitly scope these leaves OUT of the condition repair and record them here; no domain bead AC (19.4.2, 19.4.3, 19.3.1, 19.4.5) requires them (19.4.3 and 19.4.5 notes defer them to this bead). (3) Consumer/consequence: expansion is one hop (expandTypedRelationships), so a creature/ancestry/item record seeded by state-ref does not pull in the condition record it may impose; the condition is still reachable by name-mention signals (signals.ts ~L150-190, player input), by DM lookup_rules on the condition, and the imposing record's verbatim text names the condition. Consequence is reduced discoverability of condition text in creature-driven situations, not a wrong rule, wrong state, or false provenance. DISPOSITION: legitimate bounded discovery limitation under ADR 0020 (no universal discovery completeness); retain independent ownership here; NOT re-freeze-blocking; it must be disclosed as an explicit unresolved discovery limit (re-freeze bar #9) in the candidate bundle (eshyra-o9bd.19.6.3). Item (b) (placeholder relation 'condition' always overridden by sibling) produces no wrong edge; it is a representation-quality item kept here, not a live defect. No dependency change.
