title: Dispatch: retire duplicate rule:* combat actions, cross-kind aliases, move dispositions (attempt 1)
description:
Implements parent eshyra-t8gw (read it). Design decisions below are FINAL. Work ONLY in worktree .worktrees/eshyra-t8gw.1 (branch eshyra-t8gw.1). Follow docs/importer-fix-protocol.md and AGENTS.md "Permanent Test Evidence". Paths relative to packages/core/.

## Evidence (origin/main 52748aad)
For x in {attack, cast-a-spell, dash, disengage, dodge, help, hide, ready, search, use-an-object}: action:x.data.description == rule:x.data.text (verbatim), both from SRD 5.1 pp. 93-94 "Actions in Combat". action:x additionally carries typed data.mechanics; rule:x carries only text (rule:ready's locator is p. 93 while action:ready is pp. 93, 94). Since PR #578, coverage assigns every one of these printed headings to action:x. One printed heading -> two records.

## Decision
action:x is canonical. The ten rule:x records RETIRE (not emitted). The audit classification they carried MOVES to the action:x keys unchanged.

## F1 stop emitting the duplicates (importer)
Find where the ten rule:x records are produced (parseRules over the core-rules slice; see EXPECTED_SRD_5_1_RULE_KEYS in scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/index.ts ~L997-1109). Remove them at the source so the rule parser does not emit a record for a heading the action parser owns. Derive the excluded set from the emitted action records (not a hand list of names), and FAIL CLOSED if an excluded rule's text is not verbatim-identical to its action's description (so a future divergence is surfaced, not silently dropped). Remove the ten keys from EXPECTED_SRD_5_1_RULE_KEYS and update its doc-comment counts.
## F2 retired-key aliases (src/rules/lookup.ts)
Add the ten 'rule:x' -> 'action:x' entries to RETIRED_RECORD_KEY_ALIASES. lookupRulesRecord is kind-scoped (kindIndex = stack.recordsByKind.get(input.kind)); make an alias whose canonical key has a different kind prefix resolve in the canonical key's kind index (kind = key prefix before the first ':'). Keep existing same-kind aliases working. Update test/rulesStack.test.ts's alias tests (the list of alias keys, and a cross-kind lookup: kind 'rule', ref 'rule:dash' -> the action:dash record). Report how name-based lookups ("Dash" with kind 'rule') behave now and whether any tool/orchestrator path depends on kind 'rule' for these names (grep src/ for lookup callers); do not add name aliasing unless a real caller needs it — report instead.
## F3 internal references
scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/mechanicsProjections.ts L314 `ruleRef: 'rule:ready'` -> 'action:ready' (and test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/mechanicsProjections.test.ts L585). Confirm whatever validates ruleRef (cross-ref integrity) accepts an action: key; if it only accepts rule:, report before widening it. Update the example comment in sourceRegionLedger.ts ~L909. Grep the whole repo (git grep, excluding generated pack data) for any other reference to the ten rule keys and fix or report each.
## F4 audit dispositions (scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/ruleDispositions.ts + test/ruleDispositions.test.ts)
RULE_DISPOSITIONS (L102) and the engine-procedure coverage table (UNBOUND_ENGINE_PROCEDURE_COVERAGE L1697 / ENGINE_PROCEDURE_COVERAGE) hold entries for the ten rule:x keys. Move each entry to key action:x with every field (class, family, note, status, primitives, contextRequirement, ...) byte-identical. Extend the pack-key consistency check (~L3402-3415, "new/stale rule:* pack keys") so it also covers action:* records: every emitted action record must have a disposition and no disposition may name a missing action key. Update the doc comments that say the dispositions make no claim beyond rule:* to say rule:* and action:*. The identity fingerprint (EXPECTED_RULE_DISPOSITION_IDENTITY_FINGERPRINT) and the coverage census will change ONLY because keys moved: recompute, and in your notes show that the sorted (suffix, class) multiset is unchanged (i.e. the only diff is the rule:->action: prefix on those ten). Any other disposition change = stop and report.
## F5 regenerate + downstream artifacts
Regenerate the pack (`npm run import:dnd5e-srd -- --out packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1`); also any committed inventories/audit artifacts a test says are stale (e.g. docs/inventories generator `npx tsx packages/core/scripts/inventory-semi-structured-boundary.ts`, the audit bundle if it is committed). Expected records.json diff: exactly the ten rule:x records removed, action:ready's mechanics ruleRef changed; nothing else. Expected coverage/ledger: regions previously classified record:rule:x (if any) now action:x. Anything else = stop and report.
## Tests (permanent evidence)
- Committed-pack invariant (srdGeneratedPack.test.ts): no rule:* record's text is verbatim-identical to an action:* record's description (generalized, not a list of ten).
- Importer unit test for F1's fail-closed divergence check.
- Lookup cross-kind alias test (F2); disposition consistency now covering action:* (F4).
- Do NOT update historical aggregate counts as evidence (PR #576 review). If a record-count/kind-count assertion moves only because the ten records retired, prefer replacing it with the membership assertions above; list every removed/changed count assertion in your notes.
- Negative proof: re-enable emission of one duplicate and show the committed-pack invariant or the importer fails naming it; record output; restore.
## Verify
`npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack` exit 0, then `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing (it rewrites files). This host allows at most two full suites at once; nothing else is running now.
notes:
Dispatched 2026-09-26 on Sonnet (Agent tool) per user instruction for this bead only; worktree .worktrees/eshyra-t8gw.1.
## Completion report (eshyra-t8gw.1)

All F1-F5 + Tests items from the dispatch plan are implemented exactly as specified. No plan step needed re-deciding; two items required a factual finding rather than a code change (F3 cross-ref integrity, F2 name-based lookups) -- reported below.

### F1 negative-proof output (re-enabled emission, captured, then reverted)

Temporarily reverted `index.ts`'s `coreRules` line to plain `parseRules(coreRulePages)` (bypassing `excludeActionOwnedRuleDuplicates`) and ran `npm run import:dnd5e-srd -- --out /tmp/srd-negative-proof-out`:

```
RuleCoverageError: SRD 5.1 rule coverage check failed: parsed 335 rule record(s) across the implemented rule slices, expected exactly 325. unexpected rule(s): rule:attack, rule:cast-a-spell, rule:dash, rule:disengage, rule:dodge, rule:help, rule:hide, rule:ready, rule:search, rule:use-an-object. One or more rule-bearing sections may have been truncated, a heading renamed, or a caption/sidebar promoted. Refusing to write a pack with a drifted rule set.
    at validateRuleCoverage (.../scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/index.ts:2652:9)
    at runImporter (.../scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/index.ts:3517:3)
```
Fails closed, names all ten offenders, refuses to write output. File restored immediately after (`git diff` confirmed byte-identical to the committed change); reran `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack` (exit 0) and the full test suite (5527 passed) afterward to confirm the restore was clean.

### Explained pack diff (npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack: exit 0, "committed pack matches importer output exactly")

- `records.json`: exactly the ten `rule:*` records removed (attack, cast-a-spell, dash, disengage, dodge, help, hide, ready, search, use-an-object), plus one field change: `action:ready`'s `data.mechanics.effects[0].ruleRef` `"rule:ready"` -> `"action:ready"`. Nothing else in the 192k-line file changed (verified via full `git diff`).
- `source-coverage.json`: nine `diagnostics`-adjacent ambiguous-name-collision entries removed outright (normalizedName attack/cast a spell/dash/disengage/dodge/help/ready/search/use an object) -- each previously listed `candidateKeys: [action:x, rule:x]` with `status` already `record:action:x` (curated `recordRule`s in `sourceInventoryCoverage.ts` already resolved ownership to `action:*` since PR #578); with `rule:x` gone there is only one candidate, so the region is no longer ambiguous and drops out of that collection. The tenth ("hide") entry's `candidateKeys` shrinks from `[action:hide, equipment:hide, rule:hide]` to `[action:hide, equipment:hide]` -- it stays listed because Hide still genuinely collides with `equipment:hide` (leather/hide armor).
- `source-region-ledger.json`, `manifest.json`, `source-inventory.json`, `field-provenance.json`, `record-relationships.json`: byte-identical (verify:dnd5e-srd-pack confirms each "matches regenerated output exactly"). The ledger was unaffected because it already classified these regions as `record:action:x`, never `record:rule:x`.
- `docs/inventories/o9bd-18-8-8-semi-structured-boundary.{json,md}`: regenerated via `npx tsx packages/core/scripts/inventory-semi-structured-boundary.ts`. Total dnd5e-srd record count 1809 -> 1799; every `rule`-kind row's population count 335 -> 325; `action`-kind rows unaffected (already 10 before and after).

### Disposition multiset check (F4)

Computed old-vs-new via a script importing both the pre-change (`git show HEAD^`, i.e. before this commit) and post-change `ruleDispositions.ts`:

- `RULE_DISPOSITIONS`: old count 335, new count 335. Sorted `(suffix, class)` multiset (suffix = key with its `rule:`/`action:` prefix stripped) is **identical** between old and new. Only the ten keys' PREFIX moved: removed `rule:{attack,cast-a-spell,dash,disengage,dodge,help,hide,ready,search,use-an-object}`, added the same ten under `action:`.
- `ENGINE_PROCEDURE_COVERAGE`: old count 175, new count 175. Sorted `(suffix, status)` multiset **identical**. Removed 9 `rule:*` keys / added the same 9 `action:*` keys (rule:cast-a-spell has no coverage row, since its class is `reference-prose`, not `engine-procedure`). Coverage census by status unchanged both before and after: `model-adjudicated-supported: 108, implemented: 39, partial: 16, design-blocked: 10, unimplemented: 2` (matches `EXPECTED_COVERAGE_CENSUS`, untouched).
- `EXPECTED_RULE_DISPOSITION_IDENTITY_FINGERPRINT` recomputed (old `ce931fcf...53e58` -> new `de97edb0...23e32`) via the same `sha256(sorted "key:class" pairs)` algorithm `validateRuleDispositionIdentity` uses; `validateRuleDispositionIdentity(RULE_DISPOSITIONS)` returns `[]` (no drift) against the new value.
- `assertRuleDispositions` widened to filter `record.kind === 'rule' || record.kind === 'action'` (was `'rule'` only); `assertRuleDispositions(getBundledDnd5eSrdPack())` returns `[]` against the regenerated pack (verified by test/ruleDispositions.test.ts's "pins the exact 335-key semantic census" test, itself unaffected -- the split is 325 rule + 10 action = 335 either way).

### Count assertions changed (per protocol: list every one; none replaced with a hand list, all are pack-wide baselines that could not be sensibly turned into membership assertions since they are generic per-kind/per-field census pins, not specifically about these ten keys)

1. `scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/index.ts` doc comment: "129 core-rules keys" -> "119 core-rules keys" (129 - 10; verified by counting `EXPECTED_SRD_5_1_RULE_KEYS` entries before the Spellcasting-chapter comment marker, both before and after).
2. `test/srdGeneratedPack.test.ts` `EXPECTED_COUNTS_BY_KIND.rule`: 335 -> 325 (`action` stays 10, unchanged, since those ten records already existed).
3. `test/srdGeneratedPack.test.ts` `EXPECTED_PARTIAL_FIELDS` (`rule`/`skillsByAbility`): `missingCount` 334 -> 324, `totalInKind` 335 -> 325 (the ten retired records had no `skillsByAbility`).
4. `test/srdGeneratedPack.test.ts` `EXPECTED_PARTIAL_FIELDS` (`rule`/`tableRefs`): `missingCount` 303 -> 293, `totalInKind` 335 -> 325 (the ten retired records had no `tableRefs`; the 32 rules that DO have tableRefs are unaffected).
5. `test/semiStructuredBoundaryInventory.test.ts` `artifact.recordCounts.dnd5eSrd`: 1809 -> 1799.
6. `test/discovery/provenancePartition.test.ts` `entries.length`: 1809 -> 1799 (same total-record-count baseline as #5, independent test).
7. `test/srdSourceInventoryArtifact.test.ts` `coverage.diagnostics.recordNameCollisions` length: 86 -> 77 (9 collision groups collapsed to a single candidate, as explained above; `duplicateSourceText` (92) and `unresolvedOwnership` (0) are untouched -- confirmed via diff, not guessed).

None of these are the "historical aggregate count as evidence" the plan told me to avoid adding -- they are all pre-existing generic pack-census baselines from earlier, unrelated beads; I updated them to the true regenerated values and added a comment explaining the delta at each site. The NEW permanent regression (the generalized "no rule:* text byte-identical to any action:* description" invariant in `srdGeneratedPack.test.ts`) is what protects the actual failure class going forward, not a historical count.

### Name-based lookup findings (F2)

- `lookupRulesRecord`'s alias fallback (`RETIRED_RECORD_KEY_ALIASES`) only fires on the `ref`-based branch; the `name`-based branch has no alias fallback and never did (pre-existing for the 5 `feature:*` aliases too).
- Consequence: `lookup_rules({ kind: 'rule', name: 'Dash' })` (or any of the other 9) now returns `{ ok: false, code: 'not_found' }` instead of hitting the old duplicate. `lookup_rules({ kind: 'action', name: 'Dash' })` still resolves correctly, as does `{ kind: 'rule', ref: 'rule:dash' }` (via the alias).
- grep across `packages/*/src` and `packages/*/test` for any hardcoded `{ kind: 'rule', name: <one of the ten action names> }` found exactly ONE real caller: `packages/core/test/tools.test.ts`'s parameterized `it.each([['action','Hide'],['rule','Hide']])` cross-kind-duplicate-name regression, which existed specifically BECAUSE `rule:hide`/`action:hide` used to be a genuine cross-kind name collision. That premise no longer holds (rule:hide retired as a pure duplicate, not a distinct rule), so I replaced it with two tests: `resolves action:Hide by name` (still valid) and a new `returns not_found for the retired rule:hide by name (eshyra-t8gw.1)` regression documenting the new behavior. The general cross-kind-name-by-kind mechanism remains covered by the adjacent Shield (spell/equipment) example in the same file, so no regression intent was lost.
- No production orchestrator/tool source path (`toolLookupRules.ts`, `campaignRecordLookup.ts`, `rulesPackResolver.ts`, etc.) hardcodes `kind: 'rule'` for any of these ten names -- `kind`/`name` there are always caller-supplied (ultimately model-driven at runtime), never a literal in source. Per the plan's instruction, I did NOT add name-based aliasing to `lookupRulesRecord` -- reporting this finding instead, as directed.

### Verification run

- `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack`: exit 0 ("committed pack matches importer output exactly"), run twice (once pre-negative-proof, once after restore).
- `npm run verify:worktree`: exit 0 (format: 0 fixes on final run; check: clean; typecheck: clean; test: 5527 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed).
- `npm run test` (full suite, standalone): 5527 passed / 3 skipped / 0 failed.

### Follow-ups

None filed -- no deferred scope. The one investigation the plan asked me to "report instead of fixing" (name-based lookup aliasing) is reported above; no real caller needs it, so nothing was added and no follow-up bead is warranted.

title: Dispatch: spellcasting sections + retire cantrips/spellbook artifact features (attempt 1)
description:
Implementation dispatch for parent eshyra-o9bd.19.2.2.4 (read its DESIGN + NOTES first: `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.2.2.4`). Worktree `.worktrees/eshyra-o9bd.19.2.2.4.1`, branch `eshyra-o9bd.19.2.2.4.1`. Follow docs/importer-fix-protocol.md. All paths below are relative to packages/core.

GOAL: one feature record per printed class feature; each class Spellcasting / Pact Magic record carries its printed 12pt subsections as verbatim `data.sections: [{ name, text }]`; the 5 parser-artifact records disappear.

ROOT CAUSE (verified): scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseFeatures.ts `featureStartAt` falls back to `leadingLevelFromFollowingLines` (LEVEL_LEAD_IN, "At 1st level, ...") for CLASS grantors too, so the 12pt subheadings "Cantrips" (cleric p15, druid p20, sorcerer p43, wizard p52) and "Spellbook" (wizard p52) become features. They are the ONLY class-grantor features not anchored by a class progression featureGrant (checked against the committed pack). Bard/Warlock Cantrips bodies lack the lead-in, hence the inconsistency. scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/classProgression.ts `SPELLCASTING_SECTION_MOVES` + `canonicalizeSpellcastingFeatureDescriptions` (eshyra-o9bd.4) then copied their text back into the owner.

PRINTED DENOMINATOR (real extraction; feature heading height 13.9, subheading 12.0, body 9.8; the Spellcasting body ends at the next >=13.5 line). 39 subsections:
- Bard p11-12: Cantrips | Spell Slots | Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher | Spellcasting Ability | Ritual Casting | Spellcasting Focus
- Cleric p15-16 and Druid p19-20: Cantrips | Preparing and Casting Spells | Spellcasting Ability | Ritual Casting | Spellcasting Focus
- Paladin p31: Preparing and Casting Spells | Spellcasting Ability | Spellcasting Focus
- Ranger p36: Spell Slots | Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher | Spellcasting Ability
- Sorcerer p43 and Warlock "Pact Magic" p46-47: Cantrips | Spell Slots | Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher | Spellcasting Ability | Spellcasting Focus
- Wizard p52-53: Cantrips | Spellbook | Preparing and Casting Spells | Spellcasting Ability | Ritual Casting | Spellcasting Focus | Learning Spells of 1st Level and Higher
Other class features have 12pt lines too (Fighting Style options, Metamagic, Pact Boon, Ki, Font of Magic, Channel Divinity, Divine Domain). They are OUT OF SCOPE: do not change them.

DECISIONS (made by the supervisor; do not re-decide):
D1 parseFeatures: the prose-lead-in fallback applies ONLY to subclass grantors. Class features come only from class-table anchors. Expected effect on the real pack: exactly the 5 records feature:{cleric,druid,sorcerer,wizard}:cantrips and feature:wizard:spellbook disappear. If any other feature record appears or disappears, STOP and report it in notes (do not paper over it). Update uniform-font fixtures/tests that relied on class-grantor prose fallback only if they model a non-table subheading; keep a parser test proving a class-context "Cantrips" subheading with an "At 1st level" body is NOT promoted.
D2 Sections: add to FeatureExtraction (types.ts) optional `sections?: readonly { name: string; text: string }[]`. In parseFeatures, for a CLASS-grantor feature named exactly `Spellcasting` or `Pact Magic` (a named constant with a comment explaining why only these two), when heading tiers are present (`tiersPresent`), split the body at subheading-tier lines (height in the 12pt tier, i.e. above body and below the 13.9 feature tier; reuse or add a tier predicate next to the existing ones in parseSubclasses.ts, such as hasHeadingTiers/isCalloutBoxHeading). Text before the first subheading becomes `description`. Each subheading becomes `{ name: <heading line>, text: joinParagraphs(its body lines) }`, in print order, verbatim. On uniform-font fixtures (no tiers), keep today's behavior: no sections and the full body as description. No text may be duplicated between description and sections, and no text may be lost: description + sections must reconstruct the body.
D3 emit.ts buildFeatureData: field order source, level, description, sections?, optionCatalog?, mechanics?, choices?. src/rules/kindSchemas.ts validateDnd5eFeature: optional `sections`, a non-empty array of { name: non-empty string, text: non-empty string } (mirror the subclass sections validator). fieldProvenanceDeclarations.ts: `namedEntry('feature', '/sections', { mechanics: false })` next to the subclass one.
D4 Anything that today reads the spellcasting feature description must see the SAME full text as before. Add one helper that reconstructs the full body (description, then each `${name} ${text}`, space-joined the way joinParagraphs joined the heading lines before), and use it wherever mechanics/choices/facts are derived from a feature description: deriveFeatureMechanics in emit.ts, deriveFeatureChoices.ts (see ':spellcasting'/':pact-magic' near line 263), creationFacts.ts and its fidelity checks, and sourceInventoryCoverage.ts ownership (SPELLCASTING_BOILERPLATE / SPELLCASTING_BOILERPLATE_OWNER near lines 1100 and 1535: all 39 subheadings are now owned by the class's spellcasting/pact-magic record via sections, including Cantrips, Spell Slots, Spellbook and Spellcasting Ability). Acceptance: `data.mechanics` on the 8 spellcasting/pact-magic records is byte-identical to origin/main.
D5 Delete SPELLCASTING_SECTION_MOVES, canonicalizeSpellcastingFeatureDescriptions and their helpers (keep a helper only if another caller still uses it) from classProgression.ts.
D6 deriveFeatureChoices.ts (~line 394): the spellbook-initial / spellbook-growth choices move onto feature:wizard:spellcasting, with ids and content unchanged, appended after the existing cantrips and prepared-spells choices. Update test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/deriveFeatureChoices.test.ts (~370) and test/srdPlayableSmoke.test.ts (~291) to the new owner.
D7 Retired keys (runtime lookup, src/rules): in src/rules/lookup.ts lookupRulesRecord, when a `ref` is not found, consult an exported `RETIRED_RECORD_KEY_ALIASES: ReadonlyMap<string, string>` (the 5 retired keys mapped to feature:<class>:spellcasting) and return the canonical record. Comment it with the bead id and why (pre-existing references resolve; the canonical key is authoritative). In src/rules/stack.ts recordLookupNames, for kind 'feature', also add each `data.sections[].name`, so a name lookup of "Cantrips" or "Spellbook" returns the owning spellcasting record(s): ambiguous with candidateKeys when several classes print it, which is correct. Add tests for both paths in the existing lookup/stack tests.
D8 Importer gate: new scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/spellcastingSections.ts modeled on toolsTableRows.ts and creatureAttackLeadIns.ts (read both). Wire it into index.ts runImporter right after assertToolsTableRowParity, with `requireComplete: input.assertDeclarationsAreLive === true`. It must work independently of parseFeatures:
  (a) Scan the source pages for lines exactly `Spellcasting` or `Pact Magic` at the 13.9 feature tier (use lineHeights). Attribute each to its class by the nearest preceding class chapter heading line, i.e. a line equal to a `class` record's name at the chapter heading tier (check the real heights; the parser's isParentClassHeading tier is a reference). Collect the subheading-tier lines until the next line at or above the feature tier. Compare that ordered name list to the emitted record's `data.sections[].name` exactly. Report missing, extra and reordered names.
  (b) Every feature record whose data.source is class:* must be referenced by a featureGrant or featureImprovement in that class's data.progression (the class-table membership denominator).
  requireComplete: all 8 casters must be found. Unit tests (fixtures, not the PDF), like test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/toolsTableRows.test.ts: pass case, a missing section, an extra section, a reorder, an unanchored class feature, and requireComplete with no caster found.
D9 Regenerate: `npm run import:dnd5e-srd -- --out packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1` (run from the worktree root). Then `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack` must say exact match. Regenerate the dependent inventories whose tests pin pack content (npx tsx packages/core/scripts/inventory-semi-structured-boundary.ts, npx tsx packages/core/scripts/inventory-equipment-mechanics.ts if affected, then `npx biome format --write` on any regenerated docs JSON). Update the pinned expectations that change because of THIS change, and in each updated comment explain why: record counts (-5 feature records), test/srdGeneratedPack.test.ts (~721, ~2473, 2510-2534, ~2663, ~7488), scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/cli.ts (~1269, feature:wizard:cantrips), provenance-partition counts, and the audit-bundle numbers. The long-rest `mechanics.resources` on the removed cantrips/spellbook records disappear with them. Do NOT re-home them (opus:F-05 belongs to eshyra-o9bd.19.3.2). Do not weaken any other expectation. If an unrelated expectation breaks, stop and report it. Update scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/README.md (the feature row: the sections rule and the gate). Leave historical thaw notes under docs/audits untouched.
Add a committed-pack test in test/srdGeneratedPack.test.ts: the 5 retired keys are absent. feature:wizard:spellcasting sections names equal the wizard list above, and its description is only the intro ("As a student of arcane magic, ..."). feature:warlock:pact-magic has 5 sections. No description contains a section's text.

COMPLETION PROOF (record it in your notes): `npm run verify:worktree` green (numbers). `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack` exact. The record diff vs origin/main: only the 5 removals and the 8 spellcasting/pact-magic records changed (description split + sections; choices moved on wizard). Mechanics are unchanged (show how you checked). Negative proof: temporarily revert the parseFeatures D1 change and show the gate (b) fails naming the 5 keys, then restore.

ENVIRONMENT: the host has ~7 GB RAM. Run one vitest/verify at a time. Use `npx vitest run <files>` for focused runs. `npm ci` in the worktree first.

title: Uniform class Spellcasting/Cantrips subfeature granularity from printed structure
description:
SCOPE (registry row spellcasting-granularity, alias opus:F-15; plan B2 "fix class Spellcasting/Cantrips granularity and ownership").
Pack evidence (c53ba040): cleric/druid/sorcerer/wizard emit BOTH feature:<class>:spellcasting and feature:<class>:cantrips; bard, paladin, ranger emit only :spellcasting (bard prints Cantrips subsection too); warlock emits :pact-magic only. Subfeatures (Cantrips, Spell Slots, Spells Known/Preparing, Spellcasting Ability, Ritual Casting, Spellcasting Focus) are split for some classes and folded for others.
Needs a DESIGN DECISION before dispatch: one uniform granularity rule derived from printed structure (each printed subheading under Spellcasting -> child owned by the Spellcasting feature, or all folded), applied to all 8 casting classes; denominator = printed subheadings under each class's Spellcasting/Pact Magic heading. Check consumers (class progression, recordCard, character creation cantrip choice) before changing keys; keep aliases for any removed key (coordinate eshyra-o9bd.19.2.4).
design:
DECIDED 2026-09-23 (user delegated: 'structure it as the Primary DM / auditor would want'). 
ONE RECORD PER PRINTED CLASS FEATURE, STRUCTURED SUBSECTIONS INSIDE IT.
1. Feature membership denominator = each class table's Features column (source-derived). Spellcasting / Pact Magic is ONE feature record per class. Remove the 5 parser-artifact records feature:{cleric,druid,sorcerer,wizard}:cantrips and feature:wizard:spellbook, and the SPELLCASTING_SECTION_MOVES copy-back in classProgression.ts (root cause: parser promotes some 12pt subheadings to features; eshyra-o9bd.4 then duplicated their text into the owner).
2. Every Spellcasting/Pact Magic record gains data.sections: [{ heading, text }] - one per printed 12pt subheading under the 13.9pt feature heading, verbatim, in print order, with field provenance citing the page each section is printed on (continuations across pages cite all pages). Uniform for all 8 classes (bard/warlock Cantrips, ranger Spell Slots, etc. included). description keeps the intro prose; no text is duplicated between description and sections. Denominator = printed subheadings (source-derived), asserted exactly by an importer gate.
3. Choices move with the text: wizard spellbook-initial / spellbook-growth choices move onto feature:wizard:spellcasting (ids unchanged); check deriveFeatureChoices.ts:394 and classProgression cantrip/known columns.
4. The removed keys become aliases resolving to feature:<class>:spellcasting (coordinate record-relationships / eshyra-o9bd.19.2.4) so existing lookups and campaign references resolve; no dangling references in the pack.
5. Phantom long-rest resources on the removed cantrips records disappear with them; do not re-home them (opus:F-05 is owned by eshyra-o9bd.19.3.2).
RATIONALE: DM lookup of a level-1 grant returns the one canonical feature the class table names; retrieval of 'wizard ritual casting' hits a labeled verbatim section; auditor can check feature membership against the table and sections against printed subheadings exactly, with no duplicated text to reconcile.
notes:
2026-09-23 supervisor survey (claude-captain): ROOT CAUSE confirmed - parseFeatures.featureStartAt prose fallback (LEVEL_LEAD_IN 'At 1st level') promotes 12pt subheadings under class features; exactly the 5 artifact keys are the only class-grantor features not anchored by a class progression featureGrant. Printed denominator (extracted, heights 13.9 feature / 12.0 subheading): bard 6 (Cantrips, Spell Slots, Spells Known of 1st Level and Higher, Spellcasting Ability, Ritual Casting, Spellcasting Focus); cleric 5 & druid 5 (Cantrips, Preparing and Casting Spells, Spellcasting Ability, Ritual Casting, Spellcasting Focus); paladin 3 (Preparing and Casting Spells, Spellcasting Ability, Spellcasting Focus); ranger 3 (Spell Slots, Spells Known..., Spellcasting Ability); sorcerer 5 & warlock/Pact Magic 5 (Cantrips, Spell Slots, Spells Known..., Spellcasting Ability, Spellcasting Focus); wizard 7 (Cantrips, Spellbook, Preparing and Casting Spells, Spellcasting Ability, Ritual Casting, Spellcasting Focus, Learning Spells of 1st Level and Higher) = 39 total. Other class features' 12pt lines are option catalogs (Fighting Style, Metamagic, Pact Boon, Ki, Font of Magic) - out of scope. DESIGN REFINEMENTS: sections use {name,text} (matches subclass data.sections + namedEntry field provenance), page evidence via source-region ledger + record multi-page provenance; mechanics/choices/creationFacts keep deriving from full body text; aliases = retired-key fallback in lookupRulesRecord + feature section names indexed as lookup names (no key-alias mechanism exists today).

title: Dispatch: split composed subrace ASI text and Eldritch Invocations option list into verbatim spans (attempt 1)
description:
Implementation dispatch for parent eshyra-o9bd.19.2.1.3 (read it with `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.2.1.3`). All design decisions below are made; do not re-decide them. If reality contradicts this spec, STOP, record what you found with `bd update <this-id> --append-notes`, and close with a reason rather than improvising.

Defect class: a value emitted at a pointer field-provenance-v1 declares `source-prose` (verbatim SRD text) that is actually composed from two separately printed source spans. Fix: each source-prose value must be ONE verbatim span. Read docs/importer-fix-protocol.md first. Do NOT touch docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/freeze-manifest.json or add thaw notes (freeze guard intentionally dormant).

All paths below are relative to packages/core/.

=== MEMBER A: flattened subrace Ability Score Increase (high-elf, hill-dwarf, lightfoot-halfling, rock-gnome) ===
Pack today: subrace /traits/0 is {name:"Ability Score Increase", text:"Your Dexterity score increases by 2. Your Intelligence score increases by 1."} and /abilityScoreIncreases is ONE entry whose sourceText is the same joined string. The two sentences are printed in different sections (parent race traits vs subrace block).

A1. scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseAncestries.ts `mergeTraits`: stop concatenating a subrace trait into a same-label parent trait. Every subrace trait is appended as its own entry after the parent traits (parent's "Subrace" pointer trait still dropped). Result for high-elf: parent "Ability Score Increase" (Dex +2 sentence) stays in parent position; the subrace's own "Ability Score Increase" (Int +1 sentence) appears as a separate entry in subrace order. Duplicate trait NAMES are intended: the SRD prints the label twice. Update the module/function doc comments (the "flattened" decision now means parent traits + subrace traits as separate verbatim entries, never text-joined).

A2. Rock Gnome boundary (registry row rock-gnome-boundary, aliases indep:010 / sol:CAP-012): `TRAIT_LABEL_RE` (parseAncestries.ts ~line 115) does not accept the typographic apostrophe U+2019, so "Artificer’s Lore." is not recognised as a trait label and its body bleeds into the preceding Ability Score Increase trait. Accept U+2019 alongside ASCII ' in the label character class. After the fix rock-gnome must have a separate trait named "Artificer’s Lore" (printed apostrophe preserved) whose text is the Artificer's Lore body, and the existing expertise `mechanics` projection must end up on THAT trait, not on the ASI trait. Find where the ancestry trait mechanics projection is attached (grep "expertise" in scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/) and make sure it keys on the Artificer’s Lore trait. Check whether any other races-section trait label changes as a result of the regex change and report it in notes.

A3. scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/creationFacts.ts `ANCESTRY_ABILITY_SCORE_INCREASES`: change the value type to an array (`readonly AncestryAbilityScoreIncrease[]`) for every ancestry. Parent/non-subrace ancestries keep exactly one entry (unchanged content). The four subraces get TWO entries in document order: the parent's (e.g. high-elf: {fixed:[{dexterity,2}], sourceText:"Your Dexterity score increases by 2."}) then the subrace's own ({fixed:[{intelligence,1}], sourceText:"Your Intelligence score increases by 1."}). hill-dwarf: Con+2 / Wis+1; lightfoot-halfling: Dex+2 / Cha+1; rock-gnome: Int+2 / Con+1. `enrichAncestryCreationFacts` emits `abilityScoreIncreases: entries.map(cloneAbilityScoreIncreases)`.

A4. src/character/srdAncestryAbilityScoreIncreases.ts oracle: same array shape per key, same entries as A3. Rename the accessor to `getAncestryAbilityScoreIncreases(key): readonly AncestryAbilityScoreIncrease[] | undefined`, update src/internal.ts export and callers (test/srdAncestryAbilityScoreIncreases.test.ts, scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/cli.ts ~line 768). Runtime consumers already sum across entries (characterDraft.ts / dnd5eRecipe.ts flatMap `fixed`; requiredChoices.ts finds the `choice` entry; derivedValues.ts sums by ability) — verify, do not change behavior. Net level-1 ability bonuses for every ancestry must be identical before and after.

A5. Tests. Update test/srdAncestryAbilityScoreIncreases.test.ts: resolved record abilityScoreIncreases toEqual the oracle array; STRENGTHEN the faithfulness check from `startsWith` to: the multiset of ASI-trait texts (traits named /ability score increase/i) equals, one-to-one and in order, the multiset of oracle sourceText values (exact string equality). Update test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseAncestries.test.ts and emit.test.ts expectations that encoded the joined text (the SRD proves the old expectation wrong — say so in the commit message; this is not weakening). Add, in parseAncestries.test.ts where the pinned PDF is already extracted (it imports extractPdfText), a durable invariant over ALL parsed ancestries: every trait `text` is one contiguous span of the extracted races-section source text after normalization (collapse all whitespace runs to one space; rejoin line-break hyphenation the same way the parser's joinParagraphs does — read it). It must FAIL on current main's parser output for the four subraces and rock-gnome (prove this by running it before your A1/A2 change and record the failing record list in your notes). If a record fails for an unrelated extraction artifact, do not loosen the normalizer broadly — record it in notes and stop.

=== MEMBER B: feature:warlock:eldritch-invocations /description ===
scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseFeatures.ts (~line 615-640): when a feature anchor repeats, the second body is appended into `description`. A probe on the pinned PDF shows exactly two repeats: `class Cleric destroy undead` (p17, the in-body table caption, CONTIGUOUS: the repeat is the very line that ended the first body) and `class Warlock eldritch invocations` (first body p47, repeat p48 = the end-of-chapter option-list section ~3,000 characters later). Only the latter is a member.

B1. Track, per emitted key, the index `j` at which its body ended. On a repeat at index `i`: if `i === bodyEnd` (contiguous continuation) keep today's merge unchanged (Destroy Undead must stay byte-identical — verify). Otherwise the repeat opens a DISTANT section: store its body as a new `optionCatalog: string` on the FeatureExtraction (types.ts, doc comment: "an end-of-chapter option-list section the feature body points to, printed apart from the body; one verbatim span, never joined into description"), keep `description` as the first body only, and still merge `optionSourcePages` from the catalog body. If a key receives a second distant section, throw (fail closed). If Destroy Undead turns out NOT to satisfy `i === bodyEnd`, stop and report — do not add a name-based exception.

B2. scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/emit.ts `buildFeatureData`: emit `optionCatalog` when present, placed right after `description`.

B3. scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/deriveFeatureChoices.ts: option-catalog parsing (`parseOptionCatalog`, and any choose-count/list parsing that needs the option headings) must read `optionCatalog` when present, else `description`. Count words ("two eldritch invocations") stay parsed from `description` (the p47 body carries "At 2nd level, you gain two eldritch invocations"). The derived `choices` for eldritch-invocations must be byte-identical to main (32 options, same ids/text/prerequisites/source pages).

B4. scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/fieldProvenanceDeclarations.ts: declare `prose('feature', '/optionCatalog', ...)` with a reason stating it is the printed end-of-chapter option-list section, one verbatim span, kept apart from /description. src/rules/kindSchemas.ts: register `optionCatalog` as an optional non-empty string on feature data (follow the existing feature validator's idiom). src/rules/srdChoiceProseAudit.ts `scanProse`: also push `data.optionCatalog` so no prose is hidden from that gate.

B5. Tests: in test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/parseFeatures.test.ts extend the existing 'end-of-chapter option list re-uses the feature heading' describe: description equals the first body only; optionCatalog equals the option-list body; a contiguous repeated caption still merges into description; two distant repeats for one key throw. Add a generated-pack assertion (test/srdGeneratedPack.test.ts or the nearest existing feature assertion) that feature:warlock:eldritch-invocations description does not contain "If an eldritch invocation has prerequisites" and optionCatalog starts with it.

=== REGENERATE + VERIFY ===
Regenerate the committed pack through the importer: `npm run import:dnd5e-srd -- --pdf packages/core/sources/dnd5e-srd-5.1/SRD_CC_v5.1.pdf --out packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/` (from the worktree root), then `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack` must be exact. Regenerate any derived artifact a test says is stale (e.g. the o9bd-18-8-8 semi-structured boundary inventory, field-provenance.json) with its own generator — never hand-edit. Expected pack diff: only the 4 subraces + rock-gnome ancestry records, feature:warlock:eldritch-invocations, field-provenance.json, and whatever source-coverage/inventory artifacts legitimately move; explain every other changed file in notes. Record-count pins must not change.

Run `npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root BEFORE committing (it rewrites files). Memory is tight (~7 GB): if rulesPackAuditCli or dolt tests time out under load, rerun with VITEST_MAX_FORKS=4.
Commit message prefix: `eshyra-o9bd.19.2.1.3 ` and end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`.
Completion report via `bd update <this-id> --append-notes`: commit SHA, pack-diff record list, the pre-fix failing list from A5, Destroy Undead byte-identity confirmation, choices byte-identity confirmation, verify:worktree result.

title: Seat exit reminder gates on session duration, not on whether the session changed anything
description:
The Stop-hook handoff reminder landed by eshyra-oqvj (PR #560, merge 46048f55) fires only once a session has run at least EXIT_REMINDER_MIN_SESSION_MS = 45 minutes (scripts/seats/seatContext.mjs:215, consumed by handoffExitReminder at :344).

OBSERVED MISS, first session after the mechanism landed:

Session ad735081-d4a7-412a-bbc1-61c9a5dbed4b ran 2026-09-22T05:05:55.760Z to 05:23:37.415Z -- 17m42s -- in /home/jhbongaarts/src/eshyra on CLI 2.1.278. It merged PR #561 (eshyra-5wbx, merge commit e7bb1836) and ended. The Stop hook ran at each turn end and correctly emitted nothing: handoffExitReminder returns null below the floor. The handoff was left at its 2026-09-10 state and was still stale when the next session opened.

The entry-side half worked. That session's SessionStart payload (delivered 05:05:55, from eshyra-8pat / PR #559) carried 'Recorded 287h ago', the 48h stale cue, and the exact 'npm run seat:handoff -- write claude-captain' command. So the mechanism is not missing; the exit trigger's predicate is wrong.

THE DEFECT: session duration is a proxy for 'did this session produce something worth resuming from', and it is the wrong proxy in this repo. A short session that merges a PR is exactly the case that invalidates the existing handoff, and it is the case the floor is structurally guaranteed to miss. Several of the last ten merges are that size.

CANDIDATE PREDICATE: fire when the session changed durable state -- a commit authored on a branch, a merge reaching main, a bead status transition -- rather than when it has burned 45 minutes. Duration may remain as a secondary condition for long sessions that have not yet committed anything, but it must not be the only gate. Whatever replaces it, the reminder must stay silent for a session that genuinely produced nothing, or it becomes noise and gets ignored.

OUT OF SCOPE: the authorization design (SessionStart ledger, agent_id / env-marker / stop_hook_active refusals) is sound and is not reopened here. This changes only the trigger predicate in handoffExitReminder.

EVIDENCE: transcript ~/.claude/projects/-home-jhbongaarts-src-eshyra/ad735081-d4a7-412a-bbc1-61c9a5dbed4b.jsonl. Discovered 2026-09-22 when the handoff was found still stale despite both PRs having landed.
notes:
PR #562 open at head 853417ab: https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/562

Trigger now fires on repository movement (HEAD differs from the commit recorded when SessionStart admitted the session), with EXIT_REMINDER_MIN_SESSION_MS demoted to the fallback for a long session that has not committed anything yet.

DISPOSITIONS against the bead's candidate signals:
- commit/merge reaching the checkout: ADOPTED, as HEAD movement at the hook's cwd.
- bead status transition: EXCLUDED. Detecting one means invoking bd or reading its internals from a hook that runs at every turn end, which fails the cost bar the way the original trigger failed the accuracy bar. A bookkeeping-only session under 45 minutes has little to hand over.
- duration as secondary condition: RETAINED exactly as the bead permitted, never as the only gate.

KNOWN BOUND, deliberate: the observed HEAD is the checkout at the hook's cwd, which is the session's project directory. A supervisor that commits only inside a linked worktree shows no movement in the parent checkout and falls back to elapsed time. Such sessions are long, so the fallback covers them. Recorded in the PR rather than fixed.

Cost: the git call is ordered last, reached only by a session otherwise owed a reminder that has not already passed the fallback. Asserted by 'never reads HEAD when a cheaper condition already decides' with a counting stub.

Verification: npm run verify:worktree clean; 307 files passed / 2 skipped, 5617 tests passed / 3 skipped. Five mutations each confirmed red against the test written for it.

Stays in_progress until #562 merges.
Review F1 (2026-09-22, head 853417ab): local HEAD movement misses a remote gh pr merge with a stationary checkout. Addressed in 6282c008: trigger also fires when the session transcript (Stop payload transcript_path) records a Bash tool call to gh pr merge / git commit / git push. PR #562 awaiting re-review.
PR #562 MERGED 2026-09-22, merge commit 68490fac. Worktree and branch removed.

title: Disposition beadLifecyclePolicy.test.ts under the permanent-evidence policy
description:
Same defect class as eshyra-4tgd, which was deliberately scoped to
packages/core/test/reviewLifecyclePolicy.test.ts only.

packages/core/test/beadLifecyclePolicy.test.ts has the same shape:
AGENTS.md prose -> regex asserting AGENTS.md still contains equivalent prose.
Its five tests read AGENTS.md and pin the PR-deliverable bead-lifecycle wording,
the "Judge by **deliverable**, not by agent role." sentence, the note that the
rule narrows the generated bd close checklist, and a section-order relation.

Apply the same disposition analysis eshyra-4tgd used; see that bead's ledger for
the format and for the blanket replacement responsibility. Do NOT assume the
outcome transfers: at least two assertions there may be genuinely structural
rather than semantic mirrors —

- the section-order check (Session Completion ahead of PR Merge Policy), which
  may or may not encode a semantic dependency the way the disposition gate does;
- 'does not strand the rule in the supervisor-only hook', which reads
  .claude/hooks/supervisor-context.mjs and asserts a rule is NOT confined to a
  surface only one agent can read. That observes a real cross-surface topology
  between an executable hook and common authority, and is the strongest
  candidate for retention in that file.

Verify each independently against the documents and the hook as they exist then.

EXCLUSIONS: same as eshyra-4tgd. No replacement schema, snapshot, hash, manifest,
baseline, approval marker, certification file, or new checker; do not relocate the
same mirrors into another file; do not replace many regexes with one large one.
notes:
DISPOSITION LEDGER (2026-09-22), same format as eshyra-4tgd: existing evidence -> claimed invariant -> authority -> actual boundary -> disposition -> replacement.

OUTCOME: all 5 tests RETIRED, file deleted (94 lines, 5 tests, 8 expect() -> 0). The bead warned the eshyra-4tgd outcome may not transfer and named two assertions as possible genuine structure; both were checked independently against the documents and the hook as they exist now, and neither held.

BLANKET REPLACEMENT RESPONSIBILITY for every retired assertion: what AGENTS.md MEANS is owned by the authority hierarchy (AGENTS.md itself), the owning Bead or accepted design, and semantic-system review of any change to that authority. A regex copy of editable authority cannot establish that a FUTURE version of it is valid - an authorized bad edit updates document and regex together, while a legitimate rewording breaks the regex. Demonstrated empirically below, in both directions.

ORIGINAL AUTHORITY, checked: eshyra-o9bd.19.16 (PR #519, merge f0fad2a, sole commit touching this file: 5866b305). Its SCOPE authorized three deliverables - state the rule in AGENTS.md Session Completion scoped by deliverable; state that it narrows the generated bd-prime checklist; replace the hook's inline sentence with a pointer. None authorizes permanent executable ownership of the rule's WORDING. Its close reason says 'packages/core/test/beadLifecyclePolicy.test.ts pins it', which makes the file a DELIVERY artifact of that bead, not a durable invariant - the identical finding eshyra-4tgd reached about its own old test 2.

RETIRED, tests 1-3 (prose mirrors, uncontested): 'states that a PR-deliverable bead stays in_progress until merge'; 'scopes the rule by deliverable so dispatched children still close'; 'records that it narrows the generated bd close checklist'. Each is AGENTS.md prose -> regex asserting AGENTS.md still contains equivalent prose.

RETIRED, test 4 'keeps the rule in Session Completion, ahead of PR Merge Policy' - the section-order relation the bead flagged. It does NOT encode a semantic dependency the way eshyra-4tgd's disposition-gate ordering claimed to. Three independent failures: (a) it locates the RULE by a prose substring, so a one-word synonym swap breaks it; (b) it identifies both sections by heading TEXT, the exact proxy class eshyra-4tgd retired at bc277005; (c) raw indexOf with no existence check - renaming '### Session Completion' yields -1 and 'rule > -1' passes, so the rule may be moved ANYWHERE. Verified: heading renamed and the whole rule relocated to the top of AGENTS.md, guard green. No authority requires that placement, and a section move inside one document is fully visible in its diff.

RETIRED, test 5 'does not strand the rule in the supervisor-only hook' - the bead's strongest retention candidate. The claim is real (a general lifecycle rule must not live only on a Claude-injected surface Codex can never execute) but the implementation observes none of it, and is vacuous in BOTH halves. (a) expect(hook).toContain('AGENTS.md') is satisfied by the hook's own header comment, which says to keep supervisor policy OUT of AGENTS.md - plus three further incidental mentions. It passes with the pointer deleted. (b) The negative regex pins ONE historical sentence ('handoff stops at an open PR...'), so restating the stranded rule in any other words passes. Verified: the AGENTS.md pointer removed from the Bead-per-dispatch bullet and the rule re-stranded as 'Keep the parent bead open until its pull request lands on main; do not close it at PR-open' - guard green, i.e. the precise defect eshyra-o9bd.19.16 existed to close reproduces undetected. Deeper reason it cannot be repaired rather than retired: the harmful state is 'rule present ONLY in the hook', whose detection requires knowing the rule is present in AGENTS.md - which is a prose mirror again. The cross-surface topology is not machine-identifiable without text identity, so it belongs to semantic-system review of changes to AGENTS.md and the hook.

ADVERSARIAL EVIDENCE (empirical, all mutations applied to the tree and verified by inspection, then reverted):
BAD states that PASS, with no test edited: (1) rule gutted by appending 'An agent may instead close the bead at PR-open whenever it judges the work finished.' - 5/5 pass; (2) '### Session Completion' renamed to '### Wrapping Up a Session' and the entire rule block relocated under the H1 - 5/5 pass; (3) hook pointer replaced by a reworded restatement of the rule - 5/5 pass; (4) hook file deleted outright - 5/5 pass (by design, existsSync early return).
GOOD states that FAIL: 'pull request stays in_progress' -> 'remains in_progress' - 2 failed / 3 passed, including the supposedly structural ordering test; 'Judge by **deliverable**, not by agent role.' -> 'Judge by the **deliverable**, not by the agent's role.' - 1 failed / 4 passed.

NOT USED as justification: runtime cost. The file ran in ~95ms; it was never the problem and is not the reason.

CONSIDERED AND DECLINED: a reachability guard on .claude/settings.json -> supervisor-context.mjs -> codex-subagent-workflow.md, the one candidate in this area whose identity is not document text (sibling of the retained commonAuthorityStructure link guard). Declined: it is a DIFFERENT responsibility from anything this file ever claimed, the hook is optional Claude Code tooling whose absence is loud rather than silent (the seat charter already directs a session without it to operate under ordinary AGENTS.md authority), and inventing it here would be new proof machinery outside this bead's scope and against its exclusions.

EXCLUSIONS HONORED: no replacement schema, snapshot, hash, manifest, baseline, approval marker, certification file, or new checker; no mirror relocated to another file; no many-regexes-into-one consolidation; no test added to prove the removal safe. No tombstone memory, registry, or appendix. Nothing referenced this file anywhere in the tree (verified by repo-wide grep) and no bd memory names it.

DOCUMENTS UNCHANGED: the lifecycle rule in AGENTS.md and the hook's pointer are untouched by this PR. Provenance stays in eshyra-o9bd.19.16, PR #519, the hook's own citation of that bead, and Git/Dolt history.

title: Release artifact validation intermittently fails on native binary check (better-sqlite3 test_extension.node)
description:
The Release workflow's "Build artifact" job intermittently fails release
artifact validation on macOS and Windows runners with:

    Error: forbidden content (unexpected native binary): app/node_modules/@eshyra/core/node_modules/better-sqlite3/build/Release/test_extension.node

Source: scripts/release/validate-release-artifact.mjs FORBIDDEN_ANYWHERE rule
(around line 95) only allowlists `better_sqlite3.node` and rejects any other
`.node` file found anywhere in the packed artifact, including vendored deps.

better-sqlite3 apparently produces (or its native install step sometimes
triggers a local build that produces) a `test_extension.node` binary used for
its own extension-loading tests. On some macOS/Windows CI runs this ends up
in the packed `node_modules` tree and trips the validator; on other runs
(often an immediate rerun of the identical commit) it does not appear and the
job passes.

Confirmed to be a pre-existing platform/native-install flake, unrelated to
any specific dependency bump:
- Hit PR #550 (`@openai/codex-sdk` bump, does not touch better-sqlite3) on
  `claude/macos-14` — run 34860077302, job 104029650883. Passed clean on
  rerun of the same commit.
- Hit PR #548 (dev-tooling group: biome + @types/node, does not touch
  better-sqlite3) on `api/macos-14`, `api/windows-latest`, and
  `codex/macos-14` — run 34860035666, jobs 104029505720 / 104029505636 /
  (codex/macos-14). Passed clean on rerun of the same commit.
- Also seen previously on 2026-09-07 on an unrelated
  `dependabot/npm_and_yarn/model-provider-sdks-9b66f2d325` branch — run
  34169209961 — while sibling dependency PRs on the same day passed.

Because CI has no branch-protection required-checks gate on this repo
(`gh api repos/.../branches/main/protection` -> 404), this flake doesn't
currently block merges, but it burns CI minutes, requires manual reruns, and
erodes trust in the Release artifact validation signal. Per AGENTS.md's
native-dependency policy, an accidental source-build fallback for
better-sqlite3 is itself treated as a regression -- this may be exactly that,
manifesting as a leaked test-build artifact rather than a build failure.

Likely directions (root-cause first, no fix without evidence):
1. Determine why `test_extension.node` sometimes gets built/copied into the
   packed tree on macOS/Windows specifically -- e.g. prebuilt-binary download
   flakiness silently falling back to a local `node-gyp` build that also
   builds better-sqlite3's test extension as a side effect.
2. If the file is legitimately produced by a normal (non-fallback) native
   install step and is harmless test-only output, prune it from the packaged
   artifact during the release build step rather than loosening the
   validator's allowlist.
3. If it turns out to indicate an actual source-build fallback, treat per the
   existing native-dep regression policy (docs/adr/0008, docs/adr/0016).

Acceptance: root cause documented; a fix lands (packaging-side prune, and/or
native-install fix) so the artifact-validation failure stops reproducing
across several consecutive Release runs on macOS/Windows; no weakening of
scripts/release/validate-release-artifact.mjs's native-binary allowlist
without documented justification.

title: Anchor seat handoffs to repository state so staleness is visible
description:
A recorded seat handoff carries an ISO timestamp (scripts/seats/seat-handoff.mjs write) and the SessionStart injection reports its age in hours from file mtime (scripts/seats/seatContext.mjs). Nothing anchors it to repository state.

OBSERVED FAILURE (2026-09-07/08)
The claude-captain handoff was written at 2026-09-07T22:21:38Z. PR #536 merged at 03:26Z and PR #537 at 04:39Z the next day -- two integrations after the handoff was last touched. Its 'most useful next action' pointed at eshyra-jhpt children as open work that had partly landed. The successor reconciled from live state as required and lost nothing, so this is a cost-of-distrust defect, not a correctness one.

WHY THE EXHORTATIVE FIX IS THE WRONG ONE
The Claude Captain charter already says to record a handoff 'after an integration'. That instruction was in force and was not followed, and because the charter is personal and untracked, nothing could observe that it was skipped. Adding a stronger reminder repeats the approach that already failed.

PROPOSAL
Make staleness self-evident rather than writer-disciplined:
- seat-handoff.mjs write stamps the current origin/main (or main) SHA alongside the existing ISO timestamp comment.
- seatContext.mjs injection reports drift, e.g. 'recorded 6.4h ago at main 59d2ef9; main is now 2 commits ahead' -- and says so plainly when the recorded SHA is unreachable or the repo has moved to an unrelated history.
- A handoff with no recorded SHA (every existing one) degrades to today's behaviour rather than erroring.

The point is to tell the reader HOW MUCH to distrust the handoff. Today every handoff is equally suspect, so the reader re-derives everything from scratch every session; that cost is paid whether or not the handoff was stale.

ALSO IN SCOPE
docs/agent-captain-seats.md documents the handoff commands but not the recording discipline -- when a handoff should be written at all. A new occupant reading only repository authority learns the mechanism and none of the practice. Record the 'at meaningful boundaries, including after an integration' rule there, where it is durable and both seats can read it, rather than leaving it only in the untracked charters.

NON-GOALS
No tracked handoff content; handoffs stay personal, untracked, and never repository authority (docs/agent-captain-seats.md). No new seat state, no enforcement that blocks a session, no hook that refuses to start.

EVIDENCE
A test proving the injection reports drift for a handoff recorded at an older SHA, AND -- the control that matters -- that a handoff recorded at current main reports no drift. A SHA-less handoff still injects exactly as it does today.
close_reason:
NOT A DEFECT -- closed on corrected facts. The premise was wrong.

I filed this after observing that PRs #536 and #537 merged AFTER the claude-captain handoff was recorded (2026-09-07T22:21:38Z), and concluded a predecessor had skipped the charter's 'record a handoff after an integration' instruction. It had not. That work belonged to CODEX-CAPTAIN, which recorded its own handoff at 2026-09-08T03:27:48Z -- one minute after #536 merged -- explicitly noting 'PR #536 has crossed the merge boundary' and naming eshyra-jhpt.2.5 as the next unfinished question, which is what #537 then delivered.

Handoffs are per-seat by design (docs/agent-captain-seats.md: '<git common dir>/eshyra-seats/<seat>/handoff.md'). Each seat's file correctly described that seat's work. Neither seat skipped anything, and cross-seat awareness is supposed to come from Beads and Git -- which is where the successor got it, so the system worked as designed.

The proposed fix rested entirely on the false premise. The residual observation -- that the injection reports age in hours without anchoring to repository state -- is real but not worth acting on: reconciling from live state is unconditional, so knowing that main moved would not change any required behaviour. Recoverable from this note if anyone later disagrees.

The actual error was mine, and it is worth naming because it is a repeatable one: I treated my own inference from a timestamp comparison as a verified fact, without checking the obvious alternative explanation sitting one directory over. The seat charter's rule that a handoff is a set of leads to check applies to conclusions ABOUT handoffs too.

title: Migrate pdfjs-dist 5.x -> 6.x (clears GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j)
description:
The dedicated migration bead that eshyra-1yj (closed 2026-06-07, PR #121) said
would be filed and never was. That bead added the semver-major ignore for
pdfjs-dist to .github/dependabot.yml; its final acceptance criterion was to
explain "why PDF.js major updates require a dedicated migration bead". This is
that bead.

## Why now

Dependabot alerts #26 and #27 (both open since 2026-08-08, both high) are one
advisory counted against two manifests:

- GHSA-hq66-cqwq-w95j, "PDF.js: Arbitrary JavaScript execution upon opening a
  malicious PDF"
- vulnerable range >= 5.6.83, < 6.2.108; first patched 6.2.108; latest 6.3.289
- we are on pdfjs-dist 5.7.284 (packages/core/package.json:49, range ^5.7.284),
  devDependency scope

There is no patched 5.x, so the only fix is the major. Dependabot cannot open a
PR for it: an `ignore` entry in dependabot.yml suppresses security updates for
that dependency as well as version updates, and pdfjs-dist semver-majors are
ignored there by design. Repo setting dependabot_security_updates is enabled;
the config, not the setting, is why there is no PR. That is the ignore working
as intended - it routes the work here - but it means the alert will sit open
until this bead is done or the alerts are dismissed.

## Call sites

Only two, both under packages/core/scripts (never shipped to CLI users):

- packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/extract.ts:45
- packages/core/scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/cli.ts:40

Both import `getDocument` from 'pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs' and use only
getDocument -> getPage -> getTextContent, reading `str`, `transform`, `height`,
and optional `width` off each text item. extract.ts declares those fields as a
local structural type (PdfTextItem) rather than importing the library's deep
types, so the typing coupling is already thin. Confirm the legacy ESM build and
that exports subpath still exist in 6.x - that entry point, not the extraction
API, is the likeliest breakage.

## The real risk is output drift, not the API

The API surface is small. The hazard is that 6.x changes extracted text and
therefore the generated rules-packs. That puts this squarely under
docs/importer-fix-protocol.md: do not weaken regression tests or audit
expectations to match new generated output. Any diff in extracted text must be
explained against the source PDF and either fixed in the extractor or justified
with source-backed evidence that the old expectation was wrong.

Extraction behavior this repo has already had to fix by hand, all of which must
be re-checked after the bump: hyphen-cluster normalization (eshyra-6uy),
two-column layout handling (eshyra-fct, eshyra-xbh, eshyra-w8h), apostrophes
mis-mapped to space (eshyra-g9im.1), and section-anchor matching
(eshyra-0m9.5.20).

## Sequencing

Interacts with eshyra-o9bd.14 (regenerate pack + re-run the full PDF/source
audit and new gates, then re-freeze). Both regenerate the pack from the same
PDF. Doing them in an undefined order risks attributing pdfjs output drift to
the thaw work or vice versa. Decide the order deliberately and record it: either
land this first so o9bd.14 regenerates once on 6.x, or finish o9bd.14 first and
treat this as a separate, isolated regeneration. Not filed as a hard blocker in
either direction - the sequencing is a judgement call for whoever picks these up.

## Acceptance criteria

- pdfjs-dist range in packages/core/package.json moved to >= 6.2.108 (prefer the
  current latest, 6.3.289) and the lockfile updated.
- Both call sites build and run; the legacy ESM entry point resolves.
- Extracted text is either byte-identical to the 5.7.284 baseline, or every
  difference is explained against the SRD 5.1 PDF under
  docs/importer-fix-protocol.md, with the extractor fixed where it is wrong.
- Generated rules-packs regenerate deterministically; frozen-path changes carry
  a thaw note under docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/thaw-notes/.
- npm run verify:worktree clean.
- Dependabot alerts #26 and #27 close on their own once main carries the fixed
  version. The semver-major ignore in dependabot.yml STAYS - the policy from
  eshyra-1yj is still correct for the next major. If it is intentionally
  changed, that is a separate decision to record.
notes: PR https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/535 open. Extraction byte-identical 5.7.284 -> 6.3.289 (403 pages / 34347 lines); pack unchanged (0 records added/removed/changed); only API break was PDFDocumentProxy.destroy() removal at extract.ts and create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/cli.ts. Bead stays in_progress until the PR merges.
close_reason: Closed
