title: Design and evaluate persistent DM seat reconstruction across model sessions
description:
AUTHORITY / REFERENCES

- Repository workflow and review authority: AGENTS.md.
- Accepted architecture: ADR 0001 (provider-neutral model profiles and separation of rules/content/state/user-private data/generated memory); ADR 0010 (API-native versus agent-harness seam and Eshyra-owned behavior across provider sessions); both ADR 0012 records (character continuity/custody and the four content/state layers); ADR 0014 (campaign overlay canon and truth status); ADR 0017 section 8 (audit-architecture restraint); ADR 0020 (rule awareness, model adjudication, and deterministic state-integrity boundaries).
- Current Eshyra producers/consumers to map exactly: packages/core/src/orchestrator/protocol.ts (buildSystemPrompt and Hybrid Contract); packages/core/src/model/client.ts; packages/core/src/orchestrator/contextAssembler.ts and orchestrator.ts; packages/core/src/memory/recapBuilder.ts, arcSummary.ts, campaignBibleExtractor.ts, campaignArc.ts, and summary.ts; packages/cli/src/playClose.ts, playSession.ts, and playTypes.ts; packages/core/src/session/launch.ts; campaign-bible extraction/rollup; campaign overlay, campaign-ruling, character-chronicle, session resume, trace/usage, debug, and adapter implementations and tests.
- Comparative implementation evidence, not repository authority or a design to copy: gastownhall/gascity engdocs/architecture/nine-concepts.md; examples/gastown/city.toml and Gas Town config recipes; cmd/gc/cmd_prime.go and prompt rendering; cmd/gc/prime_auto_handoff_inject.go; the older Gas Town crew prompt; and session-reset behavior. These show a useful decomposition in which standing agent reconstruction and durable work/state survive a fresh model context, while handoff mail is injected separately as episodic context.
- Existing ownership that must remain separate: eshyra-wsv, eshyra-32m, eshyra-06b/.1, eshyra-x63, eshyra-d4d.6, eshyra-lupf.16, eshyra-ws9.1, eshyra-ckrg, and eshyra-f0hj. Rule discovery belongs to eshyra-o9bd.19.11/.12/.13/.15; campaign rulings, house rules, ambiguity/precedent lifecycle, and disputed-turn replay belong to eshyra-jhpt and children; future campaign-rule context scaling belongs to eshyra-umyb.

PROBLEM / PRIMARY QUESTION

Eshyra invokes frontier models transiently but presents a long-lived campaign Dungeon Master role. Current continuity is reconstructed from a generic DM system prompt, the Hybrid Contract, authoritative campaign/module/rules state, campaign rulings, bounded session/scene memory, campaign bible, arc summaries, character continuity, and other rendered context. Session recaps are deterministic compositions of accepted narration and state deltas; bible and arc maintenance are fresh model calls over persisted inputs. There is no accepted architecture yet for a campaign/table-specific standing DM charter or an explicit outgoing-DM handoff.

The primary question is:

What must Eshyra reconstruct around a fresh frontier-model invocation so that it meaningfully occupies the same long-lived campaign-DM role as its predecessor, independent of provider, model, or provider-session continuity?

Same DM means the same persistent institutional/gameplay role, not identity as a person or continuity of consciousness. The investigation must distinguish standing role reconstruction from durable campaign state, episodic handoff, and the transient model invocation. It must not presuppose that either a new entity or any new production capability is needed.

The implementation default is precise: do not introduce a new storage/entity abstraction unless a real producer/consumer requires one; first determine whether the persistent DM seat is adequately composed from existing and/or narrowly extended prompt, campaign, memory, preference, and handoff primitives.

REQUIRED CONCEPTUAL DECOMPOSITION

1. Standing DM role charter

Map buildSystemPrompt, the Hybrid Contract, live tool roster/protocol instructions, canon guidance, narration/adjudication responsibilities, and related runtime instructions. Determine which instructions are generic to every Eshyra DM and which, if any, legitimately vary by campaign or table. This is the stable role definition reconstructed for each fresh invocation, not campaign world knowledge.

2. Campaign/table-specific DM identity or charter

Evaluate whether a long-running campaign benefits from bounded, stable table-facing commitments that are neither world canon nor one-session handoff notes. Candidate evidence categories include established table style, pacing preferences, descriptive density, player-agency conventions, difficulty/lethality conventions, tone boundaries, recurring adjudication or narrative conventions, stable player-specific interaction preferences, and campaign-specific DM voice/style. These are hypotheses, not requirements.

Map every candidate against existing user-private data, campaign state, campaign bible, generated memory, character chronicle, campaign rulings, model profiles, prompts, and configuration before proposing a new producer or consumer. Do not categorically exclude table-facing style/personality continuity when it has demonstrated product value, but reject unbounded persona preservation and provider-specific behavioral quirks. Do not anthropomorphize the role.

3. Durable campaign/institutional state

Map what Eshyra already reconstructs for a fresh DM: canonical campaign state; module/adventure source and progress; campaign overlay/canon; campaign rulings; rules/source evidence and bounded capabilities; session/scene memory; campaign bible; arc summaries; character custody/chronicle/party continuity; model profiles; and every other currently rendered context section. Keep this state distinct from DM identity even when it helps a model behave continuously.

4. Episodic outgoing-DM handoff

Retain and evaluate the outgoing-handoff hypothesis as a separate path. A bounded explicit note authored for the successor may preserve immediate salience or intent that normal memory loses: subtle NPC characterization trajectory, unresolved dramatic tension, player-specific salience, deliberate setup/payoff intent, tactical/narrative setup, intentionally planted but not-yet-canonical future hooks, or the intended opening beat for the next session.

A handoff is non-authoritative generated continuity memory. It cannot directly mutate state or outrank canonical campaign/state facts, source/module/rules authority, active campaign rulings, or newer evidence. It must never capture hidden chain-of-thought or private reasoning; only concise, explicit intent/salience deliberately authored for the successor is eligible. Provenance, staleness, supersession, retention, and context budgets must be explicit if evidence supports the concept.

5. Transient model/provider session

Treat each Claude, OpenAI, or other invocation/session as an occupant of the DM role, not the durable identity itself. Preserve ADR 0010 provider neutrality: changing provider, model family, adapter family, harness session, or API conversation must not inherently create a new campaign DM. Useful continuity must come from Eshyra-owned reconstruction, never assumed hidden provider memory or same-model affinity.

INFORMATION-FLOW ANALYSIS

Map the current path source-to-consumer:

current DM standing prompt + rendered campaign context -> model invocation -> accepted narration and deterministic state effects -> scene/session memory producers -> campaign bible / arc / character continuity -> next-session context assembly -> fresh model invocation.

Then evaluate two distinct candidate paths:

- standing campaign/table DM charter -> every fresh primary-DM invocation;
- outgoing DM immediate context -> explicit bounded handoff -> next primary-DM invocation.

For each path, identify information it can faithfully preserve that the other paths cannot. Keep these categories explicit and non-convertible without an authorized producer: world facts; game rulings; table facts/preferences; long-lived DM behavioral commitments; immediate DM narrative intent/salience; generated continuity memory; and transient provider/model/session metadata.

SCOPE / EVALUATION

1. Produce the complete current information-flow and producer/consumer map with exact source references, including the primary-DM system prompt, context renderer, resume paths, memory pyramid, campaign rulings, character continuity, traces, and adapter behavior.
2. Identify legitimate candidate campaign/table charter data, its authority/privacy/lifetime, and whether an existing producer and consumer already owns it. Separate generic Eshyra DM instructions from campaign-specific behavior and from campaign facts.
3. Identify legitimate episodic handoff content that is not already faithfully present in authoritative state or generated memory. Distinguish added continuity from simple restatement.
4. Design and, where practical without committing production architecture, run a four-arm ablation over representative multi-session cases:
   A. current baseline: generic DM system prompt plus current campaign/context/memory reconstruction;
   B. standing-seat treatment: baseline plus a bounded campaign/table-specific standing DM charter, if legitimate candidate data is identified;
   C. handoff treatment: baseline plus an outgoing-DM handoff only;
   D. combined treatment: baseline plus both the standing charter and outgoing handoff.
5. Make the experiment capable of independently concluding: neither adds value; standing reconstruction only adds value; handoff only adds value; or both add independent/complementary value. Do not design scoring or fixtures so either concept must win.
6. Cover NPC characterization, unresolved dramatic tension, player-specific salience, tactical/narrative setup, intentional future hooks, table-style/pacing/agency conventions, and an intended next-session opening beat where applicable.
7. Include normal session boundaries and a deliberately hard fresh-context boundary. Include cases where provider/model and, where supported, adapter family changes. Confirm any continuity comes from Eshyra-owned reconstruction rather than retained provider context.
8. Include adversarial cases where standing-charter or handoff text contradicts canonical state, source/module/rules authority, or an active campaign ruling; inject stale/superseded material as well. Demonstrate that it cannot become authority, mutate state, or override newer evidence.
9. Evaluate the runtime auditor separately. Determine whether it needs any standing role reconstruction beyond its current constrained jurisdiction and exact rules/state evidence. Do not assume primary-DM style, narrative intent, or rich seat semantics belong in auditor context.
10. End with one evidence-backed disposition and create no implementation successor until that disposition is accepted.

EXCLUSIONS / NON-GOALS

- No change to ADR 0020 discovery, adjudication, deterministic-capability, or state-integrity boundaries; no general runtime rule-discovery work.
- Do not replace or duplicate campaign bible, session recap, arc summary, character chronicle, campaign overlay, user-private data, campaign rulings, model profiles, trace metadata, or existing prompt/context ownership.
- No new canon/campaign-rule store and no production persistence subsystem, schema, migration, DmSeat table/class/entity, persistent persona, generic agent-identity framework, or broad memory redesign in this bead.
- No hidden chain-of-thought or private model reasoning; no metaphysical/personhood claim; no unbounded personality preservation; no provider-session affinity; no requirement to keep the same provider/model between sessions.
- No gameplay-state mutation from a charter or handoff. A style/preference/intent statement is never authority for a world fact or game rule.
- No generic ADR/process/governance cleanup, review-contract/checkpoint ceremony, agent-swarm/Thunderdome/merge-queue/Wheelhouse infrastructure, Gas City port, or speculative implementation children.

DEPENDENCIES / BLOCKERS

No active dependency or parent is required. Existing memory, adapter, prompt, trace, evaluation, user-private, and campaign-ruling surfaces are evidence inputs rather than blockers. If evaluation needs campaign rulings, consume the current eshyra-jhpt read interface without redesigning its ownership. Coordinate with active model-context work only to avoid fixture or seam conflicts.

MATERIAL-CHANGE STATUS

This semantic-system investigation is non-material while it changes only design/evaluation artifacts. Any accepted production change to prompt reconstruction, campaign/table preferences, durable memory, context assembly, handoff lifecycle, model-role identity, schema, precedence, retention, or auditor inputs is material and requires a fresh implementation bead under the accepted design. Do not implement production architecture here.

REQUIRED NEXT STATE / DISPOSITION

Permanent repository evidence must record exactly one evidence outcome:

- REJECTED: current reconstruction is sufficient; no successor.
- HANDOFF ONLY: handoff has demonstrated value, but no additional standing campaign-DM identity is justified.
- STANDING SEAT ONLY: campaign/table-specific role reconstruction has value, but outgoing handoff does not.
- COMPOSED SEAT + HANDOFF: both provide demonstrated independent/complementary value and can be composed from bounded primitives.
- FIRST-CLASS SEAT FOLLOW-UP: evidence identifies a concrete producer, consumer, and lifecycle that genuinely require a new first-class durable abstraction.

These labels describe evidence outcomes, not architecture chosen in advance. Any non-rejected disposition must specify the exact bounded production successor(s), if any; do not pre-create them before the investigation disposition.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Permanent repository evidence maps, with exact source references, what standing prompt/context currently reconstructs an Eshyra DM on every fresh model call or session, including buildSystemPrompt, the Hybrid Contract, tool/runtime instructions, assembled context, resume paths, and adapter rendering.
2. The evidence classifies every relevant input as generic DM role charter, campaign/table-specific behavior, authoritative campaign/module/rules/state, campaign ruling, generated campaign/character memory, episodic handoff candidate, user-private preference/data, or transient provider/model/session metadata. No category silently becomes another.
3. The analysis states what, if anything, makes the primary DM of one campaign meaningfully distinct from a generic Eshyra DM beyond knowing campaign facts, without anthropomorphism or continuity-of-consciousness claims.
4. Every candidate standing-seat datum and handoff datum is mapped to its authority, privacy, lifetime, provenance, staleness behavior, current or proposed producer, and current or proposed consumer. The evidence identifies which already have authoritative producers/consumers and which would require a new or extended one.
5. A bounded, inspectable four-arm ablation evaluates A current baseline, B standing campaign/table charter, C outgoing handoff, and D both. Fixtures and scoring/decision rules can fail and can independently conclude neither, standing only, handoff only, or complementary value.
6. The ablation measures whether a bounded standing campaign/table DM charter improves continuity over baseline without merely restating campaign facts or duplicating existing memory, rulings, profiles, user-private data, or configuration.
7. The ablation independently measures whether an outgoing-DM handoff improves continuity over baseline by preserving explicit immediate salience/intent not already faithfully carried by current memory, and measures whether it merely restates existing context.
8. The combined arm measures interaction as well as aggregate score, so evidence can show independent, redundant, conflicting, or complementary value from standing reconstruction and handoff.
9. Evaluation includes both normal session boundaries and a deliberately hard fresh-context boundary, plus provider/model changes and representative supported adapter-family variation where practical. Useful continuity must survive without provider-owned conversation state, hidden memory, same-model affinity, or provider-session affinity.
10. Representative cases cover NPC characterization trajectory, unresolved tension, player-specific salience, tactical/narrative setup, intentional future hooks, table style/pacing/agency conventions, and an intended next-session opening beat where applicable. Permanent results report context-budget and retention costs as well as continuity quality.
11. Adversarial regression cases inject false and stale standing-charter/handoff material that conflicts with canonical state, source/module/rules authority, active campaign rulings, and newer evidence. Tests/evaluation assertions prove it cannot outrank those sources, directly mutate state, launder a preference into a world fact/rule, or silently survive supersession.
12. The evidence determines whether the persistent primary-DM seat is best represented as composition of existing primitives, a narrowly extended prompt/preference/generated-memory concept, or a genuinely new first-class durable abstraction. Any first-class recommendation names the concrete producer, consumer, lifecycle, and why composition is insufficient.
13. The runtime auditor is evaluated separately. The evidence states what standing context it needs, if anything, and proves that table style or narrative intent does not expand its constrained rules/state jurisdiction or create false authority.
14. Permanent evidence answers all twelve investigation questions in the owning bead: current standing reconstruction; category boundaries; campaign-specific DM distinction; producer/consumer ownership; standing-charter value; handoff value; combined value; fresh-context/provider-change robustness; conflict precedence; representation choice; auditor implications; and exact justified successors.
15. The final evidence records exactly one disposition: REJECTED; HANDOFF ONLY; STANDING SEAT ONLY; COMPOSED SEAT + HANDOFF; or FIRST-CLASS SEAT FOLLOW-UP. The selected outcome names exact, narrowly scoped production successor bead(s) only where evidence justifies them; no speculative child exists before disposition.

title: Campaign-rule and ambiguity context grows monotonically with campaign age
description:
DEFERRED BY DESIGN, recorded so it is not lost.

assembleCampaignRulesContext supplies every active campaign rule and every ambiguity in the resolved rules stack on every DM turn, and renderContextMessage emits all of them. Raised by a /code-review sweep of PR #524 (finding 4) as monotonic prompt growth.

This is NOT a defect today and was NOT changed, because it is the deliberate contract: eshyra-jhpt.3 says "at initial scale, supply all active campaign-rule prose on every applicable DM turn; correctness takes priority over selective retrieval", and "prompt retrieval optimization" is an explicit non-goal on that bead. The supervisor measured the per-turn full-stack ambiguity scan at ~0.13 ms over 1812 records, so cost is not currently a concern either.

It becomes real when either side grows: the rules-pack compiler's stated direction is to add more ambiguity metadata (only 3 exist in the shipped SRD pack today), and campaign_rule accumulates for the life of a campaign with no upper bound. At that point the context needs relevance selection or a budget, which is a design decision requiring its own bead and probably an ADR note, not an incidental change.

Revisit when either the ambiguity count in a shipped pack or the active-rule count in a long-running campaign makes the per-turn slice materially large. Do not fix by silently truncating; that would reintroduce the "silent canonical certainty" failure eshyra-jhpt.3 exists to prevent.

description:

Attempt 1 (935d7d9) is structurally right and is KEPT. Specifically correct, do not disturb: migration 0026 campaign_turn_position with PK (campaign_id, session_id, turn_id) and UNIQUE (campaign_id, ordinal); resolveCampaignPosition's INSERT OR IGNORE + MAX(ordinal)+1 idempotency; and above all the placement of resolveCampaignPosition BEFORE `SAVEPOINT ${TURN_SAVEPOINT}` in orchestrator.runTurn — that is exactly what makes a rolled-back-and-replayed turn keep its position, which eshyra-jhpt.8 depends on. campaign/campaignContext.ts assembleCampaignRulesContext is the right shared DM/auditor projection and eshyra-jhpt.4 should consume it verbatim. The only test added was "assigns stable campaign-wide positions across sessions and replay" (good, keep it). assembleCampaignRulesContext — the actual deliverable, and the function eshyra-jhpt.4 will reuse for auditor parity — has NO direct test, and renderContextMessage's new section has none either. The attempt-1 dispatch listed the required coverage and it was not delivered.

  b. A superseded rule and a revoked rule are absent at positions after the change and present at positions before it.

assembleContext does `input.campaignPosition === undefined ? { position: '', rules: [], ambiguities: [] } : assembleCampaignRulesContext(...)`. title: Dispatch: Supply active campaign rules and source ambiguities to DM context (attempt 1)
description:
Dispatch of eshyra-jhpt.3 (attempt 1). Spec and acceptance criteria live on eshyra-jhpt.3 and the epic eshyra-jhpt; read both, including ADR 0020 TRANSITION AMENDMENT A1 on the bead. This bead carries the supervisor's pre-planning only.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.3.1 on branch eshyra-jhpt.3.1, cut from the integration branch eshyra-jhpt (merge 4a9620e), which already contains the completed eshyra-jhpt.1 domain model and eshyra-jhpt.2 storage/seam. Work only inside that worktree.

SCOPE
DM-side context assembly, plus the campaign-position assignment this bead needs (see part 1). NO auditor parity work (.4 — but build the projection so .4 can reuse it verbatim), NO ambiguity dialogue or player prompting (.6), NO precedent inference (.7), NO replay (.8), NO CLI (.5).

PART 1 — YOU MUST FIRST ESTABLISH CAMPAIGN POSITION ASSIGNMENT. THIS IS THE CENTRAL DESIGN TASK.
eshyra-jhpt.2 made campaignPosition REQUIRED on every active-at-position query (listActiveCampaignRulesAtPosition, listActiveRulingsForAmbiguitiesAtPosition, createCampaignRuleReadSeam). Nothing in the repo can currently produce one at turn time:
  - CampaignPosition is { sessionId, turnId, ordinal } (campaign/campaignRules.ts) and its ordinal is the authoritative chronology key.
  - turnId is generated in packages/cli/src/index.ts makeId() as `turn-<base36 timestamp>-<random>` — opaque and NOT ordered.
  - turn_trace is keyed (campaign_id, session_id, turn_id) with no ordinal; only scene_log.seq and campaign_arc.sequence_no are ordinals, and neither is a campaign-wide turn counter.
So this bead owns assigning and persisting the ordinal.
REQUIRED PROPERTY, because eshyra-jhpt.8 depends on it: the SAME turn must always resolve to the SAME position. A disputed turn is rolled back and replayed, and a rule effective "at the start of the disputed turn" only keeps meaning if the replayed turn occupies the identical position. Do not derive the ordinal from COUNT(*) of turn_trace or any other row count — a rollback changes the count and silently shifts every later position.
DESIGN: add migration 0026 with a small table mapping (campaign_id, session_id, turn_id) -> ordinal, monotonically assigned per campaign on first request and IDEMPOTENT thereafter, plus a resolver (suggested `resolveCampaignPosition(db, { campaignId, sessionId, turnId })`) returning a CampaignPosition. Assign at turn start. Test that re-resolving the same turnId returns the identical ordinal, that a rolled-back-and-replayed turn keeps its position, and that ordinals increase across turns and across a session boundary. Highest existing migration after eshyra-jhpt.2 is 0025_campaign_rules.sql, so yours is 0026_*.sql. Never edit an existing migration — migrationRunner.ts checksums applied ones — and update packages/core/test/migrationLegacyAdoption.test.ts ledger expectations, which is mandatory and not a test weakening.

PART 2 — SUPPLY ACTIVE CAMPAIGN RULES TO DM CONTEXT.
packages/core/src/orchestrator/contextAssembler.ts is the DM context builder: ContextAssemblyInput -> assembleContext() -> AssembledContext -> renderContextMessage(). It currently carries no rules slice at all.
- Add a campaign-rules slice to AssembledContext and render it in renderContextMessage.
- At initial scale supply ALL active campaign-rule prose at the current position on every applicable DM turn. Correctness beats selective retrieval; do not add retrieval scoring or a budget heuristic.
- Include stable rule identity, kind, effective provenance, and linked ambiguity/interpretation provenance. Do not ask the model to execute deterministic state logic.
- USE THE eshyra-jhpt.2 QUERIES DIRECTLY. Do not write a second active-rule resolver, do not cache rules in campaign state, and do not copy pack data into campaign state. The exact same projection must be reusable by eshyra-jhpt.4 for the auditor — factor the projection so .4 calls the identical function rather than rebuilding it. This is the whole point of amendment A1 and of transition W11's prohibition on a discovery-local store.
- AMENDMENT A1: the active-rule projection must expose, per rule, the linked ambiguity ID and, where one exists, the governing pack record key, so a consumer can pair a rule with its governing source material without re-deriving the association. CampaignRuleProjection already carries `ambiguityId` and `governingRecordKeys`; confirm both survive into whatever you hand the DM, and test it.

PART 3 — SURFACE UNRESOLVED SOURCE AMBIGUITY WITHOUT INVENTING CERTAINTY.
The shipped pack contains exactly THREE ambiguities (verified by grep over packages/core/data/rules-packs/): ambiguity:create-undead-ghast-wight-composition, ambiguity:find-familiar-permanent-dismissal-after-zero-hp, ambiguity:cube-of-force-same-face-duration-reset. Relevance selection is therefore not a scaling problem at initial scale — surface every unresolved one from the active rules stack and skip retrieval optimization entirely, consistent with the bead's "correctness takes priority over selective retrieval".
- RulesAmbiguity (rules/types.ts) is { id, question, source[], affects[], interpretations[{id, summary}], canonicalResolution: null, runtimeDisposition: { status: 'engine-pending', owner: 'campaign-ruling' } }. canonicalResolution is permanently null and the owner is 'campaign-ruling' — that is the source telling you it has no answer.
- For each ambiguity with NO active ruling at the current position, the rendered context must carry the question, the enumerated interpretation ids and summaries, and an explicit statement that this is unresolved and the DM must not assert a canonical answer or silently pick one. For each ambiguity WITH an active ruling, carry the ruling's prose beside the ambiguity rather than replacing or hiding the source material.
- Use listActiveRulingsForAmbiguitiesAtPosition from eshyra-jhpt.2 for the resolved/unresolved determination. Never write a winner or default back into the pack; assert pack immutability in a test.

TESTS
Prospective and effective-turn filtering (a rule effective later is absent now, present at/after its position); superseded and revoked rules absent at positions after the change and present before; deterministic ordering; A1 association data present; all three ambiguities surfaced unresolved with interpretations and no preferred winner; an ambiguity with an active ruling carries both ruling and source; pack bytes unchanged; position idempotency per part 1.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root, BEFORE committing (it rewrites files).

Added shared assembleCampaignRulesContext projection using listActiveCampaignRulesAtPosition and listActiveRulingsForAmbiguitiesAtPosition, retaining rule identity/kind/provenance/effective position/governing record keys and immutable pack ambiguity interpretations. Wired the projection and explicit unresolved/ruling rendering into DM context; updated schema snapshot and migration ledger expectations. title: Dispatch: Require campaign position, restore discovery boundary guard, ungate checkpoint proof (attempt 3)
description:
Dispatch of eshyra-jhpt.2 (attempt 3) — three remaining defects after supervisor review of attempt 2.

Attempt 2 (75ef96d) fixed four of six findings and is KEPT. Verified by supervisor probe: the ruling/house-rule temporal divergence is genuinely gone (at replay position 5 the seam now returns the ruling active at 5, r-old, not its later successor r-new). CampaignRuleError, prospectivity validation on revoke/supersede, the position-aware ruling query, the typed CampaignRuleReadSeam return, the isAmbiguityRuling guard, and the self-sorting comment are all correct. Do not revert any of that. Three defects remain.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.2.3 on branch eshyra-jhpt.2.3, cut from 75ef96d on eshyra-jhpt.2.2. Work only inside that worktree.

FINDING 1 (SEVERE, not fixed by attempt 2) — the position-less fallback is self-referential, so it can never exclude a future rule, and a new test now enshrines that.
activeRows resolves an omitted cutoff to `MAX(effective_position) FROM campaign_rule`. The latest rule therefore always defines the cutoff to its own position and always includes itself. Supervisor probe, one house rule effective at ordinal 999, still failing on attempt 2:
    at position 1 : []
    no position   : [ 'future' ]      <- future rule still leaks
The dispatch for attempt 2 required, for whichever option was chosen, a test proving the position-less result "never returns a rule whose effective position is in the future". That condition is unsatisfiable under a rules-table MAX, and instead campaignRuleStore.test.ts:121 "uses the latest recorded position when no cutoff is supplied" asserts `toEqual(['now', 'future'])` — it encodes the defect as the expected behaviour. AGENTS.md is explicit that expectations must not be adjusted to match current output; the implementation is what changes.
FIX: take the other option — make the campaign position REQUIRED on the active-at-position path. Change listActiveCampaignRulesAtPosition and listActiveRulingsForAmbiguitiesAtPosition to require campaignPosition, and require it on createCampaignRuleReadSeam. A caller that does not know the position must not receive a silently wrong answer; eshyra-jhpt.3 and .4 always know the position, and .8 must pass the disputed turn's position. Delete the "latest recorded position" fallback and the test that asserts the leak; replace that test with one proving a future-effective rule is absent at an earlier position and present at or after its effective position. (If some caller genuinely cannot supply a position, derive "current" from campaign history — turn_trace / scene_log — never from the rules table, and say so in your notes; but required-position is the expected outcome.)

FINDING 2 (guard test weakened — and the supervisor's dispatch caused it) — restore the discovery boundary guard by moving the seam type instead.
Attempt 2 added `!line.trimStart().startsWith('import type')` to the "is not imported by runtime modules" assertion in packages/core/test/discovery/discoveryBoundary.test.ts, because campaignRuleStore.ts now imports CampaignRuleReadSeam from ../discovery/types.js. That import happened because the attempt-2 dispatch told you to import it from there. That instruction was wrong and the guard should not have been relaxed to accommodate it: the guard exists because the offline discovery pilot is experiment-only and runtime modules must not depend on it, and a compile-time dependency on an experimental module is still a dependency.
FIX: move the CampaignRuleReadSeam interface (and NULL_CAMPAIGN_RULE_SEAM, if that keeps them together sensibly) into packages/core/src/campaign/campaignRules.ts alongside CampaignRuleProjection and CampaignRulingProjection, and have packages/core/src/discovery/types.ts re-export it — exactly the pattern eshyra-jhpt.1 already established for the projection types. Then campaignRuleStore.ts imports the seam type from its own domain, no runtime module imports discovery, and discoveryBoundary.test.ts REVERTS to its original assertion with no `import type` exemption. Keep the existing discovery re-export so discovery's own consumers are unaffected. Confirm src/internal.ts still exports the seam type exactly once.
This is the one place you may edit campaignRules.ts, and only to receive the moved type.

FINDING 3 (required coverage does not run) — the checkpoint round-trip proof is entirely Dolt-gated.
The new test lives in packages/core/test/checkpoint.restore.test.ts under `describe.skipIf(!doltOk)`. The `dolt` binary is absent on this machine, so the acceptance criterion "checkpoint/restore round trips preserve identities, ordering, provenance, statuses, and effective positions" has zero local coverage; skipped tests went from 19 to 20. The Dolt gate is legitimate for `restoreToNewWorkingCopy`, but the capture half needs no Dolt at all: serializeCampaign() and canonicalize() in persistence/checkpoint/serialize.ts are pure SQLite reads over sqlite_master.
FIX: split the proof. Add an ungated test (in the campaign-rule test file, or a checkpoint serialize test) that creates rules in every relevant state - active, superseded, revoked, ambiguity-provenance ruling, disputed-turn position - then asserts serializeCampaign captures the campaign_rule table with those identities, ordering, provenance, statuses, and effective positions intact, and that canonicalize is stable across two serializations. Keep the Dolt-gated full restore test as the end-to-end half. Do not add checkpoint machinery; serialize.ts already enumerates tables from sqlite_master.

SCOPE
Storage and query APIs, plus the type move in finding 2. No prompt/context assembly (.3/.4), no ambiguity dialogue (.6), no replay orchestration (.8), no CLI (.5). Do not fix the discovery-side cast tracked by eshyra-neus. Update any call sites affected by making the position required.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root, BEFORE committing (it rewrites files). Skipped test counts must not rise above the documented baseline for reasons introduced by this bead.

Dispatched 2026-09-02: codex gpt-5.6-luna medium, YOLO, pgid 675297, worktree .worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.2.3 on branch eshyra-jhpt.2.3 (cut from 75ef96d).
Completed attempt 3 in commit 7d3c2e2. Required campaignPosition on active rule/ruling queries and read-seam creation; removed the rules-table MAX fallback and replaced its leak test with future-effective boundary coverage. Moved CampaignRuleReadSeam and NULL_CAMPAIGN_RULE_SEAM into campaign/campaignRules.ts, retained discovery re-exports, restored the strict runtime discovery-boundary guard, and exported the seam type once from internal.ts. Added ungated SQLite checkpoint serialization coverage for active, superseded, revoked, ambiguity-provenance, and disputed-turn rules with stable canonicalization. Verification: npm run verify:worktree passed; 276 test files passed, 3 skipped; 4,841 tests passed, 20 skipped (Dolt/live baseline; Dolt unavailable). No follow-ups discovered. No push/PR performed per dispatch.

title: Dispatch: Fix campaign-rule temporal semantics, seam typing, and test gaps (attempt 2)
description:
Dispatch of eshyra-jhpt.2 (attempt 2) — supervisor review fixes on top of attempt 1.

Attempt 1 (eshyra-jhpt.2.1, commit 87e7587) is largely sound and is KEPT: migration 0025 with its CHECK constraints mirroring the domain unions, the lossless provenance columns, the jsonColumn use, the SQL ordering that leans on the self-sorting position encoding, the storage-side revoked_position decision (accepted — it is storage state, and eshyra-jhpt.5 can read revocation history from it), and the migrationLegacyAdoption.test.ts ledger updates (mandatory, correct). Do not revert any of that. Supervisor review found six defects; two are severe and reproduced below.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.2.2 on branch eshyra-jhpt.2.2, cut from 87e7587 on eshyra-jhpt.2.1 so attempt 1's work is present. Work only inside that worktree.

FINDING 1 (SEVERE) — rulings and house rules use DIFFERENT temporal semantics, so they disagree at any historical or replay position.
activeRows(db, campaignId, cutoff) has two unrelated behaviours. With a cutoff it applies correct HISTORICAL semantics (effective_position <= cutoff, not-yet-revoked at cutoff, not-yet-superseded at cutoff). Without a cutoff it applies `status = 'active'` only. createCampaignRuleReadSeam then calls activeRows WITH the caller's position for house rules, but activeRulingsForAmbiguities calls activeRows(db, campaignId) with NO cutoff — so rulings are answered with current-status semantics no matter which position is being asked about.

Reproduced (supervisor probe, both rules created effective at ordinal 1 and superseded at ordinal 10, then queried at replay position 5):
    house rules at replay position 5 : [ 'h-old' ]   <- historical semantics, correct
    rulings    at replay position 5 : [ 'r-new' ]   <- current-status semantics, WRONG

At position 5 the active ruling was r-old. This breaks the epic's central scenarios: eshyra-jhpt.4 requires DM and auditor to receive equivalent active sets at the turn's effective position, and eshyra-jhpt.8 replays a disputed turn under the rules active at that turn. A ruling superseded after the disputed turn is silently replaced by its successor during replay, while an equivalent house rule is handled correctly.
FIX: one temporal predicate for both kinds. The seam interface cannot take a position on activeRulingsForAmbiguities, so bind it at construction: give createCampaignRuleReadSeam an optional campaign position that activeRulingsForAmbiguities uses, and make activeRulesAtPosition consistent with it. Also add a direct, position-aware store API for rulings (e.g. listActiveRulingsForAmbiguitiesAtPosition(db, campaignId, ambiguityIds, campaignPosition)) so eshyra-jhpt.4 and .8 can ask for a historical position without going through the position-blind seam signature. Document on the seam factory that the discovery seam is position-blind for rulings by contract and that the bound position is what makes it correct.

FINDING 2 (SEVERE) — the position-less query does not mean "unfiltered", it means "wrong": future-effective rules leak.
With no cutoff the predicate is `status = 'active'` and effective_position is ignored entirely, so a rule that does not take effect until a much later position is returned as active now.
Reproduced (one house rule effective at ordinal 999):
    at position 1 : []
    no position   : [ 'future' ]      <- future rule leaks
eshyra-jhpt.3's acceptance criteria require "all and only rules active at the current campaign position" and explicit prospective/effective-turn filtering; a caller that omits the position gets a semantically different set, not merely a broader one, which also makes DM/auditor divergence easy to introduce in .4.
FIX: give the store ONE temporal semantic. Either make the position required on the active-at-position path, or define the position-less case explicitly as "at the latest recorded position" and implement it that way (still filtering effective_position). Whichever you choose, add a test proving the position-less result equals the result at the latest recorded position, and never returns a rule whose effective position is in the future.

FINDING 3 (test coverage) — the primary seam method's positive path is never exercised, and four required tests are missing.
activeRulingsForAmbiguities can only ever return rulings with 'ambiguity' provenance, but every ruling in the test file is built with 'recurring-question' provenance, so no test creates a rule that method could return. The only assertion, `expect(seam.activeRulingsForAmbiguities(['not-q'])).toEqual([])`, passes vacuously and would still pass if the method returned nothing at all. This is the method eshyra-jhpt.6 and transition probe P7 depend on.
Also missing from the required list on eshyra-jhpt.2.1: checkpoint/restore round trip; cross-campaign isolation; disputed-turn effective positions (every test rule is 'prospective'); invalid supersession combinations.
FIX: add all of them. For the ruling path, create a real ambiguity-provenance ruling (validateCampaignRule requires the ambiguity, so pass it via the validation options — that requirement is correct, keep it) and assert it is returned for its ambiguity id, is not returned for an unrelated id, and is not returned by activeRulesAtPosition. For checkpoint/restore, note that persistence/checkpoint/serialize.ts enumerates tables from sqlite_master so campaign_rule is captured automatically — the test proves the round trip preserves identities, ordering, provenance, statuses, and effective positions; it must not add checkpoint machinery.

FINDING 4 (idiom) — storage errors are plain `Error`.
campaignRuleStore.ts throws `new Error(...)` in six places. The domain module defines CampaignRuleError and the codebase convention is a domain error class per module (campaign.ts CampaignError, itemState.ts ItemStateError, and so on). Callers cannot distinguish a campaign-rule failure from an arbitrary runtime error.
FIX: throw CampaignRuleError (imported from campaignRules.js) from the store.

FINDING 5 (type safety) — nothing proves the seam implementation satisfies the interface.
createCampaignRuleReadSeam has no return type annotation, so its object literal is only structurally typed, and the body uses `as CampaignRuleProjection[]` to force the shape. If the CampaignRuleReadSeam contract changes, this silently stops matching.
FIX: annotate the return type as CampaignRuleReadSeam (import the type from discovery/types.js, which re-exports the campaign-domain projection types) and remove the cast so the compiler checks it. The trailing `.filter((r): r is CampaignRulingProjection => ...)` is unreachable given the ambiguity-provenance filter above it — simplify it or make it a genuine narrowing.

FINDING 6 (validation gaps in the acceptance criteria) — revocation and supersession are not required to be prospective.
revokeCampaignRule accepts any revokedPosition, including one before the rule's own effectivePosition. supersedeCampaignRule does not require the successor's effectivePosition to be at or after the prior rule's, yet the historical predicate relies on the successor's position to decide when the prior stopped being active. Both produce degenerate rules that are never active at any position. "Revoke prospectively" is an explicit acceptance criterion on eshyra-jhpt.2.
FIX: reject a revocation position earlier than the rule's effective position, and reject a successor whose effective position precedes the rule it supersedes. Test both rejections.

SCOPE
Unchanged: storage and query APIs only. No prompt/context assembly (.3/.4), no ambiguity dialogue (.6), no replay orchestration (.8), no CLI (.5). Do not edit packages/core/src/campaign/campaignRules.ts — the eshyra-jhpt.1 domain model is merged and closed; if you believe it must change, file a bd issue and report it instead. Do not fix the discovery-side cast tracked by eshyra-neus.
Add a brief comment where SQL ORDER BY relies on the canonical position encoding being self-sorting, so the dependency is visible if anyone revisits the encoding.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root, BEFORE committing (it rewrites files).
notes:
Dispatched 2026-09-02: codex gpt-5.6-luna medium, YOLO, pgid 657764, worktree .worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.2.2 on branch eshyra-jhpt.2.2 (cut from 87e7587 on eshyra-jhpt.2.1).
Completed in commit 75ef96d. Fixed all six review findings: unified historical active-row semantics with latest-recorded-position fallback for omitted cutoffs; added position-aware ruling queries and bound seam position documentation; added ruling, temporal, isolation, invalid lifecycle, and checkpoint/restore coverage; replaced campaign-rule store plain Errors with CampaignRuleError; added CampaignRuleReadSeam return typing and a real ambiguity-ruling type guard; enforced prospective revocation and supersession positions. Adjusted the boundary test to distinguish required type-only imports from runtime discovery imports. Verification: npm run verify:worktree passed (275 files, 4840 tests passed, 4 documented test files skipped / 20 tests skipped). No follow-up issues discovered.

title: Dispatch: Persist campaign rules in canonical campaign history (attempt 1)
description:
Dispatch of eshyra-jhpt.2 (attempt 1). Spec and acceptance criteria live on eshyra-jhpt.2 and the epic eshyra-jhpt; read both. This bead carries the supervisor's pre-planning only.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.2.1 on branch eshyra-jhpt.2.1, cut from the integration branch eshyra-jhpt (merge dee4471, which already contains the completed eshyra-jhpt.1 domain model). Work only inside that worktree.

SCOPE
Durable storage + query APIs only. NO prompt/context assembly (.3/.4), NO ambiguity dialogue (.6), NO replay orchestration (.8), NO CLI (.5). Build on the eshyra-jhpt.1 domain model in packages/core/src/campaign/campaignRules.ts — do not redefine its types, re-derive its ordering, or fork its validation.

CODE SURVEY (verified against dee4471)

1. THE DOMAIN MODEL YOU BUILD ON (packages/core/src/campaign/campaignRules.ts, exported via src/internal.ts).
   CampaignRule { ruleIdentity, campaignId, ruleKind: 'ruling'|'house-rule', status: 'active'|'revoked'|'superseded', origin: 'player-authored'|'player-approved'|'oracle-supplied', provenance (discriminated: 'ambiguity' {ambiguityId, selectedInterpretationId} | 'recurring-question' {questionId} | 'house-rule' {rationale?}), effectivePosition: CampaignPosition, temporalMode ('prospective' | 'disputed-turn' {disputedPosition}), supersededBy: string|null, scope, governingRecordKeys, prose }.
   CampaignPosition { sessionId, turnId, ordinal }. formatCampaignPosition emits `cp1~<12-digit ordinal>~<encoded session>~<encoded turn>`, which is CANONICAL AND SELF-SORTING: byte order equals chronological order. That property was added deliberately (eshyra-jhpt.1.3) so that SQL `ORDER BY effective_position` and `WHERE effective_position <= ?` are correct WITHOUT parsing. Store the canonical string in a TEXT column and rely on it; do not store a separate ordinal integer as the sort key and do not sort in JS after a full table scan. Use validateCampaignRule / validateCampaignRules on write and projectCampaignRule for the read projection.

2. THE READ SEAM YOU MUST IMPLEMENT IS ALREADY SPECIFIED AND ALREADY CONSUMED ON MAIN.
   packages/core/src/discovery/campaignRuleSeam.ts consumes CampaignRuleReadSeam (declared in discovery/types.ts, projection types re-exported from the campaign domain). eshyra-jhpt.3's amendment A1 and the transition's W11 depend on this being the ONE campaign-rule read interface; a discovery-local store is explicitly forbidden.
   THE EXACT CONTRACT IS PINNED BY AN IN-REPO REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION: packages/core/test/discovery/support/oracleCampaignRules.ts. Read it before you design the queries. It establishes, and your DB-backed implementation must match:
     - activeRulesAtPosition returns HOUSE RULES ONLY (the oracle filters ruleKind === 'house-rule'). Rulings are NOT returned here; they are returned only by activeRulingsForAmbiguities. campaignRuleSeam.ts concatenates the two results (`[...rules, ...rulings]`), so returning rulings from both would double-process them.
     - candidateRecordKeys is a HINT, NOT A FILTER. The oracle ignores it and returns every active house rule. campaignRuleSeam.ts's own comment is explicit: "R1 is about active rules applicable to the situation, not about whether discovery already found candidates, so a rule can surface governing material even when nothing else did." A rule whose governing keys are not among the candidates must still be RETURNED — the seam then either surfaces its governing record as a new candidate or records it as an `unplaced-rule` loss. If you filter by candidateRecordKeys you will silently break that route and the loss accounting.
     - activeRulingsForAmbiguities(ids) returns active rulings whose ambiguityId is in ids.
   Only an 'ambiguity'-provenance ruling may be projected as a CampaignRulingProjection (eshyra-jhpt.1.2 fixed a fabrication defect here). Note eshyra-neus tracks the discovery-side cast that is unsound for recurring-question rulings — do NOT fix that here; it is discovery's, not storage's.

3. MIGRATIONS ARE THE ONLY SCHEMA AUTHORITY (ADR 0015). Add the next migration under packages/core/data/migrations/ (highest today is 0024_active_effect_zone_form_projections.sql, so yours is 0025_*.sql). There is no hand-maintained latest-schema DDL and no CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS repair path; migrationRunner.ts verifies checksums of applied migrations, so never edit a migration that already exists. Follow the style of 0024: explicit CHECK constraints on every closed enum, named indexes, PRIMARY KEY on (campaign_id, ...). Mirror the domain's closed unions as CHECK constraints so the DB rejects what the domain rejects. Check whether packages/core/data/schema.snapshot.sql is generated or hand-maintained and update it the way the repo expects.

4. CHECKPOINT/RESTORE IS AUTOMATIC — DO NOT BUILD A MECHANISM. packages/core/src/persistence/checkpoint/serialize.ts enumerates tables from sqlite_master ("SELECT name, sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'") and snapshots every one. A new table is therefore included for free. What you owe is a TEST proving the round trip preserves identities, ordering, provenance, statuses, and effective positions, per the acceptance criteria — not new checkpoint code.

5. CAMPAIGN SCOPE. A campaign DB is single-campaign (campaign.ts stores campaign_id in meta), but the acceptance criteria still require cross-campaign isolation and rejection of cross-campaign supersession. Carry campaign_id on the table and enforce it in queries and in validation, matching validateCampaignRules which already rejects supersession across campaigns.

DESIGN NOTES / JUDGMENT CALLS

- REVOCATION NEEDS ITS OWN POSITION COLUMN. The domain has status 'revoked' but no revocation position; the epic requires revocation to be prospective and requires active-at-position queries to be correct for a position BEFORE a later revocation. Add a revoked-at-position column (nullable, canonical position string) so "active at position P" is: status not superseded, effective_position <= P, and (revoked_position IS NULL OR revoked_position > P). Report in your notes that this field is storage-side state the eshyra-jhpt.1 domain type does not carry, and say whether you think the domain type should gain it — if you believe it should, file a bd issue rather than editing the domain model here.
- SUPERSESSION likewise: a superseded rule must stop being active from the successor's effective position, not retroactively. Make sure your active-at-position predicate gets that right and test it at a position before and after the supersession.
- Persist provenance losslessly. The projection's `provenance` is a flattened display string; the discriminated union is the real data. Store the discriminant plus its fields in typed columns (or one JSON column via persistence/jsonColumn.ts, which is the established idiom — see rules/binding.ts addonsColumn) so a round trip reconstructs the exact CampaignRule, not just its projection.
- governingRecordKeys is a string array: use jsonColumn, consistent with the rest of the codebase.

REQUIRED OUTPUTS
- Migration 0025 creating the campaign-rule table with CHECK-constrained enums and the indexes the queries need.
- A storage module (suggested packages/core/src/campaign/campaignRuleStore.ts) with create, read-by-identity, list, supersede, revoke, and active-at-position query APIs, all campaign-scoped and deterministically ordered.
- A DB-backed CampaignRuleReadSeam implementation matching the oracle contract in point 2 exactly.
- Exports added to packages/core/src/internal.ts (NOT index.ts — new core symbols default to internal per AGENTS.md § Conventions).
- Tests: create/read/list/supersede/revoke; active-at-position determinism including a position before and after both a supersession and a revocation; prospective vs disputed-turn effective positions; invalid cross-campaign and invalid supersession combinations; checkpoint/restore round trip; and a test asserting the seam implementation matches the oracle contract (house-rules-only from activeRulesAtPosition, candidateRecordKeys not used as a filter, rulings only via activeRulingsForAmbiguities).

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root, BEFORE committing (it rewrites files).
notes:
Dispatched 2026-09-02: codex gpt-5.6-luna medium, YOLO, pgid 633176, worktree .worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.2.1 on branch eshyra-jhpt.2.1 (cut from eshyra-jhpt @ dee4471).
Completed in commit 87e7587. Added migration 0025_campaign_rules.sql and regenerated schema.snapshot.sql; implemented campaignRuleStore create/get/list, prospective active-at-position queries, supersession, revocation with storage-side revoked_position, lossless provenance JSON, deterministic canonical ordering, and shared CampaignRuleReadSeam (house-rules-only activeRulesAtPosition; candidate keys remain a hint; ambiguity rulings queried separately). Added focused persistence/seam tests and updated migration expectations for v25. The domain CampaignRule type remains unchanged: revoked_position is storage-side state needed for prospective historical queries, and no domain issue was filed because this storage metadata is sufficient for the current contract. Verification: npm run verify:worktree passed (275 test files passed, 4 skipped; 4838 tests passed, 19 skipped).

title: Dispatch: Make serialized campaign position self-sorting (attempt 3)
description:
Dispatch of eshyra-jhpt.1 (attempt 3) — one focused change on top of attempts 1 and 2.

Attempts 1 (ce3f9a5) and 2 (88060a7) are ACCEPTED and stay. compareCampaignPositions is now correct: ordinal-first with codepoint tie-breaks, well covered by tests that provably fail against the old source. Do not revisit any of that. This attempt fixes one remaining defect the supervisor found in review.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.1.3 on branch eshyra-jhpt.1.3, cut from 88060a7 on eshyra-jhpt.1.2, so both prior attempts are already present. Work only inside that worktree.

FINDING 5 (correctness, forward hazard for eshyra-jhpt.2) — the SERIALIZED position is still session-first, so it is not self-sorting.
The comparator was fixed to lead with the ordinal, but formatCampaignPosition still emits `cp1~<session>~<turn>~<12-digit ordinal>`. Chronology is therefore recoverable only by parsing. Any consumer that sorts or range-compares the STRING — which is exactly what the projection hands to discovery as `effectivePosition: string`, and exactly what eshyra-jhpt.2 will store in a TEXT column — gets the wrong answer.

Reproduced, ordering:
    true chronological order        SQL `ORDER BY effective_position` yields
    cp1~s2~t1~000000000005          cp1~s10~t1~000000000006
    cp1~s10~t1~000000000006         cp1~s2~t1~000000000005
    cp1~s3~t1~000000000007          cp1~s3~t1~000000000007

Reproduced, and worse, the range predicate .2 needs for "active rules at position":
    rule   cp1~s2~t1~000000000005   (ordinal 5, chronologically active)
    cutoff cp1~s10~t1~000000000006  (ordinal 6, current position)
    ordinal 5 <= 6                          -> true  (rule IS active)
    'cp1~s2~...' <= 'cp1~s10~...'           -> false (rule is DROPPED)
An active campaign rule would be silently missing from the active set. eshyra-jhpt.2's acceptance criteria require deterministic active-at-position queries and eshyra-jhpt.4 requires DM/auditor set parity; a natural SQL implementation over this encoding violates both, and the bug would look like a storage defect rather than an encoding one.

FIX: make the canonical serialized form self-sorting by leading with the zero-padded ordinal, e.g. `cp1~<12-digit ordinal>~<encoded session>~<encoded turn>`, so that lexical/byte order over canonical strings equals chronological order and `ORDER BY` and `<=` are correct in SQL without parsing. Update formatCampaignPosition and parseCampaignPosition together, keep the round-trip and the canonical-form check, and keep the `cp1~` version prefix. compareCampaignPositions should keep comparing parsed fields (it is correct and explicit); the point of this change is that consumers who never parse are also correct.

Also update the module doc comment: it currently documents the old layout. State the new layout and add one line recording WHY the ordinal leads — that byte order over canonical positions must equal chronological order so downstream SQL ordering and range predicates are correct without parsing.

TESTS
- Update the existing format/parse assertions to the new layout.
- Add a test asserting the self-sorting property directly: build positions across sessions with lexically misleading ids (the s2/s10/s3 case above), map them to canonical strings, and assert that a plain string sort equals the chronological order, and that a `<=` string range predicate agrees with the ordinal comparison. This is the property that was missing; assert it on the strings, not only through compareCampaignPositions.
- Keep every test added by attempts 1 and 2 passing.

SCOPE
Encoding, parsing, doc comment, and tests only. No schema, no migration, no storage APIs, no context assembly, no CLI, no discovery edits. Do not change the comparator's field order or the projection logic.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root, BEFORE committing (it rewrites files).
notes:
Dispatched 2026-09-02: codex gpt-5.6-luna medium, YOLO, pgid 614991, worktree .worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.1.3 on branch eshyra-jhpt.1.3 (cut from 88060a7 on eshyra-jhpt.1.2).
Completed in commit 6947f7a. Changed canonical campaign position encoding to cp1~<12-digit ordinal>~<encoded session>~<encoded turn>, updated parser and module documentation, and added direct lexical sorting/range predicate coverage across s2/s10/s3. Verification: npm run verify:worktree passed (format/check/typecheck; 274 test files passed, 4 skipped; 4,835 tests passed, 19 skipped). No follow-up issues discovered.

title: Dispatch: Fix campaign-rule ordering, determinism, and projection provenance (attempt 2)
description:
Dispatch of eshyra-jhpt.1 (attempt 2) — supervisor review fixes on top of attempt 1.

Attempt 1 (eshyra-jhpt.1.1, commit ce3f9a5) delivered packages/core/src/campaign/campaignRules.ts and packages/core/test/campaignRules.test.ts. The structure is sound and is KEPT: the domain/projection split, the move of CampaignRuleProjection/CampaignRulingProjection out of discovery/types.ts into the campaign domain with a re-export for discovery, the validation invariants, and the internal.ts export surface are all correct and must not be reverted. Supervisor review found three defects, reproduced below. Fix exactly these; do not redesign what is working.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.1.2 on branch eshyra-jhpt.1.2, cut from eshyra-jhpt.1.1 (commit ce3f9a5) so attempt 1's work is already present. Work only inside that worktree.

FINDING 1 (SEVERE, correctness) — campaign position ordering is not chronological across sessions.
formatCampaignPosition encodes `cp1~<session>~<turn>~<12-digit ordinal>` and compareCampaignPositions compares that whole string. Session is therefore the PRIMARY sort key, so a later position sorts before an earlier one whenever session ids do not happen to sort lexically in creation order. Reproduced:
    early = { sessionId: 's2',  turnId: 't1', ordinal: 5 }   -> cp1~s2~t1~000000000005
    late  = { sessionId: 's10', turnId: 't1', ordinal: 6 }   -> cp1~s10~t1~000000000006
    compare(early, late) === 1     // positive: the EARLIER position sorts last
The module doc comment claims "Lexical comparison of canonical positions is a total order." It is a total order, but it is the wrong order — it is not chronological. orderCampaignRules is built on this compare, and eshyra-jhpt.3/.4 depend on it for "all and only the rules active at the current position, in deterministic order" and for DM/auditor set parity. A wrong-but-stable order will silently mis-order active rules across session boundaries.
FIX: the monotonic ordinal is the chronological key and must be compared FIRST, with sessionId/turnId as tie-breakers and diagnostic anchors only. Either reorder the encoding so the ordinal leads (e.g. `cp1~<ordinal>~<session>~<turn>`), or compare the parsed struct field-by-field (ordinal, then sessionId, then turnId) instead of comparing formatted strings. State in the doc comment which field is authoritative for chronology and why. Whichever you choose, formatCampaignPosition must stay round-trippable through parseCampaignPosition and stay canonical.

FINDING 2 (correctness/determinism) — compareCampaignPositions uses String.prototype.localeCompare.
localeCompare applies ICU collation in the host's default locale, which is neither codepoint order nor guaranteed stable across environments or Node ICU builds. Reproduced divergences from codepoint order on this machine (node v24.16.0, full ICU):
    'cp1~S1~t~000000000001'.localeCompare('cp1~s1~t~000000000001')  ===  1   (codepoint: -1)
    'cp1~a~t~000000000001'.localeCompare('cp1~B~t~000000000001')    === -1   (codepoint:  1)
Deterministic ordering is a stated acceptance criterion of this bead and of .3/.4; a locale-dependent comparator cannot satisfy it, and a CI or user machine with a different default locale or a small-ICU Node build can order the active rule set differently from a developer machine.
FIX: use explicit codepoint comparison (`a < b ? -1 : a > b ? 1 : 0`) or numeric/field comparison. Do not use localeCompare anywhere in this ordering path. Note orderCampaignRules also calls `a.ruleIdentity.localeCompare(b.ruleIdentity)` as its final tie-break — same problem, same fix.

FINDING 3 (truthfulness/provenance) — projectCampaignRule fabricates ambiguity provenance for a recurring-question ruling.
For ruleKind 'ruling' with provenance.kind === 'recurring-question' the projection currently emits:
    ambiguityId: `question:${provenance.questionId}`
    selectedInterpretationId: provenance.questionId
No such ambiguity exists in any rules pack and no interpretation was ever selected. The epic's central non-goal is inventing certainty the source does not carry, and ADR 0020 amendment A1 defines the projection's ambiguity id as the LINKED ambiguity id. Synthesizing both fields claims a source linkage and a player selection that never happened. It is currently inert in discovery's resolve path (campaignRuleSeam.ts only marks an ambiguity resolved when the ruling's ambiguityId matches a real pack ambiguity id, which `question:` never will), but it still flows into the packet as campaignRulings[].ambiguityId and will be read downstream as real provenance.
FIX: a recurring-question ruling has no linked ambiguity, so it must project WITHOUT ambiguityId and WITHOUT selectedInterpretationId — i.e. as a plain CampaignRuleProjection carrying ruleKind 'ruling'. Only an 'ambiguity'-provenance ruling may produce a CampaignRulingProjection. Note that packages/core/src/discovery/campaignRuleSeam.ts withRule() currently casts any ruleKind==='ruling' projection to CampaignRulingProjection; check whether that cast becomes unsound under this change and, if it does, report it in your notes and file a bd issue against eshyra-jhpt.3 rather than editing discovery behavior here — this bead is domain-model-only. Do NOT loosen CampaignRulingProjection to make the fabrication type-check.

FINDING 4 (test gap that let 1 and 2 through) — the ordering tests never cross a session or a turn.
packages/core/test/campaignRules.test.ts declares sessionId exactly once, in the `position` helper, so every position in every test shares 'session-1'. The "orders a shuffled active set deterministically" test therefore cannot observe either ordering defect.
FIX: add coverage that would have caught findings 1 and 2 — ordering across sessions with lexically-misleading ids (the s2/s10 case above), ordering across turns within a session, mixed-case and punctuation-bearing session/turn ids, and a shuffled multi-session set whose sorted result is asserted against explicit chronological expectations. Assert the comparator's sign directly, not only the sorted output.

CodeQL check on the PR is FAILURE because a NEW alert appeared:

       "may run slow on strings with many repetitions of '-'"

That is the `.replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '')` at the end of `normalizeAbilityName`.
The attempt-1 spec explicitly told the child NOT to touch it, on the reasoning
that the preceding `.replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')` collapses every run of
non-alphanumerics — `-` included, since `-` is itself outside `[a-z0-9]` — to a
single `-`, so `-+` can never span more than one character. That reasoning is
correct about RUNTIME behavior and remains true. It is simply not something
CodeQL models.

Why it surfaced only now, confirmed against the API: on `refs/heads/main` the
open-alert set is exactly the three original sites and has never included
line 262, and the byte-identical `/^-+|-+$/g` at
`packages/core/src/state/attunement.ts:442` and
`packages/cli/src/characterDraftStore.ts:51` is not flagged either. The query
reports one sink per tainted source→sink flow; `\([^)]*\)` was the reported
sink on this chain, and removing it exposed the next sink on the SAME flow.

it is the rest of the same alert, and the owning bead's goal is to clear the
alerts.

   is recorded. Do not otherwise change the two existing helpers or their
   existing tests.

2. Add a third exported helper to that module:

   ```ts
   /**
    * Trim leading and trailing runs of `ch` without the polynomial
    * backtracking reported by CodeQL's js/polynomial-redos rule. Exactly
    * equivalent to `text.replace(/^<ch>+|<ch>+$/g, '')` for a single
    * non-special character.
    */
   export function trimEdgeChar(text: string, ch: string): string {
     let start = 0;
     let end = text.length;
     while (start < end && text[start] === ch) start += 1;
     while (end > start && text[end - 1] === ch) end -= 1;
     return text.slice(start, end);
   }
   ```

   Note this is equivalent UNCONDITIONALLY — it does not depend on the
   collapse invariant described above, which is the point: the invariant stays

title: Dispatch: linear paren-scan repair for three polynomial-ReDoS sites (attempt 1)
description:
Dispatch bead for `eshyra-e1kt` (read that bead for the spec). Attempt 1.

Branch/worktree: `eshyra-e1kt.1`, cut from branch `eshyra-e1kt`.
Model config: gpt-5.6-luna, reasoning effort medium.

## What CodeQL actually flags

Three open `js/polynomial-redos` alerts (#15, #16, #17), all the SAME
recognizer shape — `/\([^)]*\)/`. The alert message is "may run slow on
strings starting with '(' and with many repetitions of '('": `[^)]` admits
`(`, so the inner star overlaps the `\(` prefix. On `"((((((..."` (no `)`)
every start position rescans to end of string — O(n^2).

- `packages/core/src/state/usageCounters.ts:259` — inside
  `normalizeAbilityName`: `.replace(/\([^)]*\)/g, ' ')`
- `packages/core/src/state/usageCounters.ts:353` — inside
  `economyFromEntryMechanics`: `entryName.replace(/\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$/, '')`.
  Alert 17 reports TWO findings for this one line: the `(` overlap above, and
  a second on "many repetitions of ' '" from the leading `\s*` against the
  `$`-anchored tail.
- `packages/core/src/state/actionEconomy.ts:441` — inside
  `normalizeLegendaryName`: `.replace(/\([^)]*\)/g, ' ')`

## Reachability — fix, do not dismiss

These are not fed only by the bundled SRD pack. `normalizeAbilityName` is
called on caller-supplied `input.ability` (`usageCounters.ts:851`, `:1024`)
and `normalizeLegendaryName` on `input.legendaryActionName`
(`actionEconomy.ts:1183`) — i.e. tool-call arguments from the model/DM path,
plus arbitrary third-party rules-pack record text. The "trusted and fixed
size" escape hatch in the parent bead does not apply to any of the three.

The neighbouring `.replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '')` (usageCounters:262) and
`.trim()` (actionEconomy:444) are NOT flagged and must not be touched: the
preceding `.replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, …)` already collapses separator runs to a
single character, so those quantifiers can never span more than one char.
`LEGENDARY_COUNT_RE` (actionEconomy:428) is likewise unflagged and out of
scope — its `\d+` sits behind the literal prefix `take `.

## Required fix shape — linear scan, behavior preserved

Precedent in this repo: commit `bf075b8` (`hasMechanicalParenNote` in
`packages/core/src/rules/srdPlayabilityAudit.ts`) replaced the same recognizer
shape with an `indexOf`-based scan, and `d4462b6` did the same for the
encounter-combatant slug. Follow that, not a bounded-repetition patch: an
`indexOf` scan reproduces the regex EXACTLY, where `\([^()]*\)` or
`\([^)]{0,N}\)` would silently change results on nested or overlong input.

Add one small shared module — suggested
`packages/core/src/state/parentheticalNames.ts` — with two exported helpers,
both pure and allocation-light, each carrying a comment that names the CodeQL
rule and states the equivalence it preserves. Both call sites in
`usageCounters.ts` and the one in `actionEconomy.ts` then import it; do not
duplicate the scan in two files.

1. `replaceParentheticals(text: string, replacement: string): string`
   — exact equivalent of `text.replace(/\([^)]*\)/g, replacement)`.
   Because `[^)]*` cannot cross a `)`, each match runs from a `(` to the
   FIRST `)` after it, and the global scan resumes just past that `)`:

   ```ts
   let out = '';
   let from = 0;
   for (;;) {
     const open = text.indexOf('(', from);
     if (open === -1) break;
     const close = text.indexOf(')', open + 1);
     if (close === -1) break;   // no ')' after open ⇒ none after any later '('
     out += text.slice(from, open) + replacement;
     from = close + 1;
   }
   return out + text.slice(from);
   ```

2. `stripTrailingParenthetical(text: string): string`
   — exact equivalent of `text.replace(/\s*\([^)]*\)\s*$/, '')`.
   That regex takes the leftmost match, which forces the `(` to be the last
   `(` in the string, the closing `)` to be the last non-space character, and
   the span between them to contain no `)`; the leading `\s*` then eats the
   whole whitespace run before that `(`. So:

   ```ts
   const end = text.trimEnd().length;          // JS \s and trim share a set
   if (end === 0 || text[end - 1] !== ')') return text;
   const open = text.lastIndexOf('(', end - 1);
   if (open === -1) return text;
   if (text.slice(open + 1, end - 1).includes(')')) return text;
   return text.slice(0, open).trimEnd();
   ```

   Note `String.prototype.trim`/`trimEnd` strip exactly WhiteSpace ∪
   LineTerminator, the same set `\s` matches, so the `\s*` ↔ `trimEnd`
   substitution is faithful — say so in the comment.

Export both from `packages/core/src/internal.ts` (new core symbols default to
internal per AGENTS.md § Conventions; do NOT add them to `index.ts`).

helpers from `../src/internal.js`, covering:

title: Clear three pre-existing high-severity polynomial-ReDoS CodeQL alerts
description:
Discovered while clearing the CodeQL alert on PR #518 (eshyra-o9bd.19.10).

Three `js/polynomial-redos` alerts, all high security-severity, are open on
main and predate that PR (it touches none of these files):

- packages/core/src/state/usageCounters.ts:258
- packages/core/src/state/usageCounters.ts:353
- packages/core/src/state/actionEconomy.ts:440

The W8 fix is the worked example of the repair shape: an unanchored `\d+` (or
similar unbounded repetition) scanned over text that is not tightly
controlled costs quadratic work across start positions when the rest of the

(`\d{1,4}`, a single-character separator class) makes the match linear and
kept the behavior identical.

Assess each of the three sites against its actual input source, bound or
restructure the expression, and add an adversarial long-input regression per
site. If a site's input is genuinely trusted and fixed-size, record that
finding and dismiss the alert with the reason rather than changing code.

No change to usage-counter or action-economy semantics; this is a
recognizer-shape repair, not a behavior change.

title: Close the bead-lifecycle gap that makes Codex close beads at PR-open
description:
PROBLEM

Codex running as a main agent closes an owning bead as soon as it opens the
PR, then reopens it when a blocking review arrives. Claude main-agent sessions
hold the bead in_progress until the PR merges. The divergence is structural,
not a model quirk.

DIAGNOSIS (verified against the tree at e30340d)

1. The only statement in the repo that resolves the question lives in
   `.claude/hooks/codex-subagent-workflow.md` (the "Bead-per-dispatch pattern"
   section): "In this repo handoff stops at an open PR: if the PR is not yet
   merged when the session ends, leave the parent in_progress with the PR URL
   in its notes and close it in a later session once merged."

   That file is injected by `.claude/settings.json` SessionStart ->
   `.claude/hooks/supervisor-context.mjs`, which Codex can never reach. The
   script's own header says so: "Codex never executes Claude Code hooks, so
   Codex-driven sessions can't reach this script at all." It further gates on
   `agent_id` (main agent only) and fail-closed on a Fable/Opus model match.

   The file header also forbids the remedy: "Keep this content OUT of
   AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, bd memories, and bead descriptions." That restriction
   is correct for supervisor policy (subagents must not be told to dispatch
   children) but the bead-lifecycle sentence is not supervisor policy; it is
   general repository lifecycle that was swept in with it.

2. AGENTS.md, the authority Codex does read, points the other way. Its
   "Session Completion" section opens "An open, unmerged PR is a complete
   handoff" and then instructs "Close finished beads and update in-progress
   ones." The natural reading is: PR open -> handoff complete -> bead finished
   -> close it. Nothing separates "the work is finished" from "the bead may
   close."

3. `bd prime` injects a generated "SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL" into BOTH Claude and
   Codex whose first checklist item is `bd close <id>` ("close completed
   issues"), marked CRITICAL and triggered on "before saying done or
   complete." AGENTS.md has a precedence rule for a disagreeing generated
   block, but it does not disagree here -- AGENTS.md is silent on
   merge-vs-open, so the generated block fills the vacuum unopposed.

The reopen-on-blocking-review behavior follows rationally from (2)+(3): if
closing at PR-open is correct, a blocking review means the work was not
finished, so the bead reopens.

SCOPE

- Add the lifecycle rule to AGENTS.md "Session Completion", scoped by
  DELIVERABLE rather than by agent role, so it stays correct for dispatched
  children: a child's deliverable is a commit handed back to an integrating
  agent, not a PR, and children must still close their own beads.
- State explicitly that the rule narrows the generated bd-prime checklist, so
  AGENTS.md's existing generated-block precedence rule engages.
- Replace the inline sentence in `.claude/hooks/codex-subagent-workflow.md`
  with a pointer to AGENTS.md, so there is one source of truth (the DRY
  principle CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md already state) and the hook's own
  "keep this content out of AGENTS.md" header stops contradicting the tree.

NON-GOALS

- No change to the supervisor/subagent boundary the hook exists to enforce:
  dispatch policy stays supervisor-only and out of AGENTS.md.
- No change to the child-dispatch protocol, which must keep closing its own
  bead and handing back a commit.
- No change to bd or its generated onboarding snippet; AGENTS.md is
  hand-maintained and narrows it, per the existing rule that this file wins
  over a generated block.
notes: PR #519 opened 2026-09-01 from branch eshyra-o9bd.19.16 (head 5866b30), awaiting review. AGENTS.md Session Completion now carries the rule scoped by deliverable; the supervisor hook points at it instead of restating it; the hook header's blanket 'keep out of AGENTS.md' is narrowed to supervisor policy. packages/core/test/beadLifecyclePolicy.test.ts pins it, verified as a real guard (4/5 assertions fail against the previous AGENTS.md, the fifth against the previous hook). Verification: 267 files, 4769 passed / 19 skipped. Bead stays in_progress until PR #519 merges -- which is the rule this PR adds.
close_reason: Merged to main as PR #519, merge commit f0fad2a. AGENTS.md Session Completion now carries the deliverable-scoped bead lifecycle rule; the supervisor hook points at it instead of restating it; the hook header's blanket 'keep out of AGENTS.md' is narrowed to supervisor policy. packages/core/test/beadLifecyclePolicy.test.ts pins it. Closing now (not at PR-open) is exactly the rule this bead added.
