title: Migrate biome.json schema pin to the installed Biome (2.5.5 -> 2.5.10)
description:
`biome.json` line 2 pins `https://biomejs.dev/schemas/2.5.5/schema.json` while
the installed `@biomejs/biome` is 2.5.10. Biome emits a `deserialize` INFO
diagnostic on every `npm run check` / `format:check` / `lint` run:

    The configuration schema version does not match the CLI version 2.5.10
      Expected: 2.5.10
      Found:    2.5.5

Info-level diagnostics do not fail the build (Biome has no exit-on-info flag),
so this is invisible to CI, which is exactly the accumulation AGENTS.md's
"Formatting & Linting" section warns about: "keep `biome.json` migrated to the
installed Biome (`npx biome migrate --write`)".

Pre-existing on `main` as of 6015db0; observed while verifying
eshyra-o9bd.19.1.15 (PR #507) and deliberately left out of that PR to keep it
scoped to the Foundation 2 registry.

Fix: run `npx biome migrate --write` from the repo root, confirm
`npm run check` reports zero diagnostics (not just zero errors), and commit the
`biome.json` change on its own branch. Per AGENTS.md's dependency rules, keep
this separate from feature work; a semver-major Biome bump is a different
decision and is not in scope here.
close_reason: Stale: resolved by PR #530 (eshyra-ldtn, merged bc190dc), which ran npx biome migrate --write as part of landing Biome 2.5.12. Verified on main at 84e8e79: biome.json $schema is 2.5.12 and matches the installed CLI (biome --version 2.5.12); 'biome check --diagnostic-level=info .' reports zero diagnostics, so the deserialize INFO this bead tracked is gone; 'biome migrate' reports 'no migration needed', i.e. the fix this bead prescribes is now a no-op. Duplicate of eshyra-2whc, filed one day earlier for the same info diagnostic.

title: Transition W15: held-out and bounded live-play evaluation (Phase 4)
description:
Workstream W15 of the integrated ADR 0020 transition design, Phase 4 (section
12.4), measured under section 13:
docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md.
That design is the accepted deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8 (PR #485, reviewed
head afd113c7090378c3a9f4122f246a6c32602a5164, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282). ADR 0020 controls.

OWNER
This bead is the single owner of held-out and live-play evaluation of the
rule-discovery experiment. No other bead owns it.

SCOPE
- Author and run HELD-OUT probe variants: probes written after the pipeline was
  tuned and never used to tune it. A held-out probe that was consulted during
  tuning is no longer held out and must be relabelled.
- Then run BOUNDED live play, only after shadow evidence (W9) exists and the
  scripted provider-neutral intervention tests (W10) pass.
- Report M1-M12 with the same instrumentation used offline and in shadow.
- Attribute every miss to the exact stage that lost it - signals, candidates,
  expansion, rule join, dedup, priority, or packet - and convert it into
  successor work for signal extraction, relationship traversal, campaign-rule
  matching, ranking, context retention, capability presentation, or auditor
  policy.

PROHIBITIONS (design sections 3.2, 12.4, 13.2; ADR 0020 section 6)
- A held-out miss bounds an awareness-failure rate on that corpus. It says
  nothing about the corpus's complement. Neither a hit nor a miss establishes or
  refutes universal retrieval completeness, and no result may be reported as if
  it did.
- No aggregate readiness score, completeness score, coverage percentage, or
  universal pass/fail. An aggregate across probes may be reported only as a count
  of probes passing, never as a rate over the rules universe.
- Presence is not use: no measurement infers model reliance from packet
  membership; auditor retries and explicit citations are correlates, never proof.
- No universal clause identity, relationship vocabulary, or corpus-wide
  capability claim.
- No campaign-rule persistence, ruling lifecycle, or discovery-local rule store:
  those remain eshyra-jhpt's.
- No phase is accepted because nothing failed: a stage that recorded no
  candidates, no routes, and no losses has failed to run.

DEPENDENCIES
W10 (context-packet intervention) must be accepted first, which in turn requires
W9 shadow evidence. Not parallel-safe.

PERMANENT EVIDENCE
Held-out probe reports carrying M1-M12 per probe with per-stage attribution of
every miss, an explicit record of which probes were held out and when they were
authored, and bounded live-play reports under the same instrumentation.

REQUIRED NEXT STATE
Held-out probes report M1-M12 with the same instrumentation; misses are
attributed to a named stage and converted into successor work rather than into a
claim about coverage.

MATERIAL CHANGE: no. It measures; it changes no contract, boundary, or runtime
behavior.
acceptance_criteria:
Held-out probe variants are authored after the pipeline was tuned and are demonstrably not used to tune it; the report records when each was authored and that it was never consulted during tuning, and any probe that was consulted is relabelled and excluded from held-out evidence. Bounded live play runs only after shadow evidence exists (W9) and the scripted provider-neutral intervention tests pass (W10). M1-M12 are reported per probe with the same instrumentation used offline and in shadow, and every miss is attributed to the exact stage that lost it and converted into named successor work. No result claims or refutes universal retrieval completeness; a held-out miss is reported as bounding an awareness-failure rate on that corpus only. No aggregate readiness score, completeness score, coverage percentage, or universal pass/fail is produced; cross-probe aggregation is reported only as a count of probes passing. No measurement infers that the model used material because it was present. A stage that records no candidates, routes, or losses is reported as failed-to-run, not as passing.

PHASE 4 EXIT DISPOSITION (added 2026-09-22 by eshyra-9l5s.5; audit T9 / finding F3; required by AGENTS.md "Permanent Test Evidence"). Phase 4 is the boundary of the bounded discovery experiment, so it is not validly closed until every piece of discovery experiment infrastructure carries an explicit disposition recorded on this bead: retained, demoted, or retired, exactly as AGENTS.md defines them. In scope: each module under packages/core/src/discovery/ (accounting, bands, blockerRepairs, campaignRuleSeam, candidates, dedup, expansion, harness, measurements, packet, packetMessage, retention, shadow, signals, structuralEquality, traceDerivation, traceProjection, types) and each file under packages/core/test/discovery/, plus the orchestrator discoveryMode seam that reaches them. Judge each by the responsibility that survives the boundary, never by root-export status and never by current runtime use alone: a retained module whose consumer is not yet integrated is recorded as retained-and-staged with its successor owner and next integration state named. blockerRepairs.ts (runtime observation of design-section-9 blockers B1-B5) must be dispositioned explicitly, since its requirement is a process artifact. A retirement names the responsibility that replaces the old claim and must not hide a source-fidelity, discovery, capability, adjudication, or state-integrity defect. This criterion records dispositions; it authorizes no code change by itself. Any removal or demotion is separately authorized work.
notes:
WORKSTREAM-TO-BEAD MAP (integrated transition design section 14, materialized
2026-07-31). Workstream numbers in these descriptions resolve as follows; judge
ownership by this map and by the dependency tree, never by bead-ID prefix.

  W1  stat-block lookup repair (B1)             eshyra-l3e5
  W2  CLI adventure-resolver repair (B2)        eshyra-seoh
  W3  strict campaign-stack repair (B3)         eshyra-6vpw
  W4  source-authority repair (B4)              eshyra-o9bd.19.2.1
  W5  item-readiness fail-open repair (B5)      eshyra-uiax
  W6  durable finding registry                  eshyra-o9bd.19.1.15
  W7  diagnostic fixture corpus                 eshyra-o9bd.19.9
  W8  offline discovery stage harness           eshyra-o9bd.19.10
  W9  runtime shadow trace integration          eshyra-o9bd.19.11
  W10 context-packet intervention               eshyra-o9bd.19.12
  W11 jhpt read-interface consumption           eshyra-o9bd.19.13
  W12 campaign rules and ruling implementation  eshyra-jhpt.1-.9 (+ A1-A4)
  W13 capability-contract normalization         eshyra-olc5.6
  W14 artifact dispositions (sections 5.1-5.6)  eshyra-o9bd.19.14
      re-freeze bar (section 5.9)               eshyra-o9bd.14, eshyra-2zyy
  W15 held-out and live-play evaluation         eshyra-o9bd.19.15

TRACEABILITY: every bead in the W7-W15 set was created 2026-07-31 to execute the
design accepted as the deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8 (PR #485, reviewed head
afd113c7090378c3a9f4122f246a6c32602a5164, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282). They are parented to the ACTIVE
transition epic (eshyra-o9bd.19, or eshyra-olc5 for W13) rather than to the
closed design bead, so lifecycle semantics stay honest; eshyra-o9bd.19.8 remains
the design authority and is referenced from each description.

BOUNDARY THAT MUST NOT ERODE (design sections 8.4 and 14.3): campaign-rule
persistence and ruling lifecycle do not move out of eshyra-jhpt under any of
these items. W11 consumes; it does not own. If the jhpt interface proves
insufficient, the correct response is an amendment or a child under eshyra-jhpt,
never a discovery-local store.

Amendment only; no parallel lifecycle bead was created, per the audit. Evidence for current cost: the discovery test files are ~16 s of summed worker time in a 45 s capped suite (2026-09-22 remeasurement on eshyra-9l5s.5); cost is not a reason to disposition early.
CORRECTION to the preceding 2026-09-22 note: discovery test files are 25.0-30.5 s of summed worker time (of 135-150 s summed across 309 files) over four capped full-suite runs, not ~16 s. Conclusion unchanged: cost is not a reason to disposition early.
ADR-0020 disposition pass 2026-09-22 (eshyra-o9bd.19 rebaseline): KEPT - W15 held-out/live evaluation is now dependency-unblocked (W10 closed) and owns the Phase 4 exit disposition of the discovery experiment infrastructure; recovery order places it after the Lane A source repairs.

title: Transition W11: consume the eshyra-jhpt campaign-rule read interface from discovery
description:
Workstream W11 of the integrated ADR 0020 transition design, section 8 (the
narrow campaign-rule read interface discovery requires):
docs/audits/rules-awareness-transition/2026-07-30-integrated-transition-design.md.
That design is the accepted deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8 (PR #485, reviewed
head afd113c7090378c3a9f4122f246a6c32602a5164, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282). ADR 0020 controls.

OWNER
This bead owns ONLY the discovery-side consumption of the eshyra-jhpt read
interface. eshyra-jhpt and its nine children remain the authoritative owner of
campaign rules and ambiguity rulings. This bead consumes that runtime; it does
not replace, duplicate, or extend it.

SCOPE (discovery side only)
Replace the W8 stub seam with real consumption of the eshyra-jhpt runtime, so
that the discovery stage pipeline and the W10 context packet can:

- request active campaign rules applicable at the adjudicated campaign position,
  through the same active-at-position query the auditor uses (eshyra-jhpt.3,
  backed by .2);
- request active rulings for discovered RulesAmbiguity IDs (eshyra-jhpt.6);
- carry ruling identity, campaign scope, provenance, and supersession status
  through to the packet unchanged (eshyra-jhpt.1, .2);
- place an active rule or ruling beside its governing pack record or ambiguity,
  using association data supplied by jhpt (amendment A1 on eshyra-jhpt.3);
- pass an active ruling to bounded capability preflight where execution depends
  on it (amendment A2 on eshyra-jhpt.6, designed with the eshyra-olc5 readiness
  owner because assertMagicItemOperationReady runs before matchStateTransition);
- record retrieval evidence in the existing accepted-turn trace (amendment A3 on
  eshyra-jhpt.4/.9), so M5 is measurable without a discovery-owned store;
- preserve the absence case: a discovered ambiguity with no active ruling keeps
  its uncertainty and never acquires silent canonical certainty
  (eshyra-jhpt.3, .6; probe P7).

THIS BEAD DOES NOT OWN, AND MUST NOT DEFINE
- the campaign-rule schema;
- the ruling schema;
- persistence or storage of rules or rulings;
- rule/ruling recording, authoring, or management tools;
- active-rule resolution (the active-at-position query);
- supersession or revocation;
- house-rule lifecycle.

All seven belong to eshyra-jhpt. Campaign overlay lore (ADR 0014,
world/campaignOverlayLore.ts) is not a substitute: it models world canon with
truth/significance/visibility, not a selected rules interpretation tied to an
ambiguity. Discovery may not resolve an ambiguity, and a capability may not
consult a ruling that did not come through jhpt.

If the jhpt interface proves insufficient, the correct response is an amendment
or a new child under eshyra-jhpt, never a discovery-local store, table, cache of
record, or shadow resolver (design section 14.3).

NON-GOALS
No ranker, ontology, or relationship vocabulary; no universal
discovery-completeness claim; no corpus-wide capability claim; no finding
disposition.

DEPENDENCIES
eshyra-jhpt.3 for the campaign-rule path; eshyra-jhpt.6 additionally for the
ruling path (which itself rests on .1, .2, .4, .5). Interface-consumption design
may proceed in parallel; the integration may not.

PERMANENT EVIDENCE
Interface-consumption tests against the real jhpt active-at-position query
(not a discovery-local fake once jhpt has landed), covering: an active rule
placed beside its governing record; an active ruling placed beside its
ambiguity; the unresolved-ambiguity absence case; supersession and revocation
reflected in what discovery receives; and an assertion that no discovery-side
rule or ruling store exists.

REQUIRED NEXT STATE
The W8 stub seam is backed by the real jhpt runtime; W10 can populate the
packet's campaign-rule and ruling fields; probe P7's ruling case and probe P10's
house-rule case run against real jhpt data.

MATERIAL CHANGE: no. It consumes an already-owned runtime across an existing
ownership boundary and adds no new authority.
acceptance_criteria:
Discovery obtains active campaign rules and active ambiguity rulings only
through the eshyra-jhpt runtime, using the same active-at-position query the
auditor uses; no discovery-side campaign-rule schema, ruling schema, persistence
table, recording tool, active-rule resolver, supersession or revocation
mechanism, or house-rule lifecycle exists anywhere in the discovery path, and a
test asserts their absence. Rule and ruling identity, kind, campaign scope,
provenance, effective position, and supersession status survive unchanged into
the packet. An active rule or ruling is placed beside its governing pack record
or ambiguity using association data supplied by jhpt (amendment A1), not
re-derived by discovery. Where execution depends on a ruling, the ruling reaches
bounded capability preflight only through the jhpt path (amendment A2), and a

title: Document self-overwriting dispatch heartbeat in supervisor workflow
description:
Detached Codex dispatches are invisible to the Claude Code UI because setsid removes them from the harness process tree, so the only liveness signal is whatever the supervisor's own monitor prints. The monitor pane is a FIXED 4-line, non-scrollable, head-truncated view of the task's captured stdout, which makes append-only heartbeats useless: every tick pushes current state further out of view.

Discovered 2026-07-26 while supervising PRs #475/#476/#477. Two wrong fixes were tried first — lengthening the tick interval, then removing periodic output entirely (which deleted the signal while claiming to improve it). The user identified the correct fix: head-insert or complete overwrite.

Overwrite is achievable: a background task can locate its own captured-output file by printing a unique marker and grepping the tasks directory for it, then truncate-and-rewrite that file each tick. Verified working. The rule is that the process must write nothing further to stdout afterwards, or the harness appends it below the rewritten content.

Document this in .claude/hooks/codex-subagent-workflow.md so future supervisor sessions do not rediscover it.

title: Normalize tables, taxonomy, identifiers, and structured source labels
design:

R1 MADNESS DURATIONS (opus:F-16): table:short-term-madness / long-term-madness / indefinite-madness carry only d100+effect columns; the durations are printed in rule:madness-effects ('subjected to an effect from the Short-Term Madness table for 1d10 minutes', long-term '1d10 x 10 hours', indefinite 'lasts until cured'). Project a duration field on each table record from that source sentence (verbatim-derived values, e.g. {dice:'1d10', unit:'minute'} / {dice:'1d10', multiplier:10, unit:'hour'} / {kind:'until-cured'}), with provenance to the rule record; validate in kindSchemas. Check consumers of these tables first.
R2 TACK/HARNESS/DRAWN VEHICLES + BARDING (sol:CAP-013): equipment records for saddles, saddlebags, carriage, cart, chariot, sled, wagon (and barding/feed/stabling if present) are category 'gear' with no grouping, though the SRD prints them in the 'Tack, Harness, and Drawn Vehicles' table. Project the printed group (e.g. subcategory 'tack-harness-drawn-vehicles') for exactly the rows of that source table (population from the table itself, not a hand list), and project the Barding rule ('Barding is armor designed to protect an animal's head, neck, chest, and body. Any type of armor shown on the Armor table can be purchased as barding. The cost is four times the equivalent armor made for humanoids, and it weighs twice as much.') as a typed transformation on the barding row/record ({costMultiplier:4, weightMultiplier:2, appliesTo:'armor-table'}). Check consumers (equipment catalog, creation equipment) first; stop if a deterministic consumer changes behavior.
R3 EMPTY CELLS (fable:F6): 484 cells are '' and 88 are an em dash. Determine against the vendored PDF whether each form matches the printed cell (blank vs em dash). If they faithfully reflect two different printed forms, disposition accepted with that evidence (no consumer is harmed by the distinction); if any '' is a lost printed dash (or vice versa), repair at the extractor and add an invariant.
R4 F-10 advancement-qualifiers ('Advancement scaling qualifiers are preserved'): identify the printed scaling qualifiers the row concerns (class/feature progression text such as 'at 5th level (2d6)', 'when you reach N level', cantrip damage scaling) by inspecting progression/scaling projections and the registry provenance; repair any qualifier lost in a projection, or disposition with evidence.
R5 DISPOSITIONS: F-34 damage-field-shape ({dice} vs flat {amount}) - both shapes validated (kindSchemas validateDamageEntry) and represent two printed forms; disposition accepted/narrowed unless a consumer is harmed. EVIDENCE: one new test file with exact source-backed assertions for R1/R2 and generalized checks where a population exists (R2 membership equals the source table's rows; R3 if repaired). Registry rows updated with reasoning. No per-record test proliferation.

title: Dispatch: end-to-end useItem regression coverage for timer re-entry (attempt 2)
description:

correctly (schema marker, timer preservation, engine wiring, curation, pack
regeneration) but did not add the end-to-end coverage its plan called for.
Supervisor diff review found two gaps. This bead closes them. No production code
should change.

curation table.

`eshyra-jw56` (which already carries the eshyra-iohn fix). Work only there.

## Gap 1 — `packages/core/test/itemState.test.ts` has no coverage at all

The bead's actual reported defect goes through `useItem`, and nothing exercises
it. Acceptance criterion 1 of eshyra-jw56 ("repeated `spell-contact-loss` cannot
extend the Cube of Force barrier") is currently unproven end to end: the engine
wiring at `packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts` ~1852
(`selectedTransition.nextState === state?.machineState && !resetsDuration`) is
only covered indirectly by unit tests of `resolveItemStateTimers`.

Add a test to `packages/core/test/itemState.test.ts` using the existing fixture
idiom in that file — see the "initializes and plays Flame Tongue toggle state"
test (~line 121) for `item()`, `giveItem`, `createInitialItemState`,
`writeItemState`, `useItem`, `useInput`, `pack()` and the
`db.prepare('UPDATE clock SET elapsed_minutes=? WHERE id=1').run()` idiom.

Build one fixture machine that mirrors the Cube of Force shape and assert all
three arms in the same test (or three focused tests):

1. enter a timed state at minute 0 -> `pendingTimers` deadline is anchored;
2. advance the clock, then fire a self-transition **without** `resetsDuration`
   -> `deadlineElapsedMinutes` and `anchorElapsedMinutes` are unchanged (this is
   the regression: it used to move);
3. advance the clock, then fire a self-transition **with**
   `resetsDuration: true` -> re-anchored to the current clock;
4. a cross-state transition into a different timed state -> fresh anchor.

Assert on the persisted state too (`readItemState`), not only the `useItem`
return value.

## Gap 2 — `packages/core/test/itemTimers.test.ts` non-matching preserved entry

The reworked test "preserves matching timers and leaves unrelated declarations
fresh" only covers the matching case (its `unmatched` variable is in fact a
match on `from`+`to`). Add the genuinely unmatched case: pass a `preserved`
array whose entries do **not** match the declaration's `to`, and assert the
declaration resolves fresh against the clock. Consider renaming the misleading
`unmatched` binding.

  your completion notes instead of changing it.

title: Dispatch: preserve item state timers on non-restating re-entry (attempt 1)
description:
Implementation dispatch for eshyra-jw56. Read `bd show eshyra-jw56` first — its
notes carry the design decision, the source-backed curation table, and the
acceptance criteria. This bead carries the pre-planning survey.

Worktree: `.worktrees/<this-bead-id>`, branch `<this-bead-id>`, cut from branch
`eshyra-jw56`. Work only inside that worktree.

## Code survey (already done — trust it, but verify before editing)

- `packages/core/src/state/itemTimers.ts` (128 lines): `resolveItemStateTimers`
  (anchors declarations to the campaign clock, rolls dice-defined durations) and
  `reconcileItemStateTimers(transitionTo, resolved)` (drops timers not owned by
  the entered state; the doc comment there states the current wrong assumption
  "re-entering a state replaces its prior deadline" — update it).
  Not exported from `src/index.ts` or `src/internal.ts`, so its signature is
  free to change. Callers: `itemState.ts:1848`, `itemResetExecutor.ts:839`.
- `packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts`:
  - `selectStateTransition` (~1285-1420) picks the transition and, at ~1392,
    collects the entered state's timer declarations into
    `result.pendingTimers`.
  - ~1837-1859 resolves them; ~2061 calls `reconcileItemStateTimers` and writes
    `pendingTimers` into the persisted state.
  - `state?.machineState` and `state?.pendingTimers` are both in scope at 1846.
  - `validateItemStateForRecord` (~461-519) validates persisted timer shape —
    unchanged by this work; preserved timers already satisfy the
    `deadline === anchor + amount * multiplier` invariant.
- `packages/core/src/rules/magicItemMechanics.ts`: `MagicItemStateMachine`
  transition type at ~96-110; validation at ~864-914 with the
  `only(transition, ['from','to','via','timer','condition','effects','onFailure','note'])`
  allowlist and the "exactly one of via, timer, or condition" rule.
- Generated pack scan found exactly three machines with a `via` self-transition
  on a timer-bearing state: records.json indices 813 (Bead of Force),
  841 (Cube of Force), 959 (Ring of Shooting Stars) — 12 transitions total.
  All three are curated in
  `packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/magicItemComplexStateMachines.ts`
  (Bead of Force ~line 108-140, Cube of Force ~line 261-306, Ring of Shooting
  Stars ~line 588-615).

## Plan

1. **Schema** (`magicItemMechanics.ts`): add `readonly resetsDuration?: true` to
   the transition type; add `'resetsDuration'` to the `only()` allowlist;
   validate that the value is exactly boolean `true` and that the transition has
   `from === to` — a `RulesPackError` otherwise, with the path in the message.
   Consider also rejecting the marker when the entered state declares no timer
   (no transition with `from === <state>` and a `timer`), which catches dead
   markers; do it if it stays simple.
2. **Timers** (`itemTimers.ts`): let `resolveItemStateTimers` reuse already-
   pending timers. Preferred shape — replace the trailing positional
   `anchorElapsedMinutes` with an options bag
   `{ anchorElapsedMinutes?: number; preserved?: readonly ItemStateTimer[] }`
   and update the `itemResetExecutor.ts:839` call plus `itemTimers.test.ts`.
   For each declaration, if `preserved` holds an entry with matching `from` and
   `to`, return it verbatim (no clock read, **no dice roll** — a dice-defined
   timer must not be re-rolled); otherwise resolve fresh. Map over declarations
   so output order stays declaration order. Fix the stale doc comment on
   `reconcileItemStateTimers`.
3. **Engine** (`itemState.ts`): surface `resetsDuration` on
   `SelectedStateTransition` from `selectStateTransition`; at the resolve site
   pass `preserved: state?.pendingTimers ?? []` when
   `selectedTransition.nextState === state?.machineState && !resetsDuration`,
   and `[]` otherwise. Do not change `reconcileItemStateTimers`'s ownership
   check — preserved timers already carry `from === nextState`.
4. **Curation** (`magicItemComplexStateMachines.ts`): add
   `resetsDuration: true` to the five Cube of Force `press-face-N` transitions
   whose `from === to`, with a short source note in the existing comment style.
   Leave `spell-contact-loss`, `move-force-sphere`, and `move-ball-lightning`
   unmarked. Do not hand-edit `records.json`.
5. **Regenerate**: `npm run import:dnd5e-srd -- --out packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1`
   (confirm the flag against `packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/cli.ts`
   before running), then `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack`. The generated diff must
   be confined to the Cube of Force machine (5 transitions gain the key). Any
   other churn: stop and report in your completion notes.
6. **Tests**:
   - `packages/core/test/itemTimers.test.ts` — preserved timers keep anchor,
     deadline and `roll`; unmatched declarations still resolve fresh; assert no
     RNG consumption for preserved dice timers (an `Rng` whose `nextInt` throws).
     The existing "replaces all stale timers when a state is entered or left"
     test encodes the old assumption; update it deliberately and say in your
     notes whether the regression contract is preserved or replaced.
   - `packages/core/test/itemState.test.ts` — end-to-end on a fixture pack:
     enter a timed state at t=0, advance the clock, self-transition without the
     marker → deadline unchanged; with the marker → re-anchored; cross-state
     transition → fresh anchor.
   - `packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/magicItemComplexStateMachines.test.ts`
     — assert the four curation rulings from the parent bead's table.
   - a schema test for the new validation rules (see
     `magicItemMechanics`-related tests under `packages/core/test/`).
   - `packages/core/test/srdGeneratedPack.test.ts` may hold baselines that need
     updating — check.
7. **Docs**: `docs/item-reset-executor.md` §"Timers and fail-closed behavior"
   describes the cancel/replace semantics; add the re-entry rule and the
   `resetsDuration` marker there.

## Constraints

- `docs/importer-fix-protocol.md` governs steps 4-6: no hand-edited generated
  records, no weakened audit expectations, and your completion note must report
  affected record IDs, the generated diff, and why each change is expected.
- Do NOT touch `docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/freeze-manifest.json`. Its
  records.json hash already mismatches on `main` (thawed re-audit; re-freeze is
  tracked by eshyra-o9bd.14).
- `npm run verify:worktree` **before** committing (it rewrites files). Commit on
  your branch. Do not push, do not open a PR, do not merge — integration is the
  dispatching agent's job. Never modify eshyra-jw56.

## Environment

title: Item state timers re-anchor on transitions that do not restate the duration
description:
Every operation transition re-resolves the entered state's timer declarations, and reconcileItemStateTimers replaces the prior deadline (packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts selectStateTransition + line ~2061). A self-transition that the source does not describe as restating the duration therefore extends it.

Confirmed for Cube of Force (eshyra-0p7c): press-face-1 at minute 0 anchors the barrier timer at deadline 1; firing 'spell-contact-loss' (a free reaction to a listed spell contacting the barrier, from face-N to face-N) at minute 1 re-anchors it to deadline 2. SRD 5.1 resets the duration only when 'pressing a different face of the cube and expending the requisite number of charges'; a spell contact only deducts charges. Repeated contacts can extend the barrier indefinitely.

Same class, pre-existing: Ring of Shooting Stars declares 'active' -> 'active' via move-ball-lightning (bonus action) alongside a 1-minute timer, so moving a sphere extends the one-minute window.

Expected: a transition should be able to enter/re-enter a state without re-anchoring that state's pending timers, defaulting to preserving the existing deadline unless the source restates the duration. Likely needs a schema-level marker on the transition (or on the timer) plus itemState/itemTimers support, and source-backed curation of which existing transitions reset.

Files: packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts, packages/core/src/state/itemTimers.ts, packages/core/src/rules/magicItemMechanics.ts, packages/core/scripts/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/magicItemComplexStateMachines.ts. Tests: packages/core/test/itemState.test.ts, packages/core/test/itemTimers.test.ts.
notes:
## Supervisor design decision (2026-07-21)

Chosen model: **state-scoped timers are preserved on re-entry by default; a
transition opts in to restating the duration.**

- Timers are already state-scoped (`reconcileItemStateTimers` drops timers whose
  `from` !== entered state), so a cross-state transition necessarily anchors
  fresh and is already correct. The defect is confined to transitions whose
  destination equals the current `machineState`.
- Rule: when `selectedTransition.nextState === state.machineState`, each declared
  timer of that state that is already pending (same `from` + `to`) keeps its
  existing `anchorElapsedMinutes` / `deadlineElapsedMinutes` / `roll`, unless the
  transition declares `resetsDuration: true`.
- New schema key `resetsDuration?: true` on `stateMachine.transitions[]`, legal
  only when `from === to`. `false` is rejected (it is the default; no dead
  declarations).
- Dice-defined timers must NOT be re-rolled when preserved (no RNG consumption).

### Source-backed curation (SRD 5.1, all three affected machines)

| item | self-transition | ruling |
|---|---|---|
| Cube of Force | `face-N --press-face-N--> face-N` | **resetsDuration: true** — "press one of the cube's faces... a barrier of invisible force springs into existence... and lasts for 1 minute" applies to any face press |
| Cube of Force | `face-N --spell-contact-loss--> face-N` | preserve — source only says "The cube loses charges when the barrier is targeted by certain spells"; no duration language |
| Bead of Force | `sphere --move-force-sphere--> sphere` | preserve — "encloses the area for 1 minute"; pushing the wall only moves the sphere |
| Ring of Shooting Stars | `active --move-ball-lightning--> active` | preserve — "last as long as you concentrate... up to 1 minute"; moving is a bonus action |

Cross-face presses (`face-N -> face-M`, M != N) keep re-anchoring, which is the
source behaviour ("pressing a different face... resetting the duration").

### Acceptance criteria

1. Repeated `spell-contact-loss` cannot extend the Cube of Force barrier.
2. Bead of Force / Ring of Shooting Stars self-transitions preserve the deadline.
3. `press-face-N` from `face-N` still re-anchors, via the explicit marker.
4. Schema rejects `resetsDuration` on a non-self transition and rejects `false`.
5. Generated pack regenerated through the importer; diff limited to the three
   machines; `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack` clean.
6. `npm run verify:worktree` clean.

### Out of scope (decided)

- `itemResetExecutor.applyDueTimer` is timer-fired only and re-anchors the
  entered state's timers deliberately (it also guards against non-advancing
  timers); no change.
- No new field on `UseItemResult['transition']` — the persisted
  `state.pendingTimers` deadline is already the observable.
- `docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/freeze-manifest.json` records.json hash
  already mismatches on `main` (thawed re-audit, re-freeze is eshyra-o9bd.14).
  Do not "fix" the manifest here.

title: staff-of-striking powerful-strike operation lacks typed per-charge damage representation
description:
Discovered during eshyra-jjti (exact-token dice conservation gate, PR #455 follow-ups): the family-match tolerance was hiding a representation question on `magic-item:staff-of-striking`.

The prose clause "For each charge you expend, the target takes an extra 1d6 force damage" is C2-owned per the reviewed master inventory (docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/2026-07-06-o9bd-18-7-7-3-magic-item-mechanics-inventory.md line ~299: "+1d6 force per charge (<=3): C2"), but the emitted record's mechanics carry no dice token for it: the `powerful-strike` operation has only `cost: [{economy: charges, amount: 'variable'}]` and the sole effect is the +3 attack/damage bonus. The daily recharge `1d6+4` conserves exactly and is unrelated.

Adjudicate under docs/importer-fix-protocol.md: either the operation should gain a typed per-charge damage representation (importer/curated-spec fix + pack regeneration), or source-backed evidence should document why a variable-cost operation without a damage formula is the reviewed representation. When resolved, remove the scoped exception `magic-item:staff-of-striking|forward|1d6` in packages/core/test/srdGeneratedPack.test.ts (the exhaustive used-exception assertion will fail if it goes stale, which is intended).

Note memory context: the o9bd 2026-07-01 reaudit found residual pack defects — re-verify the committed pack state before implementing.
notes:
## Supervisor adjudication (2026-07-21)

**Ruling: the operation gains a typed per-charge damage representation.** The
"no typed damage" state is a curation gap, not a reviewed representation.

Evidence. SRD 5.1 staff-of-striking: "When you hit with a melee attack using
it, you can expend up to 3 of its charges. For each charge you expend, the
target takes an extra 1d6 force damage." The master inventory
(2026-07-06-o9bd-18-7-7-3, line 299) classifies this "+1d6 force per charge
(<=3)" as C2 — mechanics-owned. Nothing in the reviewed record justifies
omitting it, and the near-identical sibling is already represented.

**Sibling precedent — Staff of Withering** ("expend 1 charge ... extra 2d10
necrotic damage on a hit"): `withering-strike` operation +
`c2-withering-strike-payload`, a `triggeredEffect` carrying nested
`extraDamage: { dice, type }`, `activation: { cost: 'free', trigger: 'hit with
staff' }`. Staff of Striking is the same shape with a variable cost, so it takes
the same representation. **Ring of Shooting Stars** is the precedent for the
variable-cost side: `cost: [{economy:'charges', amount:'variable'}]` plus
`activation.requirement: 'expend 1 to 3 charges'` prose.

Target representation:

    payload(
      'powerful-strike',
      'triggeredEffect',
      {
        trigger: 'hit with a melee attack using the staff',
        extraDamage: {
          dice: '1d6',
          type: 'force',
          perChargeExpended: true,
          maximumCharges: 3,
        },
      },
      [F2, F6, F9],
      { cost: 'free', trigger: 'hit with a melee attack using the staff' },
    )

Hook bindings drop F8 deliberately: there is no save DC or spell attack here.
Precedent for dropping it on no-save payloads is magicItemActivatedEffects.ts
lines ~151 ([F2, F6, F9]) and ~435 ([F6, F9]).

### Acceptance criteria

1. `magic-item:staff-of-striking` mechanics carry a `1d6` force damage token
   bound to `powerful-strike`, with the <=3 charge cap represented.
2. The scoped exception `magic-item:staff-of-striking|forward|1d6` is removed
   from `packages/core/test/srdGeneratedPack.test.ts`; the exhaustive
   used-exception assertion still passes (it fails on a stale exception, which
   is the intended self-enforcement).
3. Pack regenerated through the importer; the generated diff touches only
   `magic-item:staff-of-striking`; `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack` clean.
4. `npm run verify:worktree` clean.

### Out of scope (decided)

- **No typed maximum for variable operation costs.** Encoding "<=3 charges" as a
  schema-validated cost cap would touch every variable-cost item and the
  `costAmount` path in `packages/core/src/state/itemState.ts`. The reviewed
  precedent (Ring of Shooting Stars) keeps the cap as activation prose; here it
  is additionally carried as `maximumCharges` inside the damage payload. If a
  typed cost cap is wanted, that is its own bead.
- **No new nested-payload schema validation.** `triggeredEffect` validates only
  `trigger`/`result`/`condition`; nested payload keys are free-form across all
  existing magic items. Tightening that is a separate decision.
- Pack state re-verified before dispatch: `verify:dnd5e-srd-pack` reports the
  committed pack matches importer output exactly (0 records changed).
PR #469 open: https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/469 (branch eshyra-u5wn at 29ffa5e). All four acceptance criteria met; scoped dice-conservation exception removed. Child eshyra-kdr5 closed. Leave this bead in_progress until the PR merges.

title: Dispatch: exact-token dice conservation gate (attempt 1)
description:
Works defect bead eshyra-2n3n (read it first: full analysis with file/line refs and measured blast radius). Parent spec: eshyra-f0nz (acceptance criterion 3). This touches an SRD gate test: read `docs/importer-fix-protocol.md` BEFORE changing anything and follow it.

Branch/worktree: this bead's id, cut from eshyra-f0nz.

## Code survey (verified 2026-07-19)

- `packages/core/test/srdGeneratedPack.test.ts`: `diceFamily` (line ~956) strips `[+-].*`; the forward gate (~1094-1104) and reverse gate (~1112-1121) accept family-only matches; `mechanicsTokens` pools parent + all variant mechanics into one item-wide set. Whole-record accept lists: `FORWARD_NUMERIC_CONSERVATION_ACCEPTS` / `REVERSE_NUMERIC_CONSERVATION_ACCEPTS` (~1064-1080).
- Measured against the committed pack (2026-07-19): exact-token matching leaves exactly 3 family-only survivors — `magic-item:robe-of-useful-items` forward `4d4` vs mechanics `4d4+12` AND reverse `4d4+12` vs prose `4d4`; `magic-item:staff-of-striking` forward `1d6` vs mechanics `1d6+4`.

## Required behavior change

1. Remove the `diceFamily` tolerance: conservation requires exact normalized dice tokens in both directions.
2. Add a token-scoped exception mechanism: exceptions keyed by record key + direction + exact token, each carrying a non-empty rationale string, asserted exhaustively at the bottom of the test the same way the whole-record accept lists are (so a stale exception fails the gate). Keep the existing whole-record accepts for their current documented cases.
3. Adjudicate the 3 survivors against the SRD source text (the pack's description fields carry it; the audit inventory under docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/ has the reviewed mechanics decisions):
   - Robe of Useful Items: SRD gives the robe two of each of six fixed patches (=12) plus 4d4 additional patches; if mechanics' `4d4+12` is that reviewed synthesized total, record BOTH directions as scoped exceptions with that rationale.
   - Staff of Striking: find where `1d6+4` comes from in the record's mechanics and check it against the SRD clause. If it is a correct reviewed representation, scoped exception with rationale; if it is an importer artifact, DO NOT add an exception — fix per docs/importer-fix-protocol.md (importer/curated-spec side), and if that is out of scope for this dispatch, file a follow-up bead with `bd create` and leave the gate red is NOT acceptable — in that case stop and report in your completion notes instead of committing a weakened gate.
4. Add a tamper test in the same style as the existing negative tests: a synthetic record whose mechanics drop a prose modifier (e.g. prose `1d6+5`, mechanics `1d6`) must produce a finding under the new exact matching (this is the regression the old family match hid).
5. Do NOT regenerate the pack; this dispatch changes only the gate test (and exceptions). Per-variant/per-clause scoping of token pooling: capture as a follow-up bead if you confirm it matters; do not implement here.

## Verification

title: Rest completion omits stableRecoveries from benefits payload and persisted evidence
description:
Post-merge review of PR #457 (verified against current main, 2026-07-19).

## Defect

Rest completion hides automatic stable recoveries from its evidence. In `complete()` (`packages/core/src/state/rest.ts:588-611`), `advanceWorldTime` returns `time.stableRecoveries`, but the constructed `benefits` object copies `expiredEffects`, `previousElapsedMinutes`, `elapsedMinutes`, `inGameTime`, `narrativeLabelStale`, and `closedRecoveryWindows` from `time` while omitting `stableRecoveries`. That object is both the tool response and the persisted `benefits_json` (rest.ts:684-688).

Gameplay consequence: a short rest can wake a stable character (recovery deadline falls inside the rest's elapsed window → `adjustHp(+1)` → conscious at 1 HP) while the model and the turn auditor receive no evidence of the HP/life-state transition. Their pre-tool context still says the character is stable at 0 HP — a direct narration/audit blind spot, and the persisted rest record is incomplete for later history traversal.

## Required fix (per review)

Add `stableRecoveries: time.stableRecoveries` to the benefits payload; test both the returned tool value and the persisted `benefits_json` for a rest whose window crosses a stable-recovery deadline.

Coordinate with the advanceWorldTime atomicity bead (same review) — moving recovery resolution inside the clock transaction changes where `stableRecoveries` comes from, so these two are best fixed in one PR.

Related (same PR #457 review): Demon Armor permanent doff block, migration-0020 stranded stable characters, advanceWorldTime recovery atomicity.

Sibling beads from PR #457 post-merge review: eshyra-gacz (Demon Armor doff), eshyra-q93i (migration-0020 stranding), eshyra-r2ps (clock/recovery atomicity — fix together with this one, shared advanceWorldTime result shape).

title: Numeric-conservation gate: require exact dice tokens (family-match hides modifier drift)
description:
Post-merge review of PR #455 (verified against current main, 2026-07-19). Guard-quality hardening — no known wrong record in the committed pack.

## Weakness

The magic-item numeric-conservation gate (`packages/core/test/srdGeneratedPack.test.ts`, "magic-item numeric conservation gate") treats dice tokens as equivalent whenever their base family matches: `diceFamily` (line ~956) strips everything from the first `+`/`-`, so `1d6+5 ≈ 1d6` and `2d10-3 ≈ 2d10` in both the forward (prose→mechanics) and reverse (mechanics→prose) directions (lines ~1094-1121). A future importer regression that silently drops or invents a flat modifier stays green.

Additionally, tokens are pooled item-wide: `mechanicsTokens` merges the parent record's mechanics with every variant's mechanics into one set, so one sibling variant or unrelated effect can satisfy another occurrence's token.

## Measured blast radius (2026-07-19, committed pack)

Re-running the gate with exact-token matching produces exactly 3 family-only survivors:

- `magic-item:robe-of-useful-items` — prose `4d4` vs mechanics `4d4+12` (both directions)
- `magic-item:staff-of-striking` — prose `1d6` vs mechanics `1d6+4` (forward)

So exact-by-default is cheap: only these two records need adjudication.

## Fix direction (per review recommendation)

- Require exact normalized dice tokens by default in both directions.
- Represent intentional equivalences as narrow record+token exceptions with a rationale (mirroring the existing `FORWARD/REVERSE_NUMERIC_CONSERVATION_ACCEPTS` pattern, but scoped to the specific token, not the whole record), ideally scoped to the exact clause/variant.
- Adjudicate the two current records first: verify against the SRD source whether the `+12`/`+4` mechanics representations are correct synthesized totals (then add scoped exceptions with source-backed rationale) or importer artifacts (then fix per docs/importer-fix-protocol.md — do not weaken the expectation to match output).
- Consider scoping token pooling per-variant/per-clause so a sibling cannot satisfy another occurrence; if that is a larger change, capture what exact-token matching alone still misses.

Importer-fix-protocol applies (touches SRD audit/gate test files).

Related: sold-item `returned` payment bypass and migration-0018 oversized-stack unresolvable edge, filed from the same review.
notes:

title: Migration-0018 oversized-stack reviews with quantity <=100 are permanently unresolvable
description:
Post-merge review of PR #455 (verified against current main, 2026-07-19).

## Defect

A migrated `oversized-stack` adoption review whose row quantity is ≤ 100 is permanently unresolvable: the quarantine (which blocks item usage, resets, context projection, custody, and attunement) can never be lifted by any accepted resolution.

Code facts (all verified):

- Migration `packages/core/data/migrations/0018_inventory_adoption_review.sql` classifies migrated markers as `review_kind='oversized-stack'` purely by matching the legacy reason string (`LIKE 'stateful legacy stack quantity % exceeds the reviewed adoption maximum of % singleton instances'`). It never checks the row's *current* `inventory.quantity`.
- The kind→action mapping is exclusive: `oversized-stack` accepts only `set-reviewed-quantity` (`itemAdoptionReview.ts:48-49`, and the SQL CHECK on `inventory_adoption_resolution` enforces the same pairing at the schema level).
- The resolver rejects `set-reviewed-quantity` when `row.quantity <= MAX_MAGIC_ITEM_ADOPTION_SINGLETONS` (=100): `itemAdoption.ts:347-349` — "set-reviewed-quantity applies only to a quarantined stack above 100".

So any pre-migration marker carrying that reason string on a row whose quantity is now ≤ 100 (the legacy markers were model-writable advisory JSON, so the reason and the actual quantity were never atomically coupled; quantity could also have been legitimately corrected after the marker was written) becomes a permanent quarantine with no GM escape hatch.

## Fix direction (per review recommendation)

Migration checksums are immutable — do not edit 0018. Instead either:

1. New migration that reclassifies `oversized-stack` reviews whose row quantity is ≤ 100 as `malformed-evidence` (whose `discard-evidence` resolution works and preserves the raw evidence in `discarded_structure_json`); or
2. A resolver compatibility rule permitting an evidence-backed no-reduction resolution for this case — but note the `inventory_adoption_resolution` CHECK constrains kind→action pairs at the schema level, so option 1 (reclassification) is the cleaner path; option 2 would itself need a migration to widen the CHECK.

Add a regression test constructing the impossible state (oversized-stack review + quantity ≤ 100) and asserting it is resolvable after the fix.

Related: sold-item `returned` payment bypass and the numeric-conservation dice-modifier gate, filed from the same review.

title: Enforce byte bounds for inventory identity in model context
description: Sol review of PR #455 confirmed nearby properties/state payloads are removed, but inventory id/name strings remain unbounded in storage and tool writes. Twenty adversarially large identities can still exceed bounded-context or tool-output budgets, while truncating exact ids would make claim_item unusable. Establish write/storage limits and migration/repair behavior, then enforce a deterministic serialized byte budget without losing exact actionable identity.
design: Preserve exact IDs or fail closed with actionable repair evidence. Do not truncate an ID that a mutation tool must consume. Treat this as a general inventory boundary, not a nearby-list-only patch.
acceptance_criteria: New writes have reviewed id/name limits; legacy oversized rows are surfaced through controlled repair behavior; nearby context and pagination have a deterministic byte bound; exact claimable ids are never silently truncated; tests cover multibyte strings and over-budget pages.

Completion report (2026-07-19): Implemented migration 0019_inventory_identity_bounds with 256-byte UTF-8 id/name write guards, legacy inventory_identity_repair evidence, repair-safe shortening via ON UPDATE CASCADE, and schema snapshot regeneration. title: Add authoritative inventory wear/doff state owner
description: PR #455 review had to fail closed for every held blocksDoff item because inventory.location is free-form storage prose and cannot prove whether an item is donned. Add a closed, semantic wear-state owner and model-facing don/doff transition that preserves source curse onset/persistence, then narrow the conservative custody gate without allowing synonyms or raw state writes to bypass it.
design: Do not infer wear from arbitrary inventory.location. Keep held storage, world placement, wear state, attunement, and character curse state separate. Curse attachment must outlive item placement where the source requires it.
acceptance_criteria: Wear state is first-class and migration-safe; don/doff is a semantic atomic mutation; blocksDoff and don-triggered curse onset are source-faithful; ambiguous legacy placement fails closed; ordinary held-but-not-worn items remain transferable; full lifecycle and importer/runtime tests pass.
notes:
Dispatch plan (attempt 1, 2026-07-19, supervisor eshyra-fe3t): Codex gpt-5.6-luna in .worktrees/eshyra-mq4n branch eshyra-mq4n off eshyra-fe3t (includes stbg, dunv migration 0019, 2n1t.8.1 migration 0020). Your schema change must be migration 0021; update migrationLegacyAdoption ledger/applied pins and regenerate schema.snapshot.sql (npx tsx packages/core/scripts/generate-schema-snapshot.ts). Keep wear state separate from held storage (inventory.location free text), world placement (world_location_id), attunement, and character curse state; blocksDoff gating currently fails closed for every held item — narrow it to don/doff semantics without synonym inference. Sources of truth for curse onset/persistence: the magic-item records' curse/attunement fields (Demon Armor, Berserker Axe, Armor of Vulnerability, Shield of Missile Attraction, Robe of the Archmagi, Orb of Dragonkind).
Completion report (2026-07-19): Added migration 0021_inventory_wear_state and regenerated schema.snapshot.sql. Added authoritative inventoryWear donItem/doffItem/getInventoryWearState owner with exact model-facing don_item/doff_item tools; legacy rows without wear state fail closed for don/doff. New give/claim/reacquire/adoption rows initialize not_worn; relinquishment removes holder wear state; transfer moves state to recipient as not_worn. Narrowed blocksDoff custody gating to explicitly worn items, preserving held-not-worn transfer/removal semantics. Don attaches source-defined don-onset curse state to character conditions so it survives doff/placement. Tests added/updated for lifecycle, migration, registry, and conservative custody behavior. Verification: npm run build passed; focused suites passed (138 tests); full npm test had 4620 passed, with remaining failures caused by sandbox EPERM for child-process/loopback operations (git/node/npm spawn and 127.0.0.1 listen). npm run verify:worktree reached format then failed at check:hidden-unicode for the same sandbox spawnSync git EPERM. No follow-up product issues discovered.
Supervisor review round 1 (2026-07-19) — two blocking findings; fix in the same worktree (attempt 2), tree is uncommitted:
F1 (major, fail-open): assertInventoryCurseCustodyReady now treats a MISSING inventory_wear_state row as not-worn, so an unreviewed legacy held blocksDoff item (e.g. pre-migration Demon Armor, worn in fiction) can be dropped/sold/transferred where the previous code failed closed. Required: for a held item whose record declares curse.blocksDoff, a missing wear row is AMBIGUOUS and must fail closed (same message family as before), while an authoritative not_worn row permits custody. Missing-row ambiguity is resolved only by the adoption/repair boundary that seeds authoritative rows.
F2 (major, crash): removeItem partial-quantity relinquish inserts an inventory_wear_state row for the NEW unheld relinquished row, bound to the FORMER holder — violating the 'wear row exists iff held' invariant — and claimItem/reacquireItem then do a plain INSERT into inventory_wear_state for that id, which hits the PRIMARY KEY and throws a raw SqliteError: any claim/reacquire of a partially-dropped/sold stack is permanently broken. Required: do not create wear rows for unheld rows (drop the partial-path INSERT); keep full-relinquish DELETE; make claim/reacquire seeding collision-safe (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(inventory_id) DO UPDATE SET character_id, wear_state='not_worn', ...) so surviving rows are rebound not fatal.
Also add regression tests: claim after partial drop; reacquire after partial sell; legacy blocksDoff held item with no wear row fails closed for dropped/sold/lost/transfer/doff; invariant sweep that every inventory_wear_state row joins to a held inventory row with matching character_id (assert in relevant lifecycle tests).
Completion report (attempt 2, 2026-07-19): Fixed supervisor F1 by making held blocksDoff custody fail closed when inventory_wear_state is missing or bound to a different holder; authoritative not_worn remains allowed. Fixed F2 by removing the partial-relinquishment wear-row insert and making claim/reacquire wear seeding collision-safe upserts that rebind to the new holder and reset to not_worn. Made transfer wear maintenance the same upsert so the invariant is preserved for legacy held rows too. Added regressions for missing-row dropped/sold/lost/doff/transfer custody, claim after partial drop, reacquire after partial sell, and invariant sweeps ensuring every wear row joins a held inventory row with matching character_id. Verification: focused requested suites passed (6 files, 174 tests): domainMutations.test.ts, inventoryWear.test.ts, itemTransfer.test.ts, itemAdoption.test.ts, tools.test.ts, migrationLegacyAdoption.test.ts. npm run typecheck passed; git diff --check passed. Bead intentionally left open for supervisor verification/merge.
Supervisor: attempt-2 F1/F2 fixes re-verified in code (fail-closed ambiguity gate; wear-row-iff-held invariant; upserts at claim/reacquire/transfer). Full verify:worktree green. Committed and merged into eshyra-fe3t.

title: Make rules-pack audit CLI tests deterministic under suite load
description: The full Vitest suite intermittently times out packages/core/test/rulesPackAuditCli.test.ts at the fixed 5s default because each test cold-starts the TypeScript CLI subprocess. Observed on 2026-07-14: the strict-audit case took 5.28-6.86s under 4-6 forks and timed out, while the entire file passed alone and the suite passed with one fork. Investigate and remove the load-sensitive cold-start behavior (for example, a testable in-process command boundary or reusable compiled entrypoint) rather than raising the global timeout or merely reducing CI parallelism. If a narrow per-test timeout remains necessary after root-cause work, document why. Also assess the same subprocess pattern in importer/audit CLI tests so the deterministic fix is shared where appropriate.
acceptance_criteria: Full default-parallel npm test runs repeatedly without rulesPackAuditCli timeout failures under representative load; solution does not raise Vitest's global timeout or weaken assertions; focused rulesPackAuditCli tests remain green; design/root-cause rationale is documented in the bead/PR.
notes:
Additional 2026-07-14 evidence during PR #451 review: even VITEST_MAX_FORKS=1 full verification timed out the unchanged human-report and --json cases at 5.66s and 5.72s, while prior isolated runs passed. This rules out Vitest fork contention as a complete solution and reinforces removing/reusing the tsx subprocess cold-start boundary.
Dispatch plan (attempt 1, 2026-07-19, supervisor eshyra-fe3t): Codex gpt-5.6-luna in .worktrees/eshyra-stbg branch eshyra-stbg off eshyra-fe3t (=main 9d252b9). Completion report (2026-07-19): Replaced repeated tsx subprocess execution in rulesPackAuditCli.test.ts with an exported in-process runCli(argv, io) boundary. The thin CLI entrypoint now adapts argv/process streams and preserves fail-closed exit codes: 0 success, 1 strict findings/changes, 2 load/validation failure. Tests retain human/JSON, strict audit/diff, invalid-pack, help, and root npm-script wiring assertions without changing global timeout or weakening expectations. title: Prove campaign rules and ambiguity resolution end to end
description:
Objective
Add end-to-end tests that prove campaign-rule behavior across persistence, model context, audit, ambiguity resolution, accepted-turn commits, and immediate disputed-turn replay.

Required scenarios
1. Create Undead explicit ambiguity question prompts without invented certainty and persists an approved interpretation.
2. Create Undead mixed ghast/wight action establishes visible mixed-within-total precedent only after DM/auditor acceptance.
3. Find Familiar permanent-dismissal-after-0-HP ambiguity prompts and remains unresolved when no choice is approved.
4. Explicit "no material components" house rule is durable prose.
5. Immediate material-components objection applies from disputed-turn start, restores pre-turn state, replays, and makes replay canonical.
6. Ordinary house-rule creation applies prospectively.
7. Supersession and revocation change active sets without mutating history.
8. DM and auditor receive equivalent active rule sets at every tested position.
9. Ordinary contextual adjudication (cover/visibility/terrain suitability) creates no campaign rule.
10. A clear canonical-rule violation never becomes an implicit house rule.

Architecture and references
Exercise the public/runtime path built by eshyra-jhpt.1-.8 and PR #419 RulesAmbiguity metadata from eshyra-o9bd.18.7.9. Assert immutable pack bytes remain unchanged and campaign prose remains in canonical campaign history.

Non-goals
No live-provider tests as the sole proof; no duplicated full ambiguity registry; no arbitrary retrospective history editing; no selective-retrieval optimization benchmark; no deterministic interpretation of arbitrary house-rule prose.
acceptance_criteria:
All ten scenarios pass through realistic campaign turn/context/audit/storage boundaries; tests prove exact DM/auditor rule-set parity, checkpoint/replay timing, accepted-vs-abandoned canon, pack immutability, and no rule creation for contextual judgments or clear canonical violations; full repository verification passes.

ADR 0020 TRANSITION AMENDMENT (integrated transition design section 8.3, A3 and
A4; accepted as the deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8, PR #485, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282). Three of the ten scenarios must be
provable end to end as an explicit triple, because they are the three cases the
transition's campaign-rule probes consume:

1. UNRESOLVED AMBIGUITY - a discovered RulesAmbiguity with no active ruling keeps
   its published uncertainty, surfaces the known interpretations, and never
   acquires silent canonical certainty (existing scenarios 1 and 3).
2. RESOLVED RULING - an approved interpretation becomes a durable prose ruling
   carrying ambiguity ID, interpretation ID, kind, status, provenance, effective
   position, and supersession status, and is supplied on subsequent turns
   (existing scenarios 1 and 2).
3. NON-AMBIGUITY HOUSE RULE - the "no material components" house rule, an
   intentional override of clear canonical behavior with no underlying source
   ambiguity, is durable prose that coexists with the source material it
   overrides rather than replacing or hiding it (existing scenarios 4 and 5).

Scenario 9 (ordinary contextual adjudication creates no campaign rule) is not
weakened by any of this and remains a required negative.

Additionally, the accepted-turn trace evidence required by amendment A3 on
eshyra-jhpt.4 - which active rules and rulings were supplied for the turn, and
under which identities - must be proven end to end here, from the persisted
trace, without a second campaign-rule store or a parallel audit database.

title: Replay an immediately disputed turn under a new campaign rule
description:
Objective
Handle a player objection to the current/immediately preceding adjudication by establishing an approved ruling or house rule effective from the start of that disputed turn, restoring pre-turn state, and replaying once under the new rule.

Required behavior
Recognize an explicit objection to the immediate adjudication, obtain player-approved prose/kind, persist canonical rule identity with effective position at disputed-turn start, restore the checkpoint/state immediately before that turn, replay the same player turn with the rule active in both DM and auditor contexts, and commit the accepted replay as campaign canon. Required canonical-conflict scenario: after a material-component rejection, "we don't use spell components" creates a house rule, rolls back the disputed turn, replays under it, and commits the replay. Abandoned adjudication may remain diagnostic/provenance history but not continuing campaign canon.

Architecture and references
Use eshyra-jhpt.1-.4 for domain/storage/context parity, audited-turn staging eshyra-67qo, turn rollback proof eshyra-c07.8, and checkpoint restore foundation eshyra-7wc.5. Preserve canonical campaign history and auditor evidence across the replay boundary.

Non-goals
No arbitrary historical retroactivity or replay of older turns; no automatic objection inference; no rule without player approval; no prose-to-mechanics compiler; no automatic house rule from an unaccepted canonical violation; no changes to immutable pack semantics.
acceptance_criteria: An immediate material-components objection creates approved house-rule prose effective at disputed-turn start, restores exact pre-turn state, replays once with identical DM/auditor active rules, and makes accepted replay canonical; ordinary new rules remain prospective; failed replay preserves a recoverable canonical pre-turn state; older-turn retroactivity is rejected; diagnostic history distinguishes abandoned and canonical attempts.
notes:
Implementation uses one durable latest-turn snapshot with a full-state hash, original input/seed/actor, transactionally restored pre-turn rows, approved disputed rule, and diagnostic original trace. Only the latest unreplayed accepted turn is eligible; subsequent state changes reject replay rather than erase them. Failed replay retains pending recovery and blocks new turns; CLI /dispute retry resumes the same approved action, and quit preserves the open session. No Dolt dependency on the per-turn path.

title: Persist accepted implicit ambiguity precedents
description:
Objective
Allow an accepted player action to establish a durable campaign ruling when it unambiguously selects a known interpretation of explicit rules-pack ambiguity metadata.

Required behavior
Only operate when the pack marks the mechanic ambiguous, no active linked ruling exists, the action clearly selects exactly one known interpretation, and the DM accepts the action. Persist player-approved/accepted-adjudication prose with ambiguity and interpretation provenance, and make the precedent visible in natural language. Required scenario: "Bob summons a ghast and a wight" may establish mixed-within-total for ambiguity:create-undead-ghast-wight-composition after acceptance. Couple persistence to audited-turn acceptance so rejected/retried candidates cannot leak a precedent.

Architecture and references
Build on explicit ambiguity resolution eshyra-jhpt.6, audited-turn mutation staging eshyra-67qo, mechanics auditor eshyra-oobh, and shared DM/auditor rule context. The model may interpret whether the action clearly selects an enumerated interpretation; deterministic code validates the ambiguity/interpretation IDs and commits only with accepted turn state.

Non-goals
Do not infer house rules from actions contrary to clear canonical rules. Do not create rules for ordinary fictional judgments. Do not infer when an action fits multiple/no known interpretations. Do not silently establish a precedent without visible acknowledgement. Do not alter the rules pack.
acceptance_criteria: Accepted mixed ghast/wight action establishes one visible durable mixed-within-total ruling; rejected/retried/ambiguous actions establish none; an existing ruling prevents duplicate precedent; canonical-rule violations never infer a house rule; persistence is atomic with audited turn acceptance; DM and auditor receive the new prose on subsequent turns.

title: Resolve known rules-pack ambiguities as campaign rulings
description:
Objective
Implement pre-adjudication resolution for unresolved RulesAmbiguity metadata when no campaign ruling exists.

Required behavior
Look up ambiguity metadata from the active rules stack by stable ID, check campaign storage for an active linked ruling, and when unresolved surface the published uncertainty instead of inventing certainty. Ask the player to choose among known interpretation IDs; persist the player-approved result as prose ruling with ambiguity/interpretation provenance; make it prospectively active and available to both model contexts. Required scenario: "Can I mix a ghast and a wight?" surfaces ambiguity:create-undead-ghast-wight-composition and can persist either homogeneous-alternative or mixed-within-total. Also cover ambiguity:find-familiar-permanent-dismissal-after-zero-hp.

Architecture and references
Consume PR #419 RulesAmbiguity output from eshyra-o9bd.18.7.9. Store only campaign prose/provenance via eshyra-jhpt.2; never write a winner/default back to the immutable pack. Use shared context from eshyra-jhpt.3-.4.

Non-goals
No model-selected canonical winner; no campaign ruling without player approval; no house-rule creation for clear canonical conflicts; no resolution of ordinary contextual judgments; no arbitrary prompt/retrieval optimization.
acceptance_criteria:
Create Undead explicit question and Find Familiar unresolved question both surface source uncertainty and known interpretations; an approved choice creates one durable prose ruling linked to ambiguity and interpretation IDs; an existing active ruling prevents re-prompting; declined/no choice creates nothing; DM/auditor receive the same resulting prose; pack data remains unchanged.

ADR 0020 TRANSITION AMENDMENT A2 (integrated transition design section 8.3, R5;
accepted as the deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8, PR #485, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282): define how an active ambiguity ruling
is made available to bounded deterministic capability preflight where execution
depends on it, not only to DM and auditor context. Today no path exists from a
campaign ruling to capability code.

The verified concrete case: magic-item:cube-of-force operation press-face-1 from
state face-1 hits transition resetsDuration { kind: 'source-ambiguity',
ambiguityId: 'ambiguity:cube-of-force-same-face-duration-reset' }, and
state/itemState.ts matchStateTransition throws ItemStateAmbiguityError carrying
the ambiguity and interpretation IDs. A ruling selecting same-face-resets or
different-face-only-resets is exactly what would unblock it. Verified ordering
constraint: assertMagicItemOperationReady runs at itemState.ts:1888, BEFORE the
first matchStateTransition call at :1934, and every press-face-* operation clause
on that record is engine-pending, so readiness throws first and the ambiguity
error is currently unreachable through use_item. A2 must therefore be designed
WITH the eshyra-olc5 readiness owner (see eshyra-olc5.6, transition W13), not
against it: a ruling does not make an engine-pending clause ready, and a
capability may never consult a ruling that did not come through this runtime.

This may be satisfied as an acceptance criterion here or as a new child under
eshyra-jhpt; either way the ownership stays here. The discovery-side consumer
eshyra-o9bd.19.13 (transition W11) depends on this output and may not substitute
a discovery-local ruling store or resolver. Probe P7 of the transition design
expects both outcomes: with no active ruling the packet carries the ambiguity,
both interpretations, and an explicit unresolved state; with an active ruling the
packet carries the ruling beside the ambiguity and the capability preflight still
reports blocked.

title: Add explicit campaign-rule management workflow
description:
Objective
Provide explicit player-facing management for campaign rulings and house rules: create, review, list/inspect, edit by supersession, and revoke.

Required behavior
Require player-provided or player-approved prose and an explicit kind. Show status, origin/provenance, effective position, and supersession/revocation history. Editing creates a new durable rule that supersedes the old identity rather than mutating historical semantic content. Ordinary creation applies prospectively unless invoked by the separate immediate-adjudication objection workflow.

Architecture and references
Use eshyra-jhpt.1 domain invariants and eshyra-jhpt.2 storage APIs. Preserve canonical history and ADR 0017 pack/campaign separation.

Non-goals
No arbitrary history rewrite; no direct editing of immutable rules-pack records; no automatic deterministic mechanic generation; no implicit ambiguity precedent; no DM-only unapproved rule creation; no persistence of ordinary contextual adjudications.
acceptance_criteria: Players can create ruling/house-rule prose, review and list active/history views, supersede through a new record, and revoke prospectively; confirmations expose effective timing and provenance; tests cover status transitions, deterministic ordering, invalid edits, cross-campaign isolation, and history preservation.

title: Give the auditor exact campaign-rule context parity
description:
Objective
Supply the mechanics audit model with the exact same active campaign-rule prose set used by the primary DM for the audited turn.

Required behavior
Use one deterministic active-rule context projection for both roles. The auditor evaluates canonical pack semantics plus active rulings and house rules at the turn's effective position, including a rule established at the start of an immediately replayed disputed turn. Preserve rule IDs/kinds/provenance so audit diagnostics can identify the governing campaign rule. Add direct equivalence tests over ordering, content, status filtering, supersession, revocation, and effective position.

Architecture and references
Build on the existing mechanics-audit gate eshyra-oobh and the context/storage contracts from eshyra-jhpt.1-.3. Follow ADR 0017: models interpret approved prose; deterministic code only selects the active set and timing.

Non-goals
No independent auditor-only rule registry or retrieval policy; no auditor authority to create/modify campaign rules; no arbitrary prose compilation; no changed canonical rules-pack semantics.
acceptance_criteria:
For every tested campaign position, DM and auditor receive byte-for-byte/equivalent deterministic active rule sets; superseded/revoked/future rules are absent; disputed-turn rules are present during replay; auditor diagnostics can cite rule identity; focused tests prove parity and prevent divergent context builders.

ADR 0020 TRANSITION AMENDMENT A3 (integrated transition design section 8.3, R6;
accepted as the deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8, PR #485, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282): the accepted-turn trace must retain
durable evidence of WHICH active campaign rules and rulings were supplied for the
turn and under which identities. Parity plus rule-identity citation in
diagnostics is not the same property: parity proves DM and auditor saw the same
set, while A3 proves what that set was, after the fact, from the persisted trace.

The evidence attaches to the existing accepted-turn trace authority
(memory/turnTrace.ts TurnTraceRecord). It must NOT create a second campaign-rule
store, a discovery-owned rule registry, or a parallel audit database (ADR 0017
section 8; ADR 0020 audit-architecture restraint). eshyra-jhpt.9 proves the
property end to end.

This is what lets the transition design's M5 measurement - which active rules and
rulings were requested, which matched, and which were placed beside their
governing material - be computed without a discovery-owned store. The
discovery-side consumer eshyra-o9bd.19.13 (transition W11) depends on this output
and may not substitute a discovery-local store.

title: Supply active campaign rules and source ambiguities to DM context
description:
Objective
Make the primary DM receive the complete active campaign-rule prose set and relevant immutable rules-pack ambiguity metadata at the adjudicated campaign position.

Required behavior
At initial scale, supply all active campaign-rule prose on every applicable DM turn; correctness takes priority over selective retrieval. Include stable rule identity, kind, effective provenance, and linked ambiguity/interpretation provenance without asking the model to execute deterministic state logic. When a relevant RulesAmbiguity has no active campaign ruling, the context must preserve uncertainty and prohibit silent canonical certainty. Context assembly must use the same active-at-position query that the auditor will use.

Architecture and references
Follow ADR 0017 and docs/rules-pack-compiler.md. Consume PR #419 mechanics.ambiguities / RulesAmbiguity output from eshyra-o9bd.18.7.9. Reuse existing rules-stack lookup and campaign binding rather than copying pack data into campaign state.

Non-goals
No persistence workflow, player dialogue policy, implicit precedent creation, prompt retrieval optimization, arbitrary house-rule inference, or prose-to-mechanics compilation. Ordinary contextual DM judgments do not become campaign rules.
acceptance_criteria:
DM context contains all and only rules active at the current campaign position in deterministic order; relevant unresolved RulesAmbiguity metadata is available without a preferred/default winner; tests prove prospective/effective-turn filtering and no silent canonical certainty; no campaign prose is written to the pack.

ADR 0020 TRANSITION AMENDMENT A1 (integrated transition design section 8.3, R4;
accepted as the deliverable of eshyra-o9bd.19.8, PR #485, merge commit
042ce119aa699f04f60a1885d471335f07745282): the active-rule projection must
expose, per rule, enough association data to place an active campaign rule or
ruling beside its governing pack record or source ambiguity - the linked
ambiguity ID and, where one exists, the governing pack record key - so a
consumer can pair rule and source material without re-deriving the association.
This extends the projection only; the eshyra-jhpt.1 domain model, which already
requires a ruling to record the ambiguity ID and selected interpretation ID as
provenance, is unchanged.

The discovery-side consumer is eshyra-o9bd.19.13 (transition W11), which depends
on this output and may not substitute a discovery-local campaign-rule or ruling
store, cache of record, or shadow resolver. Campaign-rule persistence, ruling
schema, active-rule resolution, supersession, revocation, and house-rule
lifecycle remain owned here. If the projection proves insufficient for the
consumer, the correct response is an amendment or a new child under eshyra-jhpt.
