title: Dispatch: 71u1 reform a present familiar via recast_bonded_summon (Sonnet 5.5, attempt 1)
description:
Implement eshyra-71u1 (read it: bd show eshyra-71u1). Parent integration bead: eshyra-71u1. The captain has made every design decision below. Do not re-decide them. If something here contradicts the code or the SRD record text, stop and record the contradiction in your notes rather than improvising.

HARD RULE (bd memory srd-fidelity-hard-blocker): nothing may contradict the SRD. Source: packages/core/data/rules-packs/rules__dnd5e-srd-5.1/records.json, records spell:find-familiar and spell:find-steed (data.description, data.castingTime, data.mechanics.effects[0].creation.forms, data.mechanics.effects[0].transitions). Do NOT edit records.json or any importer file.

## Source facts
- Find Familiar (casting time 1 hour, ritual): "the familiar has the statistics of the chosen form" ... "If you cast this spell while you already have a familiar, you instead cause it to adopt a new form. Choose one of the forms from the above list. Your familiar transforms into the chosen creature."
  Transition reform-present-familiar: trigger cast-again, when {presence: present, link: active}, operation {kind: select-new-form}, NO changes array (presence is unchanged).
  Transition restore-and-reform-absent-familiar (already executed by s02z): when absent + active, changes presence->present, select-new-form.
  reform-pocketed-familiar (when pocket-dimension): NOT in scope. The engine models no pocket presence; that is bead eshyra-82uk.
- Find Steed has only restore-same-steed (cast-again from absent). No cast-again transition exists for a present steed, so a present steed must stay refused.

## Today (survey)
- packages/core/src/state/activeEffects.ts: findBondedRecastTransition (~5160) selects only a cast-again transition whose when.presence includes 'absent' and whose changes set presence->present. recastBondedSummon (~5231) validates the effect, then calls the finder BEFORE reading the link and actor. It then calls restoreBondedCampaignActor and appends a 'recast' event. BondedRecastTransition (~5143) carries {id, operation, forms}.
- packages/core/src/state/encounterCombatants.ts restoreBondedCampaignActor (~3142): refuses actor.status !== 'absent' with a "Reforming a present or pocketed familiar is not yet supported" message. It also checks the vanish-bonded rule, hasActiveBondLink, the active-combat projection guard and exhaustion 6. It then computes rulesRef/hpMax (new-form: lookupCreatureRecord + readCreatureHp), sets hpCurrent = effectiveHpMax(hpMax, conditions), and upserts status alive with replaceCombatLifecycle: true.
- packages/core/src/orchestrator/toolRecastBondedSummon.ts: tool description says present/pocketed is refused.
- docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md ~285-312: the recastBondedSummon paragraph.
- packages/core/test/bondedSummonRecast.test.ts: tests at ~198 ("refuses a present steed and says reforming is unsupported") and ~363 ("refuses a present familiar ... out of scope") assert the old refusal.

## Decision (captain, 2026-10-07)
1. Selection by modelled presence. Restructure recastBondedSummon so it reads the single active actor link and its campaign actor BEFORE selecting the transition. Keep the existing effect-level refusals (missing, ended, suppressed, not summoning, wrong spellRef, unknown spell record) in their current order and with their current messages. Map the actor status to presence: 'absent' -> 'absent'; 'alive' -> 'present'. Refuse any other status with a clear message that names the status, before any write (a bonded familiar or steed cannot be dying, stable or dead short of exhaustion 6, and 'escaped', 'inactive', 'unknown' and 'unconscious' are not a presence the recast can reason about). Then find the cast-again transition whose when.presence includes that presence and whose when.link includes 'active':
   - For 'absent', require changes presence->present, exactly as today. Keep the existing message "has no cast-again transition that restores an absent creature whose link is active" for that case.
   - For 'present', require that the transition changes no presence (no changes entry with axis presence). Its operation must be select-new-form; any other operation is refused as not executable (same style as the existing unsupportedOperation refusal). If there is no such transition (Find Steed), refuse with a message saying the spell has no cast-again transition for a present creature whose link is active. For the steed, that means it is already present: the SRD bonds one steed at a time, and its recast only restores an absent steed.
   Never key on the spell name. Generalize BondedRecastTransition minimally, e.g. add from: 'absent' | 'present'.
2. One engine seam. Extend restoreBondedCampaignActor rather than adding a parallel function, so the guards cannot drift. Add an input field expectedPresence: 'absent' | 'present'. For 'present': the actor must be status 'alive', and restore must be {kind: 'new-form'} (refuse 'maximum' as an engine invariant). Every other guard applies unchanged: vanish-bonded rule, active bond link, no combatant in an active combat instance (the casting time is 1 hour; adjust the message wording so it fits both cases), exhaustion level 6 (unreachable for alive, keep it). The write: same actor, rulesRef = form, hpMax = readCreatureHp(form record), hpCurrent = effectiveHpMax(hpMax, actor.conditions), status alive. Conditions, exhaustion, display name, location, state (incl. combat lifecycle and its vanish-bonded rule) stay as stored. For 'absent', behaviour is byte-for-byte as today, except that the present-case wording moves out of the absent refusal. A mismatch between expectedPresence and the actual status is refused. Update the JSDoc above the function: it is now the path from absent back to alive AND the reform of a present bonded familiar.
   HP rationale, for the docs: the familiar "has the statistics of the chosen form", and the source carries no damage across a transformation, so the reformed familiar takes the new form's hit points, as the absent restore already does.
3. Event: the same 'recast' event kind and detail shape. transitionId is the selected transition id (reform-present-familiar), and form is recorded. No new event kind, no migration.
4. Result: RecastBondedSummonResult is unchanged in shape. transitionId reports reform-present-familiar.
5. Texts. Tool description (toolRecastBondedSummon.ts): a recast of Find Familiar while the familiar is present reforms it (form REQUIRED, same actor, new form's HP, stays present). The engine does not track a familiar dismissed to its pocket dimension: such a familiar is recorded as present, and the reform has the same effect. A present Find Steed is refused. Keep the out-of-combat, suppressed, ended/released, and no-spell-slot sentences. Update the encounterCombatants.ts refusal text, which must no longer say reforming is unsupported. Search for any other "not yet supported"/"reforming" text and update it (rg -n -i 'reform|pocket' packages/core/src packages/cli/src docs).
6. Docs: docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md, the recastBondedSummon paragraph. Describe the present reform, the presence-to-transition selection, what it leaves unchanged, that pocket presence is not modelled (eshyra-82uk) and why the reform is still correct for a pocketed familiar (reform-pocketed-familiar has the same operation and no presence change), and the HP rationale. Re-derive every sentence against the source text and the real tool contract. Check other sections that mention reforming (lines ~448, ~514).
7. Exports: no root-export changes. internal.ts only if a new type needs exporting.

## Evidence (packages/core/test/bondedSummonRecast.test.ts; reuse its setup helpers)
Replace the two old present-refusal tests. Assert identities and exact values, and pin no counts:
- Present familiar (bonded as creature:bat, combat closed first) recast with form creature:owl: same actor id, rulesRef creature:owl, hpMax and hpCurrent = the owl record's HP (read it from the record in the test via the same lookup the other familiar test uses, not a literal), status alive, link still active, effect active. The result and the ledger 'recast' event carry transitionId reform-present-familiar and form creature:owl.
- A damaged present familiar (adjust_hp or the existing damage helper below its max, but above 0) reformed into the SAME form returns at that form's full HP. This pins the HP decision.
- A present familiar at exhaustion level 4 reforms to the halved effective maximum.
- Present familiar: form omitted -> refused; a form outside the list -> refused. The actor is unchanged after each.
- Present familiar with a combatant in an active combat instance -> refused, unchanged.
- Present steed -> refused with the new "no cast-again transition for a present creature" message, unchanged.
- A reformed familiar can still vanish at 0 HP (vanish-bonded kept) and then be restored by an absent recast.
- A non-alive, non-absent status (e.g. set the actor 'unconscious' or 'inactive' through whatever engine path the tests can reach; if no path can produce it, say so in your notes and skip this one) -> refused naming the status.
- All existing absent-path tests stay green and unchanged except the two replaced.

## Procedure
Work only in this worktree (/home/jhbongaarts/src/eshyra/.worktrees/eshyra-71u1.1, branch eshyra-71u1.1); use worktree paths only, never the parent checkout. Run npm run verify:worktree from the worktree root BEFORE committing (it rewrites files). It must be fully green, documented skips only; under heavy machine load the rulesPackAuditCli timeouts are environmental (bd memory rulespack-audit-cli-tests-timeout-under-external-load). Then rerun with VITEST_MAX_FORKS=6. Commit on this branch with a message starting "eshyra-71u1.1 " and ending with the line: Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

title: Model a bonded summon's pocket-dimension presence and action dismissal/recall (Find Familiar, Find Steed)
description:
Split from eshyra-71u1 (2026-10-07). The engine does not model a bonded summon's pocket-dimension presence, and it executes no action-triggered presence transition. spell:find-familiar declares temporary-pocket-dismissal (action-temporary-dismissal: present -> pocket-dimension), pocket-recall (action-recall: pocket -> present, place-in-unoccupied-space within 30 ft), permanent-dismissal-from-present-or-pocket (link none), and reform-pocketed-familiar (cast-again select-new-form, no presence change). spell:find-steed declares action-dismissal (present -> absent, link active) and release-bond (action-release from present or absent -> link none). All of these are narrated only today. A pocketed familiar is indistinguishable from a present one: it is status alive and keeps its combat projection.

Design questions to settle before implementation:
1. Representation. A new ActorStatus/CombatantLifeStatus 'pocketed' (needs a migration for the status CHECKs; must keep HP, conditions, exhaustion; is not terminal, unlike absent), or 'absent' plus a presence marker? Absent is terminal for combatant rows and implies 0 HP for vanish-bonded creatures, which argues for a distinct status.
2. Mid-combat. Dismissal and recall each cost an action, so both can happen in combat. Dismissal takes the combatant out of play (does concentration break? the familiar can't concentrate anyway; check F3 owner-removed). Recall must bring the same creature back into the same combat instance at the same HP: is initiative re-rolled, or kept? There is a remanifest path in startEncounterInTxn, but absent is terminal there.
3. A Find Steed action dismissal is present -> absent with the link active. A later recast restores it at maximum HP (restore-same-steed). This reuses the s02z restore path, but through a new entry point that is not 0 HP.
4. Release and permanent dismissal set link none. Check whether end_effect / remove_effect_target already cover this, or whether a record-driven transition tool is wanted. ambiguity:find-familiar-permanent-dismissal-after-zero-hp stays gated.
5. One record-driven tool (e.g. transition_bonded_summon { effectId, trigger }) that executes action-* transitions from the spell record, rather than per-spell tools.
Docs: docs/active-effect-lifecycle.md section 6 and sections 8-9.
design:
DESIGN DECISIONS (Claude Captain, 2026-10-08). Answers the five questions in the description.

SOURCE (spell:find-familiar, spell:find-steed records.json; SRD 5.1 p. 143 / p. 144):
- Familiar: "As an action, you can temporarily dismiss your familiar. It disappears into a pocket dimension where it awaits your summons. Alternatively, you can dismiss it forever. As an action while it is temporarily dismissed, you can cause it to reappear in any unoccupied space within 30 feet of you."
- Steed: "You can also dismiss your steed at any time as an action, causing it to disappear. In either case, casting this spell again summons the same steed, restored to its hit point maximum." / "As an action, you can release the steed from its bond at any time, causing it to disappear."
The record transitions are authority: temporary-pocket-dismissal, pocket-recall (operation place-in-unoccupied-space withinFeet 30), permanent-dismissal-from-present-or-pocket, permanent-dismissal-from-zero-hp-absence (availability source-ambiguity -> stays gated), reform-pocketed-familiar (cast-again select-new-form, no presence change); steed action-dismissal, release-bond.

Q1 REPRESENTATION. New ActorStatus 'pocketed' on the CAMPAIGN ACTOR only (migration: campaign_actor status CHECK). NOT a CombatantStatus. A pocketed actor is out of play but not terminal and keeps hp_current, hp_max, rules_ref, conditions (incl. exhaustion) and its combat lifecycle (zero_hp_rule vanish-bonded). Reasons: absent is terminal for a combatant row (I9) and for vanish-bonded implies a max-HP/new-form restore; a CombatantStatus would need every absent guard in the combat engine duplicated (a missed guard = a pocketed creature taking damage). Only a vanish-bonded actor held by an active actor link of an active, spell-sourced summoning effect whose record has a pocket-dimension presence can be pocketed.

Q2 MID-COMBAT. Initiative and turn order are model-narrated (actionEconomy.ts), so no initiative slot exists to keep or re-roll; SRD "In combat, it rolls its own initiative" stays narrated.
- Dismissal while the creature has a live combatant in the active instance: the combatant leaves play through the existing remove seam (removeCombatantFromPlay: row becomes absent, concentration break as for any leaving-play), its actor link(s) are rebound to the campaign actor immediately (same rebind the closure does), and the campaign actor ends with the right status (pocketed for the familiar's temporary dismissal, keeping the HP/conditions it had at dismissal; absent for steed dismissal / release / permanent dismissal). The stale absent row must never later overwrite the actor (closure sync / syncCombatantActor must not write an absent row onto a pocketed actor).
- Recall while a combat instance is active: the actor returns alive with everything it had, and is projected into the ACTIVE instance as a NEW combatant row (absent never returns on the same row). Factor the campaign-actor projection block of startEncounterInTxn into one internal seam used by both start_encounter and the recall, so the projection rules cannot drift. Row id: `${instance}-${slug(actorId)}` when free, else the next `-2`, `-3`... currentActorProjectionId must break ties within one instance by newest row. side/faction default to the actor's most recent row in that instance; with no such row the tool requires side. placement optional (the record's place-in-unoccupied-space within 30 ft is narrated and reported).
- Recall with no active combat: actor pocketed -> alive, nothing else changes.

Q3 STEED ACTION DISMISSAL. present -> absent with the link active: actor absent (via the existing remove seams), link and effect untouched, so start_encounter refuses it and recast_bonded_summon's restore-same-steed restores it at maximum HP (existing s02z path, no new entry point needed).

Q4 RELEASE / PERMANENT DISMISSAL (link -> none, presence -> absent). Do NOT route through end_effect: Find Familiar/Steed derive no spell-ended cleanup, so a stored 'release' policy would leave the creature alive and unbonded, contradicting "causing it to disappear". The transition takes the creature out of play (absent, from present or pocketed; a steed already absent stays absent), closes its actor link (status removed), and ends the effect with reason 'dismissed' when no active actor link remains. Afterwards the actor is an unbonded absent actor: start_encounter admits it only as a new manifestation (existing rule). permanent-dismissal-from-zero-hp-absence stays refused, naming ambiguity:find-familiar-permanent-dismissal-after-zero-hp.
Also: any OTHER path that ends a bond while the actor is pocketed (end_effect with a release policy, closure) must take it out of play (absent), never leave an unbonded pocketed actor; report it as removed.

Q5 ONE RECORD-DRIVEN TOOL. transition_bonded_summon { effectId, spellRef, trigger, side?, faction?, placement? }, trigger in action-temporary-dismissal | action-recall | action-permanent-dismissal | action-dismissal | action-release. It selects the record transition by trigger AND current presence (alive -> present, pocketed -> pocket-dimension, absent -> absent; any other status refused naming it) with link active, never by spell name; refuses a transition with an availability gate (naming the ambiguity id) and any change combination the engine does not execute. It spends no action: the description tells the model to spend the caster's action with spend_turn_resource in combat (same split as recast_bonded_summon and spell slots). Records a new active_effect_event kind (e.g. 'presence-transition') with spellRef, transitionId, trigger, actor, from, to, and the combatant ids left/entered.
recast_bonded_summon: pocketed maps to pocket-dimension, so reform-pocketed-familiar executes (stays pocketed, new form, new form's HP per the 71u1 rule); remove the "pocket presence is not modelled" text.

SPLIT OUT: a generic model-facing way to admit creatures to an active combat instance (mid-combat summons such as Conjure Animals cast in round 3 currently cannot get combatants: start_encounter only opens a new instance and only one may be active). This bead adds only the internal seam the recall needs.

title: Reform a present familiar on Find Familiar recast (cast-again select-new-form from present)
description:
From eshyra-s02z. SCOPE NARROWED 2026-10-07 (captain): reform a PRESENT familiar on Find Familiar recast (spell:find-familiar transition reform-present-familiar: cast-again, when presence present + link active, operation select-new-form, no presence change). recast_bonded_summon currently refuses any actor that is not absent.

Pocket presence is split out to its own bead (temporary dismissal, recall, reform-while-pocketed, permanent dismissal, Find Steed action-dismissal), because the engine does not model it and dismissal/recall are actions usable mid-combat. Until that lands the engine cannot tell a pocketed familiar from a present one: both are a live actor with an active bond, and reform-pocketed-familiar has the same operation and no presence change, so the executed reform is correct for either. The recorded transition is reform-present-familiar, the only presence the engine models.

Design decisions (captain):
- Selection stays record-driven: choose the cast-again transition whose when.presence matches the actor's modelled presence (absent -> 'absent', alive -> 'present') and whose when.link includes 'active'. Never key on the spell name. Find Steed has no present cast-again transition, so a present steed stays refused (the SRD allows one steed at a time; its recast only restores an absent steed).
- Reform result: same campaign actor, rulesRef = chosen form, hpMax = that creature record's HP, hpCurrent = effective maximum (exhaustion-adjusted), status stays alive. Source basis: "the familiar has the statistics of the chosen form" plus "Your familiar transforms into the chosen creature". Hit points are part of those statistics and the source carries no damage across. Conditions, exhaustion, display name and the vanish-bonded rule stay as stored, as in the absent restore.
- Refuse while the actor has a combatant in an active combat instance (the casting time is 1 hour), and for any actor status other than alive or absent.

Spec and evidence live in the dispatch child.
notes:
HP decision confirmed by user 2026-10-07: a reformed present familiar takes the new form's full HP. Source research the same day found no WotC ruling: the Sage Advice Compendium's two Find Familiar entries cover Help and Sneak Attack only; Crawford tweets and the D&D Beyond Spell Spotlight are silent on HP on reform. Community material is thin and split: one D&D Beyond forum opinion assumes health regenerates on recast; some homebrew variants (Ascended Familiar, Battle Familiar, an Improved Familiar feat) explicitly limit or grant HP. Basis kept: 'has the statistics of the chosen form' + 'transforms into the chosen creature', the same reading the absent restore uses. Docs should present this as the engine's reading of a text that is silent on carried damage, not as an official ruling.

title: Structured-field spell-list evidence is per (class,level) group, not per printed page
description: sourceInventoryCoverage.ts's spellListStructuredFieldRules attaches one shared structuredFieldEvidence.spellKeys list (naming every spell in a whole (class, level) group) to that group's owning heading. When the group's printed spell list spans a page break, buildSourceRegionLedger still splits it into one ledger entry per physical page, and every split entry carries the SAME whole-group evidence. Verified against the real SRD 5.1 corpus (eshyra-o9bd.19.2.2.3.1): 6 of the 70 (class, level) groups span a page break, affecting 93 spell records whose 'classes' field-locator pages (added in eshyra-o9bd.19.2.2.3.1 F4) therefore cite every page of the WHOLE group's list, not just the page the spell's own name is printed on. eshyra-o9bd.19.2.2.3.1 worked around this by deriving spell.data.classes' fieldLocators from the same ledger evidence the recordLocatorCompleteness.ts gate (b) checks against (enrichSpellClassFieldLocatorsFromRegionLedger in enrichProvenance.ts), so the two sides can never drift apart -- but this means the field locator is coarser than it could be (it does not pin down the exact line a spell's name prints on within a page-spanning group). A future improvement would make spellListStructuredFieldRules (or buildSourceRegionLedger's per-region evidence assignment) precise per physical page/region instead of per whole group, tightening both the field locator and the ledger's own diagnostic evidence. Not required for eshyra-o9bd.19.2.2.3.1's own invariant (the gate and the emitted locator are already mutually consistent and source-backed); this is a follow-on precision improvement, not a defect.
close_reason: Resolved in PR #576 (review fix R1): spell /classes locators now come from each spell's own list-line page and gate (b) checks against the structured-field regions' printed lines.

title: Dispatch: per-run test temp root + script temp leaks (attempt 1)
description:
Implementation dispatch for parent eshyra-knh9 (read it: `bd show eshyra-knh9`). Worktree `.worktrees/eshyra-knh9.1`, branch `eshyra-knh9.1`.

PROBLEM: the test suite and some scripts leave temp dirs under os.tmpdir() after every run. One dev host accumulated ~3,400 of them plus ~230 `<nanoid>/ssr/` Vitest caches (~49M each) and filled a 3.9G tmpfs.

SURVEY (supervisor):
- About 55 test files create dirs with `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), '<prefix>'))` and many never remove them: prefixes lw-camp-, lw-sep-, lw-doltroot-, lw-rs-, lw-rules-rs-, lw-doltbin-, lw-emptyhome-, lw-dolthome-, lw-isohome-, lw-cp-, lw-root-, lw-dolt-, lw-arc-, lw-reg-, lw-ckpt-, lw-cfg-, lw-world-, lw-fk-, lw-empty-, lw-drafts-, lw-char-registry-, lw-bin-symlink-, lw-pack-, lw-eof-, lw-play-cp-, and measure-run- (packages/core/test/measureRun.test.ts). List them all with `grep -rln "mkdtemp\|tmpdir()" packages scripts --include=*.ts --include=*.mjs`.
- Production code also creates temp dirs: packages/core/src/persistence/checkpoint/doltProvision.ts:186 `lw-dolt-dl-`. Check that it removes them on success and on failure.
- packages/core/scripts/verify-dnd5e-srd-pack/cli.ts:104 creates `verify-dnd5e-srd-pack-*` and removes it in a `finally` (line ~242), yet 21 were left behind. Find out why: a process.exit inside the try, a signal, or a caller or test that runs it with a different path. Fix the root cause.
- The `<21-char nanoid>/ssr/<sha1>` dirs (~49M each, one per run): identify which tool creates them (likely Vitest 5 / Vite module-runner or fs module cache; check node_modules/vitest and vite). Configure it to reuse a stable cache location (e.g. under node_modules/.vite or node_modules/.vitest) or to clean up after itself. If neither is possible, document why in the notes.

DESIGN (decided by the supervisor):
1. Give the test run a single per-run temp root. Add a Vitest globalSetup (wired in root vitest.config.ts) that creates `mkdtemp(join(os.tmpdir(), 'eshyra-vitest-'))` and makes it the TMPDIR every worker and every spawned child process sees. Then os.tmpdir() inside tests resolves there, and teardown `rm -rf`s the whole root. Verify that workers really inherit it: Vitest may create the pool before globalSetup runs. If they don't, use `provide`/`inject` plus a setupFiles entry that sets process.env.TMPDIR in each worker before tests import anything. Also make sure a crashed or interrupted run leaves at most that one root. On setup, removing stale `eshyra-vitest-*` roots older than some hours is acceptable if it's safe for concurrent runs (another agent may be running the suite at the same time: only remove roots whose owning PID, recorded in the root, is dead).
2. Do NOT rewrite the 55 call sites merely for style. Fix a call site only when it matters beyond cleanliness (e.g. production code, or a test whose leak escapes the per-run root because it resolves the temp path before setup).
3. Fix the scripts' own leaks (verify-dnd5e-srd-pack root cause, doltProvision if needed).
4. Tests that assert on os.tmpdir() / TMPDIR behavior (e.g. packages/core/test/nodeRuntimePolicy.test.ts, checkpoint.doltBinary.test.ts with isolated HOME) must keep their intent. Run them.
5. Evidence: add a small permanent test only if it protects a real contract, e.g. that the globalSetup's root is where os.tmpdir() points inside a worker. Don't add tests that just count files. Put the empirical proof in your notes instead.

COMPLETION PROOF (in your notes): with `TMPDIR=$HOME/.cache/tmp-knh9-proof` (create it empty), run the full `npm run test` and then `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack`, and list what remains in that dir afterwards: it should be empty or hold only the documented stable caches. Also record the same listing BEFORE your change, for comparison. Then `npm run verify:worktree` green.

ENVIRONMENT / RESOURCE RULES:
- The host has ~7 GB RAM, and another agent is working at the same time. Run EVERY full-suite command (`npm run test`, `npm run verify:worktree`, `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack`) through the shared lock: `flock /home/jhbongaarts/.cache/eshyra-verify.lock <command>`. Focused `npx vitest run <files>` runs of a few files do not need the lock.
- Your shell may still have TMPDIR=/dev/shm; that's fine, but leave nothing behind in it.
- `npm ci` in the worktree first.
notes:
## eshyra-knh9.1 completion report

### Root causes found (survey confirmed all three named in the parent bug)

1. verify-dnd5e-srd-pack/cli.ts (21 leaked dirs in the original report): every
   exit path in main()'s try block called process.exit(N) INSIDE the try whose
   finally { rmSync(tmpDir, ...) } was meant to clean up. process.exit() does
   not unwind the call stack -- it terminates in place -- so that finally was
   dead code on every invocation, success or failure. Fixed by returning the
   exit code from main() (Promise<number>) and calling process.exit(code) only
   in the module-level `main().then(...)` after main() (and its finally) has
   fully resolved. Same bug, same fix, also found and fixed in two more
   scripts caught by the same pattern search (grep for files with both
   mkdtemp and process.exit):
   - packages/core/scripts/generate-creature-name-baseline/cli.ts (identical
     shape).
   - scripts/release/smoke-installer.mjs: its shared `fail(msg)` helper called
     process.exit(1) from inside the try whose finally removes `scratch`.
     Fixed by having fail() throw instead (still logs the same "SMOKE FAILED"
     message first); an uncaught throw still unwinds through finally and Node
     exits 1 by default, same exit code as before. Not run end-to-end here
     (it drives a full release build + install.sh; not part of verify:worktree
     or npm test) -- fixed by inspection/pattern match, same proven mechanism
     as the other three.
   Checked and left alone (correctly, not a leak): doltProvision-adjacent
   packages/core/src/model/codexSdkMcpClient.ts already has a correct
   try/finally (no process.exit involved). packages/core/scripts/deep-audit-dnd5e-srd/cli.ts
   intentionally does NOT clean up its default --out dir: that directory holds
   the tool's actual deliverable (JSON reports a human is meant to open
   afterward, path printed as "Reports: <dir>"), not scratch space. Filed
   eshyra-knh9.2 (P4) noting this and suggesting it default to a repo-local
   dir instead of tmpdir() as an optional DX nit. scripts/release/build-release-artifact.mjs,
   validate-release-artifact.mjs, scripts/beads-sync.mjs, and
   scripts/seats/probe-dispatch-markers.mjs were also audited: all either use
   process.exitCode (non-terminating, safe) or call process.exit() only
   outside/after the relevant try/finally. No change needed.

2. doltProvision.ts:186 (packages/core/src/persistence/checkpoint/doltProvision.ts):
   provisionDolt() created its `work` scratch dir (mkdtempSync 'lw-dolt-dl-')
   and NEVER removed it -- no finally at all, on success or failure. Fixed by
   wrapping the download/verify/extract/install body in try/finally { rmSync(work, ...) }.

3. The <nanoid>/ssr/<sha1> caches (~49MB each, one per vitest run): confirmed
   these are Vitest's OWN internal SSR module-transform cache dirs --
   `TestProject.tmpDir` / `Vitest._tmpDir`, both literally
   `join(tmpdir(), nanoid())` in node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.DzobfTyw.js
   (vitest 5.0.1 / vite 8.3.0). Vitest does have its own cleanup
   (TestProject.clearTmpDir() -> rm(this.tmpDir), called from close()), but it
   is best-effort (wrapped in try{}catch{}) and was empirically observed to
   leave the dir behind on normal, successful `vitest run` exits (reproduced
   directly, see "design deviation" below) -- matching the ~230 leaked
   instances in the original bug report.

### Design deviation from the literal spec text (verified empirically, not a "stop")

The spec's design item 1 says: "Add a Vitest globalSetup (wired in root
vitest.config.ts)... Verify that workers really inherit it: Vitest may create
the pool before globalSetup runs. If they don't, use provide/inject plus a
setupFiles entry..." -- explicitly asking me to verify and adapt if the naive
globalSetup approach doesn't reach far enough. It doesn't, for a more
fundamental reason than worker-pool timing:

Read node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.DzobfTyw.js: `Vitest._tmpDir` and
`TestProject.tmpDir` are both CLASS-FIELD INITIALIZERS
(`= join(tmpdir(), nanoid())`), evaluated the instant `new Vitest(...)` /
`new TestProject(...)` run -- which is before ANY globalSetup file can
possibly execute (globalSetup is loaded via an instance method called later
in `_start()`). So a globalSetup hook cannot redirect TMPDIR early enough to
affect vitest's own SSR cache path, no matter how it's wired -- this isn't a
worker-inheritance timing issue, it's that the value is already computed
before user code of any kind can run.

Empirically verified (monkeypatched node:module.enableCompileCache with a
stack-trace spy; ran a scratch copy of vitest.config.ts with the redirect
moved to different points): reassigning `process.env.TMPDIR` at
vitest.config.ts MODULE EVALUATION time -- before `defineConfig()` is even
called -- DOES land inside every one of: vitest's own SSR nanoid cache, every
worker's temp dirs (measure-run-*, lw-*, ...), and even npm's own
node-compile-cache (npm's CLI calls module.enableCompileCache() on its own
startup, before vitest.config.ts loads, but that call resolves its cache
directory lazily at first write, so it still observes the reassignment).
Confirmed with a real `TMPDIR=/tmp/knh9-probe4 npx vitest run
packages/core/test/measureRun.test.ts`: every single leaked artifact (ssr
nanoid dir, measure-run-* dirs, node-compile-cache) landed inside the new
redirected root and nothing outside it.

So I implemented item 1's INTENT (one per-run temp root, TMPDIR redirected
before anything resolves a temp path, full teardown) via a different
mechanism than literally "globalSetup": a small injectable module
(scripts/vitestTempRoot.mjs, exporting `installPerRunTempRoot` +
`reapStaleTempRoots`) called at the very top of vitest.config.ts, before
`defineConfig()`. It:
  - reaps any earlier `eshyra-vitest-*` root under the real tmpdir() whose
    `owner.pid` marker names a dead PID (conservative: any ambiguous
    process.kill(pid,0) result, e.g. EPERM, is treated as "alive" and left
    alone -- safe for another agent's concurrent run on the same host);
  - creates this run's root via mkdtempSync, writes owner.pid;
  - sets env.TMPDIR / env.TMP / env.TEMP to the new root;
  - registers `process.on('exit', ...)` for cleanup -- chosen deliberately
    over relying on globalSetup's async teardown callback, because
    process.on('exit') still fires for a bare process.exit() call (unlike a
    `finally` further up the stack -- see the verify-dnd5e-srd-pack root
    cause above), so it is strictly more robust against exactly the failure
    mode this bead exists to fix. It cannot cover SIGKILL/OOM-kill, which is
    what the PID-liveness reaper is for.
This is not a "spec proved wrong, stop" situation -- the spec's own text
anticipated needing to adapt the wiring mechanism if the straightforward
approach didn't reach far enough, and gave me latitude to do so ("If they
don't [inherit it], use ..."). I used that latitude one layer further up the
same call stack (the whole vitest process, not just workers) once I had
concrete proof the hook-based approach structurally could not work. Design
item 1's actual requirements (single per-run root; TMPDIR resolves there for
every worker and spawned child; teardown rm -rfs the whole root; concurrent-
run-safe reaping of dead roots) are all met and empirically verified below.

### Files changed

- scripts/vitestTempRoot.mjs (new): installPerRunTempRoot() /
  reapStaleTempRoots(), fully dependency-injected (baseDir/env/pid/isAlive/
  registerExitHandler all overridable) so it never has to touch the real
  process.env or real os.tmpdir() to be tested.
- vitest.config.ts: calls installPerRunTempRoot() at the top, before
  defineConfig(), with a comment explaining why (see above).
- packages/core/test/vitestTempRoot.test.ts (new, permanent regression
  evidence per design item 5): 7 tests against the injectable module --
  root creation under baseDir + env.TMPDIR/TMP/TEMP all point at it +
  owner.pid written; cleanup() removes it; no exit handler registered when
  told not to; reaper removes a dead-PID root, leaves a live-PID root alone,
  leaves a marker-less (concurrently-being-created) root alone, and ignores
  unrelated directory names. This is the analogue of "the root is where
  os.tmpdir() points inside a worker" from the design spec, adapted to the
  mechanism actually used.
- packages/core/src/persistence/checkpoint/doltProvision.ts: wraps
  provisionDolt()'s download/extract/install body in try/finally to remove
  its `work` scratch dir unconditionally (was: never removed at all).
- packages/core/scripts/verify-dnd5e-srd-pack/cli.ts,
  packages/core/scripts/generate-creature-name-baseline/cli.ts,
  scripts/release/smoke-installer.mjs: process.exit()-bypasses-finally fix
  described above.

Not touched (per design item 2 -- don't rewrite the ~55 test call sites
merely for style): every lw-*/measure-run-* test fixture continues to call
mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), '<prefix>')) exactly as before. None of them can
"escape" the per-run root, because the root is installed at vitest.config.ts
module-evaluation time -- the very first thing that runs in the whole
process, before any test file is ever imported by any worker.

### Completion proof

TMPDIR=$HOME/.cache/tmp-knh9-proof (created empty each time), commands run
through `flock /home/jhbongaarts/.cache/eshyra-verify.lock`.

BEFORE (git stash of all 5 changed/new files -- i.e. original unpatched
code -- then `npm run test` immediately followed by `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack`,
both with TMPDIR pointed at the empty proof dir):
  66 top-level entries left behind, 74M total. Breakdown (prefix: count):
  lw-camp 18, lw-sep 9, lw-doltroot 5, measure-run 4, lw-rs 4, lw-doltbin 4,
  lw-emptyhome 3, lw-arc 3, lw-root 2, lw-cp 2, verify-dnd5e-srd-pack 1,
  tsx-1000 1, node-compile-cache 1, lw-rules-rs 1, lw-play-cp 1, lw-isohome 1,
  lw-fk 1, lw-empty 1, lw-dolthome 1, lw-dolt-dl 1, lw-dolt 1, plus one
  <21-char-nanoid>/ssr/<sha1> directory. Confirms both the lw-dolt-dl- leak
  (doltProvision) and the verify-dnd5e-srd-pack-* leak (finally-bypass) were
  real and present pre-fix, alongside the vitest ssr cache and the ~55 test
  fixtures.

AFTER (git stash pop to restore the fix; fresh empty proof dir; same two
commands, same TMPDIR):
  `npm run test`: 310 files passed | 2 skipped (312), 5411 tests passed |
  3 skipped (5414). Proof dir empty after this step alone (checked before
  running the second command).
  `npm run verify:dnd5e-srd-pack`: "committed pack matches importer output
  exactly" (0 diff, same as baseline -- confirms the control-flow fix does
  not change the tool's actual output).

already isolates one invocation's own text), attaching to
choices[].options[].mechanics or similar — or whether this is out of

title: Decide whether PreCompact 'bd prime' (a bd init default) is doing what it should
description: The PreCompact handler in .claude/settings.json runs 'bd prime', presumably to re-prime the agent across a compaction. That is not what a PreCompact hook's stdout does. In Claude Code 2.1.278 the PreCompact handler collects the stdout of every succeeded, non-blocked hook and returns it as newCustomInstructions — the custom instructions handed to the COMPACTION SUMMARIZER (the same field '/compact <instructions>' sets). It is not context injected for the model to act on after the compaction. So bd prime's full output (memories, command reference, workflow rules) is currently being used as summarization guidance. Evidence: the PreCompact handler builds its payload as {...base, hook_event_name:'PreCompact', trigger, custom_instructions} and returns {newCustomInstructions: <joined hook stdout>, userDisplayMessage, blockedBy}. Compare SessionStart, whose raw stdout genuinely becomes session context. Discovered while resolving eshyra-oqvj.
acceptance_criteria: Either the PreCompact handler is changed to something whose effect matches the intent (e.g. move re-priming to a PostCompact or SessionStart path, or emit a short summarizer instruction deliberately), or the bead records that feeding bd prime to the summarizer is intended and why.
notes:
PROVENANCE (checked after the bead was filed, in response to a challenge that the original framing asserted intent it had not verified):

1. MECHANISM — verified, high confidence. The PreCompact handler collects the stdout of every succeeded, non-blocked hook and returns it as newCustomInstructions. Four call sites consume it, all identically: it is merged with any user-supplied /compact text and passed as customInstructions to the summary generator. Hook stdout steers the compaction SUMMARIZER; it is not context injected for the model to act on afterwards.

2. NOT THIS REPO'S DESIGN — high confidence. 'git log -S PreCompact -- .claude/settings.json' returns exactly one commit: 1423dbe7 'bd init: initialize beads issue tracking' (2026-05-16). Never edited since. The bd binary ships this exact template: PreCompact -> matcher '' -> command 'bd prime'. It is upstream generated boilerplate, the class of thing AGENTS.md already warns about ('a stale generated block is what introduced the push-policy conflict').

3. UPSTREAM INTENT — UNRESOLVED, and the bead must not assume it. Against deliberateness: bd prime describes itself as 'Context Recovery: run after compaction, clear, or new session', which a PreCompact hook structurally cannot do; bd also installs a SessionStart hook, which fires with source=compact and DOES recover context; and bd prime's multi-KB workflow reference makes no sense as summarizer instructions. For deliberateness: upstream may want bead context to survive summarization, and the registration may have been correct on an older Claude Code whose PreCompact stdout behaved differently. That last possibility cannot be checked from here.

CONSEQUENCE IS MODEST: priming after compaction still happens via SessionStart, so nothing is lost. The cost is that a large irrelevant string is steering compaction summaries.

This is an upstream question before it is a local one.

title: Add a captain-gated exit channel for seat handoffs (PreCompact)
description: Every gated seat delivery path is SessionStart-shaped: charter injection, the handoff read, bd prime, and PreCompact -> bd prime (a context refill fired at the moment context is about to be destroyed). The seat charter's exit obligation has no gated carrier. Candidate: a second, model-gated PreCompact handler alongside the existing 'bd prime' in .claude/settings.json, reusing classifyClaudeSession (scripts/seats/seatContext.mjs:27), which has no hook_event_name guard and is already event-agnostic. PREREQUISITE: confirm the PreCompact hook payload carries a 'model' field. The classifier is fail-closed on absent model identity, so if it does not, the handler silently emits nothing — the same quiet-failure mode the Codex hook-trust section of docs/agent-captain-seats.md describes. SessionEnd cannot deliver text to a model that is already ending, and Stop fires every turn, so neither is a drop-in substitute. classifyCodexSession (seatContext.mjs:58-63) hard-refuses any non-SessionStart event, so an equivalent Codex exit channel is a separate decision requiring a deliberate widening of that guard.
acceptance_criteria: Either a gated exit-channel handler lands with evidence that its payload reaches only an eligible occupant, or the bead records why the available hook events cannot carry one.
notes: PR #560 (https://github.com/jbongaarts/eshyra/pull/560) open at head e0375856, branch eshyra-oqvj. Stays in_progress until merged. PREREQUISITE RESOLVED: no exit-side hook event carries 'model' (verified against CLI 2.1.278) — the common payload builder omits it and SessionStart adds it. PreCompact stdout becomes the compaction summarizer's newCustomInstructions, not model context; SessionEnd output goes nowhere. Stop + hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext is the only exit channel that reaches the model. Gated by a SessionStart-written occupant ledger under <git common dir>/eshyra-seats/claude-captain/sessions/. Spun out eshyra-nuf2 for the PreCompact/bd prime mismatch found along the way. verify:worktree clean: 5613 passed, 3 documented skips.

title: Foundation-1 procedure-proof test times out its 10s hook under full-suite load
description:
`packages/core/test/importers/dnd5e-srd-5.1/foundation1ProcedureProof.test.ts`
fails with `Error: Hook timed out in 10000ms` when run as part of the full
Vitest suite, and passes (43/43) when its file is run alone.

INDEPENDENTLY ESTABLISHED AS PRE-EXISTING, 2026-09-12: reproduced on a clean
detached checkout of `origin/main` at `67e0653` with no other changes —
`npm run test` there reports `1 failed | 296 passed | 2 skipped`, the same
file, the same hook timeout. It arrived with PR #545 / the Foundation-1
importer stage, not with PR #543.

WHY IT MATTERS
It is a false red on the pre-commit gate and on `main` itself. An agent that
takes it at face value either chases an unrelated change or learns to ignore a
failing gate.

LIKELY CAUSE (unverified)
A `beforeAll`/`beforeEach` hook that builds or loads importer output. Under
full-suite load (one worker per file) that work exceeds the default 10s hook
timeout; alone it does not.

CANDIDATE FIXES, in preference order
1. Raise the hook timeout for that file to reflect the real cost of the setup
   it performs. The assertions are about procedure projections, not speed.
2. Hoist the shared setup so it is paid once per suite rather than per hook.
3. Only if neither holds: give the file a dedicated pool.

Do NOT fix it by skipping the file or weakening its assertions — it is the
permanent evidence for the Foundation-1 procedure-projection work.

RELATED
A sibling pre-existing flake is filed for
`packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts > packs publishable tarballs` (same shape: a
10s timeout under full-suite load, green standalone).
notes:
2026-09-14 (eshyra-o9bd.19.1.4 / PR #546): root-caused and mitigated. The beforeAll hook reads the multi-MB SRD PDF and extracts every page; measured isolated cost is ~3.5s (3.63s, 3.49s over two runs), so vitest's default 10s had under 3x headroom against parallel workers. It went from intermittent to DETERMINISTIC (three reproductions, including one with a single worktree and more free RAM than an earlier passing run of the same base - the opposite of a transient-load signature) once PR #546 added ~23 pack-loading and discovery tests to the same run. Hook budget raised to 60s (~17x measured isolated cost) with the measurement recorded in-line. No assertion changed: a timeout bounds how long an expensive I/O fixture may take, not what counts as correct, and a genuine hang still fails. If a durable fix is wanted, the real lever is caching the extracted pages across the importer test files that each re-extract the same PDF.
2026-09-22 RE-EXAMINED under the 6-worker cap (eshyra-9l5s.2 / PR #552) by eshyra-9l5s.5. VERIFIED CAUSE: worker fan-out contention (Vitest default maxWorkers = availableParallelism() = 20 on a 7.8 GB host with swap ~91% used at idle), per audit docs/audits/test-suite-and-verification/2026-09-14-test-suite-and-verification-audit.md section 2. EVIDENCE (measured, not 'did not reproduce'): a temporary timing probe in the beforeAll hook (reverted; tree verified clean) recorded 2,817 / 2,895 / 3,222 ms across three capped full-suite runs, against 2,356 ms with the file alone. Load inflation under the cap is 1.2-1.4x, so even vitest's default 10 s would have >=3.1x headroom; the 60 s budget has ~19x. Nine capped full-suite runs this session were green. DISPOSITION: fixed at the cause by the worker cap. The 60 s hook budget from 473424d is KEPT deliberately rather than reverted: it bounds an expensive I/O fixture, not correctness, a real hang still fails, and CI runners (cap 4, slower CPUs) have not been measured for this hook. Reverting it would buy no protection. The page-extraction caching lever in the prior note is not warranted by the measurement: the file is ~1 s of in-suite time.
close_reason: Cause verified (uncapped worker fan-out) and fixed by the worker cap from eshyra-9l5s.2; hook measured at 2.8-3.2 s under the capped full suite vs 60 s budget. Evidence in notes (eshyra-9l5s.5).

title: Runtime capability-preflight cannot anticipate P8's operationId (packet-intervention finding)
description:
Finding recorded while building the packet-intervention evidence suite (eshyra-o9bd.19.12.4). packages/core/src/discovery/signals.ts requires a live-state leaf whose JSON path ends in /operationId to fire the capability-preflight signal for a magic-item candidate (see signals.ts around line 230, and packet.ts:190-200 which reads that route's evidence.operationId). Real campaign state (assembleContext's live StateSnapshot) never carries such a literal operationId field for an item instance -- it is not a real persisted campaign fact, only something the model's eventual tool choice would supply. packages/core/test/discovery/support/runtimeCampaignState.ts already documents this deliberately for P1/P2 ('Writing it into plot_flags to make a probe reach its target would hand the signals stage the record key it is supposed to discover'), and explicitly names P8's operationId as one of the fields NOT synthesized for exactly that reason.

Consequence: at a REAL runtime turn (shadow or intervene mode), P8's (magic-item:ammunition-1-2-or-3) capability preflight never fires, so the delivered/observed packet carries the NEGATIVE capability form ('no capability was positively selected'), never the POSITIVE bounded contract the OFFLINE Phase-1 harness produces for the same fixture (packetMessage.test.ts's own E4 case, and shadowRuntime.test.ts's pre-existing 'records a runtime capability outcome the shadow packet never preflighted' test, which already show m10.comparisons === [] for P8 at runtime). packetIntervention.test.ts pins this exactly: the offline positive-contract proof and the live negative-form proof are two separate, both-checked cases (see its 'E8 (positive half)' and the 'P8/default' E8 negative-half block).

This is a genuine, pre-existing Phase 2/3 boundary in the discovery pipeline (which record/operation a capability preflight can evaluate before the model has chosen a tool), not a defect in the .12.4 evidence suite or the .12.3 intervention seam. Recorded per .12.4's dispatch instruction ('if the seam looks wrong, record it and file a follow-up -- do not fix it here'). No fix is prescribed here; the parent bead's owner should decide whether this boundary is accepted permanently (documented, like P1/P2's RUNTIME_REACH losses) or whether a future workstream should give discovery an earlier, real signal for an about-to-be-invoked operationId.
notes:
Evidence: packages/core/test/discovery/packetIntervention.test.ts (E8 positive/negative halves), packages/core/test/discovery/support/runtimeCampaignState.ts header comment, packages/core/src/discovery/signals.ts:~230, packages/core/src/discovery/packet.ts:180-200.
Superseded and resolved by eshyra-o9bd.19.12.9, commit 9d37624 on branch eshyra-o9bd.19.12.9. signals.ts no longer requires a literal /operationId state leaf: capability-preflight signals derive from each bound item instance and each state-referenced record, enumerating the operations declaredItemOperationIds() (itemState.ts) reports for that record/variant. P8's real intervene turn now reaches the positive bounded contract for hit-target, and M10 reports agreement (packetIntervention.test.ts P8/default case; shadowRuntime.test.ts 'pairs a runtime capability invocation with the preflight the held item declares'). Closing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Review ShadowDelivery candidateCount/mustConsiderOverflow for redundancy with M6/M7
description: eshyra-o9bd.19.12.3 implemented ShadowDelivery's injected-true arm exactly as the parent bead specified: {mode:'intervened', injected:true, renderedBytes, renderedSha256, candidateCount, mustConsiderOverflow}. candidateCount and mustConsiderOverflow are copied verbatim from the RenderedContextPacket produced at capture time (never independently recomputed), so they cannot disagree with what was actually rendered. But they ARE, in principle, also derivable from capture.trace's canonical dispositions via measureDiscovery/deriveDiscoveryTrace (M6/M7) whenever the capture succeeded -- the same 'derive one from the other, never store both' principle that traceProjection.ts and measurements.ts apply rigorously elsewhere in this file. This is a minor, low-risk redundancy (both sides are ultimately sourced from the same render pass, not two independent computations), and the bead's spec gave the exact shape verbatim, so I implemented it as written rather than redesigning. Worth a design review: either confirm the duplication is intentional (e.g. so a reader of ONLY the delivery field, without re-deriving from trace, gets M6/M7-equivalent facts for free) or drop the two fields and have readers derive them from capture.trace instead.
close_reason: Resolved by the parent bead owner at 9754102: candidateCount and mustConsiderOverflow dropped from ShadowDelivery's injected arm. The finding was correct and the shape was the parent bead's own spec. delivery now carries only facts about the delivered text (renderedBytes, renderedSha256); M6/M7 are derived from capture.trace as everywhere else. The reader rejects either removed field as an unknown key so a stale row cannot be admitted.

title: Flaky CLI packaging test times out under full-suite load
description:
`packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts > package smoke > packs publishable tarballs with
dist output and no source/test files` intermittently fails with
`Test timed out in 10000ms` when run as part of the full Vitest suite, and
passes reliably when its file is run alone.

OBSERVED
2026-09-10/11, on `eshyra-o9bd.19.12` and on `eshyra-o9bd.19.12.2` (a branch
touching only `packages/core/src/discovery` and its tests). Three of five
`npm run verify:worktree` runs failed on it; a plain `npm run test` on the same
tree passed at 5295 passed / 20 skipped, and `npx vitest run
packages/cli/test/cli.test.ts` passed 15/15.

WHY IT MATTERS
It is a false red on the pre-commit gate. An agent that takes it at face value
either burns a cycle chasing an unrelated change or, worse, learns to ignore a
failing gate.

LIKELY CAUSE (unverified)
The test shells out to `npm pack` for both workspaces. Vitest spawns one worker
per file (296 workers observed), so under that load a real `npm pack` can
exceed the declared `timeout: 10_000`. The timeout was presumably sized against
an unloaded run.

CANDIDATE FIXES, in preference order
1. Raise the declared timeout to something that reflects packing two workspaces
   on a loaded machine. Cheapest, and the assertion is about tarball CONTENT,
   not speed — the timeout was never the thing under test.
2. Pack once per suite rather than once per test, if more than one case needs
   the tarball.
3. Only if neither holds: mark the file as needing a dedicated pool.

Do NOT fix it by deleting the assertion or by skipping the test: it guards the
published tarball against shipping source and test files, which is a real
release property.
notes: 2026-09-22 RE-EXAMINED under the 6-worker cap (eshyra-9l5s.2 / PR #552) by eshyra-9l5s.5. VERIFIED CAUSE: worker fan-out contention (default maxWorkers = 20 on this host), per audit docs/audits/test-suite-and-verification/2026-09-14-test-suite-and-verification-audit.md section 2.6. title: Restore the raw-Db guard the discovery ownership analyzer dropped
description:
Narrow follow-up from the PR #538 review (eshyra-o9bd.19.13, merged as a9196de). NOT a known defect: the reviewer inspected the production surface, found no prohibited ownership, and explicitly withdrew the generalized version of this as disproportionate. This bead captures only the cheap subset, so it is not silently lost.

BACKGROUND
The W11 ownership analyzer (packages/core/test/discovery/support/discoveryOwnership.ts) proves discovery owns no campaign-rule/ruling schema, store, cache, resolver, or lifecycle. Its second review pass named three residual bypasses; the third pass withdrew them, on the correct reasoning that no finite checker of this sort IS the ownership invariant -- a fresh shadow resolver would satisfy the behavioural adversary too.

THE ONE PIECE WORTH RESTORING
'../persistence/db.js' is on REVIEWED_FOREIGN_DEPENDENCIES because discovery legitimately takes a Db to resolve the rules stack. The analyzer does not inspect call sites, so a discovery helper doing db.prepare('SELECT * FROM campaign_rule').all() is structurally green while being exactly the discovery-owned active-rule resolver section 8.4 forbids.

Note the regression: the SUPERSEDED spelling-based guard on the same PR did ban both '.prepare(' and 'campaign_rule'. Moving to the AST analyzer was a clear net improvement but dropped that pair. Restoring it costs almost nothing.

PROPOSAL
Add to findOwnershipViolations: no discovery module may call .prepare() on anything, and no discovery module may contain a campaign-rule table name. Both are narrow and complete for what they cover -- there is exactly one way to run SQL through better-sqlite3 here. Add rejection fixtures for each, as every other rule in that analyzer has.

EXPLICIT NON-GOALS (the withdrawn generalization)
Do NOT attempt closure over every TypeScript encoding of prohibited ownership: alternate mutable-state encodings (plain array/object accumulators, custom cache instances, class static fields, IIFE closures), or type-level reshaping (inline object types, Pick<CampaignRulingProjection, ...>). The reviewer's withdrawal reasoning applies -- that is a static-analysis subsystem neither the bead nor the design asks for, and it would turn a proportionate architectural guard into proof machinery for its own sake.

EVIDENCE
A rejection fixture per new rule, plus the existing control that legitimate Db use (resolveStrictCampaignRulesStack via ../state/campaignRecordLookup.js) still passes.

title: Polish rules-pack story with final author edit
description:
Follow-up editorial refinement for the existing /rules-pack/ article originally implemented under eshyra-5f2w. The article is already good enough to ship and remain public long-term. This is optional P3 refinement, not a correctness blocker.

This task is deliberately split between agent work and human authorship. The agent may make only the narrow factual and wording corrections below, then must pause before creating a PR and explicitly ask Joseph to perform his own hand-edit pass on the article. The PR must not be created until Joseph confirms that his edits are complete. The intent is not to have an agent simulate Joseph's voice. The article has already had substantial model-assisted drafting and editing, and Joseph must perform the final personalization pass himself.

Required agent edits:
1. Replace the overstatement approximately phrased as "The pack never needed more data." Preserve the distinction that adding unstructured content was insufficient, richer semantic representation was necessary, and the deeper issue was semantic structure and execution ownership. Use wording such as "The problem was not simply that the pack needed more data." or "More data was not the answer by itself." Choose what fits the surrounding prose.
2. Replace the imprecise statement approximately phrased as "None of that survives as English." The source information does exist in prose and can be understood by a person or model. Clarify that the semantics are not deterministically enforceable while represented only as prose, using wording such as "None of that is machine-enforceable while it exists only as English prose."
3. Restore personal ownership of the importance judgment, preferring "The second example is subtler, and I think more important."
4. Rewrite the line that reads like an editing instruction, approximately "One distinction here is easy to misread, so state it flatly." Use natural prose such as "One distinction here is easy to misread, so it is worth stating flatly."
5. Rewrite the awkward "guessed at into" construction while preserving fail-closed semantics. A suitable shape is: "Prose that falls outside the reviewed shape contributes no semantics at all. The grammar fails closed rather than inventing something plausible."
6. Remove the minimizing "only" from the playtest conclusion. Preserve the boundary that the compiler owns immutable pack semantics, live state remains separate, engine execution remains separate, and playtesting changed the project's understanding of how much semantic information the pack needed to provide. Prefer wording such as: "What playtesting changed was our understanding of how much the pack itself had to say for those other layers to function."

Required human hand-edit checkpoint:
1. The implementation agent creates a branch or worktree for the task and applies only the six narrow corrections.
2. Run enough local verification to ensure the article still builds.
3. Commit the agent-authored mechanical/editorial corrections if that makes the handoff cleaner.
4. Stop before creating a PR.
5. Tell Joseph the exact worktree path, the file to edit (site/src/rules-pack.html.tmpl), and a useful local preview or build command.
6. Explicitly ask Joseph to edit the article directly and tell the agent when his personal prose pass is complete.
7. Wait for Joseph's confirmation.
8. After confirmation, inspect the diff, preserve Joseph's prose choices, and do not normalize his voice toward generic model prose. Make only obvious typo, HTML, or factual corrections if needed, preferably flagging substantive concerns instead of silently rewriting them.
9. Commit Joseph's hand-edit changes separately from the agent edits where practical. Do not add an AI co-author trailer to a commit whose substantive prose changes were written by Joseph.
10. Run full required verification, then create the PR only after the human checkpoint is complete.

Voice guidance:
Preserve Joseph's established authorial traits: analytical and curious; concrete examples before abstraction where useful; audience-calibrated jargon; dry humor that arises naturally; visible uncertainty where real; willingness to show how the conclusion was reached; and parenthetical precision where useful.
Use we for shared work, discovery, accomplishment, and credit. Use I for personal judgment, doubt, criticism, uncertainty, mistakes, and negative responsibility. Reflect praise and absorb blame.
No em dashes and no literal em dash characters or —. Do not introduce repetitive "not X, but Y" constructions, artificial three-part cadence, excessive rhetorical questions, slogan-like conclusions, generic polished transitions, or paragraphs that over-explain examples. The goal is genuine authorship, not model imitation.

Tooltip verification:
The article contains a tooltip-style author aside that previously had clipping problems. During final verification check normal desktop width and narrow/mobile width. Confirm the entire tooltip remains readable, clips on neither side, creates no horizontal scrolling, reveals on keyboard focus, and retains accessible wiring. Make a CSS change only if a real presentation problem remains.

Acceptance criteria:
- All six identified wording issues are corrected.
- No substantive architecture claim is changed.
- Joseph is explicitly invited to perform the final hand-edit pass before PR creation.
- No PR is created until Joseph confirms his hand edits are complete.
- Joseph's resulting prose edits are preserved rather than rewritten by the agent.
- The final article contains no em dashes.
- Tooltip behavior is verified at desktop and narrow widths.
- The site builds successfully.
- No unsubstituted placeholders remain.
- Homepage, article, and download links still work.
- ZIP and checksum generation still work.
- Repository-required checks pass.
- No generated rules-pack records change.
- No freeze manifests or audit artifacts change.
- The final PR description distinguishes the narrow agent corrections from Joseph's hand-edit pass.

title: What Actually Transfers?
description:
Tell the deferred story of adding a second game system.

Narrative hook and core question: After building a deeply D&D-specific compiler, what parts of the architecture were actually reusable?

Do not draft or publish until Pathfinder implementation has materially tested the abstractions. Research source and license authority, source inventory, format-appropriate extraction boundaries, structural parsing versus semantic projection, shared semantic grammars, source-grounded executable curation, pack semantics versus engine services, system-specific versus shared engine behavior, tool integration, character-creation recipes, quality bars, freeze policy, and the lesson that reuse contracts, not document heuristics. The second system is the first honest test of abstraction.

Expected architectural conclusion: only Pathfinder evidence can show which contracts transfer and which apparent abstractions were D&D-shaped assumptions.

Boundary: do not write speculative architecture storytelling based only on D&D. Do not draft or publish before meaningful Pathfinder implementation and campaign-facing evidence exists.

This bead is intentionally deferred. Treat repository history, PRs, design docs, ADRs, audits, and playtest transcripts as evidence once Pathfinder work exists. Verify claims against artifacts rather than model memory; distinguish implemented architecture from planned architecture; preserve public readability and search indexing; and follow Joseph's voice rules: analytical and curious, concrete before abstraction, dry humor when earned, deliberate we/I attribution, reflect praise, absorb blame, no em dashes, and no generic LLM prose.

title: The Adventure Is Not the World
description:
Tell the story of first-class adventure modules.

Narrative hook and core question: What is an adventure module in a system that can improvise indefinitely?

Write only after module architecture is implemented and exercised enough to tell the history honestly. Research why prompt injection of adventure text is insufficient; module as authored canonical spine; module schema and typed records; campaign binding; module progress state; DM runtime context; progress audit; module truth versus player-discovered knowledge; authored content versus campaign divergence; and how improvised consequences overlay authored content without rewriting the source module. Cover Ember Hollow only when the evidence and naming in the repository support it.

Expected architectural conclusion: an adventure module is authored scenario truth with campaign-owned progress and divergence, not the whole world and not a prompt pasted into context.

Boundaries: do not treat the current module epic as complete if it is not. Do not claim module UX or playtest maturity that artifacts do not support. Do not absorb the campaign-memory or rules-pack compiler story.

Use repository history, PRs, design docs, ADRs, audits, and playtest transcripts as evidence. Verify claims against artifacts rather than model memory; distinguish implemented from planned architecture; preserve public readability and search indexing; and follow Joseph's voice rules: analytical and curious, concrete before abstraction, dry humor when earned, deliberate we/I attribution, reflect praise, absorb blame, no em dashes, and no generic LLM prose.

title: A Save Game Is Not a History
description:
Tell the story of campaign checkpoints and history.

Narrative hook and core question: What changes when a campaign must answer not only “can I restore?” but also “what changed, when, and why?”

Research local SQLite campaign/session state, checkpoint snapshots, restore authority, Dolt's role in canonical history, semantic projections or useful diffs, rewind, timeline branching and forking, zero-ops CLI constraints, why a database in the hot gameplay path and a history system are different concerns, and how checkpointing interacts with long campaigns and auditability.

Expected architectural conclusion: a save file restores state. Campaign history also needs explainable change, chronology, and eventually branching.

Boundaries: do not claim unimplemented history UX is shipped. Distinguish current behavior, committed architecture, and future direction. Do not turn this into a generic database article.

Use repository history, PRs, design docs, ADRs, audits, and playtest transcripts as evidence. Verify factual claims against artifacts rather than model memory. Keep the story static, search-indexable, and readable without prior repository knowledge. Follow Joseph's voice rules: analytical and curious, concrete before abstraction, dry humor when earned, deliberate we/I attribution, reflect praise, absorb blame, no em dashes, and no generic LLM prose.

title: Normalize 67 SRD hyphen-space artifacts in generated record strings
description:
Finding source:
- Fable P3 found 67 mid-word hyphen-space artifacts across record strings using /[A-Za-z0-9]+- [a-z]/.
- Examples: "1st- level" in wizard/paladin spellcasting features and candle of invocation, "15- foot cone" in three mephit breath weapons, "20-foot- radius", "two- handed", "self- expression", "10-foot- cube".
- Root cause: line-break dehyphenation inserts a stray space when a compound hyphen falls at a source line break.

Why it matters:
- Visible text quality defect.
- Defeats exact phrase search on gameplay-meaningful compounds.

Acceptance criteria:
- Enumerate all 67 current matches.
- Normalize true extraction artifacts while preserving legitimate source hyphenation.
- Add a regression guard with a small explicit allowlist if needed.
- Confirm no license/provenance/source text is corrupted.

title: Clean up minor SRD spell and item modeling defects from audit
description:
Combined low-priority cleanup from the 2026-06-30 SRD audit round.

Known minor modeling issues:
- Enlarge/Reduce currently represents weapon-damage modifiers as mechanics.damage entries with fake damage types "extra" and "less". These are not real SRD damage types and should not appear in a field that deterministic damage tools interpret as dealt damage.
- Potion of healing appears as equipment:potion-of-healing with display name "Potion of healing" and magic-item:potion-of-healing with display name "Potion of Healing". The duplicate across kinds is defensible, but display capitalization should be normalized if the importer can do so without losing source fidelity.
- Add validation that spell mechanics.damage[].type only contains canonical SRD damage types unless the schema is explicitly expanded for non-damage deltas.

Acceptance criteria:
- Remodel Enlarge/Reduce as a typed weapon-damage delta/effect rather than fake direct damage types.
- Validate that mechanics.damage damage types are canonical damage types.
- Normalize Potion of Healing display name consistently across equipment and magic-item records, or document why source fidelity requires keeping the mismatch.
- Add regression tests.
close_reason: Remodeled Enlarge/Reduce's fake 'extra'/'less' damage types as typed mechanics.weaponDamageModifiers; validated mechanics.damage[].type against the 13 canonical SRD damage types; documented Potion of Healing's intentional per-kind capitalization (each spelling is source-accurate for its own physical location).

title: Add structured armor AC data for deterministic equipment calculations
description:
The SRD 5.1 equipment records preserve armor AC values as source-shaped strings, which is accurate enough for prose/display but weaker than needed for deterministic character-sheet and combat tooling.

Confirmed in the 2026-06-30 audit bundle `/home/jhbongaarts/src/dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle-0630-1.zip`:
- `equipment:chain-mail` has `data.ac: "16"`.
- `equipment:leather` has `data.ac: "11 + Dex modifier"`.
- `equipment:shield` has `data.ac: "+2"`.
- No structured fields distinguish base AC, Dex modifier allowance/cap, shield bonus, stealth disadvantage, or strength requirements as machine-executable armor rules.

This is not a current pack accuracy blocker: the string values match the source-shaped table data and existing schema/tests permit them. It is a deterministic gameplay usability gap for tools that need to compute AC without reparsing prose/formula strings.

Acceptance criteria:
- Decide and document the structured armor/equipment AC schema needed by deterministic tools.
- Emit structured armor calculation data for SRD armor and shields while retaining source text/provenance.
- Add validation/tests for representative light armor, medium armor, heavy armor, and shield records.
close_reason: Added structured data.armorClass ({base, dexModifier, dexModifierCap?} for armor; {bonus} for shields) derived deterministically from the verbatim ac cell, alongside the retained ac string. Validated in kindSchemas.ts; fails closed on any AC shape outside the four reviewed SRD 5.1 cases.

title: Add clean-environment (no native toolchain) release artifact smoke test
description: ADR 0016 (docs/adr/0016-native-dependency-install-policy-by-environment.md) requires proving that unpacked release artifacts run without a native build toolchain present, not just with a restricted PATH on a toolchain-equipped GitHub-hosted runner. Add a release.yml job that runs the unpacked launcher (bin/eshyra, no-config exit-1 path) inside an environment that genuinely lacks a C/C++ toolchain (e.g. a minimal Linux container image without build-essential/python3), fed a pre-built artifact from the existing build job. Scope initial coverage to Linux; Windows/macOS GitHub-hosted runners ship toolchains by default and cannot easily be made toolchain-free without self-hosted runners, per ADR 0016.
acceptance_criteria: A release.yml job runs the bundled CLI launcher against a genuinely toolchain-free Linux environment and asserts the same no-config behavior validate-release-artifact.mjs already checks (exit 1, expected guidance output). The job is gated the same way as other release-path checks (runs on PR when release inputs change, and on tag pushes). Documented in docs/cli-distribution.md or the ADR itself once implemented.
close_reason: Merged as PR #379 (merge commit 8db918d). clean-env-smoke.sh + the clean-env-smoke release job run the linux-x64 artifact's bundled launcher inside a toolchain-free debian:bookworm-slim container (self-checks gcc/make/python3/node absent), asserting exit 1 + setup guidance; gates tag publication. Confirmed passing in real CI. ADR 0016 layer-3 clean-env requirement now satisfied.

comments.author: Joseph Bongaarts

Implemented in PR #379. scripts/release/clean-env-smoke.sh + the clean-env-smoke release.yml job run the linux-x64 artifact's bundled launcher inside a debian:bookworm-slim container that genuinely lacks gcc/cc/make/cmake/python/python3/node/npm/node-gyp (self-checked), with a scrubbed no-config env, asserting exit 1 + setup guidance. description: Deficiency #5. Exported class record folds the Druid metal restriction into the armorProficiencies token: 'shields (druids will not wear armor or use shields made of metal)'. Schema already anticipates proficiencyNotes for exactly this. Fix: normalize Druid armorProficiencies to ["Light armor","medium armor","shields"] and emit a separate proficiencyNotes entry with the metal restriction. Generalize to any similar parenthetical mechanical note folded into a proficiency token. Re-freeze gate: no mixed mechanical note tokens in proficiency arrays.
notes: STALE-SNAPSHOT FINDING (from o9bd.11 verification 2026-06-28): the committed pack ALREADY has clean armorProficiencies:[Light armor, medium armor, shields] + a proficiencyNotes:[{field,text}] array for Druid. The metal restriction is already lifted. This bead may be largely/fully DONE — re-verify the committed pack before implementing. The o9bd.11 proficiency-note-bleed gate ships GREEN as a regression guard for this.
